Washed with scented water, it is spat back in his face. (Xuědòu Xiǎn)
Transcending all direct perception, one immediately awakens to the cause of water; its essence is luminous and stainless—whom can it wash?
Having attained non-existence, one realizes the formless body and dwells as a child of the Buddha; wondrous touch is ever-present. (Daopei Zhi)

Washing away dust and contact, both body and mind are empty and still; wondrously realizing the secret perfection, one transcends view-delusion and thought-delusion. A flawless white jade suddenly receives a blemish;
within the Assembly of Perfect Penetration, one suffers being smeared with filth. (The Poisoned Whip)

how much more so, then, are all worlds contained within empty space? When even one person among you gives rise to true realization and returns to the source, this emptiness of the ten directions will entirely vanish and perish. The Verse says:
When one person gives rise to true awakening and returns to the source, the empty space of the ten directions vanishes.
Try asking Yangqi about the chestnut burr—how does it compare to Yunmen’s “moldy cake”? (Nun Wuzhuo Zong).
Drowsiness was vast and weary thoughts arose; drinking a bowl of strong tea, my eyes opened at once.
Within the transformative influence of the King’s rule across the four seas and five lakes, there is not a single thing that is dust or defilement. (Pak Ung-hyeon)

The *Nirvāṇa-samantabhadra-bodhicitta-uttaratantra-sūtra* (The Perfect Enlightenment Sūtra). Thus have I heard. At one time, the Bhagavān entered into the great light of supernormal powers (*abhijñā*).
This is the samādhi of the luminous treasury, the abiding sustenance of the light-adornment of all Tathāgatas.

It is the ground of pure awakening for all sentient beings, the state of quiescence and equality of body and mind, the primordial limit. It is perfectly fulfilled throughout the ten directions, non-dual, and in accord with reality. The verse says:
East, west, south, and north—the waters stretch boundlessly. A hornless iron ox enters the ocean’s depths; the Thousand-Eyed Compassionate One searches but cannot find it.
Riding backward upon the Buddha hall, he enters the monks’ hall. (Yefu Creek)

[Added for inclusion] *The Sūtra of Perfect Enlightenment*: "Within the realm of non-duality, he manifests all pure lands, together with one hundred thousand great bodhisattva-mahāsattvas. The verse says:

it does not hinder one from enjoying the mist and clouds wherever one may be. (Yayufu Stream)
[Added for inclusion] *The Sūtra of Perfect Enlightenment*: "That which is not illusion does not cease. The verse says:
Neither belonging to the internal, the external, nor the intermediate, As soon as it falls into thought, one enters the realm of Māra.
A true man does not deceive himself; He turns his body around and sits firmly atop the crown of Vairocana. (Yuelin Guan)

The earth is vast and boundless as one searches for the old cave; pointing to where it was painted, it is but a speck in the eye.
Having reached this point, why need there be further words? (Yuwang Da).
[Added for inclusion] *The Sutra of Perfect Enlightenment*: "All obstacles are ultimate awakening. The Verse says:

Withered trees are filled with clouds for leaves; Falling plum blossoms become flowers of snow. Striking the paulownia wood produces the sound of timber; Dipping into the snow, one eats a winter melon.
Vast autumn sky, solitary wild goose, setting clouds. (From *Xuetang Xing*) At dawn, the heart is weary—three cups of wine;
In the afternoon, the head grows dull—a bowl of tea. When night falls, one strips off clothes and stretches out to sleep;
At the fifth watch, one starts up, eyes bleary and numb. (From *Huan’ou’an Ti*)
[Added for inclusion] *The Sutra of Perfect Enlightenment*: "Those who possess self-love also love nirvana; they suppress the root of self-love to take it as the mark of nirvana. The verse says:

thus, although one may manifest the superior fruits of conditioned virtue, these all pertain to saṃsāra and do not constitute the Path of the Sage. The verse says:
A puppet dances the *zhèzhī* with strings pulled; in a hundred ways it is clever and charming, suited to every occasion.
Since the green silk snapped when the dance ended, one can only laugh as it lets go of its hands and returns home.
The *Sūtra of Perfect Enlightenment* states: "At all times, do not give rise to deluded thoughts; yet do not attempt to extinguish those deluded minds.
Abide within the realm of deluded appearances without applying analytical cognition; and within this absence of analytical cognition, do not discriminate what is real."

The verse says: Yellow flowers in full bloom; Green bamboos in elegant rows. Warmth abounds in the lands south of the Yangtze; Cold prevails here in the northern reaches. After the traveler has departed, there is no news;
Only the mountain streams and hills remain for one to behold until old age. (Huitang Xian)
Raising his hand, he grasps the Southern Dipper; turning his body, he leans against the Northern Pole Star. Looking out from beyond the heavens, who is there like this man? (Gushan Gui)
Majestic and imposing; vast and unimpeded. Thrusting his head into the fray, he plants his feet firmly on solid ground. When the thread beneath his feet snaps, he is free;
when the mud from the tip of his nose is gone, you must cease your chiseling. Do not move it! Within these ancient scrolls of a thousand years, the medicine is compounded. (Tiantong Jue).
The lotus leaves are round and round, as round as mirrors; The water chestnuts are pointed and pointed, as pointed as awls. The wind blows the willow catkins like fur balls away;
The rain beats the pear blossoms as butterflies fly. (Jingshan Gaofeng)
Fishing for the moon amidst the mist is my lifelong vocation. My ancient strategy is lofty, yet it is not enough to boast of.
With a single cry of "Kwan-nai," heaven and earth open wide; where has the Patriarch crossed the shifting sands? (Huokan Ti)
A monkey eats a fur-worm; a black dog ascends the Buddha hall. The great earth is covered in vast snow; the clear river is as pure as a silk ribbon. (Cen Yuanji)
Cast from raw iron is an ox-head; it pulls the plow and drags the rake. The wise man laughs with joy; the foolish person is startled and bewildered.
From antiquity until today, how many hundreds of years have passed? Yet once again, at the Gate of Ghosts, one pastes up a new talisman. (Mimian Jie)
Lettuce is planted before the courtyard. From the lettuce grow chopsticks. From the chopsticks grows a lotus flower. The lotus flower bears wooden claws.
As soon as the papaya is split open, white sesame seeds spill forth. *Chen*. (Rendangren).
Last night, deep in the sands, we forged an iron covenant; Aniruddha came to join our company. We grew drunk and struck one another, only to see King Yama.
King Yama took up his brush but could not pass judgment; unable to judge, he instead exhorted us: "The affairs of both parties are like those of one family."
Do not further engage in prior reflections or subsequent calculations. [口+力].
For you to judge such a case as "great vinegar" (Wuan Quan), Zhang Guolao has trampled his gourd, and Lü Dongbin has lost his precious sword. The two meet with hands cast loose.
In his bags and baskets, there is not even a single thread left. He Xianggu blows her iron flute crosswise; she understands how to say that the Yangtze River is as still as a silken ribbon.
(From Zhengtang’s Discourse: Life and the world drift on like an unmoored boat; where one may follow the current, one should simply follow the current. Today there is wine, so drink today.
Intoxicated. No money tomorrow, so tomorrow there is worry. (Shi’an Shao).
Sleeping through spring, one does not perceive the dawn; everywhere one hears the singing birds. Last night’s sound of wind and rain—how many fallen flowers one knows not.
(Park Ung-seon): Born in spring and grown in summer, eating plain rice and coarse tea; like a fish cast into turbid water, its brilliant colors flee to a cramped dwelling. (Mu Jun-bam).
[Added for inclusion] From the *Sūtra of Perfect Enlightenment*: "I take Great Perfect Enlightenment as my monastery.

The verse says: Not a hair’s breadth left behind; moving freely in all directions. Beyond the threshold, heaven and earth are vast and open; within the Great Dharma, there is no exterior, and one wanders with ease.
Vividly clear is the meaning of the Patriarchs; vividly clear is the tip of every blade of grass. Tear asunder the net of doubt; cut off the river of craving.
Even if one possessed the power to turn back heaven, how could that compare to resting directly beneath? In the middle of the four-way crossroads, all is starkly bare;
let loose the water-buffalo of Mui Shan. (Yuanwu Keqin)
[Added for inclusion] *The Sutra of Perfect Enlightenment* states: "One should constantly maintain this thought: 'This body of mine is a combination of the four great elements.
The hair, fur, nails, and teeth all return to earth; saliva, mucus, pus, and blood all return to water; warmth returns to fire; and movement returns to wind.
When the four great elements separate, where will this illusory body now abide? " The verse says:
Where now does this delusory body abide? One should not seek waves within the flames of water. The frantic mind mistakenly recognizes its own reflection in a mirror;
how is this any different from the headless Yajnadatta who lost his head in confusion? (Fundamental Awakening I)
[Added for inclusion] *The Lotus Sūtra*: The Buddha emits a ray of light from the white tuft between his eyebrows, illuminating eighteen thousand worlds in the eastern direction. The verse says:
The Mian slave goes barefoot to the Imperial Capital; having sold all his rare treasures, he rides a white ox. Greedily attached to the marketplace, people gather there as a market;
then again, following songs and dances, he ascends the palace towers. Full of spirit and fond of elegance, the moon grows cold as pearl curtains hang from jade hooks.
Clearly, he has lost the path he came; atop a hundred-foot pole, he rolls a brocade ball. (Yuanji Cen)

[Added from the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka-sūtra*]: "Even if the entire world were filled with those like Śāriputra, and they were to exhaust their thoughts to measure it together, they could not fathom the Buddha’s wisdom.

Wuzu Yan said: "Ordinarily, when members of the monastic community give a high bow to Śākyamuni and do not prostrate to Maitreya, are they realizing the Buddha’s wisdom or not? There are those among you who have [realized it]."
He merely conceals his fangs and hides his claws. Taiping had a point of view; without sparing his eyebrows, he presents it to all of you.
When someone asks, he answers immediately according to the occasion. Pō’ān first said, "But ultimately, what is Buddha-wisdom? and then offered this verse:
Snowflakes fall in profusion; a black basin turns into a white basin. Suddenly the sun comes out, and it is once again a black basin. [Added from another source.
The *Lotus Sūtra*, in the "Universal Gate" chapter of the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara, states in verse: "As for various curses and poisonous drugs..."
"Those who wish to harm one's body, By recollecting the power of Avalokiteśvara, Return to their own persons. The Layman Dongpo added his own verse:

the harms of poison and the calamities of the conflagration were manifold. The verse says:
The butterfly and bee cease their longing for their old nests; five hundred young masters can do nothing about it. Pressed by the fire of desire, there is no road to flee;
with a foolish heart, they wish to mount the white ox-cart. The sheep and deer outside the gate serve as mere metaphors; the barking and snarling within the room are all errors.
Amidst the swirling embers and stinking smoke that cause mutual vexation, one need not stir up weapons to leave this place. (Yayufu Stream).

Therein is no birth-and-death, neither retiring nor emerging; there is neither one who remains in the world nor one who has entered parinirvāṇa. It is neither real nor unreal, neither suchness nor different.
He does not perceive the triple world as the triple world is perceived by others. Such matters as these the Tathāgata clearly sees without [obstruction].
There is an error. The verse says:
The Stele of Shen Yu atop Mount Xunlou— Its characters are green, its stone is red, and its form is strange.
If a sightless immortal were to catch even a glimpse of it, He would surely clap his hands and laugh "xi xi. The clouds darken as the Azure Dragon transforms at Gepei. (Yuanji Cen)
Fire has ravaged it, wind has devoured it, and water has soaked its roots. Yet by the stones, the traces of ancient moss still remain.
Does the Creator refuse to follow the cycles of cold and heat? Once more, he nurtures its fragrant essence to restore its soul. (Xianji Yun)
[Added for inclusion] *The Lotus Sūtra*. This sūtra opens the gate of expedient means and reveals the mark of ultimate reality.
It is profound, firm, remote, and deep, such that no one can reach it. The verse says:
Though the path traversed is remote and long, only those who arrive know this City of No Night. The drum and horn sounds chill as the lotus-water clock flows on;
the Buddha-lamp still shines with its former brilliance. (Cen Yuanji)
[Added from the Supplement] The *Lotus Sūtra* says: "This Dharma abides in its own place; the characteristics of the world are eternally constant.
Yunmen said: "Where has Old Śākyamuni gone? The verse says:
The puppy barks at the thief; the ox-calf pulls the plow. If a patch-robed monk acts like this, he has not yet even touched the skin. (Yangqi Hui)
The characteristics of the world are eternally abiding; the yellow oriole sings in the green trees. Truly, how pitiable it is—once stirred, it flies away. (Pak Ung-hyeon)
Verses from the Lotus Sūtra: The Buddha Mahābhijñājñānābhibhū sat at the site of enlightenment for ten eons.
The Buddha-dharma did not manifest before him, and he could not attain the Way of Buddhahood. The Verse says:
When the three periods of time are severed, ordinary and holy beings alike vanish; where the ten bodies are perfected, they pervade the atoms of all lands.
Responding to things without partiality according to their high or low capacities, one has not yet passed through the cultivation of great *asaṃkhyeya* kalpas. (Baoning Yong)
Sowing grain does not produce bean sprouts; how could steaming sand ever make rice?
Tathāgata Mahābhijñājñānābhibhū was a fellow who carried only one shoulder of the board. (Gushan Gui)
[Continued Collection] Sitting in meditation at the site of enlightenment for ten kalpas, one by one, from the very beginning, everything has been leaked out.
How many people in the world are there who sit waiting by the stump, brandishing their sticks as if to strike the moon in the sky? (Jingshan Gao).
The red sun shines brightly; take care not to seek it out. Pick it up and use it immediately; there is nothing that is not a treasure.
Pear trees in Zhengzhou, jujube trees in Qingzhou—generally speaking, their origins are excellent. (Yuelin Guan).

In an era of Great Peace, there is no concern for military affairs; travelers need not carry provisions on the road, and households need not bolt their doors. Having sat through ten kalpas, what has been accomplished?
My lifelong courage and resolve are now poured out all at once. (By Daochang Rong)
The Vairocana Seal was cast at the beginning of the kalpa; the ancient seal-script, though worn like an insect’s carving, remains distinct.
How laughable and how tragic that people do not recognize it, yet instead resent the calligraphy for being incomplete. (Huanxi I)

[Added for inclusion: *The Lotus Sutra*: "If there are sentient beings who hear this 'Chapter on Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva,' you should know that the merit of such persons is not small. The verse says:
The Gate of Avalokiteśvara is gathered within the Universal Gate; as soon as one puts on the lined robe, there is no shame. Last night the monkey cried upon the new ridge;
this morning the crane calls at the head of the ancient stream. When the fierce wind blows and falls, the returning light subsides;
when the fire of desire burns, it ceases right where it is. Having received the jeweled necklaces, they are of no further use; the livelihood of daily life is cool and still. (Yayufuan).
In the Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra spoken by Mañjuśrī, it is said: "The practitioner of purity does not enter nirvana;
the precept-breaking bhikṣu does not enter hell. The verse says:
Throughout his life he was carefree and unrestrained; he wandered at will through wine shops and tea houses. Neither the Han land could contain him nor the Qin state could restrain him;
once again, he rode his donkey past Yangzhou. (Baoning Yong)
Having raised a water-buffalo in the family pen, it has its own reasons for returning and departing. Now it lies peacefully nestled within the deep clouds;
Qin does not care, and Han does not claim it. (Zuyin Ming)
The crane is white and the crow is naturally black; the pine is straight and the thorn-bush is naturally crooked. A pure and serene bhikṣu-saṃgha must nevertheless enter hell. (Gushan Gui)
A lamp is hung upon the wall; a wine stand is set before the hall. When weariness comes, I strike three cups.
From where could sorrow come? (Jingshan Gaofeng)
[Continued Collection] A monk asked Dōngshān Chuàn, "When it is said that a pure practitioner does not enter nirvana, and a precept-breaking bhikṣu does not enter hell, what then?
The Master said, "When all have been delivered without a trace remaining, he returns to transcend nirvana."
The Verse says:
With marks and signs so majestic, a great man indeed; In a single lifetime, he lacks worldly wisdom and is just like a fool.
From of old, even Buddhas and Patriarchs have found him hard to look up to; How could he be confined by hell or heaven? (Danxia Chun)
The pure practitioner does not enter nirvana; the precept-breaking bhikṣu has no hell.
From Tiantai’s meeting with Xichuan, they are all one’s own kinsmen. (Zhaotang I)
Returning from drinking in the village last night, I arrived home with vigor at the third, fourth, or fifth watch. I stroked the green moss;
do not be angry that you were startled by me. (Zidehui)
The stone statue of Jiazhou; the iron ox of Shanfu. When people are level, they do not speak; when water is level, it does not flow.
(Master Wuzhuo of Ni). Paying money to dangle marionettes; risking one’s life on a swing. The whole family has no eyes to see; they cover their faces and weep to the blue heavens.
(Or the essence of the hermitage):
Those who serve the spirits consume the spirits; those who serve the Buddha consume the Buddha. When neither spirit nor Buddha is served, the entire household is utterly impoverished to the bone.
(Kentang Chong). Once the Han had ceased to govern and the Qin had ceased to collect taxes, people remained silent when things were level, and water ceased to flow when it was level. (Yuelin Guan).
A bhikṣu who has committed a grave offense practices pure conduct; within the state of equality, there is neither loss nor gain. One does not seek the tracks of fish in the water;
where can one observe the traces of birds at the edge of the sky? (Lan’an Shu)
The state has swords to quell disorder; the household lacks the White Zé Map. The immortal Zhang Guolao trampled his medicinal gourd to pieces. (By Pǔwēng Xiān)
Pure practitioners are pure; precept-breaking bhikṣus are precept-breaking. Each should remain settled within their own realm.
By all means, do not allow thieves to pass beyond the border. (Tuan’an Qi)
Drinking the government's wine and sleeping on the government's streets—one shall be executed right there, buried right there.
When Hanshan meets Shide, they clap their hands and laugh heartily. (This mountain is indeed so.)
Nirvana and hell are fundamentally no different; it is only because they have long been obscured by the eyes.
As soon as the three-legged blind donkey takes a leap, the boiling cauldrons and furnace coals are none other than my own home. (Gao Feng Miao)
In the Vimalakīrti Sūtra, Subhūti entered the house of Vimalakīrti with his alms bowl to beg for food.
At that time, Vimalakīrti took the bowl and filled it with rice, saying: "If you can regard food as equal, then all dharmas are also equal;
if all dharmas are equal, then food is also equal. Only by begging in such a manner may you take this food. And so on, until [the passage concerning] those outsiders.
"Follow the six teachers as your own teachers. Because you have left the home life under them, you too shall fall wherever those teachers fall;

only then may you accept this food. You have entered into various false views and failed to reach the further shore. You dwell among the eight difficulties and have not attained freedom from difficulty.
You are equal to the afflictions and have departed from the pure Dharma. You have attained the Samādhi of Non-contention. (1)
All sentient beings shall likewise attain this samādhi. Those who give to you are not called fields of merit;
those who make offerings to you will fall into the three evil paths. You act in concert with the various māras, serving as their companions in toil.
You are no different from the māras and all the afflictions (*kleśa*). Toward all sentient beings, you harbor enmity.
"One who slanders the Buddhas, destroys the Dharma, and is not counted among the assembly shall never attain parinirvāṇa.
If you are such a person, only then may you take this food. When Subhūti heard this, he was utterly bewildered and did not know how to respond.
Setting down his bowl, he was about to depart. A verse says:
"Boundless and limitless, there is no need for deliberation; The tide ebbs and flows, yet it is fundamentally level.
Clear or turbid, shallow or deep, bitter or bland— A single flavor, distinct and clear. (Baoning Yong)

Entering the forest without moving the grass; entering the water without stirring the waves. In the cauldron of boiling water, there is no place that is cool. Closing one’s eyes and leaping across the Yellow River. (Gushan Gui)
Sitting alone, who can know my heart? Green mountains face the setting sun. The flowers must bloom throughout the night; they do not wait for the morning breeze to blow. (Jingshan Gaofeng)
[Continued Collection] Walking alone on the streets during the day; lying down alone in the house at night. The height of the mountains does not obstruct the flight of white clouds;
the density of the bamboo does not hinder the flow of the stream. (Zhao Tang 1)
With false views, you have taken refuge with a non-Buddhist teacher; that you shall fall together with him—why doubt it? Relying on you, may your alms bowl be filled with fragrant rice;
for at this noon hour, my belly is truly hungry. (Zhang Wujin)
Seven times seven is forty-nine; six times six is thirty-six. As soon as right and wrong enter the ear, the whole family is not in harmony. (Kentang Chong)
Playing alone with the single extraction; the single extraction played alone. Walking upon the edge of a sword, silent and unmoving. (Moon Forest Contemplation).
What is produced differs in each case, yet what moistens is the universal rain. The sweet melon is sweet through to its stem; the bitter gourd is bitter down to its roots.
(Binggu Yan): Green mountains and white clouds;
azure streams and moonlight through the vines. To paint a tiger and end up with a wildcat—this only results in a single wedge. (Xutang Yu).
[Added for inclusion: In the *Vimalakīrti Sūtra*, thirty-two bodhisattvas each expounded the gate of non-duality (*advaya-dvāra*).
When it came to Mañjuśrī, he said: "Regarding all dharmas, I have no speech and no discourse; there is no demonstration and no cognition;
I am free from all questioning and answering—this is the bodhisattva’s entry into the gate of non-duality. Mañjuśrī then questioned Vimalakīrti, who remained silent. Mañjuśrī praised him.
He said: "Even to the point where there are no words or letters—this is the true entrance into the Dharma-gate of non-duality.

When he spoke these words on entering the Dharma-gate of non-duality, five thousand bodhisattvas within this assembly all entered the Dharma-gate of non-duality and attained the forbearance of the non-arising of dharmas (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*). The verse says:
Where has the Great Being Vimalakīrti gone? For a thousand ages, people have gazed after him, never reaching the end of their longing.
There is no need to ask further about the Gate of Non-duality; last night, the bright moon ascended the high peak. (Xuedou Xian)
In the void, the tracks of birds are vainly sought; the hidden bird casts its cry, again heralding spring.
If one recognizes that east and west are no different paths, the single room of Vimalakīrti will not remain submerged in obscurity. (Ciming Yuan)
In the city of Vaiśālī, they race against one another in vain competition; they deludedly claim the Southern Star is truly the Northern Dipper.
Do they know that the clam and the heron, locked in mutual entanglement, will in an instant fall entirely into the hands of the fisherman? (Great Compassion).
One, two, hundreds, thousands, tens of thousands—counting on one's fingers to seek out the patterns, the numbers cannot be grasped.
For a moment, place them before a dark window; tomorrow, I shall calculate them with you again. (Baiyun Cuan)
In spring there are a hundred flowers; in autumn, the moon. In summer there are cool breezes; in winter, the snow.
If there are no worldly concerns upon the mind, This is indeed a fine season in the human world. (Nedang Si)
The old Vimalakīrti within the city of Vaiśālī—his silence and lack of speech are full of guile.
How he will act when all thirty-two thousand lion thrones are overturned at once! (Wúyòngquán).
"Speaking, speaking, speaking—like a gale scattering snow. Silence, silence, silence—the son of thunder, where lightning flashes and crashes.
Riding the Great Peng within the pores of a lotus fiber, he casually knocks down the moon at the edge of heaven. (Lan’an Xu)

Vimalakīrti was skilled at concealing his wondrous mechanisms; in profound silence, his thunderous voice resounded through the four quarters. Throughout antiquity and the present, they have vied to transmit this true non-duality.
Who would have known that yellow leaves were used merely to stop a child’s crying? (By the nun Wuzhuo).
Whether speaking or remaining silent, all talk is but vain toil; when has the Layman ever moved so much as a hair? Emperor Shizu achieved his great deeds at thirty-six;
yet how can the Cloud Terrace compare to the loftiness of the Fishing Terrace? (By Biefeng Yin)
Entering deeply into the gate of non-duality, skillfulness is exhausted and turns into clumsiness. A single silence settles a thousand differences;
though he speaks constantly, his speech is a blazing discourse on clumsiness. For ten thousand ages, the pure wind chills to the very bone. (Songyuan Yue)
[Added for inclusion] *The Vimalakīrti Sūtra*: "Entering nirvāṇa without severing afflictions. The verse says:
Born in the morning, dying by evening—ten thousand times over. How many times a day do they meet face-to-face? Unfurling banners and deploying the ranks, they come forth;
When a single finger moves, the guest’s play is revealed. (Baiyun Cuan)

[Added for inclusion] A monk asked Touzi, "How does one enter nirvana without severing afflictions? The Master said, "This monk is creating karma for people in such a manner. The Verse says: The monk asks about the path of non-severance;

Though there is no front or back, it manifests at every point of contact. Swallowing up the vast void, he spits out the crystal palace. (Focincai)
"This monk incites people's karma; the old oil-seller tells it to others. Crying until one’s blood flows is of no use;
it is better to keep one’s mouth shut and pass through the remainder of spring. (Mañjuśrī says.)
[Added from the *Vimalakīrti Sūtra*]: "Contemplate the true mark of the body; contemplate the Buddha likewise. The Verse says:
The eyes empty the four seas, roaming freely and unrestrained; The nostrils reach the vast heavens as he walks with confident steps.
Seizing a flash of lightning to serve as a torch, He returns at high noon to strike the third watch. (Or-an Ti)
[Added for inclusion] *The Vimalakīrti Sūtra*: "When the Buddha expounds the Dharma with a single voice, some are struck with fear while others have their doubts severed.
The verse says:
"Some are struck with fear, others have their doubts severed; A single phrase clarifies both, transcending the reach of needle and chisel. Regarding this, do not give rise to even the slightest joy."
Disgust. To meet face-to-face, one must have eyes like eyebrows. (Heshan Fang).
[Added from the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*]: At mealtime, the World-Honored One put on his robes and took up his bowl, entering the city of Śrāvastī to beg for food.
Having finished begging for food in the city in due order, he returned to his original place, put away his robes and bowl, and washed his feet.
Having spread his seat, he sat down. Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying, "It is rare, World-Honored One!
The verse says: Meal finished, he sits cross-legged upon the stone bed; Between the constellations, the vital breath illuminates the heavens with light.
How many of those whose karmic consciousnesses are vast and茫然 (mángmáng) Cover their heads with patched robes, dwelling in the realm of intoxication? (Shuian 1)
Not a single word has ever been spoken of Prajñā; it deceives heaven and earth, granting as much as it pleases.
After returning from begging for alms in Jeta Grove, who else could have been the cause of this Dharma assembly? (Beijian Jian)
While begging for alms from door to door in the city of Vaiśālī, and while gathering robes and washing his feet at the Jetavana Grove, Subhūti unexpectedly praised [the Buddha] as marvelous.
How could such words be otherwise? (From *Bǎoyèyuán*).
[Added for inclusion: *The Diamond Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*: "One should abide thus; thus should one subdue the mind. Verse:
How rare, how rare is the Buddha! His wondrous principle reaches the ultimate Nirvana. How can one subdue and abide? To subdue the mind through faith is difficult indeed.

The Dharma within the two polarities is subtle; the teachings and parables of the Three Vehicles are broad. Excellent! Now listen attentively, so that the six thieves may be spared from obstruction. (Master Fu Da Shi)
Seven hands and eight feet; divine heads and demonic faces. Unopenable by staff-blows; unseverable by sword-cuts.
Leaping and bounding through Jambudvīpa thousands of times—everywhere, one does not depart from the Hall of the Empty King. (Yayufuan)
Severing the continuous flow from the teachings, one follows the current yet need not drift aimlessly. The green mountains hold fast their soaring momentum;
the vast blue sea surely knows the height of its source. (Xinwen Ben)
[Added for inclusion] *The Diamond Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*: "All marks whatsoever are empty and false.
If one perceives all marks as non-marks, then one sees the Tathāgata. Fayan said: "If one perceives all marks as non-marks, then one does not see the Tathāgata. The verse says:
Having marks and having seeking are both delusions; being formless and markless falls into partiality and desiccation.
How could there ever be an interval between this majestic and subtle [reality]? A single path of cold light dazzles the great void. (Yeyu Chuan).
Reflecting in the woods, reflecting in the sun, all are one and the same red. Blown down, blown open—all is but the wind.
A pity that those who would pluck the fragrance do not see; it is all at once entrusted to the wandering bees. (Xinwen Ben)
In the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*, it is said: "All worthy sages are distinguished by means of the unconditioned (*asaṃskṛta*) Dharma.
The verse says:
"A single piece of gold forms ten thousand vessels; all this arises from the artisan’s wisdom. Why need one go to the city of Vaiśālī for everyone there to preach non-duality?"
(Juehaiyuan). The benevolent see it and call it benevolence; the wise see it and call it wisdom. When cold, one turns toward the fire; when hot, one seeks the cool breeze.
When vigorous, one practices walking meditation (*caṅkrama*); when weary, one sleeps. One looks up at the sky and opens the mouth to draw breath. (Bao)
[Included for collection:
The *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*. All Buddhas and the *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* dharma of all Buddhas emerge from this sūtra. A monk asked Shoushan: "What is this?"
The Scripture says: “Mount,” he said, lowering his voice. “What is upholding it? Mount replied: “Do not defile it. Yefu Chuan said:

“Tell me, from where does this scripture emerge? From the summit of Mount Sumeru, from the heart of the great ocean waves. He then offered this verse: From the summit of Sumeru, From the center of the vast sea waves, It emerges—do not defile it.
The Buddhas and Patriarchs extend their compassion; truly there is expedient means. Every word is proclaimed without departing from this sutra.
If you can entrust yourself to the source from which this sutra emerges, you will immediately board an iron boat amidst the clouds. Be careful not to misunderstand.
Water flows from Mount Kunlun and rises as clouds; the fisherman and woodcutter ask for its origin. They know only that the surging waves and mountain crags are vast;
they refuse to cast their lines or wield their axes. (Touzi Qing)
Chanting for a long duration without ceasing, it is neither the meaning nor the sound. If one wishes to receive and uphold [the teachings], one must listen with the eye. (Baoxiangyuan)
[Added for inclusion] From the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*: "One should give rise to the mind without abiding anywhere. The verse says:
Sitting in stillness in the mountain hall, silence prevails at night; In profound stillness and vast emptiness, all is naturally so. What cause stirs the west wind through the forests and fields?
A single cry from a cold wild goose echoes across the long sky. (Yemufu Chuan)
One should dwell nowhere, leaving the mind vast and empty. Yet golden dust still clings within the eye. Suddenly, both sky and earth are cast off;
the great thousandfold world-scripture is all at once penetrated. (Gu Yun Quan)
One should give rise to the mind without abiding anywhere; vast, penetrating, and perfectly luminous, it is true in every place.
Directly beneath, the Eye of Correctness opens at the crown of the head, and throughout the great chiliocosm, the entire body manifests. (Dingtang’s Verse).

*Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*: "If a person is treated with contempt by others, that person’s karmic offenses from previous lives—which would have caused them to fall into the evil realms—are instead extinguished because of being treated with contempt by people in this life.
They shall attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*. The Verse says:
The bright pearl is held in the palm; those with merit are rewarded. Neither Hu nor Han can approach; there is absolutely no skill or artifice.
Since there is no skill or artifice, Pāpīyas loses his way. "Gautama, Gautama, do you recognize me? (Xuedou Xian).
Who does not know that water does not wash water? The whirlwind is ever still, yet it rushes on with great haste.
If one could calculate the days of a thousand years, one might avoid being pushed by the magistrate’s palm. (Baizhang Yuan).
The four seasons of heat and cold pass away and return again; the holy and the ordinary are but a single kṣaṇa apart. The sins and karma of those before have become the lowliness of those now;
they have overturned the mountain of the former ones' transgressions. (Zhang Wujin)
[Continued Collection]: The precious sword is not lost; the empty boat is not carved. Not losing and not carving—both sides attain it. Relying and waiting are untenable;
it remains solitary and such. Bird tracks in the void; existence and non-existence are utterly indistinguishable. Contemplate this. (Fayan Yi).
At midnight, the window is bright; a neighbor’s house is on fire. Old Bao knocks at the door; Old Li beats upon the lock. Old Wang calls for a boat;
Old Zhao crosses the ferry. The oil is spent and the lamp goes out—a scene of utter confusion. (Fujian Qin).
Succession upon succession of merits and faults; entanglement after entanglement of cause and effect. Outside the mirror, Yanruo (Evil Mind) runs wild;
with the staff’s blow, he strikes and shatters Pozhuo (Broken Oven Fall). Once the oven is shattered, they congratulate one another, yet he says, "I have been neglecting you all along. (Tiantong Jue)
[Added for inclusion] *The Diamond Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*: "The *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* attained by the Tathāgata—within this, there is neither reality nor unreality. The verse says:
Enlightenment is neither real nor false; how many men among us are true heroes? The cinnabar valley does not welcome the golden phoenix;
the azure pool vainly reflects the jade hare. (Fohuiquan)
A lifetime is like a dream or drifting clouds; with no worldly provisions, one cuts off ties with kinsmen.
Leaving behind only a pair of clear and blind eyes, one laughs at the countless people coming and going. (Yayufu Chuan)
[Added for inclusion: *The Diamond Sūtra* states: "The past mind cannot be apprehended; the present mind cannot be apprehended; the future mind cannot be apprehended.

Regarding this, Nantang Xingju recounted that when Deshan was traveling on pilgrimage, he arrived at a sesame-cake shop in Tanzhou seeking some refreshment to eat. The shopkeeper came out and asked him, "Do you have a past, present, or future mind?"
"It can be attained. The Elder pointed to that mind. Deshan was speechless. Tonight, I shall provide several turns of phrase on behalf of Deshan for you all to deliberate.
When he says, "The three minds cannot be attained," simply reply: [The fourth mind is also unattainable].
"Stop, stop! Old woman, you must not be so discourteous. Is it too rigid for you to act like this?
Or rather, tell me: from where have you obtained this news? Is it too weak to act like this?
At that time, had it been I, when he said, "The past mind cannot be apprehended," I would have [acted differently].
The present mind cannot be apprehended; the future mind cannot be apprehended. Elder, which mind do you point to?
He simply said, "Give me one that is warm," and as soon as [the monk] hesitated, he plucked out his eyes.
Then he uttered this verse:
The mind of the past, present, and future—search for it where dust is stirred and soil is scattered; nowhere can it be found. Whether sitting, lying, or walking, there is nothing that is not it.
Accept this directly beneath you; do not hesitate.
The past mind cannot be apprehended; the fishing line is gathered and the rod set aside as the autumn river turns azure. On a small boat at an ancient shore, one sleeps at ease;
beneath the bright moon, the reeds and flowers are deep and secure. The present mind cannot be apprehended; the householder’s law of the Dharma family persists through both past and present.
Counselors and fierce generals settle the borders; what need is there to speak of the pearl of Sui or the jade of Zhao?
The future mind cannot be grasped; within that which cannot be grasped, one simply attains it. The stone contains the jade, and the earth supports the mountain;
only through realization can its unfathomable depth be known. Whose fame shall flow through the ages for all to share? When the pure wind pervades the earth, how can it have limits? (Xuedou Zong)
Seeking the mind throughout the three periods of time, the mind is not to be found; the two eyes remain facing the two eyes. There is no need to leave the sword behind to mark the boat for a search;
the snow, moon, wind, and flowers are always present before one’s face. (Yemou Chuan).
When the subsequent thought arises, the preceding thought ceases. How could these thoughts of arising and ceasing ever be distinct? Summon the wooden puppet on its mechanism and ask it;
though you manipulate it from head to toe, it fundamentally has nothing to say. (Lan’an Shu)
The Taoist of the Three Clarities lacks the bones of immortality; the Śramaṇa of the Eight Teachings defiles the Sanskrit scriptures.
A dark-lacquered Kunlun dances to the flower drum; Vasubandhu and Asaṅga sigh in silent lament. (Oran Tiyi)
Last spring, when the east wind blew, the swallows were many; they arrived before the ritual of the She-sacrifice and returned to their old nests.
This year, the spring colors have already reached half their course; the curtains hang desolate, and not one has passed through. (Bao Ye Yuan)

[Added for inclusion] *The Diamond Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*: "If one sees me by means of form, or seeks me by means of sound, such a person follows a deviant path and cannot see the Tathāgata. The verse says:
Seeking the physical body through sound is not forbidden; within the shadows of a hundred flowers, one embroiders mandarin ducks.
Since one has recognized the golden needle, let the wind blow as it will—the fragrance fills one’s sleeves. (Tudu Ce)
Exhausting the faculty of hearing along with the range of sight, one knows not where to behold the Tathāgata. A few notes of a solitary bird cry out from the cold trees;
a single fleck of idle cloud spreads across the precipice. (Yuan’an Xuan)
[Added for inclusion: *The Diamond Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*: "All conditioned phenomena are like a dream, an illusion, a bubble, and a shadow;
they are like dew and also like lightning. One should contemplate them in this way. Verse:
The illusory, empty body is itself the Dharma-body; herein there is neither defilement nor dust.
If one understands how to lift the spoon and grasp the chopsticks, there is no need to ask another to sweep the floor or burn incense. (Cishou Shen)
Grasping at the moon in the water; seeking one’s head in a mirror; marking the boat to find the lost sword; riding an ox while searching for the ox.
Empty flowers, mirages, dreams, illusions, and floating bubbles—strike them all through with a single brushstroke. If you wish to rest, then rest.
With the songs of Ba, the wine of Du, and the music of the village fields—even where there is no elegance, there is elegance. (Yayufu River).

In performing tasks, let the mind dwell upon them; value and strive for refinement. Without refinement, one will ultimately fail to attain spiritual penetration. When a game of chess reaches its most desperate juncture, a move made then is truly marvelous;
when plum blossoms encounter the height of winter, their fragrance becomes all the more pure. (Clouds at Leisure)
The passing of summer and the arrival of winter are entirely unknown; existence and non-existence, names and forms, are all at once left behind.
It is just like writing Lu Tong’s poem on the lunar eclipse in a state of intoxication upon a black-lacquered screen. (Xueyan Qin)

[Supplement] From the *Buddhāvataṃsaka-sūtra*: The World-Honored One [related that] because the Bodhisattva Universal Eye (Samantacakṣus) wished to see Samantabhadra but could not find him, he entered into meditative concentration three times in succession. He surveyed the trichiliocosm in its entirety, yet though he sought Samantabhadra, he could not see him.
Returning, he informed the Buddha. The Buddha said: "You need only arise from within this tranquil samādhi."
"In a single thought-moment, one sees Samantabhadra. As soon as Puyan gave rise to this single thought, he saw Samantabhadra riding a six-tusked white elephant, dwelling in mid-air. Cuiyan Zhi said:
"How do you all understand this? Cuiyan says that Puyan toppled the World-Honored One, and the World-Honored One toppled Puyan."
"You say, where is Samantabhadra? The verse says: A solitary wild goose drifts through the cold void;
Step by step, one pursues the empty sky seeking the goose's tracks. Treading through them, the straw sandals are worn out and the heels are broken;
Majestically, one sits alone atop the Great Hero Peak. (Xiatang Yuan)
“How many tongues does Gautama have? How many eyes does this assembly possess?
In every head and every object, in every land and every speck of dust—if you deceive yourself alone, that may still be tolerable; what is most bitter is deceiving others. (Beijian Jian)
[Added from the Supplementary Collection] *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*. The World-Honored One addressed the Bodhisattva Universal Eye:
"Is there anyone who can explain the various illusory appearances that abide within the words of illusory arts? He replied, "No. The Buddha said, "Universal Eye," [proceeding as follows].
Even the illusory appearances within an illusion cannot be apprehended;
how much less so the realm of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva’s secret body, the realm of his secret speech, and the realm of his secret mind—yet one can enter into them and perceive them. The verse says:
Brilliantly it dwells within the mind; clearly it resides amidst the dust of forms. Do not mistake this world of silver for a city of false silver. (Beijian Jian)
[Added for inclusion] *The Avataṃsaka Sūtra*: "A bodhisattva takes the bodhicitta as their home and takes practice in accordance with reality as their family dharma. The verse says:
Wandering aimlessly atop the tower, he has no one to rely on; Ling Ding and Li Di are truly pitiable. The Akṣa-vana is where he enters;
The Son of the Buddha’s dwelling is accomplished nowhere else. (Beijian Jian)
[Added from the Supplement] A Verse from the Avataṃsaka Sūtra: Suppose there were a great scripture, its size equal to the three thousandfold world system, contained within a single mote of dust;
and so it is with every mote of dust. A person of keen wisdom, with pure eyes, is able to see it all.
He breaks open the mote and brings forth the scripture, extensively benefiting all sentient beings. The Verse says:
If one intends to shatter a single mote of dust, yet remains unclear regarding this sutra, how can one shatter the sutra scrolls to produce this single mote of dust? (Beijian Jian)
[Added from the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*: "I now see universally that all sentient beings possess the wisdom, virtues, and marks of the Tathāgata;
yet, because of their deluded thoughts and attachments, they do not realize them. The verse says:
Heaven covers and earth bears; formed into spheres and masses, it pervades the Dharma-realm without limit, yet when analyzed down to the subtlest atom, it has no interior.
Reaching the ultimate depth of the profound mystery, who can distinguish front from back? The Buddhas and Patriarchs come to repay their karmic debts of speech;
go ask the old teacher Nanquan. Every person eats only a single stalk of vegetables. (Tiantong Jue)
[Added for inclusion: *The Contemplation of the Dharma-realm from the Avataṃsaka Sūtra*. The Dharmakāya flowing through the five paths of rebirth is called "sentient beings.
Therefore, when sentient beings manifest, the Dharmakāya does not manifest. The verse says:
The Buddha’s true Dharma-body has lived in vain until death. He sells his own village wine, holding his own ceramic flask, yet puts on his robe to act as the host. (Beijian Jian)
[Added from the Supplementary Collection] *Laṅkāvatāra Sūtra*: The Five Dharmas, the Three Self-natures, and the Two Kinds of Non-self.
The Verse says: How could a broken jar ever again perform the function of a jar? A scorched seed does not cause the sprout of bamboo to grow.
Like that ethereal space and the son of Pāṇḍu, The falling hair-tufts and the flowers of cataracts bloom. (Gushan Gui)
The iron ox of Shanfu has white leprosy; the great statue of Jiazhou is deaf. Both suffer from the same ailment. Pshaw!
What an unpleasant lacquer bucket! (Jingshan Guangzao).
[Added for inclusion: The Heart Sutra of Prajñāpāramitā is a great divine mantra; it is a great illuminating mantra; it is the unsurpassed mantra;
it is the mantra equal to the unequaled. It is able to eliminate all suffering. The verse says:
Dàn'àn Ferry, Dàn'àn Ferry! Ten times the boat comes, nine times it capsizes.
Only Chén Shàngshě of the Three Mountains walks along the bank carrying a single umbrella. What can he do about me? (Wǔzhǔn Fàn).
This is the Great Divine Mantra; the four elements and six sense-faculties have been fundamentally non-existent from the beginning. This is the Great Illuminating Mantra;

throughout the three periods of time and the ten directions, there is no leakage. This is the Unsurpassed Mantra; the perfect radiance of the Ocean Seal has long since been manifest. This is the Peerless Mantra;

scholars, farmers, artisans, and merchants each achieve fulfillment. Why is this so? Last year’s plum blossoms and this year’s willows—their colors and fragrances remain as they were. Thus it is equal.
In leisure, he scrutinized and realized the awakening of peach blossoms. What need is there to select the Dharmakāya?
It is hidden within the Northern Dipper. (Oran’s Verse).
*Chanzong songgu lianzhu tongji*, Volume Five; *Chanzong songgu lianzhu tongji*, Volume Six.
Compiled by the Śramaṇa Faying of Ba’en Guangxiao Chan Monastery in Chizhou, Song Dynasty;
continued compilation by the Śramaṇa Puhui of Tianyi Wanshou Chan Monastery during the Shaoxing era of the Yuan Dynasty:
*The机缘 (Kaiyuan) of the Patriarchs*.
Regarding the Patriarchs of the Western Heaven:
the First Patriarch of the Western Heaven, the Venerable Mahākāśyapa, saw the World-Honored One at the assembly on Vulture Peak holding up a single flower.
With his blue-lotus eyes, he displayed it universally to the great assembly; among the millions of sages and worthies, only [Mahākāśyapa]...
Kāśyapa broke his countenance with a slight smile. The World-Honored One then said:
"I possess the Treasury of the True Dharma Eye, the wondrous mind of Nirvāṇa, the subtle and wondrous Dharma-gate of liberation that is both with and without form. I entrust this to you.
You shall protect, uphold, and circulate it, ensuring that it never comes to an end. The Verse says:
The immortal maiden brings it forth; it is a spring apart from others. She returns it once more, entrusting it to the immortal man.
How pitiable that the tattered robe but gave a slight smile; though there was reason, the bystander could not extend it. (Foyin Yuan)
The frost wind scrapes the earth, sweeping away the withered roots. Who perceives that the Master of the East has already returned his command?
Only the ridge plum tree leaks the secret first; a single branch blooms alone amidst the snow. (Fohuiquan)
Everyone says that picking up the flower and the subtle smile are it; they do not know how to use this to discern the true lineage.
If one claims that mind and eyes are realized simultaneously, one cannot avoid remaining dimly aware within a dream. (Baizhang Yuanwen)
Holding up a flower, our Buddha was at Mount Gṛdhrakūṭa; the ascetic Kāśyapa suddenly broke into a smile.
This secret word from his golden mouth was entrusted directly, not only to those in heaven and on earth. (Baoning Yong)
The "Separate Transmission" is proclaimed as the total presentation outside the teachings; Kāśyapa closed his eyes and smiled without a word.
How pitiable are the multitudes on the hundred-thousand Vulture Peak mountains, who fail to realize the single profound stroke right before them. (Zhaojue Zong)
Red lotuses bloom upon the dry land of Vulture Peak; the white-browed old man laughs without ceasing.
A thunderous, majestic resonance shakes the east and west, yet eighty thousand deluded followers have not yet glimpsed it. (Huangbo Sheng)
The World-Honored One held up a flower; Kāśyapa gave a slight smile. The calamity reaches descendants; the patriarch above did not understand.
(Yang Wuweī) Who says that Kaundinya awakened at the holding up of the flower? His slight smile remains as before, separated by the ocean’s edge.
The Yellow-Faced One sought only to transmit the Great Matter; the Red-Browed One ultimately did not strike the poor family. (Zu Yinming)
The True Eye has been transmitted from the beginning to Kāśyapa; on Vulture Peak, the seven assemblies all submitted.
With spreading branches and flourishing leaves, the ancestral gate thrives; naturally obtained heirs fill the Great Tang. (Cangtang Qing).
The World-Honored One held up a flower; Kāśyapa gave a slight smile. Not falling into the registers of *gong* or *shang*, what tune is this? The wind is clear in the ancient cave;
the moon is bright upon the cold pond. (Changling Zhuo)
The World-Honored One and Kāśyapa did not recognize one another; each set a trap for the tiger.
As for the true mark of the wondrous mind of the right eye, to whom was it entrusted on the assembly at Vulture Peak? (Zhang Wujin)
Holding up a flower to show the assembly, who understood its intent? Only Kāśyapa the Dhūta broke into a smile. Limitless white clouds could not conceal it;
it followed the flowing waters and descended into the human world. (Nan-hua Ying)
Hearing the lute, he performs a dance; seeing the flower, his face breaks into a smile. One color, two contests; in heaven and on earth alike—(Min, the Ancient Buddha).
A hundred thousand devas and humans are invited to look: among all the dhūtas, only this one opens his face in a smile. How laughable! His robes are worn through, revealing his gaunt bones;
with one shoulder bared, he reaches out a hand to don the golden robe—(Fodeng Xun).
When Kāśyapa laughed silently that day, family disgrace has never been disclosed to outsiders. Without plucking the strings of the *shao* lute, he composed a single melody;
its pure resonance continues to transcend the realms of humans and devas. (Xuefeng Yu)
The flower was plucked after the subtle smile; the spirit manifested before the plucking.
A single piece of the silver moon, without day or night, its full radiance is perfectly round for all to behold. (By Fuxincai)
The matter of the single transmission outside the teachings is most extraordinary. When the hand of Drolama held up the flower, none among the assembly could grasp it;
to whom was this boundless fragrance entrusted? (Zhengjue Yi)
When the hands of Tūlasiṃha lift the flower, how many perceive the subtle fragrance wafting on the breeze?
Aside from Mahākāśyapa at Chicken Foot Mountain, who else possesses pupils within their eyes? (Cishou Shen)
A million humans and devas gaze upward, hoping for its proclamation; the slight smile at the plucking of the flower was far too eccentric.
How many of those with deluded consciousness wander in a blur? When questioned, their weary lives boil like scalding water. (Longmen Yuan)
The seawater overturns the void, rolling in its depths; fish, dragons, shrimp, and crabs drift and sink according to their fate.
How pitiable is the golden-headed *dhūta* practitioner, who even unto this day has not ceased to laugh. (Gushan Gui)
Holding up a single flower, he was immediately enlightened; the orthodox eye was transmitted without concealment.
Flowing through past and present without interruption, every branch and leaf is fragrant. (Shushan Ru).

Holding up a single branch of flowers, his elegant style carries on the ancestral house. If one says he transmitted the Dharma of the mind, the affairs of the world are as numerous as hemp seeds. (Jingshan Gao)
Who can understand the function of Vulture Peak? Kāśyapa stole his countenance and smiled with bared brows.
As soon as he moved, the primordial secret was leaked; his descendants have upheld this supreme mystery. (Chuanfang)
[Continued Collection]: Gautama held up a flowering branch; Kāśyapa slightly opened his smiling face.
If you wish to know that the Creator is impartial, listen further to the single trill of the yellow oriole. (Shi Ming)
The Flower was plucked and personally entrusted to the Elder Dhūta; on level ground, a wave suddenly rose a fathom high.
Those of later generations who drive their stakes and row their oars measure the water with bamboo poles, falling into further confusion and dispute. (Bao Hua Jian)
Ancient tombs reveal withered bones; tracing the source, I encounter a broken bridge. After one fresh rain has passed, verdant hues fill the treetops. (By Baiyang Shun)
A three-hundred-jin iron cangue upon the neck; though the principle is clear, it cannot be vindicated.
Sitting silently before Mount Jizu, he still uses the golden robe to deceive later generations. (Master Wuzhuo Zong)
In the end, he pointlessly leaked it once more; the old man with scorched teeth chews raw iron.
The jade whip shatters the bright moon-jewel, bringing disgrace upon his descendants for their own clumsiness. (Zantang Shen)
The World-Honored One held up a flower; Kāśyapa smiled. Two orbs in the heavens shine upon one another.
If you can sever [the bonds] of Old Gautama, the Yellow River shall close its eyes with but a single leap. (Huītong Dan)

Snow weighs upon the strange pines, revealing them; the wind is high, and the wild ferry lies across. Thinking that sentient beings suffer enough, one finds there are even more suffering sentient beings. (Wan-nian Xian)
The Golden-Colored Dhūta suddenly broke into a smile; even this is but a glimpse through a tube.
Had he turned his head back at that moment, he would have avoided seeing his descendants fall into the Black Mountain. (Ying’an Hua)
The World-Honored One held up a flower; Kāśyapa gave a slight smile. A pair of iron awls—utterly without any holes or openings. (Fozhao Guang).

When the Buddha raised the branch of flowers, it was clearly like luring a thief to ruin a house; thus, down to this day, thousands of generations later, his descendants pursue evil and follow the heterodox. (Mongan Cong).
The World-Honored One never held up a flower; Kāśyapa never smiled. The great earth is entirely their descendants—who understands this one upper orifice? (Kentang Chong).
Under the bright sun and blue sky, opening one's eyes to urinate—this Yellow-Faced Gautama has made a complete blunder.
(Muan Yong) Lifting up the flower, his tail was already exposed; Kāśyapa broke into a smile, while gods and men were at a loss. (Wumen Kai)
Kāśyapa, prompted by Ānanda’s question—“Beyond the transmission of the golden robe, what else does the World-Honored One transmit?”—called out to Ānanda.
Ānanda responded, “Yes? Kāśyapa said, “Take down the banner-pole in front of the gate.
The verse says:
Behind the shadowed gate, the banner-staff is overturned; the message within this is difficult to transmit. Linglong the attendant was able to entrust it to him:
the bright pearl rolls upon the platter, and the platter rolls beneath the bright pearl. (Tiantong Jue)
Apart from the gold-embroidered robe, what other transmission is there? Knock over the old banner-pole at the gate. Do not take a single moment as the supreme omen;
let it be for people to behold after hundreds or thousands of years. (Cao Tang Qing)
Apart from the golden robe, what else is transmitted? Though the call and response are diligent, the meaning is not yet complete. Kāśyapa was further able to employ skillful means;
he toppled the banner-pole, valuing only serene stillness. (Juehaiyuan)
The blossoms and leaves shall surely share their fragrance in due time; Kāśyapa answered the summons, and his sublime scent was revealed. Now, do not inquire after the affairs of that day;
the traveler on the road has his own mouth as a monument. (By Zhengjue Yi)
Beyond the golden brocade robe, what else is transmitted? When the younger brother responds to the elder’s call, how could there be partiality?
If one were to overturn the banner-pole before the gate, it would prevent it from leaning against the wall as before. (Baizhang Yuan).
Where the Elephant King walks, the tracks of foxes vanish; his noble offspring continue this tradition. Do not speak of what will happen two thousand years hence;
even through kalpas as numerous as dust motes and grains of sand, how could it ever end? (Baoning Yong)
Beyond the transmission of the golden brocade robe, there is further obscurity; leaking the celestial mechanism, the bannerpole is overturned.
From the Eastern Land of Awakening to the Western Land of India, it cannot be propped up; until now, its calamity has reached our descendants. (Zhaojue Zong).
Holding up the golden robe, he knocks over the banner pole; at every step, he treads upon green waters and blue mountains.
(Min Gufo) At the gate of Nanda, the banner pole is knocked down; beyond the transmission of the golden robe, what else is there to transmit?
A natural outsider, certified without a teacher—what can be done? Before the Buddha of Awesome Sound. (Zhang Wujin)
Beyond the transmission of the golden brocade robe, what further transmission is there? A whip is struck down hard upon the clay ox with its horns turned back.
With one roar, the demons' hearts shatter; turning over, he tramples through the mist of the blue abyss. (Nan-hua Bing)

"A difficult elder brother, a difficult younger brother—ask about their origin. The hundred-seamed robe and golden patchwork have been transmitted through successive generations. When the younger responds to the elder’s call, what business is accomplished?
Thus one need not mistake the top of the *śālā* pole for pointing toward heaven. (Fodeng Xun)
Only when mind meets mind can they truly know one another. The golden-colored dhūta-dhara distinguishes right from wrong. The five-li signboard is viewed from outside the city walls;
when the person concerned refuses to acknowledge it, whom else can one blame? (The Dharma-hall is like this.)
On the lapis lazuli palace, he bestows the golden robe; the fragrant blossoms of the *dì* and *è* flowers join in splendor, achieving what two find difficult.
Let the banner-pole outside the gate fall prostrate, sparing us the need to inquire whether the wind moves or the banner flutters. (By Shangfang Yi)
Brothers correspond like the *jiji* birds; their calling and summoning is no ordinary matter. Beyond the golden robe, what is transmitted?
He goes before the gate of the Way and topples the bannerpole. (Mañjuśrī speaks.)
Dhūta Kāśyapa and the learned Ānanda join their palms and raise their fists; brother and brother, difficult to match, suddenly encounter one another on a narrow path.
Their eyes bulge with fury as there is nowhere to flee; they topple the flagpole right before the gate.
A man of spirit naturally possesses the ambition to pierce the heavens. (Cishou Shen)
Clad in grass and eating wood, the Way-man is lofty; having transmitted the meaning of the golden robe, his spirit is bold. Beyond this, he already knows there is no other dharma;
where the bannerpole falls, it brings trouble upon the children. (Shushan Ru).
[Continued Collection] What further transmission is there beyond the *Jinlan Chuan*? It reports that the crossbar at the gate has been toppled.
How laughable, those people out for spring excursions, drunk to the point of oblivion! The peach and plum trees fill the valley, yet they remain silent of their own accord. (Shi Jianming)
For two thousand years since the Tathāgata, the secret entrustment has been passed down through direct succession, yet it has become nothing more than a hollow rumor.
Even until now, it remains a mere public proclamation; the banner pole still leans against the gate as before. (Great Abundant Grace).
As rare as phoenix feathers and unicorn horns; how could the younger brother not know when the elder calls?
How laughable it is that after the spring rain at Lingyuan, falling flowers and flowing water find their own natural harmony. (Kaisan Ying)
After the robe was bestowed before the Many-Sons Stūpa, what further object was transmitted to be shown to people? When the pearl of the black dragon burst forth, the stupa-pole fell;
its piercing cold light reached all four neighboring realms. (Fóxìng Tài)
Casually indulging in talk of the golden robe, he immediately knocks down the flagpole right before one's face.
From this point on, the natural order turns meaningless; the cold light still chills people to the bone. (Xiatang Yuan)
The younger brother calls out to his elder brother, yet cannot paint him; who would be willing to enter within?
Since the house was broken and the people perished, until now matters have only grown more complex. (Yuelin Guan)
The younger brother calls out to the elder brother; there is propriety and righteousness. A tiger bites a great beast; a snake swallows a turtle’s nose.
He has toppled the banner-pole in front of the gate. Oṃ sulu sulu siri siri. (Tu’an Qi).
Emerald feathers; the horned head of a qilin. The younger brother responds to the elder’s call, shaking the seas and mountains.
When the road is far and the night long, cease holding the torch. Cast down the banner-pole before your gate. (Gao Yuan Quan)
The gateways of every household open onto Chang’an; not a hair’s breadth is seen, yet the field of vision is vast.
No Dharma, no person—whom can one entrust? Elder brother and younger brother deceive one another. (Xue’an Jin)

Overturning the banner-pole before the gate, he fully raises [the Dharma]—how could it involve the realm of the profound? Turning his body, he does not sit within the palace of the Sovereign of Emptiness;
the moon illuminates a thousand peaks as the night air grows cold. (Zu’ān Jiàn)
They gaze at one another; eye meets eye. There is no basis for the "separate transmission outside the scriptures.
Knock over the banner pole in front of the gate! The phoenix does not dwell upon the wutong tree. (Wunian Fan)
His favored younger brother was always by his side. When asked what he had transmitted, he replied, "My own brothers have no great matters;
they simply say that the crossbar at the gate has been overturned. (Xianji Yun).
Boiling beans while burning their own stalks; the beans weep within the cauldron. Originally grown from the same root, why is the boiling so hasty? (Yunna Qing)
[Added from the Supplementary Collection] The Ninth Patriarch, Vajramitra, asked the Eighth Patriarch, Buddhanandi:
"If parents are not my kin, who is the most intimate? If the Buddhas are not my Way, who is the ultimate Way?
The Eighth Patriarch replied with a verse: "That which you speak of is intimate with the mind; parents cannot be compared to it. That which you practice is the Way..."
"Unification. The mind of all Buddhas is precisely this. To seek outwardly for a Buddha with form is not like you.
If you wish to recognize your own original mind, it is neither through unification nor through separation. The verse says:
Idle away half a century of springtime; how pitiful, to loathe wealth yet not loathe poverty. If the Buddhas and Patriarchs do not follow the Way, what Way could one seek?
If father and mother are not kin, who else is more kin? Why labor to place the feet upon lotuses at the seven steps?
One must believe that even the silent mirror gathers dust. Since time immemorial, the Zen gate has been a firm lock and key; it is this man who leaks the family style. (Fohuiquan).
The place of seeing is solitary and perilous; the position taken is high. It is as urgent as a spark from flint, as sharp as a blade.
Arriving at the house, one asks for the way: "Where is the house? He overturns the chessboard and casts off his robe. (Xiatang Yuan)
For half his life his feet did not touch the ground; Xuan knew he had trodden all the way to the ends of the earth.
He obtained the "seal of the winter melon," which has left him staring with open eyes and agape mouth to this day. (Songyuan Yue)
Parents are clearly not one's true kin; the Patriarch pours out his very heart and liver to others.
If you can directly and personally realize this, the *udumbara* flower shall bloom as spring within the fire. (Gao-yuan Quan)
If parents are not one's kin, who then is kin? Two eyes shining brightly, framed by a pair of brows.
Unrecognized atop the Han-yuan Hall, it is precisely at this moment on Mount Min and Mount E that we meet. (Shixi Yue)

[Added for collection: The Tenth Patriarch, Venerable Pārśva, was originally named Nansheng (Difficult to Be Born). He remained in the womb for sixty years. A divine pearl appeared as a response in his mother’s dream;
on the day of his birth, the entire room was filled with radiance. Having left the household life and attained the Way, he reached a forest where Pūrṇayaśas stood before him with palms joined.
The Patriarch asked, "From where have you come? Yaśas replied, "My mind has no [origin]."
[The monk] went. The Patriarch asked, "Where do you dwell? He replied, "My mind does not abide anywhere.
The Patriarch said, "Are you not settled? He replied, "All Buddhas are likewise. The Patriarch said, "You are not the Buddhas. He replied, "The Buddhas are also not [the Buddhas].
The Patriarch, knowing him to be a vessel for the Dharma, immediately conferred upon him the tonsure and gave him the transmission, speaking this verse: "The true body is naturally true; because..."
The true teaching is indeed rational; having realized the truly real Dharma, there is neither practice nor cessation. The verse says:
Beating the drum and playing the lute, we meet as two members of the same family. A clear breeze brushes the bright moon; the earth’s edge meets the horizon of the sky.
Shattered jade congeals like morning dew; the setting sun bids farewell to the evening glow. On Cold Mountain I met Shide;
clapping my hands, we laughed "sa-sa. (Nantang Xing, No. 2)
Even the Buddhas are not [the cause]; when the impoverished son’s belly is full, having just once eaten his fill, he forgets a hundred days of hunger.
Twenty blows of the staff and ten strokes of the mallet are enough to spare him from disgracing his two eyebrows.
Lightning rolls and stars fly; pearls turn and jade revolves. Breaking through the mask of the face, the sincere heart is revealed piece by piece. (Xiatang Yuan). [Added from another source:
When the Fourteenth Patriarch, the Great Being Nāgārjuna, saw the Fifteenth Patriarch, Gaṇapati, approaching, he first ordered his attendant to place a bowl of water before him.
Upon seeing this, Gaṇapati took a needle and cast it into the water.
The Patriarch was greatly pleased by this. The verse says:
In Nāgārjuna’s bowl of water, Deva’s needle upon the wool— Everyone vies over gain and loss; every person speaks of the distant and the near.

If one does not see the wild geese in the clouds, how can one know the depth of the desert sands? A farmer moved a fragment of a foundation pillar, and beneath the pillar he found gold. (Jue of Langya)
The leaks have ceased; Changle and Weyang are tranquil. The moon pours its light upon Ganquan and Taiye in autumn.
At midnight, the sound of music returns to the imperial carriage, summoning back the sorrows of the thirty-six palaces. (Xinwenben)
The twenty-fourth patriarch, Venerable Siṃha, was once approached by the King of Kaśmīra, who held a sword before him and asked, "Have you attained the emptiness of the aggregates?
The patriarch replied, "I have already attained the emptiness of the aggregates. The king asked, "Have you transcended birth and death? The patriarch replied, "..."
[The King said,] "Since you have already transcended birth and death, you may give me your head. The Patriarch replied, "This body is not mine;
why begrudge my head? The King then brandished his blade and severed the Venerable’s head, from which white milk gushed forth several feet high.
The King’s right arm then instantly fell to the ground as well. Xuan Sha remarked, "How great was this Lion Honored One!"
This person does not even understand how to be a master. The verse says: The Venerable One’s principle is not erroneous;
Xuansha’s words are most extraordinary. The head falls following the blade’s edge; both parties are lost by no more than a hair’s breadth.
(Yongming Shou) At the head of the Yangzi River, the willows are in spring bloom; The floating catkins bring grief to the traveler at the ferry crossing.
A single sound of the *qiang* flute at dusk by the parting pavilion— You head toward Xiangxiang, while I head toward Qin. (Longmen Yuan)
The artisan’s tools are naturally distinct; he did not hesitate to let his arm fall off to eliminate the malevolent spirits. Ten thousand miles away, songs of joy celebrate the peace of the empire;
night after night, the pure radiance of the snow and moon shines forth. (Daimai Zhi)
Receiving an ox from one person and returning a horse to another; with coming and going, the rites may be known.
(Fóxìng Tài). The Boatman descended to Yangzhou; floating duckweed follows the current. A single cry of the "Hé-mǎn-zǐ" melody moves grief and sorrow for all eternity.

(Gushan Gui): To kill a person, one must be a man who kills. With a single stroke, he becomes two pieces. Though head and arms may be severed by the edge of the sword, how can this compare to the *chùlìzuàn* of the Qin era? (Jingshan Gao): To kill a person, one must be a man who kills. With a single stroke, he becomes two pieces.

Though head and arms may be severed by the edge of the sword, how can this compare to the *chùlìzuàn* of the Qin era? (Note: *Chùlìzuàn* refers to a specific type of heavy-duty drill or boring tool used in ancient times.)
The King’s precious sword is never wielded in vain; it is most marvelous that the Venerable One has encountered it.
From this, a pure breeze shall pervade the entire world; how many will know the news of this Great Peace? (Huikan Ti)
The hair-cutting sword at its hilt turns heaven and earth to black; the arm falls, mountains and rivers eclipse the sun’s light. Tossing up Mount Sumeru, he plants it upside down;
only then does one know that even pairs do not constitute a duality. (Zantang Shen)
When did the Venerable One ever realize the emptiness of the aggregates? In Kaśmīra, he personally cut down the spring breeze.
After the rain, peach blossoms fell in profusion, dyeing the flowing waters of a mountain stream crimson. (Eh! Anjian.)
Muttering "papaya" cures foot ailments; a paper-drawn Zhong Kui drives away demons.
If one could only understand how to strike the *he-luo* gong throughout one's life, one would drink wine every day and be drunk every day. (Lan’an Shu)
The Buddha-dharma and the King’s law are not two different things; to simply bring down a single stroke of the blade is not yet the ultimate truth.
(Guan of Yue-lin) The lion’s head falls; the arm of Kapiśa is broken. Each person has their own Xi Shi in the depths of their vision;
whose jar lacks the bright moon? (Xian of Pu-weng)
Encountering those who dwell among the mountains, one speaks of mountain matters: selling pine-forest breezes in the sixth month; in the human world, they would likely be beyond price.
(The solitary peak is deep.)
Face-to-face, seizing the moment like a flash of lightning. Who can employ this face-to-face seizing of the moment? With a single stroke, the body is divided to settle life and death;
the King’s fame remains weighty through ten thousand ages. (Muan Yong)
Under the sword, ten parts of reality; difficult to conceal, the solitary body is revealed. The river flows, yet the stone does not turn;
alone there is the name "Accumulated Emptiness. (Beijian Jian)
In a dream, I sought to cross a deep mountain stream; though my skills were manifold, I could not advance. Suddenly awakening, all my skills were exhausted;
by the head of the bed, the mountain moon was already at the third watch. (Shi’an Shao)

The aggregates are empty—who sees the King of Dharmas? When beholding the essence, how could the sword’s light ever be obstructed? In the ancient temple, ivy and creepers pierce through the doors and windows;
by wind and rain, the broken stele shatters its inscribed texts. (Xue’an Jin)
As night deepens, the golden basin sinks toward the horizon; upon my knees, the *jiao-tong* zither plays a melody ever more fresh.
As the mournful wind of Yi Water brushes lightly over my fingers, *luan-jiao* glue cannot mend a person whose bowels are broken with grief. (Xutang Yu)
The twenty-seventh patriarch, Prajñātāra, was invited for a meal by the King of East India. During the meal, the king asked, "Everyone here recites the sutras;
why alone do you not recite? The Master replied, "When this poor monk exhales, he does not involve himself in worldly conditions;
when he inhales, he does not dwell within the aggregates or realms. He constantly recites such a sutra hundreds of thousands of millions of times."
"Billion scrolls—not merely one or two scrolls. Fenyang Zhao said, "This merely exhausts the venerable one’s mental and physical energy.
Daowei Zhi said, "Do you all see the twenty-seventh patriarch reading the sutras?"
When walking, the heels do not touch the ground; when sitting, the mind-consciousness seems to drift like the wind.
He then composed this verse: The autumn sky is high, the moonlight joins the clouds in white; The serene Chan mind’s flavor is long-lasting. The meaning of past and present is clear and distinct;
Why need one engage in further deliberation?
The numinous rhinoceros horn plays with the moon, its brilliance containing radiance; the wooden horse roams the spring, its swiftness unrestrained.

Beneath the brows are a pair of cold, azure eyes—how could they ever penetrate the ox-hide when reading the sutras? With a clear and understanding mind, one transcends vast kalpas; with heroic strength, one breaks through the heavy siege.
The wondrous, perfect pivot turns the spiritual mechanism; Hanshan forgets the path he came by. Shide accompanies him, hand in hand, as they return home. (Tiantong Jue)
The incoming breath has never dwelt within the aggregates or realms; the outgoing breath has never involved itself with the myriad conditions.
With a single sound of a fisherman’s flute departing from Nanpu, he sleeps as before deep within the reeds. (Lan’an Xu)
Regarding the Patriarchs of the Eastern Land: the First Patriarch of the Eastern Land, the Great Master Bodhidharma, was the twenty-eighth patriarch in the Western Land.
When he first arrived in Jinling and met Emperor Wu of the Liang dynasty, the Emperor asked: "What is the primary meaning of the Noble Truths?"
The Master said, "Vast emptiness—there is no sage. [The Emperor asked,] "Who is it that faces me? The Master said, "I do not know. The Emperor did not attain realization.
The Master then broke off a reed and crossed the river to Wei. Later, the Emperor raised this matter with Master Zhi, who said, "Your Majesty, do you recognize this man?
[The Emperor] said, "I do not recognize him. Zhi said, "This is the Great Being Avalokiteśvara, transmitting the Buddha's [teaching]."
Xin-yin said, "You should send an envoy with an imperial decree to summon him. Zhi said, "Do not speak of an imperial decree from Your Majesty;
even if the people of the entire nation go, he will still not return. The verse says:

The Noble Truths are vast and open; when could they ever be defined? "Who is it facing me? he replied, "I do not know. Because of this, he crossed the river in darkness; how could he avoid the thorns that grew?
The people of the state pursued him, but he would not return; for a thousand ages and ten thousand generations, we can only remember him in vain.
"Cease your recollections! When the pure wind pervades the earth, how could there be any limit? The Master looked around and said to those present, "Is there any patriarch here?
Call him over and let him wash the old monk’s feet. (Xuedou Xian)
A guest came from beyond the mundane world; I did not recognize this one person. There is no mind to be attained that can be transmitted. For nine years he sat empty-faced against a wall.
