When Chan Master Guishan Daoyin (who succeeded Helin Su) of Jing Mountain in Hangzhou received a letter sent by Mazu, the letter contained a circle.
Upon opening the seal and seeing it, the Master drew a line through the center of the circle and sealed it back and returned it.
When National Teacher Huizhong heard of this, he said, "Master Yin was still caught."
Mazu’s Delusion. The verse says:
When Mazu saw Jingshan at that time, he subtly revealed a secret mechanism in his style.
Unwittingly, however, the old man of Nanyang leveled a pitfall on level ground as if it were a trivial matter. (Foyin Yuan)
Words spoken under delusion have their origins; spirits commune across a thousand li as easily as a mustard seed or a needle is cast.
Who knows that clouds can be made to convey messages? If I were not so, even stones would nod their heads. (Zhaojue Zong)
From the south, from the north, from the west, and from the east—though the streams and mountains differ, the clouds and moon remain the same.
For what reason does this old man of Nanyang cause people to be so restless and hurried? (Dizang’s Grace).
Master Ma’s [time was] mid-winter, a time of severe cold; Master Qin’s [time was] early summer, when it gradually grows hot.
Although the cold and heat differ, each did not miss their proper season. (Jingshan Gao)
[Added from the Supplement] National Teacher Yi arrived at the imperial court by order of Emperor Daizong of the Tang dynasty, who personally paid him respect.
One day, while the Master was in the inner palace, he rose as the Emperor approached. The Emperor asked, "Master, why do you rise?
The Master replied, "How can you, O Patron (Dānapati), perceive this poor monk within the four modes of deportment? The Verse says:
The ground of Dharma is serene and unmoving; it is likewise appropriate to stand with the body poised.
Do not seek a teacher for the Son of Heaven of the Great Tang apart from rising, sitting, and walking. (Shixi Yue)
Standing outside the majestic deportment, the entire body is within. Layer upon layer of dragon-sleeves are bestowed, yet they cannot conceal the shame on the face. (Xiyan Hui)

A sovereign of ten thousand chariots and a teacher of the realm; In daily life, he never departs from the four dignified postures. Mountains stretch long and waters flow far, yet we recall him in vain;
Yellow leaves blow in the wind, but the man has not yet returned. (Xianji Yun)
Chan Master Daolin of Niaoke in Hangzhou (a successor of Guoyi) initially went to Ximing Monastery in Chang’an to study the Avataṃsaka Sūtra.
When Emperor Daizong of the Tang dynasty summoned Chan Master Guoyi to the imperial court, he visited him there and received the Dharma.
He returned to Qinwang Mountain on West Lake. There was a tall pine tree with lush, spreading branches that curved together like a canopy;
he consequently took up residence upon it, and thus the place derived its name. He had an attendant named Huìtōng, who was formerly a palace official of Emperor Dēzōng of the Táng dynasty.
Having resigned his post to follow the Master and shave his head, he applied himself with diligence for several years without yet receiving the seal of transmission. One—
Daokai took his leave. The Master asked, "Where are you going? Daokai replied, "I am going to various regions to study the Buddha-dharma.
The Master said, "As for the Buddha-dharma, I too have a little bit. Daokai asked, "What is the Master’s Buddha-dharma?
The Master picked up some cloth-hair, blew upon it once, and Daokai attained great enlightenment at that moment; he did not return again.
He traveled about and subsequently resided at [Zhaozhou’s] side. Later, he opened the Dharma and became his primary successor; he was sometimes called the "Attendant with the Cloth. A verse says:
The attendant, with a beginner's mind, sought superior conditions; Farewell to his master, he intended to go practice Chan. Niaoke knew this to be his spiritual capacity.
Matured. A hair-whisk brandished—immediately the mind finds peace (Fenyang Zhao).
Niaoke picked up some cloth-hair and blew upon it; a single streak of cold light faces the setting sun.
Though this is the sincere heart of an old woman, awakening comes when one returns from halfway home (Shimen Yi).
Without wind, ripples rise all around; the azure topknot and silken patterns are viewed with the True Eye.
Just as the Yellow River meets its triple freeze, one beholds the dragon coiled within the Nārāyaṇa cave. (Yunju You)
When Niaoke blew on a cloth-hair, the red sun was at its highest in midday. Because King Zhao delighted in swords, the people of the entire state wore blades. (Zhenjing Wen)
Looking back with a frown, two or three fall away; how can one bear to pick up the cloth-hair again?
To take it up directly and then simply stop—those whose eyes lack the essential fiber are loathed by the whole world. (Like a withered tree.)
The decrepit old man who has forgotten all artifice is Niaoke; atop the West Lake, he controls the misty vines. When the cloth-hair was blown up, there was not much to it;
even with iron eyes and copper pupils, one can do nothing about it. (Baofeng Qian)
Niaokuo picked up a tuft of cloth and blew upon it; at Vulture Peak and Jetavana, doubts were instantly extinguished.
One must believe in the immense power of the Creator’s artistry: from a withered raft, branches grow toward the east. (Zhang Wujin)
The Master once blew upon a wisp of cloth; this case is clear, the foremost of all kōans.
If you wish to know the essential meaning herein, look at the white clouds flying as he points afar from the mountain peak. (Added by Zhengjue)
Directly beneath, no self-interest—this is Niaoke. A wisp of cloth blown up, all delusion is severed. Suddenly the eye atop the head opens;
mountains, rivers, Buddhas, and demons are pierced through. (Master Min, the Ancient Buddha).
It is difficult for even a speck of gold-dust to enter the eye; once awakened, the person of today is the person of antiquity. To gather up the entire earth is like grasping a grain of millet;
upon the tip of a single hair, the whole body is manifested. (Fujian Qin)
If you seek the Buddha-dharma, go to the South; there the Great Master of the Old Lineage will raise it aloft. Mountain flowers fill the ground in profusion;
with every breeze that comes, a fresh fragrance arises. (Longmen Yuan)
A single puff of cloth-hair: immediately one knows where to return. Cold light pervades the earth; the needle and chisel are revealed alone.
(Chuanfang) [Continued Collection] The white phoenix controls the misty clouds at Niaoke; the pearl of the black dragon shines upon the ancestral mountains and rivers.
The meaning of grasping the cloth-hair at the start: its essence and function exceed even a fraction of Vairocana. (Kefu Daozhe)
Roving cavalry gallop about in the morning breeze; the General issues his orders east of the city wall.
He takes up a golden arrowhead with a touch of subtle skill, piercing the single red dot at the heart of the flower. (Poisoned Arrow).
With two fingers, he opens his palm and grasps it; upon a single hair-tip, he blows it open. This time, he does not stand by one’s side;
do not speak of the pure breeze pervading the nine realms. (Xinwen Ben)
The place of function is naturally distinct; it does not fall back into discursive thought. Mountains, rivers, and the great earth—these fully reveal the sovereign power of the Dharma King.
(Moon Forest Contemplation)
Niaokuo picks up a tuft of cloth and blows upon it; ten-thousand-fathom solitary peaks face the setting sun. Before he has even raised his hand, one must already have a flash of realization;
had you known this earlier, you would not have been called a man of substance. (Xiuyan Rui)
The Buddha-dharma of Niaoke is not much; it lies simply in a single tuft of cloth-hair from his tattered robe.
Blown away by a single breath, where has it gone? To this day, the world is full of clamor and dispute. (Lan’an Xu)
An eighty-year-old elder must practice with vigor; blowing on a wisp of cloth, calamity is born anew. A thousand miles of blood flows from the slaughter of men;
upon the branch of a withered tree sits an old monk. (Beishan Long)
The Buddha-dharma has its fewness; within words, one sinks into a net. Where a tuft of cloth is blown up, it remains as before, not departing from its nest. (Wunian Fan)
[Added from another source] When Minister Bai Juyi asked Master Niaoke, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma?
the Master replied, "Commit no evil; practice all that is good. Bai said, "Even a three-year-old child understands how to say this.
The Master said, "Though a three-year-old child can say it, an eighty-year-old man cannot practice it."
The verse says:
Evil has no outward appearance, and goodness has no form; both are nurtured and grown within the field of one's own mind.
Without moving a blade, they are lightly pruned away; thus awakening and afflictions are equal to space. (Amitāyus)
[Added from the Supplementary Collection] Chan Master Daoming of Mount Meng in Yuanzhou (a successor of the Fifth Patriarch) once pursued Layman Lu as far as Dayu Ridge.
When the Layman saw the Master arrive, he immediately cast his robe and bowl onto a rock and said, "This robe serves as a token of faith."
"Can it be taken by force? You may take it as you wish. The Master then tried to lift it, but it remained as immovable as a mountain.
Hesitating and trembling with fear, he said, "I have come to seek the Dharma; it is not for the sake of this robe. I pray that the Practitioner will grant me instruction.
[The Practitioner] replied, "When you are neither thinking of good nor thinking of evil—at that very moment—what is that which is the Original Face of Master Ming?"
[Mañjuśrī] showed his face. The Master attained great enlightenment on the spot; sweat flowed from his entire body.
Weeping, he prostrated himself and asked, "Beyond these secret words and secret meanings you have transmitted thus far, is there any further underlying intent?
Mañjuśrī replied, "What I am telling you now is not secret. If you turn back and reflect upon your own face, the secret lies right within you. The Master said:
"Although I have been among the assembly at Huangmei, I truly had not yet realized my own original face.
Now that I have received your instruction on the point of entry, it is like a person drinking water who knows for themselves whether it is cold or warm.
The current practitioner is indeed my teacher. The Master said, "If you are thus, then I and you share the same teacher at Huangmei. Guard yourself well."
Hold fast. The verse says:
At this very moment, throughout kalpas one has never been deluded. Step by step one advances through the Three Strategies; returning home, doubt is forever severed.

(Longmen Yuan): Majestic and sublime, his wondrous features transcend all measure. Good and evil are both forgotten; there is nothing to be seen. Ten thousand miles of clouds have cleared, and the celestial realm is pure;
the ocean heart is waveless, and the lunar orb stands solitary. (Foxing Tai):
He treats Buddhas and Patriarchs with contempt, his spirit like that of a king. He directly pursues Huineng to the foot of the ridge.
Failing to obtain the robe or bowl, he encounters foul water—clearly, this is adding frost to snow. (Xiaoweng Kan).
Do not think of good, do not think of evil. The Great Compassion of the Thousand Hands is difficult to grasp.
When all that is difficult to grasp is overturned, only then will you know Puhua shaking his bell. (By Six Rocks Hui).
It cannot be traced nor can it be painted; it cannot be extolled, for it is beyond praise and suffering. The original face has nowhere to hide;
when the world perishes, it remains indestructible. (No gate opens.)
Deep in the night, he transmitted the robe to Old Lu. What a pity to kill that old, ancient wit of Huangmei! He told him, "When chasing someone, do not chase them too closely.
Indeed, he fell from his high standing once and for all. (Xuexi Jie)
The Monk Pòzào Duò of Mount Sōng (he was a successor of National Teacher Ān of Mount Sōng) once encountered a shrine on the slopes of Mount Sōng that was extremely efficacious.
In its hall there was only a single hearth, and people from near and far never ceased making offerings to it;
many living beings were slaughtered for cooking. The Master struck the hearth three times with his staff and said: "Tsk! This hearth is nothing but clay and tiles."
"Synthesized! From where does the sage come? From where does the spirit arise? To thus slaughter living beings!
He struck three more blows, and the hearth collapsed and fell apart. In an instant, a person in green robes and a towering cap appeared and bowed in salutation, saying:

"I was originally the hearth-god of this temple. Having long endured the retribution of my karma, I have now received the Master’s teaching on the Dharma of Non-arising and attained liberation from this place to be reborn in heaven. I have come specifically to express my gratitude. The Master said, "This is your own inherent nature;
it is not something I have forcefully asserted. The deity bowed twice and vanished. Later, a monk asked the Master, "I have attended at your side for a long time."
"Without having received any skillful means, what principle did the stove god realize that he was immediately reborn in heaven?
The Master said, "I simply told him that he was composed of clay and tiles; there was no other doctrine for his sake. The monk stood there reflecting.
The Master asked, "Do you understand? The monk said, "I do not. The Master said, "Why do you not understand your own inherently existing nature?
The monk bowed. The Master said, "Falling! Falling! Broken! Broken! Later, another monk recounted this to National Teacher An.
The National Teacher sighed and said, "This man has realized that all things and the self are one and the same. A verse says:
The divine hearth in the ancient temple; the essential teachings of the Chan Master. Struck by the staff, the karmic body leaps up.
(Yang Woei-wei) The hearth breaks and the earth falls; it is not a matter of calculation. Calling for tea, summoning for rice, measuring water, and boiling medicine. (Huang-po Sheng)
Fortune and misfortune, majesty and severity do not reside in the spirit. With broken cups and cold roast meat, whom does one laugh at?
Since he departed, news has been heard; even now, the village elder beats the sacrificial drum. (Longmen Yuan, No. 2)
The spring chill is piercing and biting; it freezes the young man to death. Be most careful not to let your paths diverge like those of the stars Shen and Shang; there is nothing else marvelous.
Serve with bowed head and inquire after his well-being with joy. To deliberate upon the Buddha-dharma [in this manner] would be to endanger your very life.

Relying on the hearth for spiritual power, it is not itself spiritual. Where the traces of the spirit are severed, there is but a heap of dust. The village elder does not come to beat the sacrificial drum;
striking the true cause while departing from the heterodox is a different kind of spring. (Fodeng Xun)
[Continued Collection] Is it a sage or not a sage? Is it a spirit or not a spirit? A pile of bricks and tiles formed by the accumulation of earth;
when struck with the tip of the staff, there is no news. For many years this monster has failed to become a perfected being. Now, reflecting carefully upon it:
for the sake of trivial matters, he has long harbored ignorance. (Daimpō Chi)
The nine-headed venomous *zhèn* bird soars in the heavens; the world-protector Nanda possesses eight long arms. The water flowing from beside the bamboo is cool;
the breeze coming from within the flowers is fragrant. (Nanyan Sheng)
[Added for inclusion] Pòzào Duò (Broken Oven Fall) was asked by a monk: "What is one who practices great cultivation? The Master said:
"Shouldering the pillory and wearing the shackles. "What is one who performs great work? The Master said: "Practicing dhyāna and entering samādhi. The Verse says: [Verse omitted]
Chained and shackled, one invites the charge of crime; Entering meditative absorption, one falls into a deep pit. Kicking both ends free, there is no longer any dependence;
A single idle man wanders between heaven and earth. (Bieshan Zhi)
[Added to the Collection] Chan Master Zhihuang of Hebei (a successor of the Sixth Patriarch). When he first visited the Fifth Patriarch, he followed the gradual approach.
Later, he built a hermitage and sat in meditation for over twenty years, never showing a trace of indolence.

Upon meeting the Sixth Patriarch’s disciple, Master Ce, who inspired him to earnestly seek the essentials of the Dharma, he went to visit the Sixth Patriarch. The Patriarch took pity on his long journey from afar.
He then proceeded to provide an opening and resolution. Under these words, the Master attained sudden and thorough enlightenment;
the mind he had cultivated for the preceding twenty years left behind no trace or influence whatsoever. The verse says:
Zen is neither entering nor exiting, neither walking nor sitting; sitting, standing, and walking meditation are all Zen.
If you merely guard the mountain-dwelling ghost’s cave, you will remain far removed from the West Heaven. (Benjue I)
In years past, I looked down upon this mountain fold with disdain, wishing to build a vermilion pavilion to store silks and brocades. Today I return once more, yet there is nothing to do;
I simply ride my lean horse down the sloping ridge.
[Supplement] National Teacher Huizhong of Guangzhai Monastery in the Western Capital (a successor of the Sixth Patriarch).

He resided at Dangzi Valley on Mount Baima in Nanyang for forty years without descending the mountain. Emperor Suzong of the Tang dynasty summoned him to the capital and treated him with the etiquette due to a teacher.
The Emperor asked the Master, "What Dharma have you attained? [Some say: "What Dharma did the Master receive at Caoxi? The Master replied, "Does Your Majesty see emptiness?"
"Is it a single cloud in mid-air? He replied, "I see. The Master said, "Nail it down; hang it up. The Verse says:
Where there is no opening for speech, one opens the mouth; When there is intent to return, one returns immediately. Zhaozhou does not abide within clarity;
This is not yet the time when the ewe hangs from the horn. (Cishou Shen)
[Added for inclusion] National Teacher Zhong was once asked by Emperor Suzong, "What is the Tamer of the Ten Bodies?
The Master stood up and said, "Do you understand? The Emperor replied, "I do not understand. The Master said, "Bring me the pure water pitcher for this old monk.
The verse says:
The *xián* bird dwells in an empty pond; fish pass beneath its feet. The *xián* bird knows nothing at all, even if it did know.
The emerald depths of the pool are ten thousand fathoms deep; it would simply dive straight down to catch the fish and return. (Baofeng Chun)
Bearing snow and holding frost, leaning half against the fence; within slanting shadows, her immortal form is revealed.
Spring has arrived in the village ahead last night, yet the old monk in the bamboo hut still knows nothing of it. (Xinwen Ben)
The National Teacher was asked again by Emperor Suzong, "What is the Samādhi of Non-contention? (Today this is erroneously rendered as "What is the Ten-Body Tamer?
The Master replied, "Donor, you are treading upon the crown of Vairocana. The Emperor asked, "What is the meaning of this?
The Master said, "Do not mistake it for your own pure Dharma-body. He questioned the Master again, but the Master did not look at him at all. The Emperor said:

“I am the Son of Heaven of the Great Tang,” [the Emperor] said. “Why do you not deign to look at me? The Master replied, “Do you see empty space? [The Emperor] said, “I see it. The Master asked, “Does it blink its eyes and look upon Your Majesty? Verse: The Emperor of the Great Tang Asks for a glance from the Master. The Master points to the void; He does not blink his eyes. If one can see this clearly, Then one sees the Buddha-nature. If one cannot see this clearly, How can one avoid being deluded? The Great Tang Emperor Is truly rare indeed! If one can understand this, One will surely attain the Way. If one cannot understand this, One will surely fall into error. This is the ultimate meaning; It is not something to be grasped by the intellect. If one can see it directly, One will transcend all doubt. The teacher of a single nation is but a strong designation; Nanyang alone was granted a truly excellent reputation.
The Great Tang supported the true Son of Heaven, who once trod upon the crown of Vairocana’s head. (Xuedou Xian, 2)
An iron hammer shatters the golden bones; what else remains between heaven and earth? The ocean of three thousand lands is serene and clear at night;
who knows who has entered the blue dragon’s cave?
The author’s pure regulations have no peer in the world; once he grasped the golden pincers atop the Dragon Pavilion.
How excellent it was that he pierced through the crown of Vairocana, until Mañjuśrī smiled and nodded his head. (Wu-shan Hsiu, No. 2)
The Jewel Moon contains the void as it aligns its many peaks; who can distinguish their heights and depths amidst the thin mist?
Mount Sumeru is shattered like the drum of Yanguan; thus Vairocana is brought low.
At every step, one treads upon the crown of Vairocana; yet this is not one's own pure body.
Wondrously entering the gate of emptiness, one attains the mark of emptiness—the liver and gall of the Patriarchs, the very spirit of the Buddha. (Fujian Qin)

[Added for inclusion: When Emperor Daizong ordered National Teacher [Huai] to test the Western Indian Tripitaka Master Daili, the Teacher asked, "Have you attained the supernormal power of knowing others' minds?
He replied, "I dare not say so. The Teacher said, "Tell me, where am I right now?
He replied, "The Master is the national teacher of this land; why have you gone to Sichuan to watch a boat race?"

Dewu crossed over. After a long silence, he asked again, "Tell me, where is the old monk right now? He replied, "The Master is the teacher of an entire nation; how can you be here on Tianjin Bridge watching monkeys perform? The Master said, "You have spoken well. Dewu then bowed. The Master struck him three times with his staff and drove him out. Later, when the Master was about to pass away, he called for Dewu. When Dewu arrived, the Master said, "I am leaving this world. Dewu asked, "Where will you go? The Master replied, "To the place where there is no coming or going. Dewu asked, "If there is neither coming nor going, where is that place? The Master said, "You have spoken well. Dewu then bowed. The Master passed away. Later, when the Master’s funeral rites were being prepared, Dewu entered the hall and addressed the assembly, saying, "The Master’s life span has ended; where has he gone? You should all know: the Master was not born in the east, nor did he die in the west. He simply went to the place where there is no coming or going. He then ascended the high seat and performed the funeral rites. When it came time to light the incense, he said, "The Master’s body is here; where is his spirit? He then lit the incense. When the incense was nearly finished, he said, "The Master’s spirit is here; where is his body? He then extinguished the incense. He then descended from the seat. The Master’s coffin was placed in the center of the hall. As the funeral procession was about to depart, Dewu suddenly struck the coffin three times with his staff and shouted, "Come out! At that moment, the coffin opened by itself. All present saw the Master emerge, mount the palanquin, and depart. It is said that the Master traveled far away and never returned. This is the story of Master Mazu Daoyi. It is truly a rare occurrence. How could it be otherwise? It is like the sun rising in the east and the moon setting in the west. It is like the great earth supporting all things. It is like the great ocean containing all rivers. It is like the great void encompassing all forms. It is like the great wind blowing through all space. It is like the great fire burning through all worlds. It is like the great water washing away all things. It is like the great thunder shaking all mountains. It is like the great lightning illuminating all darkness. It is like the great cloud covering all lands. It is like the great rain nourishing all seeds. It is like the great harvest ripening all fruits. It is like the great winter freezing all things. It is like the great spring bringing forth all life. It is like the great summer growing all things. It is like the great autumn gathering all things in. It is like the great day bringing forth all light. It is like the great night returning all to stillness. It is like the great birth beginning all existence. It is like the great death ending all existence. It is like the great awakening realizing all truth. It is like the great sleep forgetting all things. It is like the great dream seeing all illusions. It is like the great waking seeing all as real. It is like the great joy feeling all as bliss. It is like the great sorrow feeling all as pain. It is like the great peace feeling all as calm. It is like the great chaos feeling all as turmoil. It is like the great indecision resolving nothing. It is like the great courage facing all dangers. It is like the great cowardice fearing all dangers. It is like the great strength overcoming all obstacles. It is like the great weakness being overcome by all obstacles. It is like the great wisdom understanding all principles. It is like the great ignorance misunderstanding all principles. It is like the great clarity perceiving all phenomena. It is like the great darkness perceiving nothing. It is like the great brightness illuminating all things. It is like the great gloom obscuring all things. It is like the great depth reaching the bottom of all things. It is like the great proximity staying close by. It is like the great speed moving faster than thought. It is like the great slowness moving slower than thought. It is like the great power moving all things. It is like the great helplessness moved by all things. It is like the great freedom acting according to one's will. It is like the great constraint acting against one's will. It is like the great sovereignty ruling all beings. It is like the great servitude serving all beings. It is like the great nobility being honored by all. It is like the great meanness being despised by all. It is like the great purity being untainted by anything. It is like the great defilement being tainted by everything. It is like the great simplicity being easy to understand. It is like the great complexity being difficult to understand. After a long silence, he asked again, "Where do you say this old monk is right now? Zang was at a loss. The Master rebuked him, saying, "You wild fox spirit! Where is your supernormal power of knowing others' minds?

Zang had no reply. The verse says: The old man’s question was like a thunderclap; The wild fox spirit stood frozen, speechless. If one wishes to know the true path, One must first cut off the source of delusion.
The Tripitaka Master of Other-Mind is far too coarse; like a monkey watching someone row a boat, he fails to see the State Preceptor right before his face.
It is simply because he has been deceived by his eyes from the very beginning. (Yeyu Stream).
Responding to the myriad capacities of beings, the Sun must surely have its method; I do not yet know where to seek Nanyang.
Since losing the monkey, he has long since ceased performing on the bridge. (Lan’an Shu)
Concealing the blade and avoiding arrows, the paths are a thousand differences; for ten thousand ages, the veteran master has been ever-forgiving.
It is best that the heron finds no place to seek; at night, he sleeps with the moon amidst the reeds. (Tieshan Ren)

One day the National Teacher called to his attendant. The attendant responded. He called him thus three times, and each time the attendant responded. The Master said, "I thought it was I who was failing you; it turns out it was you who were failing me. The verse says: The National Teacher called the attendant; Three times he called, and three times he answered. "I thought it was I who failed you," "But it was you who failed me. The sound of the call is like thunder; The sound of the response is like lightning. If you can discern this within the moment, You will see that there is no separation between teacher and disciple. If you do not understand this, You will surely fall into the pit of doubt. In the end, both are lost together; How could they ever be saved? If you wish to know the truth of this matter, Look at the face of the National Teacher.
The meeting of teacher and disciple was no trivial matter; there was no reason for them to wander together through the weeds.
Whether you bear the blame or I bear it, let no one ask; let the world compete for supremacy as it pleases. (Xuedou Xian)
The National Teacher called to his attendant. He spoke twice, yet it was not right for him to eat. His ears were not deaf, yet he had nowhere to clear his name. (Touzi Qing)
The dragon’s roar and the tiger’s cry—who shares them? Clouds arise at the edge of heaven; wind blows beneath the cave.
From now on, the old man of the peaceful countryside, With his children and grandchildren holding hands, celebrates the bountiful harvest. (Foyin Yuan)
The National Teacher called his attendant three times; he was merely striking the grass to startle the snake.
Who would have known that beneath the green pines at the bottom of the ravine lies a thousand-year-old *fuling* fungus? (Huanglong Nan, 2)

The National Teacher’s words were never uttered in vain; the attendant responded three times, and all news was cut off. Having poured out his heart and soul to others throughout his life, he found that being known was not as good as being unknown.
The attendant was never once called back; the National Teacher raised wind and thunder on dry land.
Had one encountered him at that very moment, the nine-fold elixir would have been turned to ash. (Cuiyan Zhen)
An ancient awl from Nanyang in his dotage, casually casting his line upon the riverbank. The night is still and the water cold, yet the fish do not bite;
he returns with an empty boat under the bright moon. (Haiyin Xin)
The National Teacher called three times; the attendant responded three times. When a family is wealthy, the child is spoiled; when one is often ill, one understands the nature of medicine.
"I owe you," says the parrot from Longxi that can speak; "you owe me," says the blue-eyed barbarian from the West who has been laughed at to death.
If you wish to grasp the ultimate meaning of Nanyang, for the most part, as one grows old, one realizes the heart is solitary. (Fohuiquan).
When the National Teacher called his attendant three times, and the attendant responded three times, it was like blindly and chaotically thrusting needles and awls;
who knew that this was the proper ritual? (Baizhen Yuan).
The National Teacher called out three times; what does this clarify regarding antiquity and the present? Toiling in vain, one cannot help oneself.
Truly, this is because there is no prior affinity with others; it is not that others have no feeling toward me. (Zhaojue Zong)
Calling three times and responding three times, he then ceased; yet he said, "To have needlessly created an enemy is a betrayal.
To broadcast one's family's disgrace within the Great Tang—tell me, O Nanyang, are you not ashamed? (Foguo Bai).
The National Teacher called his attendant three times; the attendant responded three times. Two iron hammers without holes—those who look on must feel stifled with breath.
Neither side gains any advantage. Who, ancient or modern, can believe this? (Yuantong Xiu).
The National Teacher called his attendant three times; the attendant responded with "Yes" three times.
If one says, "You have lost me," then indeed one may be said to know the proper rites. (Zhikai Qing)

The National Teacher called his attendant three times; the attendant responded three times without fail. He knew only that his body was strong and his vigor robust, unaware that he had grown old and his heart was solitary. (Baofeng Xiang)
In Nanyang, he called the attendant three times and received three responses; it was like the state of Lu in a distant haze, or Yangzhou in a faint mist.
Turning my head, the cold river reflects the empty azure; the sunset goes westward, while the waters flow east. (By Yishang)
The State Preceptor is old and has many schemes; he cuts off the crane only to lengthen the duck.
Since neither side has sores, they are exceedingly at peace; why labor to wound such fine skin? (Zuyin Ming)
Majestically presiding over Nanyang, he transmits the ancestral command; his pure wind, chilling and majestic, stirs the entire realm. In his old age, he especially loves his late-born son;
holding his hand from time to time, he teaches him to follow the vermilion [of the Way]. (Fuxincai)
The call is clear and the response is intimate; who knows who it is that fails to repay this kindness?
The neighbor to the east leaks the affairs of the west, causing bystanders to laugh ever more freshly. (Changling Zhuo)
Three calls and three responses—the intent is already deep. Nanyang has exhausted every bit of his "old woman’s heart.
Let bystanders not say he reveals the family’s disgrace; in the end, true brass cannot be traded for gold. (Cishou Shen)
The State Preceptor and his attendant wander together at leisure; before the Hall of No Affairs, they exchange verses in response.
A hawk that pierces the heavens soars through the clouds, leaving only travelers to point toward its path. (Fujian Yongqin)

The precious sword flies on in rapid succession; piercing through the crown, it immediately penetrates the divine. When sometimes lightly pressed down, it startles the guests of the Five Lakes. (Gao’an Wu)
On the worldly path, amidst wind and waves, I have not seen you. Each time we meet, my spirit is wounded. Where do the flowing waters and falling flowers go?
Beyond the mountain cave, the peach blossoms are a spring all their own. (Gushan Gui)
A mute having a dream—to whom can it be told? Rising to face one another, eyes are dazed and blurred.
I have already laid bare my innermost heart before others; let him seek his own advantage as he may. (Jingshan Gao)
【Continued Collection】Three calls and three responsive acknowledgments; neither side fails the other. The path of Nanyang is trampled through;
its fragrance fills every road. (Wuzu Yan).
Three calls and three responses, further enriched by the resonance of names; the moon lingers at the cold window, the water returns to the vast ocean.
"I owe you, I owe you"—a total edge meeting a superior blade. (Xiatang Yuan)
To call this "ordinary" is something no one fails to understand; yet when the sword is drawn, all are utterly bewildered.
Clearly, this is a marvelous secret of the immortals, which from of old has never been permitted to be transmitted even between father and son. (Nutang Si)
"Nanyang’s three calls are like stirring up waves where there is no wind. The attendant’s response was like placing feet upon a snake.
Do you enlightened monks know or not? Ten thousand ages of pure breeze remain vast and empty. (Nun Wuzhuo Zong)
The third call requires you to know that my intent is no light matter; my lifelong liver and gall are poured out all at once. Do you know whether you have failed me or failed yourself?
Even with the finest brush and ink, it could not be painted. (Shuian I)
A single scene of such splendor cannot be captured in a painting. Deep within the inner chambers, my passion is fully unleashed. I call for Xiaoyu repeatedly, though there is no real business;
I simply wish for my husband to recognize the sound of her voice. (Lingyan An)
Fully upholding the true mandate, responding universally to high and low. Three responses and three calls—listen attentively, listen attentively!
(Moon Forest Contemplation). One day you held a cup of wine at your own home; for how many years have there been waves and dust?
Not knowing the path atop Black Rock Ridge, how many times can we seek one another as we grow old? (Wan Shi Kong).
A single arrow shoots two vultures; the two vultures fall with the stroke of the hand. Waves ripple at the city of Yueyang;
the moon fills the Tengwang Pavilion. (Xue’an Jin)
An iron collar without holes must be borne by man; it brings trouble upon descendants that is no small matter.
If you wish to prop the gate and support the household, you must further go barefoot up the mountain of blades. (No door opens).
Casting the divine cup once determines fortune or misfortune; casting again for a second divination brings even greater spiritual penetration.
One clearly perceives the events of this year, yet it is said that the affairs of next year will be different. (Wuzu Fan).

Three times he calls out, and every voice rings with the pain of his entrails. National Teacher, why did you deliberate so mistakenly? When one wishes to distinguish between enmity and gratitude, there is no place to do so;
the regions of Wu and Chu stretch vast and boundless, sharing but a single river. (Jiakuan Zhen)

At that time, vegetables were cheap; radish heads covered the ground. One could buy one for a single coin, and those who obtained them ate their fill with contented sighs. (Fujian Qin)
Seeking the truth, one awakens and enters the island of Penglai; The fragrant breeze never ceases as the pine blossoms age. Where has he gone gathering mushrooms, yet not returned?
White clouds fill the earth, with no one to sweep them away. (Jikuten-shin)
National Teacher Dayi once asked Danyuan, "If someone asks after a hundred years what the ultimate matter is, how will you respond? The Master said, "Fortunately, he is already pitiable enough;

why must he insist on having a talisman for protecting his body? The verse says: Fortunately, he is already pitiable enough; Why must he insist on having a talisman for protecting his body? If one wishes to know the ultimate matter, It is right here, before your very eyes.
Hushen Fuzi was most attuned to the numinous; wherever the National Teacher rose or sat, he would always accompany him. Danyuan attained its functional application and departed for the south;
his teaching caused the sleep-filled eyes of men to awaken. (Fenyang Zhao)
Not valuing one's own spiritual nature may still be tolerable; but as for the talisman for protecting the body, how can one endure it?
For your sake, I have communicated a message beyond the literal meaning: the autumn moon, windless, falls into the azure pool. (Haiyin Xin)
[Continued Collection] When the true Way flows and travels on foot, there is no need to carry an amulet for protection. The National Teacher truly acted out of concern for Danyuan;
it was not merely a conversation held at the parting of ways. (Xiangchuan Hong)

When the National Teacher was about to conclude his work of transformation, he took his leave of Emperor Daizong of the Tang dynasty. The Emperor said, "After the Master’s passing, what shall I, your disciple, have as a memorial?
The Teacher replied, "Tell the donor to construct a seamless stupa. The Emperor asked, "May I request the Master for the pattern of this stupa?
The Teacher remained silent for a long while and then asked, "Do you understand? The Emperor said, "I do not understand. The Teacher said, "Poor fellow!"
After [the Master] had departed, the attendant Yingzhen came to understand this matter. After the Master passed away, the Emperor summoned Yingzhen and asked about the meaning of this.
Yingzhen recited a verse: "South of Xiang, north of Tan, In the midst, gold fills the entire land.
Beneath the shadowless tree, the boat is joined; Upon the lapis lazuli palace, there is no knowing."
Shi Yingzhen later resided at Danyuan Mountain. A verse says: The seamless stupa is difficult to behold;
The clear pool does not permit the azure dragon to coil. Layer upon layer, the shadows fall;
Round and round, for ten thousand autumns and ten thousand springs, it is shown to all people. (Xuedou Xian)
From whose hands was the seamless stupa fashioned? Though there is a model, it cannot be transmitted. How can one insist on depicting it without tiers?
It shall forever hang above the crystal palace. (Baizhang Yuan).
The stupa stands without seams yet remains precarious; its jeweled bells dangle delicately from eight sides. The Great Compassionate One with a thousand hands cannot reach it;
beneath a hundredfold locks, he strikes with a golden mallet. (Arhat South)
In front is pearl and lapis lazuli; behind is agate and coral. To the left are Avalokiteśvara and Mahāsthāmaprāpta;
to the right are Samantabhadra and Mañjuśrī. In the center is a banner being blown by the wind, which says: "Hu-lu hu-lu" (Wuzu Yan).
[Continued Collection] Desiring to build the seamless stupa of Nanyang—how truly difficult it would be for Viśvakarman to take up his tools!
Since it is primordially manifest, what need is there to construct it? Behold with clear vision: it stands majestic everywhere. (Benjue 1)
Its eight facets are naturally resonant; its form, poised in the void, is steep and towering. Majestic and imposing from both within and without, how could it be divided by the six apertures?

Clinging to names while hiding the essence, mistaking appearances for reality, one fears the clarity of the green pool as if it were a coiled dragon, and fails to realize that the boatman’s bowl is already open to the heart.
How can daily life not be spontaneously perfected? (By Yuanwu Keqin)
The seamless stupa reveals no shadow; it is a vast, empty realm of true suchness (*tathatā*). The *śakara* eye flashes like lightning;
in its profound and mysterious stillness, its summit cannot be seen. (Fojian Yongqin)

The form and appearance of the stupa were known in advance before they were even raised; it stands loftily at the bottom of the sea, its reflection falling upon the treetops with radiant brilliance. (Qian’an Guang)
Who dares to know this seamless stupa? Even the National Teacher has fallen into a cheap expedient. One truly knows that the tracks of the lion have vanished;
why need one constantly inquire about right and wrong? To inquire about right and wrong—on every blade of grass, the rain and dew descend. (Dai Wuwe)
South of Xiang and north of Tan, shadows swirl in circles; from every eave and beam, wind and rain bring the chill.
Protruding from the void without a single crack, let it be viewed by people for a thousand ages—no gate opens.
The National Teacher’s pagoda-style is most sharp and new; brought forth face-to-face, it reveals no literary artifice.
Yet Danyuan added a single line, which has led to a chaotic proliferation of imitations down to the present day. (Gao Feng Miao)
[Added for inclusion] The National Teacher said: "In terms of the gradual, he returned to the ordinary and conformed to the Way; in terms of the sudden, he left no trace behind. The verse says:
Above, there is no scheme to pierce the heavens; below, there is no plot to enter the earth. At the city of Cai, thousands and tens of thousands were shattered.

It takes but a moment. (Xuedou Xian) Throughout the twenty-four hours of the day, one should return to the ordinary state; while walking, standing, sitting, or lying down, one should investigate with diligence. Though we meet, not everyone recognizes this;
when questioned, as before, they have not yet met it face-to-face. (Benjue Yi)
[Added for inclusion] When National Teacher Zhong was visited by Danxia, as soon as [Danxia] spread out his sitting mat, the Master said, "Not needed, not needed.
Danxia stepped back three paces; the Master said, "So it is, so it is. Danxia stepped forward three paces; the Master said, "It is not so, it is not so.
Danxia circumambulated the meditation seat once and departed. The Master said, "The time since the Sage has passed; people..."
There is much indolence. After thirty years, it will be difficult even to find a single monk worthy of being a teacher.
Daowei Zhe said: "Danxia may indeed be said to harbor a supreme treasure; when meeting one of wisdom, its brilliance increases.
The Great Gate of the National Teacher is wide open; those who ascend it must be the right person. Is there anyone now who can act as Danxia’s patron?

"Ma! Is there anyone among the assembly who has met with Dayang? After a long silence, he said: 'If you are not a guest from the Dragon Gate, take care not to suffer the branding of a black spot on your forehead. He then spoke in verse:"
"Not so, not so!"—a state not shared even by the thousand sages. "Just so, just so"—like a viper, a scorpion, a snake, or a venomous serpent.
"Not it, not it"—piercing to the very bone and marrow. Advancing and retreating, circling the meditation seat; the mechanism of a flashing bolt strikes two or three times. (Yinkong Sou).
[Added for inclusion: The National Teacher asked Attendant Zilin, "Where have you come from? He replied, "From south of the city.
The Master said, "What color is the grass south of the city? He replied, "It is yellow. The Master then asked a young boy, "What color is the grass south of the city?
The boy replied, "It is yellow. The Master said, "This very boy may also be granted the purple robe before the imperial curtain."
Discussing the profound mystery before the Emperor. The verse says:
"Accustomed to rowing the ferryboat, now I do not count the years. Only when the wind and waves are fierce does one truly pursue the coarse coin."
(Chang of Yuet-tang) I wish to empty my withered bowels to the very bottom. Stepping out the door, I find myself again offering this earnest advice. I urge you to turn back while there is still time;
Do not wait until the spring breeze makes the willow eyes turn green. (Yu of Hsü-tang)

[Added from the Supplementary Collection: Chan Master Xuangjue of True Enlightenment in Yongjia (who succeeded the Sixth Patriarch) had mastered the subtle and wondrous Dharma-gate of Tiantai *śamatha-vipaśyanā*.
During all four modes of deportment, he constantly remained in silent meditative contemplation. Later, encouraged by Zuoxi Lang, he traveled together with Dongyang Ce to Caoxi.
Upon his initial arrival, shaking his mendicant’s staff and carrying his water jar, he circumambulated the Patriarch three times. The Patriarch...
[The Master] said, "A śramaṇa is one who possesses three thousand codes of dignified conduct and eighty thousand subtle practices.
Great Virtue, from what direction have you come that you give rise to such great arrogance? The Teacher said, "The matter of birth and death is great;

impermanence is swift. The Patriarch said, "Why do you not realize non-arising? Once realized, how could there be any swiftness? The Teacher said, "Realization itself is non-arising. [He then ceased speaking.]
"Originally there was no 'fast,'" the Patriarch said. "It is so, it is so. At that time, the entire assembly was not without astonishment.
The Master then performed the full ritual of prostration and took his leave after a short while. The Patriarch asked, "Is your return too fast?
The Master replied, "Since it is originally non-moving, how could there be speed? The Patriarch asked, "Who knows it is non-moving? The Master replied, "You yourself, O Benevolent One."

He gave rise to a conceptual discrimination. The Patriarch said, "You have thoroughly grasped the meaning of non-arising. The Master said, "How can non-arising have a meaning? The Patriarch said, "If there is no meaning, who would engage in discrimination?

The Master said, "Discrimination, too, is not a meaning. The Patriarch sighed in praise, saying, "Excellent! Excellent! He stayed for one night; thus he was known as "One-Night Awakening" (Yi-xiu-jue). The Verse says: The Patriarch asked about the meaning of non-arising; The Master replied that there is no meaning at all. The Patriarch then asked who it is that discriminates; The Master said that discrimination itself is not a meaning. The Patriarch praised him, calling him "One-Night Awakening. This is truly the Way of the Buddhas and Patriarchs.
Realizing the perfect true mind as one's fundamental mind, there was no one to bear witness, so he brooded within himself.
Because his karmic conditions were ripe for intense inspiration, upon meeting Master Neng, he immediately attained the gold. (Fenyang Zhao)
From Yongjia he traveled ten thousand *li* to Caoxi; why did he not offer even three prostrations?
After circumambulating the meditation seat three times, he stood firm, raising his monk’s staff in a majestic manner. (Benjue I)
Turning over seas and mountains to seek a true friend, Shaking heaven and earth to behold Great Peace. The two elders do not know where they have gone;
Their ancestral style has spread its fame for a thousand ages. (Zhengfahao)
Shaking his mendicant’s staff at Caoxi, he gave rise to great arrogance; staying but one night, what a petty fellow!
In the city of Yongjia, he propagated the school’s style; the river moon and pine wind have no bounds.
(Wuchen Cai) Volume Eight, *The Linked Pearl Collection of Verses on Ancient Cases of the Chan School*, Volume Nine.
Compiled by the Śramaṇa Fasheng of Ba’en Guangxiao Chan Monastery in Chizhou, Song Dynasty;
continued compilation by the Śramaṇa Puhui of Tianyi Wanshou Chan Monastery during the Shaoxing era of the Yuan Dynasty:
*The机缘 (Kaiyuan) of the Patriarchs*.
The First Generation after the Sixth Patriarch:
Chan Master Nanyue Huairang (Successor of the Sixth Patriarch). Initially, he went to Caoxi to visit the Sixth Patriarch.
The Patriarch asked, "Where have you come from? The Master replied, "From Mount Baofeng. [The Patriarch] asked, "What kind of thing comes like this? The Master replied, "To speak..."
"If it is like a single entity, it is not correct. [The student] asked, "Can one still cultivate and realize it?

The Master said, "Cultivation and realization are not non-existent, but being defiled is not permitted. [The student] asked, "Is this very state of being undefiled that which all Buddhas protect and keep in mind?"
"Since you are thus, I am also thus. The verse says: Because the Master questioned me, I spoke of where I came from;
I reported that the meaning of Songshan does not turn back. Cultivation and realization are not non-existent, yet they are unstained;
Pushing through the clouds to see the sun, the mind immediately opens. (Fenyang Zhao)
The jade lies within the pond; the lotus emerges from the water. Though defiled, its fragrance cannot be severed—this is the comparison.
If you, Great Master, can thus take it up, then one night on Dongting, the autumn wind shall rise. (Foyin Yuan)
With horns upon his head, he comes in this manner; the Iron Ring Mountains and all their peaks are utterly rent asunder. He tramples the Jambudvīpa world, killing countless beings;
though one might pull at his nose with deep clouds, he cannot be turned back. (Baoning Yong)
Coming from the summit of Mount Song, coming thus—nothing therein is of any use; it is already but dust and grime.
Returning at once to Nan Yue to grind a piece of brick, he shines light upon the wind-chasing horse and brings it back. (Foguo Bai).
[Continued Collection] What thing comes in such a manner? Within this, what need is there to sweep away dust?
When one stares with wide eyes, it is still not seen; in vain one hangs a bright mirror upon a high dais. (Da Hong’en, 2)
To say it resembles a single object is not the point. "The wind follows the tiger; the clouds follow the dragon. This matter has never been a trivial affair.
Do not say that the absence of dharma is the true teaching.
What a magnificent way to come! When meeting the situation face-to-face, there is no detour. Walking, standing, sitting, or lying down—none of these are other things;
it is simply that people of this age do not open their eyes. (Benjue I)
The ancient road before the hall is filled with drifting white clouds; even those with azure eyes and golden heads have yet to comprehend it.
With a holeless flute and felt clappers, they softly blow away the chill of the imperial street. (Zhengtang’s Discernment)
To say it resembles a single object is immediately incorrect; only after eight years did he finally accord with the wood-seller. For the most part, its form is not much at all;
how could it ever be exhausted through use across kalpas? (Pak Ong-hyeon)
Setting out directly from Mount Song, he wanders freely through the vast expanse of heaven and earth. With not a single thing remaining, how could there be anything comparable?
A long sword leaning against the sky, its coldness overwhelms all who approach it. (The Boundless Lineage)
Master Let resided at Mount Nanyue. At that time, Mazu was staying at the Chuanfa Monastery and was constantly practicing seated meditation.
The Master, knowing him to be a vessel for the Dharma, went to him and asked, "Virtuous One, what do you hope to achieve by sitting in meditation? He replied, "I hope to become a Buddha."
One day, the Master took a brick and began rubbing it in front of the hermitage. [A monk] asked, "What are you doing by rubbing this? The Master said, "I am rubbing it to make a mirror.
[The monk] said, "How can rubbing a brick produce a mirror? The Master said, "How can sitting in meditation produce a Buddha?
[The monk] asked, "How then is it done? The Master said, "It is like a person driving a cart; if the cart does not move, one strikes the horse, not the cart."

It was exactly so. Striking the ox was precisely it. Thereupon, he realized the essential meaning beneath the words and was thus certified in mind and transmitted the Dharma, in accordance with the prophecy of the Western Patriarch that "a colt would trample the people of the world.
The Southern School was thereby established in Jiangxi. The verse says:
Polishing a brick to make a mirror, one yearns for those of like sound; when a question comes, show clearly the original mind. As soon as the wooden man is called, he turns his face and points;
the plow-ox plows forth the ancient gold. (Fenyang Shanzhao)
To grind a brick to make a mirror is not difficult; suddenly a light arises that illuminates the great thousandfold world.
How laughable are those who sit in meditation seeking the Buddha—until now they have been whipping the ox even further. (Foyin Yuan)
The "dead horse doctor" has come to a place of no use; the oxen and carriage are whipped even harder from behind. Do you know when the skin is worn through and the bones are exposed?
To bear a heavy burden, one must know that full strength of limb is required. (Baoning Yong)
Polishing a brick to make a mirror; following the precedent of beating the drum. All fish and dragons know that water is their life (Master Min, the Ancient Buddha).

Sitting in meditation to become a Buddha is a sickness of the mind; making a mirror by polishing a brick is like flowers before one's eyes. With a single pull, the golden lock of the firm barrier is severed;
with an ordinary step, one returns home at once. The colt is truly worthy of praise. Since the time of chaotic freedom, it has been donned.
This dwelling is one’s lifelong journey. (Fodeng Xun).
[Supplementary Collection] To strike the cart is to strike the ox; even the nostrils reaching to the heavens have been pierced. One has already laid bare one’s innermost heart before others;
how pitiable that throughout antiquity and today, people vainly apply the whip. (Lan’an Xu).
When the ox behind the cart feels pain in its neck, one adds the whip. One casts aside the gold and embraces the common brick.
Pursuing evil and following the heterodox until this very day—this is the mistaken transmission of the Buddha of the Immediate Mind. (Xiaoweng Kan).
Throughout my life, I have cast my heart and gall toward others. My transgressions fill the heavens and are no light matter.
Having brought Master Ma into disrepute through my reckless behavior, I have continued until now to mistake the markings on a scale for the weight they measure. (Songyuan Yue)
Sitting in meditation to achieve Buddhahood gives rise to false views; polishing a brick to make a mirror involves even more delusion. Beating the cart and beating the ox are both equally false;
it churns one’s heart and entrails, leaving no other recourse. (Hengchuan Hong)
All phenomena forgotten, a hundred thoughts reduced to ashes. In an ordinary moment, he suddenly pulls [the ox] back by the nose. A single point of mirror-light shines like the sun;
it directly causes the heart-mind of the wooden man to open. (Xueyan Qin)
[Added for inclusion] When a monk asked Master Ryōan, "When a mirror is used to cast an image, once the image has been formed, where does the brightness of the mirror go?
The Master said, "When you were a young boy, Great Virtue, where was your physical appearance?
The monk said, "But once the image is formed, why does it no longer reflect? The Master said, "Even though it does not reflect, it cannot deceive him."
Not a single point can be grasped. The verse says:
Within the skull, the eyes still see; From within the withered tree, the dragon’s roar is even more wild.
When the void is shattered and the realm of light is exhausted, Therein lies another matter for deliberation. (Cishou Shen)

The questions probe the profound, and the answers are even more mysterious; to strike a blow upon one's own person is the most elegant art. If you wish to know that single point where one cannot be deceived:
on the river, several peaks are so green they seem about to float. (Closing the room, opening it.)
[Added for collection] When Master Rang was residing at Jiangxi, where Mazu Daoshi was propagating the teachings, he asked the assembly, "Is Daoyi preaching the Dharma for the community?
The assembly replied, "He has already preached the Dharma for the community. Master Rang said, "I have not yet heard any news from anyone.
The assembly was speechless. Thereupon, he sent a monk away, saying, "Wait until the time he ascends the hall."
He simply asked, "How is it? and had the monk memorize whatever the other said. The monk went and followed the master's instructions exactly;

upon his return, he told the master, "Master Ma said, 'Since the time of chaos, for thirty years I have never lacked salt and sauce. The master approved of this. The verse says: Since the time of chaos, for thirty years, I have never lacked salt and sauce. If you can understand this, You will see the old master’s meaning.
If you cannot understand this, You will not avoid being deceived by the words. If you wish to know the source of the matter, Look at the salt and sauce on the table.
For thirty years in total confusion, I have never lacked salt or sauce. Master Mazu of Jiangxi, Reverend Let of Nanyue (Gushan Gui).
When you see clearly, you recognize the intimate; yet bringing it forth still involves a long journey.
Even one who does not err by so much as a hair’s breadth is merely someone picking up crumbs and licking their fingers. (Jingshan Gaofeng)
The family is poor and the sons are brought low; when affairs are urgent, one cannot rely on others. Opening my mouth reveals the tethering ropes;
my disheveled state brings trouble upon my neighbors. (Or-an style).
Having managed to achieve some small measure of livelihood, he shows off his talents and skills before the public.
Even if he were to trample countless people to death, he is still just an old, cunning ghost from Xichuan. (Zhong’an Kong)
Since the time of chaotic confusion, there has been no further need for salt or sauce. When the mouth opens, one sees the gallbladder;
how could this depend on words? (Yuelin Guan)
Within the flash of a stone-light, one tests what is right and what is wrong; casually, one plucks the sand from one’s eyes.
Since then, there has never been a lack of salt and sauce; I dare guarantee that this fellow has not yet arrived home. (Mukan Egen)
In years past, I passed the high-level imperial examinations and read every one of the ten thousand scrolls of books in the human world. Today, my single body finds the heavens and earth too narrow;
when I reflect on these "good things," it is better that they had never been. (Xue’an Jin)
With a wife’s anxious heart, I am constantly worried; I fear you will fall into the pickle-vats of another's house.
Once the news has been received amidst confusion, the lineage of Jiangxi shall flow forth freely. (Xutang Yu)

Chan Master Xingxi of Qingyuan in Jizhou (a successor of the Sixth Patriarch) first visited the Sixth Patriarch and asked, "What should one attend to so as not to fall into stages? The Patriarch said, "What have you been doing? The Master replied, "I do not even practice the Noble Truths. The Patriarch said, "In what stage would you then fall? The Master replied, "Since I do not even practice the Noble Truths, how could I fall into any stage? The Patriarch said, "You are indeed a person of great capacity; you may stay here. The Master stayed for three years. One day, while walking with the Patriarch, he suddenly asked, "Who is it that does not follow the Buddha-dharma? The Patriarch said, "It is you who do not follow the Buddha-dharma. Upon hearing this, the Master was greatly enlightened. He then composed a verse: "I have no teacher; The Dharma is not transmitted. My mind is like empty space, Unborn and unceasing. The Buddha-dharma is originally thus; I simply accord with its nature. The Patriarch said, "You have attained my marrow. Later, the Master resided at Qingyuan. When the people of the region first heard of his reputation, they came to pay their respects. The Master said to them, "If you wish to see the Buddha, look at your own nature; if you wish to see the Dharma, observe your own mind. If you seek outside of your own mind, you will never find it. He further said, "The Way is originally complete within yourselves; it is not something to be sought from others. Do not seek it from Buddhas, do not seek it from patriarchs, and do not seek it from teachers. If you seek it from others, you will lose your own original face. He also said, "The Way is not far; it is right before your eyes. If you turn back to look at your own mind, you will immediately realize it. If you go seeking outside, you will wander for a thousand miles. He also said, "The Way is not difficult to understand; it is simply that people create complications for themselves. If you can let go of all things, there is nothing else to be done. He also said, "The Way is not a matter of words and phrases; it is a matter of directly pointing to the human mind and seeing one's nature to become a Buddha. He also said, "The Way is not something to be grasped; it is simply a matter of not being attached to anything. If you are attached to anything, you will be lost. He also said, "The Way is not something to be cultivated; it is simply a matter of not creating afflictions. If you create afflictions, you will be lost. He also said, "The Way is not something to be attained; it is simply a matter of not losing your original mind. If you lose your original mind, you will be lost. He also said, "The Way is not something to be practiced; it is simply a matter of not creating karma. If you create karma, you will be lost. He also said, "The Way is not something to be realized; it is simply a matter of not creating views. If you create views, you will be lost. He also said, "The Way is not something to be verified; it is simply a matter of not creating doubts. If you create doubts, you will be lost. He also said, "The Way is not something to be known; it is simply a matter of not creating consciousness. If you create consciousness, you will be lost. He also said, "The Way is not something to be understood; it is simply a matter of not creating thoughts. If you create thoughts, you will be lost. He also said, "The Way is not something to be attained; it is simply a matter of not creating attachments. If you create attachments, you will be lost. He also said, "The Way is not something to be sought; it is simply a matter of not creating desires. If you create desires, you will be lost. When Jiejiu was present, his grandfather deeply esteemed him. The verse says:
The crown of the head is invisible as clouds gather in haste; The numinous branch beyond the kalpas bears no spring.
If one does not sit upon the palace of the Empty King, How could one be willing to till the fields facing the solar wheel? (Touzi Qing)
Transcendent and solitary, it is difficult to gaze upon with the correct eye; far surpassing past and present, its kind is hard to equal. Moss seals the ancient hall where no one waits;
the moon locks the azure mountains, and the phoenix does not perch. (Danxia Chun)

Without steps or grades, what is there to seek by looking? Seizing the first tally of Caoqi, he then spoke of the price of rice in Luling, as hundreds of trades and thousands of markets vied to offer their recompense. (Foguo Bai).
[Continued Collection] Meeting beyond the kalpas, they walk on the other shore; amidst the clusters of numinous sprouts, the iron ox plows. The east wind scatters the snow from a thousand crags;
in the cloudless expanse of space, the solitary moon shines bright. (It becomes withered wood.)
A single scoop from the clear pool, polished like a mirror: if there is no wind, why should waves arise of their own accord? Though you turn your body, you do not leave the original boundary;
yet if you examine it closely, how much difference is there? (Xueyan Qin)
[Added for inclusion: After Qingyuan had received the Dharma, he went to Jingju Temple on Mount Qingyuan in Jizhou.

When the Sixth Patriarch was about to pass away, the novice Xiqian (who was later known as Master Shitou of Nanyue) asked him, "After the Master has passed away, I do not know whom I should rely upon.
The Patriarch replied, "Seek it out through reflection. When the Patriarch entered nirvana, Xiqian...
Whenever he sat upright in a quiet place, he was as still as if he had forgotten his very life. The First Seat asked him, "Your teacher has already passed away;
what is the purpose of sitting here in vain? Huicheng replied, "I am following my teacher’s final instructions, which is why I am reflecting in this manner.
The Seat said, "You have a senior brother, Master Xingsi, who currently resides in Jizhou. Your karmic connection lies there," according to the teacher’s words.
"Very straightforward! It is you who are deluded. Upon hearing these words, Xuan took his leave of the Patriarch’s shrine and went directly to a place of quiet seclusion.
He composed a verse, saying:
Seeking this place to depart, Cool and free from the heat of summer. Evening rain and morning clouds rejoice in peace; Green mountains and lush [valleys]...
It is difficult for those who dwell by the water to see it; it is not difficult to see that there is a white-browed beast in the deep forest.
It turns out, after all, to be Xuan Sha’s tiger. (Gao’an Wu)
[Added for collection] Qingyuan asked Shitou, "How long has it been since the Master left the mountain ridges?
The Master said, "I do not know; however, at what time did you leave Caoxi? [Shitou] said, "Xiqian did not come from Caoxi.
The Master said, "I also know where you have gone. [Shitou] said, "Master, as you are a great man, please do not speak so hastily. Verse:
It is said:
A wooden man comes to inquire about the road to the azure heavens; the stone maiden, advanced in years, seems not to hear.
Hand in hand they walk together back to their native land, as the evening mountains stand towering, locked in heavy clouds. (Danxia Chun)
[Added for inclusion] Qingyuan asked Shitou, "Where have you come from? He replied, "From Caoxi. The Master then raised his whisk and said, "Does Caoxi have this?
He replied, "Not only does Caoxi lack it; even in the Western Heaven, there is none.
The Master said, "Have you perhaps been to the Western Heaven? He replied, "If I had gone, then there would be one. The Master said, "Not yet."
He spoke further, saying, "The Master must also speak half of it; do not rely entirely on this student.
The Master said, "I do not decline to speak to you, but I fear that in the future there will be no one to uphold it. The verse says:
White clouds conceal the jade phoenix; the red sun shines without distance. Faintly, stars cluster together; in their impartiality, they preside over the nine heavens. (Touzi Qing)
We meet at the head of the Jin River; together we ascend the wine tower. When the moon has waned and our songs and laughter have ended, we turn our heads and board our light boats. (By Yan of Dun’an)
Qingyuan instructed Shitou to take a letter to National Teacher Huairang of Nanyue, saying, "Once you have delivered the letter, return quickly;

I have a 'pickaxe' for you to dwell in the mountains. When Shitou arrived there, he had not yet presented the letter, but immediately asked, "What is it like when one does not admire the various sages and does not prize one's own spiritual essence? Nanyue replied, "Your question is too high."
Sheng said, "Why not ask him to come down? Tou replied, "I would rather sink into the depths for eternal kalpas than envy the liberation of the various sages.
Yuezhou then desisted. When Tou returned to Jingju, the Master asked, "It has not been long since you left; did you successfully deliver the letter?
Tou said, "The message was not conveyed, nor was the letter delivered. The Master asked, "How so? Tou raised [his hand].
Having finished the previous conversation, [Nanyue] said, "When you first arrived, you asked for permission from the Master for an axe; please take it now.
The Master lowered one leg. [Nanyue] bowed his head and immediately took his leave to go to Mount Nanyue. The verse says:
The sages do not seek their own spiritual prestige nor place weight upon it. One question was too high; Heaven was startled and Earth shook.
He brushed his sleeves and returned. Even when a letter arrived, he refused to open it. From this time forth, atop the flat rock, he never again crossed the mountain. (Foyin Yuan).
From of old, the ancestors have served as sovereigns; generation after generation, son to grandson, they have flourished. None among the civil and military officials recognize them;
it must be that in the golden hall there is a venerable shrine. (Baoning Yong)
A thousand li apart, where news cannot pass; why such haste upon your return? White clouds lock away the rocks before the crag;
the horned antelope hanging from its horns leaves no trace. (Like withered wood.)
Holding the axe, he came and stayed upon the mountain; he hacked open the fine peaks and ridges of Nanyue.
His descendants lost their advantage—what use would they have for it? Furthermore, Hulü laughed at Lu Ban. (Foguo Bai).
[Continued Collection] It is still possible to steer a boat with the current, but to hold the rudder against the wind is rare in this world.
Though he may be a fine fellow with his shoulder-board, in the end he cannot avoid falling into a disadvantage. (Haiyin Xin)
The matters of the direct transmission across a thousand li are not the same; one must rely upon the adze to appreciate the superior merit.
As for Zhan Ru’s seizing of the jade and returning it to Zhao—can this be compared to the single letter that communicated at that time? (Touzi Shu)
A monk asked Qingyuan, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? The Master said, "What is the price of rice in Luling? The Verse says:
Leaving home to study the Way, his mind was not yet opened; He came to ask the Master about the Great Meaning. Instead, he was asked: "How much does a bushel of rice cost in Luling?"
Price. At that moment, the state of mind and the environment were simultaneously reduced to ashes (Fenyang Zhao).
A three-eyed tortoise; a single-horned auspicious qilin. Raising clouds to bring forth evening rain; the moon over the stream brightens the night curtain.
(Fachang Yu): The mountains and rivers of Great Song span four hundred prefectures; every object at their intersection has its own origin. The price of rice in Luling remains as it was;
for the monks of the world, the path of speech is well-woven. (Zhengjue Yi).
The price of rice in Luling changes year by year. What is heard from others is often false and not necessarily true. There is no need to ask at crossroads for the general meaning;
one should simply see the original person within the high and the low. (Huanglong Nan)
The price of rice in Luling is exceptionally fresh and fine; who would discuss it without mentioning it on their lips?
Boundless pure breezes arise beyond the threshold; do not measure intimacy by the measure of grain. (Baizhang Yuan).
Do you know the price of rice in Luling or not? When settling the account, let neither side suffer a loss.
You who enter the marketplace with faith yet return empty-handed—in the end, it is simply because you love a bargain. (The Third Patriarch).
In the era of Great Peace, the work of governance leaves no trace; the customs of the rural elders are most pure. They simply engage in village songs and communal feasts;
who would know of the virtue of Shun or the benevolence of Yao? (Tiantong Jue)
Abundance and scarcity vary according to the times; why should one teach the vulgar to vainly compete for merit? Who increases or decreases the price of rice in Luling?
One should see the Patriarch when it comes to value and worth. (Cangtang Qing)

The price of rice in Luling is broadcast throughout all quarters; though the high chant and light recompense may not yet be appropriate, there is no need to concern oneself with matters of pecks and bushels when face-to-face.
Let the north and south drift on in idle conjecture. (Changling Zhuo)
What is the price of rice in Luling? Entering the market, one knows that movement is free and easy.
If you ask what it is worth over the years, it is the four hundred prefectures of the Great Song’s mountains and rivers. (Fodeng Xun)
Old Qingyuan has no seams or cracks; when asked about the Buddha-dharma, he replies with the price of rice.
If a patch-robed monk should get even a single grain to touch his lips, he will carry his staff slung across his shoulder and wander the world. (Gao’an Wu)
In Luling, few understand the price of rice; from antiquity to the present, the Buddhadharma has been debated.
The embroidery of the mandarin ducks is left for others to view, yet for no reason one must seek the golden needle. (Gushan Gui)
Old Qingyuan has no seams or cracks; when asked about the Buddha-dharma, he answered with the price of rice. A hair’s breadth of difference becomes a contentious argument.
Having no face, he makes people afraid. (Jingshan Gaofeng Yuanmiao)
[Continued Collection] The price of rice in Luling drives on Zen followers. Five Old Peaks tower loftily into the great void.
How laughable that upon the registers of Mount Hua, another Pan Lang has been added—arriving on his donkey. (Haiyin Xin)
Since ancient times, Luling has been Jizhou; to this day, no one can afford its rice prices. The green waters and blue mountains remain as they were before;
with yellow leaves and the western wind, yet another autumn has come. (Fotuoxun)
What is the meaning of the Buddha-dharma of Qingyuan? To answer with the price of rice is far too clumsy.
Blinking one's eyebrows, one walks the Great Way; do not stir up wind and waves on level ground. (Zhaotang I).
The price of rice in Luling—I report it for you to know. Amidst the vast expanse of dust, those who recognize it are rare. Turning my head, I know not where it has gone;
white clouds and flowing water remain together in mutual affinity. (Miaofeng Shan)
Piercing the azure void, pines reach a thousand feet; Cutting off the red dust, a stream flows through one valley. Satiated in eating and sleeping soundly, no person may enter;
The sun rises from the east and sinks again in the west. (Wuzu Fan)
One lineage flows purely from Shaolin; the robe of faith has reached this point, transmitting only the mind. In his ordinary teachings to the assembly, no one understands;
everyone searches instead for the price of rice in Luling. (Zhang Wujin)
The Second Generation under the Sixth Patriarch (the First Generation under Nanyue):
Chan Master Daoyi of Jiangxi, popularly known as Mazu (he was the dharma heir of Nanyue Huairang). Addressing the assembly, he said:
"All of you, believe that your own mind is the Buddha; this very mind is the Buddha-mind. Bodhidharma from the South...
Having come from the land of India to China, [Bodhidharma] transmitted the Dharma of the One Mind of the Supreme Vehicle, causing the Dharma to be equally awakened.
A monk asked, "Why does the Master say 'This very mind is Buddha'? The Patriarch said, "To stop a small child’s crying.
The monk asked, "What is it after the crying has stopped? The Patriarch said, "Neither mind nor Buddha. The monk—
