A million valiant troops set forth; the General hunts at Weicheng. Unpracticed in the strength of bow and arrow, the moon rises over the slanting Milky Way. (Cuiyan Zhen)
Mind and mind are Buddha; Buddha and mind are mind. Buddha, Buddha, mind and mind are the Buddha-mind. When mind and Buddha are realized, there is not a single thing.
The general stops his thirst at the sight of plum blossoms. (Foguo Bai)
Rabbit horns need not exist; ox horns need not be absent. Where existence and non-existence do not apply, the fragrance fills the road. (Cangtang Qing).

The wind is fierce and the leaves fall repeatedly; the mountain is high and the sun sinks quickly. Those sitting within do not see it, for beyond the window the white clouds are deep. (Changling Zhuo)

The plain zither is strung in the midsummer month; flowing water and falling blossoms deepen the scene. Listening silently, the subtle sound penetrates to its depths—a clear, cold resonance, the music of antiquity. (By Fuxincai)
The springtime of the third month is harmonious and mild; the brocade-like mountains and rivers are the same everywhere. At dawn, blue tiles are veiled by mist and the rains of Cold Food Festival;
bright red curtains are rolled up by the breeze of the blooming apricot blossoms. (Cishou Shen)
Strike it and it resounds; listen and there is nothing. It is cold as ice in the bitter winter and drenched with sweat in the scorching heat.
When asked about the path, he replies: "How many stages are there from here to Chang'an? (Huanglong Zhen).
At the Jiangxi ferry crossing, Mazu held the thoroughfare; with a single oar and solitary sail, he ferried across those of the world.
Had it not been for Damei seeing through this, the spring at the head of the ridge would have been spent in vain. (Zhang Wujin)
The hairless chain is eight-sided and brilliant; without being pushed, it turns of itself toward the north, south, east, and west.
The Sea God knows its preciousness but does not know its price; it remains for the world to illuminate the night. (Yuánwù Qín)
Her beauty is like Xi Zi when she left the golden palace; her grace is like Yang Fei leaning against the jade tower.
Still holding the lute to half-conceal her face, she makes herself all the more charming so that others may not see her fully. (Fujian Qin)
"The very mind is Buddha" is the tradition of one school; Mazu’s reputation resounds throughout the four seas.
As soon as a sharp-witted monk casts a glance, his innate nature emerges with heavenly acuity. (Fodeng Xun)
"The very mind is Buddha—do not seek it falsely; Neither mind nor Buddha—cease further inquiry. Snowflakes fly upon the flames of a red furnace;
A single point of coolness dispels all feverish affliction. (Jingshan Gaofeng)
[Continued Collection] The iron ox plows through the void between heaven and earth; peach blossoms fall petal by petal from the deep source. Once the people of Qin departed, there has been no news;
for a thousand ages, the colors of the peaks and ridges have grown ever more fresh. (Xuedou Zong)
"Mind is Buddha, the eyebrows trail the ground; neither mind nor Buddha, the two eyes are askew. Amidst a butterfly’s dream, home is ten thousand li away;
on the branch of the cuckoo, the moon is at the third watch. (Xiatang Yuan)

The mind itself is the Buddha; look no further outward for it. When the mind and Buddha are perfectly luminous, there is no need for cultivation. As the clouds clear, the distant mountains appear as a thousand points of emerald green;
as the waters harmonize with the bright moon, the entire sky is autumn. (Zuan-an Jian)
Mazu said, "Neither mind nor Buddha. Directly beneath this, there is no further nest or lair.
This year’s walnuts on the tree are superior to last year’s tangerines. (Zhengtang Bian)
A cluster of human dwellings on an island village beyond the sea; falling flowers, flowing water, and the moon at dusk. When a hundred rivers reach the ocean, they must surely stay;
after all, how could there ever have been another source? (Iron Mountain Ren)
A golden-haired lion; a hammer of cast iron. It is whole and seamless—strictly avoid the needle and awl (Wuzu Fan).
One day Mazu ascended the hall; Baizhang withdrew the sitting mat before him, and Mazu immediately descended from the seat.
The verse says:
When Baizhang served Mazu at that time, he rolled up his mat before the Master with no further private intent. Gods and humans could not fathom this as something extraordinary;
it was precisely like gathering crows to seize a phoenix chick. When a superior man glimpses it, the whole body is fully manifested; the great sun rises to illuminate the peaks.
The peak is low. (Fenyang Zhao).
Ascending the hall, Mazu rolled up his mat; Baizhang gave a man half a pound and returned him eight ounces.
Even if there were not a single crack or seam, one could not avoid clapping one's hands at the sidelines. (Quandao).
A million heroic soldiers gaze upon one another in formation; who among them can turn back the war drums? If the general’s head is not fierce, he brings disaster upon the three armies;
alas, there is no place for the true command to be carried out. (Foyin Yuan)
Ascending the hall and rolling up the mat is peerless; the radiant sun rises in glory, pervading every place.
How laughable—thunder suddenly startling the universe, yet the creature within the well does not raise its head. (Haiyin Xin)
Having ascended the lion throne, he has fully realized perfection; the scroll of the Great Wisdom Sūtra is now set in motion.
The lion’s yawn is still somewhat bearable, but the elephant king’s backward glance is truly terrifying. (Jingzhao Zhen)
The wild duck flies and the nose-tip splits; rolling up the mat, he comes again to display his ugliness and clumsiness.
Even if one were to sit alone atop the Great Hero Peak, it would still be like a second moon in the sky. (Yang Woei-wei)
Yesterday the east wind was unexpectedly fierce; peach blossoms fell in profusion like a crimson rain. Last night the east wind again went mad;
they covered the ground, yet one knows not where they have gone. (Baiyun Cuan).
Who will hang the Qin mirror upon the high terrace? Beauty and ugliness are clearly revealed, all laid bare. By the side of the Stone Woman Creek, she glares with eyes of wrath;
meeting face-to-face, there is no room for evasion. (Becoming a withered tree.)
Deep in the night, he recognized the path back; without waiting for dawn, he passed through the pass. A three-foot Mo-ye sword rests in his hand;
to this day, he sits firmly atop Mount Daxiong. (Shangfang Yi)
The tide comes; the surfer rides the crest of the waves. Grasping a red flag, he rows against the current.
Suddenly, driven by a fierce wind and retreating surges, all his skillful maneuvers cease at once. (Fojian Qín)
Having hoisted the sails, one encounters a favorable wind; in a mere moment, one reaches home a thousand *li* away.
Stepping ashore at the gate, one meets wife and children; the joy of this heart is beyond compare. (Longmen Yuan)
Rolling up [the curtain], the majestic one reveals his eyes; brought forth, he presents himself face-to-face.
With the tip of the nose stripped away, who can gaze upon him? Taking hands, they return together side by side. (Chuan’an Fang)
[Continued Collection] Mazu ascended the hall; Baizhang rolled up his mat. The true command was not followed; he twisted the crooked to make it straight. (Xuedou Xian)
A colt travels a thousand li; it follows its rolled-up rug. A single night of autumn wind arises, and yellow chrysanthemums bloom everywhere. (Shi Daoyuan)
The demon hangs up the face of Nātha; barefoot, he stands firm upon Mount Sumeru. He whips up the iron ox on the banks of the Yellow River;
at the bottom of the great ocean, he devours the coral. (Xuedou Zong)
When Mazu ascended the hall, Baizhang rolled up his mat. This is a case already established; there is no need for further seeking. (Cao Tang Qing).
As soon as Mazu began to ascend the hall, Baizhang rolled up his mat and departed.
It is not like Shi-de or Han-shan finding a place where their grievances could be cleared. (Shichuang Gong).
The wind stilled, the Five Lakes broaden; I lower my sails to gaze at will. The ripples of the waves grow still with the water; their silken hue strikes one with a chilling cold.

Raising my oars, I linger among the cloud-covered coves; shifting my boat, I ascend the emerald bay. Its fame and splendor illuminate the ancestral realm; for a thousand years, let it be beheld by all men.
(Longmen Yuan): As soon as Mazu ascended the hall, Baizhang immediately rolled up his mat. A spring breeze blows in, and flowers lie scattered across the ground in profusion.
(Gao’an Wu): The vast, surging Yangtze River reaches to the void; A single sail hoisted high, one immediately rides the wind. How joyful!
Without expending the slightest effort, Ten thousand *li* to one’s home mountain are reached in a mere inch. (Kaishan Xian)
The circumstances of rolling up the mat are truly marvelous. When heard by those in all quarters, they all knit their brows.
The stand and tray were kicked over and people scattered like stars; this straightforward man has never been deceived (Zhang Wugou).
Baizhang rolled up his mat; Mazu ascended the hall. "What? What?"—testing the practitioner to the utmost. (Yuelin Guan) A single handle of the dispassionate, snow-white blade;
who would dare to violate its edge by even a hair’s breadth? The Master and his son personally wielded it;
blood sprayed across a thousand mountains as the wind howled in rage. (Wuzhun Fan)
[Added from the Supplementary Collection] A monk asked Mazu, "What is the Buddha? Mazu replied, "The very mind is the Buddha.
The Verse says: "The very mind is the Buddha; an iron ox has no bones. A fierce dragon playing in the sea, a majestic hawk soaring to the heavens.
To swallow up the Western River is not yet considered marvelous; A lotus blooming in fire, its fragrance wafts afar. (Nantang Xing)
"Mind itself is Buddha. A dragon enters a snake's den; going out as a general and entering as a minister, he brings peace to the state and stabilizes the nation.
(Stonehead turns around. Whose meal hangs from the empty beam? Pointing it out to a small child, he commands him to look. Once untied, it is but a bag of ashes;
at that very moment, the life-root is severed. (Kaishan Jian)
Her beauty is like Xi Zi leaving the Golden Palace; her grace is like Yang Fei descending from the Jade Tower.
Spending all day intoxicated with you beneath the flowers, what could one find anywhere more refined and elegant? (Kentang Chong)

"‘The mind itself is Buddha’ is a vague and muddled notion. Failing to distinguish beans from barley, one’s life flickers away. With three cups and two bowls, one turns one’s back on father and mother;
a hundred monsters and a thousand demons dwell in the same den. (Pah! Huigan’s essence.)"
The waves of the great ocean are vast; the atmosphere of the thousand peaks is majestic. From ancient times to the present, there has been no interruption;
the paths to the south and north are open through. (Miam Jie)
The very mind is the Buddha. Chang'e does not paint her brows; as soon as she defiles them with rouge and powder, her beauty turns into ugliness. (Tianmu Li)

"The mind itself is Buddha. Like arsenic or wolf-poison, it can raise the dead and restore life; it requires no more than a single dose. (Huanxi I). [Added from another source] Once a monk asked Mazu, "What is the Buddha?

Mazu replied, "Neither mind nor Buddha. A verse says: The mind itself is Buddha; Arsenic and wolf-poison Can revive the dead. It takes but one dose. (Huanxi I) [Added from another source] Mazu, when a monk asked, "What is the Buddha? Mazu said, "Neither mind nor Buddha. The Verse says:
Jade beads from the sea, jade discs from Mount Jing; they illuminate heaven and earth—who can discern them? With a sharp blade, he cuts down the rootless tree;
ten thousand layers of peaks withdraw their mists and fogs. (Yuǎnwù Qín)
Having sold off his fields and gardens, he is destitute to the bone; one knows not where he may find a place to rest his body.
Wandering aimlessly atop the tower without restraint, he blows his iron flute crosswise as he passes over Lake Dongting. (Kaishan Xian)
The scenery and atmosphere of the second month are drifting and light; young gentlemen ride through the imperial streets.
Seated upon silver beds with saw-like chairs, they enjoy the pleasure of pouring wine; three children play the game of polo. (Muan Zhong)
Neither Buddha nor mind—this is called severing all emotions. On the mysterious path, like a bird’s track, one must hasten back. With the *śakrāloka* eye, maintain the power of adaptive response;
do not linger guarding the cold crags while the strange grasses turn green. (Nanyuan Sheng)
Clearly and distinctly, it is thus: no, no, no. Śākyamuni and Maitreya are his servants.
Vast is the universe, with countless people; how many among them are true men? (Yuelin Guan).
If you meet a swordsman on the road, you must present it; if you do not encounter a poet, do not offer it. When meeting people, speak of only three parts;
do not yet cast forth the full piece. (Wumen opens).
Once, while Mazu, Baizhang, Xitang, and Nanquan were gazing at the moon, Mazu asked, "At this very moment, what is it?
Baizhang said, "It is precisely the time for cultivation. Xitang said, "It is precisely the time for making offerings. Nanquan shook his sleeves and walked away.
Mazu remarked, "The sutras have entered the canon and Chan has returned to the sea; only Puyan alone transcends the mundane world."
The verse says:
Three beasts cross a river, each at a different depth; without needing laborious discernment, they are clearly distinguished.
How can this compare to one who sails upon the vast ocean, heedless of the waves as they pass through the sea gate? (Seal of the Ocean-Print)
The sutras have entered the canon and Chan has returned to the sea; only Puyuan alone transcends the mundane world. (Tut!
There is only the moonlight reflecting on the jade wall, yet there is no wind blowing through the leaves. (Zhaojue Zong)
The sutras enter the treasury and Chan returns to the sea. I bow my head in refuge and join my palms to uphold [this teaching]. Master Wang has transcended the mundane world;
twenty years ago he came in such a manner, yet now all his idle brilliance has vanished. (Tiantong Ju)
Master Ma plays with the moon; his three sons attend him on the left and right. Blowing a flute without holes, its pure sound fills heaven and earth. (Zhenru [interrogates].)
Brilliantly white, it gathers the azure of the void; deep and profound, it emits radiant luster. Its autumnal clarity merges with the pure sky, as the eternal night overlooks the vast ocean.
Through practice and offering, one encounters the perfect mechanism; upon merely hearing this, one acts and transcends the mundane world. The colt indeed possesses a unique distinction.
For ten thousand ages he settled heaven and earth; with a single word he wielded both killing and giving life (Wenyu Qín).
Though the sutras have entered the canon and Chan has returned to the sea, these are not yet the intimate path of a true monk. Shake off your sleeves, move forward, and go back home!
The heavy gates are shattered and thrown wide open (Kai Funing).
At Guoqing, the talented are noble; in this wealthy household, the children are pampered. Let everyone lend a hand; let neither side yield to the other.
(Jingshan Gao): Master Zhang raised three sons;
as they grew up, it was not known who among them would resolve to pursue the Way. He called them forth under the moon to inquire of their origins;
though their eyes were all alike, [he recognized the one]. (Fóxìng Tài).
[Continued Collection] Great capacity and great function. Silver mountains and iron walls. Making offerings and practicing cultivation. Eyes askance, nose straight. Shaking the sleeves and departing;
the myriad phenomena leave no trace. I dare ask you all: who is the one who hits the mark? (Chunuo Xiu).
An old man with three sons, by chance they walk together on the Road of Vipaśyin. Before the wind they sing the song of the profound mystery;
for a thousand ages their voices harmonize, yet none can match it. That time and this time—pointing to a deer as a horse, taking a turtle as proof of a tortoise.
Though they employ cleverness, it turns into clumsiness; better to spare the two flaps of skin. (Xuedou Zong)
At the ancient ferry, where no wind blows, he lowers his straight hook; the intent of the silken line is to catch the whales and turtles. Under Master Ma’s words, the family’s ugliness was revealed;
for a thousand ages, their descendants have wandered among the weeds. (Zantang Shen)
The sons manage their households, each growing fat; among them, one is most pitiable. A basket full of ink, no one will buy it;
at midnight he carries it home to dye his robes black. (Great Rest, Qian).
Each of the sons has achieved success in his own life; from the beginning, filial piety has arisen on both sides.
Greeding for the joy of a single night of family harmony, they hurriedly strike the fifth watch as dawn breaks. (Wuzhun Shanfan)

Mazu was unwell. The head of the monastery asked him, "How has your venerable state been lately, Master? Mazu replied, "The Buddha of the Sun’s Face, the Buddha of the Moon’s Face. The verse says: The Buddha of the Sun’s Face, the Buddha of the Moon’s Face— A single phrase, yet how many meanings! If you wish to see the Buddha’s true countenance, Look at the face of the present moment. The sun and moon are both clear and bright; Why do you still ask about his health? If you can understand this within a single thought, Then you will know that he is not ill at all.
Sūryamukha Buddha, Candramukha Buddha. What are the Five Emperors and Three Sovereigns? For twenty years I have undergone bitter toil;
for your sake, I have plunged directly into the Azure Dragon’s lair. How could it not be recounted? O clear-eyed monks, do not treat this with levity! (Xuedou Xian)
The sun’s face and the moon’s face; turning left and revolving right. The Great Tang beats the drum; Silla releases the arrow.
Flowing water in the front stream and the back stream; fallen blossoms, three pieces and five. The deaf do not hear the sudden peal of thunder;
they vainly gaze into the clouds for lightning. (Fohuiquan)
A young nobleman suddenly went wild; at midnight he pierced the clouds to enter the bridal chamber. The two immortal Xiannü girls displayed every artifice;
upon their eyes were embroidered mandarin ducks. (By Yanxuan Zun)
Buddha Sun-Face, Buddha Moon-Face. Night after night, morning after morning, what fine scenery! A colt tramples the people of the world to death;
the Yellow Emperor shines through the cave of spirits. (Yang Wúwéi)
The great earth, mountains, and rivers are all jewels; those who do not recognize them enter the wild weeds.
The Buddhas of the Sun’s Face and Moon’s Face appear before one; the light of the coral flashes, bright and radiant. (Baiyun Yuan)
Sitting upright upon the meditation cushion, threading a needle’s eye with a strand of silk. A gust of west wind arrives;
two or three leaves fall. (Baoning Yong)
The Buddhas Riju-mukha and Candrānanā are impartial; who can recommend the pearl from beneath the chin of the black dragon?
A full hand-grip of radiance illuminates the Ox and Dipper constellations; why need one brandish a sword while standing upon the steps? (Zhaojue Zong)
The sun’s face, the moon’s face—when the barbarian comes, the Han appears. A single point of numinous light undergoes ten thousand transformations and a thousand changes. (Zhenjing Wen).
The sun’s face, the moon’s face—stars stream forth and lightning rolls. Like a mirror facing its image without partiality, like a pearl on a platter turning of itself.
Have you not seen? Gold refined a hundred times before the tongs and hammer; silk spun as a single thread beneath the knife and ruler.
(Tiantong Jue) The sun’s face is to the east, the moon’s face is to the west; who says they fall naturally into the stream ahead?
The mountain peach has fallen away and spring has departed, yet the cuckoo still cries upon its branch. (Shangfang Yi)
Shifang’s Colt gives rise to a fierce temper; he tramples upon the crown of Vairocana. Just suffering from a pain in the spleen, now he has a headache;
even as illness comes, there is still a clever mind at work. (Zhang Wujin)

The Buddha of the Sun’s Face, the Buddha of the Moon’s Face—the great ocean surges with waves, Mount Sumeru looms abruptly; it strikes and shatters the frontal bone, and sweat breaks out on the forehead.
Even a monk with clear eyes has not yet discerned this clearly. Lift your head and look well at the soaring falcon! (Changling Zhuo)
A young maidservant paints her蛾眉 (eyebrows) before the phoenix-mirror stand; her speech is like that of one who is demented.
She says of herself, "My jade-like countenance has no equal," yet she goes to the rack to put on her silk robes. (Wuzu Yan).
On the eastern street, willow colors trail in misty green; on the western lane, peach blossoms reflect one another in red. Looking left and right, one can never gaze enough;
all at once, they are entrusted to the spring breeze. (Fojian Qín)
How is your honored state these days? "Sunny Face, Moon Face, *līlā*!
Since I first performed the Three Platforms dance, every beat has been nothing but song. (Fodeng Xun)
The sun’s face, the moon’s face; lightning flashing in the void. Gu Zhu halts his loom; the target is set for the drawn arrow. (Nanhuabing).
The sun’s face, the moon’s face—the numinous light shines through clearly. From the great earth, mountains, and rivers, to the prefectures south and north;
though this is the earnest heart of an old woman, who would have known it would cause the monastery supervisor to die of doubt? (Shushan Ru).
Sun-face, Moon-face: appearing at every turn. Squeezed together and released, they form a mass and a sheet. (Chuan’an Fang).
[Continued Collection] As soon as the golden crow caws, the sun is at its zenith; the royal road is level and smooth, penetrating everywhere.
Yet alas, the colt was born too early; as before, it tramples the great void. (Zhengjue Yi).
The face of the sun, the face of the moon. The stars shift and the constellations turn; the dawn breaks upon the Persian, yet he cannot find his head. (Cuiyan Zhen).
The face of the sun, the face of the moon—suddenly appearing, difficult to discern. A pair of clever mandarin ducks embroidered; who would not admire them?

Wearing the moon, they nestle among the reeds; following the waves, they play upon the surface of the water. In an instant, they fly up into the azure void; raising their heads, the Milky Way stretches across.
"Plainly practiced" (Xuedou Zong).
"The face of the sun, the face of the moon; empty space and a flash of lightning.

I have killed the yellow oriole; let it not sing upon the branch. How many times it has startled my dreams, preventing me from reaching Liaoxi. (Dian Niyou)
What is this honored state? To seek the autumn waves within the reflection of a clear pool—how can one distinguish the faces of the sun and moon with eyes of iron and copper?
Do you not see? With a single clap of thunder, mist shrouds the vast sky; with a thousand eyes suddenly opened, clouds disperse from the mountain peaks. (Xiatang Yuan)
A smile opens within the vermilion mirror; legs are stretched out to sleep within the white jade basin. In general, it is difficult for human life to find companionship;
when one finds the opportunity for reunion, one should simply enjoy that reunion. (Fóxìng Tái)
Where the two wheels turn, smoke and dust arise; swift as lightning, fast as a shooting star—how could they ever be halted? Before one’s eyes, the mechanism of coming and going is unimpeded;
the true command is fully applied, without inner or outer. The spirit of the great man naturally pierces the heavens;
"I am I, and you are you" (the cultivation of faithful signs).
In this ancient hall, those who arrive are rare; who knows of one sitting upright upon the rush mat?
Had it not been for the monastery master conveying the news, how could the cold radiance shine ten thousand miles away? (Zhongji Neng)
"How is the Honored Position? I ask the one most intimate to me. One cannot gather it together; the source of the illness is deep.
When casually raised, the mirror of Xuanyuan appears; even Bian Que and Lu Yi have no place to seek it. (Tu'an Qi)
A horse colt was born in Hanzhou; its illness lies in the vital organs beyond the reach of medicine.
The head of the monastery inquires after his well-being for no reason, leading him to flaunt his mere lip-service. (Tieshan Ren)
Buddha Sun-Face and Buddha Moon-Face: on the western crag, the colors of the trees hold mist; in the eastern valley, the radiance of the flowers reflects the sun.
Looking up, one cannot fathom its depths; looking down, one has already grown old. Entrust this all at once to the forest deity; where can an enlightened monk seek it?
(Tianmu Li): "The sun-face and moon-face stand out so prominently they are difficult to distinguish; as soon as one intends to lift one's eyes, there are two fragments in mid-air. (Wuzhun Fan).
A monk asked Mazu, "Transcending the four propositions and cutting off the hundred negations, I ask the Master to point directly to the meaning of the Westward Transmission.
Mazu said, "I am weary today and cannot explain it for you; go and ask Zhizang.
The monk went to ask Zhizang, who said, "Why do you not ask the Master? The monk replied, "The Master told me to come and ask you."
Cang said, "I have a headache today; I cannot explain it for you. Go ask my elder brother Hai.
The monk went to ask Hai, who said, "When I get here, I too do not understand. The monk returned and reported this to Mazu.
The Patriarch said: "The head of the storehouse is white; the head of the sea is black. The Verse says:
The head of the storehouse is white; the head of the sea is black. Even a clear-eyed monk cannot comprehend it. The colt tramples all people underfoot.
Linji was no mere "white-handed thief. Beyond the four propositions and transcending the hundred negations, in all of heaven and earth, only I know it.
(Xuedou Xian) Not knowing whom he was asking, he sought it; he held up the treasure before him, yet the other did not recognize it. He brought it forth and brought it back, questioning the merchant.
People do not distinguish east from west; they merely exhaust their strength in vain. Returning as before, they are filled with self-pity.
How many pairs of straw sandals have been worn through? (Haiyin Xin)
Beyond the hundred negations and severed from the four propositions—what words can there be? Black and white are clearly distinguished; right and biased are fixed.
Within the lion’s den there are no other beasts; where the dark dragon moves, the waves overflow the heavens. (Zhaojue Zong)
The two goddesses of the Xiang River, in the manner of immortal maidens, lean smiling against the vermilion gate on the fragrant thoroughfare.
A single stroke of rouge suffuses their cheeks with red, adding a tenfold air of natural innocence. (Fujian Qin)
The four propositions and hundred negations are all barred; the "Spring Breeze" and "Snowy White" melodies sing ever higher.
On a night of clear wind and bright moon without a cloud, who would trade a "hair-piercing" blade for a precious sword? (Nanhua Bing)
Beyond the hundred negations and the four propositions, distance and intimacy are severed. The colt tramples all under heaven to death.
The head at the mountain is white; the head at the sea is black. The Vajra outside the gate laughs and then scowls. (Yuanjue Yan)
[Continued Collection] It is like an arrow shot in the dark; it flies through the midnight hours unseen by men. It is also like a brush with its tip concealed;
though the day is bright and vast, it does not emerge. The head is hidden and white, yet the tip is black; upon the crystal palace, gold and jade are added.
Reflecting back on Bodhidharma meeting the King of Liang—who among those facing him did not recognize him? (Fujian Qin).
A short cap and light robe, narrow in the imperial style; she dances through all eighteen variations of the *hugu* flute. When the music ends and the wine is spent, she has still not returned;
upon her return, the moonlight blends with the clouds into white. (Xiatang Yuan)

The hundred negations cut off, penetrating beyond the subtle and minute; the four propositions forgotten, the supreme faculty is awakened. Though the bamboo be dense, it does not hinder the flowing stream from passing through;
though the mountain be high, how could it obstruct the white clouds from flying? (Zu’ān Jiàn)

Transcending the four propositions and cutting off the hundred negations—the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West is utterly vast and open. The head in the storehouse is white; the head in the sea is black.
One cannot bear this old thief, Master Ma! Through ten thousand ages it remains a dark expanse; filling the ditches and blocking the ravines, no one recognizes it.
(No talent for meditation). A father conceals for his son;
a son conceals for his father. A single fire, a white-handed thief—dare anyone approach? "The head is white at the front, black at the back of the sea.
Without moving a blade or a spear, he cuts off human life. (Tui’an’s marvel).
Transcending the four propositions and severing the hundred negations—how often have they passed the blame back and forth without ever realizing it?
This monk carries a shoulder-load of delusion, only to trade it for a double portion of muddled confusion on his way home. (Yuepo Ming)

The jade turns and the pearl rolls—look with clear eyes. Where there seems to be involvement, there is no involvement at all. Simply take this very thing as [the standard].
Master. (He lets out a shout and says: "A single sword leaning against the heavens; the stars and constellations grow cold.
(Stone Creek Moon). [Added from another collection: One day Mazu sealed three jars of sauce and ordered a monk to carry a letter to Baizhang.
When Baizhang assembled the assembly for the hall discourse, he opened the letter, picked up his staff, pointed at the jars, and said: "If you can speak, I shall not strike you."
He broke it. The Master said, "If you cannot break it, then break it yourself. The assembly remained silent. The Master broke it himself and returned to his quarters.

[The monk] asked, "If it is thus, from where do the Great Canon and the Lesser Canon come? The Master said, "They all come from right here; they never lack for anything.
Yuan greatly approved of this. The verse says:
If there is news, it is too heavy with sorrow; if there is no news, one sinks further into oblivion.
From this, the Great Canon and the Lesser Canon emerge; sand and earth are scattered without end. Sweet as honey, bitter as gall; bright as the sun, black as lacquer.
Smash the den of the thousand-year-old wild fox; fill the ditches and block the ravines—no one recognizes it. (Wenyu Qin)

Before the fox-doubts have ceased, one asks about the superior stream; "How can liberation bring the mind to rest?
If you accept that liberation arises from someone else, Only non-arising itself is Stonehead. (Fenyang Zhao)
Once you asked about doubt and liberation; you intended to seek a teacher’s single secret instruction.
When the Master’s compassionate intent responds to your capacity, you should regard this as the "second moon. (By Prajñā-róu)

[Added for inclusion] Once, when a monk asked Shitou, “What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? the Master said, “Ask the pillar. The monk said, “I do not understand. The Master said, “I do not understand either. The Verse says: The Patriarch came from the West; He did not come for the sake of words. If you wish to know the meaning, Go ask the wooden pillar. When the monk asked again, he was silent. The silence was like the vast sky. The meaning is not found in speech; How could it be grasped by the mind? If you can see through this, You will know the source of the Way. If you cannot yet comprehend, You must look at the pillar yourself. If you can see the pillar, You will see the Patriarch. If you can see the Patriarch, You will see the pillar. If you can see both, Then you have attained liberation. If you cannot see either, You remain lost in delusion. Do not seek outside; Seek within your own heart. If you can see your own nature, This is the ultimate truth. If you do not see your own nature, You wander in birth and death. Therefore, do not rely on words; Rely instead on direct realization. Direct realization is the true path; Words are but empty echoes. If you can hear this soundless sound, You will transcend all duality. If you can see this formless form, You will enter the realm of non-dwelling. This is the teaching of the Buddhas and Patriarchs; It is the very marrow of the Dharma. Do not doubt it; Practice it with diligence. If you practice with diligence, You will surely attain enlightenment. If you do not practice, You will remain a common person. Therefore, I urge you all: Do not waste this precious life. Seize the opportunity now; Do not wait until it is too late. If you wait until it is too late, There will be no way to escape. Therefore, I say to you: Awaken to the mind-ground! Awaken to the mind-ground! This is the urgent instruction of the Buddhas and Patriarchs. Do not let it pass in vain. If you can awaken to it, You will be free from all suffering. If you do not awaken, You will continue to suffer. Therefore, I urge you all: Awaken to the mind-ground! Awaken to the mind-ground! This is the final exhortation. Do not hesitate. Act now! Act now! This is the true teaching of the Buddhas and Patriarchs. Do not doubt it. Trust in it! Trust in it! This is the path to liberation. Do not seek elsewhere. Seek within yourself! Seek within yourself! If you can find it, You will be a true heir of the Buddhas. If you cannot find it, You are merely a follower of the shadows. Therefore, I say to you: Awaken to the mind-ground! Awaken to the mind-ground! This is the ultimate truth. Do not let it be lost. Preserve it! Preserve it! This is the legacy of the Buddhas and Patriarchs. Do not treat it lightly. Hold it fast! Hold it fast! This is the core of the Dharma. Do not let it slip away. Guard it! Guard it! This is the secret of the sages. Do not reveal it to the unready. Reveal it only to those who are ready. To those who are ready, It is the medicine that cures all illness. To those who are not ready, It is a poison that brings ruin. Therefore, I urge you all: Be careful with the Dharma. Be careful with the Dharma! This is the instruction of the Buddhas and Patriarchs. Do not misunderstand it. Understand it correctly! Understand it correctly! This is the true meaning of the coming from the West. Do not look for it in books. Look for it in your own experience. In your own experience, You will find the Way. In the Way, You will find peace. In peace, You will find liberation. In liberation, You will find the end of suffering. This is the goal of all practice. Do not seek it in vain. Seek it with sincerity. Seek it with sincerity! The Northern School [Supplement]: Chan Master Weizheng of Zhongnan Mountain (heir to Xiu of the Northern School; succeeded Ji of Mount Song). During the Dahan era of Emperor Wenzong of the Tang dynasty, the Emperor was fond of clams.
One day, among his imperial provisions, there was one that would not open even after being cracked. The Emperor—
Considering this a strange occurrence, he burned incense and offered prayers. Suddenly, the object transformed into the form of a Bodhisattva, its features fully endowed with the marks of a Brahma.

He immediately placed it in a casket made of *suvarṇa-kṣīra* sandalwood and covered it with fine brocade, then bestowed it upon Xingshan Temple so that the assembly of monks might gaze upon and worship it.
Thereupon, he questioned his ministers: "What auspicious omen is this? Some replied, "On Mount Taiyi, there is a statue of Weizheng..."
The Chan Master was profoundly enlightened in the Buddha-dharma and possessed vast learning and a powerful memory. The Emperor immediately ordered him to be summoned and questioned about the matter.
The Master said, "Your servant has heard that nothing occurs without a corresponding cause; this is merely to inspire Your Majesty’s faith.
He further cited the Sūtra, saying, "Those who are to be saved by means of this body, to them he manifests this very body and preaches the Dharma for them. The Emperor said:
The body of the Bodhisattva had already appeared, yet he had not yet heard him preach the Dharma. The Master asked, "Your Majesty, beholding this, do you consider it permanent or impermanent?
Do you believe it or not? The Emperor replied, "This is a rare and extraordinary matter; I believe it deeply.
The Master said, "Your Majesty has already heard the preaching of the Dharma. The Emperor’s heart was greatly delighted, and he issued an edict throughout the empire.
A statue of Avalokiteśvara was erected at each monastery to express gratitude for this extraordinary grace. The verse says:
"Among the species of snails, conches, and clams, The heart of the Great Tang Emperor finds delight; In his fondness, he has deep faith: Namo Avalokiteśvara!"
(Xiyuan Hui): "Mixing water with mud—how busy he was! He was exposed by him; how awkward and excessive!
Though he may have silently accorded with the Emperor’s intent, he has already cast his entire body into the cauldron of boiling oil. (Beihai Xin)
A single drop of compassion cannot be split apart; amidst the boiling cauldrons, his cheeks are filled with smiles. This extraordinary matter I, the Emperor, believe deeply;
he has come to preach the Dharma to the Sovereign. (Shixi Yue)
Within the clam and oyster lies the response-body; to speak further of preaching the Dharma is likewise not the truth. The Great Being of Potalaka is the Son of Heaven of Tang;
his sidelong glance leaves no one without the grace of a past night. (Xianjiyun)

Sixth Patriarch’s Lineage, Third Generation, Part One (Nanyue Lineage, Second Generation, Part One).
Chan Master Daizhi Huaihai of Baizhang Mountain in Hongzhou (a successor of Mazu). He visited Mazu for a second time.
Mazu took a fly-whisk from the corner of his meditation seat and showed it to him. The Master said, "Is there anything else besides this?"
The Patriarch then returned the whisk to its original place and said, "What will you use to guide others in the future? The Master took up the whisk and showed it to him.
The Patriarch said, "Is this all there is, or is there something else? The Master hung the whisk back in its original place and stood in attendance.
The Patriarch rebuked him. Later, a lay donor invited him to reside at Mount Daxiong, where the cliffs and peaks were steep and lofty.
It was so extreme that it was called "Hundred Fathoms" (Bai Zhang). One day, the Master said to the assembly, "The Buddha-dharma is no small matter.
In the past, when I was struck by Mazu’s single shout, my ears were deaf and my vision black for three days straight."
Upon hearing the case cited, Huangbo involuntarily stuck out his tongue. The verse says:

"Whenever I attended before the Master on no particular business, The Master pointed to something hanging from the corner of the meditation seat. I picked it up and returned to my original position to stand;
This distinct 'single shout' has been passed down to this day. (Fenyang Shao)
Having awakened, he travels abroad and then returns; with his total capacity and great function, he has long held the authority.
If one did not forget intellectual understanding beneath the shout, how could a fine horse ever leave its whip? (Foyin Yuan)
When we meet again at the Great Tranquil Heroic Peak, we shall walk together where the weeds grow thick.
With one turn of the head and a shout, heaven and earth darken; both ears go deaf, and none know aught. (Zhengjue Yi)
A single shout—few in the monastic groves can discern it; deaf ears from ancient times to the present, yet they stubbornly apply needles and awls.
The lantern claps its hands and laughs "he-he"; the pillar bows its head and frowns. (Haiyin Xin)
A single shout clearly guards the dead ashes; from the azure sky, wind and thunder arise. Onlookers clap their hands and laugh aloud;
only the one who knows the sound comes forth, tongue out in wonder. (Jingzhao Zhen)
Releasing and gathering—who says there is no clamor? Do you see the leakage of the mechanism? A single shout like thunder causes those who hear it to perish;
being deaf for three days is not even considered much. (Fohuiquan)
Not yet having clarified Great Wisdom, one seeks it again and again; chasing and following one another, its function is beyond mastery.
When waves are severed and currents cut off, the whole body is fully manifested; deaf for three days, who can know this sound? (Zhaojue Zong)
The sentiments of a guest turn with every step one takes; though possessing great majestic radiance, it cannot manifest.
Suddenly, a shout deafens both ears; Nata’s eyes open and Huangbo’s face appears. (Zhenjing Wen)
Looking back, the matter at hand is already the same; when teacher and disciple meet, they manifest their family tradition.
Reflecting on that day long ago when my nose ached, a single shout was so distinct it left me deaf for three days. (Foguo Bai).
The wooden horse tramples the people of Jambudvīpa; the clay ox drinks dry the waters of the vast ocean. Thunder fills the sky and the mountains crumble;
look, look—waves and billows rise from the level plain. (Baoning Yong)
Mazu personally transmitted the heart-mind of the ancient Buddha; Hai and Baizhang were his true intimates. At that time, a single shout deafened them for three days;
from then until now, there has been neither seeing nor hearing. (Zhihaiqing)
The rain has cleared, yet the wandering clouds have not yet returned; from the cloudless sky, suddenly, a clap of thunder. The plum on the ridge has already received the news of spring;
it does not bloom like the mountain peach in its ordinary way. (Shangfang Yi)
Let go and pick it up again—who is it? Amidst the green mountains, one often sees white clouds returning. Sitting alone upon the solitary peak, there is nothing more to do;
I laugh instead at the moon’s orb facing the setting glow. (Lian of Tianning Monastery in Jingzhao Prefecture)
The Colt’s single shout at Daxiong Peak / Made the skull deaf for three days. / Huangbo heard it and was so startled he stuck out his tongue;
/ From this point on, the school’s tradition was established in Jiangxi. (Zhang Wujin)
Baizhang came again to visit Mazu; upon meeting, Mazu pointed directly to the path of Caoxi.

A piece of forged iron is drawn from behind the diamond-hard skull. The three peaks of Mount Hua stand inverted in the void. (Longmen Yuan)

The whisk was personally met with a shout; at that moment, the tongue fell off. Holding it up, I present it to you; for your sake, I lift it up once more.
If you wish to know, there will be deafness for three days; the great earth is like fine dust. (Chuanfang)

Turning back to reflect on where clouds become rain, one sees only the four quarters vying to emerge from the mountains. (Cuiyan Zhen)
Father and son meet; their affinity is the same. The precious sword of Longquan is ground once more.
To clarify Mazu’s shout of that day, the mountains and rivers of the great earth are all deafened. (Cishou Shen)
A sudden clap of thunder shatters the moon in the clear pool; for three days thereafter, one remains deaf.

Father and son go hand in hand to roam amidst the grass; held up before people, how many times they bring shame upon themselves!
A single clap of thunder returns, shaking heaven and earth, until not a drop flows from the vast blue ocean. (Lan’an Xu)

A single blow to the crown of the head—a drum smeared with lethal poison; the full mechanism of life and death shakes through ancient and modern times. Only after the snow has fallen does one know the integrity of the pine and cypress;
only when affairs are difficult does one see the heart of a true man. (Nun Wuzhuo Zong)
A colt’s kicking and trampling is no donkey’s business; it must be made so that one’s descendants walk upon their own feet.

When the shout ceases, the angry thunder subsides; the family tradition is utterly lost, with not a trace remaining.

Wind and clouds meet once more in anticipation; face-to-face, it is difficult to clarify the primary function. With a single clap of thunder, heaven and earth are pressed together;

On the worldly path, amidst wind and waves, I have not seen you. My grieving heart writes its sorrows in secret—whom can I discuss them with?
A sudden clap of thunder resounds and a clear breeze arises; under the white sun, the heavens spread wide and the stars are divided. (Muan Yong)
A lone horse and a single spear, he comes this way. The array of linked iron is difficult to break through.
Suddenly, with one blow, the gong resounds; without moving a blade, he returns in victory. (Byunyun Nan).
A single shout strikes head-on like a rushing thunderclap; even those in the human world who speak of it find their souls darkened with awe.
It seems this will not merely deafen one for three days, but shall continue until now, as the seas and mountains remain shrouded in gloom. (Xue’an Jin)
The timing of the hen and the chick is of different kinds; flying stars scatter fire, and the skull is empty. When the thieving mind has died out, it is difficult to speak;
suddenly one sees the golden sun emerge from the eastern sea. (Xutang Yu)

Yang said, "Baizhang attained the great capacity; Huangbo attained the great function;

Mazu asked, "What is that? The Master replied, "Wild ducks. Mazu asked, "Where have they gone? The Master replied, "They flew away.

Master and disciple walk together through the weeds; wild ducks fly and cry, and a sudden thought arises.

A wild duck passes before the eastern stream; a thousand peaks display a chilling hue. Gazing at one another, they do not know where to return; they cannot avoid being struck from the side.

The Horse Tamer pities you for your lack of wisdom; he borrows a wild duck to convey a message.

I request the Master to speak further: A tiger’s head sprouts horns as it emerges from the wild weeds; the ten islands have reached the end of spring and their flowers wither;
the coral forests bask in the bright, radiant sun. (Xuedou Xian, 3)
The Master has also closed it off; observe the strategy from atop the Dragon-Head formation. It makes one long remember General Li:
a solitary eagle soars ten thousand miles across the edge of heaven.
"Does the Master have it yet? The golden-haired lion does not crouch on the ground; two by two and three by three, they travel the old path.
On the mountain of Mahāvīra, he snaps his fingers into the void."
The three sons have all grown up; together they take their capital to engage in business.
In the process, some losses cause the elder brother to resent the younger, while some gains cause the younger brother to resent the elder. (Baoning Yong)
I request the Master to speak: where thousands and tens of thousands have not reached— The bright sun is dimly visible as the sea turns crimson;
A clear wind blows chill as the frosty sky breaks into dawn. (Fojian Yongqin, 3)
The Master has also shut it off. Those who come after wish to tread upon the footsteps of those who came before. Though their capacities may differ—some sharp, some dull—their paths diverge;
yet in the end, they all lose by one move.
"Does the Master have it yet? For now, clarify and see within your own person; you cannot yet spread your wings to fly against the wind.
You merely pursue the ambition of a thousand li toward the blue clouds."

Once, when a monk asked Baizhang, "What is the extraordinary matter? the Master said, "Sitting alone on the Great Hero Peak. The monk bowed, and the Master struck him. The verse says: Sitting alone on the Great Hero Peak, The thousand sages are all startled;
The monk bows and receives a blow— How many can truly comprehend it?
The patriarchal domain is where celestial colts gallop; the gates of transformation unfold and roll up along different paths.
Like a flash of lightning or a spark from flint, there exists the power of shifting opportunity—how laughable it is that people come to stroke a tiger’s whiskers. (Xuedou Xian)
Majestically sitting alone, he presides over the heroic peak. A three-foot dragon-spring sword is held within his palm.
How laughable that people come to brush against the white blade; they are reduced to minced powder—who could say for whom? (Zhengjue Yi)
Majestically sitting alone on Mount Daxiong, his coughing and spitting stir the wind and chill heaven and earth. Directly beneath the staff, he opens the True Eye;
from across the clouds a thousand miles away, one gazes toward Chang’an. (By Yanxuan Zun)
Sitting alone atop the majestic peak, towering and imposing; throughout the four seas, songs and chants fill every path.
Even those whose entire bodies are like blades of steel cannot fail to raise their banners of surrender upon arriving here. (Haiyin Xin)
How could such great capacity and great function be in vain? Sitting alone upon the solitary peak, he possesses his own sovereign authority.
Should anyone transmit the King’s decree even slightly incorrectly, they shall receive three thousand blows upon the crown of their head. (Baizhang Yuanwen)
The Great Hero’s Peak stands alone, towering high; Directly beneath, his brows are parted in an "eight" character.
Fortunately, he knows when to withdraw by tucking in his head; He has never dared to easily neglect his duty. (Baoning Yong)
Sitting alone on Great Hero Peak, one speaks of the emptiness of the universe. If one does not walk upon the summit of the peak, the paths to the four seas are difficult to traverse. (Baofeng Xiang)
The pure wind encompasses the earth, its vital energy spans the heavens. Sitting alone upon the majestic peak, he possesses great authority.
With a single roar, the mountain caves split asunder; henceforth, not even the tracks of a dog shall reach his gate. (Fujian Yongqin)
[Continued Collection] Adding salt to the sauce; sending charcoal into the snow. Just as one has grasped the tiger’s whiskers, there are eyes upon the staff.
No wonder he sits alone on Mount Daxiong; his house has long since trodden upon the highest pass. (Yuánwù Qín).
Sitting alone on the peak, he carries nothing in his bag; having been caught red-handed, the evidence is clear.
If you seek further extraordinary matters, you will only soil all quarters with the saliva of wild foxes. (Wuji Pai)
Baizhang’s timing was swift as the wind; towering, he sat alone atop Great Hero Peak.
If you wish to know the most extraordinary among the extraordinary, the bright moon cannot be made to descend from the azure sky. (Shitennō Kun)
Whenever Baizhang ascended the hall, there was always an old man who would follow the assembly to listen to the Dharma. When the assembly withdrew, only the old man did not leave.
The Master asked him, "Who are you? He replied, "I am not a human being. During the time of the past Kāśyapa Buddha, I once dwelt on this mountain.
Because a student asked me, 'Does one who practices the Great Way still fall under the influence of causes?'"
"Even the fruit does not exist. The man replied, "It does not fall because of cause and effect. Consequently, he fell into the body of a wild fox for five hundred lifetimes.
Now he requests the Master to provide a turning phrase on his behalf, so that he may be released from this wild fox body. The Master said, "Ask your question."
He then asked, "Does a great practitioner of the Way still fall within the realm of cause and effect, or not? The Master replied, "One does not obscure cause and effect.
Upon these words, the old man attained great enlightenment. He prostrated and said, "I have already cast off my wild fox body. I dwell behind the mountain;
I venture to request that you follow the customary rites for a deceased monk. The Master ordered the *vinaya* master to strike the gavel and announce to the assembly: "The meal is served."
Later, when they were escorting a deceased monk, the assembly was struck with wonder and amazement. After the meal, the Master led the assembly to the base of a cliff behind the mountain.
Using his staff, he pried out a dead wild fox and performed its cremation according to the Dharma. That evening, the Master ascended the hall and recounted the preceding circumstances.
Huangbo then asked, "An ancient person gave a single erroneous response; for five hundred lifetimes," he said.
"Having fallen into the body of a wild fox, turning [the wheel of Dharma] without error—what should one do? The Master said, "Come closer and I will tell you.
Baizhang stepped forward and gave the Master a slap. The Master clapped his hands and laughed, saying, "I thought the beard was red;
it turns out there is also a red-bearded barbarian! Master Lingyuan observed the various commentaries on the Wild Fox Kōan.
The discourse concludes, and he further speaks in verse:
"The luminous Way does not fall; how could the old man have ever been mistaken? The direct words are never obscured; how could Baizhang have ever understood?"
It is not that it will not be so; it is the total manifestation of wondrous enlightenment. It neither falls into extremes nor is it obscure; it stands preeminent, marking the position of correctness.
The entire mechanism of cause and effect has its origin; in its liberated essence, rising and sinking are free from all inhibition. It is neither self nor other—who, then, is it?

Under these words, those deluded by the school’s tenets give rise to conjecture. A second question and a repeated instruction are brought forth once more; observing deeply from within, wind and thunder arise.
Turning the roar of thunder with a shout against the wind, it ceases. They swallow their breath and return home, concealing their own clumsiness.
How can they show this to others on another day? Xiongpeng pierces through the autumn sky’s moon.
A painter depicts the hells, drawing out hundreds of thousands of forms. As he sets down his brush and views them from the beginning, one’s hair stands on end in sudden horror. (Baizhang Zheng)

The old man once faced the Emperor in person that day; for five hundred lifetimes he has been filled with self-reproach. Once a word has left the mouth, it is as hard to overtake as a galloping horse;
it drags Baizhang along with him in a great throng. Whether he falls or not, whether he is deluded or enlightened, he escapes Mount Sumeru only to rush toward the vast ocean.
I send these words to those practitioners who have attained great penetration: the ten directions have always been impossible to alter. (Foyin Yuan)

Neither "not being deluded" nor "not falling" are both errors. As long as grasping and rejecting are not forgotten, one is merely calculating with conscious intellect and clinging to verbal explanations;
thus, though there is no rope, one binds oneself. When all is vast and empty like the great void, where can one search? (Haiyin Xin)
Question and answer, coming and going, exhaust all causes and conditions; they have circulated throughout the world for several hundred years.
From antiquity to the present, all monastics have passed it on—one person transmits it to another. (Jingzhao Zhen)
Neither falling nor being obscured; they form herds and packs. A lion bites a man; a hunting dog chases a clod of earth.
(Da-hong En) The Great Hero once resolved the karmic cause of the wild fox; for five hundred lifetimes prior, he had fallen into error.
If you do not yet understand "neither falling nor being obscured," how many autumns and springs will pass? (Zhao-juo Zong)
Five hundred lifetimes ago he fell as a wild fox; originally, his application was far too coarse.
If even a single character can summon such retribution, how much more so when the mind-ground is further obscured? (Foji Yu)
The Great Heroic Master within the mountains of Daxiong once spoke words that liberated the wild fox;
with a single stroke of his sword, he brought peace to the ancestral state, ensuring that the smoke of war never again arose upon the path of prosperity. (The Three Imperial Ancestors)
Neither falling nor obscuring. For monks and laypeople alike, there is originally nothing to avoid. A man of spirit has a bearing like a king; why should he begrudge being covered by a sack?
With a single *zhilu* staff, he moves freely and unrestrainedly; the wild fox leaps into the ranks of the golden-haired lion. (Yuan of Dagu Ling).
Five hundred lifetimes ago they fell into this body; now, as before, they enter the red dust of the world.
Everyone they meet says, "I have retired from office," yet one has never seen a single person beneath the forest trees. (Zhenru Zhe, 2)
In the great smelting furnace, Buddhas and patriarchs are forged; once the mold has been completely cast, those who understand are at a loss.

Among the infinite heroes of the six realms, how many can truly discern the pain? To stand on the bank of the Linchuan River envying others for catching fish is not as good as returning home to weave the net. (Baofeng Xiang)
Baizhang personally saw the wild fox; for him, his inquiry was too coarse of mind. Now I dare ask all you Chan practitioners:
have you spat out all the fox’s saliva? (The withered tree becomes [the Buddha]).
Not falling and not being obscured—rely on these to enter the leather bag. Not obscured and not falling—cast both the leather bag aside.
This makes people long remember General Li: a solitary osprey soars ten thousand miles toward the heavens. (Cangtang Qing)
Ten-thousand-fathom Hongya leans against the azure void; though there be paths in the human world, none can reach it. Alas, how can a single speck of cloud be an obstacle?
It unfurls and rolls, moving freely and swift as the wind. (Doushuai Yue)
In a moment of crisis, one speaks only with partiality and barrenness; for five hundred lifetimes, one has fallen as a wild fox.
The youthful maiden has already departed into the mists of the heavens, yet the foolish lad still guards his cold furnace. (Yuantong Xian)
Han Xin gathered Qi and secretly employed his stratagems; where Siqi was cooked, all knit their brows in sorrow.
Yet in the end, he possessed a plan for his own glory—whose else could achieve such merit that would cover a generation? (Daochangru).

Deep-seated resentment is difficult to dispel; one turns from Chu only to throw oneself into Wu. One might think that because the beard is red, he must be a barbarian, yet there is yet another barbarian with a red beard.
The majestic peak sits forever alone, its vast silence presiding over the eight directions. (Huanglong Zhen)
Great wisdom, empty and luminous, penetrates both cause and fruit; with a single word, he transcends the wild fox body.
From the towering peak, one gazes toward the misty heavens, where the arrayed stars divide their radiance to honor the North Star. (Yunxi Gong)
Before the hall of Baizhang, the wild fox was tested; it was like pressing down a gourd upon water.
Now, everywhere one enters with the full functioning of the mechanism, one may well pluck the tiger’s whiskers on the spot. (Heshan Fang)
Inquiring of wild foxes north and south of the river, it is only because they are obscured by delusion that distinctions arise.
With a single step at Hongmen, the double gates swing open; who among men is not a true hero? (Shangfang Yi)
Baizhang’s Wild Fox: What of cause and effect? Before Shancai had finished his inquiry, he saw Mañjuśrī again.
(Miaoshan Xiu) Not falling into [dualistic extremes] and not being obscured—no one present could grasp this when it was applied. A single old fox has run off into the ranks of the golden-maned lions.
(Luohan Nan): Beneath Mount Dashiong, ancient paths crisscross; within Wild Fox Rock, a lion crouches upon the earth.
A wild wind sweeps away the falling remnants of flowers; only the pure fragrance remains to strike the nose. (Fuxin Cai).
Not falling into clarity, yet not obscured by intimacy; why did this old man cast off his fox’s body?
A man of spirit sharp enough to pierce the Ox and Dipper constellations—only then can one see a person who does not tremble in the face of peril. (Shushan Chang)
A transformed being comes to question one of great cultivation; at that moment, the golden probe scrapes the eyes clear.
Having turned the wild fox into Baizhang, last night it once again howled as a jackal. (Zhang Wujin)

When a fish swims, the water becomes turbid; when a bird flies, feathers fall. Nothing can escape the ultimate mirror. The great void is vast and empty; a journey of five hundred lifetimes stretches far away.

This is solely due to the great cultivation of cause and effect. Like a swift thunderclap splitting the mountains and a wind shaking the sea, gold refined a hundred times does not change its color. (Wenyu Qin)
Sleeping drunk and waking sober, he does not return home; his single body is adrift on the edge of the world.
He cannot remain within the station of the Patriarchs and Buddhas; tonight, as always, he lodges among the reeds. (Longmen Yuan)
"Not obscured" and "not falling"—how could this old man be so mistaken? "Not falling" and "not obscured"—clearly they are thus paired.
Re-raising these to show to all people: do you all understand or not? Where the level marsh ends is the green mountain;
the traveler lies even beyond the green mountain. (Wenshu said.)
To practice without falling into error or remaining in ignorance—this is entirely the rank stench of wild fox saliva and spittle. Pick up the mouth of one’s innate, impoverished state;
force open the path through the clouds and inhale the thunderclaps. (Fozhi Yu)
Not falling away from cause and effect—when has it ever fallen? Not being oblivious to cause and effect—when has it ever escaped?
When the mirror is shattered in the hall, both ends are forgotten; shadows are swept away and tracks extinguished, leaving nothing to be sought.
With nothing to seek, what reliance or support is there? The autumn wind blows through the wutong trees, and the leaves rustle, *dai dai*. (Fóxìng Tàiyī)
As soon as a single word is truly realized, one immediately sheds the body of a wild fox. Had I known early on that rain is water, I would not have made two different sounds. (Fodeng Xun)

Baizhang’s Wild Fox: His two ears stand erect and alert. To be "liberated" (tuō) is not to be obscured; to "fall" (duò) is not to be trapped. Neither obscured nor trapped—what is this? What is the error?
If you do not harbor lingering attachment to the present moment, you will stride through the vast expanse of ten-thousand-mile clear skies. (Sushan was like this.)
Baizhang and the wild fox; the wild geese blocking the way by carrying reeds; Li Guang’s divine arrow; Zhang Zhi’s cursive calligraphy. (Gushan Gui):
Not missing, yet not falling into delusion—headstones and clods of earth. Meeting on the crossroads, the silver mountains shatter to pieces.
Clapping hands and laughing aloud: In Mingzhou there is a simple "Sack of Folly. (Jingshan Gao).
"Not falling, not being oblivious"—to merely speak of "understanding" is empty talk. To know where to return upon hearing these words is to shatter the sturdy barrier. (Chuan'an Fang).
[Continued] A bright mirror stands upon its stand, yet those who look into it are few. When a Chan practitioner reaches this point, where do they intend to go?
Even if one were to point out the autumn moon, it is originally nothing but a wild fox spirit. (Langya Huijue).
Baizhang’s Wild Fox: when the words reach them, they are coarse. Tathāgata: I have my own cottage. (Cuiyan Zhen):
The path of speech is clearly present; rely on you, sir, to examine it closely. With the rain, the west wind blows fiercely; drawing near the fire, one grows colder still.
(Daowu Zhen): Not falling into the concealment of the tip, yet not being oblivious to the distinction; he wishes for him to cast off his "fox-body" from this point on.
Everyone they meet says, "I have retired from office," but in the forest below, one has never seen a single person. (Zhenjing Wen).
One foot of water, ten feet of waves. What can be done for the five hundred lifetimes prior? It is neither falling nor being oblivious;
yet one still stumbles into the thicket of entanglements as before. A-he-he! Do you understand? If you are truly free and unencumbered—
"It does not hinder me; with 'da da' and 'he he,' the divine songs and communal dances naturally form their own melodies.
Clapping hands amidst them, they sing 'li lo. (Tiantong Jue)
Spitting blood at people, first defiling their mouths; the wild fox of Bai Zhang loses its head and runs madly.
Suddenly called back, it performs a somersault—emptiness of Zongjue.
Contemplate clearly the events of five hundred lifetimes past; how could they not be clear? How could one fail to avoid intimacy?
Cause and effect are distinct and truly terrifying; everyone says it is merely a wild fox spirit. (Muan Zhong)
Whistling spring breezes stir the blooming flowers; in the gardens, leaves unfurl and blossoms open anew. Returning home, I speak in vain to my fair companion;
before the phoenix mirror, her cloud-like tresses hang askew. (By Baiyang Shun)
"Not obscured, not falling—how do you understand this? If you understand it, you will still fall as before into the wild fox’s den. One night a cool wind arises from the painted horn;
the bright moon fills the boat as it drifts upon the rivers and lakes. (By Wén of Hóngfú Monastery in Tāizhōu)
Neither obscured nor falling, taking the wrong for the right; Baizhang’s wild fox is buried all at once in a single pit. (The nun Wuzhuo Zong).
Not one who can turn back the surging waves, he merely boasts of a leviathan leaping across the sea. When Yi You draws his arrow, the monkeys on the branches are startled.
(Proclaiming the Secret Rite).
One person’s Way does not fall; one person’s Way is not obscure. Last night a sudden gale arose;
waves beat upon the stones as if they were being crushed to powder. (Zide Hui).
Holding aloft a great mass of fire, it burns through the vast void. Bodhidharma did not understand; his eyes were blind and his ears deaf. (A poisoned whip.
It has not been long since he headed for the Eastern Mountain; how many times have the roses bloomed? The white clouds disperse of their own accord; under whose house does the bright moon fall?
(Chengtang Bian): Where worldly people dwell, I do not dwell; where worldly people walk, I do not walk.
Casting my whole body into the wild fox den, I have won five hundred lifetimes of refined elegance. (Kentang Chong).
Before the hall of Baizhang, the wild fox was discerned; within the purple silk curtain, true pearls were scattered.
In whose private villa’s pond do a pair of mandarin ducks float upon the water? (Lingyan An).
"Neither falling [into error] nor being oblivious—both are mistakes. If the grasping and the relinquishing are not yet forgotten, one is calculating with conscious intellect.
Clinging to verbal explanations, one binds oneself without a rope. When spring comes the flowers bloom; when autumn arrives the leaves fall. Mistake, mistake!
Who knows that Puhua was shaking his bell? (Suzhou Dinghui Xin)
Moving the mouth gives rise to thorns; shifting the body leads to falling as a wild fox. Zhaozhou comes to compete in wealth;
a gourd hangs on the eastern wall. (Oran’s essence).
"Not falling" and "not being obscured" are the crime of slandering others; "not being obscured" and "not falling" are binding oneself without a rope.
Pity the willow catkins following the spring breeze—sometimes they go west, sometimes they go east. (Safong Yin)
Neither falling nor deluded, toppling eastward and tumbling westward; the iron walls and silver mountains are all at once pulverized.
Neither deluded nor falling, moreover, there is no contrived effort. Truly, these words are not learned from others. (Guan Yue-lin, 2)
Neither obscured nor falling; error, error, error, error. Neither falling nor obscured; no, no, no, no. Sitting and attaining great peace;
truly difficult to grasp.
Having fallen away, one knows where to be liberated; rely on the gentleman to examine this closely. When the tide comes, there is no separate inlet;
when the leaves fall, other mountains are revealed. (Tianmu Li)
Falling into the body of a fox, then shedding that fox-body; leaves fall and flowers bloom through many springs. Fame and profit follow only the mounted traveler;
right and wrong do not reach the fisherman. (By Master Pogu Xian).
An old fox-spirit beneath Mount Daxiong has vexed the monastic communities for a thousand ages.
If she encounters a cub of the golden-maned lion, see how she will have nowhere to hide her entire body. (Shi’an Shao)
Baizhang’s wild fox; the stone woman without a husband. Once a tear falls, the vast ocean dries up. (Shuai’an Cong):
Not falling, not being oblivious—two prizes, one match. Not oblivious, not falling—a thousand errors, ten thousand mistakes. (Wumen Kai).
"Not falling into cause and effect" — the wild fox emerges. A human heart is like iron; the laws of the state are like a furnace.
"Not being ignorant of cause and effect" — one attains liberation from the wild fox. No bone upon the crown, whiskers beneath the chin. (Xu Tang Yu).
[Added from another source: Once, while Baizhang was working in the fields with the community, a monk heard the sound of the meal drum;
he raised his hoe, let out a great laugh, and returned to the monastery. The Master said, "How extraordinary! This is the gate through which Avalokiteśvara enters the principle.
Upon returning to the hall, he summoned the monk and asked, "What principle did you perceive just now that caused you to act in such a manner? The monk replied, "Just now—"
Hearing the sound of the drum, he moved to go back and eat his meal. The Master then smiled. (The verse says:
Who would say the intent lies at the edge of the hoe? A single strike pierces through the Great Thousandfold World.
After laughing heartily and bowing his head to depart, Eat your hunger when you must; do not pass it on to others. (Shui-an Yi)
A single tune before the wind stirs the sorrow of parting. Which traveler would not lift their head?
Holding a branch of flowers to half-conceal her face, she is all the more elegant that she does not let others see her. (Wuzhun Shanfu)
Heaven has fashioned this iron Kunlun; his wit and skill allow him to enter the sea-gate.
Having gathered up countless rare treasures, he returns empty-handed to exchange greetings of warmth. (By Jianweng Jing)
[Added from the Supplementary Collection: Once, a woman (the *Lian deng lu* records it as a monk) came weeping into the Dharma Hall. Baizhang asked, "What are you doing?"

The woman said, "Both my parents have passed away; I request that the Master choose an auspicious day. The Master said, "Come tomorrow, and we shall bury them all at once. The verse says: Both parents have perished; the daughter requests a date. The Master says, "Come tomorrow, and bury them all at once."
Sitting atop Baizhang Mountain is not far away; beneath the mountain, women wail and lament. All at once they are buried in the cool, refreshing earth;
only through supreme filial piety can one transcend both past and present. (Fenyang Zhao)
This principle clearly answers those who instruct others: when both parents have passed away, one turns deeply toward the Master.
Though it is said that the lamp is divided to transmit the True Dharma, it is only when they are buried all at once that one truly honors them. (Yanshou Hui)
