Last night Samantabhadra fought with Mañjuśrī; chasing him out was like removing both hands at once. Yet it is said that Zhaozhou exercised his true authority;
from this point on, the old Wang has vanished all at once. (Foyin Yuan)
Within the shadows of multicolored clouds, an immortal appears. Holding a red silk fan in his hand, he shields his face. No one casts an eye to look at the immortal;
they instead gaze at the red silk fan following behind him. (Fujian Yongqin)
The embroidered mandarin ducks are peerless in this world; yet even a master hand is surpassed by one even stronger. Having displayed their work, each returns to the fragrant chamber;
the golden needle is difficult to grasp as they pass by Xiao Lang. (Fodeng Xun)

[Continued Collection]: Both are not yet resolved. Regardless of how much or how little [of the path] one has traversed, even if one travels by night, one will not reach the destination until dawn breaks. (Yuet Tang Chang)
Mist rises and dragons roar; wind stirs and tigers howl. Two mouths, one tongue—different sounds, a single melody. This is the vision of the Buddhadharma of Mañjuśrī and Samantabhadra;

it is the face of Nanyuan and Zhaozhou, like the sun and moon. Acting according to the command, in the space of a glance, they cast everything down with full intent into the Iron Ring Mountains. (Yuánwù Qín)
The cloth drum is set before the hall to be struck; the Sleeping Dragon, startled, rises from his mountain crags. Who can capture the exquisite beauty of the thousand peaks?
A single stretch of clear river opens like an ancient mirror. (Wuan Quan)
This thief recognizes a thief; this spirit recognizes a spirit. Nanquan had no fault other than being overly alert. Zhaozhou bowed and returned to the hall.
"The first arrow was still light; the second arrow went deep. (Shi’an Shao)
The spring breeze blows down the emerald peach blossoms; a single petal flows past a hundred thousand homes.
Who is at the painted tower where wine is bought? They invite one to come and drink Zhaozhou’s tea. (Shigumi)

[Added for inclusion] Once Nanquan arrived at a manor, the master of the estate had prepared a reception in advance. The Master said, "I, this old monk, usually enter or leave without letting anyone know.
How is it that you have made such preparations? The master of the estate replied, "Last night the local deity (tudi) reported that the Master would come today.
The Master said, "Wang Laoshi’s cultivation of the Way lacks power; he was [caught by the deity]."
A spirit saw him. An attendant then asked, "Since you, Master, are a *kalyāṇamitra* (a good spiritual friend), why were you seen by a spirit?

The Master said, "Offer another portion of rice before the local deity (*dizhu*). Xuanjue said, "Where is it that one offers another portion of rice before the local deity? Yunju Xi said: [The Master said: "Offer another portion of rice before the local deity. Xuanjue asked:
"Where is it that one offers another portion of rice before the local deity? Yunju Xi said: [He then recited: "If you wish to know the Buddha’s meaning, / Just look at the present moment."
This is to reward him and this is to punish him. It is just as seen before the Earth Deity Hall: Is it Nanquan? Is it not Nanquan? The verse says:
A portion of rice before the Earth Deity’s hall, Was sought only for the sake of providing for one's mouth that year. The year of one's life falls upon the *kan* hexagram; the ghost has arrived.
Shen: I respectfully advise the Chan practitioner to cease their praise.
(Daryuanzhi) To plant flowers upon a rock is exceptionally wondrous; the spring colors upon the branches are subtly fragrant.
Their scent pervades the world, yet no one smells it; let the wild winds blow them as they will. (Iyanquan)
[Added for inclusion] Nanquan said, "In Jiangxi, Mazu says 'This very mind is Buddha. I, Old Wang, do not speak thus;
I say, 'It is not mind, it is not Buddha, it is not a thing. In speaking thus, is there any fault?
Zhaozhou bowed and departed. A monk followed him and asked, "Master, you bowed and then left immediately—what was your intention?"
"How is it? [The Master] said, "You should ask the Abbot instead. A monk asked the Master, "What was the meaning of that statement by Abbot Shen just now?
The Master said, "He indeed grasped my meaning. Verse: How is it? You should ask the Abbot instead. What was the meaning of that statement by Abbot Shen? He indeed grasped my meaning.
"It is not mind, nor is it matter. Nanda enters the blue dragon’s cave at night;
with his iron whip, he shatters the bright moon pearl, leaving the great earth as if smeared with ink. (Xuedou Zong)
Deep, deep, drawing from the wellsprings of antiquity; shallow, shallow, all is manifest as it is. The water is as clear as a jade pitcher; the river is as limpid as white silk.
Leaping out of the three-tiered waves of peach blossoms, he wears horns and holds his head high, seizing the opportunity with swift ease.
As for the fish with the branded forehead—under Mazu’s mouth, he stands in vain hesitation. (Yuǎnwù Qín)
In the ancient buddha-field, no spears were raised; later men stubbornly gave rise to clamor and dispute. When the Way is prosperous, the imperial decree is not transmitted;
when the times are clear, there is no need to sing songs of great peace. (Longmen Yuan)
Lifting up the whisk, he traveled thirty thousand miles; right now, he has rested for eight thousand years.
I shall clearly raise this from the beginning once more, leaving it for all quarters to transmit as they please. (Gushan Gui)
I turn my belly and pour out my guts to tell you: I do not know what it is that still leaves you lingering in hesitation. Now is the very moment to seize it with fierce resolve;
hand it over to those in the world who have nothing to do. (Jingshan Gaofeng)
The old barbarian king from the southern border of Vajra, wearing his robe backward, entered the Great Tang. He sold all his sandalwood ox-heads;
only his nostrils remained hanging, not tucked away in a pouch. (Zhengtang Bian)
Mind, Buddha, and phenomena—none are real. Severs the tongue and eliminates all medicinal taboos. Grasping horizontally or using upside down, it is entirely up to him;
he captures the hordes of demons alive and pierces their noses. (Nanyuan Sheng)
Not mind, not Buddha, not a thing—a whole body of golden chain bones.
Zhaozhou met the old Nanquan; he could say, "Zhengzhou produces radishes. (Wu Yuanzhao)
"It is not mind, not Buddha, not a thing. (Striking the meditation seat with the whisk) "For you, I shatter the lair of the vital spirit.
Whether known in heaven or on earth, the nostrils remain as before, starkly protruding. (Shui'an Yan)
It is not mind, not Buddha, and not an object. Six times six, based on the previous, makes thirty-six. Reflecting on this, I think of Grand Master Lu Changqing;
he knew how to say that one ought to laugh and not weep. (Nun Wuzhuo Zong).
The three peaks of Mount Hua pierce the azure sky; at their summit there is no path by which to climb.
I know not who possesses the hands of an immortal to pluck the ten-fathom lotus from the peak. (Kaishan Jian)
Hungry ghosts whip corpses; immortals pay homage to withered bones. Wild dogs howl at desolate mounds; iron mountains stand stark and solitary.
Throughout the six realms, the myriad spirits vie to raise their heads; one knows not where their nests and lairs may be. (Or: the essence of the hermitage).
How many know how to turn their bellies over and empty their entrails? There is not even a hair’s breadth left upon which to rely.
Even if one were to accept this thoroughly, it still falls into the second gear of that other house. (Lingyan).
Protruding and difficult to discern, yet discerned; the lion turns over in the lion’s den. With one roar, heaven and earth are emptied;
Mount Sumeru is startled into a towering prominence. (Yuelin Guan)
With the head shaved, the head shines; with the feet washed, the feet feel refreshed. Stripping off clothes to sleep upon the bed, one scratches the entire body for its itchiness. (Xue’an Jin)
"Not mind, not Buddha, not thing. Having exhausted the drool of the wild fox, he kicks over the mountain ghost’s den.
From within the level fields and shallow grasses, he reveals the tawny-tailed tiger; amidst the vast emptiness of the great void, he releases the magnificent falcon soaring through the heavens.
A-he-he! Exposing his wind-bone, he casually draws it forth before the multitude. Ultimately, what exactly is this?
Object. *Du du*. (Dun-ān’s Pearl).
The whale drinks the seawater until it is exhausted, revealing the coral branches. The Sea God knows its preciousness but not its price;
he leaves it for the human world to illuminate the night. (Pak Ong-hyeon).
Accustomed to playing the jade zither and the pipa, their clear notes resound clearly throughout the reaches of the world. It is lamentable that they do not enter the ears of the deaf;
in vain, the moon over the Western Mountains has once again slanted down. (Xian’an Guan)

The Master did not recognize characters; Bodhidharma did not understand Chan. In the kingdom of the Great Tang Emperor, the transformation of three thousand disciples continues as before. (Songyuan Yue)
After his karma was shattered and his house destroyed, where could his entire body find rest? Holding upside-down a flute with no holes, he blew it across the Bay of Muzi. (Ruan Yong)
It is not mind, Buddha, or things. To open one’s mouth is already to fall into error. If you intend to ask further how it is, I shall spit right in your face. (Kill Rokan E.)
It is not mind, nor is it matter. A white-headed man gives birth to a black-headed hawk.
Having seen through the mounting platform before the gate, his entire body breaks into a cold sweat as black as ink. (Peng’an’s Assembly)

the face is unwashed and the head is unwrapped. (Baoning Yong)

Once, when the monks of the East and West Halls were disputing over a cat, Master Nanquan encountered them.
He addressed the assembly, saying, "If you can speak [the truth], I shall save the cat; if you cannot, I shall kill it. The assembly was speechless. The Master then killed it.
When Zhaozhou returned from outside, the Master presented him with the previous account. Zhaozhou then took off his straw sandals, placed them on his head, and departed.
He placed it on his head and went out. The Master said, "If you had been here just now, you could have saved the cat.
He then offered this verse:
"The two abbots in the hall were not yet blind; Each claimed the cat, and I must fight for it. Nanquan cuts it in two with a single stroke."
The hand. Leaving the straw sandals for those who come after. (Fenyang Zhao). Both halls are filled with Chan monks;
they stir up dust and smoke, and there is nothing that can be done. Fortunately, Nanquan was able to issue the command;
with one stroke he cuts it in two, regardless of bias or partiality. (Xuedou Xian, 2)

Holding the wildcat by its ears, one settles life and death; Zen practitioners vainly cause their mouths to contend.

Lifting up both halls, one should see them clearly; grasping the blade, one must seize the living cat. Alas, there is no blood beneath the skin;

The wildcat, in the stillness of night, stretches itself wide; extending its paw over its head, it reveals its long claws.
Having finished patrolling the old king’s chamber, it scurries out in haste, fearing the light of day.
The snow-blade contains light that shoots toward the Dipper and Ox; not only do Heaven, Earth, ghosts, and spirits grieve.
The life-root falls into Nanquan’s hand; look directly beneath—both parts are finished. (Baoning Yong, 2)
The cat’s horns have grown back anew; the old Wang walks alone by night before his gate. Dawn breaks and he knows not where he has gone;
the boundless peaks of Mount Chu stand in vain majesty.
A single stroke, two pieces—Nanquan’s command. Directly facing him, he set up Zhaozhou’s barrier.
Had there not been the Eye of the Patriarch before one's face, it would have followed the flowing water back down to the human world. (Zhaojue Zong)
Where the smoke of the wolf-signs rises, observe the military strategy; were it not for the General, who could discern it? With two sections and one blade, he issues his commands at the battlefield;
his majestic prestige is the foundation of a hegemonic hero for a thousand ages. (Yuantong Xian)
Failing to recognize the opportunity, his eyes are as if dull; how could he discern it when the sharp edge has not yet been revealed?
At sunset, he walks off with his straw sandals upon his head, clapping his hands in secret laughter. (Like a withered tree.)

how could the golden blade from its scabbard ever be wielded recklessly? (Luo Han Nan)
The strings of Boya can be mended with phoenix-glue; the tunes are ancient and the style pure—frosty moonlight can be gathered in one's palms.
Nanquan, Nanquan! The dragon-elephants continue his footsteps. (Fuxincai, 2)
Wearing straw sandals on his head, with whom would he debate? When the four seas are windless, the waves subside of their own accord.
If one understands that when the music ends, the person is no longer seen, one will find only a few peaks of green at the river’s edge.
The five-colored marten strives with all its might; yet when the sword is drawn, all are born blind.
Dividing itself into two parts to act for one another, it truly causes the wind of sorrow to stir the earth. (Longmen Yuan, 2)

Only you, General, are permitted to establish Great Peace.
One must have the wildcat meet face-to-face to repay; it is as if the mouth were clamped shut and the throat locked.
With a single stroke, you must decide between life and death; this truly stirs a wind of sorrow that shakes the earth. (Fodeng Xun, 2)
The tavern before the hall sells its wares anew; within the house, Yangzhou excels all that is sought abroad.
With straw sandals upon his head and a lofty stride, even the scenery of late spring is full of elegance.

If there were no worthy son to offer the price, the spring would often pass in vain year after year. (Baoning Yong)
[Continued Collection] Neither noble nor base; high and low are separated by a single thread.
When benefit and harm are clearly explained to people, do the clever monks see it or not? (Ding of Daichang)
Nanquan, along with Guizong and Magu, went together to pay their respects to National Teacher Nanyang.
First, on the road, Nanquan drew a circle and said, "If you can say something, then we shall go. Guizong sat down within the circle;
Magu performed a woman’s bow. The Master said, "In that case, we shall not go. Guizong asked, "What kind of mind is this?"
As they were about to depart, the Master called out to them both, saying, "Do not go to pay your respects to the National Teacher.
Xuanjue asked, "Regarding Nanquan’s speaking in this manner, was it a word of approval or a word of disapproval?
Yunju Xi said, "Previously they were going to pay their respects to the National Teacher; why did Nanquan instead call them back? Tell me, what did the ancients mean?"
"What do you think? He recited this verse:
The National Teacher wished to see many aspects of the meaning; Sitting upright and composed, he invited [the assembly] to look. Without departing, they heard it with one voice and understood;
Having long served in the ranks, they seized the banners and flags. (Fenyang Shanzhao)
When the base arrow shot at the monkey, why did it circle the tree so straight? Of the thousands and tens of thousands, who has ever hit the mark?
Calling out to one another, come back home; do not climb the path of Caoxi. He further said:
"The path of Caoxi is level and plain; why then must you refrain from climbing? (Xuedou Xian).
When three people walk together, there will surely be someone among them who can serve as my teacher. I shall choose what is good in them and follow it;
I shall take what is not good in them and reform myself accordingly. (Cuiyan Zhen)
Three companions went together to select an official. They happened upon a night of clear wind and bright moon. Sometimes chanting, sometimes composing verse, or playing the lute;
though the night grew still and the watches deepened, they did not yet depart. Suddenly they realized it was dawn, so they returned home.
In time, there will surely be those who understand them. (Haiyin Xin)
Vast expanse of earth, snow piled a foot deep; rivers and lakes are one, impossible to distinguish. The fisherman, clad in his straw raincoat, returns under the moonlight.
Who says that for the traveler at night, the road is cut off? (Bao-ning Yong)
The three men prostrated and departed for Nanyang; halfway along the road they withdrew their bodies, yet the message had already been delivered.
There is no need to discuss east or west, north or south; this mind is of one accord across a thousand li. (Cao Tang Qing)
Skillful artistry surpasses the bold grasp; in vain do they toil and suffer. Who can distinguish between the distant and the near within this?
Fallen flowers and fragrant grasses fill the diverging paths; amidst fine rain and slanting winds, no person is seen. (Min Gufo)
"Take care, Nanyang; all is well. Three men returning from halfway shall not return empty-handed. Though the Way exists in direct perception, there are still many matters;
if you meet one who understands, please bring it forth. (Yunyan, because of this).
Those of like nature seek one another; this matter is worth discussing. A single meeting brings forth a surge of joy.
Where could two lines of verse be found idly? Who among us are not good brothers? (Longmen Yuan)
In the same pit there is no different soil; throughout the ages few have known this. Cease calling out to one another under the moon;
return instead by the old path. (Kai Fu Ning)
Nanquan, Magu, and Guizong— Their eyes of the Way were originally not fully penetrating.
They went to pay respects to the National Teacher to behold his physical marks, Yet their petty efforts reached only halfway. (Sushan Ru)
[Continued Collection] Carrying a hand-held flower drum, he reaches the foot of the city wall; wearing his hemp sandals backward, he passes through the narrow gate.
Smiling, he writes ancient characters upon pieces of firewood; everyone comes to walk under the moon at dusk. (By Yuet Tang Chang)
At a roadside inn after the midday meal, I briefly ask for directions. The master’s bamboo staff is always by his side.
Everyone they meet says, "I am going to retire from office," yet among those in the forest, one has never been seen. (Nun Wuzhuo Zong).
The breath is direct, the speech is direct; the eyes are intimate, the hands are intimate. The peaks and ridges vie for beauty; red and purple flowers compete for spring.
Though the wondrous functions of spiritual powers are fully displayed, if you wish to see the National Teacher, you are still separated by a ford. (Qian’an Ren).
A golden needle embroiders jade mandarin ducks; the stone woman holds them forth without concealment.
Just as the wooden man casts a sidelong glance, they remain paired yet never become a couple. (Wan’an Rou)
Each takes their capital to engage in business; the imperial capital is like heaven, where one must seize the fair weather. Before even stepping out the gate, they first calculate their accounts;
how can they ever reach the City of the Phoenix? (Xutang Yu)
Who is it sitting in the center of the circular image? The Master and the Lady each present their wits through a prostration.
The National Teacher’s Way pervades the world; ordinary people are not permitted to know it. (Xiangchuan Hong)

[Added from another collection] While Nanquan was enjoying the moon, Zhaozhou pointed at the moon and asked, "When did you come to be like this? The Master said, "I, Old Teacher Wang, was also like this twenty years ago.

Zhaozhou asked, "How about right now? The Master then returned to his quarters. The verse says: The moon is bright, the water is clear; The ancient path is vast and wide. Twenty years ago, he came this way; Right now, where has he gone?
He returns to the abbot’s quarters— A single hand clapping in the empty sky.
The sword falls into the cold pool; vainly one carves marks upon the boat. Frosty flowers and rushing waves bring sorrow to the heart.
If one were to rely on words to debate high and low, one would only win Nanquan’s silent response. (The Venerable Tiger Head).
Zhaozhou held forth the rhombus-patterned mirror; Old Wang personally took up the white jade mallet.
With one strike in the presence of all, the tiles were shattered. How many can truly know this mind? How many know it? Two are clearly the "Red Eyebrows.
Displaying their family’s shame before the wind and moon, they make the ancient adept of Vulture Peak laugh to tears. (Cishou Shen)
The bright moon, full and round, shines beautifully in the azure sky; Old Wang of Zhaozhou enjoys it before his steps.
The hearts and eyes of these two men are alike; their radiance has always been perfectly shared. (Benjue I)
The sword falls into the cold pond; vainly one carves marks upon the boat. Frost-flakes and surging waves bring sorrow to the heart. The old fisherman ceases his casting and returns to the deep cove;
a pair of mandarin ducks alight at the river crossing. (Shangfangyue)
[Added for inclusion] Once Zhaozhou asked Nanquan, "The Way is not outside of things; that which is outside of things is not the Way.
What is the Way outside of things? Nanquan struck him. Zhaozhou seized the staff and said, "Do not strike people wrongly in the future.

Nanquan said, "It is easy to distinguish dragons from snakes, but difficult to deceive a patch-robed monk" (the *Lian deng lu* differs slightly from this version, stating: "The Way is not outside of things; that which is outside of things is not...").

Zhaozhou went out and asked, "What is the Way beyond things? The Master struck him. Zhaozhou seized the staff and said, "Master, do not strike me; you will strike the wrong person in the future. The Master threw down the staff and said, "It is easy to distinguish dragons from snakes, but it is difficult to deceive a patch-robed monk. The verse says: A single blow, and the matter is settled; The Way is not found in words or phrases. If you wish to see the ancient one, Look at the staff in his hand. The staff is like a dragon or a snake— How can anyone deceive him? If you wish to know the true meaning, Observe the staff as it falls. With a supple grip, he conceals his edge as he enters the fray; he brings them all down with a wide-eyed stare. A hero who decides life and death in a single stroke;
a talent for both civil and military, a general and a minister combined. (Baoning Yong)

Dragons and snakes can be easily distinguished; it is the patch-robed monks who are most difficult to deceive. Their nature is as pure as the vast autumn sky; their minds are as expansive as the great ocean.

At the ends of the earth, they perceive even the finest hair-tip; they view the entire world within the palm of their hand. With the myriad dharmas as no companions, they drink the Western River dry in a single gulp.
(Nantang Xing). [Added by Zeng] When Nanquan was staying in a hermitage, a monk arrived at the hut. The Master said to the monk, "I am going up the mountain.
Wait until mealtime; prepare some rice, eat it yourself, and then send a portion up to the mountain. After a short while...
The monk finished eating by himself, then suddenly smashed all his household goods and lay down on the bed. The Master waited for him to come out;
when he did not see him return, he went back and saw the monk lying there. The Master also went to one side and lay down. The monk then got up and left.
After the Master had taken up residence there, he said: "When I previously lived in the hermitage, there was a clever practitioner who has not been seen until this very day. The verse says:
The hair-cutting sword is sharp; the waves against the current are clear. The ambition of a man of honor does not follow common sentiment.
You march north to the frontier; I strike west toward Qin. For ten thousand ages, may we together enjoy peace and prosperity. (Nantang Xing)
Short trousers, long shirts, and white ramie turbans; with a creaking sound, they hurriedly push their wheels beneath the moon.
Meeting them on the streets of Luoyang, they are all merchants engaged in trade. (Xutang Yu)
To use a machine to kill cats is not considered an excessive act; it is still far better than beating a rice-pot in the kitchen. As soon as one harbors such a mind, one invites such retribution.
What can a wicked person do against another wicked person? (From *Bao-ye-yuan*).

[Added for inclusion] Nanquan said to a presiding master (zuozhu), "Can you lecture on the sutras for me? The master replied, "The Master explains Chan for me; I shall lecture on the sutras for the Master.
The Master said, "One must not trade golden pellets for silver pellets. Verse: Nanquan’s golden pellet Is worth ten thousand pieces of gold.
If you wish to exchange it for silver, You will find yourself short by half a cent.

The ball rolls upon the platter, and the platter rolls the ball. When the opportune moment arrives, one should cast aside all artifice and contemplate the "desire for life. Though people of the world know it is precious, they do not know its value;
yet to pick it up with the hand as it comes is no difficult matter. (Zhengtang Bian)

Nanquan was once asked by a monk, "After the Master passes away, where will you go? The Master said, "I shall become a water buffalo on the mountain below. The monk said, "If I follow the Master there, will I be able to do so as well?
The Master said, "If you would follow me, you must bring back a blade of grass in your mouth. The verse says: When the hundred-year mark arrives, he becomes a water buffalo;

If you wish to follow him, you must first grasp a blade of grass. If you can truly understand this, you will see that the path is not far; If you cannot yet comprehend it, you remain lost in the world of birth and death.
It is difficult to discern within categories; one must be clear and distinct. Wearing horns and shedding hair, one has not yet awakened. Only when taking up grass in the mouth does one finally move;
every head and every thing is itself true and numinous. (Fenyang Shanzhao)
His conduct has always been among the heterodox; one knows not with whom his horns may match.
If we meet when he is chewing water and grass, he will wag his tail and shake his head like the wind across the four wilds. (Foyin Yuan)
Moving freely among those of different kinds, though one’s nostrils are pulled through, it is difficult to restrain him.
When he catches a blade of grass in his mouth at the place of encounter, he lies high upon the deep clouds, letting his hair turn white. (Fohuiquan)
While Nanquan was cutting thatch on the mountain, a monk asked, "Master, where does the road to Nanquan lead?
The Master picked up his sickle and said, "I bought this sickle for thirty coins.
The monk said, "I am not asking about this; where does the road to Nanquan lead? The Master replied, "I use it."
The swiftest. The verse says:
The scythe of reeds makes its work as swift as the wind; With thirty copper coins, a great feat is accomplished. Nanquan’s upward path is difficult to reach;
Only those who reach it know that everywhere is permeable. (Zhaojue Zong)
Thirty coins bought a bundle of reeds; held high before one’s face, it is the first tally.
If you know the path back directly beneath, you must still ascend another floor. (Yuantong Xian, 2)
Tearing through the grass to observe the wind, one probes the Zen of the Patriarchs; who would have known that within the weeds lies Nanquan? Clearly, this single phrase is free from private intent;
a piercing wind arises, and heaven and earth grow cold.
The King’s true mechanism is swift as the wind; who can penetrate the skillful means he reveals to people?
When the scythe of thatch is raised, the divine blade is exposed, startling the earthen ox as it crosses the sea to the East. (Zhikaiqing)
When asked for directions, he points out the way with clarity; thirty *qingfu* coins are not a light recompense.
When used, it is swiftest and requires no artifice; these flavorless words block the flow of the masses. (Zhenru Zhe)
This sickle of mine is used with great speed; it was bought for thirty coins at that time.
Under Nanquan’s gate, the paths diverge; I send word to the travelers: take heed! (Tiantong Jue).
A hurried Chan practitioner asked Nanquan: "The weary horse labors in vain as the whip is struck down hard; today for your sake I shall reveal it once more:
the solitary wild goose flies lightly down across the distant sky. (The Dharma Hall is like this.)
[Added from the Supplementary Collection] Nanquan said: "The Buddhas of the three periods do not know that there is; the cat and the white ox, however, do know that there is.
The verse says:
"Drinking the official wine, lying on the official street— Die where you are, be buried where you are. Countless heroes upon the battlefield," [are piled up].
Mountains piled high and peaks laid bare with corpses—(Daowei Zhi).
The Buddhas of the three periods do not know they exist; each one faces south and gazes at the Big Dipper. The cat and the white ox, however, do know they exist;
they wear horns, lift up their heads, and roar like lions. Their four corners collapse to the ground, yet they remain perfectly round; the eight-cornered millstone is empty.
Running inside, he intended to search for him, but was seized by the spine and dragged away; he caught hold of the nostrils but lost his mouth. I ask:
how does Puhua’s one-headed donkey compare to Zihu’s single dog? (Yuánwù Qín).
The Buddhas of the three periods do not know he exists; old and decrepit, he wanders abroad. His eyelids cover all five Mount Sumerus;
he performs somersaults within the great ocean. (Jingshan Gaofeng Yuanmiao, No. 2)
The wildcat and the white ox, however, truly know: the waterfall does not flow, the green mountains run. How laughable is the senseless Old Master Wáng;
he mistakes a winnowing basket for an ironing board.
The southern bird nests on the southern branch; the Hu horse whinnies in the north wind. The tabby cat and the white ox—inch by inch, they never pass one another.
Ten thousand mountains are completely cut off; ten thousand streams all flow toward the east. As soon as the Heavenly King joins his palms, Nātha strikes the imperial bell.

(Whether it be the essence of the hermitage,) the village elder sacrificing to the river god, or the beggar performing somersaults—do not view these as two different things; they are equally exposing the family’s disgrace.
(Village Elder Xian). [Added from another collection.
Nanquan, Luzu, Shanshan, and Guizong—these four left Mazu’s place and each went to dwell in a hermitage.
At the place where they parted ways on the road, the Master planted his staff in the ground and said, "If you can speak, you are hindered by this;
if you cannot speak, you are also hindered by this. Guizong dragged the staff and struck the Master once, saying:
"It is just this very thing. Master Wang said, "What do you mean by 'obstructed' and 'unobstructed'?
Luzu said, "This single phrase alone spreads throughout the world. Zong said, "Is there anything that does not spread? Luzu said, "There is."
Zong asked, "What is it that does not scatter? The Patriarch made a gesture with his palm. The verse says:

Those of the same gate are called companions; those of the same aspiration are called friends. Sharing the same gate and the same aspiration, they keep each other's company from beginning to end; yet when they grow up, they part ways.
One attains the conditions of both the beautiful and the ugly; all know that we are born from the same root. All know that we die from the same root—who else knows this?
One clear phrase spreads throughout the world; these flavorless words block the mouths of men. (Great Perfect Wisdom).
A difficult elder brother and a difficult younger brother—numbered one, two, three, and four—they were born of the same mother, each exactly alike.

Carrying their staffs and wood wherever they go, they perform their play upon meeting the stage. Do not say they are obstructed or blocked; with a single phrase, they spread throughout heaven and earth. (Fujian Qín)
Obstructed and unobstructed: when the dragon roars, the mist rises. Spread and not spread: the fly clings to the horse's tail.
North, south, east, and west—thousands of miles, ten thousand leagues. How magnificent! (The Manifestation of Perfect Enlightenment).
[Added from another source] Once, while Nanquan was inspecting the hall, he led a cow into the hall.
The Head Seat struck the cow on its back once with his hand, and the Master (Nanquan) immediately stopped. Zhaozhou then took two bundles of straw and placed them before the Head Seat.
The verse says:
Providing fodder and grass equally, you look after them well; why then must their hide and fur be uniform?
By provoking those who seek conformity within the herd, you cause their horns and heads to remain incomplete. (From *Bǎoyèyuán*)

[Added for inclusion: Nanquan visited Baizhang. Baizhang asked, "Where have you come from? The Master said, "From Jiangxi. Baizhang said, "Have you brought the portrait of Great Master Ma with you? The Master said, "This very one is it. Baizhang said, "What about the one behind him?
The Master shook his sleeves and departed. The Verse says: Nanquan came from Jiangxi; He brought the portrait of the Great Master. When asked about the one behind, He shook his sleeves and left.
The true man has no fixed abode; He does not linger in the marketplace. If you wish to see the Buddha’s countenance, Look at the face of the one who departs.
Facing the wind from eight directions—this is it alone. A single word of shaking the sleeves moves heaven and earth.
How admirable is Old Teacher Wanshi, who sells himself for neither cheap nor dear. (Longmen Yuan)
The elder brother is difficult; the younger brother is difficult. Mazu’s true essence is just this:
shaking the eighteen rapids of the West River, waves arise spontaneously upon the water though there is no wind. (Shixi Yue)
[Added from another source] Once Zhaozhou asked Nanquan, "Does it accord with the bright side, or does it accord with the dark side? Nanquan immediately returned to his quarters.
When Zhaozhou went before the Sangha hall, he said, "The old fellow at the head of the hall was rendered speechless by my single question.
The Head Seat said, "Do not say the Master had nothing to say; it is simply that you, Elder, do not understand. Zhaozhou then—
Zhengzhang said: "This blow was originally meant for the old man of the Hall to eat. Wuzu Jie said: "The real thief has run away;
the patrolman eats the blows. He also said: "Nanquan should have made the decision; instead, he invited the chaos."
The Verse says:
The Great Matter stands revealed before one, already as clear as day; Yet it must be made ten times more perfectly complete. The Head Seat in the hall is black as lacquer;
For whose sake does he take this "dark blow" on a cold spot? (Baoning Yong)
[Added by Later Editors] Nanquan addressed the assembly, saying: "Since my youth, I have raised a water buffalo.
If I intend to pasture it on the east bank of the stream, I cannot avoid consuming the king’s water and grass;
if I pasture it on the west bank, I likewise cannot avoid consuming the king’s water and grass. Now, I can do no other than accept things as they come, yet I see nothing at all."
Yes. The verse says:
"Whether going east of the stream or west of the stream, one cannot escape the official taxes on the seedlings.
Even if you provide your share of the tribute as best you can, you have not yet learned how to lead the ox wherever it stays. (Yang Woei-wei)
Hanging low, the willows darken the head of the stream; Whether east or west, one is nonetheless free. Several times I have slept drunk upon the backs of oxen;
A few notes of the transverse flute, a single wheel of autumn. (Lan’an Shu)
The Water-Ox of Nanquan is naturally so; according to his lot, he undergoes whatever changes may come. With one great laugh, heaven and earth grow narrow;
there is no further Buddha-dharma to transmit to others. (Yuelin Guan)
Not letting go of the east or west of the stream, accepting a little according to one's lot; cold and warmth are known only by oneself—clearly, to whom could this be told? (Mukan Egen)
At Nanquan, the Water Ox forgets the whip and halter; north, south, east, and west are all one family. The royal tax has been paid in full and on time;
the cowherd plays his flute as the distant mountains slant away. (Tianmu Li)
It is better to accept a little according to one's capacity. To call this an ordinary matter is already an error. Amidst green grass by the stream, horns and head are revealed;
in the misty rain, to whom does that single straw raincoat belong? (Iron Ox Seal).
[Added for inclusion] One day, while serving at a meal, Nanquan personally took a tray of raw vegetables to the head seat.
At that time, Master Shanshan Jian was serving as the head seat; he said, "Non-arising. The Master replied, "Non-arising is still the secondary.
Just as the Master had taken a few steps, the head seat called out, "Venerable Sir! Venerable Sir! The Master looked back.
[The Master] asked, "What is it? The Seat-holder said, "Do not say that 'no-birth' (wu-sheng) is merely secondary.

The Verse says: "The ancient masters patrol the hall and personally groom the living; Crossing waters and rowing boats is no easy task as plowing fields. Do not say that 'no-birth' is still secondary;
If even a hair’s breadth is not resolved, confusion runs rampant. (Zhimen Zu)
[Added for inclusion] Nanquan asked a lecture master, "What sutra do you preach? He replied, "The *Sutra on Maitreya’s Descent to Be Born in the World*.
The Master said, "When will Maitreya descend to be born? He replied, "He is currently in the heavenly palace; he has not yet come.
The Master said, "There is no Maitreya in heaven, and there is no Maitreya on earth. Dongshan raised this question to Yunju, who said, "In heaven..."
"There is no Maitreya. There is no Maitreya beneath the earth. I do not know who gave him his name. When Dongshan was thus questioned, his meditation seat shook;
he then said, "When I was at Yunyan, I once asked the Old Man [Nanquan], and my brazier shook. Today, being questioned by you, my whole body breaks into a sweat. The verse says: There is no Maitreya;

there is no Maitreya beneath the earth. Who could have given him this name? Dongshan was so shaken by the question That his meditation seat trembled. He said, "At Yunyan, I once asked the Old Man, And my brazier shook. Today, being questioned by you, My entire body breaks into a sweat."
The meditation seat trembles in alarm and is smeared with plaster; this provokes the disciples and grandsons to act like no true men.
With my staff, I strike them repeatedly across the head, so that they may come to know the Red-Bearded Barbarian. (Longmen Yuan)
[Added by Increase] Yunju Wu said: "In the past, Master Dongshan addressed the assembly, saying:
'In heaven there is no Maitreya; on earth there is no Maitreya. When one is called a thief at the crossroads of the street, tell me:
is this person joyful when called a thief by him, or is he distressed? Originally, he is neither joyful..."
Joy is also not affliction. Why? Because he has a place where he can settle. Thus, he says in verse:
"Called a thief by others, He swallows his voice and draws in his breath. Though his words may be harsh, Truly, they have a fine flavor."
One does not walk where the Tathāgata walks. A man of spirit naturally possesses a will that pierces the heavens;
from the heavens above to the earth below, there is no Maitreya. What is the reason for establishing names and designations?
Gold has its own price as gold; it is never sold to others mixed with sand. (Mañjuśrī says.)
[Added from the Supplementary Collection] Zhaozhou once asked Nanquan, "Please speak, Master, regarding that which transcends the four propositions and cuts off the hundred negations.
The Master descended from his seat and returned to his quarters. Zhaozhou said, "This old monk usually talks incessantly, yet when questioned, he cannot utter a single word.
An attendant said, "It would not be right to say the Master was speechless. Zhaozhou then struck him.
One hand of clouds. This one blow should have been taken by Master Wang himself. The verse says:
Beyond the four propositions and transcending the hundred negations, the author knows him intimately. Leaping down from the meditation seat, he simply departs.
"Following that hawk, it soars toward the sky.
(Zhimen Zu) One day Nanquan did not go to the hall for the meal. The attendant invited him to attend.
The Master said, "Today I ate my fill of oil-cakes at the manor. The attendant said, "The Master has never left or entered [the monastery]. The Master said, "Go and ask."
Just as the head of the manor was about to go out, he suddenly saw the Master returning to thank him, saying, "The Abbot came to the manor to eat oil-cakes.
The verse says: "Alas, Master Wang!
He even sold his own naked poverty. Having eaten some oil-cakes and returned, To this day he is still mocked by others."
(The Cow-herding Excursion).
Without stepping outside the gate of the square measure, he has already arrived and is seated upon the manor. What a fine serving of oil-cakes! To this day, it cannot be chewed through.
(Wan’an Ru): Riding a tiger through the marketplace, holding a torch to steal a pig; the master sleeps with eyes wide open, while the neighbor cries out that a donkey is lost.
(Wan’an Yan): Stealing and eating oil-cakes;
flaunting one’s clever tongue. Growing old and becoming a demon; deceiving gods and ghosts. (Qian’an Guang).
Asafoetida has no reality; mercury has no artifice. Old Nanquan—his manners are indeed worthy of note. (Feng by Fukan).
National Teacher Qian’an of Yanguan, Hangzhou (who succeeded Mazu), one day called to his attendant, saying, "Bring me the rhinoceros-horn fan.
The attendant replied, "It is broken. The Master said, "The fan is broken; give me back the rhinoceros."
"The ox comes. To this, there was no response. Touzi spoke on his behalf, saying, "I do not decline to bring it out, but I fear its horns and head are incomplete.
Zifu spoke on his behalf by drawing a circle and writing the character for "ox" inside it.
Shishuang spoke on his behalf, saying, "If it were the Master himself, there would be none at all. Baofu said, "The Master is advanced in years; please invite someone else."
Excellent person. The verse says:
The rhinoceros fan has been used for a long time; when questioned, it turns out one knows nothing at all.
Its boundless refreshing breeze and its horned head have all followed the clouds and rain away, impossible to pursue. (Xuedou Xian)
How pitiable is this single rhinoceros-horn fan; In vain do they say it has already been shattered. Boundless pure breezes follow wherever the hand goes;
Its towering presence rises above the mundane world. (Baizhang Yuan)
The fan is broken; the rope is for the rhinoceros. Within the circle and the square, there is a source. Who knows that the moon’s essence has endured for a thousand years?
Its subtlety lies in a single point of autumnal clarity. (Tiantong Jue)
The Master stubbornly sought the rhinoceros; in its application, who could attain freedom? The attendant did not know it possessed horns and tusks;
the rope of its nose was seized by another. (Zuyin Ming)
The bright moon shines with cold clarity; the pure breeze does not cease. How boundless is the intention of the Abbot of Yan; what need is there to seek the rhinoceros? (By Qing of Caotang)
The rhinoceros fan has been used for many years; it has passed through the hands of those who mastered the pure mechanism and was transmitted from master to disciple.
Though its horns are not complete, it is gathered up; after the rain, wind and moon fill the long river. (Fodeng Xun)
[Continued Collection] A rhinoceros on a fan from an ancient painting. Having requested it, I have already broken it; I seek the original ox.
Even if Dai Zhi were to paint it out again, it would not be that very same head from those days. (Shengyin’s "Playful Fish in Stillness")
The scorching heat steams the people; their sweat is like boiling soup. The salt used by the Salt Commissioner—how could it be ordinary?
Do not ask whether the rhinoceros horn is present as you shake the fan lightly; when it is brought forth, the pure wind cools the universe. (Huguo Long)
The rhinoceros fan has its origins. Each time it is raised, each time it is set aside. Lotus leaves tilt chaotically as pearls glisten;
after one rain, [the scene] is at the head of the emerald stream. (Lan’an Shu)
The fan is clearly and completely broken; yet Yanguan again demands the rhinoceros horn. You must know that the attendant finds it difficult to speak;
having nothing left to return, he simply desists. (Tianmu Li)
[Added from another source] One day, Master Yanguan said to the assembly, "The void is the drum; Mount Sumeru is the mallet. What kind of person can beat it? The assembly was speechless.

Someone reported this to Nanquan, who said, "Master Wang does not beat this broken drum. Fayan offered a different version, saying, "Master Wang does not beat it. The verse says: The void is the drum, Sumeru the mallet— What person can strike it?

Nanquan says he won't beat the broken drum; Fayan says he doesn't beat it at all. In the vast expanse of the great function, Who is there to raise a hand? If you can discern within the soundless sound, Then you will know the true meaning of the beating.
Nanquan Wangmo was old and without cause; he followed Yan-guan to become a music official.
The command of the Western Patriarch was strict and prohibitive, sparing him from the mistaken joy of the Chan assembly. (Nanyuan Sheng)
The void is the drum; Mount Sumeru is the mallet. When one wishes to strike, one strikes; there is no need to ask who it is. (Ying’an Hua).
The National Teacher exerts effort setting up the face-drum; this still surpasses ten thousand instances of "poisoned lacquer. One who understands how to strike Nanquan is not a skilled hand;
even today throughout the world, he shall never have his grievance heard. (Yeniping).
[Added to the Collection] A monk asked Yanguan, "What is the Dharmakāya Vairocana? The Master said, "Bring me the pure water pitcher.
When the monk brought the pitcher, the Master said, "Put it back in its original place.
After the monk had placed it there and returned, he asked again, "What is the Dharmakāya Vairocana? The Master said, "The ancient Buddhas have already passed away."
It has been a long time. The verse says:
With both hands clearly passing over the pure pitcher, one does not realize the body is already within the moat and city.
Even if one were to possess the Vajra-eye, it would still be half a month’s journey from Mount Mui (Muzhou Daozhe). (By Shangfang Yi)

The bird flies through the sky; the fish swims in the water. In rivers and lakes they forget one another; in clouds and heavens they realize their aspirations. To direct the mind with a single thread is like facing a thousand miles.
Knowing gratitude and repaying kindness—how many such instances are there in the human world? (Tiantong Jue)
Chan Master Zhichang of Guizong on Mount Lu (a successor of Mazu). One day, while he was weeding grass, a monk who was a lecturer in the sutras came to visit him.
Suddenly seeing a snake pass by, the Master cut it with his hoe. The monk said, "I have long admired Guizong;
I never expected you would be such a coarse practitioner. The Master replied, "You are coarse, and I am coarse. The monk asked, "How so?"
"This is coarse. The Master held up his hoe and asked, "What is subtle? The Master made a gesture of slaying a snake.

[The monk] said, "If it is so, then I shall follow and practice accordingly. The Master said, "Setting aside for a moment following and practicing accordingly, where did you see me slay a snake? The monk had no reply. The verse says: The hoe is raised; the snake is slain. If one follows, where is the trace? A single stroke leaves no mark; How can there be a place to find it?
The Master of Mount Lu received those of superior capacity; he displayed compassion by slaying the snake on purpose.
When the Dharma Master Gaomao was startled and terrified, he instead said, "It was a mistake born of carelessness. (Fenyang Shanzhao)
The great function, sweeping across and intersecting like a flash of lightning—though the Śakara eye is still blurred with lacquer, deluded followers argue over lip-service in their dreams;
yet one remembers following him as he went, following along with every step (the Seal of the Ocean-Print).
Performing somersaults atop a thousand-fathom pole; casting a fishing hook into the heart of the great ocean’s waves.
His grand physique possesses naturally fine bone and flesh; even without applying rouge, he is elegant and refined. (Nanhua Bing)
[Continued Collection] To slay the snake is no small matter; it is truly to cause him to escape the wheel of suffering.
The Master’s lofty mind has not yet faded—how could he speak recklessly and falsely? (Hengchuan Hong).
[Added from another source] Guizong addressed the assembly, saying: "I now wish to speak of Chan; all you sons, come forward.
When the great assembly had stepped forward, the Master said: "Listen to the practice of Avalokiteśvara, which skillfully responds to all places.
A monk asked: "What is the practice of Avalokiteśvara? The Master snapped his fingers and said: "Do you all hear it? They replied: "We hear it. The Master said: "A whole crew!"
Han: "What are you looking for here? With his staff, he drove him away, then laughed heartily and returned to the abbot’s quarters. The verse says:

Without study, a snap of the fingers transcends; The faculty of hearing is purified through perfect penetration. Transcending both hearing and non-hearing— How wondrous is the practice of Avalokiteśvara!
The tip of the staff points out the Vajra King; it serves as a bridge across perilous paths. (Yuánwù Qín). [Added from another source:
Once, while Guīzōng was plastering a wall, Bái Shèrén came by. The Master asked, "Are you a gentleman Confucian or a commoner Confucian?
Bái replied, "A gentleman Confucian. The Master then struck the mud tray once, and Bái proceeded to pass the mud over to him.

The Master received him and immediately employed him. After a long silence, he said: "Could this be the quick-witted and talented Minister Bai? He replied: "I dare not say so. The Master said: "You have only a share of excessive attachment to the mud. The Verse says: The Master received him and immediately employed him;
After a long while, he asked: "Could this be the quick-witted Minister Bai? He replied: "I dare not say so. The Master said: "You have only a share of excessive attachment to the mud."
Majestic indeed, this is no petty Confucian scholar; I have come specifically through the deep clouds to visit this recluse. Having already passed through the mud, I feel no shame;
What further need is there to speak of intimacy or distance? (Bao Ye Yuan)

Five flavors and one flavor— Having eaten them, one must belch. When the Imperial Edict was proclaimed on Gold Wheel Peak, The piercing, clear wind was truly fearsome. (Shijianming)
I brew fragrant and pure wine at a low price; even now, few travelers pass on the official road. The single flavor of returning to the source is like continuous bitterness;
how many young practitioners have missed the forest groves? (Changling Zhuo)

[Added to the Collection] A monk asked Guizong, "What is the profound principle (*xuanzhi*)? The Master said, "No one is able to comprehend it. The monk asked, "How about if one directs oneself toward it?
The Master said, "To direct oneself toward it is already to deviate. The monk asked, "How about if one does not direct oneself toward it? The Master said, "Who would seek the profound principle?
He added, "In departing from it, there is no place for you to apply your mind. The monk asked, "Is there not some gate of skillful means (*upāya-mukha*) that allows one..."
The student was granted entry. The Master said, "The wondrous power of Avalokiteśvara’s wisdom can save the world from suffering.
The student asked, "What is the wondrous power of Avalokiteśvara’s wisdom? The Master struck the lid of the cauldron three times and asked, "Do you hear it?"
The monk said, "I heard it. The Master asked, "Why did I not hear it? The monk was speechless. The Master chased him away with his staff. A verse says:
Three sounds, the cauldron lid lifts, and the Universal Gate opens wide. In the bitter sea of toil, the weary wanderer cannot be called back. The springtime radiance of ninety days is here once more.
Half [of the verse]: "Empty-flying petals dot the moss" (from *Jue'an Xiang*).
[Added from another collection. A monk asked Guizong, "What is bodhi as it meets the eye? The Master lifted his foot and said, "Do you understand?"
[The monk] said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "Three are here now; you may choose whichever you will. The Verse says:
Awakening is present before the eyes, no sand is scattered. To show him these three, he was even more thorough.
When patch-robed monks meet, they laugh "he-he"; Spring birds warble, scolding the falling flowers. (Haiyin Xin)
Guizong was once asked by Li Bo, the Regional Inspector of Jiangzhou: "I have often heard that Mount Sumeru can contain a mustard seed; I do not doubt this.
But as for a mustard seed containing Mount Sumeru—is this not mere idle talk? The Master said: "People say you, the Prefectural Governor, have read ten thousand scrolls of books;
is this true? Li Bo replied: "I dare not say so. The Master said: "Suppose your body were as large as a coconut. If you were to read ten thousand scrolls..."
"Where shall I place this scroll? Li bowed his head and remained silent. The verse says:
Letting go, the sun and moon shine bright; Holding fast, heaven and earth turn black. If you do not turn your head at this single stroke, Thorny brambles will grow everywhere.
The dragon palaces and ocean treasuries are not many; the spark of flint and the flash of lightning are not swift. Have you not seen?
Beneath Mount Zixiao, by the side of the Ink Pond, the Eight Divine Steeds chase after it like the wind, yet cannot catch up. (Buddha-Hui Spring).

A mustard seed containing Mount Sumeru—this is a groundless doubt. Casting aside lute and books, he knocks upon the gate of Chan. Suddenly hearing where ten thousand scrolls cannot be hidden, he turns his divine mechanism in a flash;
this only he himself knows. Only he himself knows: he has pulled up the red cassia tree by its roots and returned home. (Fuxincai).
A mustard seed contains Mount Sumeru—this verifies the ancestral wind. The clear mechanisms are distinct and their wondrousness is inexhaustible.
If you wish to know where the ten thousand scrolls of books come from, leap out from within the mirror of your own wisdom. (Heshan Fang)
[Continued Collection] Exhausting one’s own mind, one laughs until others’ mouths split. An octagonal millstone rolls through the void;
a golden-maned lion transforms into a dog. *Hè!* (Xuetang Xing).

With ten thousand scrolls of poetry and the classics, he emerged all at once with the prominence of a rising leader. As soon as he stepped across the threshold of the ancestral school, he deployed his strategic brilliance.

Ancient Guizong was a true elder; he merely looked to draw his bow to its full curve, unaware that anyone had seen two vultures fall. Without a hair’s breadth of deviation, he stood as firm as mountains and peaks.
His majestic presence towered over the scholarly community, and his vast, pure wind spread throughout the vast expanse of space. (Chichan Miao)
[Added from the Supplement] Chan Master Ruyuan of Shaoyou (successor of Mazu) ascended the hall.
"The direct meaning of the West—how difficult it is to speak of! O assembly, is there anyone who can speak it? Come forward and try to say it.
A monk stepped forward and, as soon as he prostrated, the Master struck him, saying, "What kind of time is this to show your head? Later generations cited this instance.
Changqing said, "It does not matter, it does not matter. Zifu spoke on his behalf, saying, "For the sake of the Master, who does not spare his own life. The verse says:
The meaning of the Patriarchs coming from the West—how can it be easily measured? To lift one's eyes is already to err in accepting it. The *śrāmaṇera* does not know how to recognize the proper time.
Section. Opening his eyes, he enters the cauldron of boiling water with majestic dignity.

(This mountain should respond. What is the true meaning of the one who comes from the West? His proclamations mostly pity those who remain halfway. Summoning the thief to the gate, he then destroys the thief;
one truly knows that he wears an amulet for warding off weapons upon his person. (Zhao Shànqī, the Vice Prefect.)

[Added to the Collection] Chan Master Daming Fachang of Meishan (he was a successor of Mazu).
After he had taken up residence on the mountain, Mazu sent a monk to him and asked, "What did you gain from seeing Mazu that you have settled here on this mountain?
The Master said, "Mazu told me, 'The very mind is Buddha,' and so I have settled right here. [The monk asked: "Mazu..."
"Recently, the Patriarch’s teaching on the Buddha-dharma has changed again. The Master asked, "How has it changed?
He replied, "Recently he has also said, 'Neither mind nor Buddha. The Master said, "This old fellow will never stop confusing people!
Let him say 'neither mind nor Buddha' all he wants; I simply stick to 'this very mind is Buddha. The monk returned and reported this to Mazu. Mazu—
He said: "The plum has ripened for the great assembly. The verse says:
Using only Mazu’s lead blade, He tears asunder the iron net that covers the heavens. In the green pond, the night rain beats upon lotus leaves;
To this day, poverty brings the regret of having too many selves. (One Barrier: Pǔ).
Wearing lotus robes and eating pine nuts while dwelling amidst deep clouds—this was surely a mistaken view of those years past.
To bury one’s life in the realization that mind is Buddha, for ten thousand years and a thousand ages, would not turn into even a speck of dust. (By Yunnan)
Your heart, sir, is as thin as a leaf; my person, I, am as pure as ice. You speak of gold, but I do not respond.
Even if we were to share a single fleeting smile by chance, who would believe that for half a lifetime I have kept watch by a solitary lamp? (By Jianweng Jing)

[Added for Collection] When Layman Pang asked Damei, "I have long heard of Damei; I wonder if the plum has ripened yet? The Master said, "Where will you apply your teeth? He replied, "Into a hundred fragments. The Master said, "Give me back the pit! Verse: The Layman’s question was like a thunderbolt; Damei’s answer was like a flash of lightning.

The plum has ripened, and it is fragrant; The pit is returned to its original source. If you can see through this, Then you are truly a man of the Way. If you cannot, you are but a common person. How many people can truly grasp this? It is not something that can be grasped by the intellect. If you wish to know the meaning of the plum, Look at the face of Damei.
The plum on Great Plum Tree has ripened; Old Pang already knew it beforehand. To verify the true essence with the Right Eye, they meet and clap their hands as they return. (Songyuan Yue)
Master Pang went in person to raise the flag of surrender; with a single stroke of his blade at the incense burner, he severed ten thousand worldly concerns.
This was not something born of past habit or mere gnawing; it was because the plum had long since ripened. (Xin’an Chou)
[Added from the Supplement] Dàmé was once traveling with Jiāshān and Dìngshān. Dìngshān said, "If there is no Buddha within birth and death, then there is no birth and death.
Jiāshān said, "If there is a Buddha within birth and death, then one is not deluded by birth and death.
The two could not agree with one another and went together to visit Dàmé. Jiāshān then asked, "I do not know which of us is right..."
"Which one is close and which one is distant? The Master said, "One is close and one is distant. Jia Shan asked, "I do not yet know which one is close.
The Master said, "Go for now and come back tomorrow. The next day, Jia Shan went to the abbot's quarters and asked again. The Master said:

Those who are close do not question; those who question are not close. After Jia Shan took up residence at his monastery, he said, "When I was first at Damei, I lost one eye. Yunfeng Yue said, "Jia Shan only knew that he lost one eye;
he did not realize that he had gained another. Yuanwu said, "In this way, there are two."
The Vajra-King of the Mouth’s precious sword merely brushes across the void; Jinshan, however, is not so.

Birth-and-death is the very foundation of all Buddhas, and all Buddhas are the furnace and bellows of birth-and-death. If one can understand this perilous and absolute reality and take it up, one will immediately realize the six supernatural powers and the eight liberations. He then spoke in verse:

Where there is a Buddha, there is no delusion; where there is no Buddha, there is nothing. At the moment the Great Plum’s “True Eye on the Crown of the Head” was struck open, intimacy and estrangement were already verified.

One family cradles the jade from Mount Jing; another person holds the pearl of the numinous serpent. Whether one loses it or exchanges it, they both return to the same source, though their paths differ.

The master artisan throws his hammer right in front of one’s face; even a swift falcon cannot catch it in the moment. One might think it is the red-bearded barbarian, yet there is another with a red beard.
Without having yet brought forth the center-point of the scale, how many practitioners have harbored grievances? Wait until the balance comes to hand.
With one's own hands, one finally knows that the weight is clearly distinguished for oneself. (Xinwen Ben).
Whether there is birth-and-death or Buddha—empty names are like a flash of lightning. A swift falcon soars across the heavens; it does not strike the hawks by the hedge.
Without lack and without excess, like the vast void; who knows who could understand this forced naming and modeling?
(Yeshu Chuan). Companions from of old have never agreed with one another; what need is there to discuss the old man on the mountain peak?
When the peach petals have fallen away in the mountain hollow, the flowing stream still winds as before around the bamboo gate. (Lan’an Shu).
Bamboo fences and thatched huts, the wine flag slants low. A single gourd ruins two households. After drinking, one knows not heaven from earth.
Returning home, the ground is covered with peach blossoms. (Xue’an Jin)
The bitter gourd is bitter from root to tip; the sweet melon is sweet to its very stem. Both flavors are unpleasant;
in the end, one enters the Yellow Springs. (Ying’an Hua)
The single word "Buddha" is a forced arrangement; existence and non-existence, birth and death, are all buried in one pit.
The Old Man of Damei has no bone in his tongue; he plants lotuses in midwinter within the fire. (Yun Chao Yan)
Blue sky, white sun. Forbid all seeking. If you ask further how it is, you are like one clutching stolen goods while crying out for injustice. (No door opens. [Added from another source:
When a monk asked Daming, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? the Master said, "There is no meaning in his coming from the West.
When Yanguan heard this, he said, "One coffin, two corpses. Xuansha [commented].
Yanguan said, "He is a master. Xuedou said, "There are three of them as well. He then offered this verse:
The eye of death within life; non-action yet function. The square inch does not shift; throughout the ten directions he plays alone.
Where skill and clumsiness cannot reach, Yanguan has a way of emerging. His own words come from his own mouth: "The roosters and dogs are noisy next door. (Yuetang Chang)
Wisdom grows through engagement with affairs; by recognizing the source, one escapes entanglement. Turning inward to understand the Way, the entire family attains prosperity.

Yet, vying for promotion while burying oneself, who can transcend the duality of favor and opposition, right and wrong? Grasp this and let it go so that it may function; with both hands supporting the plow, the water rises above the knees.
[Added to the Collection] Chan Master Lingmo of Wuxie Mountain in Wuzhou (he was a successor of Mazu).
He traveled far to visit Shitou and asked: "If our words accord with one another, I shall stay; if they do not, I shall depart. Shitou remained seated as he spoke.
The Master then turned to leave. Shitou called out after him, "Ajari! The Master turned his head. Shitou said, "From birth until death, it is only this."
"What is the point of turning your head and twisting your brain? At these words, the Master attained great enlightenment; he then broke his staff and settled there.
Dongshan said, "At that time, had it not been for my late teacher Wuxie, it would have been very difficult to take this on."
"Even so, one is still traversing the path. Changqing said, "Dangerous! Xuangjue asked, "Which part is the traversing of the path?
A monk said, "Because he realizes it within the three inches while on the path, he is thus 'on the path.
Xuangjue asked, "Does he realize his own self, or does he realize the three inches? If...
"It is oneself. Why does it become three inches? If it is three inches, why does one attain awakening?
Now tell me, what was Dongshan’s intention? Do not speak recklessly; you must be careful. The verse says:
Shitou sat holding his seat. Wuxie departed immediately. Shitou called him back; this, however, became a matter of much fuss. (Cuiyan Zhi).
Whether on the road or at home, how can one repay [the debt]? Do not seek the former master with a single standard.
Majestic as the universe is like a sovereign, it cannot avoid being half-devoid of a skull. (Longmen Yuan).
When about to depart, he called out in a loud voice and brought [the disciple] back; at that moment, his mind’s eye opened all at once.
If you wish to know that this does not rely on the power of cultivation, let life and death drift freely as they come and go. (Like a withered tree.)
Chan Master Baoji of Mount Pan in Youzhou (he was a successor of Mazu). When he first attended upon Mazu, he served as a street monk.
One day, as he went out the gate, he saw people carrying a funeral procession. A songster shook his bell and sang: "The red wheel is certain to sink in the west;
I know not to which realm the soul has departed. Beneath the curtain, the sons of mourning wailed, "Alas! Alas! The Master [heard this].
Upon seeing it, he suddenly attained realization. He reported this to Mazu, who certified his understanding. The verse says:
The sound of song meanders, the sound of weeping is mournful; It makes the old master Panshan laugh to death.
In the dark and murky places of ignorance throughout kalpas, All at once, sudden awakening radiates brilliant light. (Wenshu said.)
The crimson wheel surely sinks to the west; I do not yet know to which direction the soul has gone.
Having firmly treading upon the fields of one’s native land, the original face is revealed in full majesty. Man is simply here, never having perished;
in the Tuṣita Heaven it is no longer the world of men—one must know that there is another way to deliberate. (Fodeng Xun)
In response to the lamentations, one immediately assumes responsibility; where, in the end, does the soul go? With a leap of joy, the whole body is naturally revealed;
only then does one know that throughout the entire world, nothing has ever been hidden. (Haiyin Xin)
[Continued Collection] I do not know to which direction the soul has gone; having no place of rest, it stands forth naked and bare.
The water flows cold from the edge of the rocks; the wind comes fragrant from within the flowers. (Guan of Yue-lin).
The crimson wheel will surely sink to the west; it is unknown to which direction the soul shall go.
When the filial son has fully proclaimed this, Mount Pan has no place to hide. It cannot be hidden; it is fit to serve as a model for devas and humans. (Yuan of Dun’an)
Suddenly hearing the mournful wailing beneath the curtain, it instantly makes Tiantai face Wutai. Wind and moon remain as one across ancient and modern times;
though one possesses a mouth for the whole body, it is difficult to open. (Shuan-an Yan)
The sound of the *xiè* song is choked, its cadence long; hearing it, one’s grief suddenly breaks the heart. As before, the crimson disk sinks behind the western mountains;
throughout the great trichiliocosm, there is no place to contain this desolation. (Tianmu Li)
The dew on the leeks is chilling and truly pitiable; the white poplars and crimson banners depart with fluttering ease.
Amidst the sounds of wailing, there is no news; when it strikes the south, it stirs the north (Beojan’s *Gyeom*).
The red wheel is certain to sink in the west; I do not know to which direction the soul has gone. With one cry of bitter wailing, there is nowhere to hide;
lifting my head, I see my own father and mother face to face. (Wuzhun Shifan)
One day, while in a marketplace, Huanshan saw a man at a butcher's stall buying meat, saying, "Cut me a pound of the finest.
The butcher set down his knife and folded his hands, saying, "Prefect, which part here is not the finest?
Upon hearing this, the Master suddenly attained great enlightenment. He returned and informed Mazu of what he had realized, and Mazu certified it.
He approved of it. The verse says:
This matter is clear and not concealed; In every instance and every thing, they accord naturally. A thousand words and ten thousand phrases—no one understands them;
Yet again, they follow the warbling oriole over the low wall. (Nanhua Bing)
[Continued Collection] Seeing off a guest by the riverbank, he boards a light boat. Facing him, an old fisherman silently casts his hook. With a single pull, a scaled jewel ascends into his hand;
the distant mountains layer upon one another as the waters flow on and on. (Miaofeng Shan)
Baoshan addressed the assembly, saying: "In the three realms there is no dharma; where can one seek the mind? The four elements are fundamentally empty;
upon what does the Buddha rely to abide? The celestial sphere is unmoving, silent and wordless.
Face-to-face presentation—there is nothing more."珍重 (Take care). The verse says:
In the three realms there are no dharmas; where can one seek the mind? White clouds serve as a canopy, and flowing springs act as a zither.
One melody, two melodies—no one understands them. After the rain has passed, the autumn waters in the night pond are deep. (Xuedou Xian)
Lush and green are the bamboos that fill the courtyard before the window; Dark and deep are the mountains that face the gate.
There is yet another thing most worthy of admiration: At night, the flowing stream resounds with a gurgling murmur. (Fojian Yongqin)
In the three realms there are no dharmas; where can one seek the mind? The mountains appear as if after rain has passed; the pines hum with the melody of the wind.
Lying across or reclining upside down, there is nothing else to do; let the moss freely encroach upon the ground at will. (Fóxìng Tàiyī)
[Continued Collection] There are no dharmas in the three realms; where can one seek the mind? The moon is bright, yet the night is dark; the mountains are high, yet the waters are deep.
The three realms originally manifest from the mind; when there is no mind, the three realms naturally subside into stillness. (Fundamental Awakening I)
In the three realms there are no dharmas; where can one seek the mind? Mountain flowers are like brocade, green leaves form a shade.
With a single cry of the cuckoo, it is time to go home; yet the foolish fellow still guards his garden. (Tudu Ce)
In the three realms there are no dharmas; where can one seek the mind? Like a startled snake entering the grass, like a flying bird leaving the forest.
After the rain, the mountain hall is still in the autumn night; the clamor of the marketplace never reaches this solitary peak. (By Shanguan Zhi)
Sleeping in spring, I am unaware of the dawn; everywhere I hear the singing of birds. Last night there was the sound of wind and rain;
who knows how many flowers have fallen? (Huò Ān style).
The mountain cottage is free of dust and exceptionally pure; the pomegranate flowers bloom, shining through the curtains. The shade of the locust trees covers the ground at high noon;
as I awaken from my dream, a solitary warbler sings its note. (Closing the Room).
Willow trees hang low, about to hide the crows; after the ritual of the she, the eastern wind sweeps away the falling flowers. Where would it be best to take up my staff and invite friends?
Let us look at the mulberry and hemp on the south and north slopes of the mountain. (Yugoku Kun)
