If you can see through this, Then you will be a true master of the Dharma-king. If you cannot, Then you are merely a person of the worldly king. If you can understand this, Then you have realized the Great Sovereignty. If you cannot, Then you are still a person of the dependent realm. If you can see through this, Then you will be a true master of the Dharma-wheel. If you cannot, Then you are merely a person of the turning wheel. If you can understand this, Then you have attained the Great Turning. If you cannot, Then you are still a person of the revolving wheel. If you can see through this, Then you will be a true master of the Dharma-treasury. If you cannot, Then you are merely a person of the limited treasury. If you can understand this, Then you have realized the Great Treasury. If you cannot, Then you are still a person of the narrow treasury. If you can see through this, Then you will be a true master of the Dharma-seal. If you cannot, Then you are merely a person of the provisional seal. If you can understand this, Then you have attained the Great Seal. If you cannot, Then you are still a person of the dualistic seal. If you can see through this, Then you will be a true master of the Dharma-eye. If you cannot, Then you are merely a person of the worldly eye. If you can understand this, Then you have realized the Great Eye. If you cannot, Then you are still a person of the limited eye. If you can see through this, Then you will be a true master of the Dharma-mind. If you cannot, Then you are merely a person of the worldly mind. If you can understand this, Then you have attained the Great Mind. If you cannot, Then you are still a person of the dualistic mind. If you can see through this, Then you will be a true master of
Dwelling together and practicing together, the world knows them not; how many people encounter them face-to-face?
Even among those who continue the lineage of the house, half are but children raised by poverty and begging. (Baoning Yong)
[Added for inclusion] One day, Dayi asked Layman Pang: "This saying is one that few people have been able to avoid throughout the ages.
As for you, Layman Pang, have you been able to avoid it? He replied, "Yes. The Master brought up the previous conversation again and said, "Where have you come from?
The Master continued, "Not only now; even the ancients had this same saying. Layman Pang then... [acted].
He went out dancing. The Master said, "A wind-crazed old man! A wind-crazed old man! Who else would you have to correct your own transgressions? The Verse says:

Habituated to following the winding paths of sheep’s intestines, When meeting others, do not ask for the ford. The mountains and rivers differ from past and present; The scenery and customs change with every season.
(Fang’an Xian). [Included in the Supplementary Collection.
Because Pang Jushi came to visit Da Tong, he held up a bamboo sieve and called out, “Master Da Tong!
Master Da Tong! The Master did not look back. Jushi said, “The school of Stonehead has crumbled like ice melting away. The Master said, “If...”
"It is not possible to find another like Master Pang; it is indeed so obvious. Layman Shi threw down his colander and said, "I would rather have nothing worth even a single coin.
The Master said, "Though the coin may be worthless, how can you avoid owing it to him? Layman Shi performed a dance and withdrew.
The Master then picked up the colander and said, "Pang Gong! Pang Gong! Layman Shi replied, "You want me..."

"Basket! I want your wooden ladle. The Master performed a dance and withdrew. The layman clapped his hands and laughed, saying, "Go back, go back! The verse says: Go back, go back! The Master dances and departs. The layman claps his hands and laughs; The song of the *dhyāna* master is truly rare.
Lifting up the strainer: the pure breeze fills the universe. Setting down the strainer: gold is like dross and soil.
Pity these two ancient sages; when they meet, what need is there to dance together? (Tudu Ce).
"You love my colander; I love your ladle. The main peak has just risen high; the front peak stands towering again.
Layman Datong, you take error for right. Go back! The world is wide.
Where shall one pair of iron hammers be placed? (Xiatang Yuan)
Pujie held fast; yet he was struck by Pang Gong’s painful thorn. He was left turning left and right, following behind and trailing along.
When the bamboo sieve was lifted and they called out to one another in dance—if you say this is merely painting a cat after the model, you would surely have to cast Ziqi out of pure gold. (Shixi Yue)
[Added from another source] Daotong was asked by a monk, "How does one accord with the Way throughout the twelve hours?
The Master said, "Do you recognize the twelve hours? The monk asked, "What are the twelve hours? The Master said, "Zi, Chou, Yin, Mao.
The monk bowed. The Master presented this verse: "Throughout the twelve hours, which character is distinct? Zi, Chou, Yin, Mao—these are I."
Now it is said: "If one realizes that all phenomena are empty through the mind-only, Śākyamuni and Maitreya part ways from this point.
The verse says:
"Throughout the twelve periods of the day, are they distinct or not? My whole body is my mouth, yet it is difficult to explain. The old king of the eastern village sighs in vain in the dark."
Alas! Bodhidharma’s coming from the West held a wondrous secret (Fujian Qin).

At every moment throughout the twelve hours of the day, there is a distinct difference. Though he spoke all day long, he never truly spoke; walking, standing, sitting, and reclining were all contained within it.
Now, I shall directly provide you with this secret (Dayuan Zhi).
The signs of the zodiac—zi, chou, yin, and mao—have never been separate; thus have the ancients and those of today spoken.
When the spirit-mansion is utterly exhausted and not a single thing remains, the Buddhas and Patriarchs clearly provide the secret instruction. (Tudu Ce)
If you recognize the lines of zi, chou, yin, and mao, you must continue and inherit the tradition of this gate.
Like a king sitting upon his throne wielding a sword, both Buddha and Mara are swept away, becoming empty all at once. (Shixi Yue)
The Fourth Generation under the Sixth Patriarch (the First of the Three Generations under Nanyue):
Chan Master Lingyou of Mount Gui, Tanzhou (Successor of Baizhang). One day, while standing in attendance, Baizhang asked, "Who is there?
The Master replied, "Lingyou. Baizhang said, "Is there any fire in the hearth? The Master stirred it and said, "There is none."
The Master himself rose and poked deeply into the ashes until he found a small spark of fire. Holding it up to show him, he said, "This is not fire.
The teacher attained awakening, bowed in thanks, and explained his understanding. The Master said, "This was merely a temporary crossroads."
The Sūtra says: "If you wish to see the Buddha-nature, you should contemplate the conditions of time and season.

When the time and season arrive, it is like one who is suddenly awakened from delusion, or like one who suddenly remembers what was forgotten; only then do you realize that your own property is not obtained from another. Therefore, the Patriarch said:
"Awakening is the same as non-awakening; there is no mind and there is no dharma. It is simply the absence of delusion. The minds of ordinary people and sages are equal;
the fundamental mind and dharmas have always been spontaneously complete. Since you are now thus, protect and maintain them well yourself. (The *Chuan deng lu* records it thus;
the *Wu deng hui yuan* adds the following after "protect and maintain": The next day, he entered the mountains with Baizhang to perform manual labor. Baizhang said:

"Can you bring some fire? The Master said, "I can bring it. [The Master] asked, "Where is it? The Master then picked up a piece of wood, blew on it twice, and handed it to the Master of the Hall (Zhàng).

The Master of the Hall said, "Like a worm gnawing through wood. Verse: A single spark from a piece of wood, Blown upon, it turns to flame. The Master of the Hall, like a worm gnawing through wood, Does not know where the fire has gone.
When lifted up, it all comes down to a single spark. Suddenly it blazes forth, its flames reaching across the sky. Spreading across the wilds, it is difficult even to extinguish;
for three years, not a blade of grass shall grow. (Bao-ning Yong)
The Malla once lost the pearl from his forehead; searching everywhere, he sighed in frustration for a long time.
When those nearby pointed out that the pearl was there all along, he finally realized how coarse his lifelong efforts had been. (Da-hong Sui)
Stir the cold ashes and the fire blazes forth; at dawn, it still glows beyond the mountains.
How lamentable are those guests before Fayen’s Hall, who still go southward to inquire about the fires of Bingding. (Shangfang Yi)
The road beneath Mount Daxiong is long and winding; father and son walk together through the grass. Picking up a withered log, they present it as fire;
the household goods are secure, so measure them yourself. Fortunately, there is a thoroughfare before the gate; why not follow your steps into the setting sun?
The four seas and five lakes are the realm of dragons; the tall oaks and lush bamboos are the home of phoenix chicks. (Fodeng Xun)
[Continued Collection] The entire body is mouths; the whole body is tongues. The mouths wish to speak but do not speak; the tongues wish to say but do not say.
Whether speaking or not speaking, whether glancing or not glancing—brilliant light pervades the great thousandfold world-system.
Let the world below chatter as it pleases. (Nantang Xing)
Picking up a withered piece of firewood and blowing upon it twice, at that moment the sparks fly across the sky.
Alas, those sitting around the hearth in ignorance, looking at one another, know nothing at all. (Gao Yuanquan)
Exhausting every effort through the night for the sake of the orchid, picking here and there, it remains difficult to see.
Suddenly, the beans burst from within the cold ashes; one then takes the firewood itself as the flame. (Bieshan Zhi)
Layer upon layer, why must one display such gallantry? Once this matter is understood, one should simply cease.
Even if one sees smoke that is not fire, it will still burn the hand and further burn the head. (Bao Ye Yuan)
Tracing the root to its very bottom, one finds a single star; cold flames leap with brilliance at this moment.
Picking up a single blade of mugwort and lightly touching it, one knows not how many of the five Sumeru mountains it will burn to ashes. (Xueyan Qin)
When Guishan was serving as the head cook at Baizhang, the itinerant ascetic Sima arrived from south of Lake Hu.
He had discovered a mountain named Daming, which he said was a place where a spiritual teacher capable of sustaining fifteen hundred people could reside.
Baizhang asked, "Can an old monk like me live there? Sima replied, "That is a mountain of flesh; you, Master, are a man of bone."
"If the number of residents does not exceed one thousand, observe whether the kitchen steward (diànzuo) can remain. Call him here and speak with him.

At that time, the Head Seat (shǒuzuò), having heard this, said, "It is fitting that I go. Who is he? The Master then addressed the assembly, saying, "The one who produces a phrase that transcends the ordinary shall succeed.
He then took a pure pitcher (jìngpíng), placed it on the ground, and posed the question: "It must not be called a 'pure pitcher'."
The Master pointed to a water pitcher and asked, "What would you call this? The Head Seat replied, "It cannot be called a wooden pestle.
The Master then questioned the Kitchen Steward; the steward kicked over the pitcher and walked away. The Master laughed and said, "The Head Seat has lost the mountain to the steward.
He consequently appointed the steward to go and reside at the mountain; he was none other than Chan Master Daomiao Yuanyou of Mount Dagu, who indeed brought peace to the monastery.
A Thousand Crowds. The verse says:
To settle the hero is the pure flask; In distinguishing even a hair’s breadth, there is no more sentimentality.
Peace was originally brought about by the generals; Yet they are not permitted to witness that peace themselves. (Zhaojue Zong)
When the True Command is fully upheld, the adept knows; when the pure flask is lifted, doubt is surely resolved. One must know that Great Wisdom is a privateless mirror;
to understand this path, even the legacy of Mount Miao belongs to him. (Foji Yu)
There is a reason for the placement of the water jar; from this point on, the practitioner reaches the ultimate end.
One must believe that when the spring breeze arises over the vast fields, even where there was no elegance, it becomes elegant. (By Doushuai Yue)
Before the hall of Baizhang, he settled the Great Mui; the golden-maned lion displayed its full majesty. Kicking over the pure water jar, he returned to the original transformation;
a pure wind spreads a thousand miles, stirring the earth as all return. (Zhikaiqing)
Disregarding the signal flags before the mountain, he plunged straight into the strategic tent with a single blade. Long spears and short halberds were all useless;
he seized the General’s golden seal and returned home. (By Yi Shangfang)
The great function must be known by one who acts; with a single kick on the spot, all doubt is severed. Alas for those who fail to inherit the ancestral garden;
they merely judge right and wrong at the edge of the pitcher. (Tongzhao meets him.)
The pure pitcher is kicked over, toppling Mount Sumeru; essence and function fully manifest, surpassing past and present.
At the point where the dark barrier is penetrated and the hand is extended, one must ultimately encounter a true知音 (zhīyīn—“one who knows the sound”). (Sushan Ru).
While Guishan and Yangshan were picking tea, the Master said to Yangshan, "All day long you have been picking tea;
I hear only your voice but do not see your form. Please manifest your true form so that we may meet. Yangshan shook the tea tree. The Master said:
Yangshan said, "I have only attained its function, but not its essence. He asked, "I do not yet understand how you, Master, are.
The Master remained silent for a long while, then looked up and said, "You, Master, have only attained its essence, but not its function.
Yangshan said, "Let me give you thirty blows! (The *Wudeng Huiyuan* adds here: Yangshan said, "Master, I shall take your blows; as for my own blows..."
"To whom would you have me give the meal? The Master said, "I grant you thirty blows. Xuangjue asked, "Tell me, where does the fault lie?
The Verse says: Picking tea, do not think of anything else;
Everywhere is clearly a site of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa). Essence and function together promote the true response.
"Things. The Chan stream suddenly awakens to the fragrance before the rain.
(Fenyang Zhao) "When essence and function are fully revealed, their application is not difficult. At that time, Miu and Yang were merely deceiving one another.
If a practitioner of Chan possesses the diamond eye, they should examine the shifting of spiritual sparks with great care. (Foyin Yuan)

The dragon gives birth to dragon offspring, their full majesty contending; amidst the sound of thunderbolts, the mechanism of lightning flashes. When the rain has passed and the clouds have gathered, where have they gone?
At Mount Mui, for ten thousand ages, it alone stands towering high. (By Yuanxuan Zun)
Both essence and function are non-existent; the sun flies and the moon runs. Shaking the tree, there is silence; heaven is long and earth is enduring.
Though the command of thirty blows is strict, it is like loving one's child and failing to notice their ugliness. (Fohuiquan)
In the warmth of spring, they call to one another as they emerge from the emerald heights. Sometimes walking, sometimes sitting, they almost forget to return.
At twilight, a sudden squall of east wind and rain falls; inevitably, their entire bodies and clothes become soaked through. (Baoning Yong)
[Continued Collection] We hear only the voice of the son, but do not see the son’s form. Where the tea bush shakes, it is all too clear.
If you wish to know where Jizang is alert and awake, simply open your eyes slowly and listen. (Cishou Shen)

Family disgrace must not be broadcast abroad. In the relationship of father and son, both essence and function are fully manifest. It may still be permissible for the father to seize the son’s opportunity;
it is not virtuous for the son to seize the father’s opportunity. (Daopei Zhi)
When Old Zhang first became friends with Master Li, he intended to fine Master Li a cup of wine; instead, he was fined a cup by Master Li himself.
Among those with skillful hands, there is no one more skillful than the skillful hand. (Fujian Qín)
Tishan attained the essence; Yangshan attained the function. Essence and function are both complete. To speak a dream within a dream (a shout). (Shuan-an Yan).
Hearing the sound, the form is not seen; shaking the tree, one suddenly awakens. What need is there to debate essence and function?
Returning home, the setting sun is bright. (Hengchuan Gong)
[Added from another collection: Master Guishan asked Yangshan, "From where have you returned? He replied, "I have returned from the fields.
The Master said, "Is the grain ready for harvest yet? He replied, "It is ready for harvest. The Master said, "Do you see it as green? Do you see it as yellow?
Do you see it as neither green nor yellow? He replied, "What is behind the Master? The Master said, "Do you see it? Yangshan picked it up.
Heishu said, "When did the Master ever ask about this? The Master said, "This is like the king of geese choosing its milk.
He then offered this verse:
Not seeing green or yellow, What can be done with the rice ears? The king of geese can choose the milk; The hawk flies off to Silla.
(Tianmu Li). [Added by Zeng] During the winter months, Guishan asked Yangshan, "The weather is cold; are people cold too? Yangshan replied, "Everyone is right here.
The Master said, "Why do you not speak directly? Yangshan said, "Just now, I was not being indirect either. What about you, Reverend? The Master said, "Direct."
One must follow the current. The verse says:
The north wind displays its cold majesty; chillingly it invades skin and bone. A single phrase encompasses the sky’s chill—when has it ever admitted my traces?
Following the current, one recognizes the original body; throughout the entire world, there is nothing that is not a priceless treasure.
(Yuánwù Qín) The wind and flow are blown away by the *Dàshí* mode; the song is sung forth in the *Fùguì* *Huángzhōng* pitch.
As the waist sways to the accelerating beat at dawn, another cup of *pútáo* wine is offered. (Zhèngtáng Biàn)
Everyone is here; two hands cannot lift it up. Set it down and come forward to look: what kind of face and features does it have? (Wuji Pai).
Everyone is here. From the very beginning, there was no obstruction in following the stream. Two mouths with but one tongue—this entanglement has not yet ceased.
Across the vast, boundless earth, people are countless; how many men are able to nod their heads in understanding? (Jiyanzhong).
Everyone is inside; a scorched-tail tiger from the Southern Mountains, its fangs and claws as sharp as blades.
The sun is exactly at noon. (Yi-an Shen)
[Added for inclusion: While Guishan was sleeping, Yangshan came to inquire after him. The Master simply turned his face toward the wall.
Yangshan said, "Why have you become like this, Preceptor? The Master rose and said, "I just had a dream; try to interpret it for me."
[The Master] looked up and took a basin of water to wash his face for the Master. After a short while, Xiangyan also came to pay his respects.
The Master said, "I just had a dream; Jizi (Jiashan), you have already interpreted it.
Now, you too must interpret it for me. Xiangyan then brought over a bowl of tea. The Master said, "The insights of these two disciples surpass even those of Śāriputra. Verse:
It is said:
"Fetching water and brewing tea without missing the opportune moment; at that time, Yuanmeng was well-acquainted with the timing.
Only one such as this may be called a *siddha* guest; how could the supernatural powers of Śāriputra ever equal his? (Benjue I)
Parting the weeds to perceive the wind; lodging alone on a solitary peak; playing the stringless lute; singing the song of non-arising.
Like the tripod’s three legs of Miu, Yang, and Xiangyan, they do not expend the slightest effort when responding to the occasion, freely manifesting a thousand billion bodies at will. (Nantang Xing)
Divine mechanism and wondrous function: opening one’s eyes yet dreaming. Manifesting supernormal powers at the wrong time to display wonders and delude the masses.
(Wan’an Xian) A cup of clear snow, the early fragrance of tea; Just awakened from midday sleep, the spring day is long. Pressed upon, the entire body is nothing but eyes;
Sparse shadows across half the window turn with the slanting sun. (Xueyan Qin)
Guishan addressed the assembly, saying: "After this old monk’s hundred-year life has ended, I shall become a water buffalo on the mountain below.
On its left flank, I shall write five characters: 'The Guishan monk, So-and-so. At that time, if you call me the Guishan monk, I am still the water buffalo;
if you call me the water buffalo, I am still the Guishan monk. If you call me... [the text breaks off].
"What would suffice? (In the *Wudeng Huiyuan*, following "what would suffice," it further says: Yangshan came forth, prostrated, and withdrew.
Yunju Ying spoke on his behalf, saying: "The Master has no other title. Zifubao said:
"At that time, he should simply have made this [circle] sign and presented it. The Korean Monk made this [circle with a 'cow' inside] sign and presented it. Furthermore—
He said: "Only those who share the same Way will understand. Bāzhuo then thoroughly manifested this by presenting it as a formal transmission.

He further said: "The explanation has been explained; the commentary has been commented upon. It is well to awaken to it! Thereupon he composed a verse: The meaning of the verse is that the Dharma is not something to be grasped through words or concepts; it must be realized directly within one's own experience. Only those whose realization is identical to the Buddha’s can truly know it. Bāzhuo’s presentation was a direct pointing to this reality. He concluded that while the teachings have been fully expounded and the commentaries written, the essential point lies in personal awakening. Thus, he offered this verse to express his realization.
It is not Mount Gui, nor is it the ox; one body with two names is truly difficult to repay. Having left behind these two extremes, you must speak:
how can you express that which flows eternally?
The compassionate power of the ancient masters remains unrewarded; as soon as one hears of extraordinary signs, they scramble like oxen.
To clarify the profound principle before sound and after the phrase would have caused Moshan’s vision to be incomplete. For now, let me draw a single thread for my fellow practitioners:
the reeds are covered in snow, and chrysanthemums bloom in autumn. (Fenyang Shao)
Thousands upon thousands, tens of thousands upon tens of thousands of water-buffaloes—none emerge beyond this single one from Mount Gui.

Without a mind to manage or direct, it is ever present; yet if you seek it with deliberate intent, it cannot be found. Neither large nor small, it possesses great strength. It has but one body and two names, few people recognize it.

Let it loose according to conditions and the grasses and trees turn green; when evening comes and it is gathered back, heaven and earth turn black. In gathering and letting loose, one must attain mastery.
The nose-rope. If one does not obtain the rope, there is no standard. How many people in the world are without a rope?
They let this bull-thief run right past them face-to-face. (Huanglong Nan, 2)

In days of yore, there was the Water-Ox of Mount Gui; now he lies old and decrepit upon a desolate mound. Though his appearance is formidable and he lacks strength, for feeding and watering he remains a fine bull.
When the grasses of the four fields turn green, let him graze wherever he will; when the peaks of the thousand mountains turn white with snow, he must be gathered in early.
If one can raise him up at the proper season, what need is there to worry about the vast expanse of mulberry fields?
The water buffalo of Mount Gui is steep and lofty; clearly he reveals the hidden marvels of humanity.
When words emerge from the point of clarity, the night bird flies back to the forest at dawn. (Daowu Zhen)
Cows at the foot of the mountain, monks upon the peak; though the myriad names like sands of the Ganges are numerous, they do not suffice.
I always love the evening clouds returning before they have merged, and the distant mountains stretching infinitely in layer upon layer of azure. (Haiyin Xin)
Not the Way of Mt. Gui, not the Way of the Ox. Clearly, where can one discern the traces?
To err by even a hair’s breadth from the path taken at the time of coming, for ten thousand kalpas there will be no way to emerge. (Baizhang Yuan).
Altering the appearance and changing the head, one’s traces are difficult to conceal when facing the light.
Though one may call out the names "donkey" and "horse," how many bystanders are filled with shame? (Baoning Yong)
The mountain monk on the mountain, the ox below the mountain—clad in fur and wearing horns, they blend into the common stream.
All beings in the universe attain Buddhahood and become patriarchs; yet only Muzhou Daowu becomes a water buffalo. (Foguo Bai)
Hooves and horns clearly defined, reaching everywhere; no need for management, no need for gathering.
Simply knowing not to trespass upon another’s crops, one obtains freedom to follow conditions as they arise regarding water and grass. (Zhenru Zhe)
The old Chan master atop Mount Gui: down the mountain he merely acts as an ox.
If one cannot digest even a tiny bit of right and wrong, what need is there to speak of practicing Chan to realize one's own nature? (Baofeng Xiang)
Turning his hand back, he wrote upon the void; the task was already accomplished. In their frantic haste, people ask about the clarity of both ends.
Had Qu Yuan not encountered the fisherman, who in ten thousand ages would have discussed his solitary sobriety? (Fuxincai)
Wild paths and puddles in hoofprints deceive and kill men; long ago they once plowed through the vast fields of spring.
At times they fall into the weeds with no place to be found—this is the manifestation of the old man of Mt. Mui’s body. (Zhang Wujin)
A thousand heads and ten thousand heads are but one head; riding it here and there, one attains freedom.
Let it loose on the high plateau where water and grass abound, yet at times one must pull in the nose-rope. (Fujian Yongqin)

Moving freely among those of different kinds, one must know that even a thousand sages find it difficult to contain such a person. Blending with the light as the sun shines, the streams and mountains awaken at dawn;
laughing, he points toward that other end of heaven and earth. (Chuan-an Fang)

[Continued Collection] The Water-Ox of Mount Gui. Zen practitioners huddle their heads together to chew upon it. How pitiable—the person carrying the mortar on his back—is called a "Lingnan barbarian" (by Tian Tong Jue).
The spring chill is biting. It freezes the young to death. One must strictly avoid the conflict of the stars Shen and Shang; there is nothing else mysterious or subtle.
(Longmen Yuan) The water-buffalo of Mount Wei is beyond the common stream. It is not Mount Wei, nor is it a cow. Who in all the world can say it?
The sound of waves, the fisherman’s flute, and the fishing boat. (Nantang Xing)
One physical form, two names; entering the mud, entering the water—how pitiable!
Turning the head, one snaps the golden chain and is willing to walk upon the crown of Vairocana’s head. (Biefeng Yin)
Even after a hundred years, I fear no one will know; his name remains inscribed upon his left flank. Entering the water and entering the mud, he is difficult to pasture;
Yangshan can only ride him on one side. (Xutang Yu)

[Added from the Supplementary Collection] Master Miaoyan ascended the hall and said: "The bitter cold of mid-winter is an annual occurrence; as the movement of the sun’s shadow shifts, how is this matter?
Yangshan stepped forward and stood with his hands crossed. The Master said, "I knew well that you could not answer this question.
He then looked toward Xiangyan, who said, "I am uniquely able to answer this question. The Master followed up on the previous point.
Question: Yan also stepped forward, joined his palms, and stood there. The Master said, "Fortunately, I encountered the Son of Silence; otherwise, there would have been no understanding.
He then spoke in verse: "The movement of the sun’s course—what of it? Thread coming and thread going—surely this is mere confusion. Woven into Sichuan brocade in a thousand patterns,"
Skillful! It was nothing more than a single shuttle at that moment.
(Lan’an Shu). With hands folded, he stepped forward. Jizi did not understand. Killing and giving life—what a fine samādhi this is! Such a master!
A calamity for the monastic groves. Where the white clouds end, there are green mountains; the traveler goes even further beyond those green mountains.

(Moon Forest Contemplation). A single pole with a line catches two golden fish; without disturbing the clear waves, their intent is naturally distinct. Slanting the pull of the straw raincoat to cover [the body].
Afterward, only the empty bright moon remains, filling the rivers and lakes.

(Moon over Shixi) A single arrow silently pierces the shadow of the red sun; two hawks have already fallen from the emerald clouds. (Clouds at Leisure) One knows not that Li Guang lacked any hidden artistry;
most look instead toward where the bowstring was released. (Clouds at Leisure)
When Ni Liu Tiemo came to see Guishan, the Master said, "Old cow, you have come. Tiemo replied, "Tomorrow there is a great assembly at Tiantai for a vegetarian feast;
will you, Preceptor, go there as well? The Master then threw himself down and made a gesture of lying down. Tiemo then departed. The Verse says: The old cow arrives at the mountain gate;
The master of the house speaks with a smile. One body lies down, and the other departs; The whole world is filled with their fragrance.
Once I rode an iron horse into the layered city; when the imperial decree was proclaimed, the six kingdoms were heard to be clear. Still grasping the golden whip, I ask the returning traveler:
deep in the night, who walks with me along the Imperial Street? (Xuedou Xian)
Success achieved after a hundred battles, one grows old in great peace. Who would be willing to vie with such leisure? With jade whip and golden horse, one idles all day long;
with bright moon and pure breeze, one’s life is richly fulfilled. (Tiantong Jue)
An old cow has arrived here; tomorrow morning she departs for Mount Tai. In this single melody of white clouds, those who understand her are few;
woodcutters’ songs and fishermen’s chants pass back and forth of their own accord. (Zhang Wujin)
[Continued Collection] The host lacks virtue and the guest lacks the capacity. A flash of lightning flies amidst the sparks of a flint.
In life and death alike, in gain and loss alike—how many can truly know this mind? (Zhong’an Kong).

Cloud-nests, dreams severed; the moon’s brilliance falls in autumn. The Jade Maiden turns her body and passes through the Ox and Cow constellations. Casting off the flower crown, she returns to her old seclusion.
On the dark path and the bird-track, there is as yet no room for gathering. (Zu’an Jian)
Together we enjoy the peace and prosperity of a time when the Way flourishes; meeting one another, we never unfurl our banners or raise our spears.
Beyond the simple rice and clear tea taken as circumstances require, who knows how many there are who can lie down in weariness or stroll at leisure? (Wuzhun Fan)
The grass on the bank is lush and green, enjoying its freedom; at a mere tug, it lifts its head.
Its entire body reveals a uniform whiteness—is this not the water buffalo before the mountain? (Xueyan Qin).
Beating drums and playing the lute, we meet as one family. Having finished singing "The Yangchun," we dip into the snow to eat winter melon. (Yunna Qing).

[Added from the Supplement] A monk asked Miaoyan Shanzhao, "What is the true form of Baizhang? The Master descended from his meditation seat, joined his palms, and stood there. The monk asked, "What is the true form of the Master? The Master sat back down. The verse says: A monk asks about the true form of Baizhang; The Master descends from the seat and stands with palms joined. When asked about the true form of the Master himself, He simply sits back down.
How could this not be the true form? It is the very essence of the Buddhas and patriarchs. If you wish to see it clearly, Look at the old fellow’s face right now.
The face of Baizhang’s cat; the eyes of Guishan’s ghost. Seeing people, he merely smiles in vain; playing with objects, he does not know their names. (Songyuan Yue)
An old woman applies her makeup, staining her lips vermilion; before others, she flaunts her own fine spirit.
Her frowning brow and cold smile are exactly like those of the person beside her who covers her nose in shame. (Shifan Yan)
[Added from the Supplementary Collection] Miaoshan asked Yangshan, "Setting aside the matter of the present for a moment, how is it with the matter of antiquity?
Yangshan approached him with his hands folded. The Master said, "That is still the matter of the present. How is it with the matter of antiquity? Yangshan stepped back and stood there.
The Master said, "You have defeated me; I have defeated you. Yangshan then bowed. — Fang’an Xian.
It is said: Yangshan stepped forward and then withdrew; he looked up to the past and looked clearly into the present. Why did Guishan say, "Each yields to the other"? He then offered this verse:
Meeting at the head of the Brocade River, Hand in hand ascending the wine tower. Knowing how to treat the illness, one remains seldom ill; Understanding one's lot, one does not grieve much.
How profound is the meeting of teacher and disciple! Suddenly, seizing the opportune moment, he asks about the ancient and the present. With hands joined, he steps forward and then retreats;
having passed through a hundred refinements, the true gold is revealed. (Benjue I)

While Master Guishan was seated, Yangshan and Xiangyan were standing in attendance. The Master raised his hand and said, "Nowadays, those who act thus are few, while those who do not act thus are many.
Xiangyan moved from east to west and stood there; Yangshan moved from west to east and stood there.
The Master said, "This causal connection will, thirty years hence, be like gold cast upon the ground. Yangshan [later]...

[The monk] said, "It must also be the Master’s own proclamation for it to be effective. Yanguan said, "Even now, it is not lacking. The Master said, "Shut that dog’s mouth! Verse: The master’s staff strikes the empty sky; The golden-haired lion roars at the blue heavens.
If you wish to see the true face of the Buddha, Look directly at the tip of the staff.
A single cave, golden light, and lion cubs; together they roam and play without concern. Simultaneously, they "peck and hatch," knowing the shifts of opportunity;
the phoenix’s turn and the dragon’s coil are truly marvelous. (Fundamental Awakening, One)
Tianhuai Mountain lets fall his words to distinguish dragons from snakes; a pair of *li* pearls, utterly free of flaw or blemish. Within the lion’s den there are no other beasts;
its glorious reputation shakes the earth and reaches the ends of the world. (Yinjing Yan)
The elephant king stretches and the lion roars; crouching upon the earth, he spans the void, shifting the stars and exchanging the constellations.

He sits and cuts off the tip of the tongue, bidding the dog shut its mouth. Once cast down to the ground, it rings with a golden sound; the nine-bend Yellow River is purified to its very depths. (Nanxing).
Waiting for my lord to arrive, the moon has already set in the west. I do not speak of greetings or farewells; I am drunk as mud. At the fifth watch, where would you wish to go?
Mounting your horse to leave the gate, the crows cry out in the night. (Jichuangzhao)

The successor of the Zen school, in the place where he sits in meditation with eyes closed, plays a ball upon level ground. One must watch with urgent attention.

Guishan asked Yangshan, "How do you understand the wondrous, pure, and luminous mind? He replied, "Mountains, rivers, the great earth, the sun, moon, and stars.
The Master said, "You have grasped only its phenomena. Yangshan said, "Just now, Master, you asked..."
"What is it? The Master said, "The wondrously pure and luminous mind. [The monk] asked, "Can it be called a phenomenon?
The Master said, "Just so, just so. Verse:

The wondrous, pure, and luminous mind is the single phrase of total reality. Mountains, rivers, the great earth, the sun, moon, and stars—exposing one’s liver and draining one’s gall, they shine through from antiquity to the present.
If you are not deluded within this, the entire world is golden. (Xuedou Zong)

The Master said, “It is better to grasp that which you do not understand. The monk asked, “What is that which one does not understand?
The Master said, “It is simply whether it is you or someone else. He further said, “People of the present day should simply realize it directly beneath themselves.”
"It is not that you do not understand; it is precisely your own mind, it is precisely your own Buddha.

If you seek a single point of knowledge or understanding from the outside and take that to be the Way of Chan, you have no connection at all. This is called 'carrying manure in'; it is not called 'carrying manure out.'"
It defiles the field of your mind. This is why it is said that "it is not the Way. The Verse says:
"Delivering charcoal in the snow is enough to bring joy; Adding salt to the sauce is even better.
Often one merely follows the turning of words, Yet remains like a frog’s stride, wallowing in the mud and sand. (Dong-sou Ying)
Guishan asked Yangshan, "Where have you come from? He replied, "From the fields. The Master said, "How many people are there in the fields?
Yangshan stuck his hoe into the ground and stood with his hands folded. The Master said, "There are many people on South Mountain cutting thatch.
Yangshan pulled out the hoe and walked away. Xuansha said, "At that moment, he should have kicked the hoe over."
The Verse says:

At Miaoshan’s place of questioning, few understand; Planting [the staff] in the ground, he answered him, leaving Buddhas and Patriarchs submerged. Tashao was kicked over, yet Pangle remained unconvinced;
Thus sparing the lush greenery from being burdened by the depths of spring. (Touzi Qing)
The time for shallow planting and deep cultivation is precisely now. Entering the mud and entering the water—who else shares this?
On the Southern Mountain, many harvest the thatch grass; only father and son know it. (Baoning Yong)
I ask where you have come from, my dear friend; you plant your spade and stand with hands clasped, your mouth too weary to open.
Although you do not violate the command right before you, how can you deny that your voice resonates throughout the nine realms? (Like a withered tree.)
The Way is exhausted in the union of Master Miu-shan and his son; even as they plant their spades, they still carry the halberds and spears.
To this day, a single well shines like a mirror; from time to time, there are ripples where no wind blows. (Huang-long Chen)
In old age, one realizes that worldly attachments lead to thoughts of children and grandchildren; now, filled with shame, I must establish my own family lineage.
You must remember the words of Nanshan: "Carve them into your bones and engrave them upon your flesh to repay his kindness. (Tiantong Jue)
The golden whip strikes the cave of the azure dragon; It breathes mist and grasps clouds as it emerges from the sea gate. The vast ocean is sucked dry and ascends into the heavens;
Only thunder and lightning remain, filling the mountains and rivers. (Fuxincai)
The numbers are distinct, yet to bring them forth is difficult; there is no monk whose hair does not stand on end. One must know that there is another path within the jar;
simply look upward at the summit of Mount Sumeru. (Longmen Yuan)
Inserting the spade or joining the hands—how they differ yet are the same. It is essential to manifest the total capacity to establish great merit.
Although there are several ways to present this fully, leave behind this lofty transmission to rouse the ancestral wind. (Chuan’an Fang)

[Continued Collection] Hands joined at the chest, the spade thrust deep. How many have left their swords behind to seek them by marking the boat? Before one’s eyes, the water buffalo possesses its full horns;
the way of life in the fields has been so from ancient times to the present. Only after the snowfall does one know the steadfastness of the pine and cypress;

only when faced with difficulty does one see the heart of a true man. Mowing the thatch is entirely the business of the South Mountain; let Bodhidharma cease his talk of being at Shaolin. (Fujian Qin)
I ask you: how many people are there in the field? Placing the spade across the shoulder with hands folded, the meaning is clear. It is a pity they do not follow the Southern Mountain;
let them cast off their burdens and return home, putting an end to the need for questioning the way. (Fóxìng Tái)
Planting the spade and joining the hands—how extraordinary this matter! Who recognizes the pivot of the Master and Son of Mt. Huangbo?
Turning one’s head toward the path beneath the Southern Mountain, the man who went to cut the thatch has long since departed. (Mañjuśrī says.)
The bandits' fires meet just at the fifth watch; seeing the plunder already made, there is no need to dispute it.
In the dark, all is divided according to their share; when dawn breaks, each goes his own way. (Wuzhun Fanzhen)
Coming frequently three or five times a day, sometimes joyful and sometimes angry—do not doubt him when he changes his head and alters his face;
he is originally just the man beneath that peaked cap. (Xutang Yu)

[Added from the Supplementary Collection] While sitting in his quarters, Guishan was asked by Yangshan, "After the Master passes away, if someone asks about the Dharma-way of the late teacher, how will you respond?
The Master said, "A bowl of porridge, a bowl of rice. Yangshan said, "If there is someone who does not approve of that, what then?
The Master said, "An adept monk. Yangshan then bowed. The Master said, "When you meet people..."
One must not err in citing [the examples]. The *Huihai Yi* states: "From antiquity to the present, how many people have offered these words:
'Strict yet without majesty; reverent yet without ritual. Or they cross their staffs and raise their fists.
If it were merely like this, how could one know the place where father and son reach mutual accord? Today, I, this mountain monk, also..."
Wishing that all people might understand together, he spoke in verse:
"Do not distinguish between self and other; self and other are no different. The exhausted fish stays in the shallow pool; the sick bird perches on the reeds.
Hesitating and unable to advance, one's shoes sink into the mud. How can one obtain the Master’s single scroll of scripture?"
When Guishan was at Baizhang, the Head Dharma Master Sīmā asked him, "How do you understand the story of the wild fox?

The Master shook the door panels three times with his hand. The Master said, "Too crude. The Master added, "The Buddha-dharma is not a matter of this kind. Verse: The wild fox’s question, the Master’s answer— Three shakes of the door, no words were spared.
Sīmā called it too crude; the Master said it was not so. In the realm of the Buddhas, there is no such principle.
Who knows who shares the simultaneous movement of cause and effect? Vast and boundless, the four seas have many diverging paths. Lifting one’s head, one presses out the newly risen moon;
thus one imitates Master Zhang in painting the green eyebrows. (Fuxincai)
When spring arrives, the flowers bloom of their own accord; where, then, is that youthful countenance? Piteous are the colors within the garden, yet they do not enter the mirror. (Longmen Yuan)
A blind man comes to grab hold of a mute; they speak words of causelessness, the sprouts of illness.
Once he has grabbed him, all the places that have been itchy throughout one's life are instantly extinguished. (Fodeng Xun)

His wrists possess the strength of a thousand *qun*; who says his entire body is nothing but mud? (Xueyan Qin).
Guishan asked Yangshan, "All day long I have been discussing matters with you; what kind of business have we accomplished? Yangshan drew a line in the air.

The Master said, "If it were not for me, I would surely have been deluded by you. The verse says: All day long discussing matters together, What kind of business has been accomplished? A single stroke drawn in the air— Were it not for me, he would surely have deluded me.

The white ox was born already white; its majestic manifestation is right here—do not seek it elsewhere. I cannot conceal this intricate reality:
directly beneath, it is clearly but one head. (By Prajñārou).
The white ox stands in the open field, free from all barriers; wherever it lies, there it is at ease. It grazes on water and grass as it pleases, fully satisfied with their sweetness;
from it flows pure *amṛta* (clarified butter) to nourish the fertile fields. (Fenyang Shanzhao).
A jade-horned ox with frost-white hair stands revealed upon the open ground; its traces and origins are manifest throughout the human realm and the heavens.

It is not like the one on the Snowy Peaks that roars from time to time, nor does it act like the one at Mount Mui who was gathered in daily. Coldly inhaling the moonlight, it leaves no shadow or form; it wanders freely through lands as numerous as motes of dust.
Suddenly, a cowherd ascends the summit of Mount Sumeru and points out which end of the universe is the "other. (Dongshan Cong)
In the open field, the white ox raises the point of inquiry; following conditions, he bellows, his teeth chattering with cold.
Not knowing what it is that drinks and feeds, he eats and eats until the vast ocean is dried up. (Tiantong Ju)
[Added from the Supplementary Collection] Master Guishan asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "From the Western Capital.
The Master said, "Have you brought a letter from the host of the Western Capital? The monk said, "I dare not falsely transmit any news.
The Master said, "The innate nature of a masterful monk still endures. The monk said, "Who would eat leftover soup and rancid rice? The Master said, "Only you, O *śramaṇa* [attendant], [can]."
Lei would not eat. The monk made a gesture of vomiting. The Master said, "The one who must be carried out is this sick monk.
The monk then went out. The verse says:
Do not be surprised that meeting you brings no news; Who can forever serve as a post station for letters? Even if one were to speak a thousand kinds of words—
[The] Matter. "In whose mind has one reached the ultimate? (Lan'an Shu).

The Fourth Generation under the Sixth Patriarch (Part Two of the Third Generation under Nanyue) [Supplement] Chan Master Xiyun of Huangbo in Hongzhou (Successor of Baizhang). Initially, while traveling at Mount Tiantai, he encountered a monk.
He spoke with him and laughed as if they were old acquaintances. Looking at him closely, his gaze pierced people.

They then walked together until they reached a mountain stream where the water had suddenly risen in flood. [Nanyue] cast aside his hat, leaned on his staff, and stopped. The monk urged the Master to cross with him.
The Master said, "If you wish to cross, brother, cross yourself. The monk immediately lifted his robes and stepped through the waves as if treading on level ground. He looked back.
He said, "Come across! Come across! The Master said, "Tsk! You self-satisfied fellow! Had I known this earlier, I would have cut off your shins.
The monk sighed and said, "Truly a vessel for the Mahāyāna Dharma; I am not his equal. Having finished speaking, he vanished.
The Verse says:
The Way-man is fierce and sharp, difficult to approach; Floating his hat in midstream, he tests the master.
I recall where that man of high attainment has gone— At night deep, he passes over the level sands with the moon. (Xu Tang Yu)
The green waters of the front stream swell as the rain first clears; the floating hat atop the waves is as level as the palm of a hand.
Such is his skill and artifice from the start; let him go, letting him rush forward toward his future destination. (Shixi Yue)
[Added for inclusion] One day, while Huangbo was prostrating before the Buddha in the hall of Yanguan, the Emperor Xuanzong of the Tang dynasty was there as a novice monk (śrāmaṇera).
He asked, "If one does not seek the Buddha, does not seek the Dharma, and does not seek the Sangha, what is it that you, Elder, are seeking by performing this prostration?
The Master replied, "I do not seek the Buddha; I do not seek the Dharma; I do not seek the Sangha."
Miqiu was constantly performing prostrations in this manner. Mili asked, "What is the use of performing prostrations? The Master then struck him with his palm. Miqiu said, "That was too coarse.

The Master said, "What kind of place is this for you to speak of coarse or fine? He struck him again immediately after. The Verse says: The Master struck him; Miqiu called it coarse. The Master struck him again; Miqiu called it fine. If you wish to know the meaning of these words, Look at the two blows of the staff.
The Elephant King tramples; the Lion yawns. How marvelous! Three slaps are bestowed upon a person.
The Great Tang supports the true Son of Heaven; without moving weapons, he brings about peace and prosperity. (Kuchan Jing)
The full mechanism is revealed upon the Golden Hall; how can it compare to the moment of raising an eyebrow or blinking an eye?
Where the claws and fangs were personally wielded three times, the foundation of Great Peace was established amidst war and weapons. (Dongshan Yuan)
Once he struck the king three times with his palm; what inch of merit has the Buddha-dharma ever possessed? This coarse-behaved śramaṇa has sealed off the ultimate limit;
even now there is no ground upon which to stand in shame. (Beihai Xin)
Who shall shoulder the function of this great capacity? The solitary wind of the Ultimate Limit cannot be pursued.
The youth of Jibei has not yet understood it; the Prince already knew its splendor beforehand. (Shixi Yue)
Those who enter through the gate do not possess the family treasure. Slapping her cheek, he bestows a heavy reward with clarity.

In the past and in the future, one sees only great peace. The precious sword sweeps away the clouds and the dragon body appears; even until this very day, the six kingdoms are clear. (Nun Xianlin Ying).
Beneath one’s knees, yellow gold is precious; within the palms of one’s hands, heaven and earth are vast. One rejoices in the meeting of wind and clouds;
across the four seas, all is surging with cold waves. (By Xiyan Hui)
Thunder roars and lightning flashes as the entire mechanism stirs; this is precisely when the hidden dragon sleeps soundly. Suddenly awakening from the dream, the spring sorrow is severed;
the morning breeze blows the rain across the stream before us. (By Xianji Yun)

We meet by the banks of the Jin River; hand in hand we ascend the wine tower. Having mastered medicine, one suffers little illness;

When the State Councilor Pei was stationed at Wanling, he established a great Zen monastery and invited Master Huangbo to preach the Dharma there. Because the Master deeply cherished his former mountain retreat, the monastery was named Huangbo after him. One day, the Councilor placed a statue of the Buddha before the Master and knelt, saying, "I request the Master to bestow a name upon it. The Master called out, "Pei Xiu! The Councilor responded, "Yes? The Master said: "Your name is 'Xiu' (to cultivate). This Buddha is the 'Ultimate Cultivation. Why do you seek another name for it? If you seek another name, you will never find it. The Councilor bowed and departed. Later, when the Councilor returned to the capital, he asked the Master, "What did you say to me that day? The Master replied, "I told you that your name is 'Cultivation,' and this Buddha is the 'Ultimate Cultivation. Why seek another name? If you seek another name, you will never find it. The Councilor said, "I have understood. The Master said, "If you have understood, then go and practice cultivation. The Councilor bowed and departed. He then composed a verse: "The name is not the name; the name is the ultimate name. If one seeks another name, it is like seeking the horns of a rabbit. He sent this verse to the Master, who praised it, saying, "This is truly the work of a man of great capacity. The Councilor then had the verse inscribed on a stone tablet and erected it within the monastery. It remains there to this day. The Master later remarked, "The Councilor has attained the Way. [The Master] said, "I have finished bestowing a name upon you. The official bowed in prostration. The verse says:
Kneeling before the Master, he offered himself to request a name; Suddenly, at the very point of encounter, he called out once.
Were it not for Lord Pei, who would dare respond? He has forced even the deaf and blind to open their hearing. (Fenyang Zhao)
At that time, Prime Minister Pei forgot his name; when called by others, he immediately became alert again.
One does not know how it was before even being formed in the womb—who would dare to defile this numinous spirit? (Foyin Yuan).
Adorned with five colors, it is held aloft in the palms; the Old Barbarian has merely established a hollow name.
If you now wish to transcend all patriarchs, you must walk upon the Vajra Peak (Bao-ning Yong).
"It is not mind, nor is it Buddha. Huangbo calls him out—what thing is this? From then on, Lord Pei recognized a hollow name;
the monks of the world cannot leap out of it. (Cao Tang Qing)
Holding it up before him, he requested his name; Huangbo called out from on high with a single shout.
He stripped away his former true face, and from this point on, he was able to assist in purifying the national wind. (Chu Anfang)

[Continued Collection] Where Master Pei attained awakening, all clamor and error ceased. A foot of water can overturn ten thousand fathoms of waves. Within the mechanism of the thunderclap, the living eye is turned back;
within the sharp edge of a phrase, the war drums are silenced. On the mountain peak, the path is briefly traversed; thick with green, ten thousand branches, a single point of red.
Such springtime that moves the heart requires no more than this. (Zhandang Shen).
The name is correct and the characters are also correct. When the form is upright, the shadow must be upright. To call out "Come! and then respond with "Go!
is like mixing donkey dung with sandalwood. (Xiyan Hui)
A mere physical frame, provisionally called "Buddha"; summoned here and there, forcibly named "Who.
To know that herein it is difficult to establish anything—this Minister of State must be from the great clan of Pei. (Xianji Yun)
Huangbo said, "You are all nothing but fellows who eat dregs of wine. Do you know that within the Great Tang there are no Chan masters?
At that time, a monk asked, "The various quarters gather great crowds; why do you say instead that there are no Chan masters? Huangbo replied, "I do not say there are no Chan;

I simply say there are no masters. A verse says: All of you are dregs-eating fellows; Do you know there are no Chan masters in the Great Tang? When a monk asked about the crowds gathering in all directions, He said: "I do not say there is no Chan, It is simply that there are no masters."
Majestic and awe-inspiring, yet he does not boast of it himself. Abiding calmly within the world, he settles dragons and snakes. The Emperor of Dazhong once dared to provoke him lightly;
three times he personally encountered the brandishing of his claws and fangs. (Xuedou Xian)
Teacherless adepts fill the Great Tang; those who merely consume dregs of wine cannot understand. Passing idly through the bamboo temple, spring is already deep;
falling flowers scatter across the hue of the moss. (Fohuiquan)
Within the land of the Great Tang, there is no Chan master. Hand-in-hand with you, we shall return home. I cast my hook intending to catch a Kun or a Jing;
who would have known that I would catch this lame turtle? (Baiyun Wenzhun).
In Mount Huangbo, he clearly reveals himself to the assembly; within the Great Tang Empire, he conceals his form in darkness.
A corner of his *kāṣāya* still trails upon the ground—who among those in the monastic groves has eyes to see? (Fujian Yongqin).
In the land of the Great Tang, there are no Chan masters. They do not permit understanding; they only permit knowing.
When the flesh-bound sweatshirt is finally cast off, one then realizes that the blows and shouts were but deceptions for the foolish. (Longmen Yuan)
In the land of the Great Tang there is no Zen master; having prostrated and returned to the hall, he has no further doubts.
How laughable is the son-in-law of Heyang! He is not even equal to Linji’s little page. (Gushan Gui)
Only when you put on clothes upon your body will you escape the cold; merely speaking of food at the mouth will never satisfy one’s hunger.
This "granny’s Zen" within the land of the Great Tang—I shall today explain it through for you to the end. (Jingshan Gaofeng)
[Continued Collection] Transcending the phenomenal world, his body spans the universe; where sage and ordinary being reach their limit, not even a speck of dust can remain.
The spirit of a patch-robed monk ought to be thus: who on the field is the one to seize the banner? (Xuedou Zong)
To have dhyāna without a teacher is truly laughable; where in the Great Tang Empire could one find it?
How many weary travelers there are, who eat nothing but dregs of wine and collapse by the roadside! (Lan’an Shu).
Proclaiming the wondrous meaning amidst a thicket of brambles; emitting rays of light within a garden of thistles. Of thousands of words and myriad phrases, no one understands;
once more, following the warbling oriole over the low wall. (Huitong Dan)
Resolve is severed at the place of kin; poverty finds rest by the side of the wealthy. With a hundred thousand strings of cash girding one’s waist, one rides a crane up to Yangzhou. (Huican)
The great smelter forging gold does not follow but one path; the starless scale determines every grain and fraction.
This very lack of a teacher is the leak; the small boat has already passed beyond Lake Dongting. (Tu’an Qi)
When the hexagram is pasted on the Gate of Ghosts, even ghosts are startled; yet another sight appears: the hair-tufted Broom Star.
If one can pass through and verify the seal of Lord Guan, at night one shall walk the Imperial Street hand-in-hand. (Zhong’an Kōng).
Within the land there is no teacher; his eye is supreme. He clearly brandishes the seven-star sword.
If there were no blood beneath the skin of the patch-robed monk, he would not avoid continuing as before to eat dregs of wine. (Eh! [This is] the Mirror of the Hermitage.)
The mountain cave door has no lock; the Jian Gate is steep and lofty. The wind and dew are high and cold; it is certainly not the human realm. Is this so?

Whether it be heaven or the human world, who can know how many times [this has been asked]? As for "how many," when a monk once asked, he could not bring forth an answer. Huangbo’s entire body is nothing but mud and water.
(Yun’an Yan): Within the Great Tang Empire there is no Chan master;

one who brandishes the single-pointed staff is nowhere to be seen. Vast and boundless is the universe, and countless are the people; how many among these men are true sons of courage? (Yuelin Guan): Within the Great Tang Empire there is no Chan master;
one who brandishes the single-pointed staff is nowhere to be seen. Vast and boundless is the universe, and countless are the people; how many among these men are true sons of courage?

This is simply the bitter-mouthed Zen of one without a teacher; in all the world, none is as bitter as Huangbo. (Pak Ong-hyeon)

Huangbo replied, "I am simply performing my duties along with the assembly. Baizhang said, "It must have been a great labor for you. Huangbo replied, "How could I dare refuse such toil? Baizhang asked, "How much land have you cleared?

Huangbo took his hoe and struck the ground three times. Baizhang then shouted. Huangbo— [continued by shouting back].* *Note: The source text ends abruptly here; the traditional kōan narrative continues with Baizhang shouting, to which Huangbo shouts in response.*
He covered his ears and departed. The verse says:
When we meet and converse, the principle is not deficient; Yet in an ordinary turn of the head, we part ways. In the end, water must flow toward the sea;
In the final analysis, clouds must seek the mountain to return. (Longmen Yuan)
[Added for inclusion] Chan Master Huánzhōng of Dàcí Mountain in Hángzhōu (he was a successor of Bǎizhàng) ascended the hall and said:
"This mountain monk cannot answer questions; I can only recognize the illness. At that time, a monk stepped forward, and the Master immediately returned to his quarters.
Fǎyǎn said: "The assembly calls this 'the illness,' yet it is right before their eyes and they do not recognize it. Xuánjué said: "But tell me—"
The Great Compassionate One recognizes sickness but does not recognize sickness. This monk has come forth—is this sickness or not?
His daily walking and staying cannot be entirely sickness. If you say it is not sickness, then what of his coming forth?
The Verse says:
Light as a hair-tip, heavy as a mountain; from the earth’s edge to the world’s end, going and returning again. When the yellow leaves fall, the wind-bone is revealed;
by the water’s edge, the stones remain as variegated as before. (Xutang Yulu)
[Added from another source: One day, because Zhaozhou asked Daci, "What is the essence of *prajñā*?
the Master replied, "What is the essence of *prajñā*? Zhaozhou laughed loudly and departed. The next day, while Zhaozhou was sweeping the floor, the Master said, "What is the essence of *prajñā*?
Zhaozhou set down his broom, clapped his hands, and laughed loudly. The Master then returned to his quarters.
The Verse says: What is its essence? A laugh of "he-he. Overthrowing the one right before you is the trap for the tiger.
A bird carrying fragrance emerges from within the flowers; A dragon containing rain returns toward the cave. (Xinwen Ben)
[Added from the Supplementary Collection] Chan Master Pitan Pu’an of Taizhou (heir to Baizhang). One day, the Master visited Maoyuan.
As soon as Maoyuan rose to greet him, the Master seized him and said, "To open the mouth is to lose;

to close the mouth is to perish. Apart from these two paths, I ask you, Master, to speak otherwise. Maoyuan covered his nose with his hand. The Master let go of him and said, "The first step is easier."

The second step is more difficult. Yuan said, "Why such a frantic rush? The Master said, "Had it not been for you, Master, I would have been subject to scrutiny by those in all quarters. The verse says:
The main peak is high and the secondary peak low; how many times have we seen the clouds part only to close again? It is like the place where one can face the evening pavilion:
two peaks stand opposite each other, utterly without difference in height. (The "utterly" [絕] is like a mirror.)
In this clash, we joyfully encounter our match; fist comes and kick goes, as the two repay one another.
In that place where hands and faces intermingle, even the keenest hawk’s eye or falcon’s gaze cannot find it. (By Zhuyu Jian)
[Added for inclusion: When a monk arrived at Píngtián, the Master struck him immediately. The monk stepped forward and seized the staff. The Master said, "A moment ago you were too hasty.
The monk snatched the staff away and struck the Master in return. The Master said, "An adept! An adept! The monk bowed.
The Master stepped forward and made a gesture as if to intervene; the monk let out a great laugh, shook his sleeves, and departed. The Master said, "A grass-thief!"
A great defeat. The verse says:
The Patriarch’s command was first put into practice; it can indeed be observed. To exchange it with another is utterly groundless.
Fortunately, one strikes the man within; it will not be difficult for the grass-robber to finally recognize him. (Benjue I)
Chan Master Jingcen Zhaoxian of Changsha in Hunan (he was a successor of Nanquan).

A lean crane perches upon a withered tree; a wild ape howls atop an ancient terrace. (Dū, Xuandou Xian) Fragrant mountain breezes flutter and fly along the path.
Wildflowers fall and the grasses lie in disarray. The spring wind holds infinite, profound meaning;

Thin mists filter the crimson sun; light smoke carpets the green moss. If you seek to understand this through poetic lines, you will bury the talent of the Dharma King.

(Fojiàn Qín). [Continued Collection] Carrying my staff, I take leisurely steps through the void. The head seat in the hall asks, "Where have you come from? All hidden wonders and concealed excellences are utterly exhausted;
one does not travel back and forth through the mountains in vain. (Běnjué Yī).
Falling flowers and lush green grass are like spread brocade; springtime fills the eyes like a painted scroll.
To meet one another at the gate with such intimacy is far superior to autumn dew dripping upon lotuses. (Yuǎnwù Qín)
Fragrant grasses weave a carpet, green beneath one’s steps; Falling flowers spread brocade, their scent brushing the robes. Upon returning, I shall describe this to the sons of dhyāna:
Vast and boundless is the splendor that circles the painted beams. [Blank] [Blank] [Blank].

The monk asked, "How is it when those of the highest caliber meet one another? The Master said, "Like the hands of a dead man."
The verse says: The eyes of the dead man; the hands of the dead man. The golden crow flies, the jade hare runs. Directly cutting off the source, take it from either side.
Old Zhang falls drunk on the official street; It was originally Old Li drinking private wine. (Seu Yinkong)
[Added for collection] A monk asked Changsha, "When one has realized it, karmic obstacles are originally empty; when one has not yet realized it, one must repay past debts.

As for the Second Patriarch, was he realized or not? The Master said, "Empty. He then asked Yunmen, who said, "Certain. The Verse says: When the moon is full, the night is bright; When the sun rises, the morning is clear. If you wish to know the Second Patriarch, He is like a stone—solid and firm.

Changsha was open; Yunmen was firm. Picking up whatever came to hand, they were not acting contrivedly. To study by departing from mind, intellect, and consciousness is to emerge from the path of sages and ordinary beings.
As soon as there is even a hair’s breadth [of attachment], a flying serpent will coil around one's feet. (Daguishou)

The person who does not move atop the hundred-foot pole—though they have gained entry, it is not yet the truth.
One must advance further from the hundred-foot pole; the ten directions of the world are one’s entire body. A monk then asked, "As for that hundred-foot pole, how does one advance?
The Master said, "Mountains of Langzhou, waters of Lingzhou. The monk said, "I do not understand. The Master said:
The four seas and five lakes lie within the imperial transformation.
