When the battle of Dharma took place before the Yellow Crane Tower, hundreds of thousands of Buddhas raised their banners of victory.
Since he has no land, where does he dwell? He leaves behind for the gifted one this single poem. (Sixin Xin)
Hearing his name, one is startled through heaven and earth; to further ask where he dwells is but self-deception. Turning back, he ascends the path of return;
beneath every door, one penetrates Chang’an. (Lingyuan Qing)
The "Poem on Huanghe Lou" was composed by Cui Hao. Throughout ancient and modern times, no one has been able to match its rhymes in their own verses.
The moon’s reflection in the autumn sky is imprinted upon a thousand rivers; at the break of spring dawn, the orioles sing out everywhere. (Da Hong Sui)
Do not seek elsewhere for the sacred traces of the thousand Buddhas; Changsha’s turning of the pivot has its own source. If you wish to know the place where one is face-to-face and cannot be hidden:
it is at the Yellow Crane Tower, before the Piyangzhou Isle. (Heshan Fang)
The waters of the sea may at some time finally reveal their bottom; But throughout one's life until death, one does not know one's own mind.
If a scholar understands the phrase for turning over the body, He will surely enter the Hanlin Academy while still dressed in white. (Cishou Shen)
From atop Huanghe Lou, the four quarters stretch afar; the wind and moon filling the heavens belong to the poets. Where do the hundreds of thousands of Buddhas dwell?
The wind rises over the Long River, surging with flower-like waves. (Puyongping)
A hundred thousand Buddhas ride oxen backward; facing each other clearly, they lose the way.
They then ask the Master, "Where are you going?"—I urge you to ascend one more floor. (Huanglong Zhen)
The names of hundreds of thousands of Buddhas have been heard for a long time; where can one seek the adornment of their lands?
If you lack the eye of penetrating clarity to behold them face-to-face, you will merely follow the Boatman down to Yangzhou. (Nanhua Heng)
Though one may hear the names of hundreds of thousands of Buddhas, when has their land ever not been manifest and perfected? From this moment on, there is no returning;
once you have returned, you shall attain it. Who else can vie for the misty scenery of the Five Lakes? (Baofeng Ming)
[Continued Collection] Longmen Yuan said: "The assembly, when the scholar asked where the Buddha resides, why did Changsha speak in such a manner?
A scholar usually composes verses on the wind and the moon; why was he unable to utter a single word before Changsha?
If it had been the Yellow Crane Tower, what difficulty would there have been in posing a question? Listen."
I take up the mountain monk’s riddle and offer this verse:
"Your countenance is most wondrous and marvelous, Your radiance illuminates the ten directions. I have previously made offerings to you, And now once again come to behold you in person.

When we conversed before the Yellow Crane Tower, White artemisia and red smartweed faced each other by the riverbank. My innermost feelings were already poured forth, yet there was no one to hear them.
I understand. Only the clear wind and bright moon know.
(Tiantong Jue) As soon as red earth was used to paint a winnowing fan, why did the black rooster suddenly take flight?
Since these lines were inscribed into a new poem, one has forgotten how to return before the Yellow Crane Tower. (Yuetang Chang)
Before the Yellow Crane Tower lies Parrot Isle; the evening sun sets westward as the waters flow east.
If you wish to know where all Buddhas dwell, listen to the rustling wind-blown leaves as the moon fills the tower. (Nantang Si)
A single verse was inscribed before the Yellow Crane Tower; countless scholars lost their prosodic balance. Changsha’s "One Eye" remains long and vast;
from antiquity to the present, where has it ever left a trace? (Xinwen Ben).
Majestic and wondrous, his true marks are truly beyond compare; his distinct Brahma-voice is even more extraordinary.

Alas, those who pursue every phrase and seek the words miss the opportunity of Changsha’s face-to-face encounter. Whether you know it or not: Huanghe Lou was inscribed with a poem by Cui Hao. (Fóxìng Tàiyī).
A hundred thousand Buddhas inquire after his origins; Cui Hao once inscribed the Yellow Crane Tower. After the snow, bamboo fences and plum blossoms burst forth in profusion;
One branch leaning over the water is most elegant and refined. (Lan’an Shu)
The *xiǎn* bird guards the tree; the fish follow it in the empty pond. As the *xiǎn* passes beneath its feet, the *xiǎn* remains entirely unaware. (Dun’an Yan)
Cui Hao once inscribed a poem upon Yellow Crane Tower: "Springtime above is seldom visited by travelers; Its fragrant essence has already followed the fading spring away.
Countless mad bees cling to it, their passion never ceasing. (Zantang Shen)
Cui Hao once inscribed the Yellow Crane Tower; Changsha picked it up and called it elegant.
The entire great trichiliocosm is one's own family inheritance—when have the Buddhas ever had a fixed location? (Hunyuan Mi)
The scholar seeks fire and finds only smoke; Changsha sells stone and has an abundance of clouds.
If you wish to know on what land the thousand Buddhas dwell, you will win only the ever-increasing value of your poetry and Chan. (I’an Kwon)
A poem before the Yellow Crane Tower: "Taking a broom and painting it like a蛾眉 (eyebrow). This is the true message of the hundreds of thousands of Buddhas;
I present it clearly to you face-to-face. (Songyuan Yue)
A single cloth towel atop a hundred-foot pole clearly depicts the springtime at a wine shop.
Meeting [a friend] and returning empty-handed without drinking—clear moon and pure breeze laugh at such a person. (Yanshi Kai)

"Where do the hundreds of thousands of Buddhas dwell? Though Cui Hao once inscribed his poem on the Yellow Crane Tower, even with his guts turned upside down and his bowels emptied out, he still did not understand it.
The Great River flows eastward by itself through the ages. (Tianmu Li)
Where do the hundreds of thousands of Buddhas dwell? The poetry of the Yellow Crane Tower is not as fine as brocade.
I ask you, young scholar, have you composed it yet? Take up this one piece and do not hesitate. (Shitai Kun)
[Added from another source: While Changsha and Yangshan were enjoying the moon, Yangshan said, "Everyone possesses this very thing, yet they cannot make use of it.
The Master said, "That is exactly where you need help; let me lend you my hand to use it for you. Yangshan asked, "How would you use it?
The Master gave him a kick straight in the chest. Yangshan said, "Powerful! You are like a great tiger! From that time on, [he became renowned] throughout all quarters.
He was called "Cen the Tiger. Changqing said, "In the first case, both were masters; in the latter, both were not masters.
He then added separately, "A false dharma is difficult to support. The verse says:
Floating clouds have dispersed and the moon hangs in the sky; a rabbit conceives and gives birth to a great beast.
It leaps forth before the wind, brandishing its fangs and claws, shaking the Palace of Cold Radiance to this very day. (Cao Yuansheng)
The author’s grasp is utterly distinct: a pure breeze rises within the Palace of Vast Cold.
Though one may have stepped upon it and remains alive for a moment, one has already fallen into another's pitfall. (He opens his room.)
A monk asked Changsha, "Does the person of original nature become a Buddha or not?
The Master said, "Do you see the Emperor of the Great Tang ever cutting thatch or mowing grass himself? The monk said, "I do not know who it is that becomes a Buddha."
The Master said, "This is you becoming a Buddha. The monk was speechless. The Master asked, "Do you understand? He replied, "I do not understand.

The Master said, "It is like a person who falls because of the ground and rises because of the ground. What does the 'ground' do? Verse: Falling because of the ground, rising because of the ground— What function does the ground perform? If you wish to see the Buddha-nature, Look directly at the person before you.
Master Cen brushed his sleeves and set the great mechanism in motion; though many inquire of the Buddha, those who become Buddhas are few.
The Prince cut the thatch with his own hands, unable to add further mud upon the earth. (Fenyang Shao)
Palaces and halls stack upon one another, deep with purple vapors; the stars divide their positions, rectifying heaven and earth.
Without governing the realm of Jambudvīpa by means of the golden wheel, how could he be compared to the venerable treasure-seals of the feudal lords? (Touzi Qing)
Behind the curtains, the spring breeze is still cold at dawn. The song in the tower falters as dreams shatter. The golden carriage does not travel through the world of men;
do not envy the vastness of the sun and moon within the alchemical elixir jar. (Yunyan Yin)
[Continued Collection] How could the Great Mountain ever lack soil? How could the Tang Emperor possibly cut down the thatch? Prostrating and approaching, he joined his palms.

Ten thousand miles of distant journey from the Western Heaven—the ancient Buddha is none other than oneself; oneself is none other than the ancient Buddha. Coral glistens through the springtime of the Ten Islands;
the moon reflects and steals the splendor from the palace of the Black Dragon King. (By Yuanwu Keqin)
[Added from the Supplementary Collection] Changsha, acting on the instruction of Sansheng, had the senior monk Xiù ask the Master, “Where has Nánquán gone after his passing?
The Master said, “When Shítóu was a novice śrāmaṇera, he studied under the Sixth Patriarch.
Xiù said, “I am not asking about Shítóu seeing the Sixth Patriarch; where has Nánquán gone after his passing? The Master said, “He taught [the Dharma].”
Yixun went to see him. Xiu said, "Although the Master has a thousand-foot cold pine, he lacks a sprouting-stalk stone shoot.
The Master remained silent. Xiu said, "Thank you, Master, for your response. The Master also remained silent.
Upon returning, Xiu recounted this to Sansheng, who said, "If it were like that, it would still surpass Linji’s seven steps. Nevertheless..."
"I shall wait to verify this further. When the next day the Three Sages came up and asked, "I have heard that yesterday you, Master, spoke one phrase regarding Nanquan’s passing;
it may truly be said to outshine the past and surpass the future, something rarely heard from ancient times to the present," the Master remained silent. The verse says:
The guest sees that the roads and lanes of Changsha are the same as before; he bids the man go and inquire about the family traditions. Sumeru, ten thousand fathoms high, grinds through the ages;
to break off a bamboo arrow to measure the heavens is but a waste of effort. (Foyin Yuan)

Changsha is like washing water with water; this monk falls down by himself and gets up by himself. Sansheng sticks his head out in a special way, selling off the entire garden of peaches and plums. (Yuedang Chang)
The Old Man of Changsha, the Old Man of Changsha! Entering into principle, how can one seek his profound discourse? Last night at the third watch, the handle of the Dipper hung low;
as before, the sky was bright and the sun shone radiantly. Do you know of Nanquan’s passing into extinction?
Its transmission through ancient and modern times is truly marvelous, truly marvelous! Who among those in the snow can discern the plum blossom? (Dàyuánzhì)
The Probing Flower and Butterfly dance on the Three Platforms; the Woodpecker shakes its head and cries out like a startled drum.
Everywhere one meets the Great Tiger Cen; it turns out he is none other than the Tiger of Changsha. (Changling Zhuo)
The Zen of Radish Head is a noisy nuisance; though the frost-knife cuts it repeatedly, no trace remains. From of old, it has not been subject to human chewing;
it allows only the patch-robed monks to swallow it whole. (Zhengtang Bian)
How truly marvelous, how truly marvelous! Changsha painted a tiger, yet it turned out to be a wildcat. Once Nanquan departed, there has been no news;
he leaves only passersby to engage in idle disputes. (Fujian Qin)
Who can know the old traces of the King? How could one bear to ask the tiger’s cub further?
Even if the stone sprouts were to grow branches until their end, there would be no place to find the upward-moving principle. (Touzi Shu)
How truly marvelous, how truly marvelous! In its unfolding and rolling up, its appearing and disappearing, one beholds the complete function.
Were it not for the discerning eyes of Zhang Hua, one could not avoid following others in their judgments of right and wrong. (Shixi Yue)
[Added from the Supplementary Collection] A monk asked Changsha, "How can one transform the mountains, rivers, and lands so that they return to oneself?
The Master said, "How can one transform oneself so that it becomes mountains, rivers, and lands? The monk said, "I do not understand. The Master said:
"Under the walls of the city in Hunan, it is good for nourishing the people; rice is cheap and firewood is plentiful, sufficient for all four neighbors.
The monk remained silent. The Master showed him this verse: "Who turns the mountains and rivers? The mountains and rivers turn toward whom? Perfect penetration has no two sides."
The nature of phenomena has no place of return. The verse says:
In every dust mote and land, this body is ordinarily revealed; When doubt arises and emotion stirs, one perceives distance and intimacy. This has always been the case within the city of Hunan:
Rice is cheap and firewood is plentiful, sufficient for all four neighbors. (Baoning Yong)
Who asks of mountains and rivers when they understand the turning of the body? Only through this turning does one realize the wholeness of the true essence.
Within the pure realm there is not a single thing; behind each mountain range lies another person. (Great Perfect Wisdom)
A single luminous sphere, neither inside nor outside; in Old Lu’s mirror, not a speck of dust remains. Mountains, rivers, and the great earth are not other things;
the myriad phenomena reveal this very body. Since there is no one left who can understand this, tell them: "In Hunan, it is good to nourish the people. [Seal] □□□.
Thereupon, a monk asked Changsha, "What is the teacher of all Buddhas? The Master said, "From immeasurable kalpas past, upon whose grace and power have you relied?
The verse says: From immeasurable kalpas past, Upon whose grace and power have you relied? If you can understand this, Then you will know the teacher of all Buddhas.
Neither ink-wash nor colored pigment can capture its form; it is a mysterious spirit within the bamboo and trees.
Seeking blessings and fortune, they cast their cups and divinations, yet when the Way is explained clearly before them, they do not listen. (Baoning Yong)
Before the primordial chaos was divided, there already was He. His majestic appearance is beyond all description or model.
Changsha spoke in vain of the power of receiving grace; let us ask: has anyone ever truly recognized Him? (Shushan Chang)
Chan Master Lizong of Zihu Rock in Quzhou (a successor of Nanrong) resided at the Zihu Monastery.
He posted a sign at his gate that read: "At Zihu there is a dog; it takes people's heads from above, their hearts from within, and their feet from below.
To hesitate for even a moment is to lose one's life. Two monks from Linji’s assembly [encountered this].

As the attendant was about to lift the curtain, the Master shouted, "Look at the dog! The attendant looked back, and the Master immediately returned to his quarters. Someone once asked, "What is the dog of Zihu? The Master said, "Bark! Bark! The Verse says: Bark! Bark! The whole world is filled with this sound. If you can hear it, You will know the dog of Zihu. If you cannot hear it, You will never find the path of the Buddhas and Patriarchs. Even if you were to search for ten thousand years, You would still not encounter him. How pitiful! How regrettable! It is like a man who has lost his way. If you wish to see the true face of the Buddha, You must first pass through this barrier. If you do not pass through this barrier, You will never attain liberation. If you can pass through this barrier, You will see the Buddha’s true face. This is the teaching of the Buddhas and Patriarchs; It is the essential principle of all dharmas. If you can understand this, You will realize the meaning of the ancient sages. At Zihu’s hall, the passage of people is cut off; it is solely because the dog before the hall is so fierce. At the mere sight of its shadow or the sound of its voice, one’s heart and gall are struck with terror;
facing it head-on, how could one avoid losing one’s life? (Zhengjue Yi)
The dog of Zihu is most fierce and formidable. Those who come seeking enlightenment must not walk in darkness. When you look toward it, it seems as if it is not there;
yet it bites you dead right before your face, ending your life. (Foguo Bai).

This poor family has nothing at all; they keep only a single dog. Even if a Buddha were to appear, he would still have to meet with one bite. (Yan Ruru)
One has missed the single pivot that crosses the gate; the ready-made public case remains obscured. Where Zihu points is too intimate;
one must immediately fix the eyes upon it. (Zhe’ung Yan).

The fishing line in his hand winds and unwinds again; he strokes his small boat upon Lake Dongting. Suddenly, a fierce wave overturns the void;
gathering himself back, he has not a single skill left. (Yuepo Ming)

The Monk of Mount Juyuyu in Ezhou (a successor of Nanquan) asked a monk, "Monk, have you come here to sightsee and enjoy the scenery, or have you come to inquire about the Way and practice Zen? The monk replied, "Venerable Sir, please try to explain it yourself.
The Master said, "Carving oysters and engraving clams—this is nothing but impervious mud; your journey from afar has been in vain. The monk said, "My whole body is made of iron."
[The monk] was struck once with a mallet. The Master said, "A surrendered general is not executed. The Verse says:
With a staff of bamboo, he walks beneath the grove upon the green moss; In the turmoil of a weary life, his eyes remain unopened.
How wonderful that the flowers' redness and the water's greenness Flow forth all at once from within the cave. (Dizang’s Grace)

Wandering through mountains and playing by the waters is but an ordinary affair; returning at dawn or dusk, my hair is like frost. Treading through worn-out straw sandals, I turn my head to look back:
the sound of several cries from a monkey reaches this land of white clouds. (Baoning Yong)
Coming, they come together; going, they go together. One must know that coming and going, though occurring at the same time, do not share the same step.
A duck by the pond listens to the thunder; on the ridge, the wind blows through the trees. The Yellow River flows in nine bends, its depths forever turbid;
for three thousand years, it has been clear but once. (Fujian Qin)
[Zhuyou ascends the hall: "All of you, do not drive stakes into empty space. At that time, the senior monk Lingxu stepped forward from the assembly and said, "Empty space itself is the stake.
The Master struck him. Lingxu said, "Master, do not strike me in error. The Master then returned to his quarters. The verse says: Do not drive stakes into empty space;
Lingxu brings up the very stake. A blow lands upon the head; The Master returns to his quarters. If you wish to know the meaning, Look at the staff in his hand.
"Who understands this 'sky-nail'? Only Lingxu is most skilled at investigating it.
Though the decrepit Zuyou relies on his influence, his dragon-head and snake-tail are utterly beyond endurance. (Benjue I)
[Added to the Collection] Chan Master Tanzhao of Baima in Jingnan (a successor of Nanquan) often said, "How joyful! How joyful!
Yet when his end approached, he cried out in pain, saying, "King Yama has come to take me!
When the head of the monastery asked him, "Master, in the past you were thrown into the water by the Regional Commander, yet your countenance remained unmoved; why is it that now you [react so?]"
"It is thus. The Master raised his pillow and said, "Tell me, was it so at that time? Is it so now? The Master had no reply.
Fayan spoke on his behalf, saying, "At that time, he simply covered his ears and went out. The verse says:
One, two, three, four, five. Metal, wood, water, fire, earth. They are stirred by thunder and lightning; they are moistened by wind and rain.
Who was this fellow? When alive, he was a blur; when dead, he was a blur. (Pah! (The grace of Kṣitigarbha!)
When the sweet melon reaches its stem, it is sweet; when the bitter gourd is rooted, it is bitter. When you pick up the pillow, New Ra beats the drum at night. (Baofeng Zhao)
Lifelong clamoring for joy; at the end of life, there is no one to rely upon. The sweet melon is sweet from stem to tip;
the bitter gourd is bitter from root to fruit. (Yuanzhao’s Text)
Chan Master Yunji Shizu of Zhongnan Mountain (who succeeded Nanquan) first visited Nanquan.
He asked, "The *maṇi* jewel no one recognizes; it is intimately held within the *tathāgatagarbha*. What is this *garbha*?
Nanquan said, "That which comes and goes with you, Old Teacher Wang—that is the *garbha*. (Xuedou said: "A fellow in the weeds. The Master [Yunji]...
Xuedou said: "How is it when one does not even go back and forth? Jianquan said: "That too is a concealment.
(Xuedou said: "Adding frost to snow. The Master asked again: "What is the pearl? (Xuedou said: "Dangerous! Jianquan called out, "Master Zu!"
The Master assented. Yuanquan said, "You do not understand my words. The Master gained faith and entered [the Way].

Xuedou said, "To employ clever stratagems at the top of a hundred-foot pole is not the mark of a skilled hand. If you can apply a single eye here, such that guest and host interchange, you will be able to penetrate deeply into the tiger’s den.
If it is not so, then even if the Master and Patriarch attained enlightenment, it would still be of no avail."
He is also one who has the head of a dragon but the tail of a snake.

Distinguishing right from wrong clarifies gain and loss; responding to this, one points to all things as if they were on the palm of one's hand. Coming and going, or not coming and going—this very thing is the treasury.
The Wheel-Turning King rewarded those who had merit; the Yellow Emperor attained it through the formless (Wangxiang). It turns the pivot of function; such is its skillful artifice.
"An enlightened-eyed monk must not be reckless. (Tiantong Jue) "Coming and going is the hidden pearl;
where is it? Only by letting go can one know it is not to be sought outside. Even if the *wangxiang* finds it, it is still a matter of standing out from the ordinary.
Turn the light back upon itself and rest content. (Haiyin Xin)
[Continued Collection] The blue hawk pursues the hare; the black dragon plays with the pearl. Penetrating the unblinking blue eyes, how could the hand that illuminates objects be empty?

Coming and going, yet not coming and going—this is merely a messy smearing upon the grass. Entering the tiger’s den from atop a hundred-foot pole, clearly the moon rises over the long coral. (Yuánwù Qín).
To gather it is easy; to see it is difficult. To see it is easy; to use it is difficult. Seeing it and using it are two things that are no different.
Carelessly grasping a single flute to return home, one blows it deep into the night across the Mulu Bay. (Dun’an Yan)
Clearly, the moon rises upon the long coral; a single fragment of radiant splendor dazzles the great void. All sentient beings of the earth enjoy it together;

A single dark pearl is never obscured; throughout kalpas it has never turned away from anything.
Alas for the ignorant and deluded pauper, who day after day wanders aimlessly with the crowd. Nanquan emptied his sorrowful heart, like pouring water over a duck’s back.
Now, bringing it forth directly, he strikes it to pieces right before one’s face. (Puan Yu)

Question: "If you have attained it, you can speak of it; if you have not attained it, you still cannot speak of it. Where has Hou Bai ever been white? How could Hou Hei be black? I value Master Wang;
he is the thief among thieves in all under heaven. The Grand Officer of Thieves has once picked up the ceremonial bamboo tablets. (Zhengjue Yi)
To attain or not to attain—Heaven is vast, the earth is narrow. Whether sitting, reclining, or walking, there is no need for weary doubt.
(Zhenru Zhe). Nanquan’s attainment—how does it compare to non-attainment? A virtuous person, a noble gentleman, their deportment is without error. (Huanglong Zhen).
A relative has come from within the house. What is there within the house? He holds this single stone—vast, firm, and enduring.
Once offered to the Buddha at Vulture Peak, Śakra merely lifted it with his hand. From within his heart, what did he produce? Peace and happiness, as well as long life.
(Longmen Yuan). [Continued Collection] Nanquan said:
"If you can say it, pick up a piece of stone. Nanquan said: "If you cannot say it, pick up a piece of stone.
Within the stone there is jade, pure and without flaw; it is fit to serve as a precious gem for a high official. Seeing it, yet not seeing even a single hair’s breadth—sit!
He has never been away from his reclining posture for even a moment. There is no need for carving or engraving, nor the toil of dusting and wiping.
His majestic form is grand and its features are distinct and clear. If a person can turn their light back here and now, why wait until the future to see Maitreya? (Fujian Qin)
Attained before, not attained after; who knows that one thread runs through both five-hundred [stanzas]? Rain on the cypresses, *piao piao*; wind in the pines, *se se*.
A person beyond the mountain hears the words of the *zhègū* bird; they mistake them for the eighteen variations of the *hújiā* flute. (Shi’an Shui)
The Great Officer carves the stone; his intent is ever loftier. The King, in his old age, needlessly causes him ruin. He shatters the heavy barriers and traverses the path of life;
a single sky of wind and moon illuminates the Sahā world. (Closing the room, opening it.)
Attaining and not attaining—clearly revealing one's very heart and liver. No one understands this meaning;
it causes me to remember Nanquan. (Jianweng Jing)
Sitting and reclining through many springs, half covered in moss and half shrouded in clouds. Without edges and without seams, it is difficult to grasp;
in vain one speaks of one’s innermost heart to others. (Xianji Yun)
Held in both hands, it is difficult to cover; as before, with both hands, it is returned. With a single pillow and the pure breeze, sleep is deep and heavy;
a bird picks up a falling flower by the path before the cliff. (Nuo'an Zhao)

To raise it is easy; to see it returned is difficult. At the summit of Mount Sumeru, the celestial winds are cold.
Towering down directly into the Dragon’s Cave—who would dare even to look? (Huitang Xian).
Heaven and earth share the same root; it is naturally so. At that moment, I was still delighted to have met Nanquan, who pointed and said, "Seeing this flower is like a dream.

When the Great Officer acted as a regional governor, he visited Nanquan; citing the ancient to clarify the present, principle and phenomena were perfectly integrated.
This was precisely the moment to cast away body and life, yet for some reason he remained utterly bewildered. (Baoning Yong)
To bring it forth is easy; to see it again is difficult. Sharing the same root as heaven and earth, it is yet vast and indistinct. Nanquan points his finger and says the flowers are like a dream;
facing this, rely on you, noble one, to look closely. (Sixin Xin).
One branch, two branches, then ten thousand branches— The golden scissors are poised to cut away the drooping foliage. If it did not droop, who would know its worth?
It is simply because human hearts have changed today; It is not that the autumn fragrance has necessarily withered in a single night. (Shangfang Yi)
Mountains are moist with the jade they harbor; forests are lush where pearls lie hidden in the depths. Beholding this single flower, it is like a dream;

yet its brilliance and the root [of reality] do not follow divergent paths. Master Wáng has cast off all restrictive patterns and, amidst the very clamor of Cháng’ān, calls out to the indolent Mr. Lù (Yuánwù Qín).
Nanquan pours out his very heart for all of you: With a smile he points to the courtyard, where spring is truly elsewhere.
This is not like waiting idly by a stump for a rabbit; One must instead ride a crane up into the azure clouds. (Fujian Qín)

Who says that heaven and earth share the same root? In affairs, seeing is like contending; in principle, seeing is like intimacy. A single railing of courtyard flowers has become entirely a thing of the past;
with the wind and moon filling the heavens, with whom can one discuss them? One must laugh at Old Nanquan, who still sought to recognize people by their words.
How pitiable is Grand Master Lu Xun! Facing him, he buried his own family treasure.
(Fodeng Xun) Had he known that heaven and earth share the same root, he would not have had to come again to ask others. Instead, Nanquan personally pointed it out to him:
"In the midst of ordinary life, flowers bloom in the spring of a dream. (Gushan Gui)
Heaven and earth share the same root—here I pose a question. Before you have even raised a step, you have already lost your home. Where there is neither yin nor yang, flowers bloom once more;
the jade is originally without flaw, yet it seems as if it has flaws. (Jingshan Gaofeng)
[Continued Collection] Nanquan held fast to his command and did not grant a light recompense; once he pointed to the courtyard flowers for Lord Lu.
The whole world grows old in the midst of busyness; who would be willing to rest before death? (Zhenjing Wen).
One must know that heaven and earth share a common root; all things have from the beginning been one body.
I wonder, as for the flowers beneath Nanquan’s courtyard—how many people have looked upon them and found them like a dream? (Zhaotang 1)
Pointing out that the deep crimson is as it was of old; there is no more premature bloom upon the fragrant clusters.
Nanquan departs with the spring within his smile, leaving behind only the lingering red petals to intoxicate the bees. (Xinwen Ben)
The road to the mysterious pass of the Jade Cavern is long; how could the coiled peach tree be an ordinary fragrance?
It is concealed so as not to allow it to be seen by the world, fearing only that the spring breeze might leak its scent. (By Jeong-dang Beom)
How laughable was Master Lu of those days, Who boasted alone that nothing remained beyond his own person.
Had he not pointed out that flowers are like dreams, How could the cataracts over his two eyes have been entirely removed? (Lan’an Xu)
Never having distinguished between mud and water beneath one's feet, one stubbornly flaps the lips before others. With eyes full of fragrant flowers, this is but a dream of butterflies;
unaware that one has betrayed the spring of Luoyang. (Kentang Chong)
The same root and single substance are all like a dream; within the dream, the clear-sighted eyes grow dim. A butterfly flies over the wall and away;
one knows not whose house the spring colors have entered. (Xue’an Jin)
Heaven and earth share the same root; all things are one body. The Great Master once cited Nanquan: "Pointing out the flowers before the courtyard, they are like those at night;
how many have truly reached the balustrade? (Tianmu Li).
I have drafted this letter, intending to knock upon the celestial gates; yet often there is no one with whom I may discuss it.
Because I have incurred the light dismissal of this old man, I find myself unconsciously losing my soul as I face the wind. (Xutang Yu)
Heaven and earth share the same root—this is already clear. Great Master, why must you display such brilliance? Old Nanquan degrades the noble to the lowly;

Lu Xing turns beads into jade; Nanquan shifts the constellations. The flower shadows fill the ground at midday;
a single warbler sings as one awakens from a dream. (Nanyuan Sheng)
Heaven and earth share the same root, originally one body; even a master painter finds it difficult to depict, difficult to portray.
At the place where Nanquan shifts his step and moves his body, he draws forth the yellow oriole to alight upon the willow branches. (Xiaoyan Wei)

The Great Compassionate One asks with hand and eye; the aged King answers the pivot, arranging host and guest. He turns the spearhead back—a swift and skillful means.
From this point on, the six kingdoms are cleared of smoke and dust. (Yuan’an Xuan)
[Added from another source] Grand Master Lu asked Nanquan, "I have come here from Liuhé. Is there still a body there?
Nanquan said, "Take this clearly to heart and present it to a master. The official said, "The Master is inconceivable."
The accomplishment throughout all worlds is as follows: what was just mentioned is entirely the matter within the domain of the Great Official (the Master).
The verse says:
Tussling head-to-head before the horse, one loses footing in the encounter; do not seek it elsewhere, but cultivate and refine it face-to-face within the six directions.
The body is clearly presented to people; throughout all worlds it is fully realized. Yet, even when one sheds the old molds, there is still leakage. (Yuedang Chang)

*The Comprehensive Collection of Linked Verses on Ancient Cases in the Chan School*, Scroll Seventeen.
Compiled by the Śramaṇa Fasheng of Ba’en Guangxiao Chan Monastery in Chizhou during the Song Dynasty.

Sixth Patriarch’s Lineage,
Fourth Generation, Part Three (Continuation of the Third Generation under Nanyue).
[Added to the Collection] Lay Practitioner Ganzi of Chizhou (who met Nanquan). One day he entered Nanquan’s hall for a vegetarian feast.

At that time, Huangbo was serving as the Head Seat (*śrāmaṇera*). The practitioner requested a donation of wealth. The Head Seat said, "The two types of giving—wealth and Dharma—are equal and without distinction.
Ganzi said, "If you speak thus, how can you deserve my offering? With these words, he took his gift and went out. A short while later...
Gan entered again and said, "I request a gift of wealth. The Head Seat replied, "The two gifts of wealth and Dharma are equal and without distinction.
Gan then proceeded to distribute the alms.
The verse says: Gan Qi has both gathering and releasing; The Head Seat is thoroughly awake. Clouds gather and rain clears, the long sky is vast— One.
The mandarin ducks cannot be captured in a painting.
(Songyuan Yue) Cast here and scattered there, they present their mutual display. Before the gates of hell, the eyes of ghosts;
having seen through beyond the liver and gall of the skull, the Great Eye atop Maheśvara’s head shines once more. (Xutang Yu)
One day, Ganqi entered Nanquan’s quarters to serve congee and requested that Nanquan recite the liturgy.
Nanquan then struck the gavel and said, "I request the assembly to recite the *Mahāprajñāpāramitā* for the sake of the cat and the white ox.
Ganqi swept his sleeves and departed. After the meal, Nanquan asked the head cook, "Where is the Master?"
Zuo said, "He left right then and there. Quan then smashed the cauldron. The verse says:
A gruel offering such as this is rare in all ages; The ten benefits are perfected, and the fruit is not inferior. The cauldrons and pans are all worn through, yet no grain remains to boil;
All those near and far in the monastic groves should know this. (Fenyang Zhao)
Gan-zhi prepared congee and went to Nanquan, requesting the Master to recite the Buddha’s name before the assembly of monks.
At that moment, the cat-shaped kitchen steward said, "Let us go home," and at once all the cauldrons and pots were pierced through. (Ciming Yuan)
Two water buffaloes suddenly meet; they come and go amidst level fields and shallow grass. Where have they gone when struck by the staff?
Vastly drifting through the ages, they leave no trace forever. (Baoning Yong)
Under the mallet, much is clearly leaked away; the ordinary practice of serving congee is yet a source of confusion.
The tabby cat and the white ox have no place to be found; it is in vain that the head cook has broken the pot. (Foguo Bai).

Meeting on a divergent path, the verse has already been answered; idly blowing the *qiang* flute toward the marshes, the fisherman greedily watches the egrets at the riverbank, unaware that his small boat is drifting with the waves. (Xuefeng Yu)
Material giving is finite, while the Dharma-giving is vast; for the sake of others, he recites "Mahā" like a wildcat or a bull.
Without cause, Ganji bows his head in prostration; he provokes Nanquan to break the cauldron. (Zhang Wujin)
He came specifically to serve congee and boast of his elegance; who knew that Old Wang was even more refined?
He smashed the congee pot to reveal his ugliness and clumsiness, gathering the "wildcat" and the "white ox" all at once. (Shushan Ru).
Loud chanting and loud laughter, his nature wild and unrestrained; Fan Lang rides his donkey out from his native land.
He startles the geese upon the sands at twilight in the evening sky, As two or three rows slant away toward the sea gates. (Zantang Zhun)
The "cat" and the "white ox" chant "Mahā"; how can they compare to Nanquan smashing the cauldron?
Although the Buddha-dharma is not so very much, the monasteries throughout the world cannot do anything about it. (Gushan Gui)
Nanquan smashed the furniture of idleness; throughout the vast quarters, all have taken it as a story to contemplate. Today, for your sake, I shall recount it once more:
it is clear and distinct, leaving no room for negligence. (Jingshan Gaofeng)

[Continued Collection] Gan-zhi served congee to manifest his family tradition; Old Wang groundlessly praised the merit of the offering. When it was reported that he had gone, Gan-zhi finally smashed the cauldron.
One knows this is like drawing one's bow after the thief has fled. (Hai-yin Xin)
When Gan-zhi served congee and recited "Mahā," he saw Nanquan smash the cauldron. For all matters, simply settle them with justice;
let the four seas wage war as they please. (Zhaotang’s One).
Ganqi prepared the congee and offered his wealth; Nanquan smashed the cauldron. He lost to that white ox and stray cat, yet won a full field of cause and effect.
The two men harbored red hearts in secret, nearly killing the head cook with their doubts.
Do not doubt it—there is no need for special skill in cooking congee; one simply must stir it frequently. (Yuanwu Keqin)
"T'ai-p'ing has never struck since time immemorial; everyone must take care. In Gan-zhi’s rice there are worms;
Nan-ch’uan’s cauldron is made of iron. Behold the refined gold from the great furnace—it shall never fall among the dross and rust. (Fojian Huiqin)
Ganqi served white gruel; Nanquan used salt and vinegar. Each found their own advantage, yet even now the path is cut off. (Or-an’s Verse)
Needle-points clashing brings forth the sword; it brings misfortune upon Nanquan as he beats the rice-pot. Do not say that in his youth he was easily let off;
for the most part, those with grave offenses receive no heavy punishment. (Xiaowenkān).
Ganqi served congee; Nanquan smashed the cauldron. A common malady, utterly confusing. There is something even more laughable:
tomorrow morning they will starve the Chan monks to death. (Xue’an Jin)
When porridge is served, he earnestly requests that the recitation be performed; he strikes the gavel, and each person recites the *Mahā*.
May the merit accumulated thus far be fully perfected. Then, he goes to the kitchen and breaks the pot (Hyōnggwansong).
The practitioner loses his eyes; Nanquan breaks the cauldron. The monks in the hall do not grow weary of it;
there is but one worldly person. (Nanyan Sheng)
The Fourth Generation under the Sixth Patriarch (Third Generation under Qingyuan):
Chan Master Longtan Chongxin of Lishui (Successor of Tianhuang Huairang). Before the Master left home to become a monk, he was a baker living in front of a monastery.
Every day he would offer ten cakes to the Emperor of Heaven (Tianhuang), who accepted them.
He set aside one cake and gave it to him, saying, "I bestow this upon you to provide shade for your descendants. The Master said, "This was my future portion;
why do you say you are bestowing it upon me? The Emperor said, "This is your future portion; what fault is there in returning it to you?"
The Master attained realization thereupon and subsequently entered the monastic order. The verse says:
What was brought forth and what was to come did not differ; Longtan’s firm questioning allowed no overlap. How many have since contended with their lips and tongues?
The spring birds warble as they scold the falling flowers. (Fenyang Shao)
Each time ten cakes were brought, he would set aside one. Thinking on what it means to provide shade for one's descendants, he took them away in a circle and brought them back again;
before he knew it, the *tīrtha* (the essence) had reached the gate of his crown. (Baizhang Yuan).
Seeing a stone at the peak of Mount Nanyue, he returned to the ancient shore to consort with the sand gulls.
In vain did he divide the Hu-bread into fragrant bait, only to draw forth the golden dragon onto the straight hook. (Foguo Bai)
【Continued Collection】Held here and sent there, its form is perfectly round; its shade covers descendants, its meaning never cold.
How could it have been better than not splitting it apart at that time? Leave it whole for later generations to behold. (Wuzhun Shanfeng)
When receiving a favor, one should think of repaying it; take this one cake back. When the conditions for leaving home arrive, one’s heart will immediately turn to ash. (Hengchuan Hong)
[Added from another source] Longtan was once told by the Emperor: "In the past you honored merit and goodness; now you believe my words.

You may be named Chongxin (Venerable Faith). Thereupon, he served diligently at the Emperor's side. One day the Emperor asked him, "Since you first arrived here, I have not yet received instruction on the essential point of the mind.
The Emperor said, "From the moment you arrived, I have never failed to point out the essential point of your mind. The Master—
[The Emperor] asked, "Where did you point out [the Way]? [Yunmen] replied, "When you brought me tea, I received it for you;
when you brought me food, I accepted it for you; when you bowed, I lowered my head. Where was the essential point of the Mind not pointed out?
The Master lowered his head and remained silent for a long while. The Emperor said, "If one sees, one sees directly right now. To deliberate is already a deviation."

The Master was immediately enlightened. He asked again, "How does one maintain this? Huang said, "Roam freely according to your nature; relax and let go as circumstances arise. Simply exhaust the ordinary mind;

there is no separate 'sage's understanding'. The verse says: Roaming freely according to nature, Relaxing and letting go with conditions. Simply exhausting the ordinary mind— There is no other "sage's" understanding.
Leaving the white robe to throw oneself at a teacher—how precious is this bitter toil! Carrying tea and making inquiries, he attends to everything with his own person.
Without cause, he recounts again the affairs of three years; the street vendor selling cakes laughs himself to the ground. (Baizhang Yuanwen).

The case is settled according to the facts; gain and loss are more than half resolved. Exerting one’s full strength to take responsibility, as the boat leaves the shore, there is nothing where you do not receive instruction on how to hold the tea or serve the food.
Holy understanding and ordinary sentiment cannot come forth; with lofty head and horns, wind and thunder arise.
(Chang of Yuediang). Chan Master Zongzhi of Daowu Mountain in Tanzhou (heir to Yaoshan). Once, a monk asked, "What is the master’s profound depth?
(Alternatively: "What is the meaning of the profound and subtle mystery? The Master descended from his meditation seat, performed a woman’s bow, and said:
Thank you for coming from afar. There is nothing with which to repay your visit. The Verse says:
The Azure Dragon lies sleeping in the sea, auspicious clouds rise high; From every direction they return to the source, like the tides of ten thousand streams.
When the wooden man comes to inquire of the affairs of the Western Palace, In return he is granted a single peach from the Eastern Garden. (Touzi Qing)
Turning back, one has already fallen onto the path of the present moment. Without revealing a trace of sharp edge, how could one attain perfection?
To shift the pivot of the Shaolin gate—whom would know that this is another hall of heaven? (Cheng Kumu).

At this thatched door and wooden gate, I thank you for coming. I bow my body and prostrate myself, my smiling brows opening wide. With deep intimacy and profound secrecy, I entrust this to you personally.
Do not say you have returned empty-handed from the Mountain of Jewels. (Sushan Ru).
[Continued Collection] Bowing deeply and intimately, the rites of three generations are fully encompassed. If this meaning were not so, what would the jade and silk be for? (Wuzu Fan).
The harvest is bountiful and the times are clear; rites and righteousness abound. Meeting one another, we accompany each other with wine and song.
If one cannot drink with an open heart at this banquet, what is the use of such a day of wind and moon? (Dongsou Ying)
[Added for inclusion] Daowu visited Nanquan. Nanquan asked, "What is your name, *ācārya*? The Master replied, "Zongzhi.
Nanquan said, "When wisdom does not reach it, how can there be a 'principle' (*zong*)? The Master said, "One must strictly avoid mentioning it.
Nanquan said, "Truly, if you mention it, horns will grow. Three days later, the Master and Yunyan were sewing behind the rack.
Jianquan asked, "Master Zhiduo, you said the other day, 'At the place where wisdom does not reach, one must strictly avoid speaking;
if one speaks, horns will grow. How, then, should one practice? The Master immediately withdrew his body and entered the Sangha hall.
Jianquan returned to the abbot's quarters. The Master came back again to resume sewing his needle. Yanguan said, "Disciple, just now for your sake..."
"He did not respond at all to the Master. The Master said, "You are quite clever.
Yankou did not understand this, so he asked Nanquan, "Why did the Dharma-teacher Zhiduo not respond to the Master just now? I do not understand."
He requested the Master’s instruction. Nanquan said, “He, however, acts among the heterodox species. Yunyan asked, “What is acting among the heterodox species?
Nanquan said, “Have you not heard it said: ‘Where wisdom does not reach, one must strictly avoid speaking;
if you speak, horns will grow. You must act directly among the heterodox species. Yunyan still did not understand. Verse:
It is said: "Words cannot reach it; we are fellow travelers. Shaking his sleeves, he returned to the hall, and the assembly then sifted through the sand and gravel.
True gold cannot be distinguished from dross; there is no need for further doubt or anxiety. (Fenyang Zhao)
Beneath the adamantine limit lie ancient skulls; how many have been trampled by people until their blood splashed into the void? Let the bright moon be gathered by you as you please;
who would abandon the cold pines to the seal of white clouds? (Touzi Qing)
[Added from the Supplementary Collection] Daowu was once asked by Shishuang, "If someone asks about the ultimate matter after a hundred years have passed, what would you say to him?
The Master called for a novice; the novice responded, "Yes. The Master said, "Add some water to the pure pitcher.
After a long silence, the Master then asked Shishuang, "What was it you were just asking? As Shishuang was about to speak again, the Master immediately returned to his quarters.
Shuang had an awakening at this point. The verse says:
"Extending his hand, he returns the author's own device; In ordinary speech, he arrays his banners and spears. Seeking further inquiry, he intended to advance, then returned to the abbot’s quarters;
One phrase is clear, leaving no further doubt. (Danxia Chun)
[Added from another collection] Daowu went to Wufeng. Wufeng asked, "Do you recognize the old master Yaoshan? The Master said, "I do not recognize him. Wufeng said, "Why do you not recognize him?

The Master said, "I do not recognize him; I do not recognize him. The Verse says: The old master Yaoshan was truly a man of great capacity; Daowu’s response was like a flash of lightning. If you wish to know the source of this matter, Look at the moon reflected in the water.
In the depths of white clouds, the path is difficult to traverse; to seek its traces is already to involve effort. The wild goat hanging from the cliff leaves no shadow or trace;
yet even in such composure, one still falls into the midst of the direct and the indirect. (Danxia Chun)
[Added for inclusion: Daowu was once asked by Guishan, "Where have you come from? The Master replied, "I have come to visit the sick. Guishan asked, "How many people are ill?
The Master said, "There are those who are ill and those who are not. Guishan asked, "Is the one who is not ill perhaps the Venerable Zhi?
The Master said, "Whether one is ill or not, it has nothing to do with him. [He then departed quickly.]
"Quick! Quick! The Mountain said, "Even if you attain the Way, it has no connection with him.
The Verse says: How could the wondrous medicine ever pass the mouth? No divine physician can grasp its hand. If it exists, it was originally not non-existent;
In its ultimate emptiness, it was originally not existent. It arises without perishing; it endures without passing away. It is entirely present before the time of Weiyin.
Walking alone after the void of the kalpa, he completes the equilibrium; as heaven covers and earth supports, the sun flies and the moon runs (Tiantong Jue).
[Added from other sources: Daowu, when Zhaozhou arrived, was wearing a leopard-skin tunic and holding a *jiliao* staff, standing before the triple gate.

He waited. As soon as he saw the Prefect arrive, he called out "Nyo! in a loud voice and stood there. The Prefect said, "Wait upon me with careful attention. The Master called out "Nyo! once more and departed. The Verse says: Waiting, As soon as he saw the Prefect arrive, He called out "Nyo!
in a loud voice and stood there. The Prefect said, "Wait upon me with careful attention. The Master called out "Nyo! once more and departed.
Taking a bull from one person and returning a horse to another—leaping like a tiger and galloping like a dragon, who would dare set its price?
Even at three thousand li away, there is clamor and dispute; it is a single lump of raw iron, without a seam or fissure. (Nun Wuzhuo Zong).
Once blown upon the holeless flute; once caressed on the stringless lute. One tune, two tunes—no one understands.
After the rain has passed, the autumn waters in the night pond are deep. (Qian’an Guang)
Daowu performs a dance; it has no musical score. If you attempt to hear it with your ears, I dare not grant you permission. (Byan Xuan).
Chan Master Tansheng of Yunyan in Tanzhou (who succeeded Yaoshan), when asked by Daowu, "Of the thousand hands and eyes of Great Compassion, which one is the True Eye?
the Master replied, "It is like a person at night reaching behind them with their back turned to feel for their pillow."
Wu said, "I understand. The Master asked, "How do you understand it? Wu said, "My whole body is hands and eyes. The Master said, "You have spoken quite well;

yet you have only spoken of it eighty percent. Wu asked, "What about you, Elder Brother? The Master said, "My entire being is hands and eyes. (This is according to the *Wudeng Huiyuan*). According to the *Chuan Deng Lu*, however, it says:

[The Master said,] "You have spoken quite well; yet you have only spoken of it eighty percent. Wu asked, "What about you, Elder Brother? The Master said, "My entire being is hands and eyes. (This is according to the *Chuan Deng Lu*.)
Daowu asked, "Regarding the 'Thousand Hands and Eyes' of Great Compassion, how is it? The Master said, "When there is no lamp, how can you grasp the pillow?
Daowu said, "I understand! I understand! The Master asked, "How do you understand? Daowu said, "The whole body is eyes.
This should be taken as the correct version according to the *Chuan deng lu* (Record of the Transmission of the Lamp). The *Lian deng hui yao* (Essential Compendium of the Linked Lamps) [differs].
This differs from what is recorded in the *Jiugongsong lianzhu*, which in all cases attributes this to Yunyan asking Wudao (and so forth); I fear that [the former] may not be correct.
The verse says: "His whole body is it;
his entire being is it. Even picking it up, it is still ten thousand miles away. Spreading its wings, it surges through the clouds of the six directions."
Gathering the wind, it stirs the waters of the four oceans. What dust and mire has suddenly arisen? Why does that hair’s breadth not cease? Do you not see?
As the netted pearls hang down in patterns, their reflections multiply; from where do the hand and eye at the tip of the staff arise? (Xuědòu Xiǎn)

A single aperture, empty and penetrating; eight facets, bright and clear. Without form and without partiality, it is like spring entering the calendar; neither lingering nor obstructed, the moon travels through the sky.
With pure, precious eyes and arms of merit, where is there not his entire body? His manifest hands and eyes reveal the full mechanism;
in the vast deployment of great function, what need is there for hesitation or prohibition? (Tiantong Ju)
The younger brother calls out to his elder brother—how could this be by mere chance? They were once playing together before the old mountain.
How can one understand this with the eyes and hands of one’s whole body? Shide and Hanshan laugh until the heavens resound. (Dahong Yu)
Yanjiao was terrified when he saw his head reflected in the mirror; Naluo restored his body to its former state.
Not knowing from where his hands and eyes had arisen, he said, "My entire body is present within a single mote of dust. (Buddha-mind is just this.)

The entire body is hands and eyes; throughout the world, they have never been hidden. Reaching back to feel for the pillow at the head of the bed, he turns over in his sleep, complaining that the night is too long.
(Tianning Liaoyi of Jingzhao Prefecture)
[Continued Collection]: Guanyin’s Wondrous Sound. Eighteen, nineteen. Seen by the eye and heard by the ear, people know it exists.
Left hand grasping the *kundika*, right hand holding the willow branch; clenching and releasing, the crow flies and the hare runs. (Great Abundant Grace).
Great Compassion possesses many hands and eyes. It is like a person groping for a pillow in the night; the entire body rises up, completely subject to the驱使 (driving) of slaves and servants.
Do you not see? By fixating on the tracks of an ox, one loses the great ocean water.
As long as transformation has not been attained, there remains a reliance upon what was before. Go back! Go back! The towering waves that strike the heavens are like floating dust.
(Chang of Yuet-tang). His entire body is it; his whole person is it. Butter, curd, and clarified butter are of one flavor. From the tip of a single hair, Mount Sumeru surges forth;
a mustard seed sucks dry the waters of the vast ocean. The ten voids are swallowed up and incinerated; the true eye is vast and empty. Illumination and function are simultaneous. The person—
Both object and subject are swept away. To take it up mistakenly at the blow of the staff or under the shout is to lose it even as one turns one’s back and picks it up.
Stop! Stop! Water is water and mountains are mountains; take care not to bind yourself with no rope. (Yuánwù Qín)
The thousand hands and eyes of the Bodhisattva of Great Compassion are like a person reaching back with their hand to feel for a pillow;
it is like a monkey leaping out of a cloth bag—it does not hinder one from displaying elegance wherever one may be. (Lan’an Shu)
The whole body is it; the entire person is it. A pure and clean body is completely defiled by excrement. Dragged out and exposed, it is buffeted by a fierce wind.
Who taught him to reach behind his back to feel for his pillow? Once again, three blows! (Wuan Quan).
While Yunyan was sweeping the floor, Daowu said, "You are being far too busy. Yunyan replied, "One must know that which is not busy.
Daowu said, "In that case, there is a second moon. Yunyan held up his broom and asked, "Which moon is this?
Daowu then desisted. Hearing of this, Xuansha said, "This is precisely the first moon."
The Second Month. The verse says:
"Borrowed for the time being, it merely serves to close the gate; When its use is finished, it is withdrawn as appropriate.
The hand that plays with snakes before Elephant Bone Rock— What was done in childhood, one knows to be shameful in old age. (Tiantong Ju)
[Added from the Supplementary Collection] Yunyan was traveling with Wuzu back to Yaoshan from Nanquan.
Upon arriving, the Master asked Yaoshan, “What is it to walk among those of different species? Yaoshan said, “I am weary today; wait until another time to come.
The Master said, “I have come to the mountain specifically for this matter. Yaoshan said, “Go for now. The Master then departed, and Wuzu [said], “...”

Outside the abbot’s quarters, hearing that the Master had not yet given the kōan, he unconsciously bit his finger until it bled. He then went down to ask the Master, "Brother, you went to ask the Abbot about that causal condition; what did he say? The Master replied, "He would not speak for me, so I simply bowed my head. The verse says: The finger was bitten through, blood flowed out; The matter was not explained, and the head was lowered. The old fellow was truly a man of great capacity; How could he have been surpassed by others? If one does not understand this, It is like a blind person entering a dark room. Even if you were to explain it for ten thousand years, You would still not know its meaning. If you wish to see the Buddha, Look at the face of the man with the white hair. [The Master] said, "Go to the edge and seek out one or half of them to continue [the lineage], so that it shall not be severed. Shanshan then took his leave, looking back again and again.
The Master then called out, "Dārali! Shanshan turned his head; the Master held up his oar and said, "You thought there was something else.
Thereupon, he capsized his boat and entered the water to depart. A verse says:
Under Jia Shan’s oar, he awakened to the mind and ceased; what need to worry about body or name? He stepped upon the overturned boat.
The fisherman at Huating, ancient and modern, makes those upon the misty waves and rivers sigh with sorrow. (Zhaojue Zong)
Sedges and reeds flank the white flowers; the azure seas are autumnal. The brocade-scaled fish leaps upon the waves, caught on the golden hook.
Before one’s eyes there is no dharma to look back upon. Treading upon the overturned boat, one attains freedom. (Lohan Nan)
[Continued Collection] Not transgressing, the pure waves differ in their intent. Mouth open and eyes staring, one still hesitates.
The fishing boat has capsized, leaving no trace; the setting sun and autumn wind battle the reeds and rushes. (Fotuoxun)
The veteran of old relied on Jia Shan; his entire mechanism was exhausted, and a deep grievance was formed. Father south, son north—where is the home?
He shifts the pivot of heaven and turns the axis of earth upside down. (Xiatang Yuan)
A single stroke across the mouth, killing and giving life in full. A nod of the head three times, the nose reaches toward heaven.
To this day, the elegance of a thousand ages remains; who says that at Huating the boat was capsized? (Fozhao Guang).
Having pierced through before the opportunity arises, the disciple wishes to repay his master. A flash of lightning under the oars, sweat flows like a stream.
He capsizes the boatman’s vessel, and the waters flow on; he enters straight into the thousand peaks without turning his head. (Shui’an I)
The body hidden leaves no trace, yet there is nothing further to hide; the entire being is without reliance, meeting [reality] face-to-face.
The ancient mirror, unpolished, reflects by itself; thin mist and dew moisten the autumn light. (□□□).
Where there are no tracks, do not hide your body; look closely, and it is clearly but dust in the eye.
With the full mechanism, break through the tethering stake for donkeys; struck by the staff, the Jade Qilin emerges. (Yuanji Cen)
A bright mirror facing the dais is shattered with a single blow. Whether one comes from East Lu or West Qin, there is nothing that can or cannot be done (Kentang Chong).
A single oar splits the mouth; empty space is broken open. Three dots on a donkey’s head overturn the boat. Father and son have not yet finished this matter to this day;
it has been mistakenly transmitted as waves upon the rivers and lakes (Tiantong Jing).
The mechanism of the wheel never had a thread attached to its tip; there will surely be a golden-scaled fish that climbs the straight hook.
A single shove across the mouth is still not thorough; there is a reason why one steps upon the overturned boat. (Songyuan Yue)
The foul mouth has not opened for ten thousand kalpas; were one to transgress even by a hair’s breadth, the iron wheel follows.
When rain disperses and clouds are gathered in the night of the bright moon, who can one speak to when the waves of the river surge back? (Muan Yong)
Jiashan does not reside upon a single oar; the bright moon and reeds among the flowers are cold night after night. Who says that the news from Huating has been cut off?
The autumnal colors remain vividly present within the rivers and mountains. (Solving Emptiness).
The gathering disperses, stretching far to the edge of the sea. A nod beneath the oar loses the entire mechanism. Father south, son north—where are they now? The moon is cold;
the fisherman’s song falls upon the fishing pier. (Tianmu Li)
A sudden stroke of the oar lashes across the mouth; beneath the great ocean’s floor, fire burns the heavens. Father south, son north—where is home?
The wind fills the vast sky, the moon fills the boat. (Mongan Cong)
A golden-scaled fish, just as desired, has taken the hook; the waters of the Huating River ought now to flow westward. The fishing boat has been overturned to its very keel;
the spring wind continues to cause such turmoil, never ceasing. (By Pogu Xian)
The medicinal plaster clearly explains its efficacy; one does not know what is counterfeit or genuine within. He instructs his foolish children with repeated admonitions:
"Do not let this medical manual mislead future generations. (Xutang Yu)
A single oar at the bend of green willows; where the golden scales are caught is difficult to find. The deep waters of the long river harbor resentment;
it was not right to step upon the overturned boat. (By Hye of Seoyam)
The place where the body hides leaves no trace; the numinous bird dwells atop the shadowless tree. Where there is no trace, do not hide the body;
on the sproutless branch, the spring flowers bloom. When there is a source, who can discern it? At dawn, the western wind blows gently.
Pine-branch hairpins were cast and tossed about along a single path. (Donggu Guang).
Regarding the novice monk Yaoshan (who succeeded Yaoshan), Yaoshan asked him: "I hear that Chang’an is very bustling.
The Master replied, "In my country, all is peaceful. (Fayan offered an alternative reading: "Who said so? Yaoshan said, "Did you obtain this from studying the sutras?"

[The Master] said, "It is not obtained from reading scriptures, nor is it obtained from seeking instruction. Daoshan asked, "There are many people who do not read scriptures and do not seek instruction;

why do they not obtain it? The Master said, "I do not say that they lack it; it is simply that they are unwilling to take responsibility for it. A verse says: Not from reading scriptures, Nor from seeking instruction, Is it attained.
Many there are who do neither, Yet why do they fail? I do not say they lack it, But they refuse to accept it.
Smashing through the void into seven or eight shards, Forcibly opening the golden locks two or three layers deep, He turns his body and enters straight into the azure heights beyond;
How many travelers seek his tracks? (Like withered wood.)
Rising and falling, empty they go and empty they come; for his land, not even a speck of dust remains. On the summit of Mount Sumeru grows a rootless grass;
it does not wait for the spring breeze, yet its flowers bloom of themselves. (Touzi Qing)
The novice Gao was staying in a hermitage. One day, he came through the rain to visit Yaoshan.
Yaoshan said, "You have come. The novice replied, "I have. Yaoshan said, "It is quite soaked. The novice said, "If you don't beat this drum, why play these pipes?
Yunyan said, "There is not even leather; what drum could one beat? Daowu said, "There is not even a drum; what leather could one beat?"
The Master said: "Today is truly a magnificent performance. The Verse says:
"Spontaneously he dropped a word to question him; How could those who know the sound let it fall into this age? The Hu-ge (Horn) flute does not violate the notes of Gong or Shang;
When the jade flute is held crosswise, it blows beyond the kalpas. (Danxia Chun)
Li Ao, the Prefect of Dingzhou, had long admired the profound transformation of Yaoshan. Although he had repeatedly invited him, Yaoshan did not go.
Li Ao then went in person to visit him. Yaoshan was holding a scripture and paid him no heed. A servant said, "The Governor is here.
Li Ao, being of a narrow and impatient temperament, remarked, "Seeing the man is not as good as hearing of his fame," and brushed his sleeves, departing at once. Yaoshan said, "Too..."
Shou said, "How can you hold the ears in honor while treating the eyes with contempt? Li Hui bowed in thanks and asked, "What is the Way?
Shou pointed up and down and said, "Do you understand? Li replied, "I do not understand. Shou said, "Clouds in the blue sky; water in the pitcher.
Li was filled with joy and prostrated himself, reciting this verse: "Refined is my physical form, like that of a crane; My mind is as clear as the autumn moon."
A thousand pine trees, beneath which lie two cases of scripture. I came to ask about the Way, and there was no further teaching:
"Clouds in the blue sky, water in the pitcher. The Verse says:

Clouds in the blue sky, water in the pitcher— I fear you will misunderstand this as mere cleverness. Fenyang asks you, ghostly soul: *Note: This verse is traditionally attributed to Master Yunmen Wenyan (864–949). Listen. To manifest one’s name through supernormal powers as they truly are:
(Fenyang Zhao). "Clouds in the blue sky, water in the pitcher; hand-in-hand with you, we walk across the crimson heavens.
Turning our heads, we do not realize it is already cold and dawn has broken; a single sheet of red light rises over the sea. (Yuantong Xian).

Clouds in the blue sky, water in the pitcher; the eye follows the finger and falls into a deep pit. The wildflowers by the stream cannot endure the bitterness of frost and wind—what need is there to speak of "walking on the bottom of the deepest sea"? (Zhang Wujin)
The worthy minister of Longxi ascends Mount Yaoqiao; clouds dwell in the azure sky, water remains in the jar. When the wind is still and the clouds have vanished, the void alone is revealed;
the Jade Maiden at the Celestial Gate has never closed it. (Tianning Liaoyan of Jingzhao Prefecture)
When the ancients asked about the Way, what more was there to say? Water is in the jar; clouds are in the sky. One’s native land must be returned to, and upon returning, it is found.
At the parting pavilion, clouds and moon; at the ferry-head, a boat. (Baiyang Shun)

[Continued Collection] When the Imperial Commissioner asked about the Way in those days, he arrived at the Zen gate on a single horse with a solitary spear. Though the Master showed compassion through repeated inquiries, [the visitor] remained unenlightened;
thus, he took up his brush and let it fall upon paper, composing a poem even more illuminating. (Dongshan Cong)
Meeting on a distant road, we do not know one another; like clouds and water, our traces are ever-fleeting and without fixed destination.
Even if you possess hundreds of thousands of forms of wealth and honor, how can they compare to the absolute poverty of my own house? (Da Hong En)
Valuing the ear and disparaging the eye. Turning his back, he draws a golden-tipped arrow; looking up, he gazes at the blue sky.
The arrow has passed beyond the kingdom of Silla. (Byeonsan Qian).
Clouds in the blue sky, water in the jar. Throughout my life, I have laid bare my heart and liver to others.
True gold has its own true price; it is never sold to people mixed with sand. (Beihai Xin)
If Chen’s encounter with the Master is too far-fetched, Yunshui is once again deceiving him.
In vain he claims to have attained realization at that time; he mistakes fish eyes for bright pearls. (Tianmu Li)
"Parting the weeds to gaze at the wind—what can be done? To travel through the deep mountains, one must have the Way.
It is only because people value what they hear and despise what they see that they lead their whole bodies into the thicket of grass. (Duan’an Chang)
Now there is no meeting face-to-face; in the past, I did not hear your name. One phrase adds three more;
the verses cannot be read through. (Xiyan Hui)
[Added to the Collection] Chan Master Wuxue of Cuiwei in Jingzhao Prefecture (he was a successor of Danxia).
One day, while walking in the Dharma Hall, Touzi stepped forward to greet him with a bow and asked, "How does the Master instruct people regarding the secret purport of the West?

When [Touzi] scooped up some foul water, Nanquan bowed in thanks. The Master said, "Do not cut off the root. Nanquan replied, "When the time comes, the roots and sprouts will grow of themselves.

Offered. Who would take the foul water and pour it over again? (Shuian I).

When the lion emerges from its den and the black dragon enters its lair, a wind arises as they lift their eyes; the brains of all other beasts split asunder. To further brandish their claws and fangs—what need?
On the contrary, it results in a leakage. When the time comes, one must rely on the mechanism of the counter-throw; clearly, one must tread upon and shatter the moon in the limpid pool.
(Touzi Shu). [Added by collection] Chan Master Xingkong of Xiaoyi Temple in Jizhou (a successor of Danxia), while receiving a monk’s visit, finished the formal greetings.

Advancing not forward, retreating not backward; moving through both ends and the middle. The barbarian monk claps his hands and laughs "he-he.

Entering the forest without moving the grass; entering the water without stirring the waves. Having once reached the original source, one remains tongue-tied and beyond further fault.
If you are a traveler seeking the Way, you must attain the final word—the Great Perfect Wisdom.
Day and night, in the beginning, middle, and end, the golden crow flies and the jade hare runs;
in this state of bewilderment and silence, it is all merely shrimp leaping, unable to escape the measure (Shixi Yue).

When a guest visits the Master, as soon as they enter the gate, the roles of host and guest have never been distinguished. When the tips of arrows meet, there is no fault;
such a beginning and a complete end are truly rarely heard of. (Benjue I)
The eyes are clear and practiced in discernment; the clouds are swept away by lofty strokes. With both hands brandishing halberds, the battle never ceases.
If worldly affairs were judged with impartiality, this General would surely return to be enfeoffed as a Marquis. (Juexiangjian)
When the makers meet, arrow meets blade; within it, the density is such that not even a breeze can pass.

[Xian Tian] was visiting the monastery as a guest. Just as he was unfolding his sitting mat, the Master said, "There is no need for formal greetings;
give me back the principle of the time before patterns had yet arisen. Xian Tian said, "I have a mouth, so it is already idle enough to mock you;
why do you toil yourself to death searching for a fan for the month of December? The Master raised his staff and made a gesture to strike him, whereupon the monk seized it.

The monk said, "Bring me back the principle that existed before you even raised your staff. The Master said, "Those who follow me go north or south; those who do not follow me die staying in the east or west.
The monk said, "Setting aside following and not following for a moment, I ask the Master to point out east, west, south, and north.
The Master then struck him. A verse says: The staff was raised, and the monk was struck; East and west were both forgotten. If you wish to know the ultimate meaning, Look at the staff in his hand.
Who could surpass him at the general’s tent? Monk Chushan was not easily matched in his skillful inquiry.
Though the dragon-headed bow and sword were broken, thirty blows with the mountain cane were not too many. (Benjue 1)

"Setting aside all present words and phrases, I ask the Master to point directly to the original nature. The Master said: "How long has it been since you lost your way from the source?"
[The student] said, “I have now received the Master’s instruction. The Master said, “If I were to instruct you, I would immediately lose the source.
[The student] asked, “How is it so? The Master presented this verse: “The mind is the substance of nature; nature is the function of the mind.

"Holy One, it is like an illusion, like a dream. Master Fojian said: "The question was not in vain; the answer was not established in vain. As soon as one follows the words, ten thousand mountains appear face-to-face.

The nature of the mind has always been one in essence; whether existent or non-existent, it penetrates the void of true emptiness.
Those of past and present who wander outside of reality and remain deluded about the source—when spring enters the gardens, everything turns red everywhere. (Tudu Ce)
