Awakening does not depend on manifold sufferings; understanding comes entirely from a single fleeting moment.
To insist that a nun must be a woman is the view of a deluded person who mistakes accumulated snow for a mountain of silver. (Fenyang Shanzhao)
In the dead of night, a loud voice like that of a young spirit; within this, clarity itself possesses its own intimacies and distances.
Now, following custom, one transmits its resonance, saying: "The nun is indeed a woman. (Baoning Yong)
In the fifth month, the blazing heat is most intense; sweat flows down one’s back beyond description.
A pure breeze sweeps across the earth and strikes the face—yet this adds but more dust to the eyes of a great Chan master. (Cao Tang Qing)
When a youth learns to follow the vermilion, he traces the black where it is red. If you bring white paper, not a single dot can be applied.
If one were to apply it, it would instead become ink smeared upon the paper. (Huanglong Zhen)
Awakening is the same as when one has not yet awakened; why need one further explain it for others to know?
When the thief’s loot is exposed and there is no place to hide it, one simply says, "The nun is but a daughter. (Da-hong Sui)

[Continued Collection] Startling the assembly, they cry out in unison for the reason of awakening: "To understand that all sages do not meet [in essence], one realizes that the nun was originally just a woman;
what Buddhas or Patriarchs are there to turn over in one's heart? (Yanshou Hui).
The nun was originally a woman; the hundred-seamed Zen monk is mostly at a loss. Geese return from the desert sands with beaks agape;
swallows circle the red beams, utterly heedless. (Poban Xian).
Master Puhua of Zhenzhou (a successor of Panshan) initially received the secret instructions from Panshan in private.
Thereafter, he feigned madness and spoke without restraint. Following Panshan’s passing, he traveled to spread the Dharma in the northern regions;
whether in cities or among burial mounds, he would shake his staff and cry out: "If you come from the bright side, I strike the bright side! If you come from the dark side..."
When [the opponent] comes from the dark side, strike him; when he comes from the four directions and eight points like a whirlwind, strike him;
when emptiness itself comes, strike him by parrying blow for blow. One day, Linji commanded a monk, "If none of these ways come, what then?
The Master pushed him away and said, "Tomorrow there is a vegetarian feast at the Dabe Temple. The monk returned and reported this to Linji. Linji—
Yangshan said, "I have always suspected this fellow. The verse says:
Old and decrepit, yet clear—the two paths diverge; The tips of arrows meet, not leaning to the side. Dragons and snakes are mixed, difficult for people to distinguish;
White snow falls from the long sky by day. (Fenyang Shanzhao)
Striking both light and dark, he boasts of the Unsurpassed; only when captured does one know he has no skillful means (*kauśalya*). Since there are no skillful means, there is no naming.
To this day, who can discern the true from the false? (Haiyin Xin)
The young master in his lofty hall is drunk on *shuanglu* (double-sixes). He scatters bright pearls at random, emitting extraordinary light.
Who can discern who wins or loses with a single throw? The dice upon the board do not form a pair. (By Fozhi Yu)
Luo must insist on displaying his cleverness; how could he ever have his name inscribed upon the golden scroll? It would be better to pull off his official cap and go home;
do not ride your donkey to the gates of others. (Gushan Gui)
[Continued Collection] It is neither wind nor madness. Walking through long streets and narrow alleys like drifting mist.
Always mindful of the offerings within the monastery; these words are constantly on the lips. (Kuo’an Yuan).
In a parched sky, several peals of thunder suddenly shake; clouds drift to and fro across the distance near and far. Yet not a single drop of sweet rain has been bestowed;
instead, the wind’s force gathers them up and sweeps them back. (Yunfeng Yue)
A single squeeze shatters the silver mountains and iron walls; in the Hall of Great Compassion, they rush to the village feast.
If Shancai’s staff were useless, he would beg it from the old man Wan-hui who feigns madness. (Shui-an) (1)
In swift waters, fish find it hard to move; on high peaks, birds do not perch. One observes the shifting warmth and cold of worldly sentiments;
human faces follow the rise and fall of status. (Songyuan Yue)
With this, he rings the bell to extend the invitation; a whirlwind strikes it down upon the stand. He goes to receive his midday meal in the Hall of Great Compassion;
how strange that his elbows are bare and his skin is pierced! (Tianmu Li).
Clanging bells and shaking rings, he sells his cleverness at will; at the Great Compassion Temple, he chases after a rustic feast.
At the wooden pagoda of Heyang, stop this needless fabrication: what is this tattered straw sandal before the hall? (Xiaowen Kan).
The Great Function is fully presented; only the true practitioner knows it. Śākyamuni’s eye flashes like a bolt of lightning.
In the Hall of Great Compassion, where one turns the body around, Linji willingly became a humble servant (Gu Yanbi).
Tomorrow there is a vegetarian feast at the Hall of Great Compassion. The Iron Ring Mountains and all the peaks are completely burst open.
A pig’s head, an elephant’s trunk, a crow’s beak, and a fish’s gill—the stone man claps his hands and laughs "he-he. Hanshan and Shide are in Tiantai. (Shi’an Shi)
Once, when Puhua entered Linji’s hall at dusk to eat raw vegetables, Linji said, "This fellow looks very much like a donkey.
The Master then brayed like a donkey. Linji said to the steward, "Prepare a fine supply of fodder for him.
The Master replied, "The people of Shaoshi did not recognize him; now he has come again to Jinling. Linji’s single eye sees everywhere."
Opening for the sake of others. The verse says:
At the crossroads of the ten directions, the golden bell rings; The lame donkey and raw vegetables bloat at will. Madly flipping somersaults, Pan-shan is strange;
Kicking over the rice-bowl table, Lin-chi is startled. With one eye not yet open, you are truly a blind fellow; Striking both ends, there is a great trembling.
Fame and reputation—why must one pry open a coffin to see what lies within? If you understand this, it is simply the journey of coming and going.
(Yexuan Zun) The place where the former master revealed his true self amidst the assembly; the time when he ate vegetables before the hall of Linji.
He has exposed his tethering rope three times in succession. *Pah!* What a beggar prowling about the platform! (Jingshan Gao)
[Continued Collection] Meeting two Vermilion Eyebrows amidst the grass, their clash of arms swift as flight. Their banners and insignia from east and west are exactly alike;
let us ask, which man shall return victorious? (Above: Added by Yi).
One donkey brays, two thieves; this is fit to serve as a model for all quarters. Whether it be the "true thief" or the "grass thief," there is no need to debate them;
the Great Gate of Giving is opened wide, with no obstructions. (Jingshan Gao)
Gorging on raw vegetables like a headless donkey; caught and defeated before Linji’s hall.
With ears pricked and a long bray, he follows every kick and stamp—unaware that his karmic debts must be settled with someone else. (Tianmu Li)
[Added from the Supplementary Collection] When Puhua saw the Cavalry Officer, he shouted. The Officer also shouted. The Officer then assumed a wrestling stance.
The Cavalry Officer ordered his men to strike the Master with five blows of the staff. The Master said, "It resembles it, but it is not it.
The Verse says:
To blend with the world and harmonize with the light is the most difficult thing of all. Meeting thus is precisely a case of two madmen in the wind.
Although the Great Transformation has no fixed location, a secular official is nonetheless not a monastic official. (Fenyang Zhao)
When the faculty and its object coincide, this is the union of the false and the true. Entering the river, one gradually beholds the Great Person.
Having suffered humiliation, he receives a single blow from another; it turns out he was not a good official at all. (Jiangling Rou)
Letting go the bell of the primordial kalpa at the foot of the steps; calling out the name of the horse while wrestling.
When struck five times with the staff, there is no place for it to be cleared away; yet he says, "He is not acting as an official. (Tianmu Li)
One day, Puhua and Linji went together to a donor’s house for a meal.
Linji asked, "When a hair swallows the vast ocean and a mustard seed contains Mount Sumeru, is this the wondrous function of spiritual powers, or is it simply the natural way of things?
Puhua then kicked over the dining table. Linji said, "That is too crude. Puhua replied, "What kind of place is this?"
Xuefeng said, "I have spoken of the coarse; I have spoken of the subtle. He then left. The next day, they went together to a donor's house for a vegetarian meal.
Xuefeng asked, "How does today’s offering compare to yesterday’s? The Master again kicked over the dining table.
Xuefeng said, "You are too crude! The Master replied, "Blind fellow! What 'coarse' or 'subtle' is there to speak of in the Buddha-dharma? Xuefeng then stuck out his tongue.
The Verse says:
To recognize true gold, one must place it in fire; Repeatedly smelting and refining reveals its quality, fine or coarse.
In superior trade, there is no yielding or bargaining; A thing of excellence has always had a price of its own. (Haiyin Xin)
Meeting one who is blind and one who is coarse-born, the host of the feast and his entire family lose heart in terror.
Who recognizes these two venerable ones, the riders of dragon-elephants, as they traverse with ease upon the crown of Vairocana? (By Yanxuan Zun)
The offering of orchids was no ordinary one; twice he encountered this man kicking over the rice table.
With such a total lack of propriety as this, what cause and effect can there be for one's survival or demise? (Yang Yi, above).

[Continued Collection]: Puhua, who pulled and tugged with wild abandon; Linji, who opened his mouth and protruded his tongue—they both displayed great capacity and great function, leaking the secret pivot of the Patriarchs.
Nan-shan’s Turtle-Nose added fangs; the Cinnabar-Tail Tiger grew wings (Nantang Xing).
To enter the sea, one must be a Kunlun; having obtained the pearl, he returned it to the Wangxiang.
Twice he kicked over the rice table—what kind of donkey-raised fellow is this? (Dianniu You).
Linji was adept at "stealing in broad daylight"; Puhua was adept at "seizing the insane. This scene, a source of great laughter, became the Three Mysteries for later generations. (Biefeng Yin)
Puhua kicked over the rice table; Linji opened his mouth wide wide. He unleashed the golden-maned lion crouching on the ground, startling Mount Sumeru until it ran away.
His entire body is eyes, yet they cannot see through; his entire body is mouths, yet they can only follow after, unable to follow along.
A precious sword emerges from its scabbard, and wind and thunder roar (the poisoned whip).
[Added for inclusion: Once, when Puhua was with Linji at Heyang Muta, they were sitting together inside the meditation hall by the fire-pit.
While [Linji] was speaking, the Master (Puhua) was daily acting like a madman in the streets and markets; [Linji] did not know whether he was an ordinary man or a sage.
The Master asked, "You say, am I an ordinary man or a sage? Linji then gave a shout. The Master pointed toward Heyang Muta.
Tada said, "The son of the new bride from Heyang; the old woman’s Zen of the wooden pagoda; Linji’s little page—he alone possesses the one true eye.

Linji said, "This thief! Tada said, "Thief! Thief! and then went out. The verse says: The son of the new bride from Heyang, The old woman’s Zen of the wooden pagoda, Linji’s little page— He alone possesses the one true eye. "Thief! Thief! he cried, And then went out.
Between the *qíjì* (the noble steed) and the *nútái* (the common hack), those with discerning eyes are rare; their depth and color are mixed together indistinguishably.
Were it not for Bǎilè, who bestows his refined gaze upon them, one would not easily find a horse that pursues the wind across a thousand *lǐ*. (Hǎiyìn-xìn)
[Added from a supplementary collection: When Puhua was about to pass away, he entered the marketplace and said to the people, "Give me a *zhidu* (straight robe).
Some gave him a padded jacket; others gave him a cloth cloak, but he accepted neither. He went away shaking his rattle. Later, Linji sent someone to deliver a coffin to him.
The Master laughed and said, "That fellow Linji is so talkative," and then he accepted it. Thereupon—
He addressed the assembly, saying, "Puhua will pass away at the East Gate tomorrow. The people of the commandery followed one another to escort him out of the city.
The Master spoke in a stern voice, "The burial today does not accord with the principles of the Green Bird (Qingwu); tomorrow he shall pass away at the South Gate."
The people followed him as well. He further said, "It will be auspicious to depart through the West Gate tomorrow. As the days passed, people began to emerge more sparsely;

having emerged, they would return again, their resolve gradually slackening. On the fourth day, he personally carried his coffin out through the North Gate, shook a rattle, entered the coffin, and passed away.
The people of the commandery rushed out of the city, lifted the coffin to look at him, but he was already nowhere to be seen.
He heard only the sound of a metal gong in the air gradually fading away, unable to fathom its cause. The verse says:
"The mad wind has exhausted its function until nothing remains; A single coffin carried by eight men.
Carried out beyond the walls of Zhenzhou City, Let him listen as the wooden gong distinguishes them for itself. (Beijian Jian)
Having scooped up empty space to make it one’s neighbor, one then hides one’s body within the Big Dipper. This plunderer of emptiness—what a lot of fuss!
Still, he uses an empty coffin to deceive later generations. (Dongshan Yuan)

Master Bimō of Mount Wutai (heir to Yǒngtài Tān) constantly carried a wooden pitchfork.
Whenever he saw a monk coming to pay his respects, he would immediately thrust the fork under the monk’s chin and say, "Which demon has incited you to leave the household life?"
"That demon has been inciting you to travel as a mendicant. Whether you can speak or not, you shall die beneath my staff.
Speak quickly! Speak quickly! Few among his disciples were able to respond. One day, Master Tong of Huoshan visited him;
as soon as he saw him, he did not prostrate but instead leaped into his arms. The Master patted Tong on the back.
Three times he struck down [the staff]. Then, rising and clapping his hands, he said, "Brother Teacher, you have deceived me by coming three thousand li away. He then turned back. He spoke in verse:
"The pear trees are withered and old, my eyes are increasingly blurred; I cannot save myself and lack healing, yet I still hold a forked staff. The hunters of Lingnan at that time—"
[Zhaozhou] said, "I see. Strike this demon to death with a single blow! (Dongshan Cong).
Sitting beneath Bimoyan Rock, he held up a pitchfork; to those who came, he bade them recognize their own home. Though he urged you earnestly, none realized it;
they lost the true pitchfork and grasped at a false one. (Fenyang Shanzhao).

To sever the heavy ford, it is difficult for one who has already passed through; to hold up the pitchfork, one must believe the skull is dry. Only after reaching Mount Huo will you know the essential point:
that "dying together and living together" is not yet worth observing. (Xuedou Xian)
Uncle and nephew meet, neither suspects the other; in the end, they pat each other’s backs like simpletons.
Looking back, fearing people might laugh at them as strange, he says: "I was lured a thousand miles away by you. (Huanglong Nan)
Holding a long fork in hand, he sits at the vital pass. Who in heaven and earth would be a traveler wandering in vain?
Had he encountered a hero at that time, he would often have become the dust beneath his feet. (Foyin Yuan)
He boasted to himself that he alone held the dragon-slaying sword; yet when he encountered the true dragon, he was helpless.
It is like a general who vainly seeks battle—his merit is nil, and his brandishing of weapons is but a futile exertion. (Haiyin Xin)
Bimozha’s staff stirs the household and the realm; the coming and going of meditators are subdued by death.
Only when a Zen Buddha enters directly with a single blade does one finally know of Xiang Yu’s arrival at Wujiang. (Chongsheng Gong)
To speak is to die beneath the wordless staff. Huo Shan leaps fiercely into [the master’s] embrace.
Three thousand miles away, they are merely deceiving one another in vain. Who else can penetrate this school? (Mengan Xin).
[Continued Collection] Beneath the forked branch, one must distinguish the paths of life and death; Huo Shan directly uproots [delusions] and penetrates the heavy barrier.
Although he has deceived me for three thousand li, he has blinded the eyes of myriad sentient beings. (Nutang Si)
In this place of precipitous cliffs, there is nowhere to insert a beak. Cast aside all medicinal taboos and bare your front teeth.
Letting go of the body beneath the forked branches, one surrenders life; here, like a dragon finding water, one is deceived from three thousand miles away.
To stroke the tiger’s whiskers and seize its tail—(Huitong Dan).
Seize it and use it immediately; sesame seeds entwine one another. Looking at it in the cold stillness, those who recognize this debt of gratitude are few.
(Yuelin Guan) Holding the fishing rod at the head of a swift rapids, the vast waves surge as the evening river grows cold. Even the scaled dragon knows how to follow the hook upward;
with a single gulp, the blue sea is drained to its very bottom. (Shuiluan Cong)
Bimō sought a person for the sake of the Dharma; he specifically brandished his staff at a vital pass.
He was just caught sitting within Huóshān’s embrace; to this day, his reason remains unvindicated. (Ei! Ān Jiàn!)
His majestic presence was so awe-inspiring that one could not even hope to approach him. Yet, as soon as I leapt into his embrace, he relaxed his countenance.
Were it not for a capacity for wine as vast as the sea, how could one know his poetic courage is as great as a mountain? (Xue’an Jin)
[Added from another source: Master Zhilin of Hunan (he succeeded Yongtai Tuan). He would constantly revile Mañjuśrī and Samantabhadra, calling them both malevolent spirits.
Holding a wooden sword in his hand, he claimed to be subduing demons. As soon as he saw a monk coming to pay his respects, he would say, "The demon has come!
The demon has come! and brandish the sword wildly before returning to his quarters. He continued in this manner for twelve years. Later—
He set down his sword and remained silent. A monk asked, "Why did you subdue the demons twelve years ago?
The Master said, "A thief does not strike the home of a poor man. The monk asked, "Why do you not subdue the demons after twelve years? The Master said:
Thieves do not strike the homes of the poor. The Verse says:
Wielding it freely with the hand, every stroke is intimate; Beneath the sword of Zhilin, smoke and dust are extinguished.
No one understands the melody of the Great Peace; It brings shame upon those who settled the chaos for the Imperial House. (Xinwen Ben)
No Māra, no self; the Māra has already been subdued. This merely adds flowers to the eyes of people of this age. Today, the Mo-chao sword has no place to be used;
one knows that a thief does not strike a poor house. (Xue’an Jin)

When the sword possesses demons, they blaze ever more fiercely; when the sword is free of demons, it is naturally clear. To concern oneself only with subduing demons is to completely lose one's illumination;
one does not realize that the body itself is the essence of an old demon. (Ningshan)
[Added to the Collection] Master Gongji of the River (he succeeded Zhangjing Yun). While traveling on the Road of the Arhats, he encountered an old man riding an ox.
The Master asked, "Where does the Road of the Arhats lead? The old man patted the ox and said, "Speak! Speak! The Master shouted, "You beast!
The old man replied, "Where does the Road of the Arhats lead? The Master— [text breaks off]

[The Master] then patted the ox and said, "Speak! Speak! The old man said, "Even if it were so, there would still be hooves and horns missing. The Master struck him; the old man then patted the ox and ran away. The verse says: Speak, speak! Even if it were so, There are still hooves and horns lacking.
A blow was struck; He patted the ox and fled. How could he have known? He was already too late. If you wish to know the meaning of the Buddha’s teaching, Look at the tracks on the road.
Questioning the way and pointing out the path—neither deviates nor contradicts the other. Each strikes the ox; there is release and there is rescue.
When their sharp edges meet, they are like a needle and its eye fitting together. Vast and open is this single Road of the Arhats; let us all join hands and go and come, resting therein.
(As in the Hermitage’s usage).
The Fifth Generation after the Sixth Patriarch (the First of the Fourth Generation after Nanyue):
Chan Master Linji Yixuan of Linji in Zhenzhou (he succeeded Huangbo). Initially at Huangbo, he attended the assembly as a disciple.
At that time, the First Seat in the hall (namely, Muzhou) urged him to pose a question. The Master then asked: "How is it?"
"This is the very intent of the Patriarch’s coming from the West. Huangbo then struck him. Thus he asked three times and was struck three times.
He then took his leave of the First Seat, saying, "I have already benefited from your encouragement in engaging me in dialogue;
I have only received the Master’s blows. It is my regret that I am so dull-witted; I shall now go to travel among other quarters. The First Seat then said to Huangbo, "Yi—"
Although Xuansha was born late, he was nonetheless most extraordinary. When he took his leave, he wished for further guidance and instruction.
The following day, the Master took his leave of Huangbo, who directed him toward Dayu. The Master then went to visit Dayu. Dayu asked, "Where have you come from?
The Master replied, "I have come from Huangbo. Dayu asked, "What instructions did he give you? The Master said, "I personally asked about the West..."
[The Master] asked for the meaning of what had come. Huangbo struck him. Thus, he asked three times and was struck three times.
Not knowing where his fault lay, Xitang said, "Huangbo is so compassionate that he has exhausted himself for your sake, yet you still seek out his faults.
At this, the Master attained great enlightenment and said, "There is not much more to the Buddha-dharma after all. Xitang said, "Fool!"
He then grabbed the Master by the collar of his robe and said, "Just now you said I did not understand;
now you say there is not much to it. How much is there? Come on, how much is there? The Master struck him three times under the ribs.
Xituo pushed him away and said, "Your teacher is Huangbo; it is none of my business. The Master returned to Huangbo, who asked: The Master returned to Huangbo, who asked:
“You have returned too quickly,” the Master said. Baizhang replied, “It is precisely because my heart as an old woman is so earnest.
Mazu said, “That old fellow Dayu—wait until I see him, and I will give him a beating. Baizhang said, “Why speak of ‘waiting to see’? Strike him right now!”
He then slapped Nanquan once. Nanquan laughed heartily, "Hein, hein! (This follows the account in the *Chuan Deng Lu*;
the *Lian Zhu Yuan Ben*, the *Lian Deng Lu*, and the *Wu Deng Hui Yuan* are all largely the same with minor differences. Guishan asked Yangshan, "At that time, Linji obtained the power of Dayu."
Having gained the power of *gegen* (yellow-barked tree), Yang said, "Not only can I ride the tiger's head, I also know how to grasp its tail.
The verse says:
Three times his sleep-filled eyes were struck and would not open; Suddenly he reared up in madness, roaring like thunder. Behold the horse wearing red tassels!
Fú is simply last year’s former student, Césou (Zūn of Yexuān).
With one punch, he topples the Yellow Crane Tower; with one kick, he overturns the Parrot Isle. When there is spirit, he adds to that spirit;
where there is no elegance, he is nonetheless elegant. (Báiyún Duān).
Thunder and lightning roar and crash; sea and mountains grow dark. A family sits in sorrow, their door closed against the rain. Suddenly a wild wind arises and the black clouds disperse;
the bright sun fills the sky and the stars and constellations divide. (Bao-ning Yong)
When thunder, lightning, and wind blow, they should simply cease; the giant turtle has no means to ascend the riverbank. Turning his body around, he drinks once and the vast ocean is exhausted;
bells and drums resound across the mountains and rivers of the four hundred prefectures. (Zhaojue Zong)
He then said, "The Buddha-dharma has nothing much to it. A true man would not willingly go astray from himself.
Three punches under the ribs clearly demonstrate his faith; this was not handed down by Huangbo. (Zhenjing Wen)
Fierce in the monastic groves was Huangbo; raising his staff, he struck the traveler on the road. Upon returning to Dayu, he finally recognized his debt of gratitude;
he gave the old woman a slap across the face. (Huangbo is victorious.)
A single blow would not yet be considered extraordinary; sixty strokes of the mountain cane are far too late. In the end, he still could not discern the pain or the itch;
even when ascending the hall, he still spoke of "brushing the thorn branch. (Foguo Bai).
Three times he was turned back at the Dragon Gate with his forehead marked; amidst the thunderous waves within Gaolian Creek, he surged upward again toward the surging billows.
Breaking through the vast blue sea, his eye was opened. (Yunxi Gong)
A chick in its ninth week of incubation; a colt from a thousand-li journey. The true wind passes through the flute; the hidden mechanism releases the pivot.
When it comes crashing face-to-face, it rolls like a flash of lightning; where the miasmic clouds are rent asunder, the solitary sun shines forth.
To pluck the tiger’s whiskers—do you see it? This is truly a magnificent great man. (Tiantong Jue)
Marking his forehead three times as he descends the Dragon Gate, both cheeks are scorched by the sun until they glow like fire.
One morning, suddenly piercing the surging waves of peach blossoms, his head and horns soar forth, generating wind and clouds. Once wind and clouds arise, they cannot be detained;

with fins flapping vigorously, he returns to the Isle of Yingzhou. When the ancient dragon meets him, they exchange greetings; he spits out a bright pearl without the slightest shame. (By Shangfang Yi)
The questioner’s intent was not mere play-acting; having been struck three times, what "handle" did he have? (Min Gufo). At Vulture Peak, he was beaten severely yet did not die;
at Gao’an, he lightly brushed it aside and was revived. Seeing the opportune moment, he alone revealed the three blows;
facing such a challenge, who could discern the single shout? (Changling Zhuo).
Linji completed three summer retreats without studying under Huangbo; for the sixty blows he received, his hands and feet were left bewildered.
Suddenly awakening to the Master’s profound compassion, he instead struck him with a fist beneath the ribs. No one understands this meaning; beneath the forest trees, I recall the Three Mysteries.
(Zhang Wujin): Splitting open Mount Hua, it reaches the color of the sky; releasing the Yellow River, its sound flows to the sea. After the blind donkey has died, the thistle branch snaps;
how many people are there now in the great earth? (Longmen Yuan).

【Continued Collection】Do not cling even slightly more to the provisions for the path; fearing that the years on this forked road will only grow longer, strike three resounding blows right here and now.
Last night, as always, one lay among the reeds. (Zhenjing Wen)
Breaking through the mountain-demon’s cave of yore, The true eye is opened wide, illuminating heaven and earth. Three blows beneath the ribs—there is nothing more to it;
A single shout like thunder, bursting forth from the sea gate. (Fóxìng Tàiyī)
Huangbo never spared a blow from his staff; Gaofeng’s fist was a mistaken calculation. From this point on, thorns have grown throughout the world;
the Buddha-dharma has not gained even an inch of length. (Fozhao Guang)
To accept it under the staff is already self-deception; to listen to others’ idle chatter is certainly inappropriate.
Even if you know that the Buddha-dharma is not so vast, how can it compare to the time before you ever asked? (Dun’an Yan)
Before Huangbo’s hall, one receives the staff; beneath Dayu’s ribs, a fist comes crashing down.
If you say that the Buddha-dharma is not much, in the end it is clear that your eyes have not yet opened. (Shuan’an Yan)
One meal destroys the entire family; two more meals bring ruin upon descendants. Silver mountains and iron walls are all pierced through;
ten thousand miles of cloudless sky reveal the expanse of the universe. (Mianjie)
Huangbo Ga’ang’s old bone mallet sits upright, settling dragons and snakes throughout the world;
the bed-wetting ghost-child has no core essence—carrying one gourd, he sells to two houses. (Xiaoweng Kan).
Receiving a blow atop Mount Huangbo; a fist struck beneath the ribs at Dayu. The great purport of the Buddha-dharma remains ten thousand miles apart (Pō’ān Xiān).
Three times he knocked at the gate, yet it would not open; empty-handed, he wandered back and forth across the vast distance.
Suddenly, the mirror of karma shattered into a hundred fragments, and only then did he realize that his face had been covered in ash all along. (Muan Yong)
Calamity and fortune have no gate; one invites them from oneself. Three times struck by the blind staff upon the donkey’s waist—how pitiable is the resentment for the ruin of state and home!
Ten thousand ages of spring breeze cannot blow it away. (Tianmu Li)
When Linji met Huangbo, when had they ever walked hand-in-hand? Slapping the cheek and striking the ribs—filial piety arises on both sides. (Puweng Xian)
The wind roars as it uproots trees and whistles through the branches; clouds and rain alternate within its midst. A thousand waves and ten thousand billows startle heaven and earth;
only upon reaching the sea does one know that the message cannot pass. (Xutang Yu)
After Linji appeared in the world, he used only the staff and shouts to instruct his disciples. Whenever he saw a monk enter the gate, he would immediately shout.
A verse says:
Linji’s shout is like a thunderclap; A single sound splits the evil brain. Suddenly piercing through the Dragon’s Cave, It shatters the bright [mirror].
The pearl is broken and the horn is snapped. (Haiyin Xin).
Upon entering the gate, he immediately shouts; this is already enough to cause distress. Countless Chan practitioners still go on to discuss its comprehensive scope. (Dahong En).
Ten thousand miles of azure sky, utterly free from a speck of dust. A single clap of thunder shakes heaven and earth.
Throughout the vast universe there are countless people; how many of them now possess a true brain? (Baizhang Yuan).

A single sword settles the dust; by what means can host and guest be distinguished? As they climb mountains and cross rivers to present tribute together, who recognizes the sagely and enlightened ruler? (Da Hong Su)
Facing the front, he roars and roars like a spring thunderclap; the eyes of the ten-thousand hibernating dragons and snakes are opened wide.
Suddenly, if one turns back with no skill at all, let them lie through the ages in the dust and dirt. (Foguo Bai).
Suddenly, a shout like a bolt of lightning; though the hibernation-cave is opened, little of life remains. If there is a way to turn back, only then is there a path to use;
do not gaze at the fragrant grasses and lament for the Wangsun. (Like a place of practice).

Amidst the blazing light of the sun, a thunderclap resounds; the waves at the Dragon Gate are turbulent and the winds are high, as countless scaled dragons with embroidered fins have their foreheads marked. (Puyongping)
A single shout strikes the mark like a swift, raging thunderclap; the *śakara* eye opens at the crown of the head.
Among the seventy-two patriarchs of the West, who is capable of enduring this one blow? (Fuxincai).
With no trace left of following or reversing, and the traces of sages and ordinary beings obliterated, under the bright sun and blue sky, thunder rolls and lightning strikes.
The Treasury of the True Dharma Eye is extinguished with nothing to transmit; old man Linji was a thief who steals in broad daylight. (Yunyan’s reason).
Suddenly, with a shout like thunder, he lets nothing remain—saints or ordinary beings—from this moment on.
Even if the fires of the kalpa burn through the three periods of time, this shout remains ever-present, its nature ever more luminous. (Yun’gai Chang)
The burrows of hibernating creatures remain dark and sealed, their doors frozen shut. Suddenly, a single clap of thunder shakes the void.
Dragon and serpent, one by one, seize the clouds and mist; every inchworm feeds upon the dust and soil. (Zhang Wujin)
Upon entering the gate, he immediately roared; utterly devoid of any core substance, he led his descendants to dally with the vapors of gruel and rice.
(Jingshan Daoyuan). While Zhang Gong was not yet drunk, Li Gong supported him; from this point on, his good reputation filled the roads.
Yet the Vajra-being opened its mouth and laughed: "Who could possibly cherish your talisman for protection? (Fodeng Xun).
[Continued Collection] The Dragon Controls the Hanging River; Sea Moon in Autumn. Smoke, Mist, Wind, and Rain are Gathered at Once. Waves and Tides rush on—hard for people to comprehend.
Cutting off the thousand rivers, the waters no longer flow. (The Daoist who Carves Talismans).
Upon entering, he immediately roared, cutting off all deliberation; In vain, they brandish their double fists as he establishes the rules.
With his murderous "triangular eyes" turned back, The monastic groves suffer calamity for a thousand ages. (Fozhao Guang)
With a roar and a shout, the spirits of ten thousand people are drained; yet in the deliberations of the Buddha-dharma, there still lacks one move.
(Nirvana is without attachment). Upon meeting, he simply roars; clamor upon clamor. At the crossroads, he sweeps away the wine jars. (Dian-niu You).
Swallowing the sudden thunderclap—do not seek understanding before the sound. At the moment of biting the arrowhead at the front line, you have already missed the first move.
It does not reside where the cliff stands sheer; how could it ever moor upon level ground? Wild waters stretch white to the heavens; across the autumn sky, a solitary eagle soars.
(Should be An’gang Hua). “Zhi-hu-ye-zhe.
Snow, moon, wind, and flowers—though their heads and faces are each distinct, they belong to the same household. (Or An’gang Ti).
A thunderclap resounds in the clear sky; thorns are planted along the official road. To encounter such things is to lose one's spirit;
what was ominous before is not auspicious after. (Wuzhun Shanfeng)
Once, while Linji was working together with Huangbo on a communal labor of weeding the tea garden, Huangbo arrived late.
Linji greeted him and stood there pressing down his hoe. Huangbo said, "Are you exhausted? Linji replied, "I have only just begun digging the ground;

why do you speak of exhaustion? Huangbo struck him. Linji seized the staff and pushed Huangbo over. Huangbo called for the *karmadāna* (the monastery official), saying, "Pull me up! When the official pulled him up, Huangbo said: [The text ends here.]
"How could the Master tolerate such a windbag? Baizhang then struck the *karmadāna*. The Master was digging with a hoe and said, "In other places they perform cremation;
here, we bury people alive. Miaoyan asked Yangshan, "What was the meaning behind Huangbo striking the *karmadāna*?
Yangshan replied, "The real thief has run away, and the pursuer is taking the beating for the stolen goods."
The verse says:
Seizing the banner and pulling the drum, one must apply the spirit. Though father and son are close, the Dharma is not so.
To report this to the Chan guests from the four quarters: Do not idly act like those who wait by a stump. (Zhenjing Wen)
Among a hundred horses, there is one mule; though it kicks and stamps in every direction, there is nothing that can be done. Today, this wind-crazed Linji is just like that;
he instead ordered Huangbo to beat the *vīnā* (the monastery official). (Fujian Yongqin)
[Continued Collection] Huangbo falls to the ground. The Rector helps him up. Cremation or burial alive—pure wind has not yet ceased. (Zhenru Zhe).

Huangbo treats the living as if they were dead; Linji treats the dead as if they were alive. If the *vinaya* master does not understand the matter truly, he cannot avoid mistaking the bell for a water jar. (Chang of Yuet Tang)
[Added from another source] While Linji was planting cypress trees, Huangbo asked, "Why are you planting so many in the deep mountains?
The Master replied, "To provide a historical record for future generations. He then struck the ground twice with his spade.
Huangbo raised his staff and said, "You shall receive my beating! The Master made a series of sighing sounds. Huangbo said, "My school has reached you."
This prediction was only now revealed. Guishan asked Yangshan, "Tell me, when Huangbo’s final words merely entrusted [the Dharma] to Linji, was there perhaps another underlying intent?
Yangshan replied, "It was also entrusted to Linji. Guishan then asked, "What will it be like hereafter?
Yangshan said, "One person points south; the mandate shall prevail throughout Wu and Yue. (The character for "south" is *nan*.)
The commentary on the *stūpa* states: "Sitting alone, he shook with majesty"—this record appeared [only] now. It further states:

"If one encounters a great wind, this record also appears. Guishan said: "So it is, so it is" (both of these are recorded according to the *Chuan deng lu*; other versions differ slightly). The verse says:
Boundaries of rivers and mountains marked by oaths on leather and stone; beneath the Han Gaozu’s court was Zhang Liang. A thousand words and ten thousand phrases—no one understands them;
yet again he follows the warbling oriole over the low wall. (Cuiyan Zhen)
The hoe in my hand is used today; it is likened to oneself, as heavy as ten thousand *qun* of jade and stone.
Even were it the eight-armed Mahānārāyaṇa, though he exerted all his strength to shake it, he could not move it. (Fojian Huiqin)
Blown by the wind and beaten by the rain, the joints wither once more. A thousand-foot dragon-snake thrusts into the great void.
How laughable that these descendants lack any skill; from this point on, their entire lives have been smeared over. (Lan’an Shu)

Linji addressed the assembly, saying, "All of you, upon this lump of red flesh there is a true person of no station who constantly enters and exits through the gates of your faces. If you do not recognize him, simply ask the old monk.
At that time, a monk asked, "What is the true person of no station? The Master struck him and said, "The true person of no station!"
"What is this dried-up piece of excrement? Later, when Xuefeng heard of this, he remarked, "Linji is much like a thief who steals in broad daylight.
(This follows the account in the *Chuan deng lu*; it differs slightly from other versions in the *Lian deng hui yao*). The verse says:
The Bian-king jade is flawless, its brilliance eclipsing the sun; though the King of Qin cherished it, he could not outwit its owner.
Alas, it has once more fallen into the hands of Zhang Yi—now it returns home, filling the road with a refreshing breeze. (Foyin Yuan)
The spring breeze surges vast, warming heaven and earth; everywhere, the mountains are hidden within mists and vapors. The True Person of No Rank cannot be sought;
fallen flowers are seen again following the flowing stream. (Baiyun Yuan)
Scattering earth and raising dust, there is nowhere to hide; entering and exiting through the gate of the face, it is vast and grand. To discharge excrement and urine is but a trivial matter;
amidst this vast flow, who can distinguish the foul from the fragrant? (Baoning Yong)
Eyebrows arched, nose straight, eyes black; captured, it turns out to be a demon-servant. When a dung-clod is hurled at him, he pays no mind at all;
even as he looks at people, his face remains blurred. (Shangfang Yi)
Walking alone through the monastic groves, he was peerless; Linji’s sharp wit was irresistible.
Even now, four hundred years later, his descendants continue to raise up and proclaim these matters. (Daochangru).
The True Person of No Rank enters and exits through the gate of the face; neither "ordinary" nor "holy" can name him. How could birth and death be established?
Nevertheless, though he pervades the entire world, he has never been hidden; he is so vast and indistinct that there is nowhere to pick him up. (Yungai Chang)
"The True Person of No Rank," said Linji: "I urge you not to seek him further. On the Bird Path there is no effort, and those who travel it are rare;
at the top of the hundred-foot pole, one must reach it personally. (Tongzhao Feng)

Sounds and forms do not disturb the eyes and ears; heaven and earth are fundamentally of the same root. Suddenly hearing a bird singing beneath the crags, one turns back and arrives once more at the pine gate. (Fóxīn Cái)
The True Man of No-Rank is this bare lump of flesh; when inspiration arises, he waves his hand and departs from Chang’an. The General already possesses a fine reputation;
even if he does not receive a fief or rank, it is still a life of leisure. (Shushan Chang)

Entering and exiting through the gateway of the face, we meet at every turn; though the sun and moon have long been present, their true nature remains unrecognized. Having wandered habitually among seas and mountains, those who truly know me are few;
I shall turn my body back and lie down amidst the clouds atop the ridge. (Shushan).
Entering and exiting the gateway of the face is difficult to perceive; the True Person of No-Station is but a foot’s distance away. On the path ahead, one’s body is as light as a leaf;
one’s lofty name is as heavy as a mountain for a thousand ages. (Gushan Gui)
Seeing the village monk at the back of his head, he opens his eyes wide while dreaming. Although he manages to catch the rat, he breaks the oil jar with a single blow. (Jingshan Gaofeng)
[Continued Collection] All phenomena are of one suchness; there is no need for selection. In this one suchness, who selects and who does not select?
This very life-and-death is fundamentally bodhi. The Tathāgatas of the three periods of time share the same eye. (Changsha Cen)
Upon this mass of red flesh is the True Man of No Rank. Eight *liang* in the left eye, half a *jin* in the right eye.
Buying high and selling low: gold and silver. (Baoning Yong)
In Zhangzhou and Quanzhou of Fujian, the front plaques are like fans; one may hear of their fame, but cannot see their face (Zhenjing Wen).
A fine flower is pasted right before one’s face: if you recognize it, you are used by it; if you do not recognize it when the flower is pasted, your mouth is full of teeth.
The true person of no station offers up the new at every turn; grabbing him by the chest and twisting him, there is no falling into the roles of host and guest.
"Dry dung, dry dung! Three people take a tortoise and certify it as a turtle. (Yuet Tang Chang)
The True Person of No Station does not hide; entering and exiting through the gateway of the face, he is manifest and majestic.
Responding to conditions and engaging with beings, he appears in every instance, so that his family renown spreads throughout the Great Tang. (He Shan Fang)
Casting the seal and dissolving the seal, the true command is fully upheld. To understand the fundamental principle, there must not be a single moment’s interval.
(For the nun Wuzhuo). Spring snow fills the sky; wherever it touches, flowers bloom. One does not know which tree in the garden is the true plum.
(Nutang Si): When the joints fall from the staff, one returns to the source; amidst the flash of lightning, one plants the banner of faith.
The monastic groves suffer ruin with no place for cleansing; how many mistake this for mere verbal fatuity? (Houan’an Ti).
Linji asked the steward, "Where have you come from? The steward replied, "I have come from selling yellow rice in the prefectural city.
The Master said, "Have you sold it all? The steward said, "I have sold it all. The Master drew a line with his staff and said, "Can you sell this as well?
The steward gave a shout. The Master struck him. When the head cook arrived, the Master recounted the previous conversation. The cook—
[The Master] said, "The head monk does not understand the Master’s meaning. The Master asked, "And what about you?
The attendant bowed, and the Master struck him as well. A verse says:
The Goddess of Merit and the Lady of Darkness—neither are taken up by a wise master. In future generations, descendants will be utterly crude and ignorant;
the great framework lies abandoned upon the ground—who will lift it up? (By Zhengjue Yi).
The head of the monastery let out a shout; the chief cook prostrated. Linji’s command was uniquely transcendent throughout past and present (Zhenru Zhe).
Linji’s full potential and style were lofty; there was an eye upon his staff that could discern the finest hair of autumn. He swept away the foxes and hares with a rigorous family tradition;
he transformed fish and dragons as thunderous fire consumed them. A sword that brings life, a blade that kills—leaning against the heavens, it shines like snow, its sharpness piercing the wind.
Fur. When the first-class command is issued, flavors are distinguished; where does the pain of ten parts fall upon? (Tiantong Jue).
Holding forth the precious sword, its blade is like frost; how many times has it faced the battlefield to slay the barbarian kings?
Sentient beings and rational principles alike are cut into three pieces; a single cold radiance shoots beside the Dipper. (Baizun Yuan).
The Master selling rice is haughty in his demeanor; light as spring snow, he drifts away on his own. Just as he lands, everyone loves him;
yet unable to withstand the wind, he vanishes on the spot. (Fujian Yongqin)
A mass of crimson flames stretches across the clear sky; it makes no distinction between gold, silver, iron, or tin. Once they enter, all are made to become water;
how could a mosquito ever find a place to rest within? (Jingshan Gaofeng)

[Continued Collection] Ten thousand *li* of sky, cloudless; the blue heavens and bright sun. The Dipper turns and the stars shift; thunder rolls and lightning flashes as the banner of victory is unfurled.
He seizes the jade of ten cities, sings the song of Great Peace, and blows the holeless flute. (Nantang Xing).
Holding the "hair-cutting blade" in his grasp, he displays his full majesty; no peeping through side doors or back alleys is permitted.
Both the holy and the mundane are cut off at once, so that for a thousand ages it turns ever more radiant. (The Poison-Coated Whip)
He strikes when one shouts; he strikes when one prostrates. Great Master Linji—how well he knows the rites!
(Yi’an Shen). Whoever it may be, he cuts them off entirely. To kill, one must be a supreme general. Within the staff there is an eye as bright as the sun;
if you wish to recognize true gold, look for it in the fire. (Wuchan Cai).
[Supplement] When Linji was traveling through the capital to solicit alms, he arrived at the door of a certain household and said, "Please add to my bowl for your family's sake.
A woman said, "You are truly insatiable. The Master replied, "I have not even received any rice yet; why do you say I am insatiable?"
Baobian then closed the door. The verse says:
A thousand-fathom line hangs straight down; When the scarlet-scaled fish strikes and leaps upon the hook, Amidst slanting winds and fine rain, one sings of returning home.
Drunk and fallen by the thatched window, one knows naught of the hundred things. (Biefeng Yin)
Adding to the household bowls, he wanders through the village; suddenly, with one cry, he gives rise to insatiability. The alms-collector clearly feels there is still too little;
the gate is shut, yet he forces himself to be alert. (Tianmu Li)
When begging for food at the homes where alms bowls are added, do not hesitate when the wooden gate is closed.
Raise once more that "white-thief" hand; it shall replace those iron eyes and copper pupils. (Bya-nyi-ping)
A fly seeing blood; the *hudiguda* bird. A fist comes, and a kick is returned. Resin and lac adhere to one another.
Where it is difficult to lift up, there is even more elegance. (Xutang Yu)
[Added from another source] Linji ascended the hall. A monk stepped forward; the Master immediately shouted.
The monk also shouted, then bowed. The Master struck him. Another monk came and held up his whisk; the monk bowed, and the Master struck him. Yet another monk came;
the Master likewise held up his whisk, but the monk paid no heed, and the Master struck him as well. Another monk came to seek instruction; the Master—
[The Master] raised his whisk. A monk said, "Thank you, Preceptor, for your instruction. The Master also struck him.
Yunmen spoke on his behalf, saying, "It is only fitting for an old fellow. Dajue said, "He has attained it, indeed; yet he has still not seen the true mechanism of Linji."
The Verse says:
In general, it is difficult for those who visit a Master to find their footing; yet, wherever one finds a place to linger, one should linger there.
My own house has its own tradition: the reed flute is blown crosswise, and the universe is vast. (Cuiyan Zhen)
Both host and guest fall into the third mechanism; at every stage they unfurl their banners yet do not display them.
Within the flash of a stone-fire, victory and defeat are distinguished; one rides an iron horse backward up Mount Sumeru. (Gushan Gui)

Written at noon on the fifth day of the fifth month: May all malicious mouths and poisonous tongues be utterly eliminated. Furthermore, may it be swift as the "Ji-jí rú lù-ling" (Act with Urgency According to the Command).
There is no need to paint a spider upon the door. (Jingshan Gaofeng)
There is an eye at the tip of the staff; within that eye there is no sinew. One often encounters turbid wealth, but rarely meets pure poverty.
Having entered the cave gate, the smoke-lock has been severed; one knows not how many springs have passed upon the world. (Xue’an Jin)
In a flash of lightning, host and guest are distinguished; atop the back of empty space, the fundamental principles are established. The livelihood of the Patriarchs was nothing more than this;
the descendants of later generations have swept it all away into emptiness. (Songyuan Yue)
While Linji was ascending the hall, the two head seats of the two halls met and simultaneously let out a shout. A monk asked the Master, "Is there still guest and host?

The Master replied, "Guest and host are perfectly distinct. The Master then called to the assembly, saying, "If you wish to understand the phrase of Linji regarding guest and host, go ask the two head seats in the hall.
The verse says: Guest and host are clearly distinguished; The shout rings out, piercing the ears. If you wish to see the true meaning, Go ask the two head seats.
The two head monks of the hall are both masters of the art; the principles therein are clearly distinguished. Guest and host are as distinct and clear as a mirror;
the Master points out the flower in one’s eye. (Fenyang Shanzhao)

The mechanism of the hen pecking and the chick hatching—arrow meeting point-blank; in that fleeting moment, guest and host were distinguished. The Master, out of compassion for sentient beings, bestowed [the Dharma] upon both the ordained and the laity;
in the north, the Yellow River flows turbid to its very depths. (Ciming Yuan)
The tips of arrows meeting cause mutual clamor; Li Guang shot many double-tailed eagles.
How laughable, people coming to gaze at the horizon, while a swift falcon flies clearly past Silla. (Foyin Yuan)
The two head monks of the hall descend together and shout; the pupils of their eyes are flecked with gold dust. The awl and the knife are used as one and cannot be distinguished;
a black-lacquered Kunlun man is lost in the night moon. (Fushan Yuan)
A single shout must cause the water to flow upstream; clearly, guest and host have not yet exchanged their due responses.
If the person can understand the transmission of this news, the sun will rise from the Fu-sang tree at midnight. (Haiyin Xin)
Both halls issue their shouts together; clearly distinguished are guest and host. If you step upon this pivotal mechanism, gold from the South is as cheap as dirt.
(The grace of Kṣitigarbha).
Guest and host are clearly distinguished within each phrase; from this, the Three Mysteries shake heaven and earth.
How many travelers on the road are there today? All day long they toil in vain, rushing off by themselves. (Yunxi Gong)
The two armies clash; the author’s skill lies in the mechanism. The wealthy man’s arrangements depend on the moment.
If one encounters the hand of General Li Guang, to whom would the stability of the state and the peace of the realm be entrusted? (Cao Tang Qing).
Li Lou’s vision does not reach it; Shi Kuang’s hearing is likewise mistaken. To recognize the host and guest within this—midday, and the Milky Way descends. (Huanglong Zhen)
To repay injustice with equanimity—the royal law has no partiality. Though Linji possessed the clear eye, he was nonetheless the essence of Huanglong. (Jingshan Daoyuan)
[Continued Collection] Both halls shout together; host and guest are distinguished. Shining and functioning simultaneously, they penetrate past and present.
The true lineage of Linji transmits a flourishing transformation; the descendants have attained the profound meaning of the intent. (Daopei Zhi)

A single shout distinguishes guest and host for the occasion; do not forcibly differentiate between the known and the seen as distant or intimate. When one turns back upon oneself, the lion’s majestic ferocity is extreme;
without the sinews within the eye, one is poor for a lifetime. (Nun Wuzhuo Zong).

Linji was once asked by Senior Monk Ding, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? The Master descended from his meditation seat, seized him, gave him a slap, and then pushed him away. Ding stood there motionless. A monk standing nearby said, "Senior Monk Ding, why do you not prostrate yourself? As soon as Ding made the prostration, he suddenly attained great enlightenment. The verse says: The Great Meaning of the Buddha-dharma Is a single blow of the palm. If you can understand it right now, You will see Linji face-to-face. If you hesitate for even a moment, You will fall into the pit of birth and death. If you wish to know the Buddha-dharma, Look at the Senior Monk Ding. He was like a dragon leaping from the deep; His whole body was soaked through. He did not wait for the words to end; He immediately attained liberation. If you have not yet reached this state, Do not merely seek it in books. If you wish to see the ancient master, You must look at the Senior Monk Ding. If you can understand this, You will see Linji face-to-face. If you hesitate for even a moment, You will fall into the pit of birth and death. The total capacity of the Ultimate Limit (Duanji) continues the tracks of his predecessors; why must one bring it forth with deliberation?
When the Great Spirit (Guliang) raised his hand, it required no more than a moment to split the myriad peaks of Mount Hua into ten thousand fragments. (Xuedou Xian)
Not falling into past or future, alone transcending antiquity and the present. Calling back a thousand-year dream, a bird flies out from the ninefold heights.
With a single blow, the light bursts forth; a brand-new pellet emerges as gold from the furnace. (Tiantong Jue)
The lightning-fast pivot surpasses Zhaozhou; to guide others, one must reach the ultimate end.
Holding aloft the Xiangshanzi in his palm, he ascends straight up to the high, high twelve-story tower. (Fujian Qin)
"One blow leaves a trace; one slap leaves a welt of blood. Without the numinous root of prajñā, how can one resolve this when reaching such a point? (Nanhuang Bing).
[Continued Collection] Head and horns exposed; pointing it out, one finally sees. At the moment of seeing, there is no lingering. The needle and thread are clearly demarcated.
As soon as he steps off the bed and tries to grapple him, [the Master] thrusts out a palm—the intent of the Buddha-dharma. Sweat flows down his back as he calls him back.
A white lotus blooms toward the heavens. (Yuet Tang Chang)
Half a catty is eight *liang*; eight *liang* is half a catty. Not recognizing the iron of Yaozhou, one calls it "silver from the mountains. (Lan’an Shu)
When the imperial edict is issued from the desk, the pivot of killing and giving life is fully wielded beyond the commandant’s barrier.
Turning one’s head to gaze at the solitary peak of Mount Hua, even the Great Spirit Juling raises his banner of surrender. (Xiatang Yuan)
Fully grasping and fully letting go, there is no passage for the wind. To point it out and break through it has already missed the mark.
Though one may attain awakening upon rising from prostration, on the street corner, Old Man Li is laughing himself down. (Biefeng Yin)

[Added from the Supplementary Collection] Once Mazu (the second patriarch) arrived to visit Linji, he spread out his sitting mat and asked, "Of the twelve faces of Avalokiteśvara, which one is the true face?

The Master stepped down from his rope seat; with one hand he gathered up the sitting mat and with the other he seized Mazu, saying, "Where has the twelve-faced Avalokiteśvara gone? Mazu turned his body as if to sit.
[Master Guishan] held up his staff and struck him. Xiangguo caught it and they both entered the abbot’s quarters together.
The Verse says: The Great Compassionate Avalokiteśvara reveals His true face; The official seal does not admit a needle, yet a single thread passes through.
A rat drags a gourd—how busy it is! Ghosts struggle with lacquered buckets—no one sees them. (Gushan Gui)
Having obscured that single stroke facing one directly, they pull it here and drag it there, presenting it to one another.
One does not know that, apart from the hand of Wang Wei, who else could have painted it so perfectly? (Jingshan Gaofeng)
The Eleven-faced Avalokiteśvara—neither of these two do I recognize. Taking hands, come and go; when the form is upright, the shadow is straight.
In human life, acquaintance is valued for the sake of knowing one's true companion. Water enters water; gold is traded for gold. (Teguk Yun)

[Added from the Supplementary Collection] Linji addressed the assembly, saying: "There is one person who, for kalpas, remains on the road yet never leaves home; there is another person who, for kalpas, leaves home yet is not on the road.

Now tell me, which of these two persons deserves to receive the offerings of devas and humans? The Verse says: One person dwells on the road for kalpas without leaving home; Another leaves home for kalpas without being on the road. If you can discern this matter, you will see that the Buddhas and patriarchs are all within it. If you cannot discern it, you will surely fall into the pit of doubt. If you wish to know the meaning of the Buddhas and patriarchs, Look at the man who is neither on the road nor at home.
The thunderclap has not yet faded; the lightning leaves no trace. At the third watch, the moon enters the window; at midnight, the donkey peers into the well.
Swiftly mount a fine steed and gallop up the high tower; not a speck of dust stirs atop Mount Sumeru. (Zu’ān Yìn)
[Added from the Supplementary Collection] When Linji visited Pingtian, he saw an older sister-in-law driving an ox along the road.
The Master asked the woman, "Which way does the road to Pingtian go? The woman struck the ox and said, "This beast runs everywhere;
even when it arrives here, it does not know the way. The Master said, "I am asking you: which way does the road to Pingtian go? The woman—
[The Master] said, "This beast has been raised for five years, yet it still cannot be used. The teacher said, "If you wish to observe the person before you, first observe what they employ.

There is further the intention of pulling out nails and extracting wedges. The verse says: Five years have passed since he was born; Though raised with such care, he remains untamed. To know the master, observe his tools; Therein lies the art of removing nails and extracting wedges.
A guest at Píngtián asks for the way; He raises his white staff and strikes the plowing ox. In the spring light before one’s eyes there is not much to see:
A pair of mandarin ducks follow the flowing water. (Xiaoweng Kan)
A black staff hangs upside down over a level field; he takes his weak ox and strikes it with a heavy whip.
To further say that it has been raised for five years—this from beginning to end is nothing but "old woman Chan. (Tianmu Li)
At the edge of the white-water paddy field, he asks for the way; the snow-browed old woman strikes the plow-ox. With straw sandals on slippery mud, the green mountains stretch afar;
even one who is not a man of sorrow is moved to grief. (Hengchuan Gong)
At present, this path is as level as a whetstone. Why not stride along with dignified ease?
Provoking the old woman until her ox-nature flares up—naked and beaten, how pitiable! (Zhuyu Jian)
[Added for inclusion] A monk asked Linji, "In seizing an elephant, one employs one's full strength; in seizing a rabbit, one also employs one's full strength.

I wonder, what kind of strength is it that is fully employed? The Master said, "The strength of non-deception. Verse: Seizing an elephant or seizing a rabbit, The power is complete in both cases. What power is it that is fully employed? It is the power of not deceiving.
When power is exercised in the present moment, A single hair’s breadth of attachment becomes deception.
Who knows that the thousand peaks of the blue waters Are all swept away by the autumn wind into a single withered gourd? (Xutang Yu)
[Supplement] Linji ascended the hall. A monk came forward and prostrated. The Master immediately shouted. The monk said, "Old Monk, do not stick out your head.
The Master said, "Tell me, where does it land? The monk then shouted. Another monk asked, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma?
The Master immediately shouted. The monk prostrated. The Master said, "Tell me, was that a good shout?"
"No. The monk said, "The grass-robbers have been utterly defeated. The Master asked, "Where does the fault lie? [The monk] said, "A second offense will not be tolerated.

The Master said, "If the assembly wishes to understand the Linji phrase of host and guest, go ask the two Zen practitioners in the hall. The verse says: No, no— The thief is caught red-handed. The guest and host are clearly distinguished; The thief has been completely routed. The fault lies where? A second offense will not be tolerated. If you wish to understand the Linji phrase of host and guest, Go ask the two Zen practitioners in the hall.
Kongming Zhuge lies hidden in his thatched hut; the enlightened ruler seeks the worthy and descends from his carriage three times. To repay the General, do not act rashly;
the Master’s strategies will surely leave no cause for concern. (Chongjuekong)
[Added from the Supplementary Collection] A monk asked Linji, "What is the realm of the three eyes?
The Master said, "I shall enter with you into the Pure and Wondrous Realm, don the robes of purity, and preach the Dharma-body Buddha.
Again, I shall enter the Realm of Non-differentiation, don the robes of non-differentiation, and preach the Reward-body Buddha. Furthermore, I shall enter the Realm of Liberation..."
In the midst [of the assembly], wearing a robe of radiant light, he speaks of the Nirmāṇakāya Buddha. The verse says:

Dharmakāya, Sambhogakāya, Nirmāṇakāya— Alas! You wretched goblins and sprites! Having encountered you in the Land of the Three Eyes, I laugh to death at this "True Person of No Rank. (Jingshan Daokai)
After Linji, he resided in the East Hall of Xinghua Temple in Daming Prefecture.

On the tenth day of the fourth month of the eighth year of the Xiandong era (the Dinghai year), as he was about to pass away, he spoke this verse of transmitting the Dharma: "Following the current without ceasing—how can one ask about this?
True illumination is boundless—how can one describe it to another? Transcending form and transcending name, no one receives it; The 'blow-off-hair' sword is used."
Liaojixu ground [the inkstone]. He then addressed the assembly, saying, "After my passing, you must not extinguish my Treasury of the True Dharma Eye.
Sansheng stepped forward and said, "How would we dare extinguish the Master’s Treasury of the True Dharma Eye? The Master said:

Later, when someone asks you, what will you say to them? Baizhang then gave a shout. The Master said, “Who knew that my Treasury of the True Dharma Eye would perish at the hands of this blind donkey? The verse says: When the Great Master was about to pass away, he called for his attendant. When the attendant arrived, the Master asked, “After I am gone, if someone asks you, ‘What did the Master say? what will you answer? The attendant replied, “I would simply tell them that the Master had already passed away. The Master struck him with his staff and said, “You would have been better off being struck by a wooden mallet! He then called again for his attendant. When the attendant arrived, the Master asked, “After I am gone, if someone asks you, ‘What did the Master say? what will you answer? The attendant remained silent. The Master said, “You have truly inherited my marrow. He then called for his attendant once more. When Yuanji was about to depart for his final nirvana, he gave earnest instructions that Fayen should maintain the Dharma well. Once the shout has been let fall, the path of mud and water cannot be opened;
from this point on, few will ride upon the blind donkey. (Huanglong Nan)
Who has been able to transmit the Treasury of the True Dharma Eye? With a single shout, the vast ocean is dried to its very bottom.

Splitting apart Mount Hua—the thunder was not so fierce; Illuminating the vast sea—the moonlight was not so bright.

As he stepped out the door, they shook hands and offered repeated instructions. Often, matters arise from such admonitions. "The road is long and the night is deep;
do not carry a torch. Let us all blow it out and walk in the dark. (Pogŭng Yong)
Dingning Fayuan showed that his end was near; with one shout, the profound barrier was cut off and no longer passed through.
Since then, the blind donkey has nowhere to be found—how many have asked the old fisherman upon the river? (Zhaojue Zong).

Decisively parting from the yellow and black [pigments], he distinguishes the true masters; with a single shout right before one's face, he settles dragons and snakes. His command is like a lethal poison that none can approach;
even if one were to obtain a blind donkey, it would only serve to trample the sand in vain. (The Three Patriarchs).
Linji’s full functioning—how can it be pointed out? This blind donkey has personally met a true connoisseur.
To ensure the ancestral wind does not fall into ruin, the meaning of the flowing water and lofty mountains grows ever deeper. (Lingyuan Qing)

The final testament left in the secret chamber need not be sought again; what necessity is there for urgent instructions on the eve of departure? A single breath from the phoenix’s down startles heaven and earth;
light shines upon the waters and rocks as the four seas become pure. (Yunxi Gong)
As soon as the Hu-le drum thunders, rain pours down like a cascade; the Yellow River’s nine bends swell to flood the four oceans.
Fortunately, the sluice gates at the water-weirs can be lowered, so that the vast waters flow ten thousand li away, their rushing sound silenced. (Pú Róng Píng)
The robe of faith was entrusted to Lu Neng at midnight; it stirred up trouble among the seven hundred monks of Huangmei.

The single branch of Linji and the Eye of the True Dharma—blind donkeys have extinguished them and earned the world’s loathing. Mind-to-mind they seal one another; from patriarch to patriarch the lamp is passed. Mountains and seas are leveled.
The transformation into the Kun and Peng [mythical birds] is but a name and phrase difficult to compare with; for the most part, such skillful means can turn back what was soaring upward.
(Tiantong Jue) The road to the mysterious pass of the Jade Cave is long; the peach of immortality is not a trivial fragrance. It is concealed and not permitted to ordinary people.
I see it; I only fear the spring breeze will leak its fragrance.
(Shangfang Yi) The Vermilion Phoenix leads its fledglings to nest in the bamboo fruits; when the wild goat hangs its horns from a tree branch, it is difficult to find them.
The blind donkey has extinguished the Eye of the True Dharma; its fame resounds through the vast universe. (Fuxin Cai)
The blind donkey extinguished the Eye of the True Dharma; his descendants emerged and spread throughout the Great Tang.
One must believe that within the vast mist and waves, there is surely another way to deliberate. (Fujian Yongqin)
Ten thousand streams flow toward the source; their momentum does not cease. Fish and dragons emerge and submerge, drifting at will.
A blind donkey extinguishes the Eye of the True Dharma, until even the Yellow River flows backward. (Nan-hua Bing)
Until old age he never opened a path of words; as he was about to depart, he turned his head back and offered this earnest instruction:
"Even at the bottom of the deepest sea, one still deems it shallow; go straight to the very edge of the Diamond Ocean. (Gushan Gui)
The blind donkey’s single shout startles the multitude; how can the True Dharma be entrusted to others? The Three Essentials and Three Mysteries are all utterly extinguished;
with a dignified gesture, he waves his hand and departs from the heavy city. (Jingshan Gaofeng)
[Continued Collection] "I urge you: faith in the True Dharma is not in vain. It is laughable that, at the moment of departure, one would stroke a tiger’s whiskers.
Having already examined the records of Mount Hua, I now add Pan Lang, who rode his donkey backward. (Haiyin Xin)
The single shout of the Three Sages is rarely taken up by those who can truly grasp it. Though it is a dead snake, when skillfully handled, it comes alive.

A fly lands on putrid meat—how stiff and rigid! Yet the golden-scaled fish that has passed through the net is full of vitality. Linji was a blind donkey; a gentleman might rate him an eight. (Ctangqiang Qing).
The blind donkey extinguished the Eye of the True Dharma; Linji turned his body and immediately rode backward.
He cannot be retained within the rank of Buddhas and Patriarchs; with all traces severed, who can know him? (Cishou Shen)
When grasping hands before the ten-thousand-fathom peak, a single pure song was known by few. One saw only the blind donkey startling the universe;
one did not know to whom the Dharma-eye had been entrusted. (Xuedou Zong)
How truly marvelous! How truly marvelous! The *wutou* resembles it; the *fuzi* is like it. Ten thousand *li* away, there is but a single stream of cold water.
How many people know that Caizhou has been shattered? How many people know? Heh! The horse-faced yakṣas and the ox-headed jailers.

(Zhandang Zhun): The ancestral style of Daji is shown to future generations; the adamantine jeweled sword is sharp at the gate. With a single clap of thunder, the clouds and rain disperse; to this day, father and son have not recognized one another. (Shui-an Yan)

The Venerable Master Chen of Muzhou (whose name was Daoming; he was a successor of Huangbo) would respond with sudden abruptness whenever scholars came to challenge him with questions.
His words were steep and formidable, and practitioners from all quarters looked up to him in admiration, calling him "Venerable Master Chen.

Initially, he resided at Longxing Temple in Muzhou, where he concealed his traces and hid his capabilities. Later, he returned to Kaiyuan Temple (now renamed Doushuai), where he lived in his quarters weaving straw sandals.
Because he had been raised by his mother, he was known by the nickname "The One Who Wore Straw Sandals from Chen. Upon seeing a monk lecturing, he called out, "Lecturer!
The lecturer responded, "Yes? The Master said, "A fellow carrying a single board. The verse says:
Bestowing compassion, one simply desires universal spiritual penetration; it is not for a master to give rise to delusions at will.
One must be taught to set down the "one-sided plank" directly, so as to spare others from wasting hundreds of thousands of lifetimes. (Fenyang Shanzhao)
Muzhou called out; he judged according to the hexagram. Whether he turned back or not, he was a fellow carrying a single board.
(Yang Woei, II). He did not value his master, but valued the ultimate public justice. Who among all quarters would dare to provoke his sharp spiritual edge?

He instructed Linji to study under Huangbo; he received Yunmen as a successor to Xuefeng. Weaving sandals, he knew only how to provide meals for his mother; with the door closed, how could he speak of anything else?
The Chan School: Everywhere in the monasteries, all receive its moistening grace. One cannot fathom where the wind and thunder arise from the old dragon.
A single blow behind the head causes every step to fall into a pit; even if one calls out, they will not return—this too is merely carrying a flat board in vain.
Passing through the Barrier of Muzhou, heaven and earth are but a single eye (Changling Zhuo).
Bitingly pungent and sharp, snarling and growling; recognize Jibei as the great tree that drives Yunmen over a precipice.
His spiritual capacity was steep and peerless; his words were like withered firewood. This is what is called "Wearing Old Straw Sandals" (Yuanwu Keqin).
Do not be hasty amidst the lightning and flames; do not be heedless upon the edge of the sword-wheel.
If you casually let go your entire being and enter [the Way], you will never again offend it by even a single hair’s breadth (Gushan Zhiguang).
Muzhou carries his board; there is no room for even a blink of an eye. Whether broad or narrow, long or short—there is no need to add or subtract.
(Jingshan Daoyuan) How many have supported Muzhou as he carried his board? Those who have lost their way likely number many along the journey.
To cause one to penetrate through at the moment of these words, the mind’s eye is suddenly awakened and restored to clarity. (Chuan’an Fang)
[Continued Collection] The man from Muzhou carrying a wooden board: when doing things, do not engage in analysis. The nostrils of the patch-robed monk reach toward the heavens;
one must know the essential point beneath his words. (Nantang Xing)
Pak Silt’u’s Zen has no clever tricks; a single phrase is as clear as a physical blow.
When a guest arrives, he simply shouts, “Carrying a wooden board!”—but who knows for certain who it is that carries the board? (Lan’an Shu).
The man from Muzhou carries a wooden board; from the start he has seen only one side. Three feet of water, shallow or deep;
above and below, two layers of heaven. (Xue’an Jin)
The mountains are towering; the waters flow surging. When viewed with cold eyes, there is nowhere for shame or embarrassment to dwell.
(Biefeng Yin) Waves rise from the red furnace, flying to strike the heavens; as a fierce flame passes through the wind, who dares to peer at it?
Even with three heads and six arms, upon reaching this point, one must cease boasting of the "first principle. (Muguan Yong)

A scholar once visited Muzhou, claiming that he was proficient in twenty-four styles of calligraphy. The Master pointed a single dot in the air with his staff and asked, "Do you understand? The scholar was at a loss.

The Master said, "So you say you are proficient in twenty-four styles of calligraphy, yet you do not even recognize the eight strokes of the character 'eternity' (永). The verse says: The eight strokes of the character "eternity" Are all contained within this one dot. If you can see it, you have understood; If you cannot, you are still lost in confusion.
Even if you were to master the twenty-four styles, It would still be no more than a mere dot. If you wish to know the source of the dot, Look directly at the tip of the staff.

Not a single atom has ever differed; it does not increase throughout eons as numerous as motes of dust. The eyes of hundreds of thousands of Buddhas all share this same numinous clarity. (Mingzhao Qian)
The Zen Master’s staff is the scholar’s brush; all skillful arts emerge from his hand.
If you do not yet clearly understand the Eightfold Path of Calligraphy, there is a single dot before you, black as lacquer. (Fujian Qinqin)
[Continued Collection] A single stroke of the pivot must be applied with intimacy; pitiful, the poor son has no sinews in his eyes.
One must know the place where the eight dharmas are inscribed: the first arrow is still light, but the subsequent arrow is deep. (Shui’an 1)

Opened wide in eight characters, fully revealed. Standing alone and precarious, the Way is lofty; there are no further skills or means to speak of as one pleases.
Separately, separately. Seven of the Southern Dipper, eight of the Northern Dipper. (Huguo Qin).

Spring departs and autumn arrives; ancient and modern alike. When we meet, let us not debate how deep our connection has been over time.
Eat when hungry and drink when thirsty—there is nothing else to do—and simply let the frost and snow cover our heads as they will. (By Po-nyeong Yong)

When the mechanism is exhausted and effort forgotten, yet the bonds of gratitude and righteousness are severed, one becomes an unfilial icchantika. (Danxia Chun)
