High and lofty, the solitary peak shrouded in misty snow; beyond the kalpas, the path of concealment and manifestation is impassable. At midnight, the news of the ridge-plum blossoms shifts;
it has nothing to do with the springtime colors, yet its dark fragrance is thick. (Zhengtang Bian)
[Added from the Supplementary Collection] When Dongshan first visited Nanquan, he encountered a vegetarian feast being held for the anniversary of Mazu’s passing.
Nanquan asked, "I wonder whether Mazu will come to partake in the offerings? No one in the assembly could answer. The Master stepped forward and said, "He will come when he has a companion.
Nanquan remarked, "Although this boy is young, he is indeed fit for refinement. The Master replied, "Do not force a noble person into a lowly role."
The Verse says:
Guest of white clouds, companion of green mountains; Within this position, look at the mutual exchange. A bottomless platter held aloft with a turn of the hand;
A bowl that pierces the heart, a meal for the whole body. (Tiantong Jue)
A thousand feet of silk line hang straight down; as soon as one wave stirs, ten thousand follow. A scene on the river at evening, worthy of a painting:
the fisherman dons his single-layered raincoat and returns home. (Chandadi points out.)
The companion arrives; the earth parts and the heavens open. Cold light emerges once more from its case; upon the ancient road, not a speck of dust remains.
The myriad phenomena of the universe all join their palms in reverence; Mount Sumeru, towering and steep, performs the *samaya* dance. (Chan Master Chu’an Yin)

[Added for inclusion: Dongshan went to visit Guishan and asked, "Recently I heard the story of National Teacher Huizhong of Nanyang regarding 'insentient beings preaching the Dharma,' yet I have not yet fathomed its subtlety. Guishan said, "I also have this here, but it is rare to meet someone capable of receiving it.
The Master [Dongshan] said, "I beg the Master for instruction. Guishan said, "The mouth born of one's parents will never..."
The Master said to his disciple, "Is there anyone else who, at the same time as you, has sought the Way? Guishan replied, "Not far from here, in Shou County of Lingling, there is a stone chamber;
connected to it is the Way-man Yunyan. If you can part the weeds and catch a glimpse of his wind, he will surely be one whom you hold in high esteem.
Once the Master arrived at Yunyan’s place, he asked him about "the insentient preaching the Dharma."
"Who is it that hears? Guishan said, "The insentient hear. The Master asked, "Does the Master hear?
He replied, "If I were to hear, you would not hear me preaching the Dharma. The Master asked, "Why do I not hear?
Guishan held up his whisk and said, "Do you hear it now? The Master said, "I do not hear. Guishan said, "I am preaching the Dharma."
"You have not even heard [the sound], let alone the insentient preaching the Dharma. The Master asked, "In which scriptures does the insentient preaching the Dharma appear?
He replied, "Have you not seen it said in the *Amitābha Sūtra*: 'The waterfowl and the forest trees all recite the Buddha's name and the Dharma'?
At this, the Master attained realization and composed a verse, saying: "How truly marvelous! How truly marvelous! The insentient..."
The teaching of the Dharma is inconceivable; if one attempts to hear it with the ears, it will ultimately be difficult to comprehend.

Only when hearing occurs through the faculty of the eye does one truly know it. The Verse says: This is manifest—sentient and insentient alike. This is most intimate; there is nowhere it is not true. Striking it once, one does not hit it.
Sunk in oblivion for ten thousand kalpas, a single penetration remains unbroken; it is like a donkey pulling an iron millstone.

Once one penetrates thoroughly, using the wedge to extract the wedge, the nose is placed upon the face, and the tongue is within the mouth. Neither borrowed nor unborrowed, speaking east and west as one pleases—when one wishes to rest, one simply rests.
When it is time to rest, one simply rests. Insentient things preach the Dharma, and sentient beings listen; sentient beings preach the Dharma, and insentient things discern it.
This is not a matter of making idle interpretations. The great earth, mountains, and rivers are far too talkative;
every person possesses this "non-correspondence," which the pillar and the lantern are proclaiming to you. (Daguang Zhi)
Excellent! The myriad phenomena and the entire cosmos are all treasures; in every instance and every object, the family’s precious jewels are manifest.
To those who do not recognize them, they are but wild weeds. (Nantang Xing)
Nanyang’s master had fine bone and flesh; Dongshan Jia was difficult to fathom. Old Master Shishuang and Old Man Yunyan re-commented until the drum was broken and overturned.
Clearly traveling the official road, one does not realize they have entered the wild weeds.
Because of this entanglement, it has reached the present day; when will this vast expanse of karmic consciousness ever end? (Yuedang Chang).

Dongshan addressed the assembly, saying, "At the end of summer and the beginning of autumn, brothers, if you go east or west, you must go to a place ten thousand miles away where there is not a single blade of grass before you will succeed.
He further said, "But as for that place ten thousand miles away where there is not a single blade of grass—how do you go there?
Later, a monk went to Liuyang and related this to Shishuang. Shishuang...

The Master said, "Stepping out the door, it is all weeds. The monk returned and reported this to the Master. The Master said, "How many people could there be in the land of the Great Tang? The verse says: Stepping out the door, it is all weeds; In the land of the Great Tang, how many can truly see? If you wish to know the meaning of this, Look at the man on the street.
Stepping out the gate, there is only great bustle; ten thousand miles away, nothing has yet been perfected.
If you wish to know the path from the gate back to your home mountain, the evening mist lightly locks it in a vast expanse of green. (Fohuiquan)
The weeds stretch far and wide. Look for yourself, inside the gate and outside the gate. It is easy to set foot within a thicket of brambles;
it is difficult to turn one's body beyond the curtain of night-brightness. Look, look—how many varieties there are! For now, follow the old trees in their shared cold and emaciation;
soon, you shall follow the spring breeze into the scars of the scorched earth. (Tiantong Jue)
Stepping out the gate, it is all but weeds. The old man of Longmen is left in idleness. To the north he goes to pay homage to Mañjuśrī; to the south he comes to climb Mount Wulao.
His hair and beard are already white and gray; he regrets that his return was not sooner. Standing alone before the autumn wind, he ponders and gazes toward the rivers and islands.
It is perfectly so; there is no need for further seeking (Lóngmén Yuǎn).
Ten thousand miles, not a blade of grass. Simply proceed in this manner: as soon as you step out the door, it is all grass. Each person possesses their own warrant.

Having official credentials, what need for restraint? Under the clear breeze and the moon, the man who waits by the stump; the cool rabbit grows distant as the spring grass turns green. (Jingshan Gaofeng)
One does not emerge from the vast, winding path of weeds; even upon leaving the gate, one is still separated by the ends of the earth.
When the turning faculty is engaged and one treads the road that reaches through the night, where among the green mountains is there not one's home? (Shushan Ru).
[Continued Collection] Before the courtyard, yellow leaves fall in profusion; on the steps below, patches of moss resemble brocade patterns. Let the wild grasses outside grow green as they will;
the stone man has trodden through the clouds of the sea mountains. (Jingyin Cheng)
Ten thousand *li* without a blade of grass; as soon as one steps out the door, one is tripped up. How could it compare to not stirring up a speck of dust? The four mountains shine ever more brightly.
Standing like a sheer cliff ten thousand fathoms high, there is no way to take it upon oneself. There is nowhere to seek it. Nowhere to seek it.
Suddenly, it emerges from the tip of the staff, and one strides straight toward the Jewel Mountain to personally seize the treasure. (Yuánwù Qín)

The road to Xinfeng is level and vast; how could it merely be a matter of the square, the round, the straight, or the biased? For ten thousand miles there is not an inch of grass—what person can venture forward?

If the mechanism does not turn, one falls into the dust of worldly conditions; if one penetrates through, one transcends the winds and mists. Liuyang has truly shattered the boundaries of center and periphery;
once you step out the door, the weeds are already thick and lush. If you can seize the opportunity and understand the underlying pulse, both banks are profound and the One is incomplete.

(Fuji Jianqin): In the vast and profound path of birds, not a speck of dust remains; the jade palace stands empty, its lattices covered in green moss. The shuttle hangs on the wall as autumn sheds its bones;

Cold and heat are clearly explained to you; there is no room for deliberation or discrimination between the distant and the near.
The eaves are abruptly broken, both ends are cast off; one looks up at the vast sky and laughs anew. (Songyuan Yue)

The Master said, "A single stalk of thatch after the fire. The Verse says:
When wild fires burn, it becomes ever more new; To this day, its smoke and flames cannot be drenched by rain. A red lotus on dry land obscures the sun.

Skillfully responding to the current, the wondrous mind is profound; A bright, clear single arrow strikes the red heart.
This is not the eye of Byuki facing the front; Before one’s face, the iron mountain rises ten thousand fathoms high. (Fozhi Yu)

After a long silence, the monk asked, "What is it like when the four mountains press in from all sides?
The Master said, "I, this old monk, have also passed beneath the eaves of people's houses. The monk asked, "Do you yield or not yield? The Master said, "I do not yield.
The monk asked, "Where then will you have me go? The Master said, "Go into the parched fields of millet. The monk let out a sigh and said, "Adieu! The Master said, "Adieu."
[The Master] was heavy with illness and then sat down and passed away. The Master struck his head three times with his staff and said, "He only knows how to go like this;
he does not know how to come back like this. The verse says: [Verse omitted as per instructions]
One only understands going thus: "Sandbirds nest at night in the trees of the azure isles. One does not understand coming thus:
"A stone sprout pierces through the moss on the ancient path. Do not say that the *kūṇapa* and *jīva* have no wings; today I have personally returned by the path of birds. (Tiantong Jue)
When the measure of the sage and the sentiments of the commoner are both utterly exhausted, there is no path for turning back; the matter returns to its non-existence.
Passing beneath the eaves of the house, amidst the millet fields, one follows the same way back through the belly of a horse or the womb of a donkey. (Sok-si Moon)

[Added for Collection] Once, Longya asked Dongshan, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said, "Wait until the waters of the Dong River flow backward, and then I will tell you.
The Verse says: The waters of the Dong River flow eastward; How could they ever turn back? If you wish to know the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming, Wait for the time when the river flows upstream.
Cavernous waters have no cause to flow against the current; it is only because of seeing the suffering of others that they respond. The ancestral intent from the West is truly without intention;
when deluded thoughts and the frantic mind cease, there is simply rest. (Hengchuan Gong)

[Added from the Supplementary Collection] A monk asked Dongshan, "What is one's own self prior to the empty kalpa? The Master said, "A white bird enters the reeds. The Verse says: A white bird enters the reeds; The vast expanse of the empty sky.
If you can see this clearly, You will know the state before the kalpa.
Strike the yellow orioles! Do not let them sing upon the branches. They have startled my dreams so many times that they could not reach Liao-xi.
(From "Discriminating the Hall")
[Added for inclusion] At Dongshan, during a winter night while eating fruit, you asked Head Seat Tai:
"There is a thing that reaches up to heaven and down to earth, black as lacquer, ever present within activity, yet cannot be contained within activity.
Tell me, where does its fault lie? The Seat said, "The fault lies within activity. The Master said, "Attendant, remove [the table]."
Retreating the Fruit Tray. The verse says:
Who does not have a share of Dongshan’s fruit? To withdraw the tray is a wondrous turning of the pivot.
Tonight I shall lightly break it open for you: A sleeping cat beneath a peony flower. (Mingji Zu)

Dongshan brings disgrace to his family tradition; the Head Seat buries his own self. Together they embroider out a pair of mandarin ducks, yet for a thousand ages it remains propped up and cannot be raised. (Yuan’an Yan)
Supporting heaven and supporting earth, black as lacquer; day and night cannot be distinguished—what thing is this?
Picked up and cast into a pit of excrement, the fragrance of lotuses wafts from within the fire. (Xutang Yu)
[Added for inclusion: During a night *zana* (formal assembly), Dongshan did not light the lamps. A monk came forward to pose a question;
after the monk withdrew, the Master ordered his attendant to light the lamp. He then called out to the monk who had just asked the question.
When the monk stepped forward, the Master said, "Bring me two or three ounces of flour and give it to this venerable elder. The monk shook his sleeves and withdrew. From that time on...
He then completely gave away his robes and possessions to provide a vegetarian feast. Three years later, he took his leave of the Master.
The Master said, "The time is right. While standing in attendance, Xuefeng asked, "As for this monk who has now departed, when will he return?"
The Master said, "He only knows how to go once; he does not understand how to return. When the monk returned to the hall, he sat beneath his robes and bowl and passed away.

Fǎngshàng reported this to the Master, who said, "Even so, he still falls short of me by three lifetimes. Verse: He only knows how to go once, And cannot understand the return. Though it be so, He still lags behind this old monk by three lifetimes.
At noon in the cave, three watches are struck; travelers immediately vie for the path.
Were it not for Master Chen of Mount Hua, who among them would not travel burdened by right and wrong? (Cishou Shen)
[Added from the Supplementary Collection] Once Dongshan was visiting a sick monk. The monk asked, "What is it like when fire and wind disperse?
The Master said, "When coming, there was not a single thing; when going, let it be as it may. The monk asked, "What about being emaciated and ill?
The Master said, "You must know that there is one who does not fall ill. The monk asked, "Who is this one who does not fall ill? The Master said, "Upon awakening, there is none."
A mere fraction [of realization] leaves one separated from the mountain slope by a vast distance. A monk asked, "Is it still permissible to speculate about what lies ahead?
The Master said, "Though it is as black as lacquer, its establishment is found in the present moment. The Verse says:
After fire and wind have dispersed and scattered, one thing remains eternally numinous: the golden land of the Buddha-realm and the white jade courtyard of heaven.
Do not speculate on your future; wherever you go, you must remain alert. When the single thought-moment is pure, even in the human world there is only peace.
(Nantang Xing). [Added by Zeng] Dongshan was unwell.
A monk asked, "Master, regarding this illness, is there anyone who does not fall ill? The Master said, "There is."

The monk asked, "Does one who is not ill still look upon the Master? The Master said, "The old monk has the means to look upon him. The monk asked, "How is it when the Master looks upon him? The Master said, "When the old monk looks upon him, he does not see any illness.

A verse says: The old man’s eyes are bright and clear; He sees through the clouds and mists. When the moon is full, the water is deep; When the wind rises, the waves subside. If you wish to know the Buddha-nature, Look directly at the person before you. If you can see this way, Then you will understand the meaning of the verse.
Cast off this stinking skin-bag; seize and turn this ball of red flesh. When the nostrils at the head are straight, the skull beneath is instantly dried.
The old physician no longer sees the chronic ailment from of old; meeting the young child, the difficulty is found nearby. When the wild waters grow thin, the autumn floods have receded;
where the white clouds break, the old mountains are cold. You must eradicate it completely—do not be negligent or superficial. When all is turned over and there is no more effort, you will find it.
Position: Standing alone and lofty, you do not share a single plate with others. (Tiantong Jue) [Added by Zeng].
Once, a monk asked Dongshan, "The Master teaches students to practice the 'Bird Path. I do not know how one practices the Bird Path. The Master said, "One does not encounter a single person.
The monk asked, "How then does one practice it? The Master said, "You must simply look beneath your own feet."
The Phrase on Selflessness: [A monk] asked, "If one practices the Way of Birds, is that not precisely one's original face?
The Master said, "Why do you, Reverend, speak so perversely? The monk asked, "In what way am I perverse? The Master said:
If one is not inverted, for what reason does one instead mistake the servant for the master? [A monk] asked, "What is the original face?
The Master said, "Do not walk the path of birds. The verse says:
The ancient path stretches serenely through the vast void; yet even traveling the profound mystery remains a journey over precipices.
Though not ascending the Bird Path may seem wondrous, upon closer inspection, one has already encountered the Way. (Danxia Chun)
[Added from another source] Dongshan asked a monk, "What is the most painful thing in the world? The monk replied, "Hell is the most painful. The Master said, "Not so.
To be here beneath this thread of robes and not clarify the Great Matter—this is called the most painful. The Verse says: [Verse omitted]
The greatest suffering in human life is not knowing when to rest; chasing the waves and following the currents is truly cause for concern.
If one can transcend Buddhas and patriarchs with a single phrase, what more could one seek even while wearing a tattered robe with the head shrouded? (Kumuk Cheng)
How many varieties of boiling cauldrons and glowing coals are there? The three paths of the hells are not yet so bitter and sour.
One must believe the intimate words of Xinfeng: beneath the *kāṣāya*, do not be negligent. (Danxia Chun)
[Added for Collection] Dongshan said: "The entire Tripitaka is merely this single character 'zhi' (之).
Verse: The strokes and dots are distinct, yet there is no principle; How many times did the Old Barbarian fail to lift it up?
It would be better to entrust it to Wang Xizhi; Boundless elegance returns to his hands. (Baiyun Yuan)

[Added from the Supplement] Dongshan went to visit Xingping and immediately prostrated himself. Xingping said, "Do not prostrate before an old man. The Master said, "I am prostrating before that which is not old. Xingping said, "He does not accept prostrations. The Master said, "He has never prostrated. The Verse says: Dongshan’s prostration was truly wondrous; Xingping’s words were like a thunderclap. When the old man asked, "Who is he? The Master replied, "He is not a person. Though the verse praises the ancient worthies, It is difficult to find anyone who can match them. If you wish to see the true source, Look at the two masters’ mutual exchange. If you can understand this, You will know that the Way is not far off. If you do not understand, You will be lost in the weeds of confusion. If you can discern it clearly, Then you have attained the ultimate. If you cannot discern it, You remain stuck in the dark. This is the meaning of the ancient sages; How could it be something created by men? If you can penetrate this, You will see the ancient path. If you cannot penetrate this, You will wander in delusion. This is the teaching of the Buddhas and Patriarchs; How could it be something devised by others? If you can realize it, You will attain the fruit of liberation. If you cannot realize it, You will remain bound by suffering. This is the essential point of the transmission; How could it be something grasped by the intellect? If you can let go of it, You will enter the realm of the sages. If you cannot let go, You will be trapped in the net of views. This is the heart of the ancestral school; How could it be something fabricated by the mind? If you can transcend it, You will ride upon the wind and clouds. If you cannot transcend it, You will be submerged in the sea of birth and death. This is the final word of the patriarchs; How could it be something explained by words? If you can hear it, You will awaken to the great matter. If you cannot hear it, You will remain in the dark of ignorance. This is the legacy of the ancient masters; How could it be something transmitted by the hand? If you can receive it, You will inherit the Dharma-eye. If you cannot receive it, You will be deprived of the life-lineage. This is the secret of the Buddhas and Patriarchs; How could it be something known by the senses? If you can perceive it, You will see the moon in the water. If you cannot perceive it, You will be blinded by the mist. This is the realization of the ancient worthies; How could it be something produced by effort? If you can relax, You will rest in the natural state. If you cannot relax, You will be exhausted by striving. This is the truth of the Way; How could it be something sought through seeking? If you can stop seeking, You will find the treasure within. If you cannot stop seeking, You will wander in the wilderness. He is not an aged man who declines to receive offerings; before the world of Vīraśabda and behind the crown of Vairocana, he holds fast within the jar where the day is long, and upon being touched, the green serpent roars within the casket.
A skilled physician warns his patient: taking medicine is not as good as abstaining from certain foods. (Tiantong Jue)
"Senior Elder, do not bow to this old decayed thing. It is not easy to broadcast one's family’s disgrace even in times of peace.
The noble and honored have never gone out the door; how could they exist after the time of Vipaśyin? (Zidehui).

[Added from the Supplementary Collection] A monk asked Dongshan, "What is the aperture of the patch-robed monk? The Master said, "An eighteen-year-old daughter does not tie her skirt. The Verse says: An eighteen-year-old daughter does not tie her skirt; The whole world is her single eye.
If you wish to see her face, Look at the moon on the thirtieth day.
Few know the apertures of the patch-robed monk; he has already been recognized by the Master for his capacity.
Before the eighteen-year-old daughter has even tied her skirt, she is first taught by her mother to paint her brows. (Haixin Xin)
[Added for collection] A monk once asked Dongsan, "Regarding the saying, 'Constantly sweep and wipe it clean; do not let dust and grime settle,' why is it that one does not obtain his robe and bowl?
The Master said, "Even if one were to say, 'Originally there is not a single thing,' one still would not be worthy of obtaining his robe and bowl.
Now tell me, who is it that is truly worthy? The monk offered ninety-six different responses.
None of them were in accord. At the end, he said, "Even if you bring it here, I will not accept it. The Master deeply approved of this. The verse says:
"The Patriarch’s robe and bowl are but a farce; He did not accept them because his eyes were not yet open. Who would believe that the *Putong* era was so remote?"
How could this matter have been transmitted from the Pamir Mountains? (Benjue 1).
[Added by Zeng] When Dongshan was unwell, he had a novice monk deliver a message to Yunyan, instructing him:
"If he asks whether the Master is at ease, simply say: 'The path to Yunyan is about to be cut off. You must speak these words."
[The Master] stood back, saying, "I fear he will strike you. The śrāmaṇera took his instructions and went to deliver the message;
before the words had even faded, Yunyan struck him with a staff. The śrāmaṇera was left speechless. The verse says:
Dongshan has a path that leads through Yunyan; where the way is severed, it is difficult for one to reach through.
When the living road is opened at the tip of the staff, only then will you know there is not even a hair’s breadth of separation. (From *Juexiangjian*)
Old in years and solitary at heart is Dongshan; he leads others on a path where all climbing and grasping are severed.
If this monk understands the shift of the occasion, once gone to Yunyan he will never return again. (Zhuwu Jian)
[Added from another source] When Chan Master Shengshan Sengmi (who succeeded Yunyan) was walking with Dongshan, they suddenly saw a white rabbit run past.
The Master said, "How spirited! Dongshan asked, "What do you mean? The Master said, "It is very much like a commoner being invested as a high minister.
Dongshan said, "Even at your advanced age, you speak such words. The Master said, "What about you?"
"How is it? Dong said, "For generations a member of the gentry, for a moment fallen into ruin.
The Verse says: A nobleman of this day, a poor man from an old family; Brothers succeeding one another, high and low are interchanged.

At evening on the road, eyes do not open; Beyond the bright-night curtain, the mechanism turns. Riding an ox while wearing a hat, he comes from amidst the strange; True gold after a hundred refinements.
His golden hue remains unchanging. (Tiantong Jue, 2).

He withstands frost and snow while treading levelly through the clouds and mists. Like Yan Hui when dismissed from office, or Liang Qiuju crossing the bridge; like Xiao He and Cao Shen, whose strategies could establish the Han dynasty;
like Yaoxiao and Zhongshe, whose hearts and bodies sought to evade even Yao. Though honor and disgrace may cause alarm, he possesses deep self-confidence; his true feelings participate [in the Way].
His traces mingle with fishermen and woodcutters;

when a commoner in white robes is appointed as a high minister, such joy is hard to surpass. For a time he wandered and fell into obscurity at the ends of the earth; shifting his station and changing his pace, he was difficult for others to perceive.
Last night, he returned to lodge in the house of the Five Marquises. (Fóxìng Tàiyī)
Returning home in brocade robes, all people see him; who can know his long-lasting wealth and honor?
The silent youth laughs aloud, returning with his face filled with radiant splendor. (Iam Kwon)
[Added from the *Zuochan Sanmei Chanyi*] While Shenshan was threading a needle, Dongshan asked him, "What are you doing?
The Master said, "Threading a needle. Dongshan asked, "How is it to thread a needle? The Master said, "Every stitch is the same.
Dongshan said, "Having practiced together for twenty years, how could you speak such words? Is there really no such skill? The Master asked, "And what about you, Elder?"
It is said: "The principle is like the earth bursting into flames. The verse says:
"When the great earth bursts into flames, there is not even time for a hair to enter; in the Kunlun Mountains of the South Sea, it is so cold one wears no socks.
From patriarch to patriarch, it has been passed down as a single head-bowl. (Tiantong Jue)
Releasing in opposition and gathering in accordance, one leads a few to oppose the many. Manifestation and concealment share the same path; gain and loss are used together.

Stitch by stitch they are identical, not coming from without. When walking the same way, speech must be distinguished. Since the great earth burst into flames, the incense burner in the ancient temple has known no ash. (Chang of Yuet-tang)
[Added for inclusion] Shenshan and Dongshan were crossing a single-plank bridge. Dongshan crossed first; picking up the bridge, he called out, "Come over!

The Master called, "Jia Dali! Thereupon, Dongshan set the bridge down. The Verse says: The bridge was picked up and then set down; One side was already crossed. If you wish to know the meaning of this, Look at the two masters standing there.
On level ground, one digs a pit without cause; a wooden bridge is lifted up for people to walk upon. How can one cross the deep, cold waters?
Under the moonlit night, the golden rooster announces the fifth watch. (Danxia Chun)
[Added to the Collection] Chan Master Qingzhu of Mount Shishuang in Tanzhou (a successor of Daowu). When he arrived at Mt. Mui, he served as the rice steward.
One day, while he was sifting rice, Mui said, "Do not scatter the property of the donors. The Master replied, "I am not scattering it.
Mui picked up a single grain from the ground and asked, "You say you are not scattering it; what is this?"

Ma. The Master had no reply. Guishan said, "Do not underestimate this single grain. Hundreds of thousands of grains all arise from this one grain. The Master said, "Hundreds of thousands of grains arise from this one grain; I wonder from where this one grain arises? Guishan laughed heartily and returned to his quarters. The Verse says: The Master’s answer was silent; Guishan’s laughter was loud. The hundred thousand grains are born from one; One grain, from where does it come? He returned to the abbot’s room— A great, joyful laugh. The old man’s meaning is clear; Who can fathom its depths? If you wish to understand the source, Look at the verse below. Ten thousand granaries and a thousand storehouses of permanent assets: the origins and provenance of these must be clearly understood.
If one does not know from where a single grain was obtained, the clear, refreshing air of the western mountains after the rain will remain but a mere mirror for withered meditation. (Kuchan Jing)
Shishuang was in his quarters. A monk asked from outside the window, "Why is it that within the span of a few feet, I do not behold the Master’s countenance?
The Master said, "The entire world has never been hidden. The monk went to Xuefeng and asked, "What is the meaning of 'the entire world has never been hidden'?
Xuefeng said, "Where is it not Shishuang? When the Master heard this, he remarked, "He has understood."

With a thousand doubts and ten thousand anxieties, one knocks at the gate of Chan. Pervading the entire realm, it is not hidden; how could it be described by petty words? Even Xianggu and Xuansha were still subject to movement and stillness;
they misled other wanderers, causing them to lose the source of their return. Noble sages need not follow after sounds and forms;
for as long as earth and heaven endure, they face the gate themselves. (Fenyang Shao)
The rocks and frost have grown old and weary; beneath the moon we meet and sing our mutual verses in response. How can this compare to the guest by the Luo River who fishes?
With a single blast of his fisherman’s flute, he passes beyond the azure isles. (Fohuiquan)
My two eyes have been afflicted by congenital blindness since childhood; my two ears have always heard only sounds.
Though pointed out in myriad ways, I see nothing at all—how can I distinguish clearly with a snap of the fingers? (Baoning Yong)
Within a mere span of a few feet, one does not behold the Master’s countenance. Fortunately, it is revealed alone; who could possibly obstruct it?
Old Shishuang once pointed to the moon; the old fellow Xuefeng merely added more idle chatter. On the fishing boat is the Third Lord Xie;
behind the Diamond King’s head, raw iron has been added. (Nanhua Bing)
[Continued Collection] Within a mere span, one asks Shishuang. The Master said: "The entire realm has never been hidden. When closing a deal in a bustling marketplace, one must keep one's eyes open;
the oxen and horses of the north, the barbarians of the south seas. (Dongshan Cong)

Pervading the entire realm, it has never been hidden; though it has a thousand eyes, it is difficult to see. Although it lies within the span of a few inches, one seeks it in vain for there is no front or back.
Xianggu struggled to provoke its response, yet even therein he failed to discern it. Xuansha acted as the trigger, shooting the man with a fine arrow.

(Touzi Shu). Once, a monk asked Shishuang, "What is the Master’s deepest place? The Master said, "A hairless lock with both ends swinging. The verse says: A hairless lock with both ends swinging— Who can grasp its meaning? If you try to grasp it, you lose your life; If you do not grasp it, you are already dead. In the midst of the three realms, There is no place to hide.
If you wish to see the Buddha, Look at the face of the man on the street.
The moon sets at the third watch, and the two mountains shine bright. On the ancient road, the journey is long and moss grows thick. When the golden lock shakes, there is no hand that can violate it;
within the heart of the blue waves, the hare of the moon constantly moves. (Touzi Qing)
A hairless chain-lock is difficult to open; do not rashly conjecture within the hall of withered wood.
For a thousand ages, both ends have remained unshaken—wait for the arrival of a rhinoceros-horned monk. (Baoning Yong)
[Added for inclusion] Shishuang addressed the assembly, saying: "How does one advance further from the top of a hundred-foot pole? The verse says:
One who sits atop a hundred-foot pole, Though having gained entry, has not yet reached the truth. From the top of a hundred-foot pole, one must advance;
Throughout the worlds of the ten directions, the whole body manifests. (Changsha Cen)
Blinding the eye at the crown of the head; mistaking the markings on the scale for certainty. Willing to sacrifice body and life, one blind man leads a multitude of blind men.
(No Gate Opens). [Added from the Supplementary Collection.
Once, when Minister Pei came to visit Shishuang, the Master snatched the ceremonial tablet from the official’s hand and said, “In the hands of the Son of Heaven it is called a *gui*;
in the hands of an official it is called a *hu*. In the hands of this mountain monk, what do you call it?”
"Mo. The Master had no reply, so [Baizhang] left his ceremonial tablet behind.
The Verse says: It is not a jade scepter, nor is it a ceremonial tablet; Turning back, he enters straight into the Azure Dragon’s lair.
Having seized the pearl that illuminates the sea from the black dragon, I know your great hand has finally brought it forth. (Xuedou Xian)
It is not a *gui* (jade tablet), nor is it a *hu* (ceremonial tablet). Transmitted from patriarch to patriarch, it is no external object. Cast your gaze directly into a flash of lightning;
to accept it immediately is already to bury it. When meeting a master, you must bring it forth; those of middling or inferior capacity will be dazed upon hearing it.
Even with such abundance in this era of Great Peace, one has ultimately not left the nest. How much more so before those with clear eyes—this is specifically [for them].

He also did not speak. The Master asked, "Why do you not speak? I replied, "I am not speaking; I am not speaking.
On the way back, the Master said, "Master, you must speak for me today. If you do not speak, I shall strike you.
I said, "Strike as you please, but I will not speak. The Master then struck him, and I returned.
The abbot said, "You should leave this place; I fear that if the administrators find out, it will be inconvenient for you.
The Master then paid his respects and took his leave, retiring to a village temple. Three years later, he suddenly heard a child reciting the Avalokiteśvara Sūtra:
"To those who should be saved by the body of a bhikṣu, he immediately manifests in the body of a bhikṣu. At these words, he experienced a sudden and great awakening. He then burned incense.
He prostrated from afar and said, "I now know with certainty that the late master’s final words were not spoken in vain.
It was only because I lacked understanding that I harbored resentment toward him. Now that the master has passed away, Shishuang alone is the true successor. He then set out for Shishuang.
When Shishuang saw him, he asked, "Have you yet realized the karmic conditions regarding your previous beating of the former master?
The Master stepped forward and said, "I request the Venerable One to speak a turning word for me. Shishuang said, "Have you not heard it said: 'I will not speak of life, nor will I speak of death'?
The Master then prostrated himself. Later, when Shishuang was performing a vegetarian feast and repentance ceremony, the Master returned one day carrying a spade.
Shishuang was walking from east to west and from west to east upon the Dharma Hall platform.
The Master said, "What is this? Shishuang said, "I am seeking the sacred relics of the former master. The Master said, "The vast waves are surging and the white billows reach the heavens;
what 'sacred relics of the former master' can you seek here? Shishuang said, "This is precisely where one must exert effort. The Master said, "In this place, even a needle cannot pierce it."
[The monk] entered. "What power do you have? The Master took up his spade, placed it on his shoulder, and went out.
The verse says: Rabbits and horses have horns; oxen and sheep have none. Beyond a hair’s breadth, beyond a speck of dust—like mountains, like peaks.
The golden, numinous bones remain even now; When white waves surge to the heavens, where can they be placed? Nowhere to place them. The single sandal returned to the West, yet was once lost.
(Xuedou Xian): All day long he leans against the door and rests upon the tower; several times he has gazed into the bright mirror to comb his hair.
Since he took up the profession of a man after Pan Lang, he too knows how not to feel shame before others. (Baoning Yong).
Daowu understands speech yet has no tongue; Jianyuan has no hands yet performs boxing. Only when one’s soul is extinguished and spirit shattered can this Way be transmitted.
Shishuang acts as a son to avenge his father’s disgrace; words of bitter grievance are difficult to express.

A spade is brought forth, and looking out in all directions, there is only boundless white waves surging to the heavens. Where now are the golden sacred bones? They remain to pacify the Jambudvīpa for a thousand years.
Ten thousand years. (Miaozhanhui).
A wooden man holding a board sings amidst the clouds; a stone woman wearing boots walks upon the water. Cease further questioning of birth and death;
from of old, at noon they strike the third watch. (Changlingzhuo).
In life, the whole mechanism is manifest; in death, the whole mechanism is manifest. Not saying more, not saying more—within this there is no front or back.
Accept it directly, without a single thread of separation. It fills the vast void; the sincere heart is ever in pieces.
(Yuanwu Qin): "The hairless lock rattles at both ends; the flawless jade璧 is presented three times.
Yet he suffers the unjust amputation of his feet—how unexpected that the direct words turn out to be like an inversion. (Foxing Tai).
At that time, though he spoke with bitter earnestness, he said nothing; only upon awakening did his spiritual bones begin to be sought. Over the Lian River, the cold moon is desolate on both banks;
the floating clouds have dispersed, and the sky is as clear as if swept clean. (Meng’an Xin)
Alive, he does not speak of the Way; dead, he does not speak of the Way. A single breeze of pure wind sweeps on and on.
At once he leaked out Dao-wu’s pivot. He put on his formal robe backward and turned his cap upside down. (Chu’an Fang).
[Continued Collection] The local spirit is luminous and without a single thing; how many can recognize the golden bones?
When one walks with the spade resting upon the shoulder, great eloquence has always been as if mute. (Danxia Chun)
In life, one never encountered a true friend; after death, there is only the search for the sacred remains.
It is right here before one’s eyes—where could one look for it? Let the golden chain float or sink as it may. (Benjue 1)
The head falls off in broad daylight, yet he is caught in the dark. A deadly hand scratches him where it itches.
A heron flies through the snow and cannot be seen; a single silver pitcher hangs from the tip of a tree branch. (Xuedou Zong)
The Song of Non-Arising: A Chan guest beyond the mundane world. The singer can sing, the player can play; song and rhythm follow one another as the autumn sky brightens with the white moon.
The great Peng bird spreads its wings—the vast ocean seems narrow. A sweeping, pure wind arises from its feathers.
(By Nantang Xing)
When casting the hook at the head of a rapid torrent, the scarlet-tailed, glistening scales still hesitate.
Suddenly leaping forth from within the vast waves, they seize the mist and grasp the clouds, making the universe seem low. (Ying’an Hua)
[Supplement] Chan Master Shanhui of Jia Shan in Li Province (a successor of Chuanzi). When he first resided at Jingkou Temple, a monk asked him, "What is the Dharma-body?
The Master said, "The Dharma-body is formless. The monk asked again, "What is the Dharma-eye?
The Master said, "The Dharma-eye is flawless. At that time, Daowu let out a laugh. The Master then requested further instruction, after which [Daowu] dispersed [the assembly].
He joined the assembly of Chuanshi. After his realization, he returned to gather disciples. Daowu sent a monk to ask him, "What is the Dharma-body?
The Master replied, "The Dharma-body is formless. The monk asked again, "What is the Dharma-eye? The Master replied:
"The Dharma-eye is without flaw. When Senghui brought this up to me, I said, "This fellow has only now attained thorough penetration.
I then offered this verse: The Dharma-body is formless; The Dharma-eye is without flaw. Blowing fire with the wind; Borrowing water to offer flowers. Not a hair’s breadth is established.
Ten thousand distinctions and a thousand differences—just look at the second or third month of the coming year, when the mud-bringing swallows enter people’s homes (Cishou Shen).
Once this foul mouth opens, ten thousand kalpas pass; the slightest movement brings the iron wheel in pursuit. Clouds gather and disperse, the rain falls and clears, and the moon shines bright.
At night, who would you speak to as the river waves surge back? (Muan Yong).
Once, when a monk asked Jia Shan, "What is it like when one brushes away the dust and sees the Buddha? the Master said, "You must brandish the sword."
"If one does not brandish the sword, the fisherman will nest in the trees. Later, a monk asked Shishuang, "What is it like when one brushes away the dust and sees the Buddha?

Shishuang said, "He has no land; where would you meet him? When the monk returned and related this to the Master (Linji), the Master said, "The old monk is not without his own methods for establishing the gate.
However, as for a profound discourse on the ultimate principle, he is still a hundredfold inferior to Shishuang."
Pacing. The verse says:
A single phrase for the occasion, jade-like and jingling; inside and out, it is so clear and bright that a chill overflows the eyes. One has never dwelt within the realm of the non-outflow;
it will be difficult to perceive it within the shadows of the moon’s radiance. (Danxia Chun)
Not establishing even a hair’s breadth is already dust; how much more so to run about asking others? Brandishing the precious sword high, there is no trace;
within the moon, the Lady of the Moon reveals half her body. (The withered tree becomes.)
The sword’s spirit brushes the oxen; the army’s majesty washes away. Who else is it that brings merit by pacifying chaos?
Once the dust and mists are cleared from the four seas, the Emperor’s transformation hangs from his sleeve, spontaneously non-active. (Tiantong Jue)
The Great A Sword is in my hand; who dares meet its edge? Ten thousand peaks of green mountains, layered upon layer of white clouds.
(Jingzhao Tianning Lian) [Collected later] Every person who studies the Buddha is deceived by the heat of delusion. How many ways can one see through by brushing away the dust?
When the wild wind sweeps the ground and the clouds are blown away, one stands alone at the railing, and the universe is vast. (Biefeng Yin)
Hidden and manifest, all-encompassing, the face is never revealed. White clouds wind around the old home mountain;
at midnight, the stone man knocks on the golden lock; at dawn, the mud ox passes through the jade pass. (Rendiao Ren)

A monk asked Jiashan, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "In this state, there is neither guest nor host. The monk asked, "With whom do you converse in your daily life? The Master said, "Mañjuśrī has already gone to fetch water; Samantabhadra has not yet returned with the flowers. The verse says: In this state, there is neither guest nor host; Mañjuśrī has already gone to fetch water; Samantabhadra has not yet returned with the flowers. How could the myriad forms ever be grasped? The ten directions are all empty space. The moon shines upon the clear waves; The wind blows through the vast sky. The old master’s words are like a dragon’s roar; His response is like a tiger’s leap. If you wish to understand the meaning, Look at the clouds and the moon. The clouds and the moon are both bright; The wind and the waves are both clear. If you can see it thus, Then you will know the source of the Buddhas and Patriarchs. How many people know the place where the Master’s words are spoken? From ancient times to the present, there has been no peer with whom they can be compared. A jade horse gallops through the snow, returning at midnight;
a lang-tang antelope hangs its horns as the sun sinks in the west. (Touzi Qing)
When facing the head-on, one does not dare to open their mouth; borrowing from the side, they fall two or three steps short.
Standing out yet perfectly integrated, there is no front or back—the Buddha of the Western Heaven is the Old Gautama. (The withered tree has become [a tree]).
The Great Dharma stands alone, towering and majestic; its eight facets are translucent, surrounded by the myriad phenomena. Sitting upright facing the window, there is no fixed position;
perfectly penetrating and unimpeded, it responds to all capacities. (Sushan Ru).

A monk once asked Jia Shan, "What is the realm of Jia Shan? The Master said, "The monkey carries its young back behind the green peaks; the bird holds its flower in its beak before the azure cliffs. Later, Fayan remarked, "For twenty years, I understood this only as a discourse on the realm.

Verse: The monkey cradles its child behind the emerald crags; The bird carries its blossom before the azure rocks. For twenty years, I mistook this for a mere description of the landscape. How many have failed to see the true meaning? It is not that there is no such thing as a realm;
It is simply that one cannot grasp it with the mind. If you can see it right here, You will know the source of the ancient sages.
The moon is bright, the pines are green, and the crane’s dream is long. In the azure void, the vermilion cassia hangs like a wild sheep.
High cliffs and towering walls, a thousand peaks of snow; stone sprouts grow branches amidst the midnight frost. (Touzi Qing)
The clam holds the bright moon; the pearl is born within its belly. The dragon embraces the deep clouds; rain falls upon the void.
Do not stir up great waves across the level fields; you must simply let every drop flow toward the east. (Danxia Chun)
An ancient mirror, polished again, is as new as ever; each time it leaves its case, it startles the world.
Beneath the city of Shitou, wind and thunder roar; an aged Zen elder holds the vital ford. (Baofeng Xiang)
Twenty years ago I roamed this place; the magnolia blossomed as the monastery was newly built.
Now, returning once more to this ground of practice, the trees are old and flowerless, and the monks have white hair. (Gushan Gui)
To understand through the discourse on objects is still not it. But ask instead: how is it now?
Qīngliáng was straight from the tip of his nose; Jiāshān remains with his two eyebrows arched. (Jìngshān Gǎo)
[Continued Collection] The ancient path is buried deep in snow; fine mountains are further shrouded by clouds. The cry of wild geese is urgent beyond the heavens;
the traveler returns home at night. (Mān-ān Shù).
The moon hangs over the cold pines as the green cliffs deepen; the stone man has not yet understood the snow-song.
From of old, few have been知音 (true connoisseurs) of this melody; the crane calls out across the blue heavens from Fenglin. (Kumu Cheng)
By the mountains and by the waters, waiting for the moon to brighten; Borrowing a path through the human world for a brief while.
Now I return once more to the mountainside; There is only the lake water, no path to tread. (Tianmu Li)
[Added for inclusion] Jia Shan addressed the assembly, saying: "There is no dharma before one's eyes; the intent lies right before one's eyes.
It is not a dharma of the present moment, nor is it something reached by the ears or eyes. The verse says:
The nine-transformed elixir is difficult to reject yet easy to obtain; with a single blow, it is easy, yet returning to it is difficult.
Having met, we exhaustively discuss the matters within the alchemical cauldron, once again examining the immortal scriptures in detail. (Changling Zhuo)
In years past, all things have become demons; growing old, idly adding more white hairs. When the Way is prosperous, the Emperor’s edicts need not be proclaimed;
when times are clear, there is no need to sing songs of Great Peace. (Gushan Gui)
Do not speak of dreams before a fool; there must be seams upon a ball of raw iron. Though you speak clearly, he feigns deafness;
he merely engages in idle chatter on the outside. (Jingshan Gao)
Gripped, it cannot be made into a ball; struck, it cannot be opened. Several times De-yun descended from the steep heights.
Sometimes he traveled to the southern shore of the sea, yet secretly returned by the old path. (Zuian Yin)
[Added from another source] Once, while Jia Shan was engaged in communal labor, the Rector (Vina) ordered Furi to deliver tea. Furi said, "I have come solely for the sake of the Buddha-dharma;

I have not come to deliver tea. The Rector said, "The Abbot has commanded me to invite you, Senior. Furi replied: *Note: This passage is a classic encounter dialogue (wenda) used to illustrate the non-dual nature of reality and the transcendence of conventional concerns in Zen practice.*
The Master said, “I have already received it. Jianzhi took some tea to the place where they were working and saw the Master.
He then shook the teacup to make a sound, but the Master paid him no heed. Jianzhi said, “Three or five bowls of strong tea; my intent lies by the hoe.
The Master said, “The pitcher has the potential to pour the tea; how many bowls are there in the basket? Jianzhi said, “The pitcher has the potential to pour the tea.”
Within the blue basket there was not a single bowl; he then poured out the tea. The assembly all gazed at him with their eyes.
Xuedou said, "The assembly looks up with crane-like anticipation; we beg the Master for a word. The Master said, "When meeting a dead snake on the road, do not strike it;
carry it home in a bottomless basket. Xuedou said, "Holding the Night-Bright Talisman in one's hand, how many know the break of dawn? The Master—
He summoned the assembly. When someone had already left, he said, "Go back! and then halted the communal labor (*fǔqǐng*). The verse says:
When you encounter a dead snake on the road, do not strike it; You must cast down the bottomless basket.
Often matters arise from idle talk; Do not treat idle talk as if it were merely idle talk. (By Pogu Xian)
A fellow carrying a wooden board has no constraints; he would rather starve to death on Mount Shouyang than swear not to eat the millet of Zhou.
(Xutang Yu) When Jia Shan was serving as the head cook at Weishan, Weishan asked, "What vegetables are we eating today?
The Master replied, "Two years, the same spring. Weishan said, "Attend well to your duties. The Master replied, "The dragon dwells in the phoenix’s nest."
The Verse says:
Meeting and inquiring after the assembly of monks, do not compare it to the offering of fragrant rice from a hermitage garden. Purple qi follows the vermilion phoenix through the night;
A golden dragon entwines the branch of the moon at dawn. (Touzi Qing)

Transforming the raw into the ripe, ever renewed with the passing seasons; how wonderful that two years share the same spring. The dragon rests in its lair and the phoenix dwells in its nest, yet they stir their spirits lightly;
harmonizing flavors that fill the mouth, a delight for many. (By Zhengjue Yi)
After the rain, the moss on the Dragon Court is moist; at the end of night, the golden halls glow with the first light of red candles. Palace ladies play refined melodies of peace and prosperity;
beyond the forbidden gates, one’s keen hearing and sight are but a vain labor. (Da-hong Yu)
[Continued Collection] Within the Dragon’s Lodging and Phoenix’s Nest, two years pass as one spring. The fragrance of osmanthus flowers fills the air;
upon level ground lies the blue cloud. (Da Hongen)
[Added from another collection] Once, Jia Shan sent a junior monk to travel extensively among various Chan monasteries, yet the monk found nothing of particular interest.
Upon hearing that the Master’s reputation for the Way had spread far and wide, he returned to visit him and said, "Master, you possess such extraordinary and marvelous qualities;
why did you not tell me of them sooner? The Master replied, "When you were steaming rice, I was lighting the fire for you. When you were walking..."
"When you were serving the rice, I was spreading out my bowl. Wherein did I fail you? Because of this, the junior monk attained awakening.
The verse says: "When you steamed the rice, I applied the fire; when you served the rice, I spread out my bowl. Always acting thus, I am but an old woman."
Mind! It is simply that your own mechanism has not been activated. If the mechanism were activated, there would have been nothing extraordinary about Jia Shan;
the hundred rivers would flow backward with a clamorous din. (Chijue Chong)

[Added from the Supplementary Collection] A monk asked Jia Shan, "I do not ask about the place where one has attained realization; I request a word from the Master regarding the place where one has not yet realized.

The Master said, "The door hangs in the withered forest; discern it within the shadows. Verse: The door hangs in the withered forest; Discern it within the shadows. If you can see it here, Then you have truly met Jia Shan.
Beyond the limit of majestic sound, one cannot travel; casting off the hand, one returns home, too weary to ask the way. The sleeping palace is empty and silent;
there is no one, and only the moon fills the window with its vacant brilliance. (Danxia Chun)

The Master said, "A well-rope. The monk asked, "What is the Hīnayāna? The Master said, "A money-rope. He asked again.

The Master said, "Hand them over to the steward. The Verse says: A bamboo sieve and a wooden ladle— How many people can understand this? With a tainted bamboo sieve and an untainted wooden ladle, the brilliant Chan practitioners give rise to vain conjecture;
where can the clever masters search for them? Jin Ya knows how to wield the divine spear; Li Guang’s arrows pierced two vultures. (Jiashan Shanhui)
Mahāyāna and Hīnayāna, well-ropes and money-ropes, outflows and no-outflows, colanders and wooden ladles—when one directly accepts them as such, the nostrils are lost. (Fayun Xiu)
A bamboo sieve and a wooden ladle; a string of cash and a well-rope—these are the family traditions he has inherited, his way of life vast and open.
Let your livelihood be surrendered to the conditions as they arise; where else could the Buddha-dharma be applied? Without contrivance, simply follow along;
naturally, the mind-ground is ever peaceful and joyful. (Tiantong Jue)
The various outflows (*āsrava*) of the Two Vehicles strike against the King of Emptiness; after the snow has fallen, how can one endure the midnight frost?
(Zhang Wujin) The banners of Qin and Han crossed the desert sands; the embroidered robes of Tang and Yu presided over the palace halls. (Zhang Wujin)
A bamboo sieve and a wooden ladle; strings of cash and a well-rope. Striking tiles and drilling tortoises—this is merely exhausting one's divinations.
Cease your divinations! A qilin has but a single horn. (Nanhua Bing)
[Continued Collection]: A leaky bamboo sieve; a stainless wooden ladle. Those who study the words of Chan merely exhaust themselves in vain conjecture.
By the river stands a fisherman; casting his hook, he startles the crane from the heights of the heavens. (By Bailu Xian).
The wooden ladle and the basket, the string of cash and the rope for the bucket—speaking of the wondrous and discussing the profound are all errors.
In this state of pure peace, the nostrils block heaven and earth; there is nowhere for the monks of the world to search. When clarity comes, one grasps soil and it becomes gold;
when awakening occurs, the hundred grasses are all medicine. Breaking off the finger-joints of Jueci, he trampled through Zhaozhou’s bridge. This single phrase of ordinary life is used inexhaustibly.
Limited knowledge and views are merely matters of conjecture (Xuedou Zong).
A twelve-foot steel nail, an eight-foot iron stake—planted right in the eye, yet one still does not perceive it (Zhong’an Kong).
[Added for inclusion] When Qingping first visited Cuiwei, he asked, "What is the very meaning of the West?
Cuiwei said, "Wait until there is no one here, and I will tell you. After a long silence, the Master said, "There is no one; please, Reverend, speak."
Fawei stepped down from his meditation seat and led the Master into the bamboo grove. The Master said again, "There is no one here; I request the Master to speak.
Fawei pointed to the bamboo and said, "This stalk is so long; that stalk is so short. Although the Master understood the subtle words, he had not yet attained full penetration.
Later, when he went to reside at Dàtōng, he ascended the hall for a discourse and cited his first meeting with Cuiyan.
A subtle karmic connection. He said to the assembly, "The former master entered the mud and the water for my sake;
since then, I have not known good from evil. The verse says:
Father and son meet, their intent already manifest; why need rank and status distinguish between warmth and cold? With earnest instruction, he points out the home garden.
Matters: Having traversed the desolate wilds, one speaks of long and short.
(Dahong Su) Iron rhombuses are buried everywhere; passing through them at midnight, one does not yet realize the difficulty. At dawn, one falls wounded at the foot of the ridge;
only then does one know one has passed the Iron Gate Barrier. (Xuetang Xing)
Chan Master Datong of Mount Touzi in Shu Prefecture (a successor of Cuibei). Zhaozhou asked, "What is it like when one who has died the Great Death returns to life?
The Master said, "Night travel is not permitted; you must reach your destination by daybreak. Zhaozhou said:
I am as white as a monkey; he is even blacker than a monkey. The Verse says:
To have eyes while alive is no different from being dead; why need one examine the master regarding medicinal taboos?
Even the Ancient Buddhas said they had never been there; who knows who can scatter the dust and sand? (Xuedou Xian)
One who has undergone the great death is the same as one who lives. Three thousand chivalrous heroes follow the dust once more.
Li Ling was originally a general who captured the barbarians, yet he became a high-ranking general who surrendered to the barbarians. (Foyin Yuan)
From the dead he returns to life, his teeth bared; at the break of dawn, one must go first oneself.
In the pond of some noble villa, a pair of mandarin ducks cannot be captured in a painting. (Baiyun Yuan).
From the void is born an iron ox; its horns and head are clearly defined—how truly marvelous! It tramples the moon deep within the clear pool;
at the end of night, it is led back through the snow. (Changling Zhuo)
Zhaozhou understands how to spin without thread; Touzi is able to pierce with a needle that has no eye.
A master displays his mastery within the hands of a master; within a red heart lies a red heart. (Fujian Yongqin)
One who has undergone the great death returns to life; not permitted to travel by night, one arrives at dawn. A man from Chenzhou goes out through the gate of Xuzhou;
the eighty-year-old grandfather acts like a youth again. (Gushan Gui)

The grain does not flourish in the sun’s warmth; instead, peach and plum trees are planted in competition during spring. This turns those who once labored in the fields into, for the most part, sellers of flowers. (Jingshan Gaofeng)

Before the stage, at midnight, they manipulate puppets; their movements and dignified bearing are complete in every gesture.
Yet, if one reflects carefully, there is no principle behind it; ultimately, someone inside is pulling the strings. (Xue’an Jin)

Water flows from Kunlun, its waves rolling on; heaven is high and distant, the peaks and forests exquisite. As the meditation seat slightly descends, clouds and mountains part;
sages and ordinary beings leave no trace, as seas and mountains grow cold. (Touzi Qing)
The old woman bows low to serve her parents-in-law; rising, she struggles to avoid a face smeared with grime.
She forces her cloud-like hair into a high, tight bun—can it even hide her from the eyes of passersby? (Baizhang Yuanwen).
Touzi descends from his meditation seat; lightning flashes amidst the clouds. The barbarian monk returns to the land of Han;
heavy frost falls in the sixth month. (Fohuiquan)
Touzi reveals his total capacity: a clear breeze stirs the emerald peaks. Where, then, are the ten bodies? He has won eyes like eyebrows.
(Cai’s "Buddha-mind")
With love, he wades toward the riverbank to dangle his fishing line. Deep within the azure pool dwells a fine fish.
It is not that there is no fragrant bait on the hook; how is it that this one cannot catch him? (Changling Zhuo)
When a thief is caught, the evidence must be clearly seen. The Tamer of the Ten Bodies descended from his rope-couch.
Having once endured the nights when the monkeys wailed at the Baxia Gorge, even an iron heart and liver would break with grief. (Fujian Yongqin)
Touzi descended from his meditation seat. Who can discern it throughout their entire being? To hesitate is to create a thousand divergences;
to face it directly, it is difficult to recognize. (Jingzhao Tianning Lian)

Touzi descended from his meditation seat: "This morning I shall raise it up for you. As for those who follow like a donkey or a horse, they must by all means avoid taking it on in a confused manner. (Jingshan Gaofeng)
[Continued Collection] The Jade Unicorn, with its horns, leaves the azure heavens; the Golden Phoenix, clutching flowers, descends from the painted pavilion.
The rustic old man does not disdain the young lord’s intoxication; together they take hands and stroll through the Imperial Street. (Shui’an 1)
Touzi descended from his meditation seat: "In the end, he was no Meng Bawang. Without stirring his three-inch tongue, he could not avoid letting the ghosts divide the spoils.
Desiring to keep things straight before one's eyes, one scrambles for the contents of the bag at the critical moment. Tearing asunder the past and present, there is no face left;
wherever one moves freely, where is there any barrier? (Huigan’s version).
Touzi was asked by a monk, "What is it like when the moon is not yet full? The Master said, "He swallows three or four. [The monk] asked, "What is it like after it is full?

The Master said, "He spits out seven or eight. The Verse says: The moon is not yet full—swallowing three or four; Once it is full—spitting out seven or eight. In the midst of the bright and dark, he is free from both; The Great Way is vast and wide—where can one find its trace?
Seventh and eighth are indeed fit for contemplation; how could fourth and third be merely superficial? The numinous light shines upon heaven and earth for all eternity;
whether hidden or manifest, it is ordinary and requires no grasping. (Dongshan Cong)
Full and deficient, he once extended his inquiry to the old man; a stone tortoise holding its offspring draws forth the clear wind.
Yesterday morning a wooden horse passed through the pool; it trampled out the golden crow, crimson at midnight. (Touzi Qing)
The agent is known before and after the completion; through four, three, seven, and eight, the understanding manifests according to capacity.
This causes people to laugh long and well at the skillful swallowing and spitting out [of words], leaving it for the monastic community to create right and wrong. (Zhengjue Yi)
He swallowed three or four, yet spat out seven or eight; though they were all completely intact through his swallowing and spitting, one did not know what they were. (Baoning Yong)

[Continued Collection] Swallowed it was easy, but spitting it back out is difficult. At the summit of Mount Sumeru, the celestial winds are cold. Last night at the third watch, it was as bright as day;
I know not who shared the railing with me to gaze upon the view. (Fóxìng Tái)
Touzi, Touzi! The wheel of his spiritual mechanism is unimpeded. When he wishes to swallow, he swallows; when he wishes to spit out, he spits out.
If you still linger on the teeth and stick to the gums, how can you hope to transcend the present and surpass the ancients? (Shigan Xi)

A monk asked Touzi, "Master, while you reside on this mountain, what kind of realm do you have? The Master said, "A girl with bifurcated horns has white hair. The verse says: A girl with bifurcated horns has white hair; The mountain peaks are steep and the path is long. If you wish to know the Master's realm, Look at the moon reflected in the water.
The world of the Mountain School is distinct; it is rarely heard of in the secular realm. It can only bring delight to oneself; it is not fit to be presented to you.
Yet, to present it to you would still be extraordinary: a girl with twin-tufted hair now has white strands in her locks. (Zhengjue Yi)
A young maiden with white hair; flakes of snow fly amidst a mass of fierce flames. Among those who dwell in the mountains, who can be compared to her?
Idle clouds and flowing waters do not share the same destination. (Baizhang Yuan).
[Continued Collection] Before the Flower-Calyx Pavilion, spring is at its peak. Hazy willow catkins dance in the clear sky.
Having finished tossing the gold coins, she is too weary with grace; she leans smilingly against the winding balustrade. (Lan’an Shu)
Inquiring about the realm of dwelling in the mountains: the girl with her twin braids has already grown white. Meeting face-to-face, there is no encounter—cease further seeking.
White clouds fly over the old mountains and rivers. (Tianmu Li)
[Added for inclusion] A monk asked Touzi, "The spring rain falls incessantly; why do the hundred grasses not sprout? The Master said, "The banana tree simply grows.
A monk asked, "What is the mystery within the mystery? The Master said, "Last year it was the Dragon Boat Festival;
this year it is likewise. The monk asked, "Ultimately, how is it? The Master said, "It is neither the same nor different. Who—"

He spoke of the sequence of before and after. A monk asked, "What is the second moon? The Master said, "In the middle spring, it gradually grows warm. The monk asked, "What is the first moon? The Master said, "In the early spring, it is still cold.
The Verse says: In the middle spring, it gradually grows warm; In the early spring, it is still cold. If you wish to know the two moons, Look at the sky and the earth.
Touzi, Touzi! Surpassing the present and excelling the past, he meets people and recognizes people; his head is covered in ash and his face in dust.
For a month or two, he speaks and speaks of the cold and the warmth. Dwelling on a high peak, he beholds the misty green slopes; upon his red-lotus tongue there is no horizontal bone. (Longmen Yuan)
Early spring is still cold—the first month; mid-spring gradually warms—the second month.
If there were no worldly affairs hanging upon one’s mind, it would truly be a fine season for the human world. In Jiangnan and the two circuits of Zhejiang, the spring is cold and the autumn is hot.
(By Meng’an Yue)

Sudden and gradual, partial and complete; provisional and real, empty and existent. With a beak like a nail and a tongue of iron, eyes like the Yellow River and a mouth like the sea—this single path of pure emptiness stretches through past and present: an octagonal millstone rolls in the void. (Wenyu Qín)
He performs the Great Treasury of the Teachings; his words are upright and his speech is likewise upright. Both ends are completely severed;
a single sword leans against the cold heavens. (Yafu Creek).
One breath out, one breath in; half-closed, half-open. A feeble crane perches upon a withered tree; a mad monkey howls atop an ancient terrace.
If you wish to know this extraordinary matter, you must thoroughly tear apart your straw sandals. (Muan Yong)
[Added from the Supplementary Collection] A monk asked Touzi, "Caoxi is like pointing at the moon; Ling Shan is like painting the moon. What is the true moon?

The Master said, "Last night at the third watch, it turned toward the west. The Verse says: Caoxi is like pointing at the moon; Ling Shan is like painting the moon. If you ask what the true moon is, Last night at the third watch, it turned toward the west.
Last night at the third watch, it turned toward the west; At dawn, it fell naturally into the stream before me.
Lifting my head, I failed to recognize that perfect fullness— To whom shall these boundless pure breezes be entrusted? (Cishou Shen)
Last night at the third watch, the moon turned westward; in this dimming universe, how many are lost? The reflection turns in the clear pool as the wind first subsides;
from beyond the ridges, the faint cries of monkeys and gibbons are heard. (Lan’an Xu)
Last night at the third watch, he turned toward the west; the enlightened master points out the way for those lost.
If you seek the essential meaning within these words, you will inevitably wash mud with more mud. (Yi’an Shen)

A jade-horned ox with frost-white hair stands revealed in the open field; its traces are manifest throughout the human realm and the heavens.

[Added for inclusion] Touzi asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "I have come from the East and West Mountains to pay homage to the Patriarchs. The Master said, "The Patriarchs are not on the East and West Mountains.

The monk was speechless. The verse says: The Patriarchs are not on the East and West Mountains; If you seek them there, you will never find them. If you wish to see their true form, Look at the mountain peaks before you.
The azure dragon, trailing rain, leaves its deep cave; The colorful phoenix, clutching flowers, enters the Imperial Pass. A single phrase, throughout ancient and modern times, is without leakage;
The Patriarch is not found on the mountains of the east or west. (Xuedang Xing)

Explanation and prose dialogue: Buried in dust and mired in filth, transformation has its causes; once exposed, there is no escape.
Who knows that within the shadows, the bones are being pulled out? This requires a hand capable of the thunderous crash of a lightning bolt. (Yuedang Chang)
There was a guest fishing for giant turtles, wandering aimlessly across the Five Lakes; he did not know that within the clams in the mud, their bellies were full of black pearls. (Fujian Qín)

The verse says: The kalpa-fire blazes forth; The world is utterly consumed. Yet within this vast expanse, There is not a single thing that can be grasped. When the great earth is leveled, The ten directions are all empty. In the midst of this void, A single hair is revealed. If you can see this, Then you have attained the Way. If you cannot see it, You will surely fall into the pit. The ancient Buddhas and patriarchs, All entered through this gate. If you wish to understand, Look at the man on the mountain peak. Heaven and earth serve as the furnace, and all things are scorched. A stone man rides the waves across the clouds and mists. Wind arises at midnight with the brilliance of frost and stars;
the moon sets in icy cold that forces the hair at the temples to wither. (Touzi Qing)
[Added from the Supplementary Collection] A monk asked Touzi, “What is the person of original nature? The Master said, “Sitting together, we do not know each other.
The monk said, “If that is so, I shall go and pay my respects. The Master said, “In the dark, one writes upon a sorrowful heart; to whom can it be sent?”
The verse says:
Sitting together and traveling side by side, the world knows nothing of it; how many people encounter him face-to-face?
Even among those who carry on the family lineage, half are but poor children raised by begging. (Baoning Yong)
[Added for inclusion: Once, a monk asked Touzi, "Is it true that all sounds are the voice of the Buddha? The Master said, "Yes.
The monk said, "Master, do not let the sound of the boiling pot disturb the bowl. The Master then struck him. The monk asked again, "Whether coarse words or subtle speech..."
"All return to the primary meaning. "Is that so? The Master said, "Yes. [The monk] asked, "May I call you, Master, a donkey? The Master then struck him. The verse says:
All return to the primary meaning; Is it so? The Master says, "Yes. "May I call you, Master, a donkey? He then struck him.
Touzi, Touzi! The wheel of his spiritual mechanism turns without obstruction. Letting go of one, he gains two; here and there are the same.
How pitiable are the countless people who play with the tide—ultimately they fall back into the waves and die. Suddenly they are alive: the hundred rivers flow backward in a tumultuous roar.
(Xuedou Xian): High mountains may be climbed; the great ocean may be crossed. Touzi, Touzi—everywhere he folds and unfolds.
All sounds are the Buddha’s voice; let him recognize my bowl clanging. Coarse words return to the primary meaning; one must personally witness his [cauldron] boiling over.
Called a donkey; truly making it shine with brilliance. Struck with a swift hand until there is no way to run.
Where can that "giggling" tongue return? (Yuet Tang Chang)
A single staff is used by two houses; going and coming, there is neither self nor other.
If this monk had attained the pivot of Touzi’s teaching, he would have taken it up with his hand right then and there to strike Touzi. (Yuanwu Keqin)

[Added for inclusion] Touzi was walking with a monk through the mountains. Seeing a cicada shell, the monk asked, "The shell is right here; where has the cicada gone? The Master picked up the cicada shell and, by the monk's ear, made the sound of a cicada.

The monk attained realization. The verse says: The cicada has flown away; The empty shell remains. If you wish to hear its song, Listen closely at your own ear. The sound is clear and distinct; How could it be hidden? If you can understand this, You will know the place where the cicada went.
Light and thin as a cicada’s shell, withered and decayed like a fallen leaf; Picked up and brought close to the ear, it chirps two or three times in succession. (Nantang Xing)
