Travelers on the road vie with one another to gather the fragrant blossoms; they do not realize that springtime is passing before their very eyes.
Last night, a sudden rain shower of falling flowers left the waters of over a hundred cities fragrant. (Juexiangjian)
The partridge cries amidst the fragrance of a hundred flowers; the fair-faced young man is drunk as mud.
With eyes opened in the blazing sunlight, the grass grows lush and green at the eastern edge of the City of Blessings. (By Zhuyu Jian)
[Added for inclusion] Because a monk asked Touzi, "Among the three bodies, which body preaches the Dharma? the Master snapped his fingers.
The Verse says:
Asking about the source of the Three Bodies preaching the Dharma, A light snap of the fingers gathers the seas and mountains; The golden lock tower opens and the crimson sun shines forth.
Late evening. Deep in the night, people laugh atop the green peaks. (Touzi Qing). [Added from another collection.
A monk asked Touzi, "Are *bodhi* and afflictions one or two? The Master said, "They are two. The monk then asked, "What is *bodhi*?
The Master said, "Sit and drink tea for now. [The monk] asked, "What are afflictions?"
[The monk] was vexed. The Master said, "This monk is a nuisance; get out! The Verse says:

Entering the grass to personally seek the man within the grass, Layer upon layer there is a path, level as in the palm of one's hand. Failing to meet the great merchant, he vainly pierces through the dawn;
Though the sun is high, he still hears the striking of the third watch. (Muan Yong)
The Seventh Patriarch of the Fifth Generation under the Sixth Patriarch (the First of the Fourth Generation after Nanyue) (Miaoyang):
Chan Master Huiji Tongzhi of Yangshan in Yuanzhou (Successor of Guishan). A foreign monk arrived from mid-air.
The Master asked, "Where have you recently departed from? He replied, "From India. The Master asked, "When did you leave there? He replied—
Early that morning, the Master said, "Why have you arrived so late? He replied, "I was wandering through the mountains and enjoying the waters.
The Master said, "It is not that you lack the ability to sport in supernatural powers, O Kalyāṇamitra, but the Buddha-Dharma must be returned to an old monk like me.

He replied, "I came specifically to this land of China to pay homage to Mañjuśrī, yet I have instead encountered a 'lesser Śākyamuni. Thereupon, he produced a Sanskrit manuscript on *bīja-patra* leaves and presented it to the Master.
Having paid his respects, he ascended into the air and departed. From this time on, he was known as Little Śākyamuni. A verse says:
"Far removed from the road to Western India, so long and vast, He personally went to China to play with the ocean tides.
If one wishes for a pure breeze to arise beyond the gates, Drag him back and give him four more strokes of the rattan cane. (Nanhua Heng)
Little Śākyamuni and Great Mañjuśrī—though their names may be invoked at will, the rattan staff remains in my grasp and cannot be used;
I have been deceived and smeared with falsehood by that blue-eyed one. (Shushan Ru)
[Continued Collection] A blink of an eye is the Western Heaven and this land; a raised eyebrow is this land and the Western Heaven. With the exhalation, a thousand layers and a hundred turns;
with the inhalation, a single thought for ten thousand years. Zen, Zen. The Jambū tree stands on the southern edge of the sea. (Nantang Xing).
An Arhat came to visit Master Yangshan; one must believe that even Śrāvakas have not yet exhausted emptiness. When questioned, he did not know the pivot of the mechanism;
it turns out he simply possessed supernatural powers. (Benjue I)
When Yangshan was residing at Dongping, Guishan sent him a letter along with a mirror.
Yangshan ascended the hall, held up the mirror, and showed it to the assembly, saying: "Tell me, is this Guishan’s mirror or Dongping’s mirror?
If you say it is Dongping’s mirror, yet it was sent by Guishan. If you say it is Guishan’s mirror, yet it is currently in Dongping’s hand."
[The Master] said, "If you can speak [the truth], keep it; if you cannot speak it, I shall smash it to pieces. The assembly remained silent.
The Master then smashed it. The Verse says:
Yangshan received the mirror from Guishan and, addressing the assembly, brought it forth to issue his true command. "Dull-witted Chan followers do not open their eyes;
Yangshan drove a nail straight through their heads. (Fenyang Shao)
Holding it up clearly, one discerns the right from the wrong; among all people, not a single one opens their lips. It is like selling goods with no one to buy them;
in the end, they must return to their original owner’s house. (Dongshan Ceng)
An ancient mirror sealed away, difficult for the discerning to distinguish; shown to disciples as a practice, let the assembly observe it.
If there be any *śrāmaṇera* guests within the assembly, may they remain until now to reflect upon their shadows in its cold clarity. (Haiyin Xin)
The Master held up a mirror and presented it to the assembly. "Fools often compete over beauty and ugliness. Had it been smashed then, it could not have been sought again;
thus they would have spared their descendants' hands from being ruined. (Baizhang Yuanwu).
Guishan’s Ancient Mirror was held up by Yangshan: "The sun rises in the east, the moon sets in the west;
falling down, one knows not who has picked it up; the autumn wind whistles, the grasses grow lush. (Baoning Yong)
The master and disciple illuminate and see one another; it is no light matter. When about to show this to the assembly of Chan practitioners, they are startled.
This mirror is distinct and cannot be divided; yet in the end, it is clearly divided into two. (Foguo Bai).
The meaning of total release and total inclusion is also excellent. When Guishan sent him to Yangshan’s peak, there was a single, lovely fragment like autumn water;
though he asked three times, no one came to shatter it—let it rest (Zhihai Qing).
Father and son transmit the mirror that cuts off the dust; one must know that the autumn evening is not the same as the [ordinary] wheel.
How pitiable are the countless who lose their heads, mistakenly taking the empty flowers for spring within the mirror. (Fuxincai)
[Continued Collection] An eighty-year-old matron learns to paint her brows; her elegant grace rivals that of her youth.
Had it not been for the clear mirror to distinguish beauty from ugliness, everyone would say there was no need to apply rouge and powder. (Wang Fangyi)

As the Master stood in attendance, a crow suddenly dropped a red persimmon before him. The Master picked up the fruit, wiped it clean, and presented it to Muzhou.
Muzhou asked, "Where did you get this? The Master replied, "This is what has been moved by the virtue of the Master. Muzhou said:
"You shall not be without your share. He then divided half [of the inheritance] and gave it to his teacher. Xuefeng said, "How great was Mount Miao!
Yet he was pinned down by Yangshan with a single sitting, so that to this day he cannot rise. The verse says:
A crow dropped a persimmon before the Master; he asked, "What brings you here?"—the matter was perfectly clear. Each took half, as sweet as honey.
If you do not understand this now, what year will it be? (Fenyang Zhao).
The clarity of Muzhou and Nanquan spans from antiquity to the present. When father and son meet, their intent is profound. When the fruit ripens and its fragrance wafts, the crow carries it away;
pinching and pulling at each other, they seem to share a close bond. To understand the true point of these two men:
when the autumn moon sets, its reflection shines upon the heart of the pool. (Dongshan Cong)

"It is not that it is entirely identical, nor is it that it is entirely different. When the Great Function manifests, they take each other’s hands and return together;

The Master then took his place. A venerable one struck the gavel and said, "Now, the second seat shall preach the Dharma.
The Master rose and struck the gavel, saying, "The Mahāyāna Dharma transcends the four propositions and is beyond the hundred negations."

"Listen attentively, listen attentively. When the assembly had all dispersed, [Dongshan] woke up and related this to Guishan. Guishan said, "You have already entered the rank of the sages. The Master then prostrated. The verse says: Listen attentively, listen attentively; The assembly all scattered away.
Upon waking, he recounted it to Guishan; Guishan said, "You have already entered the rank of the sages. The Master then paid his respects. The verse says:

The oyster’s gut is split open to reveal the pearl; who would have known that my secret was leaked by this delirious speech? The long-bearded one must surely laugh at the Yang family’s disgrace.
Beyond the four propositions and transcending the hundred negations—the illness of Master Mazu and his son need no longer be treated. (Tiantong Jue)

At that time, he was able to wield the command of Magadha—why must one strike the sounding block within the hall? (Benjue I)
Under the bright sun and blue sky, he speaks a dream within a dream; what a fabrication, what a fabrication! He deceives the entire assembly. (No gate opens.

The Master held up his whisk. The Layman said, "Just so. The Master asked, "Is it upright or is it overturned?
The Layman then struck the pillar and said, "Though there is no one here, I must have the pillar bear witness. The Master threw down the whisk and said:
If you travel to various regions, feel free to present this to others.
The verse says: "Two eights make sixteen; Counting from the beginning, it is still not enough. Take them and scatter them wildly before the steps;
The ground is covered everywhere with round patches of green moss. (Baiyun Yuan)

[Added from the Supplementary Collection] Later, Yangshan went to visit Yantou. Yantou raised his whisk. The Master spread out his sitting cloth. Yantou took the whisk and placed it behind his back.

The Master draped the sitting cloth over his shoulder and departed. Yantou said, "I do not approve of your letting go; I only approve of your taking up. The Verse says: I do not approve of your letting go; I only approve of your taking up.
If you wish to know the ancient path, Look at the spring waters flowing eastward.
One erecting, one unfolding; one releasing, one withdrawing—Yangshan’s playing with danger exceeds even that of Yantou.
Fortunately, he turned the rudder and oars back with the wind; otherwise, he would have nearly overturned his fishing boat. (Duanqiao Lun)
[Added for collection] One day, Yangshan was seated in the Dharma Hall. Seeing a monk approach, the monk performed his greetings and stood with palms joined toward the east, looking at the Master.
The Master extended his left foot. The monk moved to the west and stood with palms joined;
the Master extended his right foot. The monk moved to the center and stood with palms joined; the Master withdrew both feet. The monk prostrated.
He prostrated. The Master said, "Since I have resided here, I have never struck a single person. He then took up his staff and struck him.
The monk soared into the air and departed. The verse says:
In this thatched hut, desolate, I dwell amidst the white clouds. An old friend has come from afar with sincere intent.
Once the formalities of greetings and courtesies have been concluded, it is difficult to avoid offering you a cup of tea. (By Nansou Lu).
[Added from another source] Yangshan was at Shiting in Hongzhou. After the morning gruel, while he was seated, a monk asked, "Does the Master recognize characters?
The Master replied, "I can manage a bit. The monk then circled to the right once and said, "What character is this?
The Master drew a cross on the ground. The monk then circled to the left once and said, "What character is this? The Master...

He changed the *śrīvatsa* (svastika) into a *svastika* (卍). The monk drew a circle and held his two hands up as if an asura were supporting the sun and moon, saying, "What character is this? The Master then drew a circle that enclosed the *svastika*.
The monk then made the gesture of Lohitya (Louti). The Master said, "So it is, so it is. This is what all Buddhas protect."
"Reflect: you are thus, and I am also thus. Guard and uphold this well. The monk prostrated and departed, soaring through the air. The verse says:

The emptiness surrounding the Way has not yet been filled; the hand that seals the void has not yet taken form. The subtle operation of the celestial wheel and the terrestrial axis is densely interwoven with martial warp and civil woof.
Releasing and gathering, opening and closing, it stands alone yet moves in tandem. When the mechanism is triggered at the dark pivot, the azure sky flashes like lightning;
when the eyes merge with the purple light, stars are seen in broad daylight. (Tiantong Jue)
[Added from another source: Once, the monk Siyi asked Yangshan, "Regarding the Zen school’s sudden enlightenment, what is the ultimate meaning of entering the gate?

The Master said, "This matter is extremely difficult. If one belongs to the lineage of our ancestors with superior faculties and wisdom, they will attain a thousand awakenings upon hearing it once and achieve the Great Total Retention (*dhāraṇī*).
However, those whose faculties are dull and whose wisdom is inferior must practice seated meditation and tranquility."
[The student] was at a loss. He said, "Aside from this one path, is there any other way of entry?
The Master said, "There is. [The student] asked, "How is that so? The Master said, "Where are you from? [The student] replied, "I am a man of Youzhou.
The Master said, "Do you ever think of that place? [The student] replied, "I constantly think of it. The Master said, "That which is able to think—"

Having attained this seat, you must further examine yourself; within the city of Nirvana, you are not yet at rest.
With fur and horns upon your head, we shall meet again, having exhausted every kind of hardship—how many varieties! (Da Hong En).
Without exterior yet all-encompassing; without obstruction yet profoundly empty. Gateways and walls rise tier upon tier; locks and bolts multiply layer after layer.
The wine is ever full, yet the guests lie prostrate; the meal is indeed ample, yet the farmers slumber on. Suddenly bursting forth from the void, the phoenix beats its wondrous wings;
trampling over the blue seas, the thunder ushers in the roaming dragon. (Tiantong Jue)
Inquiring after the origins of my hometown in Youzhou, the mountains and rivers appear vividly within my very lungs and liver.
When I try to find the root of my thoughts, I find nothing at all; I pull on my robe and must look back once more. (Benjue 1)
For both ordinary beings and sages, there is no divergent path. Reflecting back upon that which is being reflected upon, how few people truly know it?
The spring breeze does not reach the Peach Blossom Spring; yet leaves fall and flowers bloom according to their own time. (Cishou Shen)
[Added for collection] Yangshan asked a monk, "Where have you recently come from? The monk replied, "Mount Lu. The Master said, "Have you ever been to Wulao Peak?

The monk replied, "I have not. The Master said, "Then you, Dharma brother, have never traveled the mountains. Yunmen said, "These words were all spoken out of compassion; they are talk that descends into the weeds. The Verse says:
The old master’s words are like a hook, Casting it where the fish are hidden. If you do not know how to swallow it, You will surely be caught on the line.
Leaving the weeds, entering the weeds; following understanding to seek it out. Layer upon layer of white clouds; the red sun shines brightly. Looking left, there is no flaw;
looking right, one is already old. Do you not see how Hanshan left too early? Ten years passed before he could return, having forgotten the path by which he came. (Xuedou Xian)
How does emerging from the weeds compare to entering them? Entering the weeds with one's whole body is for the sake of compassion.
Yangshan extends his hand and follows him away; even until now, he remains at the crossroads (Benjue I).
If you wish to recognize the Five Elders’ Peak of Mount Lu, where in this midst would they not meet? A tongue without bone turns according to others;
an iron kettle for boiling tea is not the same as a small cauldron. (Cishou Shen)

[Added for inclusion] Yangshan asked Sansheng, "What is your name? Sansheng replied, "Huiji. The Master said, "Huiji is me. Sansheng said, "My name is Huiran. The Master laughed heartily. Both were free from the constraints of the mundane world; Who could fathom their profound intent? At the moment of releasing both and gathering both—ha ha! How many times does this great laughter ring out? (Benjue I)
Huiji said with firm resolve, "This is my name; fortunately I have met a Chan master who is even more generous than others.
If one compares a sharp blade to a gentleman, there is a great laugh of joy that fills the assembly with springtime. (Yuanwu Keqin)

[Added for inclusion] Once while Yangshan was warming himself by the fire, a monk came to visit him. The Master said, "A single word can exhaustively describe the mountains, rivers, and the great earth.

The monk asked, "What is this one word? The Master thrust a fire-tongs into the brazier and then moved it back to its original place. The verse says: A single word exhausts the mountains and rivers; He thrusts the tongs into the fire, Then moves them back to their former place. If you wish to understand the meaning, Look at the sparks flying from the hearth.
A single phrase brings forth the myriad phenomena; who would consent to close the heavy gates like Mahākāla? Amidst the shadows of the setting sun, the wind and waves surge violently;
unaware, the boat has drifted down to the darkening ferry.

One falls and one rises. The Lion of the Snowy Court was cautious in avoiding transgression yet harbored benevolence; he was courageous in action yet perceived righteousness.

When the clear light shines into the eyes, it seems as if one has lost their way home; when turning around with clarity, one still falls back into their original position. For the monk, there is ultimately nowhere to rest.
Dying together and living together—what "this" and what "that"? Warmth and faith break through the plum blossoms as spring arrives at the cold branches;
a cool breeze sheds the leaves as autumn clarifies the turbid waters. (Tiantong Jue)

Overthrowing and then upholding; face-to-face across a thousand miles. Only Śākyamuni, pointing his finger before the wind—even if the Sea-Seal (Sāgarāmudrā) were to emit its light, it would still be the bottom line of Xuefeng’s teaching. The entire world is Mañjuśrī; the entire world is Maitreya.
The gates of the pavilions stand open all day long; who recognizes the youth Sudhana? (Zuʼan Yin).

[Added for collection] Layman Lu once asked Yangshan, "How does one enter nirvana without severing the afflictions? The Master held up his whisk and said, "As for this very thing, how would you enter it?

The Layman replied, "Even the word 'enter' is not necessary. The Master said, "The word 'enter' was not meant for you, Layman. Verse: The whisk is raised; the question is posed. Without cutting through, one enters the realm of peace.
When the Layman says the word "enter" is unnecessary, The Master reveals that even this word was not for him.
Birth-and-death and nirvana are like turning one’s hand over or under; when the true eye is opened wide, neither exists.

Walking alone in the great space, every dust mote is a state of meditative absorption. Petal by petal, the plum blossoms on the crag drift in disarray; branch by branch, the willows by the stream dance freely. (Shimen Cong)
[Added from another source] One day Yangshan saw Xiangyan and asked, "Brother, what is your realization these days?
He replied, "According to my realization, there is not a single dharma that can be grasped by the mind. The Master said, "Your understanding still remains within the realm of objects."
Jia甲 said, "I am just like this. The Master asked, "And what about you, elder brother?
The Master said, "Do you have nothing by which you can know that there is not a single dharma that can be taken as an object of the mind?
When Guishan heard this being cited, he said, "In the future, Jizi will leave the whole world in a state of doubt. The Verse says:
Jizang’s *Xiangyan Lun* presents its own philosophical standpoint; it leaves those who hear it with ever-deepening doubt.
When meeting others, he was unwilling to speak even three words; how could he have cast away his whole heart? (Benjue I)
[Added for inclusion] While Yangshan was lying down, a monk asked, "Does the Dharma-body understand how to preach the Dharma?
The Master said, "I cannot preach it; there is another person who can. The monk asked, "Where is that person who can preach it?
The Master pushed out his pillow. When Guishan heard of this, he remarked, "Ji-zi (Yangshan) employs the affairs of the sword's edge. The verse says:

The Dharma-body preaches the Dharma; with the physical eye one perceives objects. Great wisdom appears as folly; great eloquence seems as stammering. Lifting up a winnowing fan, he threshes elsewhere;
pushing out a pillow, he reveals the sleeping bed. This is the work upon the edge of a sword—emitting a ray of light. (Yuedang Chang)
Tanaka thrusts in his spade; on the bed, he pushes the pillow. A thousand hands, a thousand eyes—how strange, how strange! (Longya spoke).
[Added by Zeng] Once, when a foreign monk came to visit Yangshan, the Master drew the shape of a half-moon on the ground.
The monk stepped forward, added a circle to it, and rubbed it away with his foot. The Master extended both hands; the monk shook out his sleeves and departed.
The Verse says:

[Added to the Collection] Chan Master Xiangyan Zhixian of Dengzhou (who succeeded Guishan). Following the passing of Baizhang, he went to study under Guishan.
Guishan asked him, "I have heard that while you were with Baizhang, when asked one thing you would answer with ten, and when asked ten things you would answer with a hundred.

"Before it has arisen, try to utter a single word of the Way! The Master returned to his quarters bewildered.
He searched through the texts he had studied over the years for a single phrase with which to respond, but in the end, he could find none. He sighed and said, "A painted cake cannot satisfy hunger.
He repeatedly requested that Baizhang explain it to him, to which Baizhang replied, "If I were to explain it to you, you would later curse me."

"I am going," he said. "What I have spoken shall ultimately concern nothing of your business. The Master then burned the texts he had studied throughout his life and declared, "In this life, I shall not study the Buddha-dharma.
I will instead become a long-wandering monk of rice and gruel, so as to spare my mind from its labors.

Leaving no trace anywhere, one’s deportment lies beyond sound and form. Those who have realized the Way in all quarters say this is the highest level of capacity.

This was composed by the mental faculty, the intellect, and consciousness; it awaits Huìjì’s personal examination of the Way.

When the staff was brought forth, his mind was immediately penetrated; tears flowed as he unconsciously fell into deep reflection. His springtime conduct and autumnal demeanor left people astonished;
transcending the past and illuminating the future, he stands peerless throughout all time. (Fenyang Zhao)

Having received the staff, he wept toward the blue heavens. He said nothing of severing what came after or illuminating what went before. Spring comes and autumn follows—how difficult for people to comprehend!
He has worn his straw sandals through until his feet are pierced. (Zhengjue Yi)
The Honored One entrusts his belongings and cries out to the azure heavens; the spring season is acting like winter—how perverse!
If there is a true patch-robed monk within this assembly, he should immediately overturn the meditation seat. (Benjue I)
The staff has been held by generations; it was entrusted by the Buddhas and Patriarchs. Huishan sent it forth, and Xiangyan broke into weeping.
Father and son met in resonance; it is a song of springtime snow. Were it not for a true知音 (one who knows the sound), its succession would be most difficult. (Shushan Ru).

Xiangyan addressed the assembly, saying: "If one discusses this matter, it is like a person climbing a tree, with a branch held in his mouth, his feet not treading on branches, and his hands not grasping branches.
Suddenly, someone below the tree asks, 'What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
If he does not answer, he violates the other's question; if he answers, he loses his life."
"Life! At such a time, how can one attain it? At that moment, the Venerable Houtou Zhao stepped forward from the assembly and said, "I do not ask about being on the tree;
please, Master, speak of the time before one has climbed the tree.
The Master then let out a great laugh. The verse says:
Xiangyan bit on a tree branch to demonstrate it to many; he sought only to lead his fellow practitioners to realize their original truth.
To hesitate is to grasp at words, resulting in the loss of body and life as numerous as dust motes. Fenyang opens the path for you through the lost way;
when clouds disperse across the vast sky, the sun and moon shine anew. (Fenyang Zhao)
Hehe! A great laugh that leaves no room for a needle or a cone. How is it when one has climbed the tree compared to when one has not yet climbed?
Even if Xiangyan possessed many clever skills, an onlooker could not help but knit his brows in dismay. (Fohuiquan)
Devising various expedients, that ancient adept was truly formidable; how could one endure branches sprouting upon branches? It is like a fine horse catching the shadow of a whip;
chasing clods of earth is not the way of a lion’s cub. (Baoning Yong)
The ancient sages, with hearts of compassion, benefited future generations; with a branch held in their mouths, they exposed their entire bodies.
Even if there were no news from the profound path, one could not avoid losing both parents at home. (Shimen Yi)
Xiangyan’s hanging words are truly worthy of appreciation: "Mouth clutching a tree branch, suspended from a tree.
At this moment, one does not inquire about the patriarchs' wits; tell me, what is that fellow's appearance like? (Dizang En).
It is difficult to turn back on a narrow path; east and west are entirely mountains. Where the traveler cannot reach, the falling flowers lie idle as the wind has stilled. (Shangfang Yi)
[Continued Collection] Standing atop the highest mountain peak, walking upon the deepest ocean floor. Newly planted pines follow the ridges; fragrant grasses grow around the pond.
Hands do not grasp the branches; feet do not tread upon the trees. Held firmly in the mouth, one misses the path right before one’s eyes.

[Added from the Supplementary Collection] Xiangyan was once asked by a monk, "What is the Way? The Master said, "A dragon’s cry within a withered tree.
The monk asked, "How about that? The Master said, "An eye within a skull. Later, he asked Shishuang, "What is the dragon’s cry within a withered tree?
Shishuang said, "It still carries a trace of joy. He asked again, "What is the eye within a skull? [Shishuang said, "It still carries a trace of fear."]
Qing said, "Frosty clouds still carry traces of consciousness. He spoke in verse:
"The dragon’s cry from a withered tree is truly the Way; The skull, devoid of consciousness, has its eyes first opened.
When consciousness is exhausted, all news is gone; How can one distinguish the clear within the turbid? (Cao Shan Ji)

[Added from the Supplementary Collection] Master Mi of Jingzhao Prefecture (also called Master Mi, or Mi Hu; successor to Guishan) asked a monk, "Where have you recently come from?"
The monk said, “Yaoshan. The Master asked, “How has Old Yaoshan been lately? He replied, “He is very much like a single slab of solid rock.
The Master said, “Is he so serious? He replied, “There is no place for you to lift him up.
The Master said, “It is not only Yaoshan; Mihu was also like this. The monk stepped forward, looked around, and stood there. The Master—
He said, "Look, look! Even a stubborn rock moves. The monk then went out. The verse says:
"What a fine piece of stubborn rock, Master Mihu! How many travelers fail to recognize it?
But when a patch-robed monk sees it, He cannot help but mistake south for north. (Daming Zhe)
[Added from another source] Mihu sent a monk to ask Yangshan, "In these times, is awakening still necessary? Yangshan said, "Awakening is not non-existent; however, it falls into the second place.

The Master deeply approved of this. The verse says: Awakening is not non-existent, yet it falls into the second place. The first head has long been lost; how can one find it again? If you wish to see the true person, look directly at the present moment. If you seek it elsewhere, you will wander for ten thousand miles.
I asked a person at the peak of the emerald crags; he pointed to the very end of the mountain, saying there was no place to settle.
Although this spares one from following further commands, how can it compare to the spiritual sprout that never violates the spring? (Touzi Qing)
At the edge of the second head, break through delusion to awaken. Swiftly cast aside the temple and abandon the trap. Even if perfected, it is not yet fully perfected;

like a redundant toe, it is difficult for the wise to discern its gnawing and chewing. The old hare weeps with autumn dew upon the ice-dish; the crow shivers as the evening wind blows chill through the jade tree.
When the time comes, Dayang will distinguish the true from the false; even with scars and blemishes, there is nothing more precious than a jade scepter. (Tiantong Jue)
A thousand awakened ones say there is no sorrow; who would dare believe they have encountered his second head? In the stillness after the Cold Food Festival, mountain flowers bloom;

The sword leaves its precious sheath because of injustice; the medicine emerges from the golden jar to save the sick.
Since time immemorial, the South has been as clear as a mirror; why must one needlessly employ armor and weapons? (Xueyan Qin)

When Xinghua was at the temporary palace in Weifeng on his return from Emperor Zhuangzong of the Later Tang’s visit to Hebei, the Emperor summoned the Master and asked, "I have obtained a treasure in the Central Plains, yet no one has ever offered a price for it. The Master said, "Please let Your Majesty show me this treasure.
The Emperor extended the two feet of his *baku-to* (head-wrap) with both hands. The Master said, "This is the treasure of the Sovereign."
"Who dares to offer a price? Xuanjue then questioned him, saying: "Tell me, did Xinghua approve of Zhuangzong or not?
If he approved of Zhuangzong, where was Xinghua’s eye? If he did not approve of Zhuangzong..."
"Where does the fault lie? The verse says:
The Emperor’s treasure is truly difficult to repay; Xinghua spoke these words as his single move. He spread out both hands, revealing the ends of his official cap;
The imperial edict hangs upon the Phoenix Pavilion. (Beita Zu)
The Prince of the Northern Barbarians draws his bow and shoots; The General of the Southern Kingdom looks up at him.
Upon the sand, nothing remains but a slanting shadow, Fluttering straight into the clouds above. (Baiyun Cuan)
The treasure of the sovereign king—Who can discern and seek it out? Not permitted to travel by night, one must arrive at dawn. That which Zhuangzong obtained was not the true thing;
only a refined connoisseur could recognize it as belonging to the old master Xinghua (Dizang’s kindness).
The King speaks of this matter to one who knows his heart. The whole world offers its sincere devotion with the loyalty of the sunflower.
He brings forth the priceless treasure of the Central Plains; it is not like the jade of Zhao or the gold of Yan. (Tiantong Jue, II)
The treasure of the Central Plains appears in Xinghua; this single segment of radiance is beyond appraisal. The imperial enterprise is worthy of being a teacher for ten thousand generations;
the Golden Wheel reigns majestically over the four quarters of the world.
The elderly bhikṣu extended his hands to present [the object] to the Honored One: "How could I dare offer a light price for Your Majesty’s precious treasure?
The atmosphere in the courtyard was harmonious and the Dragon-like countenance was pleased; yet, alas, the foreign monk smiled and nodded his head. (By Yì of Shàngfāng)
The supreme treasure has been recovered from the Central Plains; the entire nation cannot contain it. Once it has entered the hands of Xiangru, its glorious fame shall fill the Great Tang. (Fosincai)
【Continued Collection】The "One Treasure of the Central Plains" has its origins. It pressed the King until he drew his head-cloth over his face.
Reaching this point, if one lacks the ability to distinguish between the "blue and white eyes," who would dare to offer a light, superficial response when the opportunity arises? (Xiaoweng Kan).
The *fuhou* turban is raised high; the King’s treasure is revealed. The Minister of Works has seen it often, as has Old Xinghua.
At this moment of eternal union between sovereign and subject, fallen flowers fill the ground, yet no one sweeps them up. (Beihai Xin)
He has acquired the priceless treasure of the Central Plains; lifting up his head-wrap, his entire body is revealed.
It was laborious for him to have Xinghua pay a heavy price again—eight *liang* were originally but half a *jin*. (Nun Xianlin Ying).
The King’s Jewel is naturally beyond price; how could Xinghua ever dare to borrow it for a look?
Since Heaven and Earth have no partiality in their covering and supporting, they have remained until today to stabilize the Central Plains. (Xianji Yun)
Xinghua addressed the assembly, saying: "Today, there is no need for 'how' or 'what. I ask you simply to enter directly with a single blade, and Xinghua will provide you with verification.
At that time, Elder Minde came forward and prostrated; as he rose, he let out a shout.

The Master also shouted. Dede also shouted. The Master also shouted. Dede bowed. The Master said, "If it had been anyone else, thirty blows of the staff would not have been too much for them. Why? Because Minde understands how to use a shout as something other than a mere shout. He then descended from his seat. The verse says: A shout, a shout—how many are there? Each one is distinct and different.

When you strike the drum, the sound is clear; When you beat the gong, the resonance rings out. If you can distinguish them clearly, Then you will know the meaning of the ancient sages. If you cannot distinguish them clearly, You will be like a blind man groping in the dark. If you can see through them all at once, You will see the moon reflected in ten thousand rivers. If you can hear them all at once, You will hear the wind blowing through the ten directions. If you can see and hear them all at once, You will be a true person of the Way. If you cannot see or hear them all at once, You are merely a commoner of the world. Do not seek outside yourself; Seek within your own mind. If you can understand this, You will realize the truth of the Buddhas and patriarchs. If you cannot understand this, You will remain lost in delusion. Therefore, strive with all your might! Do not let this moment pass in vain!
When dragon and tiger intersect—this is that very moment. Before one can even deliberate, things have already gone awry.
A clear, decisive shout is of no use; it only causes the Zen practitioner to fall into extraordinary doubt. (Haiyin Xin)
A fierce dragon emerges from the water; a tiger leaves the mountain. Four winds arise, swirling through ten-thousand-ripped mists.
If you possess the True Eye of Aniruddha, you will traverse the three realms with your body horizontal and turn your back upon the heavens. (Yunxi Gong)
Entering directly with a single blade requires no deliberation; in the space of a moment’s hesitation, guest and host are distinguished.
You must not let Minde pass by; you should know that Xinghua’s staff was truly personal. (Gushan Gui)
In the darkness, they take each other’s hands and ascend a high mountain; when day breaks, they must go their separate ways.
Among the countless travelers on the road who have not yet returned home, how many will fall into the deep pit even with eyes wide open? (Jingshan Gaofeng)
[Continued Collection] Minde’s one shout resounded like thunder; Xinghua’s one shout echoed like thunder.
A brocade robe and jade belt—truly elegant and refined. I recall that old man Wan-hui of yore. (Lan’an Shu)
Gripping the seven-star sword to seek the author; overturning the Minister of Agriculture’s seal to face the enemy. With a single phrase in the presence of Yang, host and guest are distinguished;
the Yellow River at its nine bends flows backward. (Nanyan Sheng)
One shout, two shouts—the whole mechanism appearing and disappearing; guest and host are clearly distinguished, yet it cannot be avoided that both are blind.
Feeling for a turtle in the middle of the night; the bright moon shines upon accumulated snow. (Xue’an Jin)
Illumination and function do not occur simultaneously; those who understand know that the provisional and the real proceed together.
Though there is gain, there is likewise loss; it returns to the dragons and tigers racing against one another. (Xueyan Qin)
A monk once asked Xinghua, "What is it like when [the enemy] comes from the four directions and the eight points?

The Master said, "Strike the one in the center. The monk then bowed. The Master said, "Yesterday was a village feast; on the way back, we encountered a sudden storm and managed to take shelter inside an old temple.

The Verse says: When the four directions and eight points converge, He strikes the one in the center. Yesterday was a village feast; On the road, he met a sudden gale and torrential rain, And took refuge within an ancient temple.
This question is not merely an offense against others; it is like a bird pecking at thorns and shrubs in the air, making a clamor.
One must know that although Xinghua gallops with great speed, when he encounters rain, how could it ever wet his body? (Dongshan Cong)
The surging waves and drifting clouds—do not try to guess their course. The old fisherman leans on his oar by the edge of the cliff.
Returning empty-handed as before along the riverbank, he does not come to the imperial capital, though the customs there are the same. (Haiyin Xin)
One does not exist, and two cannot be formed. A warbler sings amidst falling flowers and fragrant grass. In the quiet courtyard, the rain has ceased and the night is just beginning;
a crescent moon rises once more from the sea. (Huìtáng Xīn)
A sudden storm of wind and rain arrives; for now, one takes shelter within an ancient temple.
Though one has entered the den of ghosts, swallowing charcoal to hide one’s form once again—(Gushan Gui).
Heavily shrouded within an ancient temple, he sighs in secret amidst piles of paper money;
the idle gods and wild ghosts are all struck with fear, solely because he knows the Sanskrit script. (Jingshan Gaofeng)
A naturally born white-marked tiger of the South Mountain; its fangs and claws have long faced the winds from all eight directions.
When the moon sets at the third watch, it passes through the marketplace; the deluded seek its tracks at dawn. (Xuetang Xing)
Carving out his heart and opening his belly to continue the transmission of the lamp; with ghostly faces and divine heads, he beats a tangled web of words.
Outstanding among all quarters, without equal—yet one knows it was merely to attend the monks’ feast. (Nanyuan Sheng)
The four quarters and eight directions extend beyond all bounds; amidst torrential rain and wild winds, there is nowhere to hide. Do not seek shelter within the ancient temple;
move your boat elsewhere, for there is a better way to deliberate. (Tianmu Li)
The dust and smoke of the north are forever stilled; The flowers and trees of Jiangnan flourish through all four seasons. There is no need to demarcate boundaries by force;
Ten thousand li of mountains and rivers are as level as the palm of a hand. (Xutang Yu)
Xinghua said to the rector Kebin, "Before long, you will become a master of the liturgical chant. Kebin replied, "I will not enter this monastery.
The Master asked, "Do you refuse to enter because you have understood, or because you have not understood? Kebin said, "It is neither of these.
The Master then struck him and said, "Rector Kebin has lost the battle of Dharma; he must pay a fine of five [coppers]."
Guàn. He prepared a single hall of steamed rice. On the following day, the Master himself struck the wooden mallet and said, "The Vinaya Master Kèbīn has not won the Dharma-battle;
he shall not eat this meal and must immediately leave the monastery. A verse says:
Two tigers fought one another, both exerting their full strength. One fell into a pit and was unable to leap back out;
had he been able to leap back, hunters throughout the world would have had no place to search for him. (Haiyin Xin)
Subduing the enemy in the battle of Dharma, he crushed the heroes; Xinghua’s strict practice revitalized the ancestral wind. Under the staff, one directly realizes the patience of the non-arising;
do not let intellectual understanding lead you into the cage of the dust. (Zhaojue Zong)

A man of substance should sever [delusions], yet he does not know how to sever them. He is a thoroughgoing man who brings transformation to others for the sake of humanity. Hereafter, let his own eyes open through the teachings.
[The Master] struck him with the staff, fined him, and expelled him from the monastery. (Zhenjing Wen)
The Lord of Lords questions the Guest of Guests; guest and host are clearly distinguished, yet ultimately intimate.
When there is reason, there is punishment and no place for words; beneath Mount Taihang, tears moisten the kerchief. (Foguo Bai).
Do not inquire at all into gain and loss, right and wrong; gathering and releasing, advancing and retreating, rest entirely with the person.
Losing money and incurring punishment are matters of everyday life; do not take up the statutes to discuss what is old or new. (Yuantong Xian)
Subduing the guest and promoting transformation, let both proceed together; white hair permeates his entire body, emerging from the crown of his head.
Having pierced through the "green and blue eyes" of the monks, he leaves the whole world to compete for the prize. (Fuxin Cai).

The vermilion mountains give birth to the *jué-zù* phoenix; the lioness gives birth to the *suān-í* lion. Under the blow of the staff, the eye of Maheśvara is revealed—this alone can boast of the "First Mechanism. (Jingshan Gaofeng)
In the battle of Dharma, I have always granted victory to my opponent; raising the banner and seizing the drum are clearly distinguished.
One must exhaust the Dharma before one knows shame; this old man of former times desired to put his words into practice. (Gushan Gui)
[Added for inclusion: Paying a fine to leave the monastery is seen by all; though one has reason, it is difficult to vindicate. A refined air suffuses his face.
Even if Xinghua had fully raised the banner, he could not avoid having his command enforced only halfway. As for this "halfway," let the clear-eyed monk examine it.

(Yezhuchuan). When Emperor Gao of Han appointed his generals, he sought only victory; who other than Han could dare to shoulder such a burden? The crimson banner stood high as the City of Transformation descended.
The Sovereign resides in the bowl, not upon the scale. (Nanyan Sheng).
The blazing sun and thundering swift lightning; in the sixth month, frost and snow drift down. Old Guchui of Xinghua is indeed too solitary and extreme.
Before the chaotic peaks, the golden-haired lion roars; when the hundred beasts hear it, their brains split asunder. (Lan’an Xu)
Fined money and expelled from the monastery, bringing disgrace upon the family. Xinghua the "Stutterer" met Kebin; father and son did not transmit the true wondrous secret.
From the tip of the staff, they struck forth the Jade Qilin. (Fozhao Guang).
Xinghua struck Kebin; with every blow, there was a trace of the mark. Though the ancients have passed away, their exemplary precedent remains.
After thirty years, how many will recognize this grace? (Nun Wuzhuo).
Xinghua’s staff struck like a crashing thunderclap; Kebin’s feet stirred up clouds of dust.
Had it not been for the General’s command beyond the frontier, how could his glorious name have been transmitted throughout the four seas? (Shu’an Yan)
Host and guest meet, yet wind and clouds differ; after the wine, the cup is refilled and ritual propriety is complete.
Striking one's own flesh and bone with a staff—within the monastic community, beating the drum turns instead into a grievance. (Huian Ti)
Xinghua drove out Kebin; Guanyin wears a ghost mask. With fingers moving inside one’s boots, one cannot avoid being seen by bystanders (Zantang Shen).

There is a path at the tip of the staff, leading to the profound ford. How could he have ever struck Ke-bin through and through? Only after the snowfall does one know the integrity of the pine and cypress;
only when night falls does one see the person holding the needle. (Kentang Chong)
Xinghua struck Kebin: a fierce tiger, mounted squarely on its waist. Raising a son who does not equal his father—his family lineage will decline for a generation. (Poban Xian)
The family code was strictly enforced, truly extraordinary; father and son, though of common flesh, had no room for negotiation.
Fined and beaten, he was driven out of the hall; yet the taste of the olive-scented tea remained long. (By Yan Yun)

The field of Dharma opens its battle; experience proves one capable of subduing the enemy. Unfurling martial strategy, he faces the General. How can it be that there is no reward for one who has committed no offense?
I await the unfolding of his wondrous plans to personally record his meritorious achievements. (Tianmu Li)
Xinghua struck Kebin; his words were direct, yet their intent was not so. From the tip of his staff, raindrops fell, striking out the Jade Qilin (The Blind Donkey saw).
[Supplementary Addition] Xuedou said: "As for Kebin’s desire to inherit the lineage, let aside the matter of Huixiang’s fine and expulsion from the monastery;
one must first obtain this beating. Now I ask you all: since the beating has already been administered, how can it be obtained?
Xuedou wishes to rectify this injustice; tonight, he shall vindicate Kebin."
[He] drove them all away at once with his staff. The verse says:
Vinaya Master Kebin was defeated in the battle of Dharma. Once, for the sake of the state, he stripped off his golden armor;

later, appearing in the world, he became a Dharma heir of Xinghua. He did not sell his precious sword because his family was poor; Xinghua’s arms were strong, yet he still complained that the bowstring lacked power. Snow.
Dongyan Ming still recognizes the high battle clouds (Xiatang Yuan).
[Added to the collection] Xinghua addressed the assembly, saying: "I have heard that they shout in the long corridors and they shout in the back quarters.
My sons, do not shout blindly or shout recklessly. Even if you could shout until Xinghua were driven into empty space,"
He collapsed. He had not a breath of life left. I waited for him to recover so that I might speak to you, but it was not yet time.
Why? Because I have never yet scattered true pearls from within the purple silk curtains for you all.
Why do you shout and clamor so wildly? The verse says:
True pearls are scattered within a purple silk curtain; does the Master of Esoteric Meaning understand them? Like the blind men feeling the elephant, the multitude speaks in vain confusion;
the ancient mirror upon the dais reveals all differences. (Haiyin Xin)
The Old Master of Xinghua was quite extraordinary. From the thirty-third heaven he leaped down; from within the purple silk canopy, he scattered true pearls.
Ancient or modern, who can appraise their value? For one ox received, a horse was returned. Need one say more? Their light illuminates the world by night.
Not seeing brocade or silver incense pouches, it has remained a mere idle talk until this very day (Shangfang Yi).
Fully upholding the Makhadeva command before the assembly—how could this be merely opening one’s lips at random?
With a shout, a blind donkey leads a pack in flight; in a dream, the five Sumerus are toppled (Jingshan Gao).
True pearls are scattered within a purple silk curtain; when Zen practitioners meet, they all engage in empty chatter.
Clapping hands and laughing aloud, "Śākyamuni and Maitreya are his slaves! (Gushan Gui).

[Added for inclusion: When Xinghua saw a fellow practitioner arrive, as soon as the monk stepped onto the Dharma Hall, Xinghua shouted. The monk also shouted. Xinghua shouted again; the monk also shouted.
Xinghua stepped forward and raised his staff. The monk shouted once more. Xinghua said, "Look at this blind fellow, still acting as the master!
As the monk hesitated, Xinghua struck him down directly from the Dharma Hall. An attendant asked, "Just now..."
"What offense has this monk committed against the Master? The Master said, "Just now he possessed both the provisional and the real;
he possessed both illumination and function. Yet when I held my hands across his face, he could not proceed.
For a blind fellow like this, if I do not strike him, what am I waiting for?"
At that time, the attendant prostrated. The verse says:
A thunderclap startles heaven and earth; how could one bear to cover one's ears and listen? One must know that Old Xinghua’s [action] was half a matter of human sentiment.
(Gushan Gui): Holding the Mo-ye sword in his grasp, the celestial Māras’ hearts fail them. O clear-eyed monks, cease further conjecture! (Jingshan Gao).
Just like an executioner of fierce and heroic spirit, he strikes a single blow at the throat;
the five viscera—liver and heart—are all cut out, only then realizing that the royal law allows no leniency. (Ret’-am Hiu)

Tall pines do not change their four-season green. How many clearly perceive the seizing and relinquishing of the opportune moment? When the battle is lost, one cannot withstand the sweeping of the broom;
the pupils in one’s eyes are the people standing before you. (Jianmen Division).
Gleaming and shimmering, the light of the water floats; Neither solitary sail nor boat is seen.
Where the slanting sun is about to set but has not yet fallen— All is the sorrow of parting souls, from ancient times to the present. (I-am Kwon)
Mount Sumeru falls and stands upright; the waters of the sea flow backward. Fellow practitioners visit one another, yet they exhaust themselves in enmity. Enough, enough!
Tomorrow the yellow chrysanthemums will make even the butterflies sorrowful. (Xue’an Jin)

When driving away the oxen of the plowman, the light is used immediately; when seizing the food of the hungry man, the light is used immediately. One cannot walk hand-in-hand with a fellow practitioner;
how could one know there is a hole pierced within the sleeve? (Nanyan Sheng)

Leaving the city for a secluded pavilion in the dark hours of sorrow, the moon sets and the stars part as one follows the horse's hooves. The wind sweeps across the morning window as the forest trees stretch far away;
deep in the night, the fires along the marshy banks flicker faintly. (Touzi Qing)

[Added from the Supplement] Chan Master Zhao (first generation) of Baoshou in Zhenzhou (successor of Linji). A monk asked, "What is to be done when the myriad objects of perception come to invade? The Master said, "Do not concern yourself with them. The Verse says: When the myriad objects come to invade, Do not concern yourself with them. If you can maintain this single phrase, You will see the Buddha within the weeds. If you do not see the weeds, How can you see the Buddha? If you can see both at once, You will be a true patch-robed monk. If you cannot see either, You are a person of no worth. If you can see the weeds and the Buddha, This is called the Great Matter. If you can see neither weeds nor Buddha, This is called the True Man of No Rank. If you can see both weeds and Buddha, This is called the Great Function. If you can see neither weeds nor Buddha, This is called the Great Stillness. If you can see weeds and Buddha simultaneously, This is called the Great Freedom. If you can see neither weeds nor Buddha, This is called the Great Emptiness. If you can see weeds and Buddha together, This is called the Great Unity. If you can see neither weeds nor Buddha, This is called the Great Non-duality. If you can see weeds and Buddha as one, This is called the Great Oneness. If you can see neither weeds nor Buddha, This is called the Great Non-existence. If you can see weeds and Buddha as distinct, This is called the Great Multiplicity. If you can see neither weeds nor Buddha, This is called the Great Non-distinction. If you can see weeds and Buddha as they are, This is called the Great Suchness. If you can see neither weeds nor Buddha, This is called the Great Non-suchness. If you can see weeds and Buddha as they truly are, This is called the Great Reality. If you can see neither weeds nor Buddha, This is called the Great Non-reality. If you can see weeds and Buddha as they manifest, This is called the Great Manifestation. If you can see neither weeds nor Buddha, This is called the Great Non-manifestation. If you can see weeds and Buddha as they appear, This is called the Great Appearance. If you can see neither weeds nor Buddha, This is called the Great Non-appearance. If you can see weeds and Buddha as they arise, This is called the Great Arising. If you can see neither weeds nor Buddha, This is called the Great Non-arising. If you can see weeds and Buddha as they perish, This is called the Great Perishing. The eldest brother is a seasoned mariner; reading the winds and setting the sails, he is truly decisive.
Let the sea monsters stir up waves and billows as they may, he passes straight through like a bird in flight, leaving no trace behind. (Seal of the Dharma-Imprint)
When ten thousand objects come to invade, do not concern yourself with them; the sword and shield are originally the foundation of great peace.
Having trodden the path by which one came at that time, one returns with confident steps under the moon. (The Opening of the Sealed Room).

[Added from the Supplement] Because Zhaozhou came to Baoshou, the Master sat with his back turned to him on the meditation seat. Zhaozhou spread out his sitting cloth and prostrated. The Master rose and entered the abbot’s quarters; Zhaozhou gathered up his sitting cloth and departed.

The verse says: The lion’s roar is heard from afar; The tiger’s tail does not hide its stripes. When the great function is revealed, Who can fathom it? He turns his back and sits facing the wall; The guest departs as the host enters. If you wish to see the true man, Look at the one who has just left.
A single movement of the strings distinguishes the melody; a falling leaf reveals the autumn. When water is level, it makes no sound; when it is level, it does not flow.
It is simply because there are no fetters beneath one's feet that one attains freedom to go or stay as one pleases. (Yuan of Dun’an)
[Added for inclusion: Baoshou was asked by a monk who came to pay his respects. The Master said, "The myriad sages of the ten thousand kalpas do not go beyond this abbot’s quarters.
The monk asked, "As for what the ancients said—that the great trichiliocosm is but a bubble on the ocean—where, then, would you place these abbot’s quarters?
The Master replied, "The thousand sages are present right now. The monk asked, "Who can testify to this? The Master said: [The text ends here].
He threw down his whisk. The monk passed from west to east and stood there; the Master struck him.
The monk said, "If one had not studied for a long time, how could one know the ultimate point? The Master said, "Thirty years from now, these words will spread widely.
Yuanwu said, "Baoshou set out his nets and spread his snares within the abbot's quarters; this monk stepped toward the bait and held it up."
Wearing horns on his head, he charged through the waves three times; three times he was enveloped by them.
Tell me, what did he gain? Do you understand? Under a heavy reward, there must be brave men. The Verse says:
When rolled up, it is a seamless whole; when unfurled, light radiates from all eight sides. Hundreds of thousands of Buddhas dwell together in a single place;
they turn the wheel of the Dharma within the palm of one's hand and unleash great power upon the field of action.
It is not only thirty years hence that the fragrance of the *campaka* flowers will waft before one’s face. (Fodeng Xun)
[Added for inclusion] Because Hu Dingjiao came to visit Baoshou, the Master asked, "Are you not Hu Dingjiao?
He replied, "I dare not. The Master said, "Can you nail the void? He replied, "Please, Master, break it open first. The Master then struck him.
[Huaihai] said, "Preceptor, do not strike me in error. The Master said, "In the future, there will be many masters who will point this out for you.
Later, Huaihai went to Zhaozhou and recounted the previous conversation. Zhaozhou asked, "For what reason were you struck by him?
[Huaihai] said, "I did not know where my fault lay. Zhaozhou said, "Even this single seam..."
"What can be done? Hu had an awakening at this point. Shouzhuo said, "For now, let us nail up this seam.
The Verse says: When the Eye of Space appears, flowers bloom; To further instruct one to break it open, matters become as tangled as hemp.
Even if you could point directly to the seam within the hall, It would be clearly like a hawk flying over Silla. (Yeyu Chuan)
Even if one were able to nail this single seam shut, upon closer inspection, it would not be the work of a true master. Pity these two old Chan elders;
they have instead revealed their family’s private shame to the laity. (Yue’an Guo)
A single seam remains clearly visible; it is difficult to strike the blow at the head. Even if you manage to clip and nail it down, in the end it will never be complete. (Gushan Gui)

Old acquaintances meeting, they speak from the heart: "May I ask how deep are the paths on the western mountain? Speaking plainly before the assembly, he displays his skill:
"The red furnace refines only to seek true gold. (Fenyang Shao)
On the road to the Western Mountains there are monkeys; their howling in the rain and moaning in the wind stir the traveler’s sorrow.
Suddenly encountering this lion cub of the forest, all manner of their wiles cease at once. (The Capable One of the Middle State).

[Added from the *Zengshou*] Baoshou asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "From the place of Cui Chan. The Master said, "Did you bring back Cui Chan’s shout? The monk said, "I did not bring it back.
The Master said, "If that is so, then you did not come from Cui Chan. The monk then shouted. The Master raised his staff; as the monk hesitated, the Master struck him immediately.
The verse says: The shout of the Great Hero is like thunder; It strikes through the ten directions at once. If you hesitate for even a moment, You will be struck by the staff of the Ancient Buddha.
A Chan practitioner from the Five Lakes knocks at the gate of meditation; it is just like a beginner learning to climb a mountain.
He leaps upward, wishing to emerge beyond the blue clouds, yet when his strength reaches the peak, even one step is difficult. (Fujian Qín)

Riding a donkey and wearing a bamboo hat, he goes south to meet [the sun]; leaping upon a horse and shaking his whip, he travels north. Two great merchants both break through the dawn;
even when the sun is high, they still hear the striking of the third watch. (Baoning Yong)
The brocade is turned inside out and the embroidery is laid face down. Brothers of the same breath are further joined as branches. To act as a man is not merely to compose songs;
one must seize the opportune time for the ancestral fields and gardens. (Yuantong Xian)
The scholar south of the city rides a donkey; the young gentleman north of the market mounts a horse. Each has four hooves that tread the earth;
together they arrive at Jinding Pond in the third month of spring. (Fujian Qín).
Their appearing and disappearing depend on whom; their rolling up and unfolding rest with me. Shaking the tongue and moving the lips, they clearly fall into verbal error.
(Tianning Liaoyi of Jingzhao Prefecture). How could a mirage ever quench thirst? When can a painted cake satisfy hunger?
I urge you not to plant thorns and briars, lest your descendants in later generations be pricked by them. (Jingshan Dahui Zonggao).
The lake’s shimmering light is even more favored in fair weather; the mountain hues, misty and hazy, are likewise wondrous in the rain.
If one were to compare West Lake to Lady Xi, whether in simple makeup or heavy adornment, she would be equally fitting in either guise. (Fodeng Xun)
When people are poor, their wisdom seems short; when horses are thin, their manes seem long. Staying alone at the Double Peak Temple, we burn a single incense stick together. (Gushan Gui)
[Continued Collection] Two children embrace a flower drum; the one on the left beats it, while the one on the right dances.
One tune, two tunes—no one understands them. Clearly, the pure wind moves through the ages. (Lan’an Xu)
A mountain temple with shifting rain and clearing skies; clouds coming and going within the caves. The stars fill the heavens and the moon is as bright as day;
who would wish to divide this realm at this moment? (De-shan Qing)
The "tortoise-nosed snake" of the Southern Mountains: when touched, both ends move; its venom is meant to harm people.
Yet it is left for the poor man to play with. (Xue’an Jin)
At twilight, pounding the grain, one rushes to the city; at midday, returning by boat, one enters the harbor late. Meeting at midnight, both shout across the distance;
unaware that much time has already slipped away. (By Xian of Zhai’an)
Two streams branch from a single source; who would have known that the correct word has instead become partial?
It is not because of fragrant grasses that one’s entrails are broken; the family lineage is shattered and falls to one side. (Dai Wuweī)

When the Third Holy One was asked by a monk, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? the Master said, "A stench attracts flies. Xinghua said, "There are plenty of flies on the back of a worn-out donkey.

The Verse says: Stench attracts flies; On the back of a worn-out donkey, there are plenty. The Patriarch’s meaning is right here; Why seek it elsewhere? If you can see through this, Then you will know the source of the ancient path. If you cannot see through this, You will only be chasing after shadows.
The jellyfish has bones; the numinous tortoise has no shell. The blind donkey’s stinking meat attracts flies.
The meaning of the Buddhas and the meaning of the patriarchs are like mountain peaks. (Zhengjue Yi, 2)
The numinous tortoise has a shell; the water jelly has no bones. To break open the spine of a donkey is enough to attract blue flies. On the ancient road of Caoxi, travelers have ceased to pass.
The donkey with its broken spine has much putrid flesh for flies. Who knows that Xinghua does not travel in vain? He is accustomed to passing before the Five-Phoenix Pavilion.
[The Master] passed by. Holding a golden whip in his hand, he celebrated the Great Peace (Baizhang Yuan).
The scenery pervading the earth is without error; for what reason do you not believe and instead give rise to doubt?
An old woman points it out for you once more: upon a lump of putrid meat, blue flies swarm. (Huangbo Xian)
[Continued Collection] Lush and verdant, they shade the lair of the Azure Dragon; the tall bamboos stand transcendent, things beyond the mundane world.
If one were to compare these tall bamboos to the lofty pines, they do not yet equal the wind-boneed majesty of those ancient trees. (Fojian Yongqin)
A lump of stinking flesh has something to discuss; beneath the skin flows fragrance like a musk pouch.
Suddenly, if a Zen practitioner bites it through with their own teeth, look—every mouthful is pure fragrance. (Longmen Yuan)
[Supplement] When the Three Sages arrived at Deshan, as soon as they spread their sitting cloths, Deshan said, "Do not spread out your cooking towels;
there is no leftover soup or stale rice here. The Master said, "Even if there were, there would be no place for it to land.

Deshan then struck him. The Master caught the staff and pushed it onto the meditation platform. Deshan laughed heartily. The Master cried out to the heavens and then went down to attend the hall. Hall.
The head seat, whose name was Tietiantai, asked: "A traveling monk must possess an official pass from his own province. What is this 'official pass from one's own province'?
The Master said: "What are you saying? The head seat asked again. The Master struck him with his sitting mat and said: "You lacquer bucket!
How many worthy and virtuous men have you offended from beginning to end? As the head seat was about to respond, [the Master struck him again].
The Master then passed on the matter of the second seat to another person. The verse says:
Calling it clouds and inhaling it as rain, A pervasive, clear breeze stirs the universe. Laughter and weeping are no ordinary sounds.
Seeing injustice on the road, there must be one who can right it; he wishes to slay the unjust man and will not speak with those who are merely "fair.
Now, where can his traces be found? Raise your eyebrows and look at the hawk! (Changling Zhuo).
Leftover soup and rancid rice have nowhere to be placed; changing hands, one beats one’s breast and strikes one’s own head to cover it up.
Two iron hammers without holes, both alike bound by no rope. (Fodeng Xun).
The northern and southern mountains face each other; east and west, the paths diverge. Without passing through the midst of the battlefield, how could one have seen General Li? (Muan Yong)
[Added from the Supplement] Master Dajue of Weifeng (heir to Linji) was asked by a monk, "What is the original body? The Master said, "My head rests on Mount Heng;
my feet tread upon Mount Beiyue. The Verse says: My head rests on Mount Heng, My feet tread upon Mount Beiyue. If you wish to know the original body, Look at the man with the staff.
Those who understand the Linji school are rare; only Dajue Xian manifested great capacity.
When someone asked about the words for the original body, he rested his head upon Mount Heng while following Mount Tai. (Dongshan Cong)
Behind the main mountain, before the secondary mountain; below is earth, above is heaven.
His arms and hands are too long for his shirt and trousers, yet he wins a bountiful year through his drunken madness. (Bao-ning Yong)
[Added from the Supplementary Collection] Chan Master Guankui Zhixian (Successor of Linji). A monk asked him, "I have long heard of Guankui;
having arrived here, I see only the hemp-soaking pond. The Master said, "You see only the hemp-soaking pond; you do not yet see Guankui."
[The monk] asked, "What is Guankui? The Master said, "As swift as a split arrow. Verse:
A single stream flows from Caoxi to Guankui; The dragon moves, and wind and rain stir the clouds and mists. With a steep mechanism like the notch of an arrow, the waves surge with urgency;
They shake the seas and mountains of Vairocana until they sink low. (Dharma Master Kefu of Zhuozhou)
[Added from the Supplementary Collection] Guankui visited Linji. Linji grabbed the Master; the Master said, "Understood, understood. Linji let him go. The Verse says:
After the rain has fallen and the clouds have dispersed, Lofty peaks rise in their dozens. Leaning on the railing, gazing again and again— To whom can one turn for companionship?

(Xiuyan Rui). [Added by Collection Master] Chan Master Shanchui of Dingzhou (also known as Chui Chan, who was a successor of Linji). The Regional Commander, Duke Wang, prepared a seat in his official residence and invited the Master to preach the Dharma.
The Master ascended the seat, took up his staff, and said: "I will strike you even if you come forth; I will not..."
[The Master] struck him as he came out. The monk stepped forward and said, "What about Cui Chan?
The Master threw down his staff and said, "I have kept you waiting for a long time, Lord Commissioner. I pray you take care. The Verse says:
The Mo-xie sword lies crosswise, its precious radiance cold; the ruffians among the gallants dare not look it straight on.
Flying across the azure heavens with a thundering roar, it leaves the very cosmos pitch black. (Baoning Yong)
Fully displaying the family style to show all people, he casts his hook into the sea to fish for the golden-scaled one. The swimming fish play in the water, leaping over the waves;
both oars and boat are cast away as he emerges from the great ford. (Yanshou Hui)
Thirteen years of habitual embroidery on silk garments; she herself cherishes these red sleeves that still hold the fragrance. People say these are the robes for her wedding day;
with a bashful smile, she has stitched out a pair of mandarin ducks. (Kongsou Yin)
[Added from the Supplement] The Monk of Lì Village in Xiāng Prefecture (he was a successor of Línjì).
While the Master was boiling tea, a monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master held up the tea spoon. The monk said, "Is this all there is to it?"
The Master threw the tea spoon into the fire. The verse says:
"The tea has not yet finished brewing when someone comes to ask; He picks up the tea spoon and presents it to him.
Had he encountered a hand capable of catching a flying swallow at that moment, His life would have been in peril—what could he have done? (Touzi Qing)
[Added to the Collection] Master Huxi (Dharma successor of Linji). A monk asked him, "Master, how many years have you been here?
The Master said, "I only see the withering in winter and the growth in summer; I do not remember the years at all. The monk said, "Excellent, not remembering!
The Master said, "What do you say—I have been here for how many years? [The monk replied: "Winter..."
"Does it wither in summer and grow long? The Master said, "A tiger in the midst of a bustling market. The Verse says:
A tiger in the center of the bustling market, Can sing but cannot dance. Its fate meets the Lord Jupiter, It does not encounter the Lord Rāhu.
(Langlangjue). The old man of Huxi dwells in a hermitage;
though many years have passed, he does not remember them at all. The tiger within his mind dwells in the bustling marketplace; on all four sides, it is like a cauldron boiling over.
(Caotang Qing). [Added from another collection:
The Abbot of Tongfeng An (who succeeded Linji) was asked by a monk, "What will you do if you suddenly encounter a tiger here?
The Master then let out a tiger’s roar. The monk made a gesture of fear. The Master laughed loudly. The monk said:
“This old thief! The Master said, “What can you do about this old monk? The Verse says:
To see it and not take it—though one thinks of it a thousand miles away. What a fine tiger! Yet its fangs and claws are not yet complete. Have you not seen?
Suddenly meeting him beneath Mount Daxiong, His majestic reputation shakes the very earth. When a great man sees it, he simply gathers it up.
"Patting a tiger's tail while stroking its whiskers. (Xuedou Xian).
[Added from another source] Chan Master Micang of Cangzhou (a successor of Linji) asked a monk, "Where have you recently come from?
The monk replied, "Jizhou Tairu. The Master said, "When you arrived at Tairu, what did Tairu say to you? The monk replied, "He knew me."
Mikawa Rokujun said, "When one arrives here, what then? The Master said, "It is no different from the road when you first set out.
Mikawa said, "The Reverend has already lost Lake Tai. The Master said, "When you came, the road was steep; now the road is level. Mikawa said, "No.
The Master said, "When you came, the road was steep; now the road is level. Mikawa said, "No."
Fang said, "This will obstruct the Master's path. The Master replied, "You lacquer-barrel fellow! What limits do you have? The Verse says:
Setting out to transcend all quarters, he arrives directly at the site. Encountering a steep and perilous road, the staff that kills and gives life transforms into a leopard.
The main road through Mikkawa is as level as a whetstone; one cannot help but find oneself inside a lacquered bucket. Without applying rouge, she is nonetheless elegant;
generally speaking, it is her very bones and flesh that are beautiful. (Fudō Shun)
[Added from the Supplementary Collection] Master Yunshan (who succeeded Linji) asked a monk, “Where have you come from? The monk replied, “From the Western Capital.
The Master said, “Have you brought a letter from the host in the Western Capital? The monk said, “I do not dare to deliver any news.
The Master said, “An adept monk naturally possesses [his own authority]. The monk said, “Who would be willing to eat leftover soup and rancid rice? The Master said:
Only the *ācārya* was unwilling to eat. The monk then made a gesture of vomiting. The Master called for his attendant and had him escort this "sick monk" out.
The verse says: This monk covers his ears and steals the bell;
Yunshan takes what is mistaken for correct. If it were a blue-eyed barbarian, there would be something else entirely.
A single stroke of self-reflection. (Mukan Egen).
[Added by Chōshū] Censor Chen Cao of Muzhou (see entry on Muzhou). One day, while ascending the tower with his subordinates, he saw several monks approaching.
An official said, "Those coming are all traveling monks. The Official (Cao) [responded].
[The official] said, "It is not so. [The monk] asked, "How do you know it is not so? The official said, "Wait until I have investigated him. A short while later, the monk arrived before the tower.
The official suddenly called out, "Head Monk! and the monks all raised their heads. The official said to the officials, "Do you still not believe what I said? The verse says:
A single word leaves the nest; a thousand births emerge from the entanglements. The wind and snow grow fierce at night; the tree breaks before the cliff.
(From the Snow Hall Collection)
Seizing the drum and snatching the banner to test the patch-robed monk—straightaway he uses black beans to exchange for his two eyes.
Having once suffered the bitterness of snow and frost in years past, he is startled even upon seeing the willow flowers fall. (Nun Wuzhuo Zong).
Having grasped the foremost mallet of Mount Sumeru, how could one with a copper head and iron brow contain him?
As the salt-and-vinegar seasoning, the oars and rudders, and the timely rain—were it not for this man, who else could it be? (Feng of Fukan).
Jixian once appraised Uqiu Zi; as the latter’s transformations were so rapid that they could not be distinguished, Jixian fled in haste.
He was bested by one gazing from a high tower, whose brilliant vision could clearly discern even the finest hair of an autumn down. (Xutang Yu)

[Added for collection: Minister Chen asked Muzhou, "What sutra are you reading? Muzhou replied, "The *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*. The Minister said, "Of the translations made during the Six Dynasties, which dynasty’s version are you reading?

Muzhou held it up and said, "All conditioned phenomena are like a dream, an illusion, a bubble, and a shadow. Verse: All conditioned phenomena Are like dreams, illusions, bubbles, and shadows. Muzhou held it up; The Minister was left speechless. If one can see this way, One will not be deluded by words. If you wish to understand the meaning of the sutra, Look at the face of the Minister. *Note: This entry is from the *Wumenguan*. The wondrous teachings transmitted through the translations of the Six Dynasties— To this day, one has not yet awakened to their essential secret.
One must believe that the aged phoenix atop the branch In springtime turns its cry into that of a yellow oriole. (Zhengtang Bian)
