*Ancestors’ Occasions for Inquiry*.
The Remainder of the Sixth Generation under the Sixth Patriarch (the Remainder of the Fifth Generation under Qingyuan) (Caodong School):
Chan Master Judu of Longya Mountain in Hunan (Successor of Dongshan). When he first visited Dongshan, one day he asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
Dongshan said, "Wait until the waters of the Dong River flow backward" (*Chuan deng lu* reads as follows).
"When the Dong River flows upstream," he said, "I will tell you. Only then did the Master realize its meaning.
The verse says: Longya had not yet stilled his wild mind; He questioned various masters without ceasing. The predecessors, pitying him, responded with sincere intent:
"Directly say: the Dong River must flow upstream. (Fenyang Zhao)
In the ancient source there is no water; how could the moon arise? A single stream divides and flows westward along the banks. At the Onion Range, cease inquiring about the dream of Mount Xiong’er;
in the snowy courtyard, do not speak of the spring at Shaolin. (Touzi Qing)

[Continued Collection] The waters of the caves have no cause to flow upstream; they respond to others because they witness their bitter suffering. The meaning of the Ancestors who came from the West is truly without intention;
when deluded thoughts and the frantic mind cease, it is simply over. (Hyōnggwam Hyong).
When Longya was at Cuiwei, he asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch? Cuiwei said, "Bring me my meditation board.
The Master then passed the meditation board to him. Cuiwei took it and struck him. The Master said, "As for striking me, you may strike as you please;
however, there is no meaning of the Patriarch here. He then asked Linji, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch?"
Linji said, "Bring me that meditation cushion. The master then passed the cushion over to him. Linji took it and struck him immediately.
The master said, "If you strike, let the Master strike; however, there is no meaning of the Patriarchs in it.

Later, a monk asked, "When the Master was traveling on pilgrimage, you questioned two venerable elders regarding the meaning of the Patriarchs. I wonder, did those two venerable elders possess the eye of the Dharma?"
"Is it clear? The Master said, "It is indeed clear, yet it still lacks the meaning of the Patriarch.
The verse says: In the mountains of Longya, the dragon has no eyes; How could dead water ever stir the ancient wind?

The meditation board and the sitting cushion cannot be used; They should be entrusted only to Master Lu. Once Master Lu has received them, what reliance can there be? Leaning back in repose, one should not seek to continue.
The Patriarchal Lamp: "Fit to face the evening clouds, they have not yet merged; The distant mountains stretch on and on, layers of boundless azure.
(Xuedou Xian) "Sūn Qing did not bow down before the Chanyu; From beginning to end, he always observed the rites of the Han Emperor.
Only after the snowfall does one know the tenacity of the pines and cypresses; Only when faced with difficulty is a true man revealed. (Fóxìng Tài)
[Continued Collection] The ancestral meaning from the West is questioned layer upon layer; the use of the meditation board and the sitting mat is the same.
Do not attempt to embellish the void; his family’s approval is like being deaf and blind. (Kumu Cheng).
The Master rode with his green dragon, never untying his mount; everyone says the Teacher is a fool.
Within the soft mud lies a sting that wounds; three times he employed the trap for tigers. (Mantan Cheng)
The meditation cushion and the Zen board face off before Longya; why does he fail to act as a true master when the opportunity arises?
The intent of his coming is stripped away before the eyes of the enlightened; I fear it will drift and fall far away. How could a sword be hung in empty space? Yet a raft floats upon the Milky Way.
The sproutless grass can conceal a fragrant elephant; a bottomless basket can hold a live snake. Today, what obstacles remain on the rivers and lakes? All is unobstructed.
Just as there are boats and carts at a ferry crossing (Tiantong Jue).
[Added by Zeng. Longya was once asked by a monk: "What is it like when two rats gnaw at the vine? The Master said:
"One must have a place to hide oneself before it can be so. The monk asked: "What is this place to hide oneself? The Master said: "Do you see me yet? (Lian Deng)
(Or is it that he has returned and seen Mañjuśrī? The verse says:
In the cold month, the moon lingers upon the distant peaks; Ten thousand acres of calm lake are sealed with the light of silk.
A fisherman’s song startles the herons from the sandbar; They fly into the reeds, their traces lost to sight. (Danxia Chun)
Majestically manifest, yet subtly difficult to perceive; though the two mice are clever, they find no opening. The wisteria vine and branches have already emerged before birth;
the True Eye faces the sun, skillfully shifting and exchanging. Old Longya’s mechanism is like meeting lightning:
the base becomes noble, and the noble becomes base. (Yuánwù Qín)
[Added from another source: Longya was once asked by National Teacher Shao, "When heaven cannot cover it and earth cannot support it, what then?

The Master said, "A seeker of the Way ought to be thus. This question was posed seventeen times in succession, and each time the Master replied, "If I were to explain it for you, I fear you would later curse me away.
Later, when Shao was residing at Tongxuan Peak, while he was in the midst of bathing—

Suddenly realizing the meaning of their previous conversation, he assumed a formal posture, faced Longya, and prostrated, saying: "If you had explained it to me back then, I certainly would have cursed him today.

He then offered this verse: Verse: The old man’s words were like a thunderclap; I was struck dumb and could not speak. Had I known the truth at that time, I would have cursed him right then and there.
Bones white as vermilion, not a thread of cloth remains; utterly naked and starkly bare. Emerging from the bath, he bows his head, his face covered in shame.
When I speak for him, he will surely scold me. (Wan’an Yan)
An iron boat floats in the center of the great ocean; it follows the waves as they surge toward the heavens. Reaching the shore with a favorable wind, no one recognizes it;
in the north of the river, iron coins have been used from of old. (Donggu Guang)

The stone tortoise speaks not, yet it is a true knower; the earless skull listens in the deep night. At daybreak, it hides within the shadowless tree;
though the great sun shines everywhere, it cannot be found. (Touzi Qing)
Who says the turtle cannot speak? Its wondrous words flow forth spontaneously. It has exhausted the meaning of the West-Come Patriarch;
yet, meeting no one who understands, it remains empty. (Benjue I)

[Added for collection] A monk asked Longya, "How does one apply effort throughout the twelve periods of the day? The Master said, "It is like a handless man performing a fist. The Verse says: A handless man performs a fist; The fist is empty, yet it is not absent.
If you wish to see the true fist, Look at the handless man.
It is like a person without hands who wishes to make a fist; who would dare to step forward and face them head-on?
If one is always thus throughout the twelve periods of the day and night, there is no need to further inquire about the Zen of the Patriarchs. (Benjue I)

[Added from the Supplementary Collection] A monk asked Longya, "What did the ancients attain that they simply ceased [their practice]? The Master said, "Like a thief entering an empty house. The Verse says: Like a thief entering an empty house, They find nothing to take away.
Having attained the state of non-attainment, They rest in peace, free from all traces.
Withered pines and wild cranes cry at the humble gate; snow fills the cold forest, heard as night falls. This very life has nothing at all;
it is no hindrance that beneath the crags lie clouds from the stream. (Gumukcheong)
Buying a hat to fit the head; measuring talent to fill a post. Even a monk with clear eyes cannot recognize him before his face.
(Zhenjing Wen) The bandit in the green woods has a righteous mind yet a wild heart; within his heart, deluded thoughts are hidden in the chamber.
Unaware, he casts himself into emptiness and enters a vacant house; in vain, he lets out a laugh of empty mockery. (Benjue Yi)

Among all beasts, he is the lion cub; he can roar with perfect mastery, shaking his entire majesty. His wondrous skills are deployed with total freedom, even able to hurl back at his opponent.
Yet, alas, Mañjuśrī sits upon him; the King of Khotan cannot pull him away. Even Sudhana the youth begins to doubt;
he thought there was none in the world who could surpass him, yet he too has been swallowed up by the six sense-objects. (Zhimen Kuan)
Chan Master Kuangren of Shushan in Fuzhou (a successor of Dongshan) heard that Master Daomian of Daguang on Mount Daibei in Fuzhou was addressing the assembly, saying:
"The phrase exists; the phrase does not exist, like a vine leaning against a tree. The Master specifically entered the mountain ranges and arrived there just as Daomian was plastering a wall.
He immediately heard [the Master] say: "I have heard you, Master, say: 'The phrase exists; the phrase does not exist, like a vine leaning against a tree.'"
"Is there a tree? he asked. "Yes," [the other] replied. The Master said, "Suddenly the tree falls and the vines wither;
where does the phrase return? Baizhang set down his mud tray and laughed heartily, returning to his quarters.
The Master said, "I have traveled three thousand *li* selling my bedding just to come for this matter; why do you deceive me? Baizhang called to his attendant.
He took two hundred coins and gave them to this senior monk (upādhyāya), instructing him, saying, "In the future, there will be 'One-Eyed Dragon' who will point it out for you.
Later, hearing that Master Mingzhao Qian of Wuzhou had appeared in the world, he went directly to pay his respects.
Mingzhao asked, "Where have you come from? The Master replied, "From Min Province. Mingzhao asked, "Have you ever been to Daopei?"
"No. The Master said, "I have arrived. [The monk] asked, "What words or phrases are there? The Master recounted the previous conversation.
Zhao said, "Miaoshan may indeed be called 'head straight and tail straight,' yet he simply did not meet a true connoisseur. The Master still did not understand.
He asked again, "When the tree falls and the vines wither, where do the phrases return? Zhao said, "It merely causes Miaoshan’s laughter to grow ever fresher. At this, the Master—

Upon hearing these words, he attained great enlightenment. He then said, "It turns out that Huishan has a blade hidden within his smile. He prostrated from afar to repent his error and offered this verse:
"The tree falls and the vines wither as I pose a single question; 'Aha-ha,' the great laughter has its reason. The wild sheep hangs from the horns—no trace to be found."
Abiding thus, even until now the laughter has not ceased. (Haiyin Xin) When the tree falls and the vines wither, there is a great burst of laughter.
No traveling by night is permitted; one must reach one’s destination at dawn. The wayfarer, greedy for his journey, goes and does not return;
by the time he returns, his parents are already old. His parents are old—there is no need to lament this; it is still better than it was on that day.
Not yet returned home, (Buddha’s Wisdom Spring), I idly dangle my straight hook by the riverbank.
There too, when a golden-scaled fish ascends the line, if it can leap thrice and take flight, it will spare the fisherman from knitting his brows in dismay. (Withered Tree Accomplished).
The wisteria withers and the tree falls—what is your intention? A single stroke, clearly displayed for others. There is a blade within the smile;
one must not misunderstand it. Head and tail perfectly aligned, yet one stumbles. (Dochangru).
A cold blade sharper than a hair-tip comes amidst smiles; the Śakrābhilagna eye allows no alteration. A golden dragon once raised its claw with one eye;
the skull felt the pain and the crown of the head opened. (Da Hong Yu)
If one were to take these words as a fixed tenet, one would betray Mingzhao, the One-Eyed Dragon. In a smile, the paths of mud and water are suddenly distinguished;
only then does one know that from a thousand miles away, we share the same wind. (Jingshan Gao)
A phrase exists and yet no phrase exists; the rattan leans against the tree. White rice has always been made from grain. On a high tower a flute is blown; the willows are like mist.
Spring winds fill the earth as flying花絮 (flying catkins) fall. (Gushan Gui)
The tree falls and the vines wither—what does this mean? Guishan opens his mouth and laughs heartily.
How pitiful, that the three-foot-long Dragon Spring Sword is called a shuttle on the wall of a potter’s house. (Fóxìng Tàiyǎn, 2)

Having sold the bedding and the money, his demeanor grew increasingly haughty with every step. Had he not been pierced by Mingzhao’s direct exposure, how could one have known there was a blade within the smile?
"When the tree falls, the vines wither"—ask Daowei! He laughs heartily, revealing his total mastery; the bedding has been sold, and the travel provisions are gone.
It is finished. When the cold autumn night arrives, whom can one blame? (Wenshu’s Way, Part Two).
It causes Miaoshan’s laughter to grow ever fresher; within that laughter lies a blade that secretly wounds people.
Those who rush along the road of Caoxi still toil in vain, laboriously seeking the ford.
The tree falls and the vines wither, yet the laughter does not cease. Who among them can discern the source of the school?
The old man of Miu-shan has taken the wrong path; coming and going in vain, he harbors a bellyful of sorrow. (Chu-an Fang, 2)
Adding to this, Mount Gui’s laughter grows ever fresh. At that moment, he presented it directly to you. Mingzhao leaked the secret of Mount Gui’s verse;
its boundless splendor is now bestowed upon others.
[Continued Collection]: "With a phrase, there is no phrase; coming bright, going dark. A living capture, a raw seizure—a swift proclamation.
Like a vine leaning against a tree; things gather according to their kind. Ginseng from overseas, *fuzi* from Shu: when the tree falls, the vine withers.
One must strictly avoid names and patterns. Where do the phrases return? *Sulu sulu*. Ha ha! A great laugh; the broken mirror does not reflect. The great earth is vast and empty."
Vast and open, he lets himself leap and bound at will (Huguo Qin). He laughs out loud with a most extraordinary "he-he.
One must surely have light radiating from between the eyebrows. This is not Mingzhao adding redundant commentary;
the monastic community would otherwise have deliberated it wrongly (Fushan Yuan).
A great laugh—its meaning is difficult to discuss. When the tree falls and the vines wither, there must be a cause for the question.

Once, when the administrative monk had finished constructing a stupa for Shushan’s longevity, he informed the Master.
The Master asked, "How much money did you give to the craftsmen? He replied, "Everything was up to you, Master.
The Master said, "Did you give three coins to the craftsmen? Or two coins? Or one coin?"
"If you can explain it, come and build a stūpa for me with me. The monk was speechless.
Later, the monk related this to Master Xian of Dalingan (i.e., Luoshan). Daling said, "Has anyone been able to explain it? [The monk] replied, "No one has been able to explain it yet.
Daling said, "When you return, tell Shushan: 'If you give three coins to the artisan, together...'"
"Furthermore, in this life you will certainly not obtain a stūpa. If you give two coins to the artisan, you and the artisan will together produce one hand.
If you give one coin to the artisan, it will cause the artisan’s eyebrows and whiskers to fall out.
The monk returned and spoke according to these instructions. The Master, assuming a dignified demeanor, gazed toward the Great Ridge and performed a *kaṭhina* ceremony.
Liti sighed and said, "I thought there was no one; yet on the Great Ridge there is an ancient Buddha who has emitted light that reaches this place.

Although it is so, it is still like a lotus flower in the month of December. Later, when Daoyi heard these words, he said, "For me to speak in such a way is already like saying that a tortoise's hair is three feet long. The verse says: I thought there was no one; On the Great Ridge there is an ancient Buddha.

One coin, two coins, and three coins—Master Shushan’s ridge is but a vain distinction. You must know that the seamless is originally priceless;
it alone reveals heaven and earth, towering amidst white clouds. (Yunyan).

you must know that even on level ground there may be deep pits. (Cishou Shen)

A red banner embroidered upon an eight-flowered ball, A crimson hand raised amidst a hundred battlefields; Since that time, he has returned with a song of victory.
The nation’s heroes have won the age of clarity. (Amitāyus).
[Added from another source] Once, National Teacher Shao asked Shushan, "What kind of realm is this 'a hundred craftsmen and a thousand layers'? The Master said:
Twisting the hemp rope with his left hand, he binds the ghost-child. The verse says:
"A hundred craftsmen, a thousand layers—desiring to question Zhou; Shushan, in his entire being, understands how to respond.
At that time, among the assembly, who could have known? It was enough to make the waters of Jiangxi flow backward. (Touzi Shu)

[Added for inclusion] Shushan was once asked by Lingquan: "The withered tree producing flowers is said to accord with others; is this a statement of 'this side' or 'that side'? The Master said, "It is also a statement of 'this side. [Lingquan] asked, "What is a statement of 'that side'? The Master said, "The stone ox breathes forth the mist of the three springs; the numinous bird does not perch in the shadowless forest. The Verse says: The withered tree produces flowers; This is the ultimate meaning. The stone ox breathes forth the spring mist; The numinous bird does not perch in the shadowless forest. If you can understand this, Then you will see the ancient path. If you do not understand, How will you avoid being deceived? The withered tree produces flowers— This is the ultimate meaning. The vast ocean is calm when the wind ceases; the mist clears and the water’s hue holds the moon in its emptiness.
A single band of cold radiance—how can one fathom its end? Who can discern within it the dragon’s shed bones? (Danxia Chun)
Master Qianfeng of Yuezhou (a successor of Dongshan) ascended the hall and said: "If you cite one, you must not cite two;
to let pass one move is to fall into the second. Yunmen stepped out from the assembly and said, "Yesterday someone came from Tiantai and went straight to Jing Mountain.
The Master said, "The head cook shall not be required for communal labor tomorrow."
He then descended from his seat. Xuedou said, "Yunmen was only able to lift with one hand; he could not press down with the other. He then offered this verse:
Ganfeng raised one, but did not raise two; Yunmen raised his hand, adding to his air of self-importance. Let the flowers bloom and fall as they are moved by the wind.
It blows; naturally its fragrance fills heaven and earth.
(Huìtáng Xīn) The single phrase before sound is like eyebrows upon a mouth; Buddhas and Patriarchs have never known it. Last night, on Mount Kunlun, they idly spoke of dreams;
a white-haired man gave birth to a black-headed child. (Dánxiá Chún)
Black and white clearly distinguished, the board is full of chess-stones; never once has a single move been flawed.
How pitiable are the countless onlookers, who remain entirely unaware that the axe handle has rotted away. (Baizhang Yuan).
The outward appearance and physical demeanor are already not true; two or three parts of the image resemble a human being. Beside it stands one who is groundless;
the most difficult to deceive is the eye itself that witnesses it. (Baoning Yong)
Tiantai and Nanyue have vanished without a trace; who else could encounter them face-to-face? Clouds rise on the eastern ridge as the western ridge turns white;
flowers bloom on the front mountain while the back mountain glows red. (Puyongping)
Boiling the sea to make salt always results in flavor; striking the void to produce sound is fundamentally without sound.
When Kunlun collides with the Persian, they walk hand-in-hand across the bottom of the sea. (Cishou Shen)
In high towers, pairs of beautiful women sit each by a jade bed at a crystal window.
Having finished embroidering mandarin ducks, they insert golden needles deep into their brocade sachets. (By Fuxing Tai)
The Persian presents the incense from Hainan; the white-eyed Kunlun comes to deliberate upon it.
The merchant does not understand the tongue-rolling speech; he merely observes that both nostrils are long. (Fozhi Yu)
The path is darkly connected between the eastern ridge and western crag. Who has ever seen Old Qianfeng? Yunmen held his hand as they walked side by side;
white clouds form a flying canopy, and the moon embraces the void. (Chu’an Fang)
[Continued Collection] Do not seek realization atop the Peak of Dryness; the Child of No Words, however, understands it well.
Letting loose a single thread to pass on the message, he has traveled throughout Tiantai and Lingnan. (Kumu Cheng)
The spring orchid and the autumn chrysanthemum—each finds its own season. Where is there any conflict? To whom can one complain for being divided into marrow and skin?
When the wind comes, the crow already senses it; when the dew is heavy, the crane knows it first. If one asks how this is so, they themselves do not know at all.
(Yuanwu Keqin): Qianfeng let go from the edge of a precipice; Shaoyang possessed a natural bearing. It was said that there is only the white monkey;
who would have known there is also the black monkey? (Foxin Cai).
Seeing one another, there is no need for anger; you are destitute and I am poor as well. You say that I rise too early, yet there are still those traveling at night. (Wannian Xian)
Bright at the head, dark in union; relaxed in release, urgent in gathering. Hands and feet suddenly exposed, yet needle and thread are still stolen away.
Raise one, do not raise two. Tiantai passed through Jingshan; he chewed up the pits of others' peach and plum—ultimately, it only damaged his own jaw. (Yuedang Chang)
Qianfeng ascended the hall and said, "The Dharma-body has three kinds of illnesses and two kinds of radiance.
One must penetrate each of these thoroughly before one can understand how to return home and sit in peace. You must know that there is still a 'higher opening' beyond this.
Yunmen stepped forward and asked, "Why does the person inside the hermitage not know what is happening outside the hermitage? The Master laughed heartily.

Mendun said, "This is still a point of doubt for students. The Master asked, "What kind of mental activity do you have? Mendun said, "I also wish for the Master to understand me. The Master said, "You must be like this before you can sit securely.
Mendun responded, "Yes, yes. Verse: The gatekeeper asks of the place where students doubt; The Master probes the nature of his mind’s movement. "I also seek the Master’s understanding," he says;
"Only by being thus can you sit at ease. In response, he simply affirms: "Yes, yes."
The shopkeeper showed the brass to the prospective buyer, saying, "It is difficult to distinguish this from genuine gold.
The buyer brushed his sleeves and walked away first, his face covered in shame and embarrassment, not daring to show anger. (Baizhang Yuanwen).

Lowering the hook across the four seas to fish for the fierce dragon; beyond the ordinary, he converses in mystery with those who know him. Meeting one another, they cast off their robes and remove their scholar’s caps;
it does not hinder them as they walk hand-in-hand up the high peak. (Fóxìng Tài)
Three kinds of illness and two kinds of light; the Dharmakāya is revealed here in its majestic presence. People of this age do not understand the meaning within;
they still attempt to measure the Dharmakāya with their own limited intellects. (Chuan-an Fang)
[Continued Collection] When the strings are moved, one hears a different melody; hearing one, one knows ten. Joining hand to hand and board to board, glue is poured into lacquer.
Not seeing what is outside the hut while inside the hut, the unperforated iron hammer remains incomprehensible. In human relations, acquaintance values the true knower.
Water entering water, gold traded for gold. (Wenyu Qín).
One who is within the hermitage does not know what lies beyond its walls; those with iron brows and copper heads are unlike others.
They swing on the flowered ceiling boards; a fierce tiger’s tongue writes the *svastika*. (Xiatang Yuan)
Qianfeng was once asked by a monk, "The *Bhagavāns* of the ten directions all share the single path to the gate of *nirvāṇa*.
I wonder, where does the beginning of that path lie? The Master struck the ground with his staff and said, "Right here.
Later, the monk requested further instruction from Yunmen. Yunmen picked up his fan and said, "This fan leaps up to the Thirty-three Heavens and strikes—"
It sticks to the nostrils of Śakra. A blow from a staff strikes the carp of the Eastern Sea; the rain pours like an overturned basin. Do you understand? The verse says:
Taking it in hand, one treats a dead horse with medicine; With the *reviving incense*, one seeks to raise the endangered. In a single moment, he presses out [the essence] throughout his entire being.
Sweat! Only then can one believe that my house does not spare its eyebrows.
(Tiantong Jue) Layer upon layer of towers and pavilions cannot be struck open; Qianfeng cleaves through them to reveal their towering majesty.
Where the Buddha-lands of the ten directions are fully manifested, in each and every gate, one beholds Sudhana. (Foxin Cai)
Mount Sumeru stands with its peak inverted; a pure breeze rises from the great ocean. In Pūrvavideha, the leaves have already fallen; in Aparagoyānī, the flowers are now in full red bloom.
(Changling’s Inscription)

Tearing apart Yunmen’s single-handled fan, breaking off Qianfeng’s single staff, amidst two or three thousand places of music and stringed instruments, and four or five hundred lanes of flowers and willows. (Jingshan Gaofeng)
Qianfeng need not point it out; Yunmen should cease beating over old relics. Naturally, the carp of the Eastern Sea strikes the nostrils of Śakra. (Gushan Gui)
[Continued Collection] A three-eyed tortoise, red as fire; a one-horned qilin, swift as a drill. The Earth-Ruler roams at night through Jambudvīpa;
sparks fly from beneath the feet of the clay ox. (Xuedou Zong)
One person travels by boat toward the land; another gallops on horseback over the point of a needle. They arrive in Chang’an at the same time and on the same day.
Of these two, one is the sharpest and most clever. (Fujian Qín).
Facing them directly, he did not cast his words blindly; responding to their capacities, he spoke straightforwardly in every case. Qianfeng and Yunmen shared the same tongue from two mouths.
If one is a person who follows like a "fox-fur" appendage, then playing with cleverness will only result in clumsiness. (Xue’an Jin)

[Added for collection] Once Yunmen arrived at Qianfeng, he said, "I ask the Master to answer me. The Master replied, "Have you even reached the old monk yet? Yunmen said, "Like this? Like this? The Master said, "I thought the monkeys were white; it turns out there are also black ones. The Verse says: The old master’s words are like a thunderclap; The bright moon shines upon the cold stream. If you wish to see the true source, Do not mistake the shadow for the substance. In the vast expanse of the empty sky, How could there be a single speck of dust? If you can understand this one phrase, You will see the ancient path clearly revealed. Even if you have attained the Way, Do not let it become a mere habit. If you do not know how to turn back, You will surely fall into the pit of views. If you can leap over the three barriers, You will transcend the four propositions. If you can see through the two gates, You will realize the single truth. This is the great function of the Buddhas and Patriarchs; It is the ultimate meaning of the ancestral school. If you can grasp it in this moment, You will be free from all doubt. If you cannot yet comprehend it, You must continue to investigate with diligence. Do not seek it outside of yourself; Seeking elsewhere is a futile waste of effort. Only when you have personally realized it Will you be able to benefit others. This is what is meant by "the old master has not yet been reached. It is not that the old master is lacking; It is simply that you have not yet arrived. If you can understand this, You will see the old master’s true face. If you do not understand, You must continue to practice. Do not rely on intellectual understanding; Relying on intellect is a trap. Only through direct realization Can you escape the net of views. This is the teaching of the Buddhas and Patriarchs; It is the lifeblood of the ancestral school. If you can enter this gate, You will attain liberation. If you cannot, you must continue to study. Do not be complacent; Complacency leads to stagnation. Only through constant effort Can you reach the ultimate source. This is the meaning of "like this? Like this? It is a call to immediate action. If you can respond in this way, You will be a true heir of the Buddhas. If you cannot, you remain a follower of the shadows. Do not mistake the shadow for the light; Mistaking the shadow for the light is a grave error. Only when you have seen through both white and black Will you be truly free. This is the verse on the old master’s words. May you all understand.
Qianfeng raised one and did not raise two; Yunmen grasped his hand to add to his spirit. He said there was only the white monkey;
who knew there was also the black monkey? (Huitang Xin)
The bowstring and the arrow notch engage one another; the netted pearls face each other. Shooting with a hundredfold accuracy, every arrow is never in vain.
Gathering all reflected images, every light is unobstructed. Having attained the *dhāraṇī* of words and phrases, they abide in the *samādhi* of playful mastery.
Its subtlety is such that it winds and turns, pervasive and perfect. It must be thus: transverse and vertical, free and at ease. (Tiantong Jue).
[Added to the Collection] Chan Master Qinshan Wensui of Lizhou (successor of Dongshan). The Zen traveler Juli came to visit him.
After performing his prostrations, he asked, "What is it like when a single arrowhead pierces through the three barriers? The Master said, "Let out the lord within the barrier and see.
The traveler said, "If that is so, then one must surely correct their errors. The Master said, "When do you wait for anything else? The traveler said, "A fine arrow indeed!"
The arrow was released, but it had no place to land, so he went outside. The Master said, "Come here first, Ācārya. Liang turned his head back;
the Master stepped down from the meditation seat, seized him, and said, "Setting aside for a moment the 'one shaft piercing the three barriers,' try to discharge an arrow for Qinshan and see.
As Liang hesitated, the Master struck him with seven blows of the staff and said, "First, listen to this fellow who talks nonsense!"
This remained a point of doubt for thirty years. A monk brought it up to Tong’an Cha.
Tong’an said, “Although Master Liang understands how to release the arrow, he has yet to hit the mark. The monk then asked, “I wonder, how can one hit the mark?
Tong’an replied, “Who is the Lord of Guanzhong? The monk returned and reported this to the Master (Linji). The Master said, “If Master Liang had…”
If you understand it thus, you will also avoid the "mouth of Qinsong. Nevertheless, although this is so, Tong’an did not have good intentions;
you must examine this for yourself before you can attain it. The verse says:
A single arrowhead pierces the three barriers; who knows the difficulty of hitting the mark? Releasing the lord within the barriers, he shifts his borders back to his original soil.
Clouds freeze and the wild geese cry alone; all sorrowful people pity their own doors. From of old, sweet melons have been sweet; from the beginning, bitter gourds have been bitter.
(Daitangding). [Added from another collection.
Qingshan was once asked by Yantou, "What is the true word? The Master replied, "Namo Buddhāya."
The verse says:
Responding to questions as they arise, responding to circumstances as they come—this is neither Chan nor the profound mystery. Later generations, for no reason, translated it out;
they took the Sanskrit words and rendered them into the language of Tang. (Tui-geng Ning)
[Added for inclusion: Qingshan, along with Yantou and Xuefeng, arrived at Deshan. One day he asked Deshan, "The Emperor of Heaven has spoken thus;
Longtan has also spoken thus. I wonder, how would you speak, Master?
Deshan said, "Try reciting what the Emperor of Heaven and Longtan said, and I shall see. As the Master was about to offer a reply, Deshan—

He struck him. The Master, having been struck, returned to the Yanshou Hall and said, "It is so, it is so; yet he strikes me too severely. Yantou said, "If you speak like this, you will not be able to say later on that you saw Deshan coming.

Fayan commented differently, saying, "It is so, it is so; yet he strikes me wrongly. The verse says: It is so, it is so; Yet he strikes me too severely. If you speak like this, You will not be able to say later on That you saw Deshan coming. Fayan comments: It is so, it is so; Yet he strikes me wrongly.
The aged one has forgotten all artifice; he is a true master. Throughout antiquity and the present, all have prized him for his total freedom from even the slightest flaw.
The single lineage of the Heavenly Emperor is manifested at Longtan; the spiritual source wells forth, yet ten thousand paths diverge. Qinshan was still subject to movement and stillness;
how could he fail to transcend speechless expression to this day? (Fenyang Zhao)
Old generals cross swords for a single season; among them, few understand gain and loss.
If Qinshan’s staff were without words, it would be even more of a contradiction. (Yanshou Hui)
[Added from the Supplementary Collection] Master Benren of Baishui, Ga’ān (successor of Dongshan), ascended the hall and said:
"I, this old monk, do not ordinarily wish to dally with the sons and daughters of others before sound or after form. Why?
Because sound is not sound, and form is not form. A monk asked, "What is sound that is not sound? The Master said, "Call it by its name."
"Can it be called 'form'? The monk asked, "What is form that is not form? The Master said, "Can it be called 'sound'?
The monk bowed. The Master said, "Tell me now: did I speak for you, or did I answer your question? If you can understand it here—"
There is a way of entry. The verse says:
Form is form, and sound is sound; where the new oriole cries, the willow smoke is light. At every gate there is a road leading to the capital;
the three islands stretch across as the sea moon shines bright. (Danxia Chun)
Sound emerges from emptiness; form arises from nothingness. Before sound and after form, they swirl in a blur, with no space between them even for a hair—how can they be called "models"?
This majestic, perfect response leaves not a grain of dust behind. What need is there for the clever forging of a furnace to laboriously analyze and separate them?
How much better it is to attain the patience of non-arising beneath the staff; its fragrance fills the path as soon as it is heard and seen. (Yuanwu Keqin)
[Added for inclusion] Chan Master Xianqi of Tiantong in Mingzhou (successor of Dongshan). The Venerable Jian asked: "The student has come here with great resolve;
I ask the Master to provide a direct answer. The Master said: "In my place, one simply empties oneself once and is finished.
What is there to be 'resolute' or 'direct' about? The Venerable said: "If you, Master, answer questions in this way, you might as well buy some straw sandals and go on a pilgrimage!"

"Good. The Master said, "Come closer. Jian approached him. The Master said, "As for my answering you in this way, where does the fault lie? Jian had no reply. The Master then struck him. The verse says:
The monk asked a question with great earnestness; The Master answered with a single blow. If one wishes to understand the ancient path, One must look directly at the present moment.
Excellently, with a single excretion, it is stilled. The rat performs on three stages; the cat blows the pí-pì-lì flute;
the tortoise lifts its head and sings a *bā-gē*. One, two, three, four, five, six, seven. (Xuedou Zong)
[Added for inclusion] Dayong Qi was asked by a monk: "What is the eye that is never deficient in its application? The Master said:
"It is just like being blind. The verse says:
Blind, deaf, mute, and speechless—far removed from the true nature of heaven. When the eyes resemble the eyebrows, the Way begins to be near.
Last night the Lord of Spring secretly issued his decree; where the yellow oriole sings, the green willows are in spring. (Danxia Chun)

[Added to the Collection] Master Xiandehé of Jingzhao Prefecture (Successor of Dongshan). He lived inconspicuously among the common people in Minchuan. He did not keep monastic requisites and did not follow the formal rules of discipline.
Wearing a single robe throughout both winter and summer, he would go along the riverbanks each day to gather shrimp and clams to sustain himself.
At nightfall, he would sleep amidst the paper money at the White Horse Temple on Mount East. The local residents called him "Shrimp Boy" (Xiànzi).
When the Chan Master Jing of Huayan heard of this, he wished to determine whether it was genuine or false. He first hid himself within the paper money offerings.
At the deep of night, as the Master returned, Jing seized him and asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
The Master immediately replied, "The wine stand and platter before the spirit altar. Jing let go of him and said, "It is not in vain that we share the same root."
Birth. The verse says:
Before the deity’s altar stands a wine tray; upon it lies an iron ball as large as a fist. With a single blow, it is shattered to pieces—not worth even half a coin.

(Yuanwu Keqin): Before the divine altar, he brushes aside the paper to inquire about the Westward Journey; directly seizing the opportune moment, he points to the wine table. With bare arms and bared shoulders, he bows his head in prostration;
though calamity descends from heaven, it does not become a disaster. (Xiatang Wenyi):
Picking clams and hauling shrimp, one obscures one's own numinous spirit. How can one fit one's whole body into an ancient temple?
Lifting the head, there is nothing but desolation beyond; what use are the eyes of a ghost from many years past? (Dongye Fu)
Pitiful indeed, amidst piles of paper money; as soon as that foul mouth opens, there is only entanglement.
Having squandered the impoverished livelihoods of the ghostly realm, even now no one passes by the ancient temple. (Dongshan Yuan)
[Added from the Supplementary Collection] Chan Master Jiufeng Puman of Ruizhou (successor of Dongshan) asked a monk, “Where have you recently come from?
The monk replied, “From Min. The Master said, “The long journey must have been difficult. The monk said, “It was not difficult; as soon as I moved my feet, I arrived.
The Master said, “Is there anyone who does not move their feet? The monk said, “There is. The Master said, “How could such a person reach this place? The monk was speechless. The Master [continued].
He drove him away with his staff. The verse says:
Layer upon layer of clouds, and again layer upon layer of water; His steps never reached the Nine Peaks.
If one has traveled so far, it must have been no easy task; Yet the master was already halfway there. (Xueyan Qin)
[Added from the Supplementary Collection] Chan Master Youqi Daoyou of Taizhou (heir to Dongshan). One day, he rang the bell and ascended the hall.
As soon as the assembly had gathered, the Master asked, "Who is striking the bell? A monk replied, "The Rector. The Master said, "Come closer.
The monk approached, and the Master struck him with his palm and then returned to his quarters to lie down. —Touzi.
Qingyun: Yet, one must urgently flee; this has occurred throughout all time. When one’s path is exhausted at a dead end, try asking those nearby.
They do not understand your inner situation, yet they truly find something to seize upon. Once questioned, they immediately demand the underlying reason.
Disregarding their own peril and ruin, they obtain a pretext from others. Though they may reap a small profit, it is nonetheless a way of harming others in secret. Not so.
"He is a skilled hand. Although this monk has suffered a loss, it is because he did not maintain his own proper bounds, bringing disaster upon himself;
this is hardly out of the ordinary. Nevertheless, even so, it remains that an ordinary man has been unjustly caught in a snare.

[Added for inclusion] Nan-yuan was asked by a monk: "When cold and heat arrive, what then? Compiled by the Śramaṇa Fasheng of Ba’en Guangxiao Chan Temple in Chizhou during the Song Dynasty.
Continued Collection of the Anecdotes of the Patriarchs by the Śramaṇa Puhui of Tianyi Wanshou Chan Monastery during the Yuan Dynasty’s Shaoxing Era;
Seventh Generation after the Sixth Patriarch, Part Two (continuation of the Sixth Generation after Nanyue).
The Second Chan Master Baoshou of Zhenzhou (who succeeded Baoshou Zhao) ascended the hall for his inaugural sermon.

Prior to this, he had requested Sansheng to act as the presiding host according to the late Baoshou’s final instructions. On the day of the opening of the hall, just as the Master was ascending the seat, Sansheng pushed forward a monk;
the Master struck him immediately. Sansheng said, "If you act as a teacher of men in such a manner, you will not only blind [the eyes of others]..."

"This monk has blinded the eyes of the entire city of Zhenzhou. The Master threw down his staff, descended from the seat, and returned to the abbot’s quarters. The verse says: The blind man of Zhending Has blinded the eyes of the whole city.
The staff is cast down; He descends and returns to the hall.
The Three Sages carry the treasure of Bāzu; Qiang pushes the monk from the assembly, intending to deliberate. The General Beyond the Frontier executes the true command;
it reaches even to the point where blind men fill the Great Tang. (Fenyang Zhao)
Just as he ascends the precious flower-king throne, the Three Sages push the monk to resolve the doubts of the assembly.
Under the staff, all is clear—there is neither old nor young; how many blind people in the world know this? (Huanglong Nan)
A golden mallet is hurled down as swift as a shooting star; a skilled hand catches it without effort. At that moment, it is cast into the vast waves;
for ten thousand ages, there is no further trace. (Baizhang Yuanwen).
Black and white not yet distinguished, every move is extraordinary. Let those idle fellows spy from the sidelines;
were it not for the hand of an immortal, who else could rival him? (Baoning Yong).
The scout horse flies back; beneath the staff, all is still. Blind men fill the city of Zhinzhou. Peace was originally established by the generals;
yet the generals are not permitted to witness that peace. (Zhenjing Wen)
In the Linji tradition, there are two rounds of exchange; pushing a monk with a staff reveals the blind path of the ancestral lineage.
Were it not for Baoshou’s eye of total functioning, who else could clarify this koan? (Foguo Bai).

To whom was the Dharma-eye transmitted and entrusted? The Three Sages pushed forward the monk to resolve the doubts of the assembly. When the General ordered him to raise [his hand], the multitude were struck with awe;
it truly reached the point where the blind and deaf were made to hear throughout the four quarters. (Zhenru Zhe)
When Baoshou first ascended the seat to open the hall, Sanxing immediately pushed forward a monk.
If you wish to know how he blinds everyone’s eyes, you should go to Caoxi and ask Old Neng (Zhihaiqing).
Facing the vanguard, one must not rely on the total mechanism; a formidable adversary must be known by a true master. Iron horses are let loose and the desert passes are still;
for a thousand ages, few have dared to ride the blind donkey. (Shangfang Yi)
Fengcheng recovers the precious sword; few in the universe recognize the man. Had it not entered the hands of Zhang Hua, how could its right and wrong have been distinguished? (By Fuxincai)
When the blade is thrust through, iron cavalry fly; where the lightning-flash strikes, golden mallets are hurled. That an entire city was blinded is but a trivial matter;
yet it has led to disputes and controversies that persist to this very day. (Fóxìng Tàiyán)
The Emperor’s decree within the realm; the General’s command beyond the frontier. Sweeping away smoke and dust across ten thousand *li*, his majestic prowess is beyond compare.
Straight within the crooked, coarse within the fine—blinding the eyes of men with a truly masterful strategy. He overturns the meditation seat and pulls the tiger’s whiskers.
When water is level, it does not flow; when a person is equanimous, they do not speak. The sword has long since departed; to etch a mark upon the boat is but a vain labor.
When the authority is in one's hand, one wields both the power of life and death. A true man attains freedom. (Nanhua Heng)
The arrow is already upon the bowstring; it must be released. To hesitate or deliberate is to miss the mark; the tip of the arrow strikes with a sudden thrust.
(Tianning Liaoyan of Jingzhao Prefecture). Baoshou opened the hall and sent forth a monk: "There is an eye upon the staff—seek clarity!
The people of the entire city are blind—who can understand? A pure breeze arises, pervading earth and heaven, past and present. (Shushan Ru).
Lifting the first hammer of Mount Sumeru—lightning and sparks are far too slow. Where the Elephant King walks, the fox tracks vanish;
when the Lion roars, the hundred beasts tremble. (Jingshan Gaofeng)
The staff-head blinds an entire city; Sansheng incites Baoshou’s anger. The true command can only be raised by half;
one blind man leads a multitude of blind men along (Gushan Gui).
[Continued Collection] Having raised a son, he wishes to gamble; his entire body is not bound by even an inch of silk. He enters the den of right and wrong with his whole being;
within the gateway of birth and extinction, he proclaims [his views] with his full mouth. (Zhengtang Bian)
A thousand-person tent in the north of the passes; ten-thousand-bushel ships in the south of the river. Sitting within the Bodhi-nest, all these are said to be mere empty rumors. (Shi’an Shui)
Bao-shou was the second generation [of his lineage]. Previously, while at Bao-shou, he served as the master of offerings.
Bao-shou asked him, "Before your parents were born, bring me back your original face. The Master stood there until late at night, yet his responses did not accord with the truth.

The next day, he took his leave. Baoshou asked, “Where are you going? The Master replied, “To the South to study the Buddha-dharma. Baoshou said, “For now, stay here and act as a street monk (*fangjie*). If it is the Buddha-dharma, it can be discussed even amidst the vast turmoil of the secular world. One day, while in the marketplace, he saw two men fighting. One man stepped forward, struck the other with a single punch, and said, “You—” [Baoshou then said,] “This is the Buddha-dharma! The Master was greatly enlightened upon hearing this. He bowed and departed. Baoshou called out to him from behind, “Wait! Wait! The Master looked back. Baoshou said, “I have always known that you would come to the South. The Master then returned to Baoshou’s place. One day, Baoshou asked, “What dharma do you practice? The Master replied, “I practice the dharma of non-practice. Baoshou said, “If you practice the dharma of non-practice, what dharma will you teach others? The Master said, “I do not know how to teach others. Baoshou said, “Since you do not know how to teach others, why do you say you practice the dharma of non-practice? The Master said, “I do not know how to practice it myself. Baoshou said, “If you do not know how to practice it yourself, how can you say you practice the dharma of non-practice? The Master said, “I do not know how to practice it myself, yet I do not know how to teach others. Baoshou said, “If you do not know how to practice it yourself and do not know how to teach others, then you are truly practicing the Buddha-dharma. The Master then bowed. Later, when the Master was traveling through Xiangzhou, he stayed at the residence of the official Wang Shouzhi. One day, Wang asked, “What is the meaning of Bodhidharma coming from the West? The Master replied, “The Great Way has no gate; it is simply a matter of directly pointing to the human mind and seeing one’s nature to become a Buddha. Wang said, “I have heard this before. The Master said, “Have you ever seen it? Wang said, “I have not. The Master said, “Then you have merely heard of it; you have not yet seen it. Wang said, “Please show me. The Master said, “The official is already wearing his cap and gown; where is the Buddha? Wang was greatly enlightened upon hearing this. He then invited the Master to reside at the temple of Mount Zhongnan. One day, the Master was sitting in meditation when he suddenly heard the sound of a dog barking. He immediately attained great enlightenment. He composed a verse: “The Great Way has no gate; / It is simply a matter of directly pointing to the human mind. / Seeing one’s nature and becoming a Buddha / Is like the dog barking in the courtyard. He then went to see Baoshou. Baoshou asked, “What dharma do you practice now? The Master replied, “I practice the dharma of non-practice. Baoshou said, “If you practice the dharma of non-practice, what dharma will you teach others? The Master said, “I do not know how to teach others. The Master said, “I do not know how to practice it myself, yet I do not know how to teach others. Baoshou said, “If you do not know how to practice it yourself and do not know how to teach others, then you are truly practicing the Buddha-dharma. The Master then bowed. "What is this face? Upon seeing him, the Master suddenly attained great enlightenment. He returned and informed Baoshou, who deeply approved. The verse says:
Two spiritual friends meet in the bustling marketplace; Their faces have no origin—how much effort is wasted! Even grinding one's bones to powder would not suffice.
In response: A single phrase, clearly realized, transcends ten billion worlds (the Seal of the Ocean).
Traveling everywhere—north, south, east, and west—at nightfall one returns as the moon is like a hook. A gust of spring wind scatters the flowers in disarray;
without realizing it, one ponders and nods the head in the dark. (Kumu Cheng)
"Most wonderful! Most wonderful! To know one's nature and life within this—strike the nose and give a punch;
at that moment, it is struck directly. (Wuzu Yan)
In the middle of the crossroads, there is no place for the six to be gathered; the original face leaves no trace of its path.
Even if one were to attain clear realization, one has already fallen into my second category. (Heshan Fang)
With a single punch, he topples the Yellow Crane Tower; with a single kick, he overturns the Parrot Isle.
Fortunately, there are bystanders who lend their strength; he himself sits upright watching Yangzhou. (Fóxìng Tái)
A single blow leaves one with no face; the blue-eyed barbarian monk cannot look enough. Autumn comes and yellow leaves fall in profusion;
six times six turns back into thirty-six. (Nanhua Heng)
[Continued Collection] Baoshou acted as a street peddler. In the midst of a bustling marketplace, he realized it: before one's parents were born, such is the faceless state—most extraordinary.
When the Great Function manifests, there are no rules or regulations. (Yuánwù Qín)
The spring colors linger; the willow hues are lush. Peach blossoms still cling to the branches of the apricot trees.
If you wish to know the original face that has no features, look for it only among the dust—the true man is found therein. (Fojian Yongqin)
Passing through by borrowing the road, one is faceless; because of the heterodox, the orthodox is struck with a fist.
Under the gate of the patch-robed monks, there is no involvement; it is like using pure gold to exchange for brass. (Nanyuan Sheng)

Not a hair’s breadth remains; moving forward and backward with total freedom. Beyond the threshold, heaven and earth are vast and open; within the Great Dharma, there is no exterior, and one wanders at ease.
Clear and bright is the meaning of the Patriarchs; clear and bright is the tip of every blade of grass. Tear asunder the net of doubt; cut off the river of craving.
Even if one possessed the power to turn back heaven, how could it compare to resting directly beneath?
In the middle of the four-way crossroads, utterly naked and bare—let loose the water-buffalo of Guishan! (Yuánwù Qín)

[Added from the Supplementary Collection] Mingzai of Xiyuan was in Xu Prefecture. Hearing that Nan’uan had begun his teaching career at Ruzhou, he, who had previously been a fellow student, went specifically to visit him.
As soon as he entered the monastery, he said, "I prostrate to the Master; I have no gift to offer for my human affairs."
"Since coming from Xuzhou, you have brought with you a razor from Jiangxi, Master. The Head of the Monastery said this. The Master pinched the Head’s hand once.
The Head said, "Attendant, take it away. The Master brushed his sleeve across [the Head] and departed. The Head said, "Alala!"
*La ā la la.* The Verse says:
Before the gate of Nan-yuan, do not presume to look; Whoever ascends it loses their full majesty. Xu-zhou has received the news from Jiangxi;
The meeting of needle and magnet is known only to oneself. (Haiyin-xin)
[Added to the Collection] Chan Master Liaojiao of Luzu Mountain in Chizhou (heir to Guankui). A monk asked, "What is the tree of the Twin Śāla groves?
The Master said, "The formless body within the body with form. The monk asked, "What is the formless body?"
The Master said: "An iron Kunlun under a golden incense burner.
The Verse says: Within the body of form is the formless body; An iron Kunlun beneath a golden incense burner. Since his departure from the Twin Trees, there has been no news;
Dust and wind fill the road for those who come and go. (Fang’an Xian)
[Added from the Supplementary Collection: Chan Master Rubo of Zifu in Jizhou (he succeeded Yuta Mu).
Once, when Minister Chen Cao came to visit, the Master drew a circle. Chen said, "I have come as a disciple already lacking in aptitude;
why draw this circle? The Master placed a single dot in the center. Chen said, "I thought you were the captain of a ship from South India."
The Master then returned to his quarters and closed the door.
The verse says: "Round and round the pearls swirl; jade chimes ring out. A horse carries, a donkey bears, atop an iron boat. Entrusted to the carefree traveler of sea and mountain:
When fishing for the giant tortoise, let down a single hook. He further said: "No monk in the world can leap out [of this]. (Xuedou Xian)
The net is spread across the heavens; the great whale and the giant turtle do not ascend it. Turning its body beneath the water, it leaps over the waves before the billows.
Whether there or here, across thousands of miles, it can turn back even where there is no foothold. Closing the abbot’s quarters, he relies on what came before.
Gathering both and releasing both, half-closing and half-opening, the host and guest employ their full being. The stone woman and the old Huangmei (Chang of Yuet Tang).
Lord Li wished to urge Lord Zhang to drink wine, but was instead fined a cup by him. Pearls circle in a perfect round—do not misunderstand this.
Returning home, he claps his hands and laughs heartily. (By Biefeng Yin)

Chan Master Huìqīng of Bājiāoshān in Yǐngzhōu (a successor of Nántă Yǒng) ascended the hall. Holding up his staff, he said: "If you have a staff, I give you a staff; if you have no staff, I take away your staff. He leaned on the staff and descended from the seat. The verse says: If you have a staff, I give you a staff; If you have no staff, I take it away. Leaning on the staff, he descends from the seat— Who can discern the meaning of this? A single staff, long and straight, Is like a dragon emerging from the deep. If you can see through it, It is like a jewel in the palm of your hand. If you cannot, You will surely fall into the pit of doubt. Do not seek it elsewhere— It is right here before your eyes. If you can understand this, You will be a true patch-robed monk. If you do not, You are but a common person. Do not be deceived by appearances— This is the ultimate reality. If you can grasp it, You will transcend all traces. If you cannot, You remain bound by the world. Do not hesitate— Take it up and go! If you can act thus, You are a true heir of the Buddhas and patriarchs. If you cannot, You are merely a follower of the mundane. Do not let this pass for nothing— This is the great matter of life and death. If you can realize it, You will attain liberation. If you do not, You will wander in samsara. Do not be deluded— This is the true teaching of the Buddhas. If you can practice it, You will reach the other shore. If you do not, You will remain in the sea of suffering. Do not look back— Press forward with resolve! If you can do so, You will be a true son of the Buddha. If you cannot, You are but a worldly man. Do not waste this moment— This is the time to awaken. If you can awaken now, You will never again be lost. If you do not, You will continue to suffer. Do not be negligent— This is the path to enlightenment. If you can follow it, You will attain the Way. If you do not, You will remain in darkness. Do not doubt this— This is the heart of the Dharma. If you can trust it, You will find peace. If you do not, You will remain in turmoil. Do not look for it outside— It is within your own nature. If you can recognize it, You will be free from all attachments. If you do not, You will be bound by them. Do not be distracted— This is the essential point. If you can maintain it, You will be steadfast. If you do not, You will waver. Do not let it slip away— This is the treasure of the mind. If you can hold it, You will be secure. If you do not, You will be vulnerable. Do not be careless— This is the source of wisdom. If you can cultivate it, You will be enlightened. If you do not, You will remain ignorant. Do not be complacent— This is the work of a lifetime. If you can accomplish it, You will be fulfilled. If you do not, You will be empty-handed. Do not wait until it is too late— This is the moment of truth. If you can act now, You will succeed. If you do not, You will fail. Do not be hesitant— This is the time to decide. If you can choose now, You will be victorious. If you do not, You will be defeated. Do not let this opportunity pass— This is the gateway to liberation. If you can enter it, You will be saved. If you do not, You will be lost. Do not be afraid— This is the path of the Buddhas. If you can walk it, You will be safe. If you do not, You will be in danger. Do not turn back— This is the way of the patriarchs. If you can follow it, You will be at home. If you do not, You will be a stranger. Do not be confused— This is the true reality. If you can see it, You will be clear. If you do not, You will be blind. Do not be deluded— This is the ultimate truth. If you can realize it, You will be awakened. If you do not, You will remain asleep. Do not be negligent— This is the work of a bodhisattva. If you can strive for it, You will be diligent. If you do not, You will be lax. Do not be lazy— This is the path of the sages. If you can tread it, You will be noble. If you do not, You will be base. Do not be lowly— This is the height of the Dharma. If you can ascend it, You will be high. If you do not, You will be low. Do not be humble— This is the greatness of the Way. If you can embrace it, You will be vast. If you do not, You will be narrow. Do not be small-minded— This is the breadth of the universe. If you can encompass it, You will be all-pervading. If you do not, You will be limited. Do not be confined— This is the freedom of the mind. If you can be free, You will be liberated. If you do not, You will be bound. Do not be fettered— This is the state of nirvana. If you can attain it, You will be peaceful. If you do not, You will be restless. Do not be troubled— This is the stillness of the heart. If you can rest in it, You will be calm. If you do not, You will be agitated. Do not be disturbed— This is the tranquility of the Dharma. If you can abide in it, You will be serene. If you do not, You will be turbulent. Do not be wavering— This is the stability of the Way. If you can be steady, You will be firm. If you do not, You will be unstable. Do not be fickle— This is the constancy of the mind. If you can be constant, You will be enduring. If you do not, You will be fleeting. Do not be transient— This is the eternity of the Dharma. If you can dwell in it, You will be eternal. If you do not, You will be impermanent. Do not be temporary— This is the permanence of the truth. If you can realize it, You will be timeless. If you do not, You will be subject to time. Do not be bound by time— This is the liberation from birth and death. If you can transcend it, You will be beyond all limits. If you do not, You will remain within them. Do not be confined— This is the vastness of the sky. If you can soar in it, You will be unobstructed. If you do not, You will be hindered. Do not be blocked— This is the openness of the mind. If you can be open, You will be unimpeded. If you do not, You will be obstructed. Do not be hindered— This is the clarity of the Dharma-eye. If you can see clearly, You will be enlightened. If you do not, You will remain in darkness. Do not be obscured— This is the light of the sun. If you can receive it, You will be bright. If you do not, You will be dim. If you do not, You will be shallow. Do not be superficial— This is the bottomless abyss. If you can reach it, You will be bottomless. If you do not, You will be finite. Existence and non-existence, past and present—these are two heavy barriers. For a Zen practitioner with the true eye, it is difficult to pass through them.
If you wish to traverse the Great Road to Chang’an, do not listen to the Kunlun man as he speaks of coming and going. (Touzi Qing)
Bajiao showed the assembly that there is no peer in the world; giving and taking, vertical and horizontal, are not easily intimate. When the rain disperses and the clouds dissolve, where has he gone?
He leaves but empty air, causing the traveler’s tears to soak his kerchief. (Zhengjue Yi)
If you can pick it up before your face, well; if not, I shall snatch it away from behind.
Alas for that thing of jet-black luster—strike it once, and a thousand doors and ten thousand gates shall fly open. (Baoning Yong)
Seizing or relinquishing at the opportune moment, one attains freedom. Upon meeting, one must strictly avoid raising the eyes again. Turning the body, one must surely know the proper timing;
if you hesitate, the mountain staff will reach its end. (The withered tree becomes [the staff]).
The *bājiāo* staff is a matter of giving and taking; one must simply have the eyes alive and alert in the wind.
A single moment of dullness creates a lifetime of separation, and one’s nostrils will be seized and pulled by another. (Fozhi Yu)
Existence and non-existence, giving and taking—how much clamor and confusion! When the staff stands across the path, there is nothing that can be done.
It is better to hold it askew by the side of the meditation chair, so as to avoid letting others climb up its long branches. (Mañjuśrī said.)
At the crossroads, ready-made goods are on display; intending to bargain, one misses the opportunity like a lacquer bucket.
(Jingshan Daokai) [Continued Addition] No trace of unfolding, no mark of unrolling; at midday in a clear sky, a thunderclap rumbles. The patch-robed monks are startled and lose their way;
the wailing of spirits and the weeping of ghosts—how can its limit be known? (Xuedou Zhongyi)
Riding the boat as the waters rise; following the mud to fashion a Buddha. The boat moves and the Buddha is formed; the water and mud are not separate things.
When there is a staff, he gives you a staff; amidst the boat, he lightly strokes the oars. When there is no staff, he takes away the staff; from the Buddha’s face, the marks emerge with artistry.
The skilled hand’s *bāzǎo* eye does not open; from where do they come to block the valleys and fill the ditches?
(Yuedang Chang). Amidst the blazing sunlight, wind, rain, thunder, and hail; the ocean waters flow backward; Mount Sumeru stands overturned; beasts run and birds fly.
Tumbling down from a precipice; a general from beyond the frontier captures him alive. He plucks the whiskers of a fierce tiger and breaks the horn of a blue dragon. (Nantang Xing)
When they scold each other, you have the advantage of catching their beaks; when they spit at each other, you have the advantage of splashing them with water.
To casually touch the head of a snake—clapping hands, "la la li li! (Wan’an Yan).
Bajiao raises his staff, startling the myriad phenomena of the universe; the frog flies across the Brahma Heaven;
the eyebrows have always been above the eyes. (Nirvāṇa-Asaṅga).
In the land of *gǔ*-poison, the water must not be tasted; were even a single drop to touch another, the entire family would perish.
(Kěntáng Chōng). You have more that you must give face-to-face; he does not snatch it away from behind one’s back. Suddenly at midnight, he transforms into a dragon and departs;
black rain and dark winds tear the earth open with thunder. (Xūtáng Yú).
[Added from the Supplementary Collection] Gushan Gui said: "The Fifth Patriarch used the story of the staff to request instruction from Baiyun.

Baiyun said: 'Do you wish to understand? Add a little where there is too much; subtract a little where there is too little. Why is this so? 'The secret instructions of the immortals are not transmitted even between father and son.
Master Baiyun was very much like one who takes a single coin as his capital and makes ten thousand coins his profit."

Little do you realize that it is like a skilled gambler who says, "I am winning today, yet I am poor. The Old Chan Master said: "Add a little where there is much; subtract a little where there is little. Naturally, you will be perfectly suited wherever you go. This method of calculation saves immense effort. Do you all wish to understand this? Thereupon he spoke in verse: A skilled gambler, though winning, says he is poor; The Old Chan Master’s words are truly profound. Add a bit where there is excess; Subtract a bit where there is lack. Naturally, you will be exactly right everywhere. This reckoning is most economical of labor. Do you wish to understand it? Listen well! Listen well! If you can grasp this, you will be free from doubt. If you cannot grasp it, you will remain confused forever. It is not that there is anything lacking; It is simply that you have failed to see it clearly. When the mind is at ease, all things are as they should be; When the mind is unsettled, all things are in disarray. Cease asking about Vimalakīrti lying ill in the city; Mount Luo passes its time in vain. There is no difficulty at all in crossing the shifting sands;
do not listen to the oriole singing in that forest. (Touzi Qing)
One does not ask, two does not rest; one must directly recognize that hook-tip.
Turning back again and again to meet you, one rolls a brocade ball in the heart of a swift current. (Lan’an Xu)
The Seventh Generation after the Sixth Patriarch, Part Three (The First of the Sixth Generation after Qingyuan) (Tianhuang):
Chan Master Shiyuan of Ruiyan in Taizhou (he succeeded Yantou). The Master subsequently resided at Ruiyan in Danchun.
He sat upon a flat rock, appearing like a fool all day long. Every day he would call out, "Master! and when there was a response, he would say, "Stay alert!
In the future, do not let others deceive you. Later, a monk visited Xuansha, and Xuansha asked him:
"Where did he recently pass away? [The monk] replied, "Ruian. The Sandalwood Monk asked, "What words or phrases did he use to instruct his disciples?
The monk recounted the previous conversation. The Sandalwood Monk said, "All are alike in playing with the spirit; it is truly extraordinary. He then asked, "Why did you not remain there?
[The monk] replied, "He has already passed away. The Sandalwood Monk said, "Can he still be called upon to respond now? The monk—
Without opposition. The verse says:
Throughout one's life, one constantly calls out to the "Master. Not subject to deception by others, he stands utterly apart. Where has this present clarity gone today?
The pines and cypresses all over the mountain rise up in a mournful wind. (From Foguo Bai)
A curved new moon gathers three stars; who would believe that the Mind-King is fundamentally at peace?
How laughable is the old abbot of Ruiyan, calling out in the deep night, forcing himself to be alert. (Zuyin Ming)
The house style of Ruiyan: "Call out, Master! Last night on the South Mountain, a tiger bit a great beast.
(Jingshan Gaofeng) One master has died; one master has lived. If you can skillfully manipulate this vital spirit, you will transcend both ends.

(Gushan Gui): Once one has called out to oneself and responded, one becomes alert; not subject to deception, the principle is not slighted. Within the pond, the fragrance of white lotuses has not yet ceased;
before the eaves, the mountain colors are green throughout the four seasons. (Baiyang Shun)
[Continued Collection] Ruìyán constantly calls out, "The Host. He soars forth from the highest peak of Mount Sumeru. The great earth is overturned, yet there is no place to find him;
a single melody of flute and song resounds within the painted pavilion. (Tiānyī Zhé)
Without resorting to staff or shouts, he calls out to the "host. Like a king of geese discerning milk from water, the duck species are not the same.
(High plateau spring). Water washing water, gold exchanging gold; at Ruiyan, the grandmotherly heart is thorough:
carrying his own bottle, he goes to buy village wine, yet puts on his robe and returns as the host. (Amitābha).
Those who study the Way do not recognize the Real, for they have only known the spirit from of old.
The very root of birth and death throughout immeasurable kalpas—fools call this the "original body. (No Gate Opens).
The vast stone platform is shrouded in secret green moss; throughout the day he sits in full lotus posture, his two temples worn thin.
Even if one were never to call out to him, how could one ever have deceived this Master? (Tianmu Li)
A single tune before the wind stirs the sentiment of parting; its ancient melody has no one to join in completing it.
Singing it myself, pouring for myself, and drinking from it, even now I remain unawakened. (Bieshan Zhi)
Chan Master Daoxian of Luoshan in Fuzhou (he was a successor of Yantou). The King of Min invited him to open the hall.
The Master ascended the seat; as he was just gathering up his *saṃghāṭī* robe, he said, "Take care," and immediately descended from the seat.
The King of Min stepped forward, took hold of his hand, and said, "How is this assembly on Vulture Peak any different from today? The Master replied, "I thought you were a layman."

[The *Wudeng Huiyuan* records that the Military Governor of Min, having tasted the flavor of his Dharma, invited him to reside at Luoshan, where he was titled Chan Master Fabao. When he ascended the hall for the opening of the dharma assembly, as soon as he adjusted his robes, he said, "Take care!

At that time the assembly did not disperse; after a long pause, the Master spoke again: "Those who do not yet understand, come forward. A monk stepped out and bowed. The Master raised his voice and said, "How bitter it is! As the monk prepared to ask a question, the Master shouted him out.
This differs slightly from the previously recorded kōan. The Verse says:
Luoshan Renjun could not restrain his impatience; he fully displayed the family style with a single roar.
Though paper and ink were as vast as mountains, the writing could never be exhausted. Monks, do not seek within the meaning. (Dongshan Cong)
Flurries of snowflakes illuminate the heavens of Min; the Ruler of Min rejoices at this encounter, his joy redoubled.
Once the spring breeze blows across the great earth, not a single flake remains before the steps. (Baiyun Yuan).

Upon the seat of Mount Sumeru, he gathers his *kaṣāya*; from the ocean-mouth of his voice, the tide-sound proclaims the Great Capacity. The Great Donor, Lord of the World, is able to discern with clarity;
this auspicious assembly at Vulture Peak shines ever more brightly. (Shushan Ru)

【Continued Collection】A single path straight as a bowstring; for a thousand ages there shall be no peer. Even if one possessed the "biting the arrowhead" mechanism, their skull would be reduced to powder. (Baitang Ya)
The *udumbara* flower appearing in this world is most difficult to behold; its extraordinary fragrance drifts upon the cold morning breeze.
Were it not for the World-Honored One casting his compassionate gaze upon it, it would have been regarded as nothing more than a common flower among the wild weeds. (From *Bǎoyèyuán*)

[Added from the Supplementary Collection] When Luoshan first visited Shishuang, he asked, "What is it like when arising and ceasing never cease? Shishuang replied, "You must become like cold ashes and withered wood;
you must go where a single thought lasts ten thousand years; you must go where the casket covers the universe; you must go where there is pure clarity without a single speck.
The Master did not attain realization. Later, he visited Yantou and presented his previous question. Yantou shouted, "Who is it that arises?"

Extinction. At this, the Master attained great enlightenment. (The *Wudeng Huiyuan* records that he once visited Shishuang and asked: "When going and staying are not at peace, what should one do? Shishuang replied: "You must simply exhaust them completely.")

Zhaoqing spent an entire summer scolding [the Master]. At the end of the summer, he came in person to inquire about the matter; the Master then recounted it clearly for him.

"The venerable elders of all quarters all say they 'receive things and benefit beings. But let me ask you: what about those three kinds of patients—the blind, the deaf, and the mute?"

if you speak with him, his ears do not hear, and his mouth is mute. If you cannot receive him in this way, then the Buddhadharma is entirely devoid of efficacy.
At that time, a monk came forward and said, "Master, regarding the three types of sick people, do you still permit others to deliberate upon this?
The Master said, "I do. "How would you deliberate upon it? the monk asked. The monk then bowed respectfully and departed.

The Master said, "Not so, not so. (Fayan said: "When I saw Master Luohan cite these words of the monk at that time, I immediately understood the three types of sick people. Yunju Xi said: "Is this monk capable or not? If one says..."

[The monk] said, “I understand. Xuan Sha also said, “It is not so. If it were that you do not understand, why did Fa Yan say, “Because of this monk’s words, I have understood the three types of sick people”? Elder, you have no business here; let us discuss this further. Everyone must know this.
A monk took these words and went to seek instruction from Yunmen. Yunmen said, “Prostrate yourself.
When the monk rose from his prostration, Yunmen struck him with his staff. As the monk stepped back, Yunmen said, “It is not that you are blind. He then called to him again.

"Come forward. The monk stepped forward. The Gatekeeper said, "Are you not deaf? The monk replied, "I am not. The Gatekeeper said, "Do you understand? He replied, "I do not. The Gatekeeper said, "Are you not mute?
At these words, the monk attained realization. The verse says: Come forward, come forward; Are you deaf? Are you mute? If you can hear and speak, Why do you still not understand?
Blind, deaf, mute, and speechless; utterly cut off from all worldly expedients. Above heaven and below heaven, there is only that which is laughable and that which is tragic.

Even Li Zhu could not distinguish true colors, and how could Shi Kuang recognize the dark strings? How can these compare to sitting alone beneath a vacant window, where leaves fall and flowers bloom each in their own time?
He further asked: "Do you understand? An unperforated iron hammer. (Xuedou Xian)
Retreating and then approaching, engaging in debate face-to-face; meeting by chance, it is difficult to turn one's face away. A spring breeze suddenly shakes the courtyard before us;
once again, we see tens of thousands of falling petals. (Baiyun Cuan)
The Old Man Yunmen was intimate with his own hands and eyes; he blew on the fire by means of the wind, exhausting no effort of spirit.
The blind could see, and the deaf could hear. Although there were no words, they hung upon his lips. For the three kinds of sick people, there is but one Dharma-gate.

(Fojiàn Qín): "The blind, the deaf, and the mute cannot be reached; Xuánshā has wasted his efforts in vain. Biǎnquè and Lúyī fold their hands and retreat; all three suffer from a terminal illness. (Gūshān Guī): "The blind, the deaf, and the mute cannot be reached;

Xuan Sha’s words on the three types of sick people transcend Yunmen’s “six non-receptions. Do not wait for right and wrong to enter your ears;
those who once knew you well have turned into enemies. (Jingshan Daoyuan)
[Continued Collection: Even those who are temporarily deaf, blind, mute, or afflicted by disease must manifest our school and be verified as true adepts. A vajra cuts through iron like crumbling mud;
the moment one stirs to penetrate the golden [nature], one has lost Xuansha. (Fenyang Shao)

If you wish to know the three kinds of people: their application of principle is ever fresh; there is not even a hair’s breadth of dharma that can act as a defilement for them, whether internal or external. (Yongming Shou)
One, two, three—seeing, hearing, and perceiving—who is it that suddenly dissolves them? Where the flowers cluster, the partridges cry;
