In the midst of it all, half the tree’s fruit has fallen away. (Cuiyan Zhen)
Xuan Sha had three ways of receiving people; these are currently before the eyes and ears of all. Do not fail to open your eyes, lest you wet your bed.
In vain, one might move mountains and block the seas. Amidst the flowers, the secluded bird calls without ceasing; the spring scenery fills the earth—who will buy it? (The Poison-Coated Staff).
Xuan Sha’s three types of sick people: when the principle is present, it does not depend on a loud voice.
This drew forth Old Man Xiangyan, who came to hang himself from a tree. (Longmen Yuan)
Xuansha used poison to expel the poison of others; three types of patients dwell under one roof. How laughable is the old, ancient sage Yunmen!
He loses his coin in the river and searches for it in the river. (Oran’s Verse)
The blind, the deaf, and the mute do not interfere with one another; do not be deceived by Xuansha’s reckless flattery. I shall once more reveal this single phrase for you:
the Old Lord wears a cap of mulberry bark. (Darkness in the chamber, clarity within.)
Deaf, blind, mute, and speechless—caught and defeated! Yet he asks further: "How is it? Deaf, blind, mute, and speechless.
(Yuelin Guan) He employs various expedient means to test the master; who has personally seen Old Xuansha? Deaf ears, mute mouth, and blind eyes.
The sentient beings of the five turbidities are as numerous as hemp seeds. (Hengchuan Gong)

"I bow to you so that I may pay my respects"—he laughs at himself for being illogical. Is it only Old Man Xuansha who is not right? (Juehai Yuan).
"Because of me, you receive my prostration. To fall, he helps one up; to walk, one simply walks;

The Master did not recognize characters; Bodhidharma did not understand Chan. Xuansha never spoke these words;

A sharp sword severs one's own life-root; do not rely on grass or wood for support. If you transmit even a single dharma to another person, you will forever enter the Hell of the Severed Tongue. (Gushan Gui)
"Because of me, you receive my prostrations. Oxherd leads the ox to drink water; on the bank, hoof meets hoof;

Do not nod off while your eyes are open. (Zhaotang strikes once).

Do not let out flatulence or discharge excrement; do not bring trouble upon the people of the world by causing them to mistakenly identify their own nature.

"I do not yet know what your honorable intention is," [the student] asked. The Master said, "In this Sahā world there are four heavy obstructions.

If a person can penetrate through them, I will grant that you have emerged from the realms of the aggregates. Dongchan Qi said, "The Elder of old, having seen through it, said, 'My body and mind are like the great earth and empty space.

Dong said: "If you wish to act as a teacher for humans and devas, there is truly a tiger ahead.

The verse says: A tiger before, a tiger behind— One must look with urgency. A chilling and fierce majesty, With raw and fierce claws and talons. Throughout antiquity and today, woodcutters have never looked back;
How many have lost their bodies and lives? If one looks back, He sits firmly and majestically, blocking the path ahead of the mountain.
(Buddha-Wisdom Spring).
A fierce tiger stands in the path, alone displaying its majesty; its claws and fangs are truly as sharp as awls.
How pitiable are those who perish without realizing it—how deeply tragic to gather up their shattered bones. (Bao-ning Yong)
The Great Compassionate Master of the Patriarchal Abbot’s quarters—your words are truly those of an ancient adept.
With divine light soaring from behind his crown for ten thousand miles, how could he dare frighten the ignorant with birth and death? (Longmen Yuan)
If you wish to recognize Xuansha’s tiger, who is it that beholds him face-to-face? Passing directly through the secure barrier, the entire mechanism transcends Buddhas and patriarchs. (Heshan Fang)
[Continued Collection] "Xuan Sha saw a tiger and said, 'This is you. How many people clearly realize their own nature? Form and sound fill the great void;
yet some still rely on even a hair's breadth of support. (Yongming Shou)
Old Xuansha was far too talkative; face-to-face, he clearly and repeatedly leaked the secret. If a patch-robed monk accepts it at this point, upon examination, he cannot avoid having grit in his eye.
Who can distinguish between one grain of grit and another? A fire breaks out in Silla, burning the feet hot.
(Seal of the Ocean-Print).
Within the mountains there are tigers and men; in the world there are men and tigers. They constantly whet the knives hidden within their smiles; their sharp fangs and claws are terrifying.
I send word to you, O flower-pawed cat: do not let him climb the tree.
(Cishou Shen) There is a tiger ahead; it turns out to be you. What more can be said? Suffering, suffering! (Yuedang Chang)
One day, Xuansha sent a monk to deliver a letter to Master Xuefeng. When Xuefeng opened the seal, he found only three sheets of blank paper.
He asked the monk, "Do you understand? The monk said, "I do not understand. Xuefeng said, "Have you not heard it said that 'gentlemen share the same breeze even a thousand miles apart'?
The monk returned and reported this to Xuansha. Xuansha said, "That old monk has missed the mark."
"I do not know. The verse says:
Thus he sent a messenger with a letter to convey a message from afar; it was not for the sake of the written words, but to reveal his family style. Upon returning, he reported Xuan Sha’s words;
having missed the point despite the clarity, he sealed the principle once more. (Fenyang Zhao)
Xuansha sealed a blank sheet of paper; Old Xue was likewise of the same wind. Those who miss the mark find it hard to understand;
the ancient melody is not the same. (Zhenru Zhe)
Xuansha sealed a blank sheet of paper; Old Xue held up a torch and donned his robe. It turns out he could not read;
in broad daylight he runs about Mount Sumeru. (Yun’gai Zhi)
Xuansha’s elephant bones and owl eyes—on three sheets of white paper, one should simply write them down. Those who share the same breeze from a thousand miles away mostly misunderstand;
a single staff is supported by two people. (Cishou Shen)

Treading over the fishing boat, he inherits his family’s legacy; laughing as he emerges from the reeds, the moon is perfectly full. The earth is vast and heaven is long—a single scroll of three widths;
for whom does he proclaim this shared wind across a thousand miles? (By Fuxincai)
Three sheets of white paper were sent in communication; unfolded across a thousand li, they share the same wind. The "Yangchun" melody turns into the "Huqia" flute song;
it is not that the wind blows in a different tune. (Fóxìng Tái)
[Continued Collection] Three sheets of white paper exchange greetings; a thousand miles away, the wind and moon are the same, filling the boat.
Having seized the lofty banner, he employs it in its entirety; like a coiling snake, he swings a mallet within its mouth. (Danxia Chun)
A blank sheet of paper, sealed and sent to Xuefeng; thus Xuefeng rejoiced in their shared style. In the interim, they missed each other’s point, yet no one recognized it.
After the midday meal, the evening bell tolls at the river city. (Fotuoxun)
A blank sheet of paper rushes forth to ascend Xuefeng; though Xuefeng is a thousand miles away, we share the same wind.
Xuansha’s misstep is difficult for people to comprehend; an iron caldron is not the same as a tea kettle. (Zhenjing Wen)
The partridges and quails cry out together night after night; under the moon, people cannot bear to hear them. They cry until their throats bleed, yet it is of no use;
it would be better to keep one's mouth shut and pass through the remainder of spring. (Wenshu said.)
Three sheets of white paper; a thousand miles share the same breeze. The Master missed the mark; the patch-robed monks lose their way.
The golden sun flies out from the eastern sea-gate. The wind follows the tiger, and the clouds follow the dragon. (By Yunan)
"A thousand li away, we share the same wind; our vision does not differ. When the monk reported these words to Xuansha, [the Master] did not know how he had missed the mark.
Is it that Xuansha missed him? (Hengchuan Gong).

Suddenly kicking it over, he knew to cease; he would no longer travel through the green mountains of the Hundred Yue.
From then on, the moon upon the rivers of the Seven Min has, until this day, shone in vain upon the fishing boat. (By Foguo Bai)
Xie Sanlang on his fishing boat kicks over Mount Sumeru and returns to his native land.
He must surely laugh at the traveler who has not yet returned, lingering and lodging as a sojourner in a foreign realm. (Benjue I)
Before he had even left Mindi, he was already back home; no sooner had he mounted his flying vulture than his eyes grew dim.
How laughable that Master Zeng was yet more heartless, letting go lightly with his black staff—Old Xuansha! (Duan’an Yan)
[Supplementary Addition] When Xuansha traveled south to Putian County, the local officials staged a hundred performances of acrobatics and theatrical entertainment to welcome him.
The following day, the Master asked the Elder Xiaotang, "Where did all that commotion go yesterday? Xiaotang lifted a corner of his patched robe.
The Master said, "I suspect this has nothing to do with it. Fayen offered a different interpretation, saying, "Yesterday there was much..."
[The Master] slightly cleared the clamor. Faldeng said separately: "Today it is even more laughable. He spoke in verse:

"A boat hidden in a night ravine, A paddle placed upon a clear source. Fish and dragons do not yet know that water is their life; Yet a broken chopstick need not hinder one from stirring it for a moment.
Master Xuansha, Old Tang, the lid meeting the box, the arrowhead and the point, the probing pole and the shadow-grass—[all these] are but the old man’s retraction and concealment.
The tortoise nests in the lotus; this is but playful sport. The multicolored scales play among the algae.
(Tiantong Jue) Today is silent and solemn; yesterday was noisy and clamorous. When the wind ceases, the flowers still fall; where the birds cry, the mountains grow more secluded.
(Bei Jian Jian): A person in front raises the corner of his *kāṣāya*. How laughable that he groundlessly reveals his ugliness! These two elders’ *fengliu* (wind-and-water style) flows from the house;
they have not yet clarified that one further point above. (Wu Ji Pai).
[Added for inclusion] Xuansha asked Jingqing, "The scriptures state that for a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva, not seeing a single dharma is a great fault.
Now tell me, what dharma do they not see? Jingqing pointed to a pillar and said, "Is it that you do not see this dharma?
(Tongan Xian remarked aside: "I know the Master does not act rashly. The Master said, "Clear water and white sand in Zhejiang."
"Rice comes from you eating it; the Buddha-dharma has not yet been encountered. (Xuánjué said: "Tell me, when Xuánshā spoke thus, what was his intention?

Have you not seen the monk ask Dōngshān, 'Not seeing a single dharma is a great error'—what does this mean? Dōngshān said, 'Not seeing a single dharma is a fine saying. Zhàngzǔ Yīxiùjué said, 'Not seeing a single dharma is the Tathāgata; only then can one be named Avalokiteśvara.
Bodhisattva Samantabhadra also said, 'Not seeing a single dharma is a great error. Which one is right and which one is wrong? Try to judge for me!"). Verse:
It is said:
"Old Master Xue’s lineage is lofty and his progeny flourish; moreover, he is deeply affectionate toward the noble bonds of kinship.
Though his management of the household affairs resembles that of others, there is one who, craving the cup, has fallen into the weeds (Xutang Yu)."
Secret mechanisms are deeply laid as traps; sharp blades swiftly clash in combat. No one recognizes the horses sweating with toil;
yet their epoch-making merit is recounted anew. (Dong-sou Ying)

Xuan Sha was once asked by Jingqing: "A student has newly entered the monastic community; I beg the Master to point out a path of entry. The Master said: "Do you hear the sound of the Yanxi stream? He replied: "I do. The Master said: "That is your point of entry" (the *Wudeng Huiyuan* reads: the Master said, "Enter from here"). The verse says: The sound of the stream at Yanxi— From this very place, one enters. If you can hear it with your own ears, Then you have found the gate. If you cannot yet hear it, How will you ever enter? It is not that there is no way in; It is simply that you yourself lack the means. If you wish to know the path of entry, Listen to the sound of the flowing water. If you can hear it, you have already entered; If you cannot hear it, you have never been outside. From here, people have their heads and feet all soaked; though they manage to pass through the throat, they cannot avoid a fit of gasping distress.
The wind whistles and the waves drift on; from where does the pure breeze arise? The person is in a wooden luan boat. (Fohuiquan)

A single drop of the Yan River water—few in the four seas have heard of it. Even if one were to attain profound realization of it, it would still be nothing more than playing with one’s own spirit. (Fayun Xiu)
Heaven-born son of Kunlun with azure eyes, possessing arts that surpass others yet remaining unaware of them himself. How many times the black winds have overturned the great ocean;
amidst the waves he emerges and submerges, sporting at ease. (Baiyun Yuan).

The wind scatters a thousand peaks of shattered jade snow; the rain drops upon the cliff flowers, bringing spring to the ten thousand nations. One can listen to the intent of the flowing waters at Yanxi:
their murmuring continues all day long, yet one hears it as if not hearing it at all. (Luo Han Nan)
In his final years, Xuansha entrusted [the Dharma] to Jingqing; turning the hearing inward, he came to listen to the sound of the river at Yanxi.
Now that the Canglang River remains for washing one’s ears, who would be willing to come to the stream and wash their cap-strings? (Min Gufo).
Flowing on without question or explanation, it is simply because it is too intimate. Who has ever heard it together? Mountains and rivers all leak it forth at once. (Chu’an Fang)
[Continued Collection] Xuansha’s pointing was profoundly deep; to draw the line, one must rely on an inch-long needle.
Whether you hear or do not hear the words spoken outside the gate, I urge you not to seek it at Yanxi. (Wenshu said).
Heaven and earth stand alone; enter from this very place. The wind cannot touch it; the rain cannot wet it.
(Yuelin Guan) A stream of cold spring water flows down into the emerald mists. Xuan Sha brought it forth as the true mechanism.
Although Jingqing entered through hearing, how could flowing water ever wash away right and wrong? (Tieshan Ren)

[Added from the Supplementary Collection] Once, while Xuansha was in the midst of his formal meditation session, he heard the sound of a swallow and said, "He speaks deeply of the true reality (*dharmatā*) and skillfully expounds the essential teachings.

He then descended from his seat. At that time, a monk requested further instruction, saying, "I do not understand. The Master replied, "Go! Who would believe you? The verse says: The swallow’s cry is the profound Dharma; Xuansha’s words are the ultimate truth. Who can fathom the depths of this mystery? Only one who has personally realized it knows.

The purple swallow flies in, circling the painted beams; Deeply discussing the true nature (*dharmatā*), its resonance flows on and on. A thousand words and ten thousand phrases—no one understands them;
It follows the warbling oriole over the low wall once more. (Benjue I)

In my humble official service, I have hurried north and south; for long I have pined for the dust of the traveler’s road. Amidst the misty rain and smoke, I deeply recall the spring of my old garden. (By Yan Shouhui)
Killing and living race against one another; not shared by the thousand sages. To save the eyebrows, one loses the nostrils. (Kōsoku In). [Added from other sources:
Once a monk asked Xuansha, "What is the student’s own self? The Master said, "Why do you use your own self?
(Another version says, "This is your own self. Yunmen said, "A person of immeasurable capacity has been turned around by the flow of words."

A monk asked, "What is the student's own self? The Gatekeeper said, "Suddenly, if someone on the road calls out, 'Monk, come to the vegetarian feast,' you too will receive a meal according to your lot.
The Verse says: Suddenly, on the road, someone calls out, "Monk, come to the vegetarian feast! You too, according to your lot, Receive a meal to eat.
It is you yourself. Do not be so dull-witted as to miss the point. Groups of two or three patch-robed monks merely say, "Sleep early and rise late" (Dazhong Long).
Xuan Sha is ahead of the donkey; Yun Men is behind the horse. If you ask further how it is, shut the dog’s mouth.
(Xue’an Jin). Once, when a monk asked Xuan Sha, “What is the pure Dharma-body? the Master said, “Dripping pus.”
The verse says:
"Every drop is a body of festering pus; On the fishing boat, the family style is revealed.
People look only at the fishing line, Failing to see the reeds facing the red smartweed. (Tianyi Hui)
Drops of pus, golden light streaming; the entire Dharma-body revealed, majestic and grand. On the banks of the Jiaolu River he once manifested transformation;
a single-leafed fishing boat drifts upon the vast and boundless. (Yang Wuwai)
The pure Dharma-body is beyond compare; yet after illness, it still drips with pus as before. Swallows and wild geese cry out until autumn light fades;
fallen leaves drift down, all the same shade of red. (Lan’an Shu)
Drops and drips—his entire body is festering pus. Not a single drop falls to the east or west.
If one says this is not for those who know the sound, they cannot avoid being caught by the wind blowing through a different tune. (Gao Feng Miao)
[Added from the *Zuochan Sanmei Jing*] Once, while a monk was attending him, Xuansha pointed with his staff at a small white spot on the ground before him and asked, "Do you see it?
The monk replied, "I see it. The Master asked this three times, and the monk said, "I see it," three times as well. The Master said:
"You see it and I see it as well. Why do you say that one does not see it? The verse says: You see it, I see it; it is fully manifest.
Only after breaking through the thorny forest Does one know there is no front or back. Let this single point penetrate from ancient times to the present.
Before black and white were yet distinguished, where could one discern it? [Blank] [Blank] [Blank]
Xuansha was once asked by a monk, "What is the matter that is most intimate? The Master said, "I am Xie Sanlang. The Verse says:
Originally a guest on a fishing boat, By chance I shaved my hair and beard and donned the kashaya. Within the rank of the Buddhas and Patriarchs, I am not left behind.
Abiding. Night falls and, as before, one lodges among the reeds (Xuédòu Xiǎn).
Personally extending the definitive inquiry, he asks you: Do not compare this to the transmission from Liúshā to Shàoshī.
Last night the wild geese returned behind the twin ridges; the Xiè family stood before the bright moon (Tóuzǐ Qīng).

The mountains of Min and the waves of the Cang River stretch on and on. Father and son make their living upon a single fishing boat. Suddenly, it capsizes; in this profound shock, one awakens to realization.
Everyone gather up the gear; come and go, let there be rest. (Cao Tang Qing).
In this season of late autumn, the realm of water and clouds; a thousand acres of reeds have not yet been touched by frost.
The river scenery is not sold in fragments; it is bestowed all at once upon Xie Sanlang. (Zuyin Ming)
[Continued Collection] Whispering reeds reflect the flowing river; A lone oar and solitary sail drift upon a small boat. I pay no heed to the fine rain and slanting wind;
My single mind rests only at the tip of the fishing rod. (By Xiaowenkān)
[Added to the Collection] Xuansha addressed the assembly, saying: "If we discuss this matter, it is like a plot of land.
The four boundaries have been demarcated and the contract signed; it has already been sold to everyone. Only the tree in the center still belongs to this old monk. The verse says:
"Ten thousand matters depend on Master Wang; the tree is not yet yours. The broad-faced butcher became a Buddha;
the Great Master of the Second Patriarch paid his debts. (Gushan Gui)
The grandfather’s fields and gardens have all been sold; the boundaries on all four sides have not been preserved.
Alas, because there remains the tree in the center, the vexation of the spring breeze has not ceased at last. (Jingshan Gaofeng)
The grandfather’s fields and gardens all belong to me; how could the trees within them have belonged to another?
I shall uproot them along with their branches, leaves, and roots—to see if my descendants possess such noble spirit. (Duan’an Yan)
Xuan Sha once pointed to the pass above; the Chan practitioners of the four seas have not yet awakened to its leisure.
Only the Son of Heaven of the Han Dynasty was noble; at Pengcheng’s Gai, the signal flags returned. (Jiangshan Ai)

[Added from the Supplementary Collection] Xuansha said: "Before the face of a deceased monk is precisely the *bodhi* encountered at every glance; it is the divine light ten thousand miles away, the mark behind the crown. The verse says:
Among those on the ridges, Xuansha is most extraordinary; his "hanging words" are not easily matched by any quarter.
To test the true mind before a deceased monk, later followers must examine them closely without evasion. (Shimen Cong)
Although the deceased monk is not truly "deceased," since the Way of Bodhi is naturally penetrating, if you further deliberate and analyze through dualistic paths,
you will not only lack understanding but will also be deaf (Bānruòróu).
Among them, none is more direct than Xuansha: "Every sight is entirely true; the words are not far-fetched. Before the deceased, one personally attests to it;
there is no partiality and no further entanglement. The monastic communities are vast and their debates endless, like grasping at illusory flowers in empty space. (Fenyang Shanzhao)
[Supplement] Tianyi Huai said: "Setting aside for a moment the case of the deceased monk, what exactly is that which is behind a living person? The verse says:
Setting aside for a moment the matters before the deceased monk, how does one encounter them behind the living?
Since the Cloud South country was first shattered, it has reached all the way to the North of the Passes until now. (Benjue 1)

[Added for inclusion] Xuansha said: "The divine light ten thousand miles away is the mark behind the head; when the head has vanished, where can one look? The matter is accomplished and the intention has ceased; this trace of arrival pervades every place.

The wise, upon hearing this briefly, should extract it with vigor; do not wait until in an instant you have lost your head. The Verse says: The divine light shines ten thousand miles beyond the head; When the head has sunk, where can one seek it? The task is done and the purpose fulfilled; This trace of arrival is present everywhere.
The wise, having heard this but a moment, Should grasp it with sudden force; Do not wait until in an instant You lose your head.
Divine light shines from behind his crown, illuminating the boundless. How could the narrow confines of ten thousand *li* suffice to describe it?
If you ask for the essential meaning of Xuansha’s intent: the skull is cold at midnight under a frosty sky. (Benjue I)

[Added from the Supplementary Collection] Once Xuansha visited the Hermitage Master of Three Pecks. As soon as they met, the master said, "Do not be offended that, having lived in the mountains for so long, I have no sitting mat.

The Master [Xuansha] said, "Everyone has one; why does the hermitage master not? He replied, "Sit down first and drink some tea. The Master said, "So it turns out the hermitage master does indeed have one. The Verse says: The sitting mat is spread out before the eyes— Who would dare to doubt it?

If you do not see it yourself, How can you avoid being deceived by others? When the wind blows, the grass bends; When the wind ceases, the grass stands upright. If you wish to know its true form, Look at the mountain peaks and the river currents.
The paths leading to and from Bang-an intersect; at every step, one follows the tracks left behind. The mountains are remote and the years have passed long since anyone has arrived;
a stream flows through, nourishing the tall pines. (Suan Cong)
[Added from another collection: When Xuansha saw Gushan approaching, he drew a circle. Gushan said, "No one can get out of this.
The Master said, "I knew you would be making your living in the womb of a donkey or a horse. Gushan asked, "And what about you, Preceptor?
The Master said, "No one can get out of this. Gushan said, "If that is how you act, Preceptor..."
"You have spoken it. Why have I not been able to speak it? The Master said, "I have attained it;
you have not. He spoke in verse:
"The author seeks well the medicine for the unailing; Where could it be placed within a horse's belly or a donkey's womb? On that day at Gushan, how pitiable!"
Born! His nostrils were plucked away by someone (Original Awakening One).
[Added from another source] Xuansha saw three newly arrived monks; he himself struck the work-call drum three times and was about to return to his quarters.
Once the newcomer has completed the formal observances (*vidhi*), he likewise strikes the *pingsong* drum three times. He then enters the Sangha hall.
A long-resident monk reports, "The newcomer has slighted the Master. The Master says, "Strike the bell to assemble the community for an investigation.
When the assembly has gathered, the newcomer does not attend. The Master orders an attendant to go and summon him; as soon as the newcomer comes out—
In the Dharma Hall, [the Master] patted the back of his attendant and said, "The Master calls for you.
When the attendant reached the Master’s quarters, the newly arrived monk returned to the hall. The long-resident monk then asked, "Why did the Master not examine the newcomer?
The Master replied, "I have already examined you. Mostan Yin remarked, "What a pity he let him off so easily!"
This monk then offered this verse:
"Xuan Sha clearly repairs the mountain path; the newly arrived secretly passes through Chen Cang. Traveling by night, they do not meet; at dawn, they reach Xianyang together.
Strict commands and regulations are enforced; clearly, the four seas are as clear as a mirror. What more could there be?"
Seeking the Boundaries of Abiding.
*The Comprehensive Collection of Linked Verses on the Ancient Cases of the Chan School*, Scroll Thirty-one;
*The Comprehensive Collection of Linked Verses on the Ancient Cases of the Chan School*, Scroll Thirty-two.
Compiled by the Śramaṇa Faying of Ba’en Guangxiao Chan Monastery in Chizhou, Song Dynasty;
continued by the Śramaṇa Puhui of Tianyi Wanshou Chan Monastery during the Shaoxing era of the Yuan Dynasty. *Ancestors’ Occasions for Inquiry* (Zushi Jiyuan).
The Fourth of the Seventh Generation after the Sixth Patriarch (The Second of the Sixth Generation after Qingyuan):
Chan Master Changqing Huileng of Fuzhou (who succeeded Xuefeng). While traveling in the mountains with Baofu, Baofu asked:
An ancient said, "At the summit of Mount Miaofeng, do not immediately grasp this; is it even so?
The Master said, "It is indeed so, yet it is a great pity. A monk asked Gushan, "As for Master Ling’s saying such a thing..."
"What do you think? Shanshan said, "If Master Sun had not spoken these words, it could be said that skulls would cover the wilds and bleached bones would stretch across the mountains. The verse says:
Because he ascended the high and magnificent [peak] to its very summit, the monk’s inquiry was already fully resolved. This is indeed most regrettable;
I only fear that, though sharing the same voice, we shall wander in different places. (Fenyang Zhao)
On the solitary peak of Wondrous Summit, the grass grows lush and thick. Picking it up with clarity, to whom could it be entrusted?
Were it not for Sūn Gōng, who discerned the essential point, how many would know that the skull has fallen to the ground? (Xuědòu Xiǎn)
Eighty-four thousand, not just one by one; within the Seven Golden Mountains, the seas flow on and on. The summit of Mount Sumeru is as level as the palm of a hand.
Who holds the long pole to fish for the giant turtle? (Cao Tang Qing).
Holding hands and walking together, with whom do we travel? Before our eyes, we see only Mount Sumeru. Clouds and mud do not obstruct the path of our coming;
entrust it to your descendants to behold wherever they may go. (Fuxincai)

[Continued Collection] Biting the steel points and clashing in combat—this is the work of a master. Not failing to respond to these inquiries that have come. Knowing the time and season to act according to circumstances;
what a pity this person turns instead to sighing in lamentation. (By Prajñā-róu).
This very thing is indeed most regrettable; to direct the mind toward it is already to travel three thousand miles.
The traveler pines for the road, the guest longs for home; Bodhidharma carries a single sandal upon his staff. (Daitang Ding)
Suddenly ascending the solitary peak of Mount Sumeru, the vast expanse is windless yet the waves run deep.
Aside from Jingqing and Changqing, who else at this moment could truly be a connoisseur? (Bao Ye Yuan)

How could the mountain of the power of vows be worth boasting of? Hidden bodies and exposed shadows are as numerous as hemp seeds.
Were it not for Baofu having personally seen them, who would believe that Master Ling further scatters sand? (Bao Ye Yuan)

[Added from the Supplement] Changqing said, "If everyone were like today, the Old Barbarian would have hope. Baofu said, "If everyone were like today, the Old Barbarian would be hopeless. The verse says: If everyone were like today, the Old Barbarian would have hope; If everyone were like today, the Old Barbarian would be hopeless. The ancient path is not far away; It is right here before one's feet.
If you can see it clearly, Then you will know what is meant by "the Old Barbarian."
The heavens are high as wild geese soar into the clouds; the earth is solemn as crickets and grasshoppers cry out as they enter the weeds.
It is entirely within the landscape of autumn, while the traveler’s sorrows follow the sentiments of a foreign land. (Dong-sou Ying)
[Added for inclusion] Changqing ascended the hall and said: "If you encounter a fellow traveler on the path and pass each other shoulder-to-shoulder, the task of a lifetime of study is finished.
He then offered this verse:
Meeting by chance on the road, we pass each other arm-in-arm; Lift up your eyebrows—do not let the moment slip away! Throughout your life’s study, what have you clarified?
Matters: Once awakened, how could they be dissolved in even a single kṣaṇa?
(One Original Awakening). [Added from another source: When a monk asked Changqing, "How can one attain freedom from doubt and delusion? the Master simply extended both hands.
The monk did not offer a word in reply. The Master said, "Ask me again, and I will tell you. When the monk asked again, the Master sat with his arms bared.
The monk bowed; the Master asked, "How do you understand this? The monk replied, "Today the wind has risen."
The Master said, "To speak in such a manner shows you have not yet settled your understanding.

What essential point do you have regarding the past and present that could equal Changqing? If you can bring it forth, I will allow you to be the master of this discourse. The monk merely stood there.
The Master then asked, "What kind of person are you? He replied, "A man from the north. The Master said, "North and south..."
"Three thousand *li* away, why do you study false speech? The monk had no reply. The verse says:
When the hand is extended, ten-thousand-fathom cliffs crumble; In the dried-up river there is no water, and the moon does not come.
If you have doubts, ask Páng Jùshī another time: Who accompanies the stone woman at Huangméi? (Tíuzǐ Qīng)

[Added from the Supplementary Collection] A monk asked Changqing, "When there is a question and there is an answer, the roles of guest and host are clearly defined. But when there is neither question nor answer, what then?
The Master said, "Everyone they meet says they have retired from office; yet among the trees, not a single person has ever been seen."
The Verse says:
Everyone says my mind has found rest; But when questioned, where has it ever been? To speak with one’s mouth while the heart disagrees is to deceive oneself;
In the swift current of karma, one drifts along at its mercy. (Zhimen Zu)

[Added for inclusion] Changqing was once asked by a monk: "When many hands sift through gold, who is it that obtains it? The Master said, "Those with skill obtain it. The monk asked, "Does this student obtain it as well? The Master said, "It is still very far off. The Verse says: When many hands sift through the gold, Who is it that obtains it?

If you have skill, you shall find it; But if you lack it, you will not. Even if you ask, "Do I obtain it too? The Master replies, "It is still very far off. How could one ever grasp it with the mind? Only when the mind is exhausted is there attainment. If you wish to know the true meaning, Look at the golden light upon the mountain peak.
Among the many hands sifting for gold, who is it that finds any? How could a speck of dust or a single obstruction possibly hinder them?
The vast waves stretch far and wide, yet the gold remains distant; with the four requisites unfulfilled, they return empty-handed. (Zhimen Zu)
When many hands sift for gold, who can obtain it? Only those with skillful artistry can surely succeed. The Prince of Sui obtained the pearl, as heard in the west of the capital;
Bian He presented the jade, located in the north of the river. (Zantang Zhun)
Chan Master Congzhan Baofu of Zhangzhou (a successor of Xuefeng). Changqing said:
"It would be better to say that Arhats possess the three poisons than to say that the Tathāgata has two kinds of speech; yet it is not that the Tathāgata has no speech."
"However, there are only two kinds of speech. The Master asked, "What is the Tathāgata’s speech?
He replied, "How could a deaf person hear it? The Master said, "I knew well that you would speak from the second head.
Qing then asked, "What is the Tathāgata’s speech? The Master said, "Go drink tea. Yunju Xi said, "Where..."

This is where Changqing speaks from the second head. The verse says: The heads are the first and the second; The sleeping dragon does not look into still water. Where there is no place, the moon appears and the waves are clear;

Where there is a place, the wind rises and the waves surge. Leng Chan-guest, Leng Chan-guest! For three months at the Dragon Gate, you shall suffer the humiliation of having your snout struck. (Xuedou Xian)
The Tathāgata’s words are raised for you, yet even a deaf person can hear them. You have not yet escaped mixing mud with soil;
even drinking tea at Baofu is foolishness. It is like beating a cloth drum at Leimen. (Fohuiquan)
The Tathāgata does not speak with two kinds of words. Three times three makes nine; one must count them repeatedly. What deaf person could possibly hear this?
A fox-fur cloak cannot avoid eventually changing its master. (Baizhang Yuanwen).
Neither right nor wrong, all returns to the grasp; having heard or seen, one is separated by mountains and passes.
Only then does one know that this kind of Tathāgata’s speech does not lie within the realm of human sentiment or intellectual understanding. (Fojian Qin)
The first head, the second head—clear breezes and bright moon, both lingering on and on. Where now are the general’s warhorses?
Wild grasses and idle flowers fill the earth with sorrow. (Nan-hua Bing)
[Continued Collection] Bumping against walls and crashing into barriers; the crooked does not conceal the straight. Plucking leaves and picking flowers; better frugality than luxury.
An Arhat possesses the three poisons; a Tathāgata has two words. How can a deaf person hope to hear?
As before, "Go drink tea. Old Baofu, old Baofu! Even iron eyes and copper pupils have been lost. (Yuedang Chang)
"Simply go and drink tea. Do you know the second head? Pity the old Changqing; he has needlessly stirred up a storm of grief. (Bao Ye Yuan)
Baofu once cited Xuefeng’s ascent to the hall, where he said: "Venerable elders, I have already met you at Wangzhou Pavilion;
I have already met you at Wushan Ridge; I have already met you before the Sangha Hall.
Baofu raised this to ask Geyu: "Setting aside for a moment the meeting before the Sangha Hall, as for Wangzhou..."
At the state pavilion on Wushan Ridge, where do they meet? Guo Hu takes long strides back to the abbot’s quarters;
the Master bows his head and enters the monks’ hall. The verse says:
Wangzhou, Wushi, and Tangqian— They meet and encounter one another in myriads.
Only Ehu and Baofu— At this moment, their meeting allows for shifting and changing. (Fenyang Zhao)
At Wangzhou and Wushi, we constantly meet; why then, O Zen practitioner, do you turn your back?
Though Baofu and Ehu attained their intent, they buried their weapons and never unfurled their banners. (Haixin Xin)
Climbing mountains and crossing waters—how trivial! Meeting by chance, he specifically asks the way. How laughable is the scholar Mr.
Pan of Mount Hua, Riding his donkey backward on the road to Chang’an. (Da-hong Sui)
Dense and profound, majestic and grand—already two or three [generations] have passed. Originally there is nothing; what more could one desire? When the deluded see this, they give rise to joy;
when the true author meets them, his face is full of shame. (Longmen Yuan)
Wangzhou’s Wushan and the Sangha Hall—vulgar consciousness vast and boundless, impossible to withstand.
When the monk’s staff is raised, the five lakes and four seas boil like hot water. (Jingshan Gaofeng)

[Continued Collection] A lotus fiber draws in the whale and the turtle; a needle-point rolls as a mustard seed is cast. At Wanzhou and Wushan Ridge, before the song is even sung, the response has already been given.
The Great Tang beats the drum and Silla dances; face-to-face presentation, yet not seen. (Yuánwù Qín).
Facing Wanzhou and Wushan before the Sangha Hall, he strides swiftly with head bowed, separated by a great thousandfold world-system.
If one is a cub of the man-eating lion, one turns back and does not remain upon the tips of the blades of grass. (One Old Man, as it were).
[Added for inclusion] Baofu was once asked by a monk: "Throughout his life, what words or phrases did Xuefeng have that could be compared to 'the wild goat hanging from a horn'?

The Master said, "I cannot fail to be a disciple of Xuefeng. The Verse says: The wild goat hangs from the horn; The tracks of the bird are lost in the void. If you wish to know the meaning of this, Look at the face of the old man.
Habituated to acting in front of others; subtract three and add nine. Though possessing eyes, one has never looked; having no home, one can run of one’s own accord.
These words of Xuefeng are like a wild goat hanging from a branch—there is no reason for you to become his disciple.
Observe the strategies on the battlefield of dragons and snakes. (Yuedang Chang)
Xuefeng, I wonder what words he spoke that could compare to the time when a wild sheep hangs its horns from a tree?
When struck, all naturally dance in harmony; there is no need for a Qiang flute to blow through the clouds. (Xu Tang Yu)
[Added for inclusion] Baofu asked a monk, "What is that in the hall? The monk replied, "Wait until the Master has made a definitive judgment.
The Master said, "Śākyamuni Buddha. The monk said, "Master, do not deceive people. The Master said, "In fact, it is you who are deceiving me.

Who would have known there is not a single drop? (Wuzu Fan)
[Added from another source] One day, Jingqing struck the bell himself in front of the Sangha Hall and said, "Xuan Sha has spoken the bottom; Xuan Sha has spoken the bottom.
A monk asked, "What did Xuan Sha say? The Master drew a circle. The monk said, "If you had not practiced for a long time, how would you know it was like this?
The Master said, "Losing money and then suffering punishment" (the *Zongmen Tongyao* reads: "The Master said, 'Return me the price for my straw sandals'").
Xuedou said, "In the end, Caizhou was broken. Yuanwu said, "There is a hard thorn in the soft mud.
The verse says: Jingqing cast a single bait into the heart of the lake;
A scaled dragon leaped from the waves onto the hook. He nearly snapped the line at the tip of the pole.

A line. It draws the onlookers down to the fishing platform. (Moon over Shixi). [Added from another collection. Jingqing asked Xuefeng: "The ancients have said... Xuefeng then lay down flat on his back. After a long while, he rose and said, "What were you asking? The Master asked again. Xuefeng said, "A fellow who lives in vain and dies in vain. Verse: The fishing line is cast; The hook descends into the deep. The moon shines upon Shixi; The wind blows across the river. Jingqing’s question was like a clear mirror; Xuefeng’s answer was like a vast expanse. One who asks again is already lost; One who answers once more is a fool. To live in vain and die in vain— How many such people are there? If you can discern this at once, You will see the ancient path clearly revealed. If you cannot yet comprehend it, You must look within your own heart. Do not seek it elsewhere; It is right here before you. If you can understand this, You will know that the ancients were not deceiving you. If you do not understand, You will surely fall into the pit of delusion. Do not wait for the spring breeze to blow; Do not wait for the autumn moon to rise. Right now, in this very moment, You must realize it for yourself. If you can realize it, Then you are a true person of the Way. If you cannot realize it, You are merely a ghost haunting the mountains and rivers. Do not doubt this; It is the ultimate truth. If you can understand this, You will see that the Buddhas and patriarchs are all within you. If you do not understand, You will wander in birth and death forevermore. Do not hesitate; Resolve your mind now. If you can resolve your mind, You will attain liberation. If you cannot resolve your mind, You will remain bound by delusion. This is the essential teaching; Do not let it pass in vain. If you can grasp it, You will see the source of the Way. If you cannot grasp it, You will miss the opportunity of a lifetime. Do not look outward; Look inward with clarity. If you look inward with clarity, You will see the light of the Dharma. If you see the light of the Dharma, You will realize the nature of reality. This is the true transmission; Do not treat it lightly. If you treat it lightly, You will lose the precious jewel. Do not seek it in books; Seek it in your own experience. If you seek it in your own experience, You will find the true teacher. If you find the true teacher, You will receive the true Dharma. This is the final word; There is nothing more to say. If you can hear this, You will be free from all doubt. If you cannot hear this, You will remain in the dark. Do not wait for tomorrow; Realize it today. If you realize it today, You will transcend birth and death. If you transcend birth and death, You will be a Buddha. This is the ultimate goal; Do not seek anything else. If you seek anything else, You will wander in confusion. Do not doubt the ancients; Trust in their wisdom. If you trust in their wisdom, You will attain enlightenment. If you attain enlightenment, You will benefit all beings. This is the great compassion; Do not neglect it. If you neglect it, You will suffer in the three realms. Do not fear the path; Walk it with courage. If you walk it with courage, You will reach the destination. If you reach the destination, You will be at peace. This is the true liberation; Do not seek outside of yourself. If you seek outside of yourself, You will never find it. Do not look for it in the sky; Look for it in the earth. If you look for it in the earth, You will find the foundation of reality. If you find the foundation of reality, You will dwell in the Dharma-realm. This is the eternal abode; Do not leave it. If you leave it, You will fall back into delusion. Do not forget this teaching; Hold it fast in your heart. If you hold it fast in your heart, You will never be separated from the Buddha. This is the true lineage; Do not break it. If you break it, You will sever the thread of the Dharma. Do not be heedless; Be mindful at all times. If you are mindful at all times, You will be protected by the Buddhas. If you are protected by the Buddhas, You will be safe from all harm. This is the supreme protection; Do not disregard it. If you disregard it, You will invite calamity. Do not seek fame or profit; Seek only the Way. If you seek only the Way, You will attain the fruit of Buddhahood. This is the ultimate attainment; Do not seek anything else. If you seek anything else, You will stray from the path. Do not be distracted; Focus your mind. If you focus your mind, You will see the truth. If you see the truth, You will be liberated. This is the final instruction; Do not doubt it. If you doubt it, You will remain in bondage. Do not seek it in words; Seek it in silence. If you seek it in silence, You will hear the sound of the Dharma. If you hear the sound of the Dharma, You will understand the meaning. This is the true meaning; Do not misunderstand it. If you misunderstand it, You will create obstacles for yourself. Do not be arrogant; Be humble and sincere. If you are humble and sincere, You will receive the grace of the Buddhas. If you receive the grace of the Buddhas, You will be able to help others. This is the true purpose; Do not forget it. If you forget it, You will lose the benefit of your practice. Do not be lazy; Exert yourself. If you exert yourself, You will achieve success. If you achieve success, You will fulfill your vow. This is the fulfillment of the vow; Do not abandon it. If you abandon it, You will fail in your mission. Do not be discouraged; Remain steadfast. If you remain steadfast, You will overcome all difficulties. If you overcome all difficulties, You will reach the end of the path. This is the end of the path; Do not turn back. If you turn back, You will regress in your practice. Do not seek the easy way; Follow the difficult path. If you follow the difficult path, You will attain the ultimate truth. If you attain the ultimate truth, You will be a true Bodhisattva. This is the true Bodhisattva path; Do not deviate from it. If you deviate from it, You will fall into the ranks of the common. Do not seek worldly gain; Seek only spiritual awakening. If you seek only spiritual awakening, You will be free from all attachments. If you are free from all attachments, You will be at peace in all circumstances. This is the peace of the Dharma; Do not lose it. If you lose it, You will be tossed about by the winds of passion. Do not be distracted by appearances; See through them all. If you see through them all, You will see the empty nature of things. If you see the empty nature of things, You will be liberated from all views. This is the liberation from all views; Do not cling to them. If you cling to them, You will be bound by your own delusions. Do not seek the truth in the past; Seek it in the present. If you seek it in the present, You will find it right here. If you find it right here, You will be enlightened. This is the moment of enlightenment; Do not miss it. If you miss it, You will waste this precious life. Do not be afraid of death; Death is the gateway to liberation. If you view death as the gateway to liberation, You will be free from all fear. If you are free from all fear, You will be a true hero. This is the true heroism; Do not imitate it. If you imitate it, You will be a false hero. Do not seek the truth in the future; Seek it in the here and now. If you seek it in the here and now, You will realize the eternal truth. If you realize the eternal truth, You will be one with the Buddhas. This is the oneness with the Buddhas; Do not separate from it. If you separate from it, You will be alienated from the Dharma
Ordinarily, one loves guests and regrets their absence; yet when they arrive, one is too lazy to converse with them. Lying empty-handed, one realizes too late that sleep was not properly taken;
all toil has been in vain as the red flames fall into cold ashes. (Touzi Qing)
[Added from the Supplement] Once, a monk asked Jingqing, "Is there still Buddha-dharma at the beginning of the new year? The Master said, "There is.
The monk asked, "What is the Buddha-dharma of the new year? The Master said, "The first day of the new year inaugurates the reign; all things are renewed."
[The monk] said, "I thank the Master for his reply. The Master said, "Today Jingqing has suffered a loss.
The Verse says: A cup of seven jewels filled with grape wine; Golden-flower paper inscribed with verses of tranquility.
In the silent courtyard, amidst the spring breeze, no one sees; Leisurely, he blows the jade flute of the Sovereign. (Xinwen Ben)
In response to the question regarding the Dharma on New Year’s Day, he said: "There is. For the month with fewer days, it remains as before: twenty-nine.
The Jade Unicorn snaps the golden bridle and lets out a great roar amidst the clouds. (Lan’an Shu).
[Supplement] Furthermore, a monk asked Mingjiao Kuan, "Is there still Buddha-dharma at the beginning of the new year?
The Master said, "No. The monk said, "Every day is a good day; every year is a good year. Why then is there none? The Master said, "When Zhang Gong drinks wine, Li Gong gets drunk.
The monk said, "Old and decrepit as you are, you have a dragon's head but a snake's tail. The Master said, "Ming."
The Master said, "Today I have lost the advantage. He spoke in verse:
"In the New Year, when asked about the Buddha-dharma, he replied, 'There is none. If you understand this, you will find as before that you remain halfway along the path.
Who would take up a small boat with a flute on a clear night, Blowing through Lake Dongting under the bright moon? (Lan’an Shu)
In the New Year, the Dharma spreads its true breeze; it makes one laugh to see the old man on the street celebrating the year. Where can one go when the three-tiered waves are high?
In vain do they try to determine the male and female with a pair of swords. (Xuetang’s Verse)
Nantang Xing said: "Jingqing says that when there is something, one loses the advantage; Mingjiao says that even when there is nothing, one loses the advantage.
But tell me, where does the confusion lie? Jingshan Guangzhen said: "One person stands atop a high, lofty peak without revealing his head;
another walks on the bottom of a deep, profound sea without getting his feet wet. This is it.
This is so; it cannot be said that there is not some degree of confusion. The verse says:
In the new year, the sights and things gradually revive and flourish. As for the Buddha-dharma, it is a vain labor to ask whether it exists or not. Gain and loss, right and wrong—all are cast aside.
The nostrils of the Persian merchant have always been coarse. (Jianlong Yuan)
A secure and secret field; the playful exercise of supernormal powers (*abhijñā*). At the beginning of a new year of the Buddha-Dharma, both existence and non-existence lose their advantage.
All things are uniformly equal to empty space; how could one allow for the establishment of a fixed point? The wind upon the grass carries out the Patriarchal Command.
Who says that once the thunder ceases, its sound does not continue? (Wenyu Qín)

Regarding the Buddha-dharma for the New Year, Jingqing says: "One must believe that the words of a parent come from the parent’s own mouth. Regarding the Buddha-dharma for the New Year, Mingjiao says:
"The bearded man from the Western Heaven has no whiskers. It is laughable that both elders have lost their advantage; the Persian from the South Sea has lost his nose.
On this night of Great Peace, it is as if frost were added upon snow. In the cold of the year, Sun Bin [was spared].
Sheathing the sword: Xie Sanlang on the fishing boat. (Fujian Qín).
[Added by Zhìshōu] National Teacher Shényàn of Gǔshān Xīngshèng in Fúzhōu (who succeeded Xuěfēng). One day he visited Xuěfēng.
Feng knew that his conditions were ripe; suddenly rising, he seized him and asked, "What is this?
The Master attained sudden and complete awakening, yet he forgot even that realization, doing nothing but waving his hand back and forth. Feng said, "Are you applying intellectual reasoning?"
He asked, "What principle is there in this? Feng examined his profound realization, patted him, and certified him. He spoke in verse:
"Suddenly seized by Master Zeng by the chest, The paths of a lifetime are suddenly exhausted. Without cause, he raises his hand and gives a light shake;
The Great Peak of the South is made to laugh until it falls. (Zhuyu Jian)
[Added from the Supplementary Collection] Gushan ascended the hall for formal instruction. He issued a statement, saying: "Under the gate of Gushan, one must not cough.
At that time, a monk coughed once. The Master said: "What are you doing? The monk replied: "I have a cold. The Master said: "A cold is acceptable."
The Verse says:
A single arrow flies across the vast void to the nine-layered city; the old man Xue’s lineage style resounds with vigor.
It is said that the imperial guards proclaim the edicts; over there, no one at all is permitted to pass. (Xutang Yu)
[Added for inclusion] Gushan had a verse with which he addressed the assembly, saying: "Directly beneath, it is still difficult to comprehend; Seeking through words only makes it more remote.
If one speaks of Buddhas and Patriarchs, They are, by nature, separated by the ends of the earth. (The *Wudeng Huiyuan* states under this verse: The Master raised this question to a monk.
"How do you understand this? The monk remained silent. The Master then said to his attendant, "I do not understand; please provide a turning phrase on my behalf.
The attendant replied, "When the Master speaks thus, it is still as far apart as the ends of heaven and earth. The monk related this to the Master.
The Master called the attendant and asked, "Did you provide that turning phrase for this monk? The attendant replied, "Yes."
The Master then struck him and drove him out of the monastery. The verse says:
"The National Teacher’s model was too compassionate; How does entering the weeds compare to emerging from them?
The holy arrow that pierces through the nine layers— As before, it stands apart, separated by the vast heavens. (Shixi Yue)
Chan Master Lingcan of Cuiyan in Mingzhou (a successor of Xuefeng) ascended the hall and said:
"During this summer, I have been conversing with my brothers; look, are Cuiyan’s eyebrows still there? (This follows what is recorded in the *Chuan deng lu* [Record of the Transmission of the Lamp];

the *Wudeng huiyuan* [Compendium of the Five Lamps] differs from the *Chuan deng lu*, stating instead: "During this summer, I have been talking east and west with my brothers; look, are Cuiyan's eyebrows still there?")

Cuiyan Zhi said, "Exerting one's full strength for the sake of the assembly; yet disaster arises from within the private door. Cuiyan’s demonstration to his disciples is peerless through the ages. To respond with the character "Pass" (Guān) is to lose one's money and incur punishment.

Old Baofu’s attempts at suppression and praise are difficult to fathom; Cuiyan’s incessant prattle is clearly that of a thief. When a white jade disc is without flaw, who can distinguish the true from the false?
Changqing and Xiang’an knew each other intimately; their eyebrows had grown back.
(Xuedou Xian) The green mountains rise steeply; the clear waters flow on. They have passed through the nostrils and caused the eyebrows to fall away completely. (Dahong Sui)
As a thief, Baofu carries his shackles and confesses to the crime; as a man, Changqing loses the truth and pursues delusion.
Yunmen shuts himself away in his room like the moon over the autumn river; Cuoyan grows old and decrepit, with his eyebrows above his eyes (Sixin Xin).
[Continued Collection] A golden mallet pierces through his blood-red cloud-penetrating robe; his authority beyond the threshold is bold and majestic.
Having shattered the mountain-demon’s cave, he casts his line into the depths of the azure pool to catch the whale and the turtle. (Nantang Xing)
The celestial Māra slanders the Buddha; like the dogs of Jie barking at Yao. How illustrious is the Great Man! His sacred virtue may shine forth.
(Mongan Eok) Whom does the ten-thousand-jin crossbow shoot? Before the arrow leaves the string, the target’s life is lost.
It brings misfortune upon the blind turtle who loses its floating wood; it seeks to pass through fire to sift the golden dust. (I’an Gwon)
When speaking, one must first ensure the heart is free from shame; in undertaking affairs, one should follow what is most reasonable and long-standing.
Do not emulate those in the villages who lack integrity, deliberating wrongly from morning until night. (Xutang Yu)
The Venerable Fu of Taiyuan (who succeeded Xuefeng). Gushan asked him, "Before your parents were born, where was your nose?
The Master said, "Brother, you go first. Gushan said, "Now that they are born, tell me where it is.
The Master did not approve. Gushan then asked, "How about this? The Master said, "Take the fan in your hand."
The Master came forward. Mount and Shanzi questioned him again. The Master remained silent. Mount, unable to fathom this, struck him with a punch. The Verse says:
Before the parents were yet born, where was the nose? The old masters of the monastic groves are all ignorant of the phrase for "concealing the body."
Although Gushan saw the opportune moment, he could not avoid bolstering his own school’s gate; Tanyuan Fu waved his fan, fiddling with trivial household items.
Deep is the spring within the mountains; flying flowers fall in countless numbers. (Fohui Quan)
Before the parents were born, birth was already just so. A single act of grasping is most extraordinary; directly beneath it, all is like a lotus in the fire.
Illuminating the present and shining upon the past, it exhausts the subtle and reaches the profound. How deeply pitiable! A pure breeze forever fills the seat.
"In a single thought, eight thousand years. (Yuánwù Qín).
[Supplement] "At the head of the Gāo'ān滩, all was shattered to pieces; before Elephant Bone Peak, eyes were fixed in folly.
I dare say Gǔshān has no nostrils; for a thousand ages the monastic groves have laughed heartily. (Zhèngtáng Biàn).
[Added for inclusion: Layman Fu went to visit Xuefeng. Upon hearing of his arrival, Xuefeng assembled the community.

When the Master reached the Dharma Hall, he looked toward Xuefeng and then descended to attend to the administrative duties. The next day, he went back up to pay his respects and said, "Yesterday, I offended you, Preceptor.
Xuefeng said, "I know it is such a matter; let it be. The Verse says:
General Li Guang was without peer throughout antiquity and the present. Penetrating deep into the enemy's camp, he preserved his life and avoided harm.
Without moving a blade, he achieved small victories; to this day, his illustrious reputation remains at the frontier passes. (Haiyin Xin)
Xuefeng gathered the assembly to await Master Fu; as soon as he ascended the hall and cast a glance, everyone was scattered to the east and west.
The next day, Xuefeng said, "I have offended you. How many layers of kōans are there from of old? (Benjiao 1)
Whetting the needle point on iron; plucking hair from a cow’s back. Using much for little; working cold and burning hot.
Going straight up to the Dharma Hall and then coming down—this is to provoke the Abbot’s heavy commentary and annotation. Knowing this sort of thing, let it rest; let it rest.
Vastly filling the valleys and the ditches. (Yuedang Chang).
His vigorous spirit was like a rainbow as he ascended the Dharma Hall; he went to the fence and bound the *gāndhaka* (wooden bolt) with perfect precision.
If one says he offended the Old Monk, it is like adding frost needlessly to snow. (By Chengyan Yu).

[Added from a supplementary collection: When Master Fu was first lecturing on the *Nirvāṇa Sūtra* at Guangxiao Temple in Yangzhou, there was a Chan practitioner who had been detained by the snow and went to listen to the lecture.

When the discourse reached the "three causes of Buddha-nature" and the "Dharmakāya of the three virtues," and the Master expounded extensively upon the wondrous principle of the Dharmakāya, the Chan practitioner could not help but laugh.
After the lecture concluded, the Master invited the Chan practitioner for tea and said, "I have long..."
"Your aspirations are narrow and inferior; you rely on the literal text to explain the meaning, which has justly invited my laughter. I hope you will instruct me.

The Zen practitioner said, "I truly laugh at you, Master of the Tripitaka, for not recognizing the Dharmakāya. The Master replied, "In such an explanation as this, where is there anything that is not correct?"
The student said, "I request that the Master explain it once more. The Master said, "The principle of the Dharma-body is like the great void:
vertically it exhausts the three periods of time, horizontally it spans the ten directions; it encompasses the eight poles and includes the two polarities.

Responding to conditions and manifesting in response to stimuli, there is nowhere it does not pervade. The student said, "I do not say that what the Master has said is incorrect; it is simply that he has explained it [in a certain way]."
"The matter of the dimensions and limits of the Dharma-body—I truly do not yet recognize the Dharma-body within me.
The Master said, "Since it is so, you should speak for me. [The student] asked, "Master, do you believe it? The Master replied, "How could I dare not believe it?

[The student] said, "If that is so, Master, suspend your lectures for ten days. Sit upright in your room, contemplate in stillness, and gather and collect your mind and thoughts. [The student] did so.

He cast off all adverse conditions at once. Following the instructions he had been given, from the first watch of the night until the fifth watch, he suddenly attained realization upon hearing the sound of drums and horns.
He knocked on the Chan master’s door and asked, "Who is there? The master replied, "It is I.
The Chan master rebuked him, saying, "I instructed you to transmit and uphold the Great Teaching and preach the Dharma in place of the Buddha; why have you been here all night?"

A man was lying drunk on the street. The Master said, "Dharma Master, you have been lecturing on the sutras until now, yet you have been pinching and twisting the nostrils of your own biological parents.

From this day forward, I dare not do such a thing again. The man replied, "Go for now; let us meet tomorrow. The Master then ceased his lectures and traveled extensively throughout all quarters. The verse says: The drunken man lies on the street; The Master speaks of the Dharma. He tells him he has been pinching his own parents’ noses;
From this day forth, he dares not act thus again. "Go for now; we shall meet tomorrow," he says. The Master then stops his lectures and wanders far and wide.
A single melody of the *Shanyu* wind-drums extends far; wherever Master Fu hears it, it resonates with the notes of *gong* and *shang*.
To this day, every night, the traveler from Weiyang listens in vain at the tower’s edge, his heart breaking with sorrow. (Benjue I)
Who will blow the painted horn by the river city? A single melody of plum blossoms is heard from across the shore. The lingering wine has just awakened as the golden incense burner grows cold;
the moon still shines bright upon the branches of the *hai-tang*. (Lan’an Shu)

The elephant king and his calf follow one another; people on the bank watch as their hooves tread upon hooves. They eat the fragrant grass delicately until they know fullness;
returning, they do not wait for the sun to sink low. (Xutang Yu)
When the Venerable Fu was leaving for Mount Gu to attend an invitation from the Great King, Xuefeng saw him off at the gate.
Upon returning to the Dharma Hall, Xuefeng said, "A single arrow of sainthood has shot straight into the innermost city.
The Master said, "He has not yet reached the ultimate. Xuefeng said, "He is a man of thorough penetration. The Master said, "If you do not believe me, wait until I go there myself."
Having verified this, he pursued him to the middle of the road and asked, "Where are you going, elder brother?
Shanshan said, "I am going to the Ninefold Imperial City. The Master said, "What if you suddenly encounter an encirclement by a three-fold army? Shanshan said:
"His own house has a path that reaches through the heavens. The Master said, "In that case, he has left the palace and lost the hall.
Shanshan said, "Where would he not be called Honored One? The Master shook his sleeves and turned back. Feng asked, "How was it? The Master said:

"A fine holy arrow has been broken in mid-flight. He then related the previous story. Feng said, "That fellow’s words remain. The Master said, "This old, frozen lump of filth actually still possesses some local sentiment.
The Verse says: A fine holy arrow has been broken in mid-flight; The old man’s words remain. What a pity this old, frozen lump of filth Still retains a trace of local sentiment.
In the celestial caverns there are no walls and the moon has no obstruction. The Master of the Morning Star knocks his teeth together. The wind shakes the ancient altar and pine seeds fall;
it strikes the back of his head, and his paper cap tilts askew. (Juexiangjian)
The Blue Youth double-reins his jade-colored steed as it neighs; He wears a pale white spring robe girdled with a green sash.
Returning at midnight, he passes beneath the flowers; His golden whip strikes down a flurry of scattered red petals. (Zhuyou Jian, No. 2)

Within the nine-layered city, it is not distant at all; Arrows are shot through layer after layer, yet they abound. Suddenly encountering a place surrounded by the three armies, There is clearly a path that leads straight to the heavens.
Chan Master Yunmen Wenyan of Shaoyang (who succeeded Xuefeng), the founding patriarch of Yunmen, addressed the assembly, saying: "Everyone possesses their own radiance;
yet when one looks for it, it is not seen, being shrouded in darkness. What is this self-radiance of yours? He then provided his own verse in its place:
"The kitchen, the storehouse, and the main gate. He further said: "A good thing is not as good as having none at all. Verse:
It is said: "Self-illumination stands alone in its brilliance; for you, I shall open a single thread. When the flowers fall, the tree casts no shadow; when looking, who does not see?
Seeing or not seeing—riding a cow backward, one enters the Buddha hall. (Xuedou Xian)
Utterly dark and dull, there is no need to look; it supports heaven and earth in a vast, black expanse. The three gates and the kitchen stand facing each other forever;
a single path leads through pines and wind, filling the courtyard with cold. (Baiyun Yuan).
Vague and indistinct; as if lost, yet as if present. Striking it, bumping into it—the kitchen, the storehouse, and the triple gate.
The golden sun cannot illuminate it through; the jade hare races westward again. One does not know what thing this is, yet it is able to serve as the root of heaven and earth. (Fuxincai).

Beyond the night-bright curtain, a thousand peaks are exquisite; before the phoenix-mirror stand, ten thousand phenomena differ. Traces are swept away and footprints extinguished; not even a grain’s weight is established.
Who is the Buddha hall? Who is the incense kitchen? Striking out, one produces the five-colored marrow of the phoenix;
smashing it to pieces, one breaks the bright moon pearl of the black dragon. (Yuánwù Qín)
[Continued Collection] Black, black. Regardless of east or west, north or south, the three gates of the kitchen and storehouse face one another, towering high;

they support the heavens and buttress the earth, all gathered together in ink-black. Though it is a fine matter, it is better not to have it at all. I dare say that Shaoyang would not understand this. (Zhengjue Yi)
Everyone possesses their own inner radiance; when one looks for it, it is not seen, shrouded in dark gloom.
Kick down the triple gate and the kitchen storehouse; at that moment, light and darkness naturally part. (Weyo Am)
Yunmen ascended the hall and said: "Within the realm of heaven and earth, amidst the universe, there is a single treasure hidden within the mountain of form.

He takes the lantern and places it inside the Buddha Hall; he brings the triple gate and puts it upon the lantern. What is this? He provided his own substitute response: "The mind shifts as it pursues objects. He also said: "Clouds arise and thunder resounds. The verse says: Within the realm of heaven and earth, A single treasure is hidden within the mountain of form.
He takes the lantern and places it in the Buddha Hall, Brings the triple gate and sets it atop the lantern. What is this? The mind shifts as it pursues objects. Clouds rise and thunder resounds.
Look! On the ancient bank, who is there holding the fishing rod? The clouds drift slowly; the waters stretch vast and wide.
The bright moon and the reeds—look for yourself, sir. (Xuedou Xian)
White clouds on the ridge unfurl and then roll back; the bright moon at the edge of the sky departs and then returns.
Bowing my head, I enter beneath the thatched eaves; unaware, I laugh "he-he" several times. (Baizhang Yuan).
Look! Wild grasses and idle flowers are in utter disarray. It is spring upon the Drifting Lake (Dongting) by the river in the third month.
Smoke and mist fly past the banks of the Xiao and Xiang rivers. (Miaoshan Xiù)
The Imperial Net interlaces in tens of thousands of ways; the mountain of forms dissolves away, yet the circle of shadows remains whole. To take it up is not that there is no place to seek it;
it resides right here within the heavens, the earth, and the universe. (Fuxincai)
The tiger and leopard display their patterns; the qilin reveals its head and horns. Illuminating heaven and shining upon the earth, they pile up like mountains and accumulate like peaks.
When the face-gate is shattered, one transcends form and sound; when the net is severed, one untangles the glue and removes the bonds. Lay down the weapons of war at the tips of the hundred grasses;
a solitary falcon soars ten thousand miles through the autumn sky. (Wenyu Qin)
[Continued Collection] It is right when opening the eyes; it is right when closing the eyes. To hesitate or deliberate—to let such a move pass by (Dun’an Yan).
Faintly from the misty village comes the sound of barking dogs; I seek to find them, yet I cannot see a single house.
Suddenly, at the place where the bridge ends and the stream turns back, Three or four blossoms of emerald peach drift down. (Lun of Duqiao)
Yunmen addressed the assembly, saying: "I will not ask you about the period before the fifteenth day.
Bring forth a single phrase for the period after the fifteenth day. The assembly was speechless. Yunmen spoke on their behalf, saying: "Every day is a good day. The verse says:
Setting aside one, he grasps seven; above, below, and in the four quarters, there is no equal. Walking slowly, he tramples the sound of flowing water;
looking out freely, he traces the tracks of soaring birds. The grass is lush and the mist is dense; wildflowers grow profusely by the side of the empty crag.
A snap of the fingers is enough to evoke pity for the *śūnyatā* (the empty being). Do not touch it; if you touch it, there are thirty blows.
(Xuedou Xian) Every day is a good day. When the wind comes, the tree nods its head. Amidst the misty vapors of the Nine Rivers, the moon rises upon the Xie family’s tower.
(Seal of the Ocean-Print).
Every day is a fine day. Who says there is no peer? A sweet melon is sweet all the way to its stem; yet it may not necessarily be as sweet as honey.
(Great and Profound Grace).
The ice melts upon the north bank of the River; flowers bloom upon the southern branches of the trees. Spring colors exist everywhere; even at the ends of the earth, one has already returned home.

(Increasing above). [Continued Collection] Breaking two into one, dividing three into six. When counting the beads on the rosary, the count falls short; the Southern Dipper is grasped by hand, the Northern Dipper is touched as the body turns.
The doors and windows burst open, facing directly the balcony; the jade hare and golden crow revolve like axle-pins.
Whether the Dharma is transmitted or not, whether it is attained or not—who knows that the spring branches are green along the road?
(Yuánwù Qín). Every day is a good day; the Buddha-dharma and worldly dharmas are both fully perfected. There is no need to seek out the mysterious and profound in a forced manner;
simply attend to the fact that the alms bowl becomes wet twice a day. (Ní Wúzhuó Zǒng).

Yunmen ascended the hall and said, "Awaken to the Way by hearing sounds; clarify the mind by seeing forms. He then raised his hand and said, "The Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara buys a sesame cake with money. Lowering his hand, he said, "It turns out it was just a steamed bun. The verse says: Hearing sounds, one awakens to the Way; Seeing forms, one clarifies the mind. Raising his hand, he says: "Avalokiteśvara buys a sesame cake with money. Lowering his hand, he says: "It turns out it was just a steamed bun. How could this be anything other than the Great Matter? If you can understand this at once, Then you will see that the Buddhas and patriarchs Are all within your own hands. If you do not understand, You will surely fall into the pit of doubt. Do not seek it outside yourself; Seeking it outside is a mistake. If you can comprehend it right here, You will know that the Way is not far off. If you still hesitate and look elsewhere, You are like a person seeking a rabbit's horn. This is the true meaning of the ancestral gate; It is not something to be grasped through conceptual thought. Having purchased it with joyful heart, he hurried home; unaware that letting go would instead result in error.
Even if one were to transcend the crown of Vairocana, one still falls into Shao Yang’s second level of function. (Shangfang Yi)
In the small courtyard, the spring breeze is especially cold. A beautiful woman leans in silence against the balustrade.
No one listens to her heart-rending melody; she plays the lute once more beneath the moon. (Cishou Shen)
When seeing forms, the light of mind manifests; when hearing sounds, the Way is already revealed. Amidst flashing lightning, one distinguishes black from white;

within the ocean-tide voice, one discerns the musical scales of *gong* and *shang*. Old Shaoyang’s gate of compassion is universal; he strikes the trigger with a crossbow of a thousand *jin*. (Wenyu Qín).
Seeing forms and clarifying the mind—this matter is already settled; hearing sounds and awakening to the Way—this is even more profound.
Through the power of Avalokiteśvara’s wondrous wisdom and compassion, the *utpala* flower blooms amidst the thorny brambles. (Jingshan Gaofeng)
Homage to Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva. With a red lotus tongue upon Mount Potalaka, we know not when he will attain Buddhahood;
to forge a sword, one must use the iron of Bingzhou. (Gushan Gui)

[Continued Collection] A sudden fall is nothing other than itself; no contrivance is required. Covering is sovereign; hidden and manifest, it encompasses all. Lifting one’s head, one loses the old path;
grasping the oar, one immediately boards another’s ferry. Turning the easy into the difficult, extracting poverty to create wealth—ten thousand people go thus. (Yuet Tang Chang)

Suddenly transcending the phrases of seeing forms and hearing sounds, Not involving the words of clarifying the mind or awakening to the Way: Flowers fall and birds sing at the temple beneath the crags;
The moon is bright as a person calls for the ferryboat at the riverhead. (Xue’an Jin)
A single melody before the wind—truly, who is it? The tune is so lofty, how could it deign to descend into this age?
Seeing no one who understands the meaning within the music, He takes up his cloud-flute once more and plays it intentionally. (Jianweng Jing)
