Yunmen draws back his gaze with a smile; if you hesitate, you will meet his "Gùjiàn-yī" (the look and the "eh").
Even with all the stratagems of Zhang Liang, in the end, they would find it difficult to apply here. (Beitapu Zu)
Yunmen’s glance back has its own underlying reason. If even a single point fails to reach it, then "rest, rest, rest, rest" (Zhenjing Wen).
Shaoyang’s single mirror is a lump of raw iron; bite through it directly—do not resent being deceived (Gushan Gui).
[Continued Collection] Yunmen’s “Withdrawing the Gaze” Verse: The monk’s eyelids are heavy; the eyelids are so heavy they weigh seven or eight catties. A thundering chariot cannot move them.
When it cannot be moved, he recites the verse on withdrawing the gaze: at that time, chant the name of Amitābha three or two times to offer prayers for the deceased Li of East Village.
The Bearded One was born in the Western Heaven; Old Meng of the mountains is robust and healthy. At the Fútián Monastery, the poor child cries out:
"Give me a single coin of great brilliance! (Wǔzǔ Jiè).
Master Yunyang was the most urgent and incisive of men. Even before one had entered the gate, he had already distinguished them.
If you try to take it up within the scope of conceptual reflection, he will strike you down with a great staff like the moon falling from the edge of heaven. (Dian Niyou).
Yunmen was once asked by a monk, "What is the master’s family style?

The Master said, "There is someone reading a book at the gate" (The *Wudeng Huiyuan* records this as "there is a reader coming to report," or alternatively, "a reader outside the gate comes to report"). The Verse says:
Every monastery has its own established tradition; this matter is not the same as that of Yunmen.
If there were anyone reading books outside the gate, even if it were Yan Hui himself, he would not be admitted. (Beita Zu)
The family tradition of this establishment is not without its private principles. Only Yunmen’s words remain suspect:

"If you, who have been instructed to study books, should arrive here, report it at once; you must know this! It is for the sake of that old Du Fu and Wang Mojie, who loved my lofty chanting and off-rhymed verses. (Juehai Yuan)
Those who study the books must examine this most carefully. A stringless lute is difficult to meet with one who knows its sound. I shall tell you of the true family tradition:
when descending from the steps and advancing forward, he moves with a majestic grace like a pair of wings. (Fohuiquan).
[Continued Collection] A scholar has reported this. How could it be a matter of "the particles zhi, hu, and zhe"? Both Confucius and the Duke of Zhou failed to reach the Master’s gate. (Tianmu Li)
Yunmen was once asked by a monk, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said, "Watching the mountains in broad daylight. The Verse says:
Watching the mountains in broad daylight is also ordinary; The meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West is a vain debate. A golden-maned lion is rarely encountered.
There is. For the most part, foxes are called wolves. (Beitang Zu). Viewing the mountains is pleasant by day;
a clear breeze brushes past the white clouds. Where did the fire come from last night? It has burned out the graves of the ancients.
(Jingyin Furi of Tokyo) Gazing at the mountains in the sunlight, all that meets the eye is green; A thousand crags and ten thousand ravines compete in their winding expanse.
The cave entrance seems as if veiled by clouds, yet those who arrive must know the path is level and plain. (Yang Wuwe)
"Looking at the mountains in the daylight. These words are concise and the speech is direct. For those of later generations and beginners, it is essential to contemplate this with earnest attention.
(Huangbo Sheng). Kuangzhen did not spare his two eyebrows; looking at the mountains in the daylight, he met the patriarch’s pivot. When the winter solstice fire burns, spring turns green again;
one should simply allow birds and beasts to understand their mutual dependence. (Sanzong).
After the rain, two or three peaks rise above the river; Layered with mist and haze, their weight is beyond reckoning. To look upon them with the eyes is truly to be blind;
Yet when heard by the ears, one’s hearing surpasses that of heaven. (Fojian Qín)

[Continued Collection] Tanran once asked the Master for his well-being. How can this compare to the single phrase transmitted by Shaoyang? In broad daylight, dew falls upon the immortal’s palm at Mount Hua;
deep in the night, the monkey cries as the moon hangs before the eaves. (Touzi Qing)
"Looking at the mountains in the sunlight—how difficult, how difficult! Layer upon layer of sheer cliffs, ridge after ridge of perilous peaks.
One sees only the misty light flickering; who knows the gurgling of the waterfalls? (Shangfang Yi)
It is good to look at the mountains in the daylight. In what way is it good? If you wish to see Old Yunmen, do not fall into the second phrase. (Yuelin Guan)
"Looking at the mountains in the sunlight answers the question; clearly opening one's mouth reveals the heart and liver.
If you seek the fundamental principle within these words, you will fall among the towering, layered peaks. (Tuingeng Ning)

Compiled by the Śramaṇa Fasheng of Ba’en Guangxiao Chan Temple in Chizhou during the Song Dynasty.
Compiled by the Śramaṇa Puhui of Tianyi Wanshou Chan Monastery during the Yuan Shaoxing era,
this is a continuation of the Recorded Sayings of the Patriarchs from the Sixth Patriarch down to the Seventh Generation (specifically the third of the sixth generation under Qingyuan).
Yunmen was once asked by a monk, "What is the phrase that penetrates the Dharma-body? The Master said, "Hide your body within the Big Dipper. Verse:
Hiding one’s body within the Big Dipper is most clear; It is only because people do not see with precision. They vainly express their minds and intentions with clever artifice.
To understand it is like digging a deep pit on level ground; how could the dim lamp ever be changed by the daylight?
Green bamboo and yellow flowers grow everywhere upon the earth. (Fenyang Shao)
The aged Yunmen launches an iron boat; South of the Yangtze and North of it, all vie to gaze upon it. How pitiable are the countless fishermen with their lines cast out;
following the crowd, they wander aimlessly, losing their fishing rods. (Xuedou Xian)
Yunmen penetrates the Dharma-body; where is this person of the Dharma-body? Wild geese return to the northern passes;
the parrot longs for Western Qin. (Lingzhu Tong)
The Southern Peak is high, the Northern Peak is low; travelers weep with tears as the rain hesitates. Last night the Fire Star moved into Ox and Dipper;
it shines upon those in Western Jambudvīpa who do not know. (Touzi Qing)

The Dragon Gate was hewn through to let the azure waters flow; how could the torrential rains and surging floods ever cease their dust? The Immortal of Exile seized the moon and sank it to the bottom of the river;
the fisherman’s boat laughs to scorn the family of Xié. (Tianyi Hui)
To penetrate the Dragon Gate is exceptionally difficult; Yet it creates waves rising from level ground.
If common scales wish to obtain the favor of wind and thunder, First look within the surging waves of peach blossoms. (Foyin Yuan)
When someone asks about penetrating the Dharma-body, respond by pointing it out as the situation requires: "The great earth is like glue and lacquer;
the long river’s waves knit their brows. (Fahua Ju).
The phrase of the North Star’s hidden body: look where Yunmen speaks. The Southern Dipper divides into six points; the Northern Dipper’s seven stars cluster together.
Spring rains fall in misty moisture; autumn winds blow with chilling rustle. Kunlun leads the white elephant; the song enters Great Peace.
(Fushan Yuan): "The Northern Dipper conceals its body to be revealed; from this, the Dharma-body is manifest in full majesty.
Yunmen has deceived his followers until this very day, leaving them to measure it in vain. (Yujian Lin).
All stars in the heavens bow toward the North; no water in the human world does not flow toward the East.
If people of this age wish to know the place where the body is hidden, they should lift up their winnowing basket and find spring elsewhere. (Huanglong Nan)
Yunmen penetrates the Dharma-body; from this point on, there is neither distance nor intimacy. All say the breeze is warm, yet the cold of the three springs has been renewed. (Daowu Zhen)
East, west, south, north; above, below, and the four intermediate directions. Stretching across the universe, he crushes Mount Sumeru (revealing the sweet fragrance of heaven).
The young masters of the Five Tombs are accustomed to wandering among the flowers; the poor scholars who have not yet passed the examinations have always been many.
Watching others’ wealth and honor from a cold, detached place, one cannot help but wonder what will become of their official head-covers (Baizhang Yuan).
There is a reason for the "phrase of the North Star’s hidden body. Before north and south are clarified, spears and halberds arise.
On a wind-clear, moon-bright night without a cloud, do not mistake the literary star for the Ox or Plow constellations. (Zhaojue Zong)
Rising in the east and sinking in the west; the Northern Dipper conceals its body. Such is the decree of the Dharma King: its virtue has no neighbor.
(Zhenjing Wen) The phrase "the Northern Dipper conceals its body" is most profound; failing to clarify what lies above it, one labors in vain to transmit it.
The Yellow River rolls to its depths from antiquity to the present; the three peaks of Mount Hua point toward the heavens. (Sanzong Zushi)

The body hidden within the Big Dipper is most distinct; Cloudless on all four sides, the Great Clarity is vast and open. Monkeys and birds cry out of their own accord, and the mountains are naturally silent;
Water flows beneath the crags with a cool, clear resonance. (Qing of the Hermitage)
The Big Dipper hides its body; sitting, one finds no peace. Opening the window, the setting sun rests upon the precarious railing. Clouds gather and the moon emerges; the void is like water.
In every shrine and every mote of dust, all are of one and the same nature. (Fuxincai)
What need is there for the Star of Literature and the Star of Wine? At once they were bestowed upon this Master.
With lofty chanting and great intoxication, three thousand poems remain for the world to accompany the moonlight. (Wuzu Yan)
The light penetrates through the crown of Vairocana’s head; when night falls, the stars turn and hide within the Dipper. The Chan master does not need to recite the talismans of the Celestial Master;
he too understands how to join the heavens and step upon the *gang*. (Zhang Wujin)

The "Hiding the Body" phrase of the Northern Dipper—how many tens of thousands of ways have been debated! People greedily gaze at the moon in the sky; who perceives the cold that makes their hair stand on end? (Shushan Ru)
Yunmen penetrates the Dharma-body; his clear words reveal the intimacy. Taking a step, he ascends the mountain peak; the summit is so high it neighbors the moon. (Chu’an Fang)
Myriad thousands in the north, south, east, and west; heaven and earth, above and below, both boundless. Meeting and seeing one another, they laugh "he-he";
snapping fingers and looking up, the moon is halfway through the sky. (Puyun Yuan)
[Continued Collection] Yunmen penetrates the Dharma-body; he cuts off Śākyamuni’s voice. Mañjuśrī need not be despondent;
Samantabhadra need not linger in reflection. (Wuzu Ji)

The matter of the North Star concealing its body is straightforward. The Dharma-body is formless; where could it possibly pass through? Later generations do not understand the intent of those who came before them;
they are like those rowing a boat beneath the water trying to catch the moon in the sky. (Fahua raises this case.)
The "Hiding the Body" phrase of the Northern Dipper: to deliberate upon it is already an error. The white hawk piercing the heavens has no longing for its old nest. (Cishou Shen)
Satiated with gruel and rice, all is but a single sound of snoring. Sleeping early and rising late—what need is there to wait for a noble rank?
(Dianiu You) Last night the eastern wind fell the myriad blossoms; half followed the flowing water, half followed the wind. What need is there to pole a small boat beneath the bright moon?
It naturally connects with a branch of the Peach Blossom Spring. (Kaishan Zu)
Hiding his body within the Big Dipper, the Way flourishes ever more; a three-legged toad wears a brocade loincloth. How many sick cats eat dead mice?
At midday they lift their heads, yet their eyes have no light. (Dongshan Kong)
Heaven and earth are vast and boundless; how can you say they conceal the Big Dipper? Old Yunmen with his lame feet has not yet understood three, eight, and nine. (Tianmu Li)
Hiding one's body within the Northern Dipper, appearing and disappearing in empty space—speak a single phrase, and the sun will rise in the east. (Heunggwam Gung)
Yunmen was once asked by a monk, "What is the teaching of the one lifetime? The Master said, "I speak in response to each.
He added this verse:
To speak in response to each is utterly solitary; A holeless iron hammer strikes down another wedge. Beneath the Jambu tree, he laughs heartily.
Last night the black dragon snapped its horns and broke them. Adieu, adieu! The old man of Shaoyang has obtained a single peg.
(Xuedou Xian) Facing this one teaching, a hawk from the vast heavens; through ten thousand layers of clouds, it makes but a single dash.
Old Shaoyang, old Shaoyang—search for him north, south, east, or west, and he is nowhere to be found. (Zhengjue Yi)
One word for all. The scroll ends at five thousand and forty-eight. Wind, flowers, snow, and moon shall flow on;
add forged iron behind the Diamond Mind. (Wuzu Yan)
To speak of one thing—how extraordinary! A single mass of iron fills the void. When hunger comes, they disregard their food like thunder;
each one gathers his head and struggles to bite and chew. (Longmen Yuan)
To speak of it as one: the five teachings and three vehicles are all encompassed therein. Within the dragon palaces and ocean treasuries, one moves with total freedom.
A mud ox at the bottom of the water swallows the moon. (Fóxìng Tài)

[Continued Collection]: The Dragon of the Ocean Treasury. Golden texts and jade registers from the palace; meeting capacities and observing faculties, breaking through barriers and striking the vital points.

Over three hundred assemblies, the fundamental principles were revitalized; for forty-nine years, it was all with one tongue. "A-la-la!"—in response to the One Teaching, these words of ultimate truth are like cutting through iron. (By Yuanwu Keqin)
Yunmen was once asked by a monk: "When it is neither the mechanism before one's eyes, nor the matter before one's eyes, what then?
The Master said: "Turn the statement upside down. The verse says:
To overturn one explanation and divide it into sections—to determine for you that those who die together are born together—is not something reserved for the rare "phoenix feathers" (the prodigies).
Thirty-three people entered the tiger’s den; each distinct, tumultuous, and hurried, like the moon reflected in water. (Xuedou Xian)
To speak of it perversely: it clears the bones and marrow. Ten thousand miles, not a single cloud; cast down a mass of snow. Parting, parting!
This old Zen elder would rather let his tongue die. (Zhengjue Yi)
To speak thus perversely is mere loquacity; for no reason, you have leaked the celestial mechanism. All under the four seas and nine provinces labor in vain.
You have flown out from the Dragon Palace only to burrow into an ant hole. (By Xuanzun)
[Continued Collection]: This thief recognizes a thief. Using a wedge to extract a wedge; bird tracks in the sky, clouds; mirror images, the moon in water.
It is the "Teacher’s Method for Confusing the Lion’s Tracks" and the "Old Cat’s Way of Finding Secure Ground on a Tree.
With lively agility, he overturns a single statement at ease, turning the foxes’ den upside down. (Yuánwù Qín).
A monk asked Yunmen, “What is the samādhi of every dust mote? The Master said, “Rice in the bowl;
water in the bucket. The Verse says: Rice in the bowl;
water in the bucket. The talkative master finds it hard to open his beak. The positions of the Northern Dipper and Southern Star are no different.
White waves surge from level ground; whether you intend to stop them or not, they neither cease nor halt. Every one of them is a son of a wealthy man without trousers (Xuedou Xian).
Three thousand blows in the morning are not many; eight hundred blows in the evening are not few. The rice in the bowl, the water in the bucket—
Water. Before people, one must absolutely avoid being unclear. (Baizhang Yuan). In every particle of dust is samādhi;
here and there, nothing is external. A thousand peaks face the mountain; a hundred rivers flow to the sea.
There is not a single dharma that is not as it was from the Tathāgata. It is simply this majestic Avalokiteśvara. (Tiantong Jue).
To see it and not grasp it; to contemplate it from a thousand miles away. A ladle listens for what is coming; a colander has no ears.

When the flowers bloom in the second and third months, the fragrant spring wind rises at the crossroads. Directly beneath this, do not even attempt to conceive of it—rice in the bowl, water in the bucket. (Zantang Zhun)

[Continued Collection] Rice in the bowl, water in the bucket. Opening the mouth to reveal one’s very heart, seeking a true friend. As soon as one conceives a thought, one falls behind by two or three steps;
facing each other, suddenly they are thousands of miles apart. Master Shaoyang [Yunmen Wenyan] was worth a little more. As for the principle of "severing metal," who could share it?
As for a heart like a rock, only he alone could be thus. (Tiantong Ju).
The Samādhi of every mote of dust. A bowl of rice and a bucket of water—within the eyes of Yunmen, inside the body of this monk.
Squeezed together and brought forth, there is nowhere to hide; wherever you touch or strike it, it buries you. (Chang of Yuedang).
Rice in the bowl, water in the bucket; the dog bites people without baring its teeth.
How laughable is that old, ancient fellow of Shaoyang—having fallen to the ground, he has not yet risen to this day. (Wuan Quan)
Buying at the south end at a high price, selling at the north end at a low price; one may only hear the name, but must not see the face. (Qian’an Ren).
Yunmen was asked by a monk, "What is the single phrase of Yunmen? The Master said, "The twenty-fifth day of the twelfth month" (*The Wudeng Huiyuan records this as:
"What is the single melody of Yunmen? The Master said, "The twenty-fifth day of the twelfth month. The monk asked, "How about the one who sings it? The Master said, "Now, take it slowly"). Verse:
It is said:
On the twenty-fifth day of the twelfth month, one song transcends past and present. The great radish of Zhenzhou grows in deep soil (Fohuiquan).
Yunmen’s Single Song, twenty-five [verses]: it does not involve the notes gong, shang, jue, zhi, or yu.
When someone asks me about the origin of this song, clouds rise on the southern mountain and rain falls on the northern mountain. (Huanglong Nan)
The twenty-fifth day of the twelfth month: a single song no one can raise. The old, ancient cypress of Shaoyang counts them from the beginning on his fingers. (Yang Woei-wei)
A single melody of the ancient *Shao* tune, pure and clear; For many years, wood and stone have been refined into essence. Gongling has passed on—where is the man?
Only the cuckoo remains, crying beneath the bright moon. (Da Hong Su)
On the twenty-fifth day of the twelfth month, riding a donkey without beating the drum; the spring wind brings forth the hundred grasses, adding fresh earth to the graves. (Zhenjing Wen)
The twenty-fifth day of the twelfth month: the melody of Shao Yang is universal. If you wish to realize the meaning within it, take the primordial heaven as the ancestor of the mind. (Tongzhao Feng)
I recall the old master Yunmen, that ancient tapper; he once used this very day to instruct those present. How marvelous!
This matter from two hundred years ago continues to be blown like the melody of a *huqia* flute. (Yuantong Xian)
How lofty is the style of Yunmen’s melodic strains! They cause those in sorrow to feel utterly helpless.
The bright moon and clear wind are beyond price; they are bestowed all at once upon the siddha. (Changling Zhuo)
The Single Tune of Shaoyang: twenty-five [notes], not belonging to the five musical tones, spanning from antiquity to the present. In every land, the wondrous power of Avalokiteśvara’s wisdom;
in every speck of dust, he is able to save the world from suffering. (Min Gufo)
[Continued Collection] The twenty-fifth day of the twelfth month: A new song from Yunmen. Every time it is brought up, it makes the people of Luoyang laugh to death. (Nantang Si)
On the twenty-fifth day of the twelfth month, Yunmen gave up his innermost being; he played this single melody with all his heart.
Its pure sound transcends the Great Antiquity; let the clear-eyed monk cease his blundering. (Kentang Chong)
A single song from Yunmen penetrates the marrow and the very bones. Like a clearing snow across a thousand peaks, the cold plum blossoms its buds.
This "prince of the simultaneous peck and strike" sounds his wooden clapper with refined elegance. (Songyuan Yue)
The Single Tune of Yunmen has never had a musical score from the beginning; its resonance transcends the five notes, and its melody soars for a thousand ages.
Among these, who can know the subtle meaning? How many times have I sought to cast Ziqi in gold? (Wuzhun Fanzhen)

One, two, three, four, five, six. The blue-eyed barbarian monk’s count is incomplete. At Shaolin, it was said in vain that he transmitted it to Shen Guang;
yet the story of folding his robes and returning to Western India—Western India is vast and boundless, with nowhere to seek him.
Last night, however, he stayed overnight facing the Milk Peak. (Xuedou Xian)

Unrestrained in its six aspects, the melody is most fresh; what need is there for the dust to swirl around the rafters when one can sing? A gentle breeze fills the railing as a thousand trees of flowers bloom;
this is a spring distinct from that of heaven and earth. (Baiyun Yuan)
Not established as one, not contained within six; suddenly appearing, what further trace remains? Boundless green mountains cannot retain it;
falling flowers and flowing water are far too leisurely. (Yuánwù Qín)

【Continued Collection】 Village songs and communal dances are the *nāga-samādhi*; scabies-dogs and mud-pigs are the pure body. When the sense organs and their objects are thoroughly penetrated, there is no Buddha-dharma;
the *udumbara* flower blooms in the spring of the Ten Continents. (Xiuyan Rui)
Six are not included, and one is not established. Where can the pure Dharma-body be sought? Last night, a gust of wind blew through the leaves;
it swept away all floating clouds, and the moon shone upon the wall. (Closing the room, opening it.)
Yunmen was once asked by a monk, "What is the discourse that transcends Buddhas and patriarchs? The Master said, "A steamed bun.
The Verse says:
The discourse on transcendence is asked about most often by Zen guests; Is it seen when the seams are torn open? Even when the steamed bun is brought forth, it is still not [the answer].
It remains so; to this day, the world is filled with clamor and dispute (Xuedou Xian).
The Son of Heaven provides shade for his descendants; Longtan obtained one. Three generations have swallowed it whole; no one dares to bite through it.
It began when Shao Yang brought it forth; intending to bestow blessings, he instead bestowed calamity.
At that time, there was no one to excise the root of the illness, and until now, it has become a nest of misfortune. (Zhengjue Yi)
Transcending Buddhas and surpassing Patriarchs—how can this be proclaimed? Satiating the midday meal with steamed buns, eating to one’s heart’s content.
In Hunan they spread out their bowls; in Silla they chew. The Arabs and Persians seek a ferryboat. (Ciming Yuan)
Du Chanhe, Du Chanhe! A single steamed bun—what can one do about it? Let your head touch the ground as you prostrate;
the boatman of the Eastern Sea has sailed off to Silla. (Yunfeng Yue)
Yunmen’s hu-buns were small in size; how could they compare to the vast ovens of Fahua? Once full, one may go about as one pleases, even with eyes like a drawn sword;
who asks after the idle Bodhidharma from the West? (Baiyun Cuan)

"Discourse that transcends Buddhas and surpasses patriarchs—presented face-to-face, who will receive it? Not realizing the arrow has already passed over Silla, they needlessly scramble for a piece of bread, shaking the very earth. (Zhenjing Wen)
Shaoyang’s “Humble Cake” in Response to a Zen Practitioner: In the discourse of Buddhas and Patriarchs, the Way is most intimate. It does not fall within the reach of verbal explanations;
cease all conjecture. Turn your head and recognize your own precious treasure. (Yujue You)
He would have soared through the air to ascend the ninefold heavens, yet the red silk beneath his feet held him fast. Fortunately, the Dragon Spring sword had not yet emerged from its scabbard;
thus, he employed a mere lead blade for this single cut. (The Dharma Hall is like this.)
How pitiable and laughable is old Shaoyang! He picks up a piece of rice cake, and its fragrance fills his nostrils.
If one truly knew its flavor, one would be overcome with shame covering one's entire face. (Wenshu said.)
The master’s skillful means do not follow the current. Picking up a sesame cake, he uses it to answer the critical pivot of the teaching.
Even were a monk to transcend the Buddhas and patriarchs, in the end, he would not exchange it for a full, snoring belly. (Huanglong Zhen).
Yunmen’s dialogue on "millet cakes" with Chao—how many practitioners of Chan have failed to see through it?
If one were a true disciple of the Confucian school, one would naturally know that [the Master's disciples] numbered three thousand. (Fodeng Xun)
[Continued Collection]: Yunmen’s single steamed bun is chewed by the monks of the world. Unless one has teeth made of iron, they will often swallow it whole.
It is easy to swallow, but difficult to spit out. Do not say that it has always been just like ordinary flour;
only by treading upon the pivot of Shao Yang can one stir up waves upon level ground. (Cishou Shen).
Chao-t'an spoke of "millet cakes" to suit the occasion; chasing after clods of earth reveals one is no lion’s cub.
When the withered leaves have been swept away by the frosty wind, only then does one see the pine of ancient age through the winter cold. (Shui-an I)
Yunmen was once asked by a monk, "What is the place where all Buddhas emerge? The Master said, "On the water above the mountain to the east. The Verse says:
On the water above the mountain to the east, The place of emergence is most clear. Behold the Buddhas as numerous as motes of dust, As waves surge from all four directions.
(Buddha-Wisdom Spring).
The place where all Buddhas emerge: Water walking atop the Eastern Mountain. A single snap of the fingers before one’s eyes, and the manifestation is clearly revealed.
The Sun-Face and Moon-Face pass by; the Buddha’s hand and the donkey’s feet are displayed. All receive this power of grace, which delivers deluded minds beyond words. (Zhenjing Wen)
The Buddhas walk upon the water in the eastern mountains; they lift their heads and take their steps, yet fall into a deep pit.
Who knows that with but a single foot they drag through mud and water? Failing to realize this, they must travel back ten thousand leagues. (Yunxi Gong)
The place where all Buddhas emerge: walking upon the water of East Mountain. Packing your bags with no companion, you go forth alone toward the journey ahead. (Da Hong Yu)
[Continued Collection] The place where all Buddhas manifest their bodies: Water flows uphill on East Mountain; facing south, one gazes at the Big Dipper;
at noon, the third watch is struck. (Zhandang Zhun)
Walking on water atop Eastern Mountain; a short tunic not dyed black. A withered pine painted on the wall; a donkey eating grass in the back garden.
The thirty-two marks and eighty minor characteristics; bare-chested, bumping into sand bees. Drunk to the point of collapse, falling over one’s clothes (or: the body of Oran).
The place where all Buddhas emerge: Water flows uphill on the eastern mountain; bamboo shoots grow askew beneath the stones;
flowers bloom upside down upon the precipice. (Juebaoqing)
To truly understand "Walking on Water atop Eastern Mountain": by the stream, the stone maiden blows the sheng flute at night; the wooden man holds the board and strikes it amidst the clouds.
A single melody of Liangzhou concludes just as the second watch begins. (Shi’an Shao)
"Up walking on the water at East Mountain; Qianyuan, benefit, firmness, and success. A single character is muddled, and the talented scholars vie with one another for it. (Shu'an Cong)
The place where all Buddhas emerge from the body—how can it be measured in a thousand ways? On East Mountain, one walks upon the water;
in the blink of an eye, one passes beyond Fusang. (Jingsou Jue)
Yunmen was once asked by a monk, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "A dry piece of shit. The Verse says:
I bow my head to the golden countenance, the dry piece of shit; Manifesting forms in response to things like the moon in water. Fragrance and stench both arise from the Buddha’s mouth;
Ordinary and sage alike share the same tongue according to the teaching. (Fujian Qin)
Our Buddha, the Tathāgata, is a dry dung pellet; according to capacity, he is impartial throughout the world.
Those who, deluded, mistake their heads for reflections and toil in vain—though they face his compassionate countenance, they treat it as if it were commonplace. (Tàipíng Gǔ)
The Buddha spoke only of the "dry dung wedge. This not only extracts the nail but also pulls out the wedge.
Were it not for the old master of Shaoyang, how could such intimate words have issued from his own tongue? (Fodeng Xun)
There is no need for translations into Chinese; there is no use for the transmission of Sanskrit. The eyes of Maheśvara face us directly, yet are separated by the Western Heavens. (Gushan Gui)

Yunmen’s “dry shit-stick” completely transcends the Dharma, Reward, and Transformation bodies. With nothing to do, he goes out into the mountains to roam, with a hundred coins hanging from the head of his staff. (Jingshan Daoyuan)
The questions are clear and the answers fresh; half smiling, half appearing angry. Look at the roads in the second and third months:
which branch does not bear spring? (By Huīyīn Jìng).
[Continued Collection] Shao Yang’s “Dry Dung”: For many years it has been as hard as iron. It is laughable that Han-lu the hound can do nothing about it;
he barks and whines in resentment at the moon in the heavens. (Dian Niu You)
Cloud Gate (Yunmen) lets out a great lion’s roar; he takes his innermost heart and carves it open for whom? His eyes are like falling stars, yet people remain bewildered;
madmen chase after stench, vying to know what exists. Do you not see? Yantou had these words:
"A dog that bites on a dung-stick is no good dog. (Lan’an Xu)
When asked, the Buddha replied, "A dried piece of excrement. This clear principle is difficult to clarify or refute.
The Vajra sword kills people upside down; for blunt steel, one uses only Silla iron. (Mongan Yue)
Yunmen, that little servant boy, lets out a great lion’s roar; he has gained half of his nostrils, yet he does not know he has lost his mouth. (Songyuan Yue)
"Nothing but a dry piece of dung. Yunmen was far too talkative. He has exhausted all the mechanisms before one's eyes;
empty space spurts forth blood. (Duan’an Chang)
A monk asked Yunmen, "What is it like when the trees wither and the leaves fall? The Master said, "The body is exposed to the golden wind.

He then offered this verse: "The question has its source; the answer is likewise in accord. The three phrases may be distinguished: a single arrow-point pierces the vast void. Over the great wilds, the cool breeze blows."

The wind whistles; across the vast sky, the drizzling rain falls mistily. Do you not see the guest who has sat for so long at Shaolin and has not yet returned, quietly leaning against Mount Xiong’er in its dense thickets? (Xuedou Xian)
The golden wind is revealed in its essence, pervading every place; why wait for leaves to fall before one knows autumn?
On the Clear Wind Tower, the events of those years remain as they were, and even now the laughter does not cease. (Master Quan Daodao).
The question sets forth the heading; the answer penetrates the core of the inquiry. The tree withers and its leaves fall; the essence is revealed by the golden wind.
If you wish to recognize Old Yunmen now, after autumn, the frosty forest turns entirely red. (Lingyuan Qing)
While practicing the causal path, do not let your arms dangle; seeking from others is not as good as seeking within oneself.

The mountain crags before one’s eyes still remain; everywhere, no wind stirs the waves. Suddenly, the cry of a wild goose is heard—all is contained within the nest of the sorrowful person. (Changling Zhuo)
When do the trees wither and their leaves fall? The body is exposed to the golden wind on a September day. True Suchness fills the eyes, yet people do not realize it;
across the entire valley, the wind and moon are perfectly serene. (Fojian Qín)
A cool breeze falls upon the trees as the autumn mountains of Chu stir; Cicadas fill the branches, chirping incessantly in the cold. Red smartweeds and white pondweed bloom along both banks;
I know not who dwells within this fishing boat. (Fóxìng Tái)
The essence of the golden wind is revealed; what more need be said? The Great Way has from the beginning been free from change. A single leaf drifts through the void as the sky becomes like water;
at the river’s edge, people call for the ferryman’s boat. (By Baiyang Shun)
[Continued Collection] When skin and fur have fallen away entirely, only the true reality remains. The whole body reveals the golden wind, transcending beyond the three phrases. (Benjue 1)
Silent, desolate, and utterly empty; throughout the world, yellow leaves fall in profusion. East, west, south, and north—there is no obstruction;
across the ten-thousand-li expanse of the long sky, a solitary falcon soars. (Zhai-an Xian)
The tree withers and its leaves fall; I offer this inquiry in jest. The body is exposed to the golden wind, yet one mistakenly traces its tracks.
This brings trouble upon descendants who fail to undergo the transformation of a leopard. In an ordinary moment, they fall into the thicket of weeds. (Tianmu Li).
Yunmen was once asked by a monk, "If one does not give rise to a single thought, is there still transgression?
The Master said, "Mount Sumeru. The verse says:
Not giving rise to a single thought—how could this penetrate the Source? Truth and falsehood are distinguished within a single phrase. Striking it, flowers bloom; both are closed off.
Mouth. Mount Sumeru serves as a screen directly before one’s face (Dongshan Cong).
When thoughts do not arise, Mount Sumeru stands firm; traveling upon its perilous paths is difficult. They vie with one another to gaze far upward toward the gateway of the sea.
The four oceans are vast and boundless; the seven golden mountains are cold. (Zhengjue Yi).
The author’s mastery is total and never in vain; responding to conditions, he brings forth Mount Sumeru. When people reach their limit, they cannot attain the adamantine boundary;
year after year, they pursue one another, laboring upon the road. (Huanglong Nan).
A single thought does not arise; Mount Sumeru stands firm. To follow words and chase after phrases makes understanding increasingly difficult. The scarlet-tailed carp has been its lifelong pursuit;
it is only because of an ordinary person grasping the fishing rod. (Yang Woei-wei)
Mount Sumeru blocks the universe; the Great Compassionate One with a thousand eyes cannot see through it.
Unless one can personally master the art of riding a cow backward, one will spend a lifetime following after others. (Baizhang Yuan).
Standing before a ten-thousand-fathom peak is most unconventional; in the blink of an eye, one falls over the precipice.
He whose entire body is not harmed by so much as a single hair—neither in heaven nor among men shall he be buried. (Baoning Yong)
The questions and answers followed his impulses, sometimes shallow and sometimes profound; Yunmen was truly one who had fully saturated the monastic groves.
Nowadays, people compete and scramble like those running around Mount Sumeru; countless ordinary people are submerged in the depths. (Fotu Xun)
Without giving rise to a single thought, Mount Sumeru surges from the sea; take it up and use it immediately—no need for other needles or awls (Zhenjing Wen).
Skillfully responding to the occasion is difficult for the artist; the eyebrows and whiskers are boundless yet manifest on the tip of a hair.
Coming from the West, he passed by with his brows knit; the Persian from the South gazed upward (Zhaojue Zong).
Mount Sumeru towers high, difficult to behold; mists and waters stretch vast as ten-thousand fathoms converge.
If you wish to seek the ultimate point of Yunmen, seize the clear breeze and ask one question. (Dizang En)
A single thought, deep and silent, transcends existence and non-existence; stretching across the void, it brings forth the Great Mount Meru.
Even if the jade hare and golden crow were to suddenly traverse the palaces, they would fall halfway through their journey. (Zhang Wujin)
Majestic and towering is this single Mount Sumeru; bearing such a weight is no matter of coarse physical strength.
Even if one cannot comprehend it through words and speech, one must still come face-to-face to receive the smearing of mud. (Jingshan Gaofeng)
A bright mirror stands upon its stand, as still as water; Without cause, it suddenly gives rise to dust and grime. Accumulated until mountains and peaks stand before one’s face;
Even the Great Compassionate One with a thousand hands cannot tear them apart. (Fóxìng Tàiyǔ)
When a single wave stirs, the myriad waves follow; in the drowning maelstrom of the mundane world, how few know this?
Lofty Mount Sumeru spans the universe—by whom else can such wondrous, all-pervading function be exercised? (Sushan Ru).

【Continued Collection】 Not giving rise to a single thought—this is the Way. It is said: "Sumeru is but a morsel of flesh on the tip of the tongue; the lips are but two pieces of skin. Yunmen’s functional pivot is as wondrous as this:
it does not fall into the categories of right and wrong, or knowing and not knowing. (Tiantong Jue)

Stone sprouts send forth shoots; the mud ox roars at the moon. Who would have thought that those on the same boat are as far apart as Hu and Yue? When responding to conditions, Mount Sumeru surges forth;
when not a single thought arises, where is there any snow to clear? The Vajra sword cuts straight through the head. (Wenyu Qin)
A single thought does not arise—Mount Sumeru. Standing out alone at the head, look directly with your eyes. Taking up a single strand of thread, he lightly trips him over.
At the door of every house, one passes through Chang’an. (Shui-an Yi)

Without giving rise to a single thought, he stands out like Mount Sumeru; neither sage nor ordinary person can discern him. This ancient master (Songyuan Yue) was asked by a monk: "What is the pure Dharma-body? The Master said: "A flower garden railing. [The monk] asked: "How is it when one goes directly like this? The Master said: "A golden-maned lion. The Verse says: A flower garden railing—how vast! A golden-maned lion—how majestic! If you can see through these two lines, You will know the old master’s meaning. The pure Dharma-body is not something to be sought; It is right here before your very eyes. If you can recognize it at once, You will transcend the three realms of existence. If you hesitate for even a moment, You will fall into the pit of birth and death. Do not seek it elsewhere— It is right within your own mind. If you can understand this, You will be free from all doubt. This is the teaching of the Buddhas and Patriarchs; It is the essential point of the ancestral school. If you can grasp it in a single stroke, You will be like a dragon leaping from the water. If you do not understand, You will remain a prisoner of delusion. Do not look for it in scriptures or commentaries; Do not seek it in words or phrases. If you can see it clearly, You will realize the Way yourself. This is the true transmission of the Buddhas and Patriarchs; It is the ultimate truth of the ancestral school. Do not be careless with the flower vases; the star is in the scales, not on the plate.
To proceed thus is utterly groundless. Behold the golden-maned lion! (Xuědòu Xiǎn)
The wandering traveler rushes about, finding no moment of rest; he knows only to pursue song and joy outside his gate. His own fields have long been neglected and overgrown;
he looks only at the flower and herb gardens of the world. (From *Kumu cheng*)
In this place, there is a flower and medicinal herb garden in the third month of spring; the Chan practitioners of the Five Lakes need not look at it.
Seeking branches and plucking leaves will make it difficult to understand; observe closely the distinct fangs and claws. (Yunxi Gong)
The springtime splendor of Jingu Valley fills the eyes; the red *yao* flowers hang with their fragrance in profusion.
Last night a gust of west wind brought a chill, and now fallen petals cover the ground in countless numbers. The young nobles lie drunk and do not know to return home;
they still reach for golden cups by the balustrade. (Shangfang Yi)
The pure Dharma-body is a flower-and-medicine railing; the eyebrows pierce and topple Mount Sumeru.
Who has taken up the jade flute to transmit its plaintive sorrow? Blowing past the reeds, the bright moon is curved. (By Fozhi Yu)
[Continued Collection] The Flower-Railing of the Pure Dharmakāya: Clearly manifest, not deceiving by even a single point. Who can grasp its meaning within the spring breeze?
When the time comes, look closely before the steps. (Retired Plowman Ning)
A monk asked Yunmen, “What is the student’s own self? The Master said, “Wandering through mountains and enjoying the waters. The monk asked, “What is the Master’s own self?

The Master said, “Fortunately, the *karmadāna* is not here. The verse says: Wandering through mountains and enjoying the waters— Fortunately, the *karmadāna* is not here. If you wish to know the Master’s own self, Look at the clouds and the moon.
Before Mount Nanyue and behind Mount Jing, the sound of the waterfalls roars like thunder and lightning.
Casting off his straw hat, he walks with his head bared; treading upon his grass sandals, he runs barefoot. (Fohuiquan)
When a student of the Way wanders through mountains and plays by the waters, they know only to tread until their straw sandals are worn through,
forgetting their age when they first set out (Yang Woei).

Wandering through mountains and playing by the waters, one must investigate the fundamental principle; do not treat it as a mere pastime. Wandering through mountains and playing by the waters—(Huangbo Sheng).
With a staff of bamboo, one walks beneath the trees upon the mossy ground; the toil of a restless life has yet to open its eyes.
How wonderful it is that falling flowers follow the green water, all at once flowing out from within the cave—(Dizang En).

Wandering through mountains and playing by the waters is but an ordinary affair; morning and evening I return, my hair already like frost. Treading through worn-out straw sandals, I turn my head to look back:
the sound of several cries from a monkey echoes through the land of white clouds. (By Ning of Kaifu)
[Continued Collection] Wandering mountains and playing by waters are as numerous as hemp seeds; who recognizes the old master of Shaoyang?
He has cut off the three-inch tongue of the lame monk; turning one’s head, it is all but one’s former life. (Kentang Chong)
Wandering and playing in the water—ten thousand, ten million, a thousand, a hundred—who has penetrated Shao Yang’s words that carry the profound within them? (Tieshan Ren).
Morning in the Western Heaven, evening in the Eastern Land; wandering in the water and roaming the mountains, strolling with unhurried steps—this is the immovable site of enlightenment.
It is not that it is also within; who can serve as witness? Shishuang’s "Horned Tiger" (Daitang Ding) says:
"The Elder Wang of East Village has never seen this before; he takes another person's field and calls it his own land."

(Severing Phenomena and Reflecting). Yunmen was once asked by a monk: "If one kills one's father and mother, one repents before the Buddha; but where does one repent for killing the Buddhas and the Patriarchs? The Master said: "Exposed. The Verse says: Severing phenomena and reflecting, The great matter is right here. Killing the Buddhas and Patriarchs— Where is there any place to repent? A single word, "Exposed," Is like a bright mirror. If you can see through it, You will not fall into the pit of the two vehicles. If you cannot see through it, You will surely sink into the sea of birth and death. This is the Great Matter of the Buddhas and Patriarchs. How could it be something else? If you wish to understand this matter, You must first sever all conceptualizations. If you can sever them, Then you will naturally be free from delusion. If you do not sever them, You will surely be caught in the net of views. Therefore, Yunmen’s "Exposed" Is like a sword that cuts through the clouds. If you can see through it, You will immediately attain liberation. If you cannot see through it, You will remain bound by the traces of words. This is the teaching of the Buddhas and Patriarchs. Do not seek it elsewhere. If you seek it elsewhere, You will wander in birth and death forever. Therefore, you must sever all conceptualizations. Only then will you be able to see. If you can see, You will realize the Way of the Buddhas and Patriarchs. If you cannot see, You will be lost in the darkness of ignorance. This is the Great Matter of the Buddhas and Patriarchs. Do not doubt it. If you have no doubt, You will immediately attain liberation. If you have doubt, You will remain bound by the traces of words. Therefore, you must sever all conceptualizations. The spark from flint and the falling star were never so swift; how slow is the turning of the celestial sphere and the flash of lightning!
A character revealed through the clouds suddenly emerges; when you look directly at it, the hawk is already in flight. (Zhengjue Yi)

Stirring up dust and scattering soil, there is no place to take refuge; leading the gate straight before the imperial tower, one turns the head and sees not the path by which one came—below is the Yellow Springs, above is Heaven. (Baiyun Yuan).
Lù. Transcending the school and surpassing the patriarchs—people say he burns the "returning-soul" incense; I say he beats the "poison-coating" drum.
(Tiantong Jue) [Continued Collection] The heavy gate with its golden lock requires no key; without moving the root of the tongue, Shaoyang already knew. (Dianniu You)

Beating gongs and drums, they turn the prow of the boat; like a sweeping wind, waves overturn as they shout through the surging current. Barefoot, they board the vessel to take advantage of the swift opportunity;
with a favorable breeze, they are sent off downstream toward Yangzhou. (Wan’an Yan)
Yunmen’s bare exposure was as fierce as a tiger; Master Bodhidharma was no patriarch. Have you not seen the old man of Yanguan?
He took Mount Sumeru for a mallet and empty space for a drum. And have you not seen the old man of Heshan who knew how to beat the drum?
Enough with such crude confusion! A sweet melon is sweet to its very stem; a bitter gourd is bitter from root to tip. (A shout) — Ying’an Hua.
The Dipper shifts as wind and thunder roar; the stars move as mountains and rivers darken. Who knows that beneath this scholar’s cap lies none other than the sorrowful man of old? (Tuigou Yun)
Yunmen was once asked by a monk, "What is the True Dharma Eye? The Master said, "Pervasive. Fengxue said, "Blind.
Huanglong Xin said, "Say 'blind' again; at least that way we can see each other. The verse says: Pervasive. Blind. Say "blind" again. At least that way we can see each other.
The single character "Pǔ" (Universal) is by no means ordinary; lift your head and look at the flash of lightning.
If you hesitate to deliberate or give rise to intellectual understanding, alas, it is like gouging out flesh to create a wound upon your own body. (Dongshan Cong)
The single character "Pǔ" (Universal) is naturally distinct; when viewed with fixed eyes, it is like a flash of lightning. The vast universe is boundless, leaving no place to seek it;
yet when one steps upon the scale-weight, it is as hard as iron. (Zhengjue Yi).
To speak of the Buddha and his teaching at such length is like adding a point to an arrow—how utterly foolish!
A clear-eyed monk sees it from the side: a single staff carried by two people. (Dafu Zhi)
Coming from the summit—truly blind indeed. Illuminating heaven and reflecting the earth, they do not exist at the same time.
Do not raise your hands within the Great Compassionate One’s palms; walking alone at night, who can know it? (Baizhang Yuan).
Simply being without any mind, one naturally accords with the Great Way. Its application depends on the occasion; do not differentiate between what is subtle and what is not. (Zhenjingwen)
Responding to the capacity of the occasion, Old Shaoyang never emerged; Fayan’s inquiry was met with the word "Pu.
Had this opportunity not been for a true son of the Lion, it would have been but a dream passing through the Xiao and Xiang rivers. (Yuantong Xian)
[Continued Collection] Zhengfayan Pu: Many clever monks err in their citations. Do not err in your citations. Winter solstice to Cold Food Festival is one hundred and five days. (Yang Woei-wu).
Brightness and darkness are paired as illumination and function are divided; how many people have personally reached the gate of Mengchang?
Not recognizing the true Maitreya on the street, one instead asks the World-Honored One at Vulture Peak. (Xiatang Yuan)
Yunmen was once asked by a monk, "What is the mechanism of the simultaneous pecking and hatching? The Master said, "An echo. Verse:
When asked about the mechanism of pecking and hatching, Yunmen replied, "An echo. Yesterday thunder shook the heavens; Last night the mountain waters rose high.

(Zhenjingwen): The mechanism of the "peck and hatch" responds with a word; like thunder and lightning passing through the void, it suddenly pours down from the heights. Last night, the torrential rain fell across the heavens;
in many places, waves and billows struck the fishing boats. (Yuantongxian)
[Continued Collection]: The White Ox asks the Cat; Empty Space answers the Myriad Phenomena. Like lightning, its trace does not linger; in the hollow valley, who responds to the echo?
*Chup!* *Zuo!*—the pure mechanism is experienced within the palm. Turning one's head, one treads upon the patterns of the Qin era.
The entanglements upon the tongue grow ten thousand feet long. (Xinwen Ben).

One sip and one peck; the resonance meets head-on. The mother does not leave her nest, yet the chick has already emerged from its shell. (Severing the traces of conceptual mirrors. Yunmen was once asked by a monk, "What is the Sword of Yunmen? The Master said, "The Patriarch. Verse: One sip and one peck, the sound meets head-on. The mother does not leave her nest, yet the chick has already emerged from its shell. The sword of Yunmen is the Patriarch. A single phrase cuts through all doubts. The thousand sages are reduced to ashes. The three vehicles are left behind. The Great Way is right here before you. The whole world is contained within a single hair. The ten directions are encompassed in a single thought. The great function is manifest in this very moment. The ancient mirror shines brightly. The moon reflects in the water. The wind blows across the mountains. The vast sky is clear and open. The bright pearl is revealed. The golden needle pierces the eye. The iron hammerhead smashes the skull. The Great Matter is settled at once. The source of all things is revealed. The meaning is exhausted in a single word. The truth is present in every action. The ancient path is wide and open. Cloud Gate was asked about the "hair-cutting" precious sword: "When one who comes meets the opportunity, how could it remain? When meeting a swordsman on the road, what then?
The person in the steamer joins hands and flees southward. (Beitang Zu)
The precious sword that shaves hair need not be drawn; its pure light, bursting from the scabbard, pierces the Dipper and Ox constellations.
Its full manifestation in daily life is unseen by people; Yunmen’s patriarchal character shall repay you. (Yunxi Gong)
Three feet of autumn light are hidden within the case; when meeting a master, its edge and brilliance are revealed.
Now that the smoke of war has settled across the four frontiers, he unfurls no red banner as he returns to his native land. (Yuantong Xian)

[Added from the Supplement] Yunmen was once asked by a monk, "What is the 'hair-blistering sword'? The Master said, "Bone. He also said, "Flesh. The verse says: Bones. Flesh. The hair-blistering sword is truly sharp; It cuts through all things without leaving a trace. If you ask what it is like, I say: it is not even a hair's breadth. How could it ever compare to the sword of the Yellow Emperor? It is simply the sword of the Buddha. The Buddha’s sword is the sword of the patriarchs; The patriarchs’ sword is the sword of the Buddhas. If you can see it clearly, Then you will know its true form. If you cannot see it clearly, Then you will fall into the pit of doubt. Do not seek it in words or phrases; Do not look for it in the scriptures. If you can understand this directly, Then you will see the Buddha’s true face. If you do not understand this directly, Then you will remain lost in the dark. This is the hair-blistering sword of Yunmen; It cuts through the root of all delusion. If you can grasp it in an instant, Then you will transcend birth and death. If you hesitate for a moment, Then you will be pierced by the cold steel. Do not seek it in the external world; Seek it within your own mind. If you can see it clearly, Then you will attain liberation. If you do not see it clearly, Then you will remain bound. This is the hair-blistering sword of Yunmen; It is the sword that cuts through the three realms. If you can wield it with ease, Then you will be a true master. If you cannot wield it with ease, Then you are but a common man. Do not seek it in the external world; Seek it within your own mind. Yunmen was asked by a monk, "Is it true that the Buddha-dharma is like the moon in the water? The Master said, "In the clear waves, there is no path to penetrate. The monk asked, "From where did you, Master, obtain this?

The Master said, "If you ask again, from where would it come? The monk asked, "At such a time as this, what is it? The Master said, "Layer upon layer, the mountain passes and roads. The verse says: The clear waves leave no path to pass through; From where could you have obtained it? If you ask again, from where would it come? At such a time, it is the layered mountain passes and roads.
It is evident that the moon in the water is not difficult to grasp; it is simply that people of this age do not touch it with their own hands. Old Master Shao Shi has brought it forth;
though the mountain passes are layered and deep, its radiance is ever more fresh and new. (Baiyun Yuan).
Pervading the entire realm, nothing is hidden; the clear waves are serene and still. Exchanging blows to meet the occasion, the arrowheads point directly at one another.
Grasping the tongs of the ultimate upward path—where even sparks from flint and flashes of lightning cannot reach—one is thus separated by mountains and passes.
In the azure depths beyond the clouds, there is no connection. (Yuánwù Qín)
[Continued Collection] Only when the life-root is exhausted can the gate be closed. One push, one squeeze; like lightning flashing and thunder rolling. The Buddha-dharma is like the moon in water;
it is spoken from within the ears and the eyes. To err by a hair’s breadth is to lose by a thousand miles. How many times have we known this in the north, south, east, and west? (By Chō of Gattō).
In the clear waves there is no path through; few know the point of turning. Having hewn down the cassia tree in the moon, to whom shall the pure light be entrusted? (Zantang Shen)

Yunmen addressed the assembly, saying: "Medicine and illness treat one another. The entire earth is medicine; which of these is the self? Verse: The avoidance of medicine has long been a test for masters;
Their instruction of disciples is intimate, yet illnesses are as numerous as hemp. All those who know throughout the ten directions and three periods of time...
Consciousness is like a thundering chariot amidst the blazing light of the sun (Fifth Patriarch’s Precept).
The mutual treatment of medicine and disease is truly lamentable; how can one fall into the ranks of the heterodox regarding this? Before a word is spoken, who can discern the truth?
By the time the mouth opens, the sprouts of conceptualization are already visible. Do not dwell on thoughts or engage in idle speculation; it is merely a vain exertion of biased views.
In chaotic confusion. There are many such as these in the world; their lack of shame is as numerous as hemp seeds.
(Beitazuo): "The entire earth is medicine. How great is the error of past and present! One need not close the door to build a carriage; the thoroughfare is naturally vast and open.
Mistaken, mistaken! The nostrils reach the heavens, yet they have been pierced through (Xuedou Xian).

With the left eye one sees neither mountains nor rivers; with the right eye one sees neither sun nor moon. It reaches the point that when the hundred flowers bloom, each and every one shall be distinguished for you (Baiyun Yuan).
【Continued Collection】The fingers emerge from within the sleeves; the beak is exposed in the water. The fingers bend and the eyes open; the beak wags and the body rises.
Medicine and disease do not treat one another—what need is there for the entire earth? One might as well laugh at old Yunmen for losing his mother-born nose. (Yuet Tang Chang)
Exceedingly clamorous and chaotic, yet fully encompassing both killing and giving life; there is no one to take it up, nor anything to be sought after.
The spirit within the realm, the strategy beyond the pass—retreating three thousand li. The entire great earth is medicine. A mistake, a mistake! The seven-starred sharp sword flashes with light.
(Yuanwu Keqin). Yunmen asked a monk, "The radiant, tranquil illumination pervades the sands of the Ganges—this is not the speech of the scholar Zhang Zhuo?
The monk said, "It is. The Master said, "Your words have fallen into error. The Verse says:
Leaves and paths crisscrossing, one attains freedom; the sturdy lock is turned, the wondrous function fully gathered. Within this, the secret meaning is difficult for people to comprehend;
with a shout, one must cause the water to flow backward. (Heshan Fang)
Ten-thousand-foot Dragon Gate, its momentum leaning against the void; letting go at the precipice to distinguish the fish from the dragons.
People of this age look only upon the fishing line, failing to see the reeds facing the red dock-herbs. (Yue’an Guo)
Question comes and answer goes, without partiality; how can one pass through the iron walls and silver mountains? Seizing and relinquishing according to the occasion, words fall into the trap;
thus, for a thousand ages, the wind of sorrow stirs. (Shushan Ru).
[Continued Collection] Bestowing and taking away proceed together to determine right and wrong; Shao Yang’s application is too solitary and precarious.
If this monk were granted the Vajra Eye, the Zhao jade and the city of Lin would return as one. (Master Min, the Ancient Buddha).
I have clearly written it out for you to see: the meaning lies on the hook, not on the platter.
Even if a stone man could open his mouth, he would still be deceived by his own tongue. (Songyuan Yue)
When one is at the capital, one sighs with deep sorrow; had one’s breathing been correct, the people of the world would not have been killed by error. (Shigumiyi).

In every place, green willows are fit for tethering horses; at every household door, one can see through to Chang'an.
The great highway is as level as the palm of a hand; it is simply that people find it difficult to set foot upon it. (Cishou Shen)
Your waters flow toward the east; the waters of Chu flow from the south. Both return to the great ocean, where salt and fresh become one single taste.
A patch-robed monk who possesses the eye at the crown of his head—try to distinguish shallow from deep within this. (Fóxìng Tái)
The entire great treasury of the teachings speaks of this very thing. Yunmen’s “It blows down” — what is it?
Even if you were to thoroughly penetrate the source here, by the time you blink your eyes, you have already missed it. (Zeweng Yan)
[Added from the Supplementary Collection] A monk asked Yunmen, "When birth and death arrive, how can one dispel them? The Master extended his hand and said, "Give me back birth and death.

(An alternative version reads: "When birth and death arrive, how can one avoid them? The Master said, "Where are they? The Verse says: When the questioner asks about birth and death, The Master extends his hand to show it clearly. If you can understand this within a single thought, Then you will see that there is no place for it to dwell.
A needle-eye fish swallows the great chiliocosm; a gnat spits out Mount Sumeru. The vast void encompasses all without exception;
the myriad phenomena are entirely contained within one’s fingertips. Rising and ceasing, departing and returning—the path across the stone bridge is severed, and the whole body is black.
Which is Huading? Which is Tiantai? (Yuanwu Keqin)
Hungry, one eats rice; weary, one sleeps. Beyond the walls of Chang’an, a vast expanse of level fields—devoid of center or periphery, transcending words and explanations.
The general does not recognize his steed, the black Zui; the rhinoceros at the bottom of the sea whips its own horn. (Daitangding)
[Added for inclusion] Yunmen was once asked by a monk: "At the end of summer and the beginning of autumn, if someone on the road ahead asks you a question, how will you respond?
The Master said, "The assembly, step back. The monk asked, "I do not understand; where does the fault lie? The Master said: [The assembly, step back.]
"Return to me the ninety days' worth of rice money! The Verse says: The assembly steps back;
the monk’s conduct—how could it rely on mechanical devices? How could it permit conceptual investigation? The old fisherman, weathered by experience, is accustomed to wind and waves;
he does not employ oars or rudders, but lets his boat drift with the current. (Tiantong Ju)
At the end of summer and the beginning of autumn, tens of millions upon tens of millions. The path of Stonehead is slippery; one’s sandals are worn through.
This monk flips swiftly over the edge of a sword, yet even he must pay Yunmen for his meal (Shitian Xun).
[Added for inclusion] Yunmen was once asked by a monk, "What is the matter that lies beyond the Dharma-body? The Master said, "It is not difficult to tell you what lies beyond;
how will you understand the Dharma-body? [The monk] said, "I ask the Master to examine this for me. The Master said:
Jian said, "Set that aside for now. How do you understand the Dharma-body? The monk replied, "Just so, just so. The Master said, "This is merely what you have learned on the long benches.
Let me ask you: does the Dharma-body know how to eat? The monk was speechless. The verse says: Just so, just so— This is what you’ve learned on the long benches.
I ask you now: Does the Dharma-body know how to eat? The monk had no reply.
A single gulp of the West River leaves no trace; the Tathāgatas of the three ages swallow it all in one mouth.
Phoenix marrow and dragon liver, the fragrant food of Saṃghāṭa—having tasted them all in myriad ways, there is no need for further discussion. (Nantang Xing, III)
The spiritual pivot of Shaoyang was like a sudden clap of thunder. When a monk asked whether the Dharmakaya eats food or not, those who merely parrot words could not suddenly utter an answer.
Mountains, rivers, and the great earth served as a mere meal; the four seas and five lakes were swallowed in a single gulp.
Failing to recognize Yunmen’s upward-moving pivot, you merely seek his downward-turning words and give rise to doubt. How can one eat when one’s entire body is rice?
Having no mouth from the start, one has never been hungry.
[Added for inclusion: Yunmen asked a newly arrived monk, "Where are you from? The monk replied, "A man from Silla. The Master said, "What did you bring across the sea?
The monk said, "The grass bandits were utterly defeated. The Master said, "Why are they in my hands? The monk said, "Exactly so.
The Master said, "Plop! [The monk] had no reply. Benjue once remarked: "These two have heads."
The "Tale of the Tailless Man. He then offered this verse:
"A monk from Silla is rarely encountered; when inquiring about the wind and moon, they are much the same. A pity that for a mountain one strives with but a single basket of earth;
In vain do host and guest exert themselves, each achieving no merit."

[Added for inclusion] Yunmen said, "A fortune-teller in a village of three households divines here and there; even if he suddenly hits upon the truth, it is not certain. A monk then asked, "What is it like when he suddenly hits upon the truth?

The Master said, "I humbly submit. The Verse says: A fortune-teller in a village of three households, Divining east and west, Suddenly hitting upon the truth—still not certain. When suddenly hitting upon the truth, I humbly submit.
Selling divinations in a village of three households, he discerns the origins of good fortune, misfortune, calamity, and blessing.
Suddenly, when a monk comes to consult him, he answers the matter of life and death with a single phrase. (Benjue I)

Raising his hand to grasp the Southern Dipper, shifting his body to lean against the Northern Pole; to look out from beyond the heavens, one must be a person of this caliber. (Shui’an I)
The sound is like clinking jade at the quiet frontier gate; who would believe that a recluse does not see you? When the flowers reach the *haitang*, they are about to fall into stillness;
yet the embroidered robe is still perfumed with musk. (Xutang Yu)
When the General’s command was issued, the banners flashed; the Hu cavalry were thrown into disarray, their majesty utterly lost.
Though there were those who suddenly displayed great prowess and speed, they did not realize their own bodies were already trapped within a heavy encirclement. (Duanqiao Lun)
[Added for inclusion] Yunmen addressed the assembly, saying: "The ancient Buddha intersects with the pillar; what is this? What is its level of response? A monk remained silent. The Master said:
"You ask, and I will tell you. The monk then asked. The Master said: "Thirty coins for a single cord. [The monk asked:
"What is 'thirty coins for a single cord'? The Master said: "Give him a beating! [This was the Master’s own substitute answer.]
The previous statement said: "Clouds rise on the southern mountain; it rains on the northern mountain. The verse says:
Clouds on the southern mountain, rain on the northern mountain; the four, seven, two, and three look upon one another's faces. A monk from Silla enters the hall.
In the land of the Great Tang, before the drum has even been struck, there is suffering within joy and joy within suffering. Who says that gold is like dross?
(Xuedou Xian). A single divine light is from the beginning unrevealed; it transcends both views and conditions, being thus yet without "thusness," and it exceeds the measure of the mundane mind.
When there is no "being appropriate," the pollen of cliff-flowers becomes honey in the bees' cells; the growth of wild grasses becomes fragrance in the musk deer's navel.
According to their kind, they are three feet or sixteen feet tall—vividly, everywhere they appear, they are manifest and majestic. (Tiantong Jue)
Gathering clouds over the Southern Mountains; pouring rain upon the Northern Mountains. The dew-pillar laughs "he-he"; the lantern transcends the Buddhas and Patriarchs.
Rising in the center and sinking at the edges—India and China alike. The gates of the pavilions stand open all day long;
the village elder does not know where he has gone. (Wenyu Qín).
The head of the ancient Buddha supports the heavens; the stone pillar’s feet tread upon the earth. From antiquity to the present, they have formed a single body.
His head supports the heavens while wearing a cap; his feet tread the earth without sandals. Together they attend the midday meal at the Hall of Great Compassion. (Fujian Qin)

[Added for inclusion] Yunmen once said: "The lantern is you yourself; the one who holds the bowl and eats rice is not you yourself.
A monk asked, "What is it like when the rice is oneself? The Master said, "This wild fox spirit, a fellow from a village of three households.
The Master then said, "Come, come! It is not that you say the rice is [yourself]."
[The student] said, "It is I. The Master said, "When will you ever dream of a fellow from a village of three houses?
The Verse says: All day long he eats his rice, yet prizes his own effort; He does not recognize that the lantern is the alms bowl.
How many fellows from villages of three houses Frantically catch catfish upon the trees! (Cishou Shen)
