In years past, I once knocked at Muzhou’s barrier; I have been ungrateful for his kindness and taken it for granted. I hear that even his Wu dialect has changed completely;
his speech now sounds just like that of the barbarians from Guangnan. (Xutang Yu)
[Added from the Supplement] Yunmen was once asked by a monk: "What is it like when one brushes away the dust and sees the Buddha?
The Master said: "The Buddha is also dust. Wan’an Yan served as the West Hall Abbot at Lushan Yuan Tong.

While leading the assembly into the meditation hall for private instruction, he raised this *gong'an* and questioned Ciyuan An. As soon as Ciyuan let out a shout, Wan’an struck his chest with his hand and said: "The Buddha is also..."
Dust. Again, he recited a verse:
"Shake off the dust to see the Buddha; the Buddha, too, is but dust. Question ended, answer ended—turning over directly beneath. I urge you to drink one more cup of wine:
Once you have passed the Yang Pass to the west, there will be no old friends."
[Added from the Supplementary Collection] A monk asked Yunmen, “What is the single path of Yunmen? The Master said, “Intimacy. The Verse says:
Yunmen’s single path is intimacy; Not a speck of dust can enter the eye. Since the era of war and weapons in the Five Dynasties, How many have seen such peace and prosperity? (Yang Wuwe)

[Added from the Supplementary Collection] Yunmen addressed the assembly, saying: "The staff has transformed into a dragon and swallowed up the universe. Where do the mountains, rivers, and the great earth come from? Verse: The staff transforms into a dragon; It swallows the universe whole.
Mountains, rivers, and the vast earth— From where could they have come?
The staff swallows heaven and earth; it is in vain to speak of rushing through the peach-blossom waves. Those who "burn their tails" do not need to seize the clouds or snatch the mist;
those who "expose their scales" need not lose heart or forget their souls. Having taken it up, whether heard or not, one must simply be free and easy;
do not continue to be confused and distracted. Forgive these seventy-two blows for now—there are one hundred and fifty more.
Hard to let go of you. (Xuedou Xian) Having nurtured the transformative material of Huanglong, suddenly there is a clap of thunder on level ground.
Intending to show it face-to-face to others, he swallows up heaven and earth and spits it back out. (Fujian Qin)
The staff of the patch-robed monk is a dragon, yet it is not revered; held crosswise, it swallows Buddhas and patriarchs; grasped upside down, it shakes heaven and earth.
With eyes that have pupils and skin that has blood, one must truly receive a mark for every blow.
Let the tabby cat and the white ox stop their mocking; right now, serving intimately, there are no descendants. (Touzi Shu)
[Added from the Supplementary Collection] A monk asked Yunmen, “What is it like when there has been long rain and no clearing?
The Master said, “Zha! The Verse says: Long rain with no clearing; Yunmen says, “Zha! The wild geese cry out as they spread their wings;
the dragons withdraw their scales and manes. Is this the season? Is it the Buddha-dharma? One arrow hitting two targets—do not vainly speculate. The pupils in the eyes; the eyebrows drooping.
(Fo-zhi Yu): Yunmen’s single stroke—this blade of hair that shines through its scabbard; had it not been for Zhang Hua, all this would have been in vain, mere blinking of eyes.
(Yuepo Ming). [Added by Zeng].
Yunmen asked a monk, "Where have you recently come from? The monk replied, "Xichan. The Master said, "What words or phrases did Xichan have?
The monk spread his two hands. The Master gave him a slap and said, "I still have your story. The Master then spread his own two hands.
[The Master] struck him with his hand. The monk remained silent; the Master struck him again. The Verse says:
Head and tail of the tiger gathered at once; A formidable wind blows through the four hundred prefectures.
Yet he asks: "Why was it so perilous? The Master says: "I let one move pass. (Xuedou Xian)
When the mountain was about to be completed, he did not advance even a single basketful of earth. Old and decrepit Yunmen sat and reaped the benefit.

His skill in hooking sea turtles and catching whales is sublime; he has long been accustomed to descending into the ocean and traversing the waves. Releasing slowly and pulling swiftly, he finds his own ease;
drifting like a house upon the water, how carefree he is! (By Yuet Tang Chang).

[Added from the Supplementary Collection] Yunmen was once asked by a monk, "What is it like when all-encompassing wisdom penetrates without obstruction? The Master said, "Sweeping the floor and pouring water—His Excellency has arrived. The Verse says: Sweeping the floor and pouring water— His Excellency has arrived. If you can understand this at once, You will see the source of the patriarchs. If you hesitate for even a moment, You will fall into the weeds of birth and death. How many people in the world Can avoid being deceived? If you wish to know the meaning of this verse, Look at the face of the old man on the wall.
Sweeping the floor and splashing water—the young master has arrived. Everyone has a bright mirror hanging on a high stand.
Beneath the azure command banner, he laughs heartily; why should his clear eyes not open wide for this special occasion? (Cishou Shen)
Sweeping the floor and splashing water—the young master arrives. With a loud, commanding shout, the embroidered banners part. A jade unicorn descends from heaven to bring auspiciousness to the world;
he is truly fit to be a general or a minister among men. (Shuian I)
The all-knowing penetration is unobstructed; the Master comes sweeping the floor and splashing water.
Face-to-face, seizing the opportune moment like a flash of lightning, Hanshan claps his hands and laughs heartily. (Zhu’an Guang)
Once, when a monk who was a lecturer visited Yunmen, after some time had passed, the monk said, "Before arriving at Yunmen, it was just like the new moon;
once I arrived, however, it became all crooked and bent. Yunmen, having perceived this, called him over and asked, "Did you say that?
The monk replied, "I did. Yunmen said, "Very good. Let me ask you: what is the new moon?"
The monk then struck his forehead and made a gesture of gazing at the moon. The Master said, "If you continue like this, you will lose your eyesight in the future.
After ten days had passed, the monk returned. The Master asked again, "Have you understood yet?
He replied, "I have not understood. The Master said, "Ask me. The monk then asked, "What is the newly risen moon? The Master said, "A curve."
It was curved. The monk was at a loss. Later, he indeed lost his eyesight. The Verse says:
Yunmen’s new moon is curved and bent; A narrow view first reveals a single stripe of the leopard. To transform iron into gold is easy;
To exhort others to eliminate right and wrong is difficult. (Cishou Shen)
Just like the newly risen moon; two mouths with but one tongue. Reaching the end, it is winding and crooked; carrying fire into the cowpen.
When asked about him, he strikes his forehead with his hand. Who knows that among black monkeys there is a white one? Later, losing his eyes will surely prove it true.
If you wish to see a tall man wading through deep water—(Yuet-tang Chang).

[Added from the Supplementary Collection] Yunmen ascended the hall. Upon hearing the sound of the bell, he said, "The world is so vast; why do you wrap yourself in the seven-strip robe [the monastic cassock] because of the sound of the bell?

A monk remained silent. The Master said, "There are many frogs at the head of Qili Tan. Verse: The world is vast and wide, Yet one wraps oneself in the seven-strip robe for the sake of a bell’s sound. The monk is speechless— At the head of Qili Tan, there are many frogs.
The seven-strip robe is donned as the bell tolls; throughout the world, the marks of a bhikṣu cannot be concealed.
If one seeks [the Buddha] through form or sound, then Elder Brother Kāśyapa was a delusion. (Gushan Gui)
At the head of Qīlǐ Tān, there are many clams; as soon as the sun emerges from the horizon, they all open their shells.
Though my liver and gall have been exposed throughout my life, how could a cunning falcon ever come to pursue such a foul odor? (Wú'ān Quán)
The sound of the bell causes the *uttarāsaṅga* to be drawn on; with a hand of faith, what is grasped requires no more.
How laughable that Master Ming of those years—how frantic his pursuit, how much he rushed about! (Shu’ān Zōng)
I ask you: when the bell-sound is struck by one wearing the seven-fold robe, it lightly strikes and awakens ignorance.
To buy a sesame cake is merely a deception; how bitter! Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva. (Xia'an Wu)
If you understand, all things are one family; if you do not understand, there are ten thousand distinctions and a thousand differences. If you do not understand, all things are one family;
if you understand, there are ten thousand distinctions and a thousand differences. (The Gateless Barrier).
[Added for inclusion] Yunmen was once asked by a monk, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said, "Speak when you have nothing.
Another time he said, "There is porridge and rice on the long benches," or else, "The mountains, rivers, and the great earth.
A verse says:
Sometimes a boat goes with the current; turning the rudder, one sees it again go against the wind. When the boat reaches the shore, people disembark onto land.
Mountains upon mountains, and waters upon waters. (The Mirror of the Ultimate Image).
Gold and rubble are cast about at will; though of high value, no one offers a price. The ground becomes a scene of disorder. (Bamboo Cottage)
[Added from another source] Yunmen said: "To reach the point where heaven and earth have not even a hair’s breadth of flaw is still a 'turning phrase.
Only when you do not see a single color is this half of the teaching presented. You must further know there is a time for the 'full presentation.
The verse says:
Playing with danger atop a hundred-foot pole; casting one’s body across the sea of right and wrong.
There is yet another moment for the total upholding [of the Way], which is fit only for sorrow and cannot be recounted. (Songyuan Yue)
[Added for inclusion] Yunmen was once asked by a monk, "What is the first phrase? The Master said, "Seven times nine is sixty-three. The Verse says:
Seven, nine, six, three; do not say this is mere conversation. If the one present does not realize it, go further and ask Gautama. (Benjue I)

[Added for inclusion] One day Yunmen asked Mingjiao, "How many steamed buns did you eat today? He replied, "Five. The Master said, "How many did the pillar eat?

Casually hanging out, he asked for the reason; not failing his lifelong commitment, he answered with full disclosure. To exert one's utmost strength for others, it must be thorough;

[Added for inclusion: Yunmen held up a steamed bun and said, "I only provide offerings for those from the two provinces of Zhejiang; I do not provide offerings for those from the north.
The assembly was speechless. [Yunmen] spoke on their behalf: "The weather is cold and the days are short; let two people share one bowl."
The verse says:
Half lies south of the Yellow River, half north of it; a single expanse of void, solidified like ink-black.
To contemplate this in cold silence brings one to the brink of despair—how vexing is this old thief Yunmen! (Longhua edition).
[Added by Yinzhou] Once, while at a meal, Yunmen picked up his spoon and chopsticks and said, "I do not offer alms to monks from the South;
I only offer them to monks from the North. At that time, a monk asked, "Why do you not offer alms to monks from the South?
The Master replied, "I wish to leave him stunned. The monk asked, "Why then do you only offer them to monks from the North? The Master replied, "One arrow, two targets."
A monk brought up a question, asking: "As for that previous meaning, what is it? The Master said: "If it is good, then it shares in the glory. He then offered this verse:

"The spoon and chopsticks are brought forth and presented to all; They do not serve the Southern monks, nor do they serve the Northern monks. Even if one's eyes were exchanged, it would never be known."
I observe that such superficial chatter is entirely lacking in true awareness (the first instance of *benjue*).
When Yunmen was at the midday meal, he asked a monk, "Is it the person who eats the rice, or does the rice eat the person? The monk remained silent.
The Master provided this substitute answer on his behalf: "Thank you for answering my question. The Verse says: [Verse omitted]
The aged Yunmen forcefully points out the way for the deluded; this monk remains speechless, manifesting his total capacity.
I urge you not to seek it elsewhere: once fully satiated, one naturally forgets all hunger. (Tieshan Ren)

[Added from another source] When Yunmen arrived in Jiangzhou, Chancellor Chen Cao invited him for a vegetarian feast. As soon as he saw him, the Chancellor asked: "I do not ask about the Confucian classics;
the masters themselves preside over the Three Vehicles and the twelve divisions of the teachings. What, then, is the matter of a monk’s traveling pilgrimage?
The Master replied: "How many people have you questioned so far? The Chancellor said: "I am questioning you, the Venerable One, right now. The Master [remained silent].
[The monk] said, "Setting that aside for now, what is the meaning of the teachings? [The Master] said, "Yellow scrolls and red axes.
The Master said, "This is merely written words and language. What is the meaning of the teachings? [The monk] said, "The mouth wishes to speak, yet words fail;
the mind wishes to contemplate, yet thoughts vanish. The Master said, "'The mouth wishes to speak, yet words fail'—this is a response to [the external]."
Someone said, "The mind desires to take something as an object, yet its deliberations vanish. This is done to counteract deluded thoughts.

What is the intended meaning of this teaching? Xuefeng remained silent. The monk asked, "I have heard that you, Minister, are studying the *Lotus Sūtra*; is this true? He replied, "It is true. The Master said, "The sūtra states:
'All livelihoods and productive enterprises are entirely non-contradictory with the true nature (*dharmatā*')."
"Tell me, how many people have fallen from their positions in the Heaven of Neither-Perception-Nor-Non-Perception? Book was speechless. The Master said, "Minister, do not be so hasty.
Even monks who have mastered the Three Sutras and Five Treatises cast them aside to enter the monastic forests;
after ten or twenty years there, they still cannot manage it. How could you, Minister, possibly understand? Book prostrated himself and said, "I..."
The Faults of the Armor. The Verse says:
A veteran skilled in war carries no provisions; seizing the drum and snatching the banner, his momentum is irresistible. Who can discern the tiger’s gallop and the dragon’s stride?
Reflecting on benevolence and righteousness, one conquers the violent and strong. (Compiled by Master Niu Wuzhu).
[Added from another source] Yunmen ascended the hall and, picking up his staff, said: "Ordinary people truly claim it exists; those of the Two Vehicles analyze it and claim it does not exist;
Pratyekabuddhas call it illusory existence; Bodhisattvas realize its emptiness in its very substance.
When members of our monastic community see this staff, they simply call it a staff. When walking, simply walk; when sitting, simply sit. Do not disturb it."
The verse says:
"Regarding the Two Vehicles and Bodhisattvas, why speak of 'exhaustion'? As for Buddhas and ordinary people, when will they ever cease? Matters of the world are simply settled by the path of justice;
The human heart is difficult to make like water flowing forever. (Gushan Gui)
He pulls open the locks of the golden hall; he strikes the bells of the jade towers. A thousand kinds of grass weep upon the dew;
a single type of pine sighs in the wind. (Jingshan Gaofeng)
Yunmen was such an old *ācārya*; when will you understand the core of this patch-robed monk? Let the staff remain unmoved;
as spring arrives, one cannot help but pull back the branches. (Lan’an Shu)

The gallbladder follows the rapids until they are all exhausted; the mind flies with every wave. When the boatman reports that the rapids have ended, the mind and gallbladder both return at once. (Gufeng Yuan)

[Added from another source] Yunmen ascended the hall and said: "When light does not penetrate through, there are two kinds of illness. First, there is the case where one is not clear regarding all things and there seems to be an object before one's face;

this is one. Furthermore, even if one has penetrated through so that all dharmas are empty, yet there is still a lingering sense as if there were some kind of thing remaining—this too is light that has not penetrated through.
Moreover, the Dharma-body also has two kinds of illness... [The text continues with the first illness: "Attaining..."
One reaches the Dharma-body, yet because attachment to dharmas has not been forgotten, one's own views still persist;
to remain seated at the side of the Dharma-body is the first [obstacle]. Even if you manage to penetrate through to the Dharma-body, it is still not permissible to let it go.
If you examine it closely, what kind of lingering scent remains? That too is a sickness. The verse says:
The myriad phenomena of the universe stand majestic and towering. To penetrate through them without obstruction is to leave no barrier for the eye.

Who has the power to sweep away the traces at the gate? Hidden within the breast, a sentiment naturally arises. A boat lies across the wild crossing, reflecting the autumnal azure; the oars enter the reeds, shining bright as snow.
An old fisherman, his embroidered robe worn, harbors thoughts of heading to the market; he drifts upon a single leaf, sailing over the crests of the waves. (Tiantong Jue)
Yunmen addressed the assembly, saying: "Reading a thousand scrolls of scripture is but words upon paper. The verse says:
Before heaven and after earth, it is fundamentally vast and empty. Tearing through the weeds to seek the fragrance, one finds joy on the path.
Without the spring breeze, the flowers would not bloom; Yet once they have bloomed, they are blown away by the wind. (Huian Ti)

[Added for inclusion] Yunmen was once asked by a monk, "What is the meaning behind Bodhidharma’s wall-gazing? The Master said, "Reciting the *Saptāha* [the seven-day sutra]. Another monk asked Nanquan, "What is the meaning behind Bodhidharma’s wall-gazing?

Nanquan said, "The weather is cold, and I have no blanket to cover me. The Verse says: Reciting the *Saptāha*, The weather is cold, and there is no blanket. If you wish to know the meaning of the wall-gazing, Look at the moon reflected in the water.
One person is skilled at climbing the pole; another is skilled at drilling through the well. Though their arts differ, they all suffer from the same malady.
If one recognizes this malady, the nostrils of every patch-robed monk will have been pierced through. (Cishou Shen)
Yunmen’s “Seventh Day”: To open one’s mouth is to lose it; the tongue is made bald—what breath remains? (Dongshan Yuan).
Bodhidharma’s wall-gazing and Yunmen’s “Seventh Day”—these two are like lacquer buckets; they are mostly empty and little substantial. A monk with clear eyes [sees through them].
How can one understand this thoroughly? You should know that the sword has long since departed; there is no need to mark the boat and search for its traces.
(Wuxiang Fan). [Added from another source: Chan Master Guyan Youyuan of Tanzhou (he succeeded Daguang). A monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
The Master said, "At midnight, a crow wears snow upon its head; at dawn, a mute person embraces it."
Return. The verse says:
Auspicious mists and auspicious smoke lock the Jade Tower; the Prince in his prime enjoys carefree leisure. Upon the lapis lazuli hall he rides the golden horse;
before the Hall of the Bright Moon he rolls the embroidered ball. (Danxia Chun)
[Added to the Collection] Chan Master Baizun Shanzang of Jingzhao (Successor of Daguang). A monk asked, "What is the place of deepest depth? The Master said, "A short man crossing a deep stream.
Verse: The short man crosses the deep stream; How can one fathom his depths? If you wish to know the ultimate source, Look at the water flowing before your eyes.
The white-haired youth possesses even greater wisdom; at the third watch of the night, he crosses the vast expanse.
Moving to and fro with effortless spontaneity without interruption, he requires neither boat nor raft. (Danxia Chun)

Picking up a tuft of cloth hair invites much talk from others; how can it compare to the single phrase transmitted by Heishan? With one beat of the drum, the universe resounds;
where ice ten thousand feet thick, a lotus suddenly blooms. (Touzi Qing)
First pulling stones, second carrying earth; to trigger the mechanism, one must use a crossbow of a thousand *qian*. The Old Teacher Xianggu once rolled a ball;
how does he compare to Heyshan, who knows how to beat the drum? I inform you: do not be reckless! What is sweet is sweet, and what is bitter is bitter.
(Xuedou Xian): One, two, three, four, five. Heyushan knows how to beat the drum. With the wondrous power of wisdom, Avalokiteśvara can save the world from suffering.
(Chengjue Yi): When the drum of Nanfan is struck in broad daylight, the myriad phenomena and the vast universe hear it standing still on the ground.
Were it not for everyone joining in this collective performance, it would be difficult to sustain from day until dusk. (Xue’an Jin)
Straw sandals serve as a crown, and pines are fashioned into hairpins; with such uniform elegance, his vision is sharp.
The pure sound resides only at the wind-swept eaves; all day long, no one comes down from the steps. (Xutang Yu)
Heishan understands how to beat the drum; the great earth has not a single inch of soil. If you are not a person from Handan, you must strictly avoid learning the Tang gait. (Wuxiang Fan)
[Added to the Collection] Chan Master Changcha of Tongan on Fengxi Mountain in Hongzhou (a successor of Jiufeng). He asked a monk, "The realm of the eye has no light;
how can one see? The monk said, "The Big Dipper turns east, and the Southern Dipper shifts west. The Master said:
When the Master entered the Grand Ancestral Temple, he said, "In this way, then, under the gate of Tong'an, the Way is cut off and humanity is abandoned.
The Teacher said, "He cradles an infant in his arms, intending to manifest the Imperial Edict. The Verse says:
From Silla across the sea to Nanyue and Tiantai, not even a speck of dust can obstruct them; how could they involve themselves in coming or going? Turn your head and withdraw your thoughts.
The gates of liberation open; yet, looking back, one recalls Sudhana seeking his noble friends. Having wandered through a hundred cities, he did not know when to turn back.
(Xuedou Zong) [Added from another source:
When a monk asked Tongan, "What is the家风 (family style/tradition) of the Phoenix’s Nest? the Master said, "The Phoenix’s Nest has no home."
Feng said, "Since this is where the phoenix perches, why is there no 'house style' (family tradition)? The Master said, "I do not welcome guests; I do not wait for visitors.

Feng said, "If that is so, what is the purpose of seeking throughout the four seas? The Master said, "The food on the platter is provided by others. Verse: The phoenix perches upon the ancient pine; The house style is not something to be sought. Though the plum blossoms fall in profusion, The fragrance naturally fills the courtyard. When the wind blows through the pines, The sound is heard from afar. If you wish to know the true meaning, Look at the plum tree in the garden.
The World-Honored One swallows it in a single mouth; thus, the mountain is deep and still as the moon turns yellow. The light divides behind the crown of his head, awakening a thousand gates at dawn;
sitting, I watch the spring return to the scorched earth. (Zidehui)

The secret palace is tightly surrounded; the dawn is still cold. Moss is damp upon the vermilion steps before the imperial court has yet formed its ranks.
Precious incense and phoenix-tapered candles merge into clouds and mist; silently the curtains hang down, concealing the Emperor’s countenance. (Danxia Chun)
[Added from another source: A monk asked Tong’an, “The new year is just approaching and the old year has already passed;
is there anyone who does not undergo the New Year’s observance? The Master said, “There is. The monk asked, “Who is it that does not undergo the New Year’s observance? The Master said, “How so?”
[The monk] said, "If that is so, then one does not observe the New Year. The Master said, "The horns of the New Year have already blown atop the city walls;
by the window, the lamp of the past year still flickers. The Verse says: The horns of the New Year have already blown atop the city walls; By the window, the lamp of the past year still flickers.
The old year ends and the new year begins—this serves as a point for inquiry. From this moment on, Tong’an has let things be in a state of vast openness.
I rely upon you at the high tower: do not blow the flute; let us all remain there leaning against the balustrade. (Lan’an Shu)
The ox-horn is blown with a mournful sound atop the tower; before the lamp, one is lost in the dream of a butterfly. If you wish now to understand the meaning of non-transmigration:
when the sun rises in the east, it sets in the west at night. (Wuji Hui)
[Added to the Collection] Master Boryun of Silla (in the *Wudeng Huiyuan*, he is recorded as Baeryun of Silla, successor to Gusan Chang).
A monk asked, "What is Chan? The Master said, "An ancient tomb is not made into a home. The monk asked, "What is the Way?
The Master said, "In vain are the tracks of carriages and horses. The monk asked, "What are the Teachings? The Master said, "The palm-leaf sutras."
Unable to contain it all. The verse says:
The old kingdom has enjoyed peace for many years; Even with white hair, one still clings to the conditions of this life.
Only the cowherd boy understands how to forget his achievements; He lazily lets the ox roam, never raising the whip. (Gu-zhong bu-wei-jia—Dan-xia Chun)
Forty-nine years of proclamations are completed; over five thousand scrolls exhaust all verbal explanations.
Yet that single phrase of wondrous clarity lies beyond the era of Vidyutghoṣa—the hornless mud ox sleeps in the snow (though the palm leaves cannot contain it).
The palm leaves cannot contain it all; a single phrase, free from self-interest, is the seal of the myriad dharmas. Though the thousand sages have their mouths full, they cannot proclaim it;
the plum blossoms on the ridge betray the news of spring’s arrival. (Xuedou Zong, Verse 4)
Ancient tombs do not serve as homes; the fisherman raises his oars and emerges from the reeds. The waters are deep and windless, the river moon hangs far aloft;
across the vast sky, the evening clouds have been entirely swept away.
No need for the tracks of carriages or horses; since King Wen departed, there has been no further news. Amidst the reflection of the moonlight lies the fishing pier;
through ten thousand ages, the pure breeze remains ever-clear and distinct.

The single arrowhead has pierced through all three barriers; the past exploits of the sweating horse need no longer be picked up or handled. You must know that the old pavilion swiftly welcomed the dragon boat;
in those years, he once seized the silken prize.
[Added to the Collection] Chan Master Daling of Silla (successor of Gushan Zang). A monk asked: "What is meant by 'purity in all places'?

The Master said: "When jade branches are cut, every inch is treasure; when sandalwood is split, every fragment is fragrant. Verse: Cutting the jade branches, every inch is treasure; Splitting the sandalwood, every slice is fragrant.
Heaven and earth are entirely a land of gold; all phenomena fully manifest the pure and wondrous body. The jade maiden turns her back to the wind, neither clever nor clumsy;
the sprouts and flowers flourish in their brilliance, unaware of spring. (Danxia Chun)
[Added to the Collection] Master Furi of Hangzhou (heir to Yunju). One day, during a great communal labor service (*mahāpravāraṇā*), the Rector requested the Master to deliver tea.
The Master said, "I have come for the sake of the Buddha-dharma; I have not come to deliver tea.
The Rector replied, "The Abbot has commanded you, Senior, to deliver the tea. The Master said, "I shall comply with the Abbot’s command," and then he took [the tea].
The Master went to the work area and rattled his tea bowl to make a sound. Jia Shan looked back, and the Master said, "Three or five bowls of strong tea;
the intent lies at the edge of the mattock. Jia Shan said, "The pitcher has the intention to pour tea; how many bowls are there in the basket?
The Master said, "The pitcher has the intention to pour tea; there is not a single bowl in the basket," and he immediately poured the tea and served it.
At that moment, the entire assembly raised their eyes. The Master said, "The assembly gazes with crane-like expectation; I pray for a word from the Master.
Shishuang said, "If you encounter a dead snake on the road, do not strike it; carry it home in a bottomless basket.
The Master said, "Holding a night-bright talisman in hand, how many know when the dawn breaks? Shishuang said, "The assembly has someone; go back, go back."
Go! From here, dwell in universal practice (*pǔqǐng*). The verse says:
When you encounter a dead snake on the road, do not strike it; You must cast away the bottomless basket.
Often matters arise from idle talk; Do not treat idle talk as if it were merely idle talk. (Master Pogu Xian)
A man of the eaves and boards, free from constraints—starving to death on Mount Shouyang, he vowed never to eat the millet of Zhou. (Xutang Yu).
[Added by Zeng] Chan Master Tong’an Pi of Fengxi Mountain in Hongzhou (a successor of Yunju). A monk asked, "What is the master’s house style?
The Master said, "The golden rooster carries its chicks back to the void; the jade hare holds its young toward the moon."

Ziwei asked, "If a guest should suddenly arrive, how will you receive them? The Master said, "The golden fruit was plucked by the monkey at dawn; the jade flower is carried back by the phoenix at dusk. The Verse says: The golden fruit was plucked by the monkey at dawn;
The jade flower is carried back by the phoenix at dusk. The host and guest both enter the gate together; The moon shines upon the clear waters of the river.

At midday, smoke gathers and the mountains stand out sharply; at the end of night, the sky is pale and the moon is full and lovely. In this state of total, silent illumination, the cold night is long;
brightness and darkness are perfectly integrated before any sign has yet emerged. (Danxia Chun)
A sheet of silk like falling snow, Is fashioned into a pair of carp. If you wish to know the matters within my heart, Look at the writing inside my belly. (Fang’an Xian)
Before the white jade steps, golden phoenixes dance; atop the golden hall, the jade rooster crows.
Coming from the center and arriving through the simultaneous—last night the snow was deep, and the moon was at its brightest. (Xueyan Qin)
[Added from another source] Tongan Pui was asked by a monk: "To explain the meaning based on the scriptures is to be at enmity with the Buddhas of the three periods;
to depart from even a single word of the scriptures is to speak like a demon. What is the principle behind this? The Master said: "A solitary peak rises loftily, unclad by misty vines."
A crescent moon travels across the void; drifting clouds are naturally distinct. The verse says:
Clouds fly high on their own, and waters flow of their own accord. The sea and sky are vast and wide, where a solitary boat floats.
At nightfall, it does not seek lodging in a reed cove; It transcends both the middle and the two ends. (Danxia Chun)
[Added from the Supplement] Chan Master Qian of Zhuxi in Shexian (he was a successor of Yunju). When National Teacher Yao came to pay his respects, he heard the sound of a dog biting a "spirit mouse.
The National Teacher asked, "What is that sound? The Master replied, "It is the sound of a dog biting a spirit mouse."

[The monk] asked, "Since it is a numinous mouse, why was it bitten by a dog? The Master said, "It has been bitten to death. [The monk] said, "What a fine dog! The Master then struck him. [The monk] said, "Do not strike me;

this is my *huatou* (critical phrase). The Master ceased. A verse says: The numinous mouse was bitten by the dog; The dog was struck by the Master. If you wish to know the meaning of this, Look at the dog’s tail.
A needle-point carves iron; the Buddha’s face scrapes gold. Where there is nothing, it is as if there were something. As soon as the hand comes forth, all are startled.
(Yuedang Chang) The rat is no longer clever; the official horses tread upon one another. Even if they were to ride the wind, they would jostle and crush each other.
Amidst the chaos of war, the foundation of Great Peace is established. A formidable reputation resounds through the monastery. (Fodeng Xun)
[Zhu Xi] asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "From Guangnan. The Master said, "Are there any extraordinary or venerable elders there?
The monk said, "As for extraordinary or venerable elders, no one speaks of them; there is only one person who is utterly shameless.
The Master asked, "Who is that? The monk pointed to the Master. The Master said, "Indeed, he is shameless."

[The Master] said, "If it were not Zhu Xi, people of this age would have no idea what to do. The monk covered his nose with his hand. The monk stepped forward, and the Master struck him. [The monk] said, "Exactly so! The Master said, "This old monk’s administrative duties are too numerous. The monk brushed out his sleeves and departed. The Master laughed heartily and said, "Lotus roots on the Pan-tuo Rock. The Verse says: The lotus root on the Pan-tuo Rock, Its fragrance permeates the ten directions. When the wind blows, the scent spreads; Who can grasp its essence? If you wish to know the Patriarch’s meaning, Look at the monk covering his nose. A single blow from the staff— It is like a thunderclap. If you can discern the intent within this, You will see the ancient path clearly revealed. Otherwise, you remain lost in the dark. How could you ever avoid being deceived? The Master’s laughter is vast and deep; The sound echoes through the mountains and rivers. If you can understand this moment, You will realize the truth of the Buddhas and Patriarchs. Do not seek it elsewhere— It is right here before your eyes.

If you can see it thus, You will naturally be free from doubt. If you cannot, You must continue to seek diligently. Do not rely on words and phrases; Directly point to the source. Only then will you understand the Master’s intent. This is the true transmission of the Dharma.
He stumbles home in disorder; upon arriving home, he stumbles about in disorder. He seizes the Jade Qilin and bites off another’s hand. (Yuedang Chang)
Questioning the wondrous and venerable elders, they point out those shameless fellows. In the field of battle, the colored banners fly in confusion;
head and tail are both preserved, beginning and end form a single thread. A peach ripens once every three thousand years;
who has personally seen lotus roots grow upon rocks? (Fodeng Xun)
A guest who parts the weeds to gaze at the wind; a sharp wit comes like a split arrow. Upon the Paṇḍaka Rock, the lotus blooms with iron flowers all night long. (Fang’an Xian)
A most extraordinary old master, a person of great shamelessness: a lotus upon a flat rock—how delightful to behold its fresh bloom once more. (Shixi Yue)

He stands upright, pointing out the road to Chang’an, yet alas, travelers are unwilling to walk it. (Danxia Chun)
The ten-thousand-fathom cliff is suddenly opened; a message passes directly across one's face. A single white silk ribbon flies forth, breaking the colors of the green mountains. (Suan Cong)
Yunju was asked by a monk, "What is it like when one encounters a fierce tiger on the road? The Master said, "A thousand people, ten thousand people do not encounter it;

why then is it you who encounter it? The verse says: A thousand people, ten thousand people do not encounter it; Why then is it you who encounter it? If you can see through this, The tiger has already been subdued.
No rouge or powder applied; no green silk robes hung. With an air of leisurely ease, her蛾眉 (yúméi—“butterfly brows”) are drawn with light ink. (Shu’ān Zōng)
[Added for inclusion: Yunju Jian was asked by a monk, "What is the Bodhisattva Red-Crested King?
The Master said, "Why ask this red-headed fellow? Gao’an Wu said: "This is precisely the matter that transcends the school and surpasses the conventional;
it is truly a point where there is no place for intellectual understanding. One must first awaken, and furthermore, be able to practice and tread the path, only then will it be attained."
"Can you all understand this clearly? He then spoke in verse:
"The Bodhisattva Red-Crested King was originally a red-headed fellow; He startled Li San the Black, who spent his entire life selling charcoal."

[Added to the Collection] Monk Yunju of Silla (successor of Yunju). A monk asked, "What is the teacher of all Buddhas?
The Master said, "Mañjuśrī cocks his ear. The Verse says:
In the light of formlessness, the body has not yet manifested; pure, empty, and vast, how could it be a neighbor? A single bright moon shines upon the window;
in the desolate jade palace, no person is seen. (Danxia Chun)

[Added from the Supplementary Collection] Chan Master Huaguang of Heshan in Fuzhou (a successor of Caoshan). A monk asked, "What is the very meaning of the coming from the West? The Master said, "If you do not prostrate, when else would you wait? The Verse says: If you do not prostrate, when else would you wait? The iron ox has already passed the mountain pass. The golden-haired lion roars at the blue heavens; The jade rabbit leaps within the cold palace. The thousand sages have all been swallowed up by the single word; The myriad phenomena are entirely encompassed by the one phrase. The great matter is settled in a single moment; The three bodies are complete within a single thought. The ten directions are all within the palm of the hand; The four seas are contained within the eye of the pupil. The Great Way is vast and wide, without boundaries; The True Dharma is profound and subtle, beyond measure. The ancient mirror shines brightly before the eyes; The clear moon reflects clearly in the water. If you wish to see the Buddha-nature, Look directly at the face before your own eyes. If you can understand this at once, You will immediately realize the source of the Way. If you hesitate for even a moment, You will fall into the pit of birth and death. Do not seek it elsewhere— It is right here, right now. If you can recognize it in this very instant, You will know that it is not something created. The Master’s words are like a thunderclap; They strike the heart and leave no room for doubt. The monk’s question was about the ultimate meaning; The Master’s answer was a direct blow. If you can grasp this in a flash, You will see the light of the ancestral hall. If you fail to see through this, You will wander in the dark for a thousand eons. The empty hall is silent and cold in the deep night; I take my jade lute and play it beneath the moon. Were it not for one who understands, ears would be pressed vainly to the side;
How could the mournful wind and flowing water have anything to do with it? (Danxia Chun)
[Added from the Supplementary Collection] Chan Master Hongtong of Mount Yuwang in Changning County, Hengzhou (a successor of Caoshan). A monk asked, "What is the house style of the Master?
The Master said, "My entire person is not worth even five cents. The monk said, "You are truly living in such poverty.
The Master said, "It was thus in ancient times. The monk asked, "How do you provide for it? The Master said, "According to my household."
Abundance and Frugality. The Verse says:
The ancestral family style lacks a single coin; Within pure poverty, there is even more pure poverty.
Wearing clothes and eating food according to abundance or scarcity— In every thing and every circumstance, the most intimate is employed. (Danxia Chun)
[Added from the Supplement] Chan Master Congzhi of Jinfeng in Fuzhou (he succeeded Caoshan).
Holding up a pillow, he showed it to a monk and said, "Everyone calls this a 'pillow,' but Jinfeng says it is not. The monk asked, "I wonder, what do you, the Master, call it?
The Master picked up the pillow and said, "If that is so, then follow it accordingly. The Master then said: [The rest of the dialogue follows].
"What do you call this? he asked. [The monk] said, "A pillow. The Master said, "It has fallen into the den of Jinfeng.
Verse: Calamities sent by Heaven may still be avoided; Calamities one creates for oneself cannot be escaped. (Wanshan Ning)
Within the hollow of Golden Peak, there is no clamor or error. Will you understand when the pillow is picked up? With a single cry from the returning swan, the spring dream is severed;
only then does one realize that body and world are but the awakening to the "South of the Locust Tree" (Nanke). (Fang’an Xian)
Grasping the whole lump is a fine standard; even "flashing stone-fire" is already too late.
Without falling into the trap of Jin-feng, one must seek advantage with empty hands. (Shixi Yue)

If one is a Ziqi who can listen to the tuning of the strings, Who would take the resonance of pines for the chirping of autumn cicadas? (Dahong Su)
"Three in the morning and four in the evening—how little! Four in the evening and three in the morning—how much more!
If one cannot discern the quantity of what is much or little, from this arises the clamor of "existence" and "non-existence. To be free from such clamor: Oṃ sulu-siri svāhā.
(Buddha-nature Tai). Who lacks it? Who possesses it?
This is the Way of the total functioning. To turn back upon oneself at the moment of speaking is not clever enough.

Even if one has already set out before the words are raised, one is mistakenly taking a winnowing basket for an ironing board. A-ha-ha! If a person can immediately ride a donkey backward, their whole life—
Do not follow after others blindly. (Xiuyan Rui). [Added by Zeng].
Regarding the question asked of Hugu Cheng by a monk: "What is the original mind? The Master said: "The rhinoceros develops patterns on its horns from gazing at the moon;
the elephant receives flowers within its tusks when startled by thunder. A Verse says:

A three-legged numinous tortoise scampers along the desolate path; a branch of auspicious grass hangs down amidst the chaotic peaks. Mount Kunlun contains the Jade Mountain, its luster smooth and radiant;
the cool hare conceives her embryo, yet the moon does not yet know it. (Danxia Chun)

Huguo Chengyin was asked by a monk, "What is the mark of the Brahma-voice? The Master said, "Donkeys bray in Hebei; dogs bark in Henan. The Verse says: Donkeys bray in the north, Dogs bark in the south.
The Brahma-voice is not far off— Just listen with your own ears.
Maudgalyāyana sought the Buddha’s mark of Brahma-sound; he exhausted all his supernatural powers yet could not see its limit. Who can awaken to the braying of donkeys and the barking of dogs?
This perfect sound, vast and resonant, is revealed to humans and devas. (Da Hong Su)
[Added from the Supplementary Collection] When a monk asked Hugu Chengyin, "What is one's original father and mother? the Master said, "He whose head does not turn white.
The monk asked, "With what shall I make an offering? The Master said, "Diligently prepared rice without grain; before the hall, no inquiry after kin."
The Verse says:
Leaving the gate, the whole world lacks a known friend; Entering the door, my eyes are filled but see no kin. In this empty chamber, cold at night, what is there?
Only the bright moon in the azure sky serves as neighbor. (Danxia Chun)
[Added for inclusion: When a monk asked Hugu Chengyin, "What is it like when a crane stands upon a withered pine?
The Master said, "The one beneath the earth is thoroughly embarrassed. He asked, "During the Huichang persecution of Buddhism, where did the Dharma-protecting benevolent spirits go?
The Master said, "The two by the main gate are thoroughly embarrassed. He asked, "When a drop of water freezes solid..."
"How is it? The Master said, "After the sun has risen, there is a scene of utter embarrassment. The verse says: Standing like a crane upon a solitary pine, no other can equal him;
How could he be like a goose or duck, familiarizing himself with common fowl? Having transformed and departed from Liao Yang, he left no trace behind;
The spiritual tree stands tall and remote, where even the phoenix does not perch. (Da Hong Sui)
The guardian deity at the gate of the temple divined its fate; the purge of the Huichang era was a bitter blow to its very nose. When the time came, Heaven and Earth exerted their power together;
in the end, it returned to its rightful lord.
Ice forms and drips of water appear; how pure and lofty this matter! Yet when the sun rises in the east, it is no longer firm. How could mountain streams and ravines retain it?
In the end, it returns to the great ocean to become waves and surges.
Ambitious wills stand tall, though the temples have not yet turned gray. A man need not fear failing to become a marquis.
Reflecting back on those who passed down a legacy of purity and integrity, they washed their ears at the head of the stream and would not drink from the ox’s trough. (Tiantong Jue)
[Added from the Supplement] Chan Master Zangyu of Baoci in Tanzhou (successor of Longya). A monk asked: "When emotion arises, wisdom is obstructed;
when thought changes, the essence becomes distinct. But what is it like when emotion has not yet arisen? The Master said: "Obstructed. The monk asked:
"When emotion has not yet arisen, what is it that is obstructed? The Master said: "This lad has not yet met anyone [worthy of him]. Verse:
It is said: "The ancients were separated by a single barrier; this is the life-vein of the patch-robed monks. If you wish to recognize the 'single thread,' two five-hundred [coins] make one thousand.

(Tianyi Huai) When emotion has not yet arisen, there is a separation; the golden-haired lion often loses its luster. Foxes run to and fro outside the gate, laughing to death the thicket [of delusions].
The old Chan guest Lin (Yang Wuwe):
"How can one communicate when the insentient is separated? Between a hair’s breadth, the paths are ten thousandfold.
A pity for those who run empty at both ends; they cannot see the essence directly. (Baiyun Yuan).
Baoci’s single “separation” is the life-vein of the Buddhas and Patriarchs; sent forth and withdrawn, it is unfathomable to both sages and ordinary beings.

(Kai Fu Ning). [Continued Collection] Separation. In a cloudless blue sky, thunder and lightning crash. Among the monks of the monasteries, as numerous as rice and hemp, how many are true *siddha* guests? (Dazhong Long).
A boat from Jiangnan, a vessel from Hainan; holding the tiller and hoisting the sails, one knows the rhythm of the beat. Following the waves and drifting with the currents, when will it ever cease?
Casting off the oars, one arrives home, yet the head is already white. (Da Hong Su).
A partition. A Central Asian monk with pierced ears and black eyes; to the west of Dongyuan is Zhaozhou.
In Guanyinyuan, Maitreya is enshrined. (Shimen Xian).
[Added from the Supplementary Collection] Chan Master Guangde Yan of Wancu Mountain in Xiangzhou (he succeeded Qinglin Qian). A monk asked, "What is the phrase that penetrates the Dharma-body?
The Master said, "Lacking the strength to ascend mountains or wade through waters; in a thatched hut, there is no one who understands."

The Verse says: In essence, he is wondrous; in probing the profound, he has traversed the entire journey. How can he compare to the rustic elder who walks differently amidst the crowd? Having forgotten his efforts in daily life, his mind is level and secure.
He need not serve a sovereign, thus avoiding the shock of favor and disgrace. (Danxia Chun)

[Added to the Collection] Chan Master Xianyun of Shimen in Xiangzhou (Successor of Qinglin Qian). A monk asked, "What is the house style of the Master? The Master said, "Riding a thousand-li elephant alone beyond the mundane world; striking a golden bell beneath ten-thousand-year-old pines. The Verse says: Riding an elephant alone beyond the world, Beneath ancient pines, he strikes the golden bell. The sound of the bell reaches the heavens, And the fragrance of the pines fills the earth. If you wish to see the Master’s true face, Look at this very moment—where is it? The spring breeze blows over the green mountains, And the autumn moon shines upon the clear waters. If you can understand this, Then you will know the Master’s house style. If you cannot understand this, You have missed the point entirely. How many people in the world can truly comprehend it? Only one person in ten thousand can see through it. If you can see through it, Then you are a fellow traveler on the Way. If you cannot see through it, You are merely a common mortal. Do not seek it elsewhere— It is right here before your eyes. If you can understand this, Then you will know the Master’s house style. If you cannot understand this, You have missed the point entirely. How many people in the world can truly comprehend it? The moon is dim and hazy outside the night-bright curtain; riding an elephant, he turns over and strikes the precious bell.
Its great resonance ascends beyond the three realms—why does the deaf man still sleep so soundly? (Danxia Chun)
[Added for inclusion: Chan Master Shandao of Mount Muping in Yuanzhou (he succeeded Wen of Panlong). Initially, he visited Luopo and asked:
"Before a single bubble has even arisen, how does one discern the course of the water? Luopo said: "Move the boat to understand the current; raise the oar to distinguish the waves.
The Master did not find resonance with this, so he went to visit Panlong. He asked the same question as before. Panlong—
He said: "When the boat is moved, one does not part from the water; yet as soon as the oars are raised, one is lost to the source. The Master attained awakening through this. The Verse says:
"The golden crow and jade hare race each other, Shattering the darkness before the time of Vimalacitra. If you say there is something else in the azure sky,"
On the road, the wooden man still knits his brows. (Danxia Chun).
Shifting the boat, he never departs from the clear source; raising the oars, how could the rising waves be endured?
If you wish to understand that the first bubble has not yet emerged, the wooden man is ready for joint study at midnight. (Benjue Yi)
Flowing on, this single stream mingles with the eternal current; As soon as it touches the waves, it never ceases.
The banks are wide, the wind is clear, and the bright moon shines; An old fisherman rows his boat to rest upon the sandbars. (Manna Cheng)

[Added from another source] A monk asked Muping, "What is the meaning of the Westward Journey? The Master said, "Look eastward at the head of the stone ram. The Verse says: Look eastward at the head of the stone ram; The Westward Journey’s meaning is right here.
If you can see it in this way, Then you will know the ancient road.
Muping Daogao was most difficult to surpass. When someone asked, "What is the meaning of the Westward Journey? he replied: "The stone ram’s head looks toward the east;

the moon has just risen, illuminating the entire hillside. He spoke directly, so there is no need for much doubt: "When the sea is clear and the waves have stilled, the myriad phenomena are revealed. (Fenyang Shanzhao)
The Old Barbarian traveled ten thousand *li* toward China; even until now, he can do nothing about it.
How laughable that the cowherd boy asks no one for the way—he passes over the front slope with a single long blast of his flute. (Foyin Yuan)
Without the labor of the axe, one fumbles with cleverness and ends up clumsy; the tattered robe covers the whole body, and the hair on the head and beard is like snow.

Wearing a pair of broken straw sandals, he tramples the moon upon the clear pool. The Patriarch’s meaning lies in the stone ram’s head pointing east; how can one speak of the matter before the single bubble?
(Dayan Fashun): "Muping was originally without any axe; why inflict the scars of moxibustion upon healthy flesh? To point directly to the intimate meaning of the Westward Transmission:
look eastward at the head of the stone ram. (Zhaojue Zong)
[Continued Collection] A stone ram’s head looks toward the east; the vast expanse of the great earth is deceived by its own eyes. The moon reflects in the cold pool, clear to the very bottom;
the clouds withdraw from Mount Hua, revealing its jagged peaks. (Yuan’an Xuan)
The stone ram’s head looks toward the east; the Patriarch’s intent is clear, yet those who understand it are rare. Without sparing himself, he points directly at the sun;
today is the ninth day, and the chrysanthemums are variegated. (This mountain responds.)
The Comprehensive Collection of Linked Verses on Ancient Cases in the Chan School, Volume Thirty-Four.
The Comprehensive Collection of Linked Verses on Ancient Cases in the Chan School, Volume Thirty-Five.
Compiled by the Śramaṇa Fasheng of Ba’en Guangxiao Chan Temple in Chizhou during the Song Dynasty.
Continued Collection of the Anecdotes of the Patriarchs by the Śramaṇa Puhui of Tianyi Wanshou Chan Monastery during the Yuan Shaoxing Era;
the Eighth Generation after the Sixth Patriarch (Part One), being the Seventh Generation prior to the Lineage of Nanyue.

(Linji) Chan Master Yanzhao of Fengxue in Ruizhou (a successor of Nanyuan). While the Master was spending the summer retreat within the official residence of Governor Li in Yingzhou, a general assembly was convened and he was invited to ascend the seat. He then said:
"The Heart-Seal of the Patriarchs is like the mechanism of an iron ox: if you go away, it seals you; if you stay, it shatters you. But what about when you neither go nor stay?"
"Not abiding. A seal is precisely not a seal; it is simply so. "Is there anyone who can say this?
At that time, the Elder Lupi came forward and asked, "This student possesses the faculty of the Iron Ox; I request the Master not to apply his seal.
The Master said, "I am accustomed to hooking whales and leviathans in vast surging waves, yet I sigh over the snail’s slow steps as it wallows in the mud and sand. Lupi paused and reflected.
The Master shouted, "Elder, why do you not advance a word? Bei hesitated. The Master then struck him with a fly-whisk and asked, "Do you still remember the *huatou*?
Try to bring it up. As Bei was about to open his mouth, the Master struck him again with the fly-whisk.
The cowherd said, "I know for certain that the Buddha-dharma and the King’s law are one and the same. The Master asked, "What have you seen?"
"What kind of principle is this? The Herdsman said, "To fail to sever when one ought to sever only invites further chaos. The Master then descended from his seat and uttered this verse:
"Having captured Lupi and mounted the iron ox, The weapons and armor of the Three Mysteries have not yet been lightly requited. Beside the city of King Chu, the rivers flow toward the sea."
Water. A single gulp caused it to flow backward once more (Xuédòu Xiǎn).
At the sharp edge where the wall stands erect is the mechanism of the iron ox; the precious sword is brandished in ten directions, horizontal and vertical. An entire army of rebels is ground to dust;
they sing the song of victory together as they return to an age of peace (Bǎoíng Yǒng).
The exemplary standards of the successive sages never permit a single lapse. Attempting to leap over the iron ox, one’s head is suddenly struck and shattered.
Lu Pei hesitated when he ought to have severed [the doubt]; in the flash of lightning and the flight of stars, he was captured alive.
A shout delivered with such momentum as a thunderclap—its three mysteries and martial armor shake the monastic forests. (Wenyu Qin)

【Continued Collection】The mechanism of the Iron Ox: sealing it and breaking the seal. It penetrates through the crown of Vairocana’s head and returns to sit upon the tongue of the Transformation Buddha.
Fengxue met his match; Lupi suffered a defeat. Upon the staff and beneath the shout, it is like lightning or sparks from flint.
"Clearly visible, the bright pearl is divided on the platter"—if you raise your eyebrows, you have already missed it. (Tiantong Jue)
The total edge of the blade conquers the iron-ox mechanism; even lightning-fast and thundering speed is already too slow.

To casually capture the old man of Lupi—though one possessed fierce strategy, what could be done? Do you not see? Within the realm there is spirit and resolve, beyond the barrier there is sovereign authority;
to hesitate or deliberate before charging forward is to have one’s entire clan exterminated. (Lan’an Xu)
A single phrase is like a crossbow bolt released; the moment one conceives a doubt, one is caught in a heavy siege.
Clearly, the Buddha-dharma is the same as the royal law; it is known only by the herdsman of that time. (Jianweng Jing)
Fengxue ascended the hall and said: "If you establish even a single speck of dust, the state will flourish and the country will prosper, yet the village elders will frown.

If you do not establish even a single speck of dust, the state will perish and the country will fall, yet the village elders will be at peace. If you can understand this clearly, you have no share in it, O *kalyāṇamitra*."
"It is all this old monk. If you do not understand this, then the old monk is actually you, the disciple (*kalyāṇamitra*).
You and the old monk can both enlighten the people of the world, and we can both blind the people of the world.
Do you wish to recognize the disciple? [He] gives a single clap to the right and says: 'It is here. Do you wish to recognize the old monk? [He] gives a single clap to the left."
The Master said: "It is right here. The Verse says:
Let the rustic old man not even knit his brows; For now, let him plan the foundation for the state and its people. Where are the strategists and the fierce generals today?
Only the solitary self knows the pure breeze across ten thousand li. (Xuedou Xian)

Establishing the state, he still brings joy to the rustic elders; his majesty extends beyond the borders without raising a cloud of dust. His mastery of both civil and martial arts is unfathomable from any angle;
throughout the vastness of the universe, how many men are there like him? (Baizhang Yuan).
White-haired, he rose by the Wei River to dangle his fishing line; how does this compare to the pure hunger of those on Mount Shouyang?
It is merely within a single speck of dust that fortune and misfortune are distinguished; lofty fame and meritorious deeds—both are difficult to obliterate. (Tiantong Jue, II)
How much joy, how much sorrow? Behold the two brows of the rustic elder. The realm is peaceful and still as a mirror;
with waters diminished and mountains bare, all is one autumn.
[Appendix] Wuzu Fayan said: "Tàipíng (Peaceful Stability) is not like this. If you establish even a single speck of dust, the grass before the Dharma Hall will grow ten feet deep;
if you do not establish even a single speck of dust, it is like adding flowers upon brocade. Why is this? Have you not seen it said? The verse says:
Eighty-one (9x9). When the poor fellow has finished his suffering, he intends to stretch out his legs and sleep; but then the mosquitoes, gadflies, and fleas come out.
Behold, first releasing both and then gathering them both back: some raise shouts of joy, while others are filled with sorrow. All sages and worthies vanish like a flash of lightning;
the great chiliocosm is but a bubble on the ocean. (Xueyan Qin)
House and state clearly attained through freedom; prosperity and decline entirely gathered within a single speck of dust. The general’s warhorse sleeps in deep repose;
let the wild weeds fill the earth with sorrow as they please. (Zhuwu Jian)
[Added for inclusion] Fengxue went to visit Nanyuan. Nanyuan asked, "Where have you recently come from? The Master replied, "From the South.
Nanyuan said, "How do they discuss the single blow and the single shout in the South? The Master said, "They discuss them as something extraordinary. Nanyuan said, "It is not so here.
The Master asked, "I wonder, how do you discuss the single blow and the single shout here? Nanyuan said—
"Under the staff is the patience of non-arising; facing the critical moment, one sees no teacher. The Master then attained realization. The Verse says:
A shout is like a probing rod or a blade of grass; Without a teacher, the life-blood flows through the red thread.
Failing to recognize General Li in the open light, One merely studies the single arrow that pierces the willow. (Nanyuan Sheng)
Fengxue was once asked by a monk: "When speech and silence involve transcendence and subtlety, how can one pass through them without transgression? The Master said:

"I always remember that in the third month of Jiangnan, where the partridges cry, the flowers are fragrant in their hundreds. The Verse says: Speech and silence involve transcendence and subtlety; How can one pass through them without transgression? I always remember that in the third month of Jiangnan, Where the partridges cry, the flowers are fragrant in their hundreds.
Where the partridges cry, the hundred flowers are fragrant; clapping hands, a burst of laughter.
Recalling the places I traveled in years past, I see someone being sent off into the setting sun through the mountain valleys. (Haerin Sin)
Where the partridges cry, a hundred flowers bloom fresh. In this land by the river, the roads have always been level and clear. To inform those travelers on the road who have not yet returned:
the family members you seek are not at their fishing boats. (Baofeng Ming)
Quickly mount a fine steed and ascend the high tower; north, south, east, and west, you shall have freedom.
It is best to have a hundred thousand strings of cash girdled at your waist; then come again, riding a crane, to Yangzhou. (Gushan Gui)
Suddenly stepping out the door, one first sees the road; Hardly has one set foot down when one boards the boat. The secret instructions of the immortals are truly worthy of treasuring;
Though father and son are close, they cannot be transmitted. (Jingshan Gaofeng)
[Continued Collection] Amidst the shadows of colored clouds, a celestial being appears. In hand, he holds a red silk fan to shield his face.
One must quickly fix one’s gaze upon the immortal; do not look at the fan in the immortal’s hand. (Fujian Qín)

A phrase that reveals no trace of its skeletal structure; before a word is spoken, it has already been entrusted. You advance with your mouth chattering, yet I know you are utterly at a loss for words. (Wumen).
Fengxue was once asked by a monk, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "Bamboo-staff whips under the Zhangling Mountain.
The verse says:
Bamboo-staff whips under the Zhangling Mountain; North and south, travelers by the tens of thousands. Do not blame me for not dismounting when we meet.
Horses: East and West each have their own destiny.

(Ciming Yuan) Under the Bamboo Whip of Staff Grove Mountain, branches and joints sparse by the ancient stream— If you wish to understand the Master’s opening of the True Eye, a full orb shines at midnight upon the autumn sky. (Haiyin Xin)
Under the Bamboo Grove Hill, bamboo-tendon whips; with ropes and hooks, they pull through the fire. Dragged near, they cannot be pushed back;
circling around, they end up before the Prefect (Daowu Zhen).
The bamboo-stem whip beneath the Staff Grove Mountain—whether held by its head or its tail, it is always the same.
Do not blame Xuansha for not crossing the ridge; his house was originally a fishing boat. (Yunfeng Yue)
Under the Śāla grove, bamboo-stalk whips; water in the deep ravine, the moon in the sky. The fine horse does not know where it has gone;
Ānanda remains as before, in the presence of the World-Honored One. (Zhenjing Wen)
Under the mountain at Zhànglín, there are whips made of bamboo fibers; travelers from south and north, by the tens of thousands.
How laughable, the guests in this hall who have no affairs—they lie deep within the clouds and do not pay court to the Emperor. (Yúnxī Gōng)
The bamboo-stem whip from beneath the Staff Grove Mountain—drawn forth, it still bears the smoke of the cold crags.
It once lent its strength to help one cross a broken bridge; yet now, it is not worth half a penny. (Shangfang Yi)
[Continued Collection] Under the Bamboo Staff Grove, a whip made of bamboo sinew; in the sixth month, travelers exhale smoke from their mouths.
I once saw it atop Mount Zhurong: ten full moons rising over the level fields. (Dongshan Kong)
The bamboo-stalk whip beneath Mount Yaṣṭivana; the tongue of Gavāmpati reaching to heaven. The factions have always been loath to go empty-handed;
the news of establishing the house lies in the wild fields. (Or the essence of the hermitage).
Fengxue was once asked by a monk, "What is the pure Dharma-body? The Master said, "The horseherd’s wife at the sands of Jinsha.
Verse: Within the sands of Jinsha, the horseherd’s wife;
The patriarch, seizing the moment, utters a word. He laughs at himself as the arrow pierces the red sun.
A shadow—whom can it be said to leave no trace when cutting through water?

(Zhengjue Yi). When meeting others, everyone says they have gone to the mountains; yet beneath the forest trees, not a single person has ever been seen. Turning one’s head to face south, one gazes at the Northern Dipper;
the golden rooster has already announced the spring of the fifth watch. (Fushan Yuan).
The mechanism that cuts through iron—how can it be measured? The thousand eyes opened at once cannot peer into it.
When a Zen practitioner reaches this point, they merely have a distant reputation; they mistakenly take a *chali* for a *nirali*. (Haerin)
In what year did you marry the young lord of the Ma family? On the jade bed, you shared joy upon the phoenix pillow. Turning back toward the painted bridge, the bitterness of parting;
With falling flowers and flowing water, a thousand rows of tears. (Zhang Wujin)
[Continued Collection] A woman of such exquisite beauty, from whose house does she hail? A lad of a hundredfold intelligence—what a horse!
It is laughable that they made an appointment by the sands of the Jinshe River; in the end, their union was never realized as a pair. (In the style of Huan'an).
[Added from the Supplementary Collection] Fengxue was once asked by a monk, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "How is it that you are not the Buddha?

The monk said, "I do not yet understand; I beg the Master to point it out again. The Master said, "My home is to the east of the Sea Gate; the Fusang tree is the first to be illuminated [by the sun]. The Verse says: How is it that you are not the Buddha? Your home lies to the east of the Sea Gate. The Fusang tree is the very first to receive the light.
A single ray of white hair-light between the eyebrows—throughout kalpas, where could it have been hidden? The eternal night is vast and silent, the sky has not yet dawned;
one must further raise one’s brow and gaze toward the Fusang tree. (Baoning Yong)

[Added for collection: Fengxue went to Huanglong. Huanglong said, "The stone horn pierces the path through the clouds; what is the meaning of the hanging branches? The Master said, "Red clouds enshroud the jade image;

it embraces the peaks and illuminates the plains. Huanglong said, "If that is so, then I shall follow you. The Master said, "Venerable Sir, lower your voice. Verse: The stone horn pierces the path through the clouds, Hanging branches cast their shadow over the earth. Red clouds enshroud the jade image, Embracing the peaks and illuminating the plains. If you say, "I shall follow you," Then lower your voice, O Venerable One.
A priceless bright pearl hangs in the darkness; at night, one attempts to pierce a wooden man.
Who would have known that it was seen by the earthen ox, who swallowed it into the abyss of crimson mists and azure waves? (Touzi Qing)
[Added for inclusion] Fengxue was once asked by a monk, "What is the Way? The Master said, "Before the Five-Phoenix Pavilion. The monk asked, "What is one who is on the Way?
The Master said, "Ask the City God. The Verse says: Before the Five-Phoenix Pavilion, The City God’s office stands tall. If you wish to know the Way, Go ask the official in charge.

The deep palace and forbidden halls are separated by layered gates; the curtains are still, and from the eaves purple qi hangs down. Moss covers the ground, blocking access to the court for audiences;
when family members point the way, do not hesitate. (Touzi Qing).
[Added from the Supplementary Collection] Fengxue was once asked by a monk: "When deer form a herd, how can one shoot the leader among them? He replied:
"The fishing boat has reached the banks of the Xiao and Xiang rivers; with breath choked, there is no one to ask the white gulls. The Verse says:
In the Forbidden Palace and inner chambers, the hearing and sight are perilous. Reflecting on the side, standing alone, the crimson decree hangs down.
The clouds of the Han region are severed; the marsh islands stretch far away. Monkeys howl at the mountain peaks as the solitary moon follows. (Touzi Qing)

With kindness, he once extended a question to an old man: "Singing at the Eastern Mountain, chanting at the Northern Mountain. To play with the tide, one must be a traveler from the Wu River;
for the parting words, let them belong to a person of the Han lands. (Touzi Qing)

Fengxue was once asked by a monk: "The ancient melody has no rhyme or tune; how can one harmonize with it? The Master said: "A wooden cock crows at midnight; a straw dog barks as day breaks. The Verse says:

A wooden cock cries out in the dead of night; A straw dog barks as the light of dawn appears. The ancient melody is not a tune for the ear; How could it ever be matched by words? If you wish to understand this matter, Look directly at the face before your parents were born.
The moonlight of the ancient crag locks the heavy clouds; Withered trees welcome the fragrance, lingering with spring at evening. Last night the Milky Way was separated from the Southern Dipper;
The golden crow followed the phoenix across the celestial wheel. (Touzi Qing)
[Added from the Supplementary Collection: Chan Master An of Yingqiao in Ruzhou, whose style name was Tiehu (he succeeded Nan’uan).
While he was warming himself by the fire, Minister Zhong asked him, “The three realms are ablaze; how can one escape? The Master used his incense spoon to poke open the fire.
Zhong was deliberating over his words when the Master called out, "Minister! Minister! At that moment, Zhong suddenly attained realization.
The verse says: The three realms blaze fiercely like a mass of fire; The practitioner has no place to rest. In haste, he stirs the flames and calls the Minister;
He takes no heed of the eyebrows above his eyes. Though the eyebrows fall away, the person still lives; Only the cold ashes of the dead fire can understand.
Escape the pit! I report this to you, Zen practitioner: hurry and leap out! Do not let it be that at noon one strikes the third watch.
(Fojian Qín) Loudly stirring the fire, he calls for the Minister: the flames blaze to the heavens, driving right across his face.
If you can sit steadily right here, let the snow fill the streets outside the gate. (Yeyu Chuan)
The three realms are ablaze; one must seek liberation from them. Seeing spring arrive, one sees spring depart. Yet he does not see the coming and going of spring;
the sun rises in the east and sets in the west at night. (Xianji Yun)

Who is the true connoisseur who will retrieve it and restore it? (Touzi Qing)

**[Added] Chan Master Jiche of Bajiao Mountain in Yingzhou (Successor of Bajiao Qing)** A monk asked: "If there is a person who neither abandons birth-and-death nor realizes nirvana, will you still take them by the hand?
The Master said: "I do not take them by the hand. The monk asked: "Why do you not take them by the hand? The Master said: "At Linxi, I had a rough understanding of what is good and what is bad.
**Verse:** Not abandoning life, not seeking extinction, The path of the sages is difficult to fathom. When the old man of Linxi met him, He knew at once he was no ordinary fellow.
It is said:
A hundred-year-old child comes out the door, his entire body red and raw, covered in dust. He walks leisurely through the fire upon a cool ground;
those who understand have no cause to dare approach him. (Touzi Qing)
The Eighth Generation under the Sixth Patriarch (Part Two) [Supplemental Entry] (Seventh Generation under Qingyuan):
Chan Master Huiji of Huanglong Mountain in Ezhou (Heir to Xuanquan Yan). A monk asked, "What is it like when the wind is calm and the waves are still?
The Master said, "Five *liang* hang from the top of a hundred-foot pole. The Verse says:
At the top of a hundred-foot pole, five *liang* of weight hang down; across the desolate sands and boundless desert, one lets oneself be carried by the wind.
How pitiable are the countless travelers on the Canglang River, who still clutch their south-pointing needle to determine where they shall return. (Gong of Shilin)
Chan Master Mingzhao Deqian of Wuzhou (a successor of Luoshan). One day, when the weather was cold, he ascended the hall.
As soon as the assembly had gathered, the Master said, "The wind at the mountain peak is somewhat harsh; this is not a place for you to settle your body or establish your life.
Return first to a warm room to deliberate. He then returned to his quarters. The assembly followed him there and stood in formation. The Master spoke again: "As soon as..."
Upon arriving at the warm room, he saw people nodding off. He drove them all out at once with his staff. The verse says: Within the hall it was exceptionally cold;
who among the many would dare face it head-on? One sees only the western wind sweeping the ground, yet who knows that a single leaf stirs with autumn?
To go to a warm place is to stop and imprison oneself; no one is there to plug the throat. One must surely believe in the High [Mastery].
The Emperor’s achievements are vast; both banks of the Hongguo Canal were reclaimed at once.
(Fohuiquan) Severing the wind’s head, it is difficult to advance or retreat. It is not easy for monks traveling together to observe one another.
Before reaching Tongguan, the sky has already dawned; it is unbearable to turn back and gaze toward Chang’an. (Kaifuning)
The wind at the peak is somewhat harsh, making it difficult to stand firm; as soon as warmth begins to flow, drowsiness sets in.
I laugh, then, at Mingzhao’s wasted effort, needlessly forcing a reconciliation between two sides. (Gushan Gui)
At midnight, the bright star appears at the meridian; yet the fool still waits for the dawn’s crowing cock.
Piteous indeed, he does not know the stench of his own excrement, yet wishes to pick it up anew and present it to others. (Jingshan Gao)
Before the wind, he reveals a flawless jade disk; within the room, he holds aloft a wish-fulfilling jewel.
Twice he offered it to him, yet he did not recognize it; alas, it has wandered lost upon rivers and lakes. (Fóxìng Tái)
[Continued Collection]: "The *xián-niǎo* bird guards an empty pond; fish pass beneath its feet, yet the *xián-niǎo* remains entirely unaware. (Lan’an Xu).
The wind-head has long since been tamed; he further buries himself in warmth.
This causes his traces to remain for a thousand ages, making it all in vain that he ate Luoshan’s white rice. (Jieshi Peng)
The wind at the peak is somewhat harsh, leaving no place to rest; in the warmth, there is not a single word to deliberate upon.
Old and decrepit, unable to cure the world’s afflictions, one vainly takes lethal poison for clarified butter. (Dongshan Yuan)
If calculation at the beginning fails, arrangement at the end will also be incorrect.
Had there been people of the present day in ancient times, they would not have fallen into the trap of others. (Duànqiáo Lún)

A tiger with a swallowtail is difficult to approach; to draw near is to bring one’s own life to an end.
Unless one can personally seize the tiger by its head, the head will naturally be upright and the tail likewise straight. (Gushan Gui)
The seventh is Yantu without a tail; his reputation for eating oxen is already enough to boast of. The forest of monks clamors with their lips and teeth;
