The seventh one has no tail; not falling into the ranks, he alone bares his claws and fangs. If you attempt to reach him with a calculating mind, you will never see him.
You must believe that this is a lotus blooming amidst the flames. (Songyuan Yue)
Chan Master Guicheng Dizang of Fuzhou (who succeeded Xuansha) asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "From the South.
The Master said, "How is the Buddha-dharma in the South? The monk said, "It is full of endless debate and discussion.
The Master said, "How can it compare to my place here, where we till the fields and exchange labor for our meals? The monk said, "But what about the three realms? The Master—
He asked: "What do you call the three realms? The verse says:
Plowing fields to buy rice to eat— Who can discern the truth within these words? After noon, the meal bell tolls; True gold has never lost its luster.
(Yunfeng Yue): Plowing the fields to obtain food to eat;
the Buddha-dharma requires deliberation. In a single word, one transcends the three realms; the numinous faculty emits wondrous light.
(Lingyuan Qing): Plowing the fields for a meal, one waits for those yet to come; the profound and subtle discussion is left to others' conjecture.
Upon the shadowless tree hang the sun and moon—how many people here have their minds extinguished? (Min Gufo).
All manner of doctrines and explanations are merely forced constructs; transmitted from mouth to ear, they become fragmented and distorted.

Plowing the fields to earn one’s meal is a matter of daily life, something those who have not reached full realization do not understand. Once realization is complete, one knows there is nothing further to seek;

like Zhang Liang, one ultimately does not prize the rank of marquis. Forgetting artifice, one returns to dwell among fish and birds; washing one’s feet in the Canglang River, the misty waters are gathered in. (Tiantong Jue)
Plowing fields and eating one's fill have their own reasons; one need not see fit to toil in pursuit of things outside. Do not say that because the mind is weary, the body must also be exhausted;
for the most part, both skill and clumsiness must be fully gathered in. (Yunyan).

[Continued Collection] A thousand-jin weight triggers the heavy mechanism; for a thousand ages, one looks up to his legacy. Though he offered fifteen cities, how could they have been exchanged for the *xiāng-rú* jade?
Amidst such vast deliberation, how can it compare to planting fields to earn one’s meal? One piece of extraordinary affinity—both parts are marvelous.
If you wish to know the *padma* flower amidst the flames, neither heaven nor earth can surpass it. (Fujian Qín)
Plowing the fields for a broad meal; once full, lying down with legs stretched long. Taking the three realms and placing them on the left side.
This drew forth the old, ancient fellow Longya, who held in his hand a broken wooden ladle. (Wuzhun Shanfan)

The wind rises and the tree’s heart trembles; clouds arise and the nature stirs up dust. If you clarify the affairs of today, you will obscure the person of original source. (Lóngjì Xiū)
If one is taught to grasp at objects, one enters the muddled ford; as long as there is even a hair’s breadth of it, it is but dust. Do not believe that in the past there were no forms or marks;
seeking a "knowledgeable friend" (kalyāṇamitra) outside is likewise not true. (Cao Tang Qing).
Clouds arise within the cavern’s shade; the wind stirs, resonating through the forest. If you would understand the affairs of today, half a catty is but eight ounces. (Shangfang Peak)
When trees move, the wind shakes; when dust arises, clouds form. Since ancient times, how has the Supreme Lord Laojun ever had the surname Li? (Duanqiao Lun).
Zen Master Zhihong of Mount Dailong in Dingzhou (he succeeded Baizhao Yuan) was asked by a monk:
"The physical body decays; what is the indestructible Dharma-body? The Master said: "Mountain flowers bloom like brocade; the mountain stream is crystal clear."
Like a blue lotus. The verse says: Question:
I have never known this before. Answer: I still do not understand. The moon is cold and the wind is high; in the ancient crags, the cypress trees are frigid.
How laughable it is to meet a person who has realized the Way and respond with neither speech nor silence! Holding a white jade whip in hand, he shatters all the dragon-pearls. He does not strike.
Shattering the increase of flaws and impurities. The state has three thousand articles of law and offenses. (Xuedou Xian).
Mountain flowers are like brocade, the water is like indigo; clouds rest upon high peaks, the moon is in the pool. Two earthen oxen fight their way into the sea;
the traveler takes off his trousers and carries them on the head of his staff. (Dizang En).
Mountain flowers like brocade, spring remains forever; Creek water like indigo, deep and translucent blue.
Walking at ease into the depths of white clouds, One must know there is another world within the caverns above. (Fojian Qinqin)

The physical body decays; this is the common sentiment of the world. A single point of numinous light shines everywhere with crystalline clarity. The mountain stream is like indigo, the flowers are like brocade.
Where, then, is the Dharma-body not manifest? (Nantang Xing)
Clouds disperse and the moon’s orb fills the sky; mist clears and the mountain peaks rise high. The clay ox traverses the vast ocean; as he turns a corner, wind and waves arise.
(Lian of Tianning Monastery in Jingzhao Prefecture)
[Continued Collection] Mountain flowers like brocade, mountain waters like indigo. Personally seeing Mañjuśrī, he engages in conversation.
With a light squeeze at the crossroads, "three before" matches "three after. (Xiatang Yuan)
The scenery of Dàlóng is most secluded and exquisite; mountain streams and wild flowers shine brightly before the eyes.
What need is there to inquire about the solid *dharmakāya*? This splendor has long existed prior to the kalpa-jar. (Lǐ Tiānmù)
Mountain flowers like brocade, mountain waters like indigo; Emerging from heaven and earth, they reveal no face. I once trod the path by the banks of the Wuling Stream;
The springtime within the caverns differs from that of the human world. (Wuzhun Shanfeng)

Moss grows upon the ancient hall, the images appear unsettled; The frosty wind from all eight directions presses one with cold.
Suddenly the sound of the Dharma is played—whom can it be understood by? Heaven and humanity alike listen to the tinkling jade chimes. (Da-hong Su)
In the ancient hall where no Buddha resides, from whence comes this Brahma-sound? Awakened by a call within a dream, the gates of the pavilions open.
A single point of numinous light, free from all dust, shines through antiquity and surges through the present, pervading the nine realms. (Nantang Xing)
[Added from the Supplementary Collection] Chan Master Tong’an Zhi (successor of Tong’an Pi) of Hongzhou. A monk asked: "How does one proclaim that which is beyond the reach of the two capacities?

The Master said: "Not encountered anywhere; not lost within the mystery. Verse: Not encountered anywhere, Not lost within the mystery. The thousand sages have no place to rest their feet; The myriad phenomena are all of one source. If you wish to know the meaning of this, Look at the face of the old man. Do not seek it elsewhere— It is right here before your eyes.
Neither here nor there can they be encountered; A single word, free from self-interest, does not abide in the center.
The crimson sun sinks behind the western peaks, Leaving only its solitary reflection to shine upon the eastern stream. (Danxia Chun)

[Added from the *Tongan Zhi*]: A monk asked, "Since every word and phrase falls into the present age, I, a student, have come before you; I pray that the Master will point directly. The Master said, "I do not speak of what is before the eyes;

I am not deluded regarding what follows the sentence. He asked again, "What is the matter that transcends the upward direction? The Master said, "It stands utterly alone and cannot be exchanged; to set up a marker is already to deviate.

The Verse says: The words and phrases are all exhausted; The path of the ancients is cut off. If you try to grasp it with the mind, You will surely fall into error. When the wind blows and the clouds disperse, The moon shines clearly upon the mountain peaks. If you wish to see the ancient road, Look at the traces left by the wild ox.
The sky darkens and the clouds deepen; the crows fly away. The egret stands in the snow facing the reeds. Fortunately, this does not belong to the affairs of the present age.
If you seek to understand it after the words or before the sound, you have already missed the mark. (Xueyan Qin)
[Added from the Supplementary Collection] Chan Master Guangde Yi of Xiangzhou (successor of Guangde Yan). A monk asked: "An ancient said, 'The path of language is cut off;

it is neither past, future, nor present. What is the principle of this? The Master said: "How many kalpas have passed since Maitreya entered nirvana? Yet Huiming has still not descended to Kapilavastu. The Verse says: The path of language is cut off; It is neither past, future, nor present.
How many kalpas have passed since Maitreya entered nirvana? Yet Huiming has still not descended to Kapilavastu.

The wondrous, profound, and perfect finger points to the foremost capacity. At the times of descending, attaining enlightenment, and entering nirvana—at Kapilavastu, Magadha, and the twin śāla trees—clinging to these is fundamentally not it. (Danxia Chun)

[Added for Collection] Regarding the meaning of "Extensive Virtue" (Guǎngdé), when a monk asked: "How is it when one has long carried [the burden] but does not encounter the right time? The Master said:
"The fan is opened, yet no one meets [with it]; the humble alley cannot gather it in. The Verse says:
The wondrous body is majestic and its marks and signs are complete; Walking alone across the azure sky, he treads upon golden lotuses.
He is still too weary even to sit upon the thousand-petaled flower pedestal; How could he ever deign to wear a tattered, soiled robe? (Danxia Chun)
[Added from the Supplement] Chan Master Guangde Zhou of Xiangzhou (heir to Guangde Yan). A monk asked:
"The scriptures state that Ajita neither cuts off afflictions nor cultivates dhyāna-concentration, yet the Buddha prophesied that this person will undoubtedly attain Buddhahood.

How is this principle to be understood? The Master said: "The salt is exhausted, and the charcoal is gone. The monk said: "When the salt is exhausted and the charcoal is gone, it is like—" [The Master said: "It is like the time when the salt is exhausted and the charcoal is gone."
"What? The Master said, "Do not speak of your sorrows to one who is already sorrowful; to speak of them to one who is sorrowful is to kill them with grief.
The verse says:
"Gathering and releasing according to the occasion have their standards, yet when leaving the gate or entering the house, it is difficult to discuss. You must [know] the road to Chang'an."
"Arrive! Do not squat in the grass of a deep village. (Xu Tang Yu).
[Added from another collection] Chan Master Huiche of Shimen in Xiangzhou (successor of Shimen Yun). A monk asked, "How does one advance on the ground of the reality-realm (*bhūtatathatā*)?
The Master said, "The bird-path has no front. The monk said, "The white clouds hide within the secluded valley."
The Sparrow. When the mind is set upon its dwelling place, it becomes lost amidst the mountains.
The verse says: White clouds conceal the white sparrow in the deep valley; When the mind is set upon its dwelling place, it is lost amidst the mountains.
Even if one does not dwell in the place where the mind rests, One still falls into Yishan’s second level of teaching. (Lan’an Xu)
Shimen Chere was asked by a monk, "What is the one phrase transmitted outside the teachings of the Three Vehicles? The Master said, "Old Wang of East Village burns paper money at night.

The Verse says: Old Wang of East Village Burns paper money at night; He does not know That the Three Vehicles are empty. If you wish to understand the meaning, Look at the moon reflected in the water.
The old king of the eastern village burns paper money at night; his straw sandals tread upon the earth, his cap points toward heaven. His house lacks a *Bai Ze* to ward off calamity or fortune;
in poverty they scorch one another, in hunger they torment one another. (Dongshan Cong)
Outside the teachings of the Three Vehicles, there is a separate transmission; many blind men who know much call it Chan. The patch-robed monks of the world cannot reach it through study;
Old Wang of the eastern village burns paper money at night. (Yang Wuwai)
The old king of Dongcun burns paper money at night; dust and mist fill his eyes, and smoke issues from his mouth. He summons gods and spirits, becoming a monster;
a three-legged toad flies up into the heavens. (Dizang’s Grace)
In the old village of Dongcun, the King burns paper money at night; wild ghosts and idle spirits fill the space before one’s eyes.
Cease further seeking the profound meaning from others; the Xiexia family is not at the fishing boat. (Shangfang Yi)

[Continued Collection] Old Wang burns paper money at night; by day he gazes upon the stars and moon. He prostrates himself to pay homage to the Compassionate Honored One, holding fragrant incense in his hands as he burns it. (Daowu Zhen)
Eating wood and wearing grass, passing my days as circumstances allow; this body has won the joy of being true to its nature.
Suddenly, when questioned about the phrase of the separate transmission outside the teachings, one cannot avoid burning paper money to lead the ghosts and spirits. (Bao Ye Yuan)

Among the clusters of auspicious grass, I am too weary to sleep; walking slowly everywhere, I am utterly serene. With fur on my body and horns upon my head, I am difficult for people to recognize;
tell the boy Mang not to use the whip. (Danxia Chun)

When someone lightly asks about the ultimate meaning within the profound mystery, one simply bares one's heart and liver to tell them.
At the moment the wooden man secretly furrows his two brows, how can the stone woman, despite her many words, do anything about it? (Touzi Qing)
Profound meaning! Profound meaning! Money and wealth hang upon the wall; the family gate is fortunately at peace.
By day, one summons gods and leads in ghosts. (Yang Wuweī)
The profound meaning is clearly shown to the student: wealth hangs on the wall as gold and silver.
Six scrolls of linked pearls worth three thousand strings of cash—this does not relieve hunger and cold, nor does it relieve poverty. (Zhang Wujin)
[Added for Collection] Chan Master Yuanming Yuangmi of Dingshou (Successor of Yunmen) ascends the hall.
"The great assembly has reached the ultimate limit; even the Buddhas of the three periods have their mouths hung upon the wall.
Yet there is still one person who laughs heartily, 'Ha ha! If you can recognize this person, your studies are complete. Verse:
Two blind men enter a dark and treacherous path; at sunset they rest by the reeds and briefly find relief. How can this compare to the stone man sleeping through the midnight?
It spares him the need for Shun to yield his throne or Yu to dwell in the forests. You must know that the blossoming of flowers has nothing to do with the wood;
when walking without feet, one has already encountered the Way. Yesterday morning the wind rose on the Chang'an road; it was originally Kunlun advancing his national map. (Touzi Qing).
Gathering it in, he seizes the throat. Wind-polished and cloud-wiped, the waters are cold and the sky is autumnal. Do not say that the scaled dragon lacks flavor;
he has fished out the moon with a single hook from the Canglang River. (Tiantong Jue)
The green mountains are the father, the white clouds are the child; when the clouds disperse, the green mountains know nothing at all.
The jade hare sleeps by day upon the ground of cloud-mother; the golden crow lodges by night upon the non-sprouting branch. (Zu’an Jian)
Chan Master Haodian of Xinkai Monastery in Baling, Yuezhou (a successor of Yunmen). A monk asked, "What is the Way? The Master said, "A person with clear eyes falls into a well.
The Verse says: A person with clear eyes falls into a well; Though he has fallen, he does not lose his footing. If you wish to know the ultimate meaning, Look at the bright moon in the sky.
Falling into the well, one must clearly understand the mechanism for exiting it; one should simply lift the eyes and move the pupils with radiance.
If one is thus bold and free from even the slightest obstruction, one attains the ultimate return within the vast expanse of the Patriarchal Way. (Dongshan Cong)
North, south, east, and west, I ask people in vain; you have opened many new mouths to guide those lost at the ford. From now on, the Eight Steeds will pursue the wind with urgency;
one can only look up in vain at the drifting dust beneath one's feet. (Foyin Yuan)
What a fine person with clear eyes falling into a well! When will this talk in the monastic groves ever cease?
Before the mind has reached the groundless state, ten thousand kinds and a thousand variations flow along with the current. (Zhengjue Yi)
A person with clear vision falls into a well; a divine elixir penetrates the golden cauldron. The slave of Kunlun in the black waters passes the night atop Mount Mantian. (Juehaiyuan)
On an autumn night, beneath a frosty sky, the moon shines bright. Looking up at the constellations, it is about the third watch.
A great highway stretches out as level as the palm of a hand; why hinder your return by traveling until dawn? (Bao-ning Yong)
An eye-opening person falls into a well; the ancient terrace of Persia. The three-tiered waves of the Dragon Gate;
in stagnant water, fish dry their gills. (Changling Zhuo)
[Continued Collection] A person with clear eyes falls into a well. The West is on the eastern ridge. Having seized a steamed bun, he opens his fist to find it is a fried cake. (Haoyin Xin).
Speech is not frivolous, and laughter does not come unbidden. A clumsy setup, yet a clever arrangement. The monkey beats the board;
the rustic old man dances the San-tai. (Yazufu-chuan).
A single phrase from Baling: facing each other, yet deceiving one another. The great earth is as level as the palm of a hand;
why do you act so recklessly? (Yue’an Guo).
Who can understand this leading by the head? Sitting and cutting off at the crown of Vairocana. I bow my head to Old Baling:
an eye-bright person has fallen into the well. (Yuelin Guan)
A man with clear vision falls into a well; deep kindness brings deep resentment. When the ocean dries up, its bottom will finally be seen;
when a person dies, their heart remains unknown. (Pak Ong-hyeon)
A monk asked Baling, "What is the 'whisker-cutting sword'? The Master said, "Coral branches branch out, supporting the moon. The Verse says:

Seeking the level in what is not level, great skill appears as if clumsy. Whether pointing with a finger or a palm, it leans against the sky and reflects the snow. In the great forge, it is ground to a fine edge.
The grindstone does not stop turning; the skilled craftsman brushes and polishes it without ceasing. Farewell, farewell! Coral branches reach up, supporting the moon.
(Xuedou Xian) Coral branches reach up, supporting the moon; its brilliance strikes the Dipper, yet its sharp edge is not yet fully seen. From the four seas, all come to offer tribute.
Afterward, heaven and earth shine together with a cold, precious light (Baiyun Yuan).
Its value is three thousand pieces of gold and cannot be depicted; let it be called a model by force for a thousand ages.
Because the smoke and dust of the north have long been stilled, one remembers the cries of the *shàgū* birds in Jiangnan (Changling Zhuo).
[Continued Collection] Having escaped the service of a frontier garrison, he comes instead to steal the springtime beauty of the imperial gardens.
He speaks in low tones before the Imperial Street, unaware that he has run into an official investigating appearances and conduct. (Xinwen Ben)
A monk asked Baling, "What is the school of Deva? The Master said, "Snow in a silver bowl.
He then offered this verse:
The old and the new are opened up; the point is distinct. If one can say, "Snow in a silver bowl," Then among the ninety-six [heretical schools], they shall know it for themselves.
Not knowing, he instead asks the moon at the edge of the sky. The School of Deva, the School of Deva—beneath the red banner, a pure wind arises.
(Xuedou Xian) Refined gold from the great furnace, a bright moon in a clear pool; whether north, south, east, or west, who can distinguish superiority or inferiority? Last night, the spring breeze...
A gust of wind arrives, sweeping away the snow from a thousand mountains and ten thousand peaks.
(Haiyin Xin) On the assembly of devas and humans, black and white are distinguished; before the hall of dragons and elephants, right and wrong are settled.
What need is there to speak of demons, spirits, or strange species? Let them all be led to return together within this very place. (Baoning Yong)

Snow held within a silver bowl; a precious moon contained within a crystal pitcher. Even if one were fully versed in the four Vedas, upon reaching this point, they would merely wag their tongues in vain.
The mandate of the Western Heaven is stern; yet in this land, it is yet different. (Fóxìng Tàiyī)
[Continued Collection]: The Silver Bowl Snow of the Deva School melts away; Mount Tai crumbles and the vast ocean dries up.
Beneath the crimson banner, a pure wind arises, blowing down the willow blossoms as hard as iron. (Fuxincai)

A monk asked Ba’ling, “Are the meaning of the Patriarchs and the meaning of the teachings the same or different? The Master said, “When the rooster is cold, it climbs the tree; when the duck is cold, it goes down into the water. The Verse says: When the rooster is cold, it climbs the tree; When the duck is cold, it dives into the water. The ancient path is not far from here; One must simply know how to walk it. If you can discern this within yourself, You will see that there is no duality between the two. If you do not understand this now, How will you ever know it later? The great matter of birth and death— How can one avoid being deceived by others? If you wish to attain liberation, You must first sever the root of delusion. Do not seek outside yourself; Seeking outside is a futile effort. If you can turn back and look within, You will find the true source of the Way. The myriad phenomena are all empty and still; The ten directions are originally one. If you can realize this in an instant, You will transcend the world of birth and death. Do not cling to words and phrases; Words and phrases are but empty echoes. If you grasp at them, you will be lost; If you let go, you will be free. The Great Matter is right before your eyes— Why do you fail to recognize it? If you can see through this now, You will never again fall into error. Picking up a tortoise’s hair, one laughs heartily; with a single blow, ten thousand layers of locks are opened. Even if a wax figure were as solid as ice, what would it matter?

Chan Master Chengyuan of Xianglin Monastery in Qingcheng, Yizhou (a successor of Yunmen). A monk asked, "What is the very meaning of the coming from the West?

The Master said, "Sitting for too long leads to fatigue. The monk asked, "What about when one turns back immediately? The Master said, "Falling into a deep pit. The Verse says: Sitting for too long leads to fatigue; Turning back immediately is falling into a deep pit. If you wish to see the true meaning of the coming from the West, Look at the old man on the mountain peak.
One, two, ten thousand, a million. Cast off the headstall, unload the pack-saddle. Turning left, turning right, they follow after.
Zihu wants to strike Liu Tiemo. (Xuedou Xian)
In the Fragrant Forest there are no miscellaneous trees; every single one is sandalwood. Suddenly a wild fire breaks out, and the pure wind makes heaven and earth vast.
The Patriarch’s intent is reported to you all: sitting for too long naturally leads to weariness. (By Yanxuan Zun)
How greatly mistaken are those of the Chan school! They do nothing but seek a medicine for when they are not ill.
If one knew that afflictions are themselves bodhi, then even the fatigue of sitting for a long time would be peaceful and joyful. (Fujian Yongqin)

Bodhidharma did not understand—what a great difficulty, what a great difficulty! (Xuedou Xian).
In the twelfth month, fire burns the mountains; two suns appear at the edge of the sky. Xianglin never understood this;
he sat in vain at the Jiamen Pass. (Foyin Yuan)
A monk asked about what lies beneath the robe. The Master replied: "Fire burning the mountains; even a Buddha’s hand cannot stop it. The human mind seems as if it were indifferent. (Zhengjue Yi)
The year draws to a close and the late autumn brings bitter cold; the leaves of the thousand trees have all withered away.
Blazing wild fires leave no flowing water behind; they must surely follow the wind across other mountains. (By Yishang)
The great masters of the ancient forests speak Chan with ease; they do not hang Chan upon the surface of their lips.
Valleys deep and mountains remote, empty and without form—where could a person call out so that the resonance is not perfect? (Tiantong Jué)
Burning the mountains in the twelfth month—this is groundlessly superfluous. Wrapping brocade around a stone; encasing a clod of mud in iron.
(Yuánwù Qín) In the twelfth month, the mountain fires stretch across the sky. How can the affairs within the patched robe be transmitted?
In my old age, I do not wait for auspicious times; when weary, I simply stretch out both legs and sleep. (Báiyáng Shùn)
[Continued Collection] How magnificent! In the twelfth month, fire burns the mountains.
[Blank]. The nests know the wind; the caves know the rain. Piteous is Xie Sanlang, rowing his boat by himself under the moon. (Wenshu Neng).
In the twelfth month, one burns the mountains; facing them, there is only heat and deception. In a sudden flash, one awakens and finds oneself in Chang’an.
Alas! How many travelers have yet to return? To seek oil from sand is truly pitiable. (Shichuang Gong)
In the twelfth month, the fire burns the mountains at Xianglin; even those with iron eyes and copper pupils find it difficult to see.
A single spark lightly struck behind the head, and three thousand *li* away, the skulls have dried. (Zhu’an Guang)
In the twelfth month, fire burns the mountains; bitter to the taste is the *huanglian* (Coptis). Together they approach the eve of the year;
Dou Ba wears his coarse cloth shirt. How truly pitiable! Hand in hand, they enter the Yellow Springs. (Wan’an Yan)
Under the hem of the patched robe, one tends the fire as the mountains burn; in the twelfth month, poverty strikes to the very bone.
How laughable that this continuity has never ceased—the eyebrows are scorched crimson and the face is parched dry. (Tiantong Jing)
In the twelfth month, the fires burn the mountains at Xianglin; look back upon this austere tradition.
Only when one truly steps lightly amidst the clamor does one realize that it is midday and yet the third watch strikes. (By Bai Zhuo)
In the twelfth month, the mountains are set ablaze; heaven is vast and earth is wide. Wherever one strikes or brushes against it, the very marrow of one’s bones and the hairs on one’s skin grow cold.
(Songyuan Yue) In the twelfth month, fire burns the mountains; heaven is broad and earth is wide. Bodhisattva Sadāprarudita suffers, selling his heart and liver throughout the marketplace.
(At the high plateau spring).
Setting fire to the mountains in the twelfth month—what deception is there? A lacquer bucket is not happy; do not persist in your reckless drilling. (Puweng Xian).

[Added from the Supplement] Once, when a monk asked Xianglin, "What is the livelihood of a patch-robed monk? the Master said, "Plowing fields in one's ears. The verse says: In the ears, he plants his fields; In the nostrils, he sows the seeds. When the autumn harvest ripens, He gathers it all at once. The whole world is his single bowl; How could there be any lack? If you wish to know the source, Look at the clouds in the sky.
Planting fields within the ears; a mouthful of smoke. Zhong Kui can dance the eighteen beats;
Old Zhang rides the raft up to the Ninth Heaven. (Wuan Quan).

[Added for collection: A monk asked Xianglin, "Who is the master of ten thousand acres of wasteland? The Master said, "Look, look; the twelfth month is ending. Verse: Ten thousand acres of wasteland— Who is the master? Look, look; the twelfth month is ending. The weeds are all withered away. The moonlight shines bright upon the empty fields. In the vast expanse of the autumn sky, There is not a single cloud to be seen.
The embroidered ball is tossed out before the painted hall; its wondrous turning is impartial, its essence naturally round.
If you truly wish to perform the business of the sword’s edge, you must see Old Yunmen once more. (Shiji Ming)
Of these ten thousand acres of wasteland, who is the master? One must know that there is a source for the answer.
If no one within this can truly understand, look—December is already drawing to a close. (By Jianweng Jing)
Look at the end of the twelfth month: how are your daily affairs? The wealthy lament that a thousand mouths are too few;
the poor resent that even one body is too many. (Yunna Qing).

[Added from the Supplement] Because a monk asked Xianglin, "What is the single bowl of lamp-light within the room? the Master said, "Three people testify that a tortoise becomes a turtle. The Verse says: Three people testify that a tortoise becomes a turtle; The light of the single bowl fills the room. If you can see it clearly right now, There is no need to seek it elsewhere.
A plot hatched before six ears does not succeed. Speaking directly reveals one’s true heart. Who comes to flicker the lamp-flame within the room?
A child with white hair has two newly sprouted tufts at his temples. (Touzi Qing)
Brilliant and pure light pervades the entire realm, leaving nothing hidden. Sound cannot be cast out; how could form ever be made manifest?
Right here, nails are severed and iron is cut through, eradicating all ancient tracks and byways. Surpassing Linji and Deshan, these three men mistake a tortoise for a turtle.
Distinct and separate. Each time one drinks the water, each time one chokes. (Yuánwù Qín).
Three people take a tortoise and certify it as a soft-shelled turtle. The mud-ox at the bottom of the well has its breath choked.
Even if one’s eloquence flows like a cascading river, there is no way to clear one’s innocence through reasoning. A solitary radiance shines resolutely, ever bright and pure. (Fóxìng Tài).
Three people try to prove that a tortoise is a turtle; a single blast from Vairambha wind blows them all out.
From this point on, they will be threading needles in the dark, their nostrils torn to pieces like scattered flowers. (Shui-an I)
The three men take a tortoise and certify it as a turtle; they have just leaked the celestial mechanism. The wooden man sings atop the ridge;
the stone woman sheds blood from her eyes. (Lan’an Xu)

A single bright lamp within a room may, in an ordinary moment, be extinguished with a single blow; naturally, one can no longer distinguish east from west, thereby sparing oneself the embarrassment of mistaking a tortoise for a turtle. (Tui’an Qi)

Chan Master Shouchu of Dongshan in Xiangzhou (he was a successor of Yunmen). When he first visited Yunmen, Yunmen asked, "Where have you recently come from?
The Master replied, "From Chadu. Yunmen asked, "Where were you during the summer retreat?
The Master replied, "In Hunan. Yunmen asked, "When did you leave Hunan? The Master replied, "Last autumn. Yunmen said, "I grant you thirty blows!"
The Master asked, "Where does the fault lie? [Zhaozhou] replied, "In Jiangxi and Hunan, they are already like this.

At these words, the Master was suddenly enlightened. (The *Wudeng Huiyuan* records: When he first visited Yunmen, Yunmen asked, "Where have you recently come from? Zhaozhou said, "Chadu. Yunmen asked, "Where were you during the summer retreat? Zhaozhou said, "Baoci in Hunan. Yunmen asked, "When did you leave there?

Zhaozhou said, "On the twenty-fifth of the eighth month. Yunmen said, "I grant you three blows of the staff. On the following day, Zhaozhou went up to pay his respects and said, "Yesterday, I received the Master’s gift of three blows of the staff.")

[The Master] did not know where his fault lay. [Dongshan] said, “You rice-bag! You go off to Jiangxi and Hunan acting just like this. At these words, the Master attained great enlightenment. He then said, “In the future, I shall dwell in uninhabited places, without storing a single grain of rice or planting a single stalk of vegetable. I will receive those coming and going from the ten directions and help them all pull out their nails and extract their wedges.

I will strip away their greasy hats and take off their foul-smelling cloth robes, teaching them to be carefree as monks of non-action. Would that not be joyful? Yunmen said, “Your body is the size of a coconut, yet you open such a large mouth! The Master then bowed. The Verse says: A rice-bag goes off to Jiangxi and Hunan; Under the words, he attained great enlightenment. He will pull out nails and extract wedges for all;

How joyful it will be to be a monk of non-action! Yunmen’s words were sharp as a sword; The Master’s bow was deep and true. The Great Way is vast and boundless; Who can measure its depth? A single word, and the whole world is overturned; A single phrase, and the myriad phenomena are revealed. If you wish to see the ancient one, Look at the Master’s bow.
To break the three barriers with a single arrow is not difficult; how is it that you still remain within the realm of right and wrong? It takes great effort to lift up this "rice-bag" (the body);
only after three blows does one realize the bone-chilling cold. (Baizhang Yuanwen)
Three blows at that time could not turn him back; the iron gate was struck heavily before the lock finally opened.
Alas, he did not store even a single grain of rice, yet he welcomed all who came and went at the crossroads. (Baoning Yong)
From of old, the Great Way leads straight to Chang’an; at every step, one must keep one’s eyes open. At five *li*, one knows only that it is five *li*;
only upon reaching the end does one realize how difficult the path’s forks have been. (Kumu Cheng)
In the eighth month of last year, I left Hunan; I traversed ten thousand peaks and myriad mountains.
Had I not received the three blows of Yunmen’s staff, I would not have known that the tiger’s body bears its dark stripes. (Cishou Shen)
The old ox sits firm in Shao Yang; beyond the lakes of Jiangxi, he swiftly returns the favor. At that time, the iron barrier was raised high;
it was not necessarily that the Yellow River does not flow backward. (Baofeng Xiang)
The precious sword that whets its own hair is wondrous when it meets the occasion; cutting jade as if it were mud, who could possibly fathom it?
Without striking the blade’s edge, the true command is fully maintained; the Dharma King’s Heart-Seal is now opened for you. (Heshan Fang)
Yunmen’s staff has eyes; beneath Dongshan’s feet, clouds arise. Once one pierces through the myriad phenomena of the universe, one can traverse freely across the sea. (Fuxin Cai)
The clarity of this question-and-answer exchange is surely no accident; one must know that words which grate against the ear are loyal counsel.
Dongshan’s eyes turned like copper bells, yet he was stubbornly deceived three times by Yunmen. (Wenshu said:)
I offer you three prostrations with deep reverence; An embarrassment for the old master Yunmen.
A traveler of the Five Lakes, crossing waters and piercing clouds— With what would he sustain his livelihood? (Longmen Yuan)
[Continued Collection] Seeing the rabbit, one releases the hawk; because of walking, one swings the arms. When the bare bones are exhausted, squareness and roundness become wealth and honor.
Even after three blows of the staff have been released, one still hesitates; only by pushing further does one recognize the sharpness of the awl’s point.
Held up alone, beyond the mechanism of the single-legged staff—even clear-eyed monks do not yet understand it. (Yuánwù Qín).
Yunmen, you rice-bag! A venomous snake blocking the ancient road; it injures anyone who touches it—dare anyone look upon it with a direct eye? (Wuxiang Fan).
Dongshan was first asked by a monk, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "Three pounds of hemp. The Verse says:
Three pounds of hemp-skin need no scale; How could the scale-head tolerate a fly sitting upon it? As soon as a single thought arises, the sinews and bones are exposed;
To labor further in seeking the zero-point of the balance is in vain. (Beitang Zu)
A bull’s head painted in five colors, with its forehead dotted with gold; on a bright spring morning in the second month, all farmers take this as their model.
At the Cold Food Festival, celebrating the new year, three or five hundred pieces of iron coin [are offered]. (Fuyan Ya)
The golden crow hastens, the jade hare speeds; how could a skillful response ever involve a slight touch? To manifest the matter and seize the opportunity, one meets Dongshan;
the lame tortoise and blind turtle enter the empty valley. Flowers cluster, brocade clusters; bamboo in the south, wood in the north.
Reflecting on Great Officer Lu of Changqing, who understood that one should laugh and not weep (Xuedou Xian):
"A leap year once every three years is known to all, yet there are those who are negligent and fail to keep track of the time. Last night the wild geese returned as the frontier passes grew cold;
frost-laden wutong leaves fell in profusion once more" (the old edition reads: "A harsh wind blew, blossoming the branches of the moonlit tree"). (Touzi Qing)
How can one divide the seeds of the hemp? Boiling tea with last winter’s snow will sober you from your intoxication.
There is yet a path that travelers have not reached; wild flowers hold their smiles upon the old branches of spring. (Fachang Yu)
Beating the drum and playing the lute, we meet as two members of the same family. Last year it was the Fith of the Fifth Month; this year, once again, it is returned to him. (Fushan Yuan)
Gazing askance, he reads the Sanskrit script; curling his tongue, he recites the mantras. Blowing fire from his long, pointed beak, smoke rises from the full hearth. (Dagui Zhi)
"What is the Buddha? "Three catties of hemp. (A shout! The vast expanse of the great earth brings sorrow unto death.
(Cuiyan Zhen) A single crescent moon newly risen; Eyebrows painted across the azure sky. Fish in the water avoid the hook; Birds beyond the clouds guard against the bow.
(Yexuan Zun) asked: "Three catties of hemp for the Buddha;
fear of night tea for the monks' feast. Since spring comes after the Cold Food Festival, ancient trees resound with the cawing of cold crows."
(Seal of the Ocean-Print).

Fellow practitioners, seeking the Way, ask for the ford to the thoroughfare. Coming to叩 (knock upon) the Master for the Buddha’s true cause, he speaks for them: "Three catties of hemp are most excellent.
"Three catties" is proclaimed throughout the world as sharp and new. How many craftsmen have repeatedly picked it up? Yet, alas, the monastics and laypeople...
Regarding the distinction between the distant and the intimate: Your son now weighs it again on a heavy scale. Prince Nanda dismembered his entire body (Daowu Zhen).
Dongshan had the saying, "Three pounds of hemp" (Mazu). A patch-robed monk raised his fists and asked about the critical pass. It makes me recall looking at the cursive script of old;
after Zhang Xuan (Zhangdian), there has been no one else. (Yunfeng Yue).
Clouds rise as the thousand mountains awaken at dawn; the wind rises high as the ten-thousand trees turn autumnal. Beneath the waters of Stonehead City, waves beat upon the fishing boat. (Fohuiquan)
The weight is clearly defined; I do not betray you. Let no anger arise within the pupils of your eyes.
Of the three hundred and sixty thousand days of a hundred-year life, when you find a moment of joy, simply rejoice therein. (Baizhang Yuanwen)
Dongshan’s “three pounds of flax”: clearly, he was missing one move. The patch-robed monk cannot let it go; seeking through words, he grasps at empty air. (Yungai Zhi)

In the third month of spring in Jiangnan, the world is like the *zhègūtiān* bird’s song. After the rain, the scenery of all the peaks is fresh and bright. Having traveled to the ends of the earth, I have come to understand the ways of the world:
to buy shoes, one must pay with "Great Light" coins. (By the Third Patriarch)
A cubit-long jade璧 is not considered weighty; a single word must not be taken lightly. Grasp the meaning at the tip of the hook; do not fixate on the zero point of the scale. (Dizang’s Grace).
The southern heavens are warm, the northern heavens are cold; water and land communicate with one another, not difficult to see.
Boundless yellow flowers alongside emerald bamboo—let them be viewed by those of a thousand ages past and present. (Cao Tang Qing).
Dongshan’s three pounds of flax: bestowed upon people before the Hall of the Bright Moon.
As soon as those with azure eyes and shaggy brows lift their heads, they are again startled by the clouds and rain. (Changling Zhuo)
Three catty of Dongshan hemp is enough for weighing; a shift of a single grain of dust creates ten thousand miles of error.
Weeping until the blood flows is of no use; last night, as always, one lay among the reeds. (Zhang Wujin)
The momentum of a thousand peaks halts at the foot of the mountain; the roar of ten thousand streams vanishes into the sea.
A golden bullet bursts forth from the red furnace; the eyes blink and the face-skin burns. (Nanhua Bing)
The wild goose and crane soar a thousand li with a single flight; the piercing falcon soars to the very heavens. The phoenix is no ordinary bird of this world;
it appears as an auspicious omen only at its appointed time. (Longmen Yuan)
[Continued Collection]: "Dongshan’s 'Three Pounds of Hemp. Brass does not trade for gold; spending money to buy five colors to paint a celestial deity on a wall. (Langya Huijue)

Dongshan’s “three pounds of flax”: its weight does not deceive people; his words are rare, yet the matters he asks about are difficult to fathom; his appearance is ancient, yet it is easy for the spirit to be transmitted (Cishou Shen).
The samādhi of the present moment: measuring water and beating the pestle; leaking the celestial mechanism; losing money and meeting with retribution (Mañjuśrī Neng).
Dongshan’s Buddha-talk about "three catties of hemp" has bound and killed the old masters of the forest.
How wonderful—a single note of the flute before the wind; in the fifth month, plum blossoms fall upon the river city. (Shi Jianming)
The bell rings when struck; the valley receives the echo. The pond reflects the moon; the mirror contains the image. This was never about performing a task or seizing an opportunity;
how could it be about scratching before the itch arises? To turn iron into gold; to set the upright against the crooked. One arrow, two eagles; one slap, blood on both palms. Do you not see?
Sparse yet without leakage—vast indeed is the net of Heaven. (Wenyu Qin)
Donkey’s tail, pig’s head, ox’s hoofprints—three catties of hemp skin reveal the message. Master Zhizang’s staff-tip holds scissors and a ruler;
from of old, when it rains, the steps at the foot of the stairs get wet. (Yuanquan Lian)
Old Dongshan makes no distinction between the intimate and the distant; he answers the Buddha-dharma with "three pounds of flax. Having no face, he earns the hatred of others;
yet to see through him thoroughly would be to bring ruin upon oneself. (Miaofeng Shan)
The waters cut off the flow; the mountains loom abruptly. For you, I release the falcon from the vast heavens.
When one intends to act for even a fleeting moment before the wind, the moment it lifts its eyes, it has already become a nest. Not a nest! *Du du du!* (Tudu Ce).
[Added for inclusion] Initially, when a monk asked Dongshan, "What is the Eye of the True Dharma? the Master said, "A paper wick without oil.
The verse says:
The master of the Dongshan school has but a slight advantage; testing a true adept with a paper wick without oil. Old and decrepit Chan practitioners have eyes like needles;
those who speak of Chan and speak of the Way are as numerous as hemp seeds. (Cuiyan Zhen)
[Added for inclusion] When Dongshan first ascended the hall, he said: "Words do not unfold the matter; speech does not meet the occasion. Those who rely on words perish;
those who linger in phrases are deluded. Can you grasp this? Within the domain of you monks, reaching this point, you must possess the eye that discerns the Dharma before you can succeed.
Yet, even so, Dongshan’s speaking in such a manner carries a fault. Tell me, what is the fault?
"In what place? The verse says:
"One simply must pull out the wedge and extract the nail; for others, one unties the glue and removes the bonds.
How is it that Old Man Dongshan first wraps a python around his own feet? (Gushan Gui).
Words cannot fully express the matter; speech does not hit the mark. Those who merely receive the words perish; those who stagnate in phrases are deluded.
When meeting people, do not make a single mistaken move. (Jingshan Daokai)
In performing the task, there is no turning back; when the opportunity arises, it passes through a single thread. Dongshan lacks the sinews of vision;
he enters hell like an arrow. (Nanyuan Sheng)
[Added to the Collection] Chan Master Fengxian Shen of Jinling (a successor of Yunmen). While traveling with Master Tongming, they saw people pulling in a net by the Huai River.
A fish had escaped through the mesh. The Master said, "Brother Ming, how clever!
You are just like a true monk. Tongming said, "Even so, it would have been better had he not run right into the net in the first place."
Luo Hao. The Master said, "Brother Ming, you still lack awakening. It was not until midnight that Ming attained realization (Ming refers to Chan Master Zhiming of Qingliang in Jinling;
various lineage records refer to him as the Elder Shengming). The verse says:
A golden-scaled fish that has passed through the net is a true monk; he is not startled by iron walls and silver mountains.
At the third watch of the night, Minglao finally glimpsed his ground; let the thousand peaks remain in their layers of blue. (Daiman Zhi)
Leaping out of the net, he soars away. What a naturally gifted and eminent monk! How could he compare to when he had not yet entered the net?
Only upon awakening does one become a true connoisseur. (Gushan Gui)
How magnificent! With a single leap he penetrates the deep abyss; the thunderbolt pursues him, but he does not return. One must laugh at those who burn their tails at the Dragon Gate;
they remain with their foreheads marked by the scales amidst the waves. (Jingshan Gao)
A lion bites a person; a mad dog chases a clod of earth. Only after coming from thirty li away does one finally awaken.
How is this different from not entering in the first place? (Yeyu Valley).

Again he asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said, "Do not, do not."
The verse says: The ancients were singularly silent; one must strictly avoid pecking and scratching. Linji temporarily entrusted it to the storehouse; Deshan suddenly fell into desolation.
He cut off the mechanisms of Buddhas and patriarchs, revealing that one stroke at the crown of the head. Examine and deliberate carefully: clearly, there is still one stroke missing.
Tell me, what is missing? (Xuetang Xing). No, no.
He draws out a single broken tethering rope; let the Buddhas and all sentient beings be at liberty—his nostrils that pierce the heavens have been pierced through all. (Songyuan Yue).

Blended yet unmixed, its essence is ever void; In the mingling light of snow and moon, nothing can compare.
Responding to myriad circumstances without hindrance, A single cloud freely rolls up and unfurls (its own radiance).

The bride rides the donkey while the mother-in-law leads it. Who is behind and who is ahead? Zhang San and Li Si join their hands in greeting the year of Yao.
All the sages of antiquity were likewise thus; whether rising or sitting, they were neither anxious nor indifferent.
If someone asks, you must say to them: "The bride rides the donkey while the mother-in-law leads it. (Shending Yin)

Whether one attains it or not, whether the transmission is passed on or not—once one has returned to the root and attained the essential meaning, what more is there to say? I recall that in the past, Shoushan once let it leak out:
"The daughter-in-law rides the donkey, while the mother-in-law leads her. (Huanglong Nan)
Carrying a handle in hand and treading on a tail with his feet, he looks up at the sky and listens to the flowing water.
At daybreak he is sent out to the roadside; at night’s quiet, he returns to his thatched hut. (Daowu Zhen).
The bride rides the donkey while her mother-in-law leads it; Old Wang steers an iron ship through the air. A sail is hung at the bottom of a well where the wind is fierce;
atop the summit of Mount Sumeru, the waves overflow to the heavens. (Seal of the Ocean-Mudra)
The bride rides the donkey while her mother-in-law leads it; bystanders laugh at their topsy-turvy way. Returning home, she looks up to see the evening clouds gathering;
the moon on the ridge has not yet reached its full orb. (Lian of Tianning Monastery, Jingzhao Prefecture)
Seven hands and eight feet; three heads and two faces. Hearing with the ears, one does not hear; looking with the eyes, one does not see. To weep until the blood flows is of no avail;
it is better to seal one’s mouth and pass through the remainder of spring. (Baoning Yong)
Zhangdian was no match for Shoushan Dian; without moving a single hair’s breadth, he manifested every marvel.
Yet Huanglong was able to bring it forth once more—how could those with clear eyes in the four quarters fail to transmit it? The daughter-in-law rides the donkey while her mother-in-law leads it;
Bending down, she picks up a single coin. At the crossroads, she claps her hands and laughs; Old Wang of the eastern village has a hole in his roof. (Zhenjing Wen)
Shoushan has a saying passed down through all time: "Do not say this saying is perverse and topsy-turvy;
when the new bride, drunk, rides off on her donkey, people laugh as the mother-in-law pulls it. (Foguo Bai).
The bride rides the donkey while her mother-in-law leads it; her face is like the full moon, her eyes like lotuses. Once again, she uses her silken sleeves to pull and guide him.
This one segment of elegance pervades the great thousandfold world-system. (Cishou Shen)
The daughter-in-law rides the donkey while her mother-in-law leads it; her graceful bearing is naturally elegant.
One can only laugh at the neighbor’s daughter who mimics her, adding ugliness for others rather than achieving beauty. (Tiantong Jue)
Do not ask about the daughter-in-law or the mother-in-law; avoid troubling those on the high road with idle chatter. When you meet rice, eat rice; when you meet tea, drink tea.
Entering and exiting through the same gate—what an enemy from past lives! (Wuzu Yan)
The bride rides the donkey while her mother-in-law leads it; a jade-green patterned swirl atop her head. She stirs up dust and soil, yet cannot find it;
it turns out to be right before the old mountain. (Mañjuśrī said:)
The bride rides the donkey while her mother-in-law leads; ten thousand li across the vast blue sea, they board an iron ship.
The jagged islands divide the various nations; the shimmering starry river shares one common sky. (Nan Hua Bing)
Mother-in-law and daughter-in-law share the same lineage; though they are but a few inches apart, the road to their home is not far.
How laughable are those who, riding a donkey, seek the donkey itself—they have mistaken the saddle-bridge for their life’s purpose all along. (Gushan Gui)
The bride rides the donkey while her mother-in-law leads; step by step they follow one another, yet the whip is not used. Having returned to the painted hall, no one recognizes her;
from now on, she will be too weary to appear before others again. (Jingshan Gaofeng)
The mother-in-law and daughter-in-law cherish each other most deeply. When the daughter-in-law rides her donkey, the mother-in-law leads it by the halter.
How many times have they returned home drunk under the bright moon, led into the painted hall to the accompaniment of pipes and songs? (By Hugu)
[Continued Collection] The new bride joyfully rides the donkey; the mother-in-law leads it by the whip. At night, the stone pillar sprouts branches;
facing south, she gazes at the Big Dipper. (Zantang Shen)
The new bride rides the donkey while her mother-in-law leads it. Among the grass, there are countless ordinary people. Who is behind and who is ahead?
There is no need to needlessly apply the whip with such severity. (Muan Zhong)
A lame donkey must be led by its mistress; the daughter-in-law, coy and foolish, is too lazy to crack the whip. At home she knows only seventy-two;
only upon leaving the door does she see that they have become three thousand. (Jiantan Ji)
