A torch before every door; clearly evident from ancient times to the present, you must take note. After the fifth-watch bell, listen for the crowing of the cock;
the dawn official who misses the hour does not wear his cap. (Shimen Cong)
Before the gate, the torches return to the Jewel Mountain; disciples of the profound study fill the nine realms. On the shores of the South Sea, waves arise;
the felt hats of the Western Barbarians are now cut in the current style. (Cuiyan Zhen)
Who would believe it when he returns empty-handed? A donkey-load or a horse-load enters the gate;
every household raises its torch, and at midnight the sky is as bright as day. (Baiyun Wenzhun)
When reaching the Mountain of Jewels, what is there to do? Returning empty-handed, the gain is great.
Before every door is a torch, as bright as the sun and moon, illuminating the mountains and rivers. (Fujian Yongqin)
A monk asked Shoushan, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? The Master said, "Beside the city of King Chu, the River Ru flows eastward. The Verse says:
Beside the ancient city of King Chu, the Ru River flows toward the east. On both banks, anglers vie to cast their lines;
how many among them can truly use a straight hook? (Zhengjue Yi)
The waters east of the Bǔwáng fortress flow on; chasing the currents and following the waves, when will they ever cease? Who would say that Xiè Láng’s livelihood lies here?
Deep in the night, the bright moon ascends his solitary boat. (Fóhuìquán)
The waters flow eastward from the banks of the King of Chu’s city; the trees fall and the vines wither, yet the laughter does not cease.
It is truly so since Touzi departed; no one else has been able to speak of this "you-you. (Zhenjing Wen)
The waters flow eastward from the banks of King Chu’s city; from ancient times to the present, they reach the sea as their ultimate destination.
If the surging waves and drifting currents do not cease, one must yield to the fisherman who glides upon his solitary boat. (Miaoshan Xiu)
The waters by the walls of the state of Chu flow eastward; as soon as the boat sets sail, it is struck by a headwind. Amidst the reeds of Lu-hua Bay, one hears the fishermen’s calls;
the tea-kettle for brewing tea is no different from an iron smoothing-iron. (Third Patriarch)
The waters flow eastward from the banks of the King of Chu’s city; day and night, the waves and surges depart without ceasing.
Suddenly, beneath a crag, one encounters a traveler from the Xiang River, who says that the current still flows on, vast and unending. (Yunxi Gong)
A thousand waves and ten thousand ripples never cease; departing oars and arriving sails are vast beyond measure. Xie Ke awakens from sleep to find the solitary moon white;
idly I blow a single flute against the wind at the river crossing. (Puyongping)
[Added for Collection] By the walls of the King of Chu’s city, the waters flow east; a Chan monk from the south travels north.
May his eyes be made to discern clearly from the shallow depths; yet how can the scales and compass escape the common stream? With a golden probe, I pluck away the cataracts for you;
a boot is strapped onto a donkey’s back to play with a ball. (Cuiyan Zhen)
By the walls of the King of Chu’s city, the water flows east; a one-legged mountain shiao kicks a breath-ball.
Greedily clinging to the eighteen *ṣaḍāyatana*-flowers, the headless boatman sails down to Yangzhou. (Xiatang Yuan)
The heat departs and the cold arrives; spring follows autumn. The setting sun goes west, the waters flow east.
Vast and boundless is the universe, with countless people; who among them has ever reached the very source? (Xueyan Qin)
At Shoushan, a monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said, "Blown by the wind and scorched by the sun. The Verse says:

Scorched by the sun and blown by the wind for countless years, It would be difficult for a traveler on the dusty road to discern it. If you conceive a thought, you have already gone three fathoms deep.
A foot. Who else can be taught to inquire into the mystery within this? (Dongshan Cong).

Blown by the wind and scorched by the sun, few people know it. Looking up to the former sages for this very pivot, even if you had attained realization throughout kalpas of past lives, the barbarian monk with pierced ears would still frown. (Fahua Ju).
Scorched by the sun and buffeted by the wind, one asks where the Patriarch came from. Red dust stretches across the wilds; the eyes can hardly be raised. How many are busily engaged in toil?
In the deep spring of the second month, the dragon’s roar stirs the earth. (Cuiyan Zhen)
Blown by the wind and scorched by the sun, he lies prostrate in the wild grass. Upon encountering the toxic vapors, his entire body collapses. (Tianning Lian).
How extraordinary it is to be scorched by the sun and blown by the wind! Genqiang is but a lone horseman, a son of a military family.
From of old, the imperial domain has been fundamentally free of affairs; who else could have stirred up this dust and smoke? (Emperor Taizong).
Scorched by the sun and buffeted by the wind at the head of the road—when a monk sees this, let there be no lingering delay.
I have now arrived here, filled with sorrow; leaves fall and flowers bloom red through many autumns. (Yunxi Gong)
【Continued Collection】Blown by the wind and scorched by the sun; dots of vermilion and dots of lacquer. Passersby sigh in lamentation: with whom do they have any acquaintance? (Fenyang Zhao).

[Added for inclusion] Shoushan held up a bamboo stick and showed it to the assembly, saying: "All of you, if you call this a bamboo stick, you commit the fault of 'contact'; if you do not call it a bamboo stick, you commit the fault of 'aversion.

Now tell me, all of you: what do you call it? Speak quickly! Speak quickly! The verse says: If you call it a bamboo stick, you commit the fault of contact; If you do not call it a bamboo stick, you commit the fault of aversion. If you can avoid both contact and aversion, Then you may see the Master of Shoushan.
Raising the bamboo whisk brings forth life and death; how could one ever allow people to scribble about it recklessly?
A single stroke across the back—if you can realize it—then even silver mountains and iron walls will shine with brilliance. (Zhao Tang 1)
He held up his bamboo staff; [the monk] immediately arrived home. If Bimozhi had not understood, he would have followed after him brandishing his fork. (Gushan Gui)
Whether facing it or turning away from it, there is no obstruction; clearly and brightly, it is raised aloft. The blade that can cut hair does not move at all;
the entire earth is the clanging of swords. (Jingshan Gaofeng)
Neither touching nor turning away, one needlessly exerts oneself in conjecture. Opening the mouth to deliberate further—white clouds stretch for thousands of miles. (Cian Yuan)
The black-lacquered bamboo whisk is neither touch nor aversion; the great earth, mountains, and rivers are all pulverized. The man-eating lion suddenly turns its body around;
do not act like a hunting hound that still chases after clods of earth. (Duan’an Yan)
He reviles others and yet reviles himself; he is angry with others and yet is angry with himself. Guard yourself! Be cautious!
What goes out from you will return to you. (Wan’an Yan)
Discerning dragons and snakes, the eyes settle heaven and earth; the myriad stars and constellations of the sky shine forth clearly.
Raising his bamboo staff, he speaks of "contradiction" and "contact"—how vividly he pierces the head and plunges it into the glue-pot! (Xiaoweng is capable.)
He raises his bamboo whisk and issues commands of killing and giving life; back and touch race against one another, while Buddhas and Patriarchs beg for their lives.
(Wumen Kai) The wild jackal howls; the lion roars. Their entire livelihood is destroyed, leaving no room for a word to be spoken. (Xutang Yu)
[Added for inclusion] Shoushan addressed the assembly, saying: "Venerable seniors, do not shout blindly or shout recklessly. I have told you before:
when one is the guest, one remains the guest from beginning to end; when one is the host, one remains the host from beginning to end.
There is no second guest, nor is there a second host. If there were two guests or two hosts, both would become blind men. Therefore it is said: If I..."
When you stand, I must sit; when I sit, you must stand. If I sit, I sit together with you; if I stand, I stand together with you.
Although it is thus, one must first apply the eye [of insight] to achieve this. The verse says:
Guest and host, existence and non-existence—both are cast aside; the hidden treasury must emerge from ordinary sentiment. With no place to rest, the door is opened;
when the moon reaches midnight, it dares not shine bright. (Virtue Hall’s Fū)
[Added to the Collection] A monk asked Shoushan, "What is the point where the student is intimately close? The Master said, "The fiftieth day of the fifth month;
the day the spring returns. The monk asked, "Ultimately, what is it? The Master said, "Winter arrives; it is the hundred-and-fifth day of Cold Food Festival."
The verse says:
At dusk, dark clouds gather over the deep wilderness; After the Double Ninth, the chrysanthemums bloom anew.
Were it not for the vanishing ice on the western peaks, How could spring arrive across the eastern mountains? (Touzi Qing)
[Added for inclusion] Shoushan was asked by a monk: "What is the path of bodhi? The Master said, "Five li from Xiangxian. [The monk asked:

"What about the matter that transcends this? The Master said, "Coming here is not easy. Verse: Five li from Xiangxian, The road of bodhi is clear. To ask about the matter beyond, One must come with no small effort.
Asking for the way at the end of a road, intending to press on; green willows and the song of orioles see off the traveler.
"The signpost says five li," he tells you—do not say that it has never pointed the way before. (Touzi Qing)
[Added from the Supplementary Collection] Shoushan was once asked by a monk, "What is the place where a student applies the mind?
The Master said, "I am surprised that your question is so late. The Verse says:

Before speaking, it is difficult to clarify the states of delusion and enlightenment; only when words are uttered can one reveal the person of sincere heart. One merely craves progress and seeks the jade of fame;
who would believe that the spiritual sprout does not require the spring? (Touzi Qing)
The Ninth Generation under the Sixth Patriarch (Part Two); the Eighth Generation under Qingyuan (Part One). [Fayan School] (Supplementary Collection):
Chan Master Fayan Wenyi of Qingliang Monastery in Shengzhou (he succeeded Luohan Chen). While traveling on pilgrimage, he encountered sudden heavy rain;
the mountain streams surged and overflowed, so he stayed temporarily at Dizang Monastery to the west of the city. Because...
He went to see Master Chanbin. Chanbin asked, "Where are you going, Senior Monk? He replied, "I am traveling on pilgrimage. Chanbin asked, "What is the matter of traveling on pilgrimage?

The Master said, "I do not know. Chanbin said, "Not knowing is most intimate. At these words, the Master attained sudden enlightenment. The verse says: Not knowing is most intimate; A single phrase cuts through the root. When the spring wind blows, The ten thousand things are all revived.
Now, with learning as vast as it was then, all subtle dust has been shed until one reaches the state of non-knowing.
Let it be short or long, there is no need for trimming or patching; let it be high or low, it is naturally held level. Whether the household is prosperous or frugal, use it as the occasion demands;

whether the field is spacious or narrow, move through it at ease with every step. As for the business of traveling on foot thirty years ago—it is clearly a betrayal of one’s own eyebrows. (Tiantong Ju)
[Added from another source] During Fayen’s opening of the hall, the senior monk Zifang arrived from Changqing.
The Master cited a verse by the late Chan Master Ling of Changqing and asked: "What is the body revealed alone amidst the myriad phenomena?
Zifang raised his whisk. The Master said, "Even if you understand it this way, how can you attain it? Zifang replied, "What is the Master’s own intention?"

"What? the Master asked. "What do you call 'the myriad phenomena'? [The monk] replied, "The ancients did not negate the myriad phenomena. The Master said, "'Amidst the myriad phenomena, the body alone is revealed.

Why speak of negating or not negating? At these words, the monk attained sudden and thorough enlightenment. The verse says: The myriad phenomena are all here; The body alone is revealed. If one does not know where to look, How can one avoid being deceived? The ancients did not negate them; They simply pointed directly at them. If you wish to see the Buddha, Look at the face before your eyes.
Amidst the myriad phenomena, the body alone is revealed. Each time we meet, we are closer. East, west, south, and north—all are the transformation of our Sovereign.
Do not laboriously seek the ferry crossing in Jiangnan. (Fushan Yuan)
Seeing the Buddha by leaving behind conceptual thought; breaking through the dust to bring forth the sutras; manifesting the family dharma—by whom was this gateway established?
Day after day the boat travels as the river’s silken expanse remains still; spring follows the grasses where the scorched earth turns green.

Whether you push it aside or not, listen to these earnest instructions: when the three paths fall into ruin, one may return at once; the pine and chrysanthemums of years past remain fragrant. (Tiantong Ju)

The Chan Master Fayen was asked by the monk Huichao, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "You are Huichao. Thereupon, the monk attained awakening. The Verse says: The master of the Dharma-eye school, Holding the staff, he struck the thief. If you can understand this, You will see that the thief has been caught. But if you still do not comprehend, I shall explain it for you once more: It is simply you yourself. Do not seek it elsewhere. If you go elsewhere to seek it, You will never find it. If you wish to know the Buddha, Look directly at your own face. Do not ask about others; Just look within your own mind. If you can see your own nature, You will realize the Way. This is the true meaning of the Buddha. Do not doubt this for a moment. If you doubt it, you will wander in birth and death. If you do not doubt it, you will transcend the world. Thus, the monk Huichao Attained realization upon hearing these words. This is the transmission of the Dharma-eye. Do not let it be lost. Preserve it well. This is the teaching of the Buddhas and Patriarchs. Do not fail to practice it. If you practice it, you will become a Buddha. If you do not practice it, you remain an ordinary person. Therefore, strive with all your might. Do not be negligent. This is the essential point. Do not misunderstand it. Understand it clearly. Then you will be free from delusion. This is the ultimate truth. There is nothing else to it. Just as the Master said: "You are Huichao. This is the very essence of the Buddha. Do not look outside yourself. Seeking outside is a mistake. Returning to oneself is the way. This is the heart of the matter. Do not let it pass in vain. Preserve it in your heart. This is the Dharma-eye treasury. Do not let it be obscured. Keep it bright and clear. Then you will see the light. This is the path of the sages. Do not follow the common crowd. Follow the sages' way. Then you will attain liberation. This is the final word. There is no other teaching. Trust in this alone. Do not seek elsewhere. If you seek elsewhere, you will be lost. Therefore, return to your own nature. This is the true Buddha. Do not doubt it. Doubt leads to suffering. Without doubt, there is peace. Peace is the state of Buddhahood. Thus, the monk Huichao Was enlightened in an instant. This is the power of the Dharma-eye. Do not underestimate its strength. It is the sword that cuts through delusion. Use it wisely. This is the legacy of the Buddhas. Do not let it die out. Pass it on to future generations. This is the work of a patriarch. Do not fail in your duty. Maintain the lineage. This is the true transmission. There is no other way. Trust in this alone. And you will find the Way. This is the end of the verse. May it be so. Amen.
Question: The Buddha’s head is perfectly formed without deficiency; do not compete in cleverness or display sharp wit.
If true gold were not forged in the furnace, how could one mistake gold for clay? (Fenyang Zhao)
The spring wind cannot stir the waters of the River Kingdom; the partridges cry deep within the flowers. When the three-tiered waves rise high, the fish transform into dragons;
yet the foolish man still scoops out the water from the night pond. (Xuedou Xian)
Traveling over treacherous crags, one asks about the difficulty of the road; someone asks for the way to the northern village or the southern.
In Chang’an, there are countless people coming and going; how many can pass through the pass without their bell? (Touzi Qing)
A monk asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "You are Huichao. [The monk] prostrated, stepped forward, and joined his palms;
he pondered for ten thousand miles, yet it remained far away. (Ciming Yuan)
Inverting official transactions, they do not yield to one another. Questioning the Buddha, they say it is Huichao. Alas, seeing a patch-robed monk, they give rise to strange interpretations;
they mistake a rainbow for a bridge to the immortal realm. (Tianyi Hui)
The mirror on the stand is so refined it excludes both the fine and the coarse; who says that when a barbarian arrives, the barbarian is immediately reflected?
Phenomena do not yield to one another, so do not ask; how pitiful that the world is muddled by names and forms. (Foyin Yuan)
The wooden man travels a thousand li; the swift horse does not shift its hooves. As the setting sun rests upon the southern lands, it neighs toward the north with the wind. (By Zhengjue Yi)
For wondrous function, one need not a frost-sharpened blade; for being able to play, why necessarily strings of jade?
At three o'clock after midnight in the bitter cold, sitting idly and sleeping idly as the clouds disperse. (Cuiyan Zhen)
As soon as the first day of the New Year arrives, it is truly spring. In the warm breeze, there is nowhere that does not exude a sense of joy.
How many travelers seeking spring along the way have mistaken the yellow oriole for the cuckoo? (Fohui Quan)
With a single large coin, one buys a piece of oil-cake; having eaten it into one's belly, one is immediately no longer hungry. (Baizhang Yuanwen).
Striking the stone, fire emerges; yet the fire-light never burns on its own. In a jade pool ten thousand fathoms deep, one sees the blue sky directly below. (Cangtang Qing)
A single elixir pill, as large as a fist; If one takes it, one ascends to immortality upon level ground.
If even a hair’s breadth of worldly attachment remains, One will miss the eight thousand li to Penglai. (Cishou Shen)
From three thousand li away, I gaze upon my hometown; layered clouds and waters stretch the traveler’s road long.
I warned you not to go down into the mountains, yet now I truly hear the cries of the monkeys that break one’s heart. (By Shangfang Yi)
He neighs at the mere sight of the wind, yet he is trapped on the salt cart. When Bo Le turns his gaze back, the value [of the horse] differs by ten thousandfold.
It is truly laughable that upon the slopes of Mount Yu today, one mistakes a common hack for a dragon colt. (Purongping)
The questioner asked the Buddha how he would answer Huichao: "Though the scale-weights may settle the price and allow for concessions, one cannot see two hawks falling from within the clouds;
the arrow has already passed ten thousand miles beyond Silla. (Changling Zhuo)
Questioning the Buddha, he said, "This is Huichao. A single phrase that meets the occasion leaves no room for leniency;
to hesitate and seek further on the road is to face ten thousand miles of layered passes and mountains. (Yunxi Gong)
Presented face-to-face, it is not difficult to see; yet the skull-mirror’s awareness remains coarse and indistinct. Even when the Great Spirit raises his hand, he cannot split it apart;
only then does one believe that what has come before was nothing but a kicking and bumping round ball. (Nanhua Bing)

The questioner asked the Buddha clearly, and Huichao received a direct answer; half a catty is eight ounces—there is no leniency. This has been a calamity for the monastic forests for ten thousand ages;
the harm done by such foul speech leaves a resentment that will not fade. (Zhenxie Le)
A sick man meets a skilled physician; a hungry person encounters a king’s banquet. Finding salt within the sauce;
bringing charcoal to one in the snow. (Yuánwù Qín). Borrowing the wife’s skirt to bow at the wife’s shrine; when asked about the Buddha, he said only, "Your wisdom surpasses [mine].
Beneath the Stone City for ten thousand ages, the waters ultimately return to the great sea to become surging waves. (Fódēng Xuán).
When asked about the Buddha, he replied, "It is Huichao. The roots and stems are intertwined with the branches and twigs;
the vast spring breeze is difficult to avoid. Which single sprout gives rise to heaven and earth? (Chuanfang).
[Continued Collection] The slightly sour plum has just begun to form its kernel; the oriole grows old and the flowers wither, their traces already ancient.
One night the southern wind shifts the handle of the Dipper; tomorrow, the misty willows have no concern for spring. (By Zhengtang Bian)
"A single character enters the gate of officialdom; nine oxen cannot pull one out. *Tsk!* This wild fox spirit has lost its nostrils entirely. (Yuelin Guan)
Huichao asked the Buddha, "Why is the Buddha so distant? Responding to the occasion with the occasion, he answered Huichao:
"At this point, one must truly brandish the blade; otherwise, the fisherman will simply settle in his nest. (Jue Tiezui)
Fayan was asked by a monk: "What is one drop of water from Cao’s spring? The Master said:
"It is one drop of water from Cao’s spring. The Verse says:
One drop of water from Cao’s spring— From this, waves and billows arise. Peach blossoms flow out from within the grotto; A fisherman’s boat at night...
Overnighting amidst the reeds and flowers (Yang Wuwai).
A single drop from the Cao source is the Cao source itself; ten thousand streams flow surging toward the sea gate.
Countless travelers on the raft fail to realize it; where wind and waves surge, there the dragon coils. (Zhaojue Zong)
A single drop from the Cao Source has long been clear and still; it flows forth into a thousand rivers, forever free of the sound of waves. How many wanderers are there in the great ocean?
Wandering aimlessly, they walk along the water’s edge in vain. (Baiyun Yuan)
Waiting by the stump does not result in catching the rabbit; the *wangxiang* spirit obtains the dark pearl. A single drop of the Cao-yuan water clearly irrigates the Five Lakes. (Fuxincai)
A single drop from Caoxi flows as an extraordinary current; it enters the vast blue ocean, crowning all under heaven.
Though fishing lines have been cast through many perilous waves, never has it been heard that the fisherman’s boat was lost. (Cao Tang Qing)
A single drop from the Cao Yuan source establishes the point of inquiry; at Qingliang’s response, the truth lies beyond words. All streams are cut off as the ultimate source is reached;
yet the hundred rivers continue their course toward the heavens. (Fodeng Xun)
[Continued Collection] "Receive a bull from one person; return a horse to another. Cherish the source of Cao; you should know the proper etiquette.
Thunder rolls and surges as the ocean waves arise—who can cut off the current and not follow downstream? To follow downstream:
at noon, the hour of midnight strikes. (Chan Master Shao).
When the source of the Cao River is reached in a single drop from the mouth, who would have known it was merely painting a cat after the model?
Within the sleeve lies the three-foot Dragon Spring Sword; though it shatters every skull, no one knows it. (Biefeng Yin)
[Appendix] When Fayen gave this response, National Teacher Shao of Tiantai heard it and attained sudden enlightenment.
All the doubts and stagnations of his life were dispersed like melting ice. He reported his realization to the Master, who said:
"In the future, you shall be venerated by kings; you will cause the ancestral Way to shine with great brilliance. I am not your equal. The Verse says:

A single drop of water from the source of Cao; they scold one another, vying to thrust out their beaks. The quail and sparrow chirp in vain, while the steed Huailou has already galloped a thousand li.
(The Moon Cave is pure.)

[Added from another source] Fayan was once asked by a monk: "I have heard it said in the teachings that 'from the ground of non-abiding, all dharmas are established. What is this ground of non-abiding? The Master said: "Form arises before substance;

names arise before naming. The Verse says: Form arises before substance; Names arise before naming. The myriad things are like flowers in the sky; The ten directions are empty and still. If you wish to know the ground of non-abiding, Look at the moon reflected in the water.
No trace remains; all news is cut off. White clouds have no root; what color is the clear breeze? It disperses the canopy of heaven without artifice, yet sustains the earth with power.
It penetrates the profound source of a thousand ages and establishes the model for the myriad phenomena.
When the motes of dust in a world-system meet in reverse, every place is Samantabhadra; when the gates of the pavilions open, every point is Maitreya. (Tiantong Ju).
[Added from another source] Fayan asked Elder Jue, "Did you come by boat or by land? He replied, "By boat. The Master said, "Where is the boat?

He replied, "The boat is in the river. Jue withdrew. The Master then asked a monk standing nearby, "Do you say that this monk just now possessed the eye [of insight], or did he not? Verse: The boat comes, the boat goes; The boat is in the river.
If you can discern its coming and going, Then you have truly seen the boat.
Water does not wash water; gold is not bartered for gold. One obtains a horse by mistaking its coat color; one delights in the zither by tuning its silk strings.
From tying knots and drawing trigrams, there have been such matters as these, until the true and pure heart of Pangu was utterly lost. (Tiantong Jue)
Fayan asked Xiu, the Mountain Head: "A difference of a hair’s breadth results in worlds as far apart as heaven and earth.
How do you understand this, elder brother? Xiu said, "A difference of a hair’s breadth results in worlds as far apart as heaven and earth.
The Master said, "How can it be right to speak thus? Xiu said, "I am simply like this. What about you, Master Brother? The Master said, "A difference of a hair’s breadth..."
Heaven and earth were as far apart as could be. Xiu then performed a prostration. The verse says:
The Master intentionally questioned his fellow man; A single blow divided the two paths by a hair’s breadth. Re-examining it, one can then understand the clear intent;
Naturally pure and bright, it does not come from hearing. (Fenyang Shao)
In those days, the Six Kingdoms were already at peace; having enjoyed peace for some time, they knew nothing of war.
Master Xiu devised the "Long Snake" formation, yet everyone in the world understands the nature of life and death. (Foyin Yuan)
How pitiable and how laughable is Master Xiushan! He falls on the ground because he rose from the ground.
This foremost pivot, revealed face-to-face, cannot be hidden; it makes one recall the old Yunmen. (Zhengjue Yi)
Sajang of Seokseong inquired kindly of his fellow practitioner; without speaking of east or west, he pointed directly south.
The two paths of light and dark, where they come and go, wind and turn indistinctly amidst the mist and mists. (Bonyung Yong)
The golden-scaled dragon wishes to transform, yet meets with its forehead being branded by another. Raising its head, it gazes upon surging billows;
where the waves clash and seize the clouds, the wind is high and heaven and earth are cold. (Fohuiquan)
When a fly sits on the head of the scale, it tilts and leans; for ten thousand generations, the balance has illuminated what is uneven.
When the exact weight down to the finest fraction (zhi-cho) is revealed, it ultimately yields to the fixed star of the scale-pan. (Tiantong Jue)
【Continued Collection】A hair’s breadth of error separates heaven from earth. What loss or gain is there in Longji’s Qingliang?
Between "yu" and "lu," "dao" and "diao," who can distinguish them? Milk in water is chosen by the Goose King. (Benjue I)
A single path as straight as a bowstring; the message of long-term peace has been delivered. Myriad states all bring tribute; the four seas have seen the smoke of war extinguished.
(The chamber is closed, yet opened).

[Added for inclusion] Fayan addressed the assembly, saying: "If you recognize the bench, you have more than enough room all around. Yunmen came forward and said: "If you recognize the bench, heaven and earth are vastly different.
The Verse says: Recognizing the bench, one has ample space on all sides; Recognizing the bench, heaven and earth are worlds apart.
I know not how I shall repay the sovereign’s grace. Clouds rise over rivers and lakes, the waves form ripples. A single ancient sail, riding upon my inspiration, departs;
With whom will I travel as we pass through the Celestial Gate? (Baoning Yong)
One does not exist, and two cannot be formed. A singing oriole cries amidst falling flowers and flowing waters. In the quiet courtyard, the rain has ceased and night is half spent;
a sliver of moon rises once more from the bottom of the sea. (Xiang Tianqing)

Pines are straight and thorns are crooked; cranes are long and ducks are short. From the ages of Fuxi and Huangdi to the present day, people have all been immersed in the mysteries of order and chaos.

When at peace, the dragon lies hidden in the abyss; when at ease, the soaring bird sheds its tether. Why then, since our patriarchs came from the West, have gain and loss, right and wrong, been so intertwined?
The lotus turns with the wind through the void; the boat cuts across the current to reach the shore. Within this, there is the clever monk.
Behold the methods of Qingliang (Tiantong Jue).
An old general holds aloft his white jade whip; the two colts gallop away with elegant grace.
Those who debate gain and loss throughout past and present merely gaze in vain before the evening rain on the western mountains (Zhengtang Bian).
Qingliang pointed it out; the two monks rolled up [the scroll]. One gained, one lost—who can understand their mutual entrustment?
We see only peach blossoms chasing the flowing water; how many have personally reached the Peach Blossom Spring? (Kentang Chong).
[Added for inclusion] A monk asked Fayan, "Who arrives first before the hall of the ancient Buddha?
The Master said, "The one who does not move a step. Verse:
Those who reach the hall before the ancient Buddhas are rare; meeting them is difficult, for their triggering mechanism is like a flash of lightning.
A dragon in stagnant water will never become a sage; though startled awake, it remains as before with eyes covered in rheum. (Tianyi Huai)

[Added by Zengshou] A monk asked Fayan, "What is the matter of kalpas of dust? The Master said, "It is all present right now. The verse says: The matter of kalpas of dust is not past; It is entirely contained within this very moment. If you wish to see the ancient Buddhas, Just look at the face before you.
All matters from aeons of dust-like kalpas are fully present right now. The Patriarch did not understand; he sat facing a wall in deep reflection.
(Yang Woei). [Added by Ch'ing-yu]: Fa-yen asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk said, "From Si-chou.
The Master said, "Has the Great Sage appeared at the pagoda this year? He replied, "He has not. The Master said, "Go. The monk then departed. The Master then asked [another monk]:
A bystander asked, "Do you say this monk has ever been to Sizhou? The monk also had no reply.
The verse says:
The wondrous, perfect golden ground is free from even a speck of dust; One who arrives there should contemplate the formless reality. Do not say that the Gate of Mystery is difficult to approach.
Turning toward him, he said: "Lifting your head, you are already among those within the pagoda" (Xuedou Zong).
[Added by Zeng] Fayan heard the vegetarian fish drum and asked a monk, "Do you hear it? If you heard it just now, you do not hear it now."
If you hear it now, it is as if you did not hear it before. The verse says: Hearing with the ears like one who is deaf;
speaking with the mouth like one who is mute. Regarding the tongue of the Dharma-eye, who is real and who is false? (By the Nun Wuzhuo).

Jinlao clearly arrived at Wutai; Xushan truly came to Min. The *vina* and the abbot face each other across the gate;
speaking of them makes one’s eyes open wide. (Zhengjue Yi)

Vast and open, without dependence; lofty and leisurely, unrestrained. When the state and its people are at peace, one reaches a place where few others go. With a modicum of power, one distinguishes the ranks;
with a vast and expansive mind and body, all is free from right and wrong. Right and wrong being transcended, one stands apart within the Great Square, where there are no tracks or ruts.
(Tiantong Jue). Chan Master Shaoshou, Abbot of Longji Mountain in Fuzhou (who succeeded Luohan Chen), while traveling on pilgrimage with Wugong and Fayen, arrived at Dizang.
While they were warming themselves by the fire and discussing a kōan, Dizang entered and asked, "The mountain..."
Heshang Da-di asked the Elder, "Are you and I the same or different? The Master said, "Not different. He then held up two fingers and said, "Two.

Because of this, the three of them became fellow students (this account is found in the *Jiují*; however, according to the *Chuándēnglù*, it differs somewhat from this version, stating that they first studied together with Fǎyǎn at Dìzàng, where their realization reached its peak;

later, as they were departing for Jiànyáng, Fǎyǎn suddenly asked: "The ancients said, 'Among the myriad phenomena, the body alone is revealed. Does this negate the myriad phenomena, or does it not? [Da-di replied: "It negates them.")

[The Master] said, "The myriad phenomena. The Teacher said, "I do not reject the myriad phenomena. [The Master] said, "What do you mean by 'rejecting' or 'not rejecting'? Confused, he returned to Dizang. Dizang said, "It has not been long since you left; why have you come back?

The Teacher said, "There was a matter that remained undecided, so how could I have feared the toil of traversing mountains and rivers? Dizang said, "That you have traversed so many mountains and rivers is no small feat. The Teacher did not yet understand the point, so he asked, "An ancient said, 'Among the myriad phenomena, the body alone is revealed.

What is the meaning of this? Dizang said, "Do you say the ancient rejected the myriad phenomena, or did he not reject them? The Teacher said, "He did not reject them. Dizang said, "Then there are two. The Teacher was struck with awe. After deep reflection, he asked again, "I wonder, did the ancient reject [the phenomena]?"

Xiang did not dismiss the myriad phenomena. Dizang asked, "What do you call 'the myriad phenomena'? At these words, the Master attained sudden enlightenment (and took his leave of Dizang once more). The verse says:
Entering the hospital, the tall reeds are entirely beyond doubt; it is all because one has not yet reached the pivot of the Patriarch’s mechanism.

Vainly studying learning to contend over long and short, one fills the belly with empty, idle words. You may distinguish the great earth, mountains, and rivers, yet when asked, you say you do not distinguish them—just like a fool.
When a person is struck by the madness of delusion, they see established conduct and do not raise an eyebrow. (Fenyang Zhao)
Mountains, rivers, and the great earth are both universal and particular; yet within the mouth, the mother-born tongue has not yet emerged.
Those many-knowing Chan practitioners force a distinction where none exists; how could a turtle ever run out of a jar? (Foyin Yuan)
Dizang, seizing the moment, held up his finger; the old masters of the past have yet to catch a glimpse of it. Heaven turns and earth revolves, yet it remains as ordinary as ever;
for ten thousand autumns and ten thousand ages, there are but two iron bars. (Baiyun Yuan).
Discussions on identity and difference are manifold; yet how many times has this old fellow ever moved his tongue? From ancient times to the present, none have been able to carry it away;
a pair of spiritual swords lean against the cold of heaven. (Baoning Yong)
[Continued Collection] Cease contending with yourself and the mountains and rivers; once the spears and shields are set in motion, there is no help for it.
Behold the General deploy his martial strategy: with two cold swords, he settles dragons and snakes. (Yuye Chuan)
How many kinds of talk are there at the hearth? How can one observe it at the very moment of its own occurrence? Arise directly and display your skill;
mountains, rivers, and the great earth are pitch black. (Xutang Yu)
[Added for inclusion] Longji addressed the assembly, saying: "The ordinary person possesses the dharmas of an ordinary person, yet the ordinary person does not know them;
the sage possesses the dharmas of a sage, yet the sage does not realize them. If the sage were to realize them, he would be an ordinary person;
if the ordinary person were to know them, he would be a sage. These words possess one principle and two meanings. If one can discern them, it will not hinder one from attaining Buddhahood.
Within the Dharma there is a point of entry. If you cannot discern it, do not say that you have no doubts.
The Verse says: The ordinary is entirely the sacred; the sacred is entirely the ordinary. Investigating the reality, cast aside names and penetrate directly.
Thoroughly penetrating and transcending the realm of both the ordinary and the sacred, the wordless child speaks incessantly. (Lingyuan Qing)
Cut away the tangled vines of public proclamations; do not employ such "it is," "it is not," "it is so," or "it is thus.
Even if you are thoroughly proficient in the meaning of every phrase, you cannot avoid calling a donkey a horse. (Wan’an Yan)
Merged peaks rise ten thousand feet high; before a word is spoken, my feet already ache. If one does not ascend upon the clouds, how could one know the chill of the stars? (Xutang Yu)
[Added from another source] Longji was asked by a monk: "When the kalpa-fire blazes forth and the great trichiliocosm is utterly destroyed, I wonder:
does this [reality] perish or not? The Master said, "It does not perish. The monk asked, "Why does it not perish? The Master said, "Because it is identical to the great trichiliocosm."

The verse says: Question: If one carves out the heart? Answer: It is like splitting open the belly. Within the words, the self turns back; why labor over such haste? The kalpa-fire burns everything together with the great trichiliocosm;
the total function remains unmoving while the sword’s edge whirls. At the peak of Longji Mountain, the dragon retreats its bones; this is the *Yanmadian* (Flaming Sky).
The drum atop [the mountain] startles the surging rapids.
(□□□). [Added by Zengshou. Longji addressed the assembly, saying: "If it is a pillar, you do not see the pillar; if it is not a pillar, you do not see the pillar.
Once 'is' and 'is not' have been discarded, realize it within 'is' and 'is not'. The verse says:
Both "is" and "is not" are neither; there is also no "not being so," for it is merely a weary exertion of deduction.
Once both ends are severed and one has returned home, who else is it that reveals the universe alone? (Lingyuan Qing)
If you can point it out, flowers move and butterflies arrive together. If you cannot point it out, you carry the spring water and return with the moon.
"It is good" is like saying the pears of Zhengzhou surpass the dates of Qingzhou. "It is not good" is like saying the road to Mount Xiang leads to the island of Penglai.
Even if you say "it is," there is no connection; even if you say "it is not," there is no connection. Treading upon a scale-weight, hard as iron; the Vajra sword cuts directly through the head.
A-he-he! Do you understand? When one knows few things, afflictions are few; where one recognizes many people, disputes are many.
(Qu'an has already [said it]).
To come from "is" and "is not" is easy; to depart from "is not" and "is" is difficult.
When "is" and "is not" are here ground away until exhausted, a single luminous pearl shines forth, chilling the gallbladder. (Yunna Qing)

The void is the drum, Mount Sumeru the mallet; though those who strike it are many, those who hear it are few. At midnight, the skull awakens from its dream;
with the bright moon filling one’s head, one thinks no more of returning home. (Danxia Chun)
[Added from the Supplementary Collection] A monk asked Liangshan, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said, "Do not speak nonsense.
The verse says:
The national laws are stern; those who violate them face peril. A movement of even a hair’s breadth is followed by the iron wheel. When the mind sprouts, the mouth responds across three thousand li.
When teeth are bared and words emerge, who can bear the bitter resentment? (Touzi Qing)

[Lian-shan increased the collection. A monk asked, "Are the meaning of the Patriarchs and the meaning of the Teachings the same or different? The Master said: "The golden crow rises in the east, and all people value it; the jade hare sinks in the west, and even Buddhas and Patriarchs are bewildered.
The Verse says: The golden crow rises in the east, All people hold it in high esteem; The jade hare sinks in the west, Even Buddhas and Patriarchs are lost.

Though the words at the assembly on Vulture Peak were universal, the phrases before the peak of Shaoshi have not yet taken form. Auspicious grasses grow thick and lush, beautiful as they hold the moon;
cold pines stand dense and verdant, emerging green from the clouds. (Danxia Chun)

[Added from another source] A monk asked Liangshan, "What is the matter of daily life? The Master said, "Jade points through the color of lapis lazuli; though red dust fills the eyes, not a grain of sand is seen. The Verse says: Jade points through the color of lapis lazuli;
Though red dust fills the eyes, not a grain of sand is seen. If you wish to know the matter of daily life, Look at the clouds and the moon in the sky.

The kalpa-fire blazes fiercely within the abode of formlessness; at the golden gate, one beholds no household of jade towers. In the precious heavens, the clouds are thin and the silver river is cold;
amidst these vast surging waves, how could the sands be moved? (Danxia Chun)
[Added from the Supplementary Collection] Chan Master Defu of Mount Yungding in Huian Commandery (he succeeded Huguoyuan).

When the Military Governor of Chengdu invited him to ascend the seat in the government yamen, a military officer from the music corps came forward to prostrate. As he rose, he looked back toward the mounting platform and said:
"Drink up the waters of the West River in a single gulp. [The monk] did not ask further; he requested, "Please swallow the mounting platform before the steps.
The Master opened both hands and sang out, "Wipe it clean and bring it here! At this, the military commander attained a sudden awakening. The verse says:
He has swallowed the mounting platform before the steps; meeting people, even his mouth finds it difficult to open. Do not be surprised that this play-cloak is brought forth again;
it was once used for village songs and community dances. (Xiaoweng is capable).

(Linji) [Added by Zeng]: Chan Master Wenshu Yingzhen of Dingzhou (heir to Deshan Mi). A monk asked: "The myriad dharmas return to the One; to what does the One return? The Master said:
"The Yellow River has nine bends. Verse: The myriad dharmas return to the One; The One returns to the source of the river. The Yellow River flows through nine bends; How could it ever reach the sea?
Questioning the Dharma to its ultimate cause, where does it return? The Yellow River flows through waves of azure ripples.
One must know that beyond the clouds, atop a thousand peaks, there stands a sacred pine, cold with dripping dew. (Touzi Qing)
The road ends and the cliff breaks off; there is no way forward. Fortunately, an old mountain man points out the source. The Yellow River, with its nine bends, is clear to the bottom.
Who would have known it was a different world altogether? (Lan’an Xu)
The nine bends cannot tolerate even a sidelong glance; who understands how to navigate the waves?
Mañjuśrī once displayed his heaven-turning hand, until the ten thousand tributary streams were dried up at their source. (Mukan Yong)

[Added for inclusion] Regarding the true cause of Mañjuśrī: A monk asked, "What was the meaning of the ancients hanging down one foot? The Master said, "Sitting too long leads to fatigue. The Verse says: Sitting for a long time results in weariness; The ancients hung down one foot.
If you wish to see the true source, Look at the face before your parents were born.
The letter was sent in haste and returned with equal speed; one foot has begun the response to follow in its tracks. Who can fully comprehend the weariness born of sitting for so long?
Like snow falling upon a red furnace, it naturally finds resonance within. (Touzi Qing)
[Added for Collection] Chan Master Nantai Qin of Mount Nanyue (Successor of Deshan Mi). A monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?

The Master said, "An inch of tortoise hair weighs seven pounds. Verse: An inch of tortoise hair weighs seven pounds; The whole body is covered in scales. If you wish to know the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West, Look at the moon reflected in the water.
Ordinarily silent when not meeting anyone, speaking immediately wounds the truth as if being too intimate.
Disregarding the phoenixes resting in the fire, he startles the stone tiger, causing it to harbor secret resentment. (Touzi Qing)

Treading upon the iron-like hardness of a scale-weight; the bewildered Chan practitioners have not yet glimpsed it.
On the mountain peaks in midwinter, fiery clouds arise; in the sixth month, heavy snow falls from the vast heavens. (Yunfeng Yue)
Treading upon a scale-weight as hard as iron, at such a time one cannot speak of reason.
A shooting star flies through the land of Silla, heading straight for Yunmen’s finger-tip. (Baizhang Yuan).
Strolling at ease through the red dust, no one asks of my length or brevity. Returning as the day draws to a close, a sliver of moon illuminates the vast blue waters.
(Lian of Tianting Monastery, Jingzhao Prefecture)
[Continued Collection] The cowherd returns home riding his ox backward; in the city during the day, he does not cease until evening.
Treading upon a scale-weight as hard as iron, who would have known the boatman was heading for Yangzhou? (Fotuoxun)

[Added for Collection] Wuzu Ji was asked by Zhimen: "I do not ask about the passing of summer and the coming of winter; what is it like when we meet beneath the forest trees? The Master said, "Listen to the jade water-clock before the Five-Phoenix Pavilion. He asked, "What can be done about the fact that the Mountain of the Lord is high and the Mountain of the Altar is low? The Master said, "Strike the golden bell atop the summit of Mount Sumeru. The Verse says: Passing summer and coming winter—what need to ask? Meeting beneath the forest trees—how can one describe it? Before the Five-Phoenix Pavilion, listen to the jade clock; On the peak of Mount Sumeru, strike the golden bell. The Mountain of the Lord is high, the Mountain of the Altar is low; Yet atop the summit, the golden bell is struck. The clouds and mist are naturally pure and clear; The sun and moon shine brightly without obstruction. If you wish to know the matter of the patriarchs, Just look at the ancient traces of the Buddhas. The mountain peaks are steep and the cliffs are deep; The path is difficult to traverse, and few reach the top. When the golden bell is struck upon the summit, All within the four seas hear it clearly. The sound reaches far, penetrating the ten directions; It is heard by all who dwell in the three realms. If you can understand this at once, Then you will see the ancient traces of the Buddhas. If you cannot yet comprehend it, Then you must look at the ancient traces of the Buddhas. High atop the mountain peaks, silver waves surge; deep within the ocean floor, red dust rises. Golden bells and jade water-chimes respond to one another, leaving the vast multitude of people across the world in doubt.
Were it not for the true creator, who could inquire at the frontier passes? Holding the whip, he turns his head back.
The four seas are good neighbors. Have you not seen how Zhongni and Wenbo Xue met beneath their overturned canopies—how wondrous and extraordinary! (Yuanwu Qin).
Listening to the jade water-chimes before the Five Phoenix Pavilion, one strikes the golden bell atop the summit of Mount Sumeru; the Great Spirit raises his hand, yet it requires no more.
Zi (Ji) broke through the ten million layers of Mount Hua (i.e., Anjue).
Chan Master Zhimen Guanzuo of Suizhou formerly resided at Beita in Fuzhou (he was a successor of Xianglin Yuan).
A monk asked, "What is it like when the lotus flower has not yet emerged from the water? The Master said, "The lotus flower. [The monk] asked, "What is it like after it has emerged?
The Master said, "The lotus leaf. The Verse says: The lotus flower before emerging from the water— The lotus flower. After it has emerged— The lotus leaf.
"The lotus flower and its leaves inform you: emerging from the water is just as it was when not yet emerged. Ask the Old Man Wang north of the river and south of the river;
one doubt resolved, another doubt arises. (Xuedou Xian)
There is a reason for the lotus and its petals: when separated from mud and water, they are utterly free of dust and stain.
One can recall the place where the nine dragons first bathed him; with every step east or west, a flower blooms. (Baiyun Cuan)
Lotus flowers and lotus leaves together in the pond; year after year, the blossoms and leaves are green interspersed with red. The spring waters ripple, clear to the very bottom;
a single cry of a bird amidst the wind of the fifth watch. (Zhang Wujin)
Smoke enshrouds the greenery beyond the railing; the wind shakes the fragrant stalks in the pond. Thank you, O lady washing clothes, for not plucking them;
they remain in the rain to shelter the mandarin ducks. (Cishou Shen)
The filaments of the lotus petals part; their boundless fragrance is bestowed upon you.
If you can discern the path to the celestial realms in a mere snap of the fingers, you shall be able to walk level-footed through the azure clouds. (Changling Zhuo)
The fragrance of the buds penetrates the cold moon at the heart of the waves; the green leaves sway lightly in the breeze upon the surface of the water.
Look at the moment when they have not yet emerged: it is all contained within a single pool. (Fojian Qín)
Mud and water are not yet separated, yet the red lotuses bloom; after the rain has ceased, their fragrance first permeates the blue waves.
Though a thousand paths of thought may lead one astray, a single turn toward the root brings immediate realization. (Fodeng Xun)
[Continued Collection] The lotus flower and its petals are neither marvelous nor mysterious. The emerald pool is limpid and transparent; the bright moon is perfectly full.
Best of all is the peace of an era without a single concern, allowing the songs of woodcutters to fill every village along the river. (Fuxincai)
The white lotus does not clarify what is hidden; the red flower emerges from the water yet does not face the sun. Wanderers, do not attempt to pass on news of it;
there is naturally a pure breeze that carries its fragrance afar. (Danxia Chun)
The lotus flower and lotus leaves serve as a conduit for you; the exchange of questions and answers is like arrows meeting at their tips.
When you face it directly, the fragrant scent comes forth inexhaustibly; you must know that it does not reside within the lotus pond. (Benjue I)
How is it to emerge from the water compared to not yet emerging? There is a reason for the lotus and its leaves. In the Golden Land, Dīpaṃkara beckoned from afar;
at Jiangling, the Wise One pointed to the dark head. (Tayuan Yue)

Lotus leaves, round and full, hold aloft emerald canopies; lotus flowers, bright and radiant, vie with one another for crimson adornment. Their fragrance transcends all categories, yet no one offers it as tribute;
once more, they follow the warm summer breeze across the wild pond. (Yungeng Jing)

A single expanse of empty stillness, beyond all conceptualization or emotion; from this, humans and devas see emptiness arise.
The oyster holds the bright moon—how profound its intent! It has once waged war against the Chan school. (Xuedou Xian)
The clam holds the bright moon; the hare carries a fetus in her womb. Infinite Zen practitioners cannot split them open. With eyes of iron and pupils of copper, what can they do?
Three thousand miles away, there is laughter and mirth. (Changling Zhuo)
The oyster holds the bright moon; the autumn waves are cold. The rabbit conceives in her womb; the night essence is frigid. A vast expanse of pure light forms a single whole.
One must surely turn back one's head and observe it well. (Fojian Yongqin)
[Continued Collection] The oyster holds within it the essence of the dark hare; how profound is its meaning! When essence and function are made clear, they transcend past and present.
The melody of the snow-song is so lofty that those who can harmonize with it are few; one knows not where the true connoisseur may be found. (Benjue I)
The jade hare conceives within her womb; the oyster holds the bright moon. The timing is precisely the Mid-Autumn Festival:
a single luminous pearl rolls upon the jade platter, utterly flawless and radiantly pure. (Cishou Shen)
[Added from the *Zengshou*] When a monk asked Zhimen, "What is the Buddha? the Master said, "Wearing straw sandals, walk barefoot.
The monk asked, "What is the matter beyond the Buddha? The Master said, "Carrying the sun and moon upon the tip of my staff."
The Verse says:
On the road, the bustling barefoot man Treads through the dust and wind until his straw sandals are worn away.
Amidst the bustle of east, west, south, and north, He frequently lifts his staff, which carries the sun and moon. (Foguo Bai)
Treading through grass shoes, walking barefoot; when a monk reaches this point, there is no fixed pattern.
With the sun and moon carried upon the tip of his staff, he wanders freely throughout the nine provinces and the four seas. (Zhenru Zhe)
The gate of wisdom truly captures the ancestral style; it lets loose Yunmen’s broad and long tongue. Great wisdom appears as if ignorant; great skill seems as if clumsy.
Though one exhausts all effort, one may still fail to penetrate through. Do not pile up more earth upon level ground;
do not drive stakes into empty space. (Tiantong Jue)
On the tip of his staff he hoists the sun and moon; hiding his body within the Big Dipper, how extraordinary!
The ocean of three thousand worlds is deep in night, yet a single point of snow has emerged from the new furnace. (Nantang Xing, 2)
Treading through worn-out straw sandals, he walks barefoot; the indignation in his breast surges toward the Ox and the Dipper. Upon the summit of Mount Sumeru he strikes the golden bell;
amidst the field of a hundred battles he roars like a lion.
Treading through worn-out straw sandals, he walks barefoot; with such grand air, he flaunts his family’s disgrace abroad.
Knowing only how to adjust his robes before others, he fails to notice his clothes have torn, revealing both elbows. (Chan Master Zui’an Yin)
[Added from another source] Master Xiang of Lotus Peak at Tiantai (he was the successor of Fengxian Shen).
On the day he passed away, he held up his staff and showed it to the assembly, saying, "When the ancients reached this point, why did they refuse to stay? No one in the assembly could answer.
The Master then said, "It was because their journey lacked strength. He spoke again, asking, "Ultimately, how is it? and he crossed his staff [over his body].

Jian said, "Carrying my staff across my shoulder, I heed no one; I go straight into a thousand peaks and ten thousand peaks. Having finished speaking, he passed away. The verse says: Carrying the staff across the shoulder, Heeding not others, He goes straight into a thousand peaks and ten thousand peaks.
Having finished speaking, he passed away. The verse says:
Dust in the eyes, soil in the ears; a thousand peaks, ten thousand peaks, yet he refuses to stay.
Falling flowers and flowing water stretch vast and boundless; raising his eyebrows, where has he gone? (Xuedou Xian)
Abiding yet not abiding, the sun is at its zenith. Master Lotus Hermitage, who can grant you permission? Carrying my staff slung across my shoulder, I heed no one;
amidst a thousand peaks and ten thousand peaks, where is this place? (Cuiyan Zhen)
The author still consents to remaining halfway; if one does not stop halfway, what then?
Carrying his staff across a thousand peaks, who in the clouds beyond can see him? (Benjue I)
Roaming luxuriantly amidst the flash of a stone-light; Linji’s “white-handed” theft has no peer.
He overturned Mount Hua until the heavens turned black—how many know their own bodies are upon the imperial tower? (Wuan Quan)
The Tenth Generation under the Sixth Patriarch (I)—Part One (Nanyue’s Ninth Generation) (Linji):

Chan Master Shanzhao of Taizi Monastery in Fenzhou (Successor of Shoushan). A monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said, "A green silk fan provides enough breeze for coolness. Verse: A green silk fan provides enough breeze for coolness; The Patriarch’s meaning is right here before you. If you seek it elsewhere, you will wander in confusion;

Do not look for it in the ancient scriptures. The wind blows freely across the nine heavens; The moon shines clearly through the ten directions. If you can understand this at once, You will see the true face of the Buddha.
A preeminent figure in the monastic forests, he settled at Fenyang; his reputation spread and his fame traveled, shaking the eight directions.
When people asked about the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West, he replied: "The fan provides sufficient wind and coolness. (Zhengjue Yi)
A fan of blue silk provides sufficient breeze and coolness. The ultimate pivot of the Dharma is skillfully raised and displayed.
When the moon shines bright and the gibbons cry out through the Three Gorges at night, where could anyone hear this without their bowels breaking? (Fohuiquan)
A fan of blue silk provides sufficient breeze and coolness; only when one personally wields it can one begin to quell the madness [of the mind].
One merely loves that which is perfectly round and seamless, yet before others, one’s eyes are as vacant as those of a sheep. (Baizun Yuanwen)
A fan of blue silk provides sufficient breeze and coolness; throughout daily life, when has it ever concealed anything?
How laughable are the countless guests within the dust, shielding their hands from the western sun as their sweat flows like boiling water. (Cishou Shen)
Fenyang’s green fan is priceless; because its cool breeze never ceases.
Have you not seen how many followers the Abbot of Yanguan had, all vying with one another to seek out the rhinoceros? (Shangfang Yi)
The style is perfectly rounded and the wondrous meaning profound; casually picking it up, he reveals it to those who know.
Though sweat poured down his back as he applied himself, once the midnight air was fresh, he felt he had let his heart down. (Fujian Yongqin, No. 2)
The Patriarch’s intent was already leaked by the Master; the round green fans provide sufficient coolness from the breeze.
The Chan practitioner, not yet understanding, asks again: "Alone and desolate, he passed through Luoyang."
Only when one can personally attain this swaying stillness does madness cease. The wind moves the lotus flowers, and the fragrance fills the hall.
Since attaining the true destination once, there is no intention to cool others; people cool themselves of their own accord. (Chu’an Fang)
[Continued Collection] Sipping vinegar and biting aged ginger; the Persian’s nostrils are long. Having caught a whiff of flavor, the mother-in-law is the father’s mother. (Kentang Chong)
A fan of blue silk provides sufficient breeze and coolness; its dignified form is perfectly round and unrevealed.
Picked up with the hand as it comes, it is used wherever one goes; the pure mechanism was never in Fenyang. (Wanshi Kong)

[Added for inclusion] Fenyang addressed the assembly, saying: "If you recognize the staff, your journey as a pilgrim is complete. Sanjiao said: "If you recognize the staff, you will enter hell like an arrow. The verse says: If you recognize the staff, your pilgrimage is finished; If you recognize the staff, you enter hell like an arrow. The staff is the staff; what is there to seek? When the staff is broken, where can one find it? The staff is the staff; what is there to seek? When the staff is broken, where can one find it?
On level ground, he abruptly establishes the topic of discourse; a voice that pierces the heavens, shaking with the chill of a raging tide.
Even if one were to recognize this staff, it would still be viewed as a sealed letter serving as a token of trust. (Xiaoweng Kan).

Vastly and aimlessly he studied the art of slaying dragons; people say his labor was spent in vain. Were it not for one who has personally reached that state, who could discuss with him the depths of failure and success? (Xutang Yu)
[Added for inclusion: Miaofengshan remarked, "Wrong. He also cited the words of Sanjiao and concluded by saying, "Wrong. I, the old monk, am not like this.
To recognize the staff as "wrong," he then offered this verse:
The three errors of Miaofeng are not medicine for those without illness. Pangjushi sells a colander; Qingping speaks of a wooden ladle.
[Added from another source] Fenyang addressed the assembly, saying: "One who expounds the Dharma must possess the Ten Wisdoms Identical to Reality.

If one does not possess the Ten Wisdoms Identical to Reality, one cannot distinguish between the heterodox and the orthodox, nor differentiate the monastic from the lay, and thus cannot act as a guide for devas and humans."
The eyes and mind discern right from wrong. It is like a bird flying through the sky with its wings broken; it is like an arrow shot at a target with its string severed.
Because the string is severed, the target is not hit; because the wings are broken, flight through the sky is impossible.
When the string is strong and the wings are firm, both the sky and the target are thoroughly penetrated. What is this "Ten Wisdoms Identical with Reality"? [I ask] you, venerable elders.
He pointed them out: first, same substance; second, same great matter; third, same in total practice; fourth, same true resolve; fifth, same universal pervasiveness;
sixth, same full endowment; seventh, same in gain and loss; eighth, same in birth and death; ninth, same in the roar of sound;
tenth, same in attaining entry. He further asked: "With what kind of person does one attain entry? With whom?"
A roar in unison. What is this "being the same in life and death"? What thing is "the same in gain and loss"? Which one is "the same in being fully endowed"?
What is it that is "the same in pervading everywhere"? Who is "the same in true resolve"? Who is able to "participate as one in all"?
Which one is "the same in the Great Matter"? What object is "the same in its single substance"? Is there anyone who can bring forth [an answer]?
Those who can point it out do not begrudge their compassion; those who cannot point it out have not yet attained the eye of study.
You must discern this thoroughly and recognize right from wrong. The true face is present right now. Jingshan Gaofeng said:
"If Yangshan had not possessed this true face present right now at the end, he would have met with a total failure. Nevertheless, even so..."
"I have lost my children and grandchildren. [He lets out] a shout. The verse says:
Rabbit horns and tortoise hair planted before the eyes; An iron mountain facing one, its form towering and steep. East, west, south, north—no door through which to enter;
Eons of ignorance reduced to ashes this very moment.
The ten knowledges share the same true face; among them, one knowledge is the root source.
If a person wishes to recognize the old man of Fenyang, he must split the Three Mysteries into two sides. (Hong Juefan)
For ten years I searched the lakes and seas for an enemy; failing to find an enemy, I would not cease my quest.
The peony blooms as the face of a Bodhisattva; the palmyra leaf grows as the head of a yakṣa. (Gushan Gui)
The painting captures the *tathatā* so vividly; amidst the flowers, its wings are spread wide. The yellow oriole peeks with bated breath, not daring to alight upon the branch. (Zhengtang Bian)
The "Yangchun" and "Bai-xue" melodies are difficult for others to harmonize; the clear mirror and icy pitcher are not easily beheld. A single tangle of willow threads cannot be gathered in;
they are draped by the gentle breeze upon the jade balustrade. (In the style of He’o-an).
[Added to the Collection] Chan Master Guisheng of Guangjiao Monastery in Ye County, Ruizhou (successor of Shoushan). A monk asked, "What is the place where a student applies his mind in secret?
The Master said, "Rolling a ball through a bustling marketplace. The monk asked, "What is the meaning of this? The Master said, "Invite everyone to look. Verse:
Rolling a ball through the noisy market, Everyone is invited to gaze. The true meaning lies right here; Who can see it clearly?
Rolling the ball in the bustling marketplace, all people gaze on. A gust of clear wind blows, chilling the face. To settle turmoil, there is no need for a double-edged sword;
to bring life back, what necessity is there for the Nine-Return Elixir? (Ji’an Jue)
Chan Master Yunchong of Guyin Mountain in Xiangzhou (also known as Shimen Cong and Cizhao Cong; he was a successor of Shoushan).
A monk asked, "The sun passes and the moon comes, and before one realizes it, the years have grown old. Is there anyone who does not grow old? The Master said:

"Is there? [The questioner] asked, "What is it that does not age? The Master said, "A coiled dragon exerts its strength with a loud cry; as evening falls, its spiritual essence becomes even more abundant.
The Verse says: A coiled dragon exerts its strength with a loud cry; As evening falls, its spiritual essence becomes even more abundant.
No clouds within the cavern—this is another heaven. Peach blossoms like brocade, willows like mist. The immortals do not reckon winter or summer;
when the rocks crumble and the pines wither, a year has passed. (Amitāyus).
When a monk asked Cizhao Cong, "What is the Way? the Master said, "The thirtieth day of the twelfth lunar month.
The verse says:
The thirtieth day of the twelfth lunar month— Open your mouth and it is already an imperial edict. If you intend to ask "What is it? again, Tomorrow will be the first day of the first lunar month.
(Wuzu Fayan): On the thirtieth day of the twelfth lunar month, the True Man has good news: wearing a cap, he walks through the empty mountains; wearing boots, he stands upon the water.
(Cyunna’s Commemoration).
Chan Master Yuanlian of Guanghui Monastery in Ruzhou (a successor of Shoushan). When he first arrived at Shoushan, Shoushan asked, "Where have you recently departed from?
The Master replied, "From Hanshang. Shoushan held up his fist and said, "Is there still this in Hanshang?"
[The Master] said, "What kind of bowl is this that makes such a ringing sound? Shan said, "Blind! The Master said, "Exactly so," and after giving a single clap, he departed.
On another day, he asked again, "When a student has personally reached the Treasure Mountain but returns empty-handed, what then?
Shan said, "A torch before every door. The Master attained great enlightenment and said, "I, [the student],..."

Who would believe it when you return empty-handed? A donkey-load or a horse-load brought through the gate;
every household raises its torches as the midnight sky opens like broad daylight. (Baizhang Yuan).
When reaching the Mountain of Jewels, what is there to do? Returning empty-handed, the gain is great. Before every door is a torch;
as bright as the sun and moon, it illuminates the mountains and rivers. (Fujian Qin)

Chan Master Zhixian of Beichen Monastery in Tanzhou (heir to Fuyan Ya). On the eve of the New Year, he gave a small *chan* (sermon), saying:
"The year has ended and the age is exhausted; there is nothing with which to celebrate the year-end with you all. This old monk shall roast a white ox from the open field."
[The Master] cooks millet porridge, boils wild vegetable soup, and burns firewood to keep warm. After everyone has eaten, they sing the *murata raku* (village field music).
Why? To avoid leaning on others' doorways or huddling by others' walls, only to be called "Master" by the people of the age.
He descends from his seat and returns to the Abbot’s quarters. When night falls, the *vinaya-dhara* enters the quarters to pay his respects.
[The guest] said, "A man from the county has come to summon the Master. The Master asked, "For what purpose?
He replied, "He says that the Master slaughters oxen but does not surrender the hides and horns.

The Master then took off his hat, threw it on the ground, and as the other picked it up, the Master descended from his meditation seat, grabbed him by the chest, and shouted, "Thief! Thief! The other then [took the hat].

The Master covered the head of his attendant with his robe and said, "It is cold; let us return, Preceptor. The attendant laughed loudly and went out. At that time, Fachang Yu was serving as the attendant. The Master looked at Chang and asked, "How do you resolve this koan? Chang replied, "Paper is selling for high prices in Tanzhou; one case covers all. The Verse says: The Master covers the head with his robe, The cold wind blows through the night. One indictment settles the matter; The whole assembly is enlightened. The Master’s intent is like a thunderclap; The attendant’s laughter is like a spring peal. The ancient path is wide and open; Who would dare to tread it? If you can see through this, You will know the meaning of the verse. If you cannot yet discern it, Look at the words of the ancients. Having tucked away the leather and horn, one must attend to the loom. Letting go, one immediately ties up the work and returns home. Leave it to this time when the yellow snow falls;
the whole family gathers around the fire as they close the wooden gate. (Baiyun Yuan).
The Buddha-nature must be revealed through its essential characteristics and boundaries. At the New Year’s Eve of Beichan, the profound ford was opened;
amidst the assembly, he alone wielded the blade of Cook Ding with unrestrained mastery. Even until now, this story remains fresh. (Lingyuan Qing, 2)
Coming to examine the skin and bones to seek a true friend, a single word that strikes the mark is worth ten thousand pieces of gold.
If you do not understand when the hat is thrown down, how can you avoid picking up the flower-needle before your eyes?
Where is the ox whose hide is divided and horns are bound? The hairpins, bracelets, jars, and basins are all but a single gold. Do not say there are no rules for such great function;
when meeting the opportunity, it must be like a mustard seed entering a needle’s eye. (Cao Tang Qing)
The white ox in the open field must be cooked at once; for the year-end feast, prepare a simple soup of wild greens.
Do not say that the flavor within is meager; you must know that it fills the bellies of all under heaven. (Puyongping)

In the Northern Chan tradition, they slaughter the white ox for the New Year feast; an official document arrives urgently from the government demanding its delivery. He stands there and hands over its hide and horns; in haste, he casts down his old helmet. (Mañjuśrī says: *Note: This is a verse by Wumen Huikai from the *Wumen Guan* (The Gateless Barrier), Case 29. The "white ox" refers to the Buddha-nature or the fundamental reality;
the "official document" represents the demands of worldly conditions or karmic constraints. To "cast down the old helmet" signifies the relinquishing of one's former identity or attachments.*

[Continued Collection] At the end of the year during the night watch at Beichan, a clever arrangement was made out of the ordinary. The Rector extended his hand; the thread went out and the silk came back.
The Master of the Fields hurried the clappers; Baolao danced the San-tai. Had he been commanded to issue the true edict, they would have been made alive and buried in a single pit. (Shi’an Shi)
The white ox is cooked and all is truly joyful; yet the hide and horns must still be pursued by the authorities.
Having paid the tax at the eaves of the cap, before the lamp, the drum and gong toll as the night draws long. (Tianmu Li)
[Added to the Collection] Bei Chan was asked by a monk, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "It cannot be lifted by a spoon.
The Verse says: It cannot be lifted by a spoon; it cannot be stirred open by chopsticks. With palms joined in praise, he said: "Excellent! Excellent! (Shushan Ru).

[Added for inclusion]: Chan Master Xiaocong of Dongshan in Ruizhou (he was a successor of Wenshu Zhen). He used to carry firewood up the mountain himself. On the way, he encountered a monk who asked, "There is firewood on the mountain;

why are you carrying it away? The Master set the firewood down on the ground and said, "Do you understand? The monk replied, "I do not understand. The Master said, "I want to burn it. Verse: Carrying wood upon his back, he climbs the mountain peak; Meeting a monk on the path, he sets it down with ease. "I want to burn it"—these words are like a thunderclap; The entire world is filled with the fragrance of incense.
Do not guess when this journey will end; heading north, you must surely reach Mount Wutai.
If you encounter the place where Mañjuśrī emits light, earnestly remember me when you return. (Xutang Yu)
Carrying firewood and suffering from the heat upon one's back; meeting on a narrow path, there is no room for discussion. Beyond the green mountains, where thin smoke and setting sun linger;
across the ground, the scars of axes and hatchets cannot be gathered up. (Gong of Shilin)
Dongshan Cong said: "The entire Great Canon of the Teachings is merely this single character 'zhi' (之).
Verse: The strokes and dots are distinct, yet there is no principle; How many times did the Old Barbarian fail to lift it up?
It is better to entrust it to General Wang; Boundless elegance returns to his hands. (Baizhang Yuan)

[Added for Collection] Because of a monk’s question, Dongshan Cong said: "Since you are the Great Sage of Sizhou, why do you appear in Yangzhou? The Master replied: "A gentleman loves wealth, but he acquires it through the proper way.

The Verse says: A gentleman loves wealth, But takes it by the right path. When the Great Sage of Sizhou Appears in Yangzhou, He is like the moon reflected in ten thousand streams; How could there be two moons? If you wish to know the Great Sage, Look at the man on the street.
Sizhou suddenly manifested in Yangzhou; the discourse-paths of the world’s masters are dense. A gentleman may love wealth, but he takes it according to the Way.
The Persian from the South Sea has a coarse nostril. (Ciming Yuan)
The Jade Hall has a path for men to reach; that my name is not upon the Golden Banner leaves me only with shame.
I have long lamented that, though this poor scholar has read every book to the end, in his old age he has not yet donned even a single green robe. (By Boting Yong)
[Added from the Supplementary Collection] Chan Master Chongxian of Xuedou Mountain in Mingzhou (a successor of Zhimen Zu) addressed the assembly, saying:

"The blade from Longquan and an axe share the same substance, yet their sharpness and dullness differ vastly. A hack and a thoroughbred horse travel the same road, yet their speed and slowness are distinct. A verse says:

To say that something resembling lang-jan is still jade; to claim that brass is like gold—these are my own regrets for having a nature so common and base, lacking yet a brilliant mirror of the mind (Fojian Qin).
[Added for inclusion] Xuedou addressed the assembly, saying: "It is like when the world is about to perish and the great waters surge forth.
Within them, immeasurable sentient beings—some submerged, some not—are wailing piteously to one another and look up toward the vast blue sky, all crying out, 'Save us!
At that moment, a celestial being from the Fourth Dhyāna Heaven sees this and, upon seeing them, lets out a loud shout: 'Alas, you multitudes!'"
"Born! I previously warned you, telling you to come up here frequently, yet you would not listen.
Now, what remedy is there? (Clapping his hands) Return to the hall! The verse says:
Beyond the kalpas, the sound of waves fills the world; sentient beings have no place to climb or grasp.
Vast and empty is the realm of pure void beyond the heavens—who can understand ascending through the air to the celestial gates of the Sovereign? (Guītáng Jūshì)

[Added from the Supplementary Collection] When Xuedou was residing at Cuifeng, several monks arrived. The Master said, "New arrivals? The monks replied, "Yes. The Master said, "Go to the hall for instruction.
Just as the monks were about to leave, the Master called out again, "Come here, come here! The monks turned their heads; the Master said, "It is rare to have monks arrive from Dongting.

I shall give you each a cup of tea to drink. The Verse says: The mountain peaks are high and steep, Yet the path is not difficult to traverse. If you can turn your head and look back, A cup of tea is served right before you.
The introductory phrase has already been answered; calling away and summoning back is the second head.
Those who do not know the taste of tea upon reaching this point are merely busily buying a boat for Lake Dongting in vain. (Xutang Yu)
[Added for inclusion] Xuedou revised the *Fishing Father* verse by Chuanzi, saying: "The night is still and the water cold; the fish do not bite.
The boat is filled with the bright moon as he returns home. Verse:
When the shimmering golden scales leap upon the waves, At Huating, he lingered to admire them and was slow to descend the hook.
Who would have known that Xue Lao was so practiced at casting his line? Without disturbing the billows, he caught him. (Baiyun Yuan)
